column5: Eliphaz's unnamed wife
column7: The Bible does not give this woman's name. The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz, and his concubine Timna separately bore Amalek ([[@1036011-1036012|Gen 36:11-12]]).

column5: Ezekiel’s wife, whose death became a sign
column7: God said he would take away from Ezekiel "the desire of your eyes" ([[@26024016|Ezek 24:16]]). That evening his wife died, and because Ezekiel did not mourn, as he had been commanded, he became a sign to the people ([[@26024018|Ezek 24:18]]; [[@26024024|Ezek 24:24]]).

column5: Mother of Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai
column7: The Bible does not give her name. The sons born to Hezron were Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai ([[@13002009|1 Chr 2:9]]).

column5: Jerahmeel’s wife, likely the mother of Ram
column7: The Bible does not give her name. Jerahmeel’s sons included Ram ([[@13002025|1 Chr 2:25]]), and he also had 'another wife,' Atarah, who bore Onam ([[@13002026|1 Chr 2:26]]).

column5: Mother of Shallum
column7: The Bible does not give the mother’s name in this verse. Josiah’s sons were Johanan, Jehoiakim, Zedekiah, and Shallum ([[@13003015|1 Chr 3:15]]).

column5: Woman who looked back and turned to salt
column7: When Sodom was destroyed, the angels urged Lot to take his wife and two daughters and leave ([[@1019015|Gen 19:15]]). But Lot's wife looked back and became a pillar of salt ([[@1019026|Gen 19:26]]).

column5: Peter's wife, whose mother Jesus healed
column7: Jesus went into Peter's house and healed his mother-in-law, who was lying sick with a fever ([[@40008014-40008015|Matt 8:14-15]]). Paul says that Cephas (Peter) took along a believing wife ([[@46009005|1 Cor 9:5]]).

column5: Mother of Shaul, Simeon’s son
column7: She was the wife of Simeon, Jacob’s son, and her name is not given. Simeon’s son Shaul was "the son of a Canaanite woman" ([[@1046010|Gen 46:10]]; [[@2006015|Exod 6:15]]).

column5: Solomon’s daughter, wife of Ben Abinadab
column7: She was Solomon’s daughter. She became the wife of Ben Abinadab, the officer over all the height of Dor ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004011|1 Kgs 4:11]]).

column5: Moses' older brother, Israel's first high priest
column7: He was a Levite and the older brother of Moses. Because he spoke well, he was given the task of speaking to the people in Moses' place ([[@2004014-2004016|Exod 4:14-16]]). God appointed Aaron and his sons to serve as priests ([[@2028001|Exod 28:1]]). He also did a great wrong at the foot of Mount Sinai when he made a golden calf at the people's demand ([[@2032004|Exod 32:4]]). When he died on Mount Hor, his garments were put on his son Eleazar ([[@4020028|Num 20:28]]).

column5: Eunuch of King Ahasuerus
column7: He was one of the seven eunuchs serving in the king’s presence whom King Ahasuerus sent to bring Queen Vashti ([[@17001010-17001011|Esth 1:10-11]]).

column5: River of Damascus
column7: This is the river of Damascus that Naaman, when told to wash seven times in the Jordan, said was better than all the waters of Israel ([[@12005010-12005012|2 Kgs 5:10-12]]).

column5: A warm, familiar word for 'father'
column7: Abba is an Aramaic word for calling one's father in a warm, familiar way. It appears three times in the Bible, always together as "Abba, Father". Before he was arrested, Jesus prayed, calling out "Abba, Father", asking him to take this cup away, yet asking that his Father's will be done ([[@41014036|Mark 14:36]]). Paul said that believers have received the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, "Abba! Father!", and that God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts ([[@45008015|Rom 8:15]]; [[@48004006|Gal 4:6]]).

column5: Father of Adoniram, Solomon’s labor officer
column7: He was the father of Adoniram, who was over the forced labor in Solomon’s time ([[@11004006|1 Kgs 4:6]]). Adoniram oversaw the workers sent to Lebanon ([[@11005014|1 Kgs 5:14]]).

column5: Father of Shelemiah
column7: He was the father of Shelemiah, whom King Jehoiakim sent to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But the LORD hid them ([[@24036026|Jer 36:26]]).

column5: Merarite, ancestor of Ethan
column7: He was a Levite of the sons of Merari and the grandfather of Ethan the singer. Ethan’s father Kishi was the son of Abdi ([[@13006044|1 Chr 6:44]]).

column5: Father of Kish, a Levite in Hezekiah’s time
column7: He was the father of Kish, a Levite of the sons of Merari who arose to cleanse the temple in Hezekiah’s time ([[@14029012|2 Chr 29:12]]).

column5: Man who had married a foreign wife
column7: He was one of the sons of Elam who had married foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010026|Ezra 10:26]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Father of Ahi, a Gadite chief
column7: He was the son of Guni in the genealogy of the Gadites and the father of Ahi, who became a chief ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005015|1 Chr 5:15]]).

column5: A Levite town of the tribe of Asher
column7: It was a town of the tribe of Asher that was given to the Levites descended from Gershon ([[@6021030|Josh 21:30]]; [[@13006074|1 Chr 6:74]]).

column5: Judge from Pirathon in Ephraim
column7: The son of Hillel the Pirathonite, he became judge of Israel and judged for eight years ([[@7012013-7012014|Judg 12:13-14]]). He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, and when he died he was buried in Pirathon ([[@7012015|Judg 12:15]]).

column5: Benjamite, son of Shashak
column7: He was one of the sons of Shashak in the genealogy of Benjamin ([[@13008023-13008025|1 Chr 8:23-25]]). Other people with the same name also appear in the Bible.

column5: Firstborn of Jeiel, the father of Gibeon
column7: He was the firstborn son of Jeiel, the father of Gibeon who lived in Gibeon, and of his wife Maacah ([[@13008029-13008030|1 Chr 8:29-30]]; [[@13009036|1 Chr 9:36]]).

column5: Adam's second son, the righteous man killed by Cain
column7: He was the second son of Adam and Eve, and he was a keeper of sheep ([[@1004002|Gen 4:2]]). Abel brought the firstborn of his flock and its fat, and the LORD accepted Abel and his offering ([[@1004004|Gen 4:4]]). His brother Cain, very angry that his own offering was not accepted, attacked Abel in the field and killed him ([[@1004005|Gen 4:5]], 8). Hebrews says that "By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain," and so was declared righteous, and Jesus also called him "righteous Abel" ([[@58011004|Heb 11:4]]; [[@40023035|Matt 23:35]]).

column5: Stone where the LORD’s ark was set
column7: This was the great stone in the field of Joshua of Beth Shemesh on which the LORD’s ark was set down when it came back from the Philistines ([[@9006014-9006015|1 Sam 6:14-15]]). The stone was still in that field when this was written ([[@9006018|1 Sam 6:18]]).

column5: Northern Israelite town, also called Abel Maim
column7: It was a town in the north of Israel. When Sheba the son of Bichri, who rebelled against David, hid there, Joab besieged the town and tried to tear down its wall ([[@10020015|2 Sam 20:15]]). Then a wise woman of the town called to Joab and tried to save the town, reminding him that people used to say, "They shall surely ask counsel at Abel," and in the end the townspeople cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab, and Joab withdrew ([[@10020016-10020022|2 Sam 20:16-22]]). Later Ben Hadad king of Syria attacked this town, and Chronicles, telling the same event, calls it Abel Maim ([[@11015020|1 Kgs 15:20]]; [[@14016004|2 Chr 16:4]]). Later still, Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria took it and carried its people away captive ([[@12015029|2 Kgs 15:29]]).

column5: Place where Jephthah struck Ammon
column7: When the judge Jephthah fought the children of Ammon, he struck them with a very great slaughter from Aroer all the way to Abelcheramim ([[@7011032-7011033|Judg 11:32-33]]).

column5: The hometown of Elisha
column7: The Midianite army, chased by Gideon, fled as far as the border of this place ([[@7007022|Judg 7:22]]). The prophet Elisha was 'the son of Shaphat of Abel Meholah' ([[@11019016|1 Kgs 19:16]]).

column5: Mother of King Hezekiah
column7: She was the mother of King Hezekiah of Judah and the daughter of Zechariah ([[@12018002|2 Kgs 18:2]]). In 2 Chronicles her name is written 'Abijah' ([[@14029001|2 Chr 29:1]]).

column5: One of David's mighty men, an Arbathite
column7: He was one of David's mighty men, an Arbathite ([[@10023031|2 Sam 23:31]]). In the list in 1 Chronicles, 'Abiel the Arbathite' appears in the same place ([[@13011032|1 Chr 11:32]]).

column5: Wife of Hezron, mother of Ashhur
column7: She was the wife of Hezron of the tribe of Judah. After Hezron died in Caleb Ephrathah, she bore Ashhur the father of Tekoa ([[@13002024|1 Chr 2:24]]).

column5: Priest in David's time
column7: He was the son of Ahimelech. When Saul killed the priests of Nob, he alone escaped and fled to David ([[@9022020|1 Sam 22:20]]). He came with an ephod in his hand and helped David inquire of God ([[@9023006-9023009|1 Sam 23:6-9]]). He served as priest alongside Zadok throughout David's reign ([[@10020025|2 Sam 20:25]]), but because he sided with Adonijah, Solomon sent him to his hometown of Anathoth and removed him from the priesthood. This fulfilled the word spoken about the house of Eli ([[@11002026-11002027|1 Kgs 2:26-27]]).

column5: Son of Midian, descendant of Keturah
column7: He was a son of Midian, whom Abraham fathered by his later wife Keturah ([[@1025002|Gen 25:2]], 4). Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, and Eldaah were his brothers ([[@13001033|1 Chr 1:33]]).

column5: Leader of the tribe of Benjamin in the wilderness
column7: He was the son of Gideoni and the leader of the children of Benjamin in the wilderness ([[@4001011|Num 1:11]]; [[@4002022|Num 2:22]]). On the ninth day he brought the offering on behalf of the children of Benjamin ([[@4007060|Num 7:60]]).

column5: Benjamite, father of Kish and Ner
column7: He was a man of the tribe of Benjamin, and Saul's father Kish is introduced as "Kish the son of Abiel" ([[@9009001|1 Sam 9:1]]). Ner, the father of Saul's army commander Abner, is also said to be the son of Abiel ([[@9014051|1 Sam 14:51]]). The genealogy in Chronicles says that Ner was the father of Kish and Kish the father of Saul ([[@13008033|1 Chr 8:33]]), so scholars differ on exactly how Abiel was related to Saul.

column5: The family in Manasseh to which Gideon belonged
column7: It was a family of the tribe of Manasseh, named first when the children of Manasseh received their lots by families ([[@6017002|Josh 17:2]]). In the genealogy of Numbers it is written as 'the family of the Iezerites' ([[@4026030|Num 26:30]]). Joash, the father of the judge Gideon, belonged to this family, and their town was Ophrah ([[@7006011|Judg 6:11]]). When the LORD's Spirit came on Gideon and he blew a trumpet, the Abiezrites all gathered to follow him ([[@7006034|Judg 6:34]]).

column5: An Anathothite, one of David's mighty men
column7: He was from Anathoth and was one of David's mighty men ([[@10023027|2 Sam 23:27]]). As the ninth commander, for the ninth month, he was in charge of a division of twenty-four thousand ([[@13027012|1 Chr 27:12]]).

column5: Manassite, son of Hammolecheth
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Manasseh as a son born to Hammolecheth. His brothers were Ishhod and Mahlah ([[@13007018|1 Chr 7:18]]).

column5: Nabal's wife, later David's wife
column7: She was the wife of Nabal of Carmel, and the Bible introduces her as a woman who "was intelligent and had a beautiful face" ([[@9025003|1 Sam 25:3]]). When her husband insulted David's young men, she quickly prepared bread, wine, and sheep and went out to meet David, calming his anger ([[@9025018|1 Sam 25:18]]). David blessed the LORD who had sent her and praised her good sense for keeping him from shedding blood ([[@9025032-9025033|1 Sam 25:32-33]]). After Nabal died, she became David's wife and bore him a son, Chileab ([[@10003003|2 Sam 3:3]]).

column5: David's sister, mother of Amasa
column7: She was a sister of Jesse's sons, and so David's sister ([[@13002016|1 Chr 2:16]]). She bore Amasa to Jether the Ishmaelite ([[@13002017|1 Chr 2:17]]).

column5: Father of Zuriel, Merarite chief
column7: He was the father of Zuriel, who became the prince of the families of Merari in the wilderness. The families of Merari camped on the north side of the tabernacle ([[@4003035|Num 3:35]]).

column5: Wife of Abishur
column7: She was the wife of Abishur, a descendant of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah, and she bore Ahban and Molid ([[@13002028-13002029|1 Chr 2:28-29]]).

column5: Gadite who lived in Gilead
column7: He was the son of Huri in the genealogy of Gad, and his sons lived in Gilead in Bashan ([[@13005014|1 Chr 5:14]]; [[@13005016|1 Chr 5:16]]).

column5: Mother of Mahalath, Rehoboam’s wife
column7: She was the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse. She was the mother of Mahalath, who became Rehoboam’s wife ([[@14011018|2 Chr 11:18]]).

column5: Father of Esther
column7: He was Mordecai's uncle and Esther's father ([[@17002015|Esth 2:15]]). In the letter about Purim, too, she is called 'Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail' ([[@17009029|Esth 9:29]]).

column5: Aaron's second son, who died for strange fire
column7: Aaron's second son, he was set apart as a priest along with his older brother Nadab and his younger brothers Eleazar and Ithamar ([[@2028001|Exod 28:1]]). At Mount Sinai he went up with Moses, Aaron, and the seventy elders and saw God ([[@2024009-2024010|Exod 24:9-10]]). But with Nadab he offered incense with strange fire that the LORD had not commanded, and fire came out from before the LORD and consumed them ([[@3010001-3010002|Lev 10:1-2]]). They had no sons ([[@4003004|Num 3:4]]).

column5: Benjamite, son of Bela
column7: He was one of the sons of Bela, Benjamin’s firstborn ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]; [[@13008003|1 Chr 8:3]]). His brothers included Addar and Gera.

column5: Second son of Samuel
column7: The second son of Samuel, he became a judge in Beersheba along with his older brother Joel ([[@9008002|1 Sam 8:2]]). But the two sons did not walk in their father's ways and took bribes ([[@9008003|1 Sam 8:3]]).

column5: Jeroboam’s son who died young
column7: He was a son of Jeroboam king of Israel, and he fell sick ([[@11014001|1 Kgs 14:1]]). Just as the prophet Ahijah had said, he died as his mother reached the threshold of the house in Tirzah ([[@11014012|1 Kgs 14:12]]; [[@11014017|1 Kgs 14:17]]).

column5: Son of Rehoboam and king of Judah
column7: He was the son of Rehoboam; he succeeded him as king of Judah and reigned three years in Jerusalem ([[@14013001-14013002|2 Chr 13:1-2]]). Kings calls him Abijam and says he walked in the sins of his father and his heart was not perfect with God ([[@11015001-11015003|1 Kgs 15:1-3]]). When he fought against Jeroboam king of Israel, he had only half as many soldiers, but he stood on Mount Zemaraim and called out to Israel not to fight against the LORD ([[@14013003-14013012|2 Chr 13:3-12]]). When the people of Judah relied on the LORD, God struck Jeroboam and Israel ([[@14013015|2 Chr 13:15]]).

column5: Benjamite, son of Becher
column7: He was one of the sons of Becher, Benjamin’s son. All of Becher’s sons were heads of their fathers’ houses and mighty men of valor ([[@13007008-13007009|1 Chr 7:8-9]]).

column5: Ancestor of the eighth priestly division
column7: When the priestly divisions were assigned by lot in David's time, the eighth lot fell to him ([[@13024010|1 Chr 24:10]]). Zacharias, the father of John the Baptist, was a priest of 'the priestly division of Abijah' ([[@42001005|Luke 1:5]]).

column5: A priest who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time
column7: He was one of the priests who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010007|Neh 10:7]]). The same name also appears in the list of priests who returned with Zerubbabel ([[@16012004|Neh 12:4]]).

column5: Region ruled by Lysanias
column7: This was the region Lysanias ruled as tetrarch around the time John the Baptist began his ministry ([[@42003001-42003002|Luke 3:1-2]]).

column5: Son of Joktan, descendant of Shem
column7: He was a son of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, and is named among Joktan's many sons, such as Almodad and Sheleph ([[@1010026|Gen 10:26]], 28; [[@13001022|1 Chr 1:22]]).

column5: King of Gerar in Abraham's and Isaac's time
column7: He was the king of Gerar who took Sarah when Abraham said his wife was his sister. When God appeared to him in a dream and warned him, he sent Sarah back ([[@1020002-1020007|Gen 20:2-7]]). Later he made a covenant with Abraham at Beersheba ([[@1021027-1021032|Gen 21:27-32]]). An Abimelech, Philistine king of Gerar, also appears in Isaac's time; when he found out that Isaac had called Rebekah his sister, he rebuked him and ordered his people not to harm them ([[@1026008-1026011|Gen 26:8-11]]). Scholars differ on whether the Abimelech of the two stories is the same person.

column5: Gideon's son, who made himself king of Shechem
column7: Abimelech was Gideon's son by his concubine in Shechem ([[@7008031|Judg 8:31]]). After Gideon died, he won the support of the men of Shechem, killed his seventy brothers on one stone at Ophrah, and became king ([[@7009005-7009006|Judg 9:5-6]]). Only the youngest, Jotham, survived by hiding, and he rebuked the men of Shechem from the top of Mount Gerizim ([[@7009007|Judg 9:7]]). Abimelech ruled for three years; while he was attacking Thebez, a woman threw an upper millstone that broke his skull, so he had his armor bearer run him through, and he died ([[@7009053-7009054|Judg 9:53-54]]).

column5: The man who kept the ark at home
column7: The men of Kiriath Jearim brought the ark of the LORD into his house, and his son Eleazar was set apart to keep it ([[@9007001|1 Sam 7:1]]). Later David moved the ark out of his house ([[@10006003|2 Sam 6:3]]).

column5: A son of King Saul
column7: He was a son of King Saul who died in battle against the Philistines along with his brothers Jonathan and Malchishua ([[@9031002|1 Sam 31:2]]; [[@13008033|1 Chr 8:33]]).

column5: Jesse's second son, David's brother
column7: He was Jesse's second son, who passed before Samuel but was not chosen ([[@9016008|1 Sam 16:8]]). He went to war following Saul along with his older brother Eliab ([[@9017013|1 Sam 17:13]]).

column5: Officer who was Solomon’s son-in-law
column7: He was one of Solomon’s twelve officers and was in charge of all the height of Dor. He married Solomon’s daughter Taphath ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004011|1 Kgs 4:11]]).

column5: Father of Barak
column7: He was the father of Barak, who defeated Sisera together with Deborah ([[@7004006|Judg 4:6]]). Barak was often called 'Barak the son of Abinoam' ([[@7004012|Judg 4:12]]; [[@7005001|Judg 5:1]]).

column5: Reubenite swallowed by the earth for opposing Moses
column7: He was the son of Eliab, a Reubenite, and together with his brother Dathan he joined Korah's company and rose up against Moses and Aaron ([[@4016001|Num 16:1]]). When Moses called for them, they refused, saying, "We won’t come up!" ([[@4016012|Num 16:12]]). As soon as Moses finished speaking, the ground split open and swallowed them and their households, and they went down alive into Sheol ([[@4016031-4016033|Num 16:31-33]]). The Psalms also remember this: "The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abiram" ([[@19106017|Ps 106:17]]).

column5: Firstborn son of Hiel of Bethel
column7: He was the firstborn son whom Hiel of Bethel lost when he laid the foundation of Jericho as he rebuilt it ([[@11016034|1 Kgs 16:34]]). It happened just as Joshua had sworn ([[@6006026|Josh 6:26]]).

column5: The Shunammite woman who served old King David
column7: She was the beautiful Shunammite woman brought in to care for King David when he was old ([[@11001003-11001004|1 Kgs 1:3-4]]). Later Adonijah asked to have her as his wife, which stirred Solomon's anger ([[@11002017-11002022|1 Kgs 2:17-22]]).

column5: David's nephew and a brave commander
column7: He was the son of Zeruiah and the brother of Joab and Asahel ([[@10002018|2 Sam 2:18]]). When he went into Saul's camp with David at night, he wanted to strike Saul with the spear, but David stopped him, telling him not to strike "the LORD’s anointed" ([[@9026007-9026009|1 Sam 26:7-9]]). In the battle against Absalom he led a third of the army ([[@10018002|2 Sam 18:2]]). He saved David by striking down Ishbibenob, the Philistine who meant to kill David ([[@10021016-10021017|2 Sam 21:16-17]]).

column5: Son of Phinehas
column7: He was a descendant of Aaron, the son of Phinehas and the father of Bukki ([[@13006004-13006005|1 Chr 6:4-5]]). His name also appears in Ezra's genealogy ([[@15007005|Ezra 7:5]]).

column5: Benjamite, son of Bela
column7: He was one of the sons of Bela, Benjamin’s firstborn ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]; [[@13008003-13008004|1 Chr 8:3-4]]). He is a different person from the priest Abishua of the same name.

column5: Son of Shammai, descendant of Judah
column7: From the family of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah, he was the grandson of Onam and the son of Shammai ([[@13002028|1 Chr 2:28]]). His wife Abihail bore him Ahban and Molid ([[@13002029|1 Chr 2:29]]).

column5: Wife of David, mother of Shephatiah
column7: She was a wife of David and the mother of Shephatiah, David's fifth son. Her name appears in the lists of David's sons ([[@10003004|2 Sam 3:4]]; [[@13003003|1 Chr 3:3]]).

column5: Benjamite, son of Shaharaim
column7: He was a son of Shaharaim, a Benjamite. Shaharaim fathered Abitub and Elpaal by his wife Hushim ([[@13008008|1 Chr 8:8]]; [[@13008011|1 Chr 8:11]]).

column5: Saul's cousin and army commander
column7: Abner was the son of Ner, Saul's uncle, and the commander of Saul's army ([[@9014050|1 Sam 14:50]]). When David came back after killing Goliath, Abner brought him before Saul ([[@9017057|1 Sam 17:57]]). After Saul died, he made Saul's son Ishbosheth king over Israel and opposed David ([[@10002008-10002009|2 Sam 2:8-9]]). Later he came to make peace with David, but he was killed at the gate of Hebron by Joab, who wanted to avenge his brother Asahel ([[@10003027|2 Sam 3:27]]).

column5: Father of faith, Israel's first patriarch
column7: He was the son of Terah, and at first his name was Abram ([[@1011026|Gen 11:26]]). God called him, and he left his country, his relatives, and his father's house and went to Canaan ([[@1012001|Gen 12:1]]). He became an example of faith, as the words "He believed in the LORD, who credited it to him for righteousness" show ([[@1015006|Gen 15:6]]). God changed his name to Abraham, saying he would make him the father of a multitude of nations ([[@1017005|Gen 17:5]]).

column5: A campsite in the wilderness
column7: It was where Israel camped after leaving Jotbathah on their journey through the wilderness ([[@4033034|Num 33:34]]). From there they set out and camped at Ezion Geber ([[@4033035|Num 33:35]]).

column5: The son who rebelled against his father David
column7: He was David's third son, born to Maacah, the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur ([[@10003003|2 Sam 3:3]]). Because of what happened to his sister Tamar, he killed his older brother Amnon and fled to Geshur ([[@10013028|2 Sam 13:28]], 38). After he came back, he stole the hearts of the people of Israel and rebelled, claiming to be king in Hebron ([[@10015010|2 Sam 15:10]]). During the battle his hair caught in an oak and he was left hanging, and he died after Joab thrust darts into him; David wept bitterly, crying, "My son Absalom!" ([[@10018009-10018014|2 Sam 18:9-14]], 33).

column5: City in Nimrod’s kingdom
column7: It was one of the cities in the land of Shinar where the kingdom of Nimrod, son of Cush, began. It is named along with Babel, Erech, and Calneh ([[@1010008-1010010|Gen 10:8-10]]).

column5: Coastal town Asher did not take
column7: It was one of the towns whose inhabitants the tribe of Asher did not drive out ([[@7001031|Judg 1:31]]). Many scholars see it as the same place as Ptolemais ([[@44021007|Acts 21:7]]) in the New Testament.

column5: Southern region of Greece that included Corinth
column7: It was the southern region of Greece; in New Testament times it was a Roman province, and Corinth was in it ([[@47001001|2 Cor 1:1]]). While Paul was staying in Corinth, Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, and the Jews brought Paul before his judgment seat ([[@44018012|Acts 18:12]]). The people of Achaia, together with those of Macedonia, gladly gave a contribution for the poor among the saints in Jerusalem ([[@45015026|Rom 15:26]]). Paul called the household of Stephanas "the first fruits of Achaia" ([[@46016015|1 Cor 16:15]]).

column5: Corinthian believer who visited Paul
column7: He was a Corinthian believer who came to Paul with Stephanas and Fortunatus. Paul rejoiced, saying that they had supplied what was lacking on the Corinthians' part ([[@46016017|1 Cor 16:17]]).

column5: Man of Judah who stole devoted things
column7: He was a great-grandson of Zerah of the tribe of Judah and the son of Carmi, and when Jericho was attacked he secretly took some of the things devoted to the LORD ([[@6007001|Josh 7:1]]). After that, Israel went up to attack Ai, lost about thirty-six men, and was driven back ([[@6007005|Josh 7:5]]). When lots were cast, Achan was picked out, and he confessed that he had coveted a beautiful Babylonian robe, two hundred shekels of silver, and a wedge of gold and had hidden them in the ground in the middle of his tent ([[@6007018-6007021|Josh 7:18-21]]). Israel took Achan and everything that belonged to him to the Valley of Achor, stoned him, and burned them with fire ([[@6007024-6007025|Josh 7:24-25]]).

column5: Father of Baal Hanan, king of Edom
column7: He was the father of Baal Hanan, king of Edom. Baal Hanan became king of Edom in place of Shaul after Shaul died ([[@1036038|Gen 36:38]]; [[@13001049|1 Chr 1:49]]).

column5: An official of King Josiah
column7: He was the son of Micaiah, one of the men King Josiah sent to inquire of the LORD about the book of the law that had been found ([[@12022012-12022014|2 Kgs 22:12-14]]).

column5: King of Gath with whom David took refuge
column7: He was the king of the Philistine city of Gath. When David first fled from Saul to him, Achish's servants recognized David, and David got out of danger by pretending to be insane ([[@9021010-9021013|1 Sam 21:10-13]]). Later, when David came again with six hundred men, Achish took him in and gave him Ziklag ([[@9027002-9027006|1 Sam 27:2-6]]). Achish trusted David and wanted to take him into battle, but the Philistine lords objected, so he sent David back ([[@9029009|1 Sam 29:9]]). Scholars differ on whether 'Achish the son of Maacah' in Solomon's time is the same person ([[@11002039|1 Kgs 2:39]]).

column5: The valley where Achan was stoned
column7: It was the valley to which Joshua brought Achan and everything that belonged to him, and a heap of stones was raised over him there ([[@6007024-6007026|Josh 7:24-26]]). Hosea promised that God would give "the valley of Achor for a door of hope" ([[@28002015|Hos 2:15]]).

column5: Caleb's daughter, Othniel's wife
column7: She was Caleb's daughter and became the wife of Othniel, who captured Kiriath Sepher ([[@6015016-6015017|Josh 15:16-17]]). She asked her father for springs of water and received the upper springs and the lower springs ([[@6015019|Josh 15:19]]).

column5: Daughter of Caleb
column7: The genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles says "the daughter of Caleb was Achsah" ([[@13002049|1 Chr 2:49]]). Some take her to be the same as Caleb’s daughter Achsah, who became Othniel’s wife ([[@6015016-6015017|Josh 15:16-17]]).

column5: A Canaanite town Joshua defeated
column7: It was the town of a king who came out with Jabin king of Hazor to fight against Israel ([[@6011001|Josh 11:1]]). The king of Achshaph is among the kings Joshua defeated, and the town later fell within the border of the tribe of Asher ([[@6012020|Josh 12:20]]; [[@6019025|Josh 19:25]]).

column5: A town in the lowland of Judah
column7: It was a town in the lowland of the tribe of Judah, listed with Keilah and Mareshah ([[@6015044|Josh 15:44]]). Micah said, "The houses of Achzib will be a deceitful thing to the kings of Israel" ([[@33001014|Mic 1:14]]).

column5: Coastal town in the land of Asher
column7: It lay by the sea where the border of the tribe of Asher ended ([[@6019029|Josh 19:29]]). The tribe of Asher did not drive out its inhabitants ([[@7001031|Judg 1:31]]).

column5: Town on Judah’s southern border
column7: It was one of the towns given to the tribe of Judah, near the border of Edom in the south ([[@6015021-6015022|Josh 15:21-22]]).

column5: Lamech's wife, mother of Jabal and Jubal
column7: She was one of Lamech's two wives ([[@1004019|Gen 4:19]]). She bore Jabal, the father of those who keep livestock, and Jubal, the father of all who play the harp and pipe ([[@1004020-1004021|Gen 4:20-21]]).

column5: Esau's wife, mother of Eliphaz
column7: She was a Canaanite woman whom Esau married, the daughter of Elon the Hittite ([[@1036002|Gen 36:2]]). Adah bore Eliphaz to Esau ([[@1036004|Gen 36:4]]). Many chiefs of Edom, such as Teman and Amalek, came from Eliphaz, and the Bible calls them "the descendants of Adah" ([[@1036012|Gen 36:12]], 16). Genesis 26 says that Esau married Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite ([[@1026034|Gen 26:34]]), so scholars differ on whether she is the same person as Adah.

column5: Grandfather of King Josiah
column7: He was from Bozkath and was the father of Jedidah, the mother of Josiah king of Judah ([[@12022001|2 Kgs 22:1]]). Josiah did what was right in the LORD’s eyes ([[@12022002|2 Kgs 22:2]]).

column5: Benjamite, son of Shimei
column7: He was a son of Shimei in the genealogy of Benjamin. His brothers were Beraiah and Shimrath ([[@13008021|1 Chr 8:21]]).

column5: Priest in Jerusalem after the exile
column7: He was a priest who returned from exile and lived in Jerusalem, the son of Jeroham and the grandson of Pashhur ([[@13009012|1 Chr 9:12]]; [[@16011012|Neh 11:12]]).

column5: Father of Maaseiah, a captain
column7: He was the father of Maaseiah, one of the captains of hundreds with whom the priest Jehoiada made a covenant to make Joash king ([[@14023001|2 Chr 23:1]]).

column5: Son of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: He was one of the sons of Bani who had married foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010029|Ezra 10:29]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Man who had married a foreign wife
column7: This name appears in the list of those who had married foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010039|Ezra 10:39]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Ancestor of Maaseiah in Jerusalem
column7: He was an ancestor of Maaseiah, a man of Judah who lived in Jerusalem in Nehemiah’s time. Maaseiah’s family line goes back to the Shilonite ([[@16011005|Neh 11:5]]).

column5: Son of Haman
column7: He was one of the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. The Jews killed Haman’s ten sons in the citadel of Susa ([[@17009006-17009010|Esth 9:6-10]]).

column5: First man God created
column7: He was the first man, whom God formed from the dust and into whose nostrils he breathed the breath of life ([[@1002007|Gen 2:7]]). God placed him in the garden of Eden, and Adam gave names to all the animals ([[@1002020|Gen 2:20]]). But he ate the fruit of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, which God had told him not to eat, and so through one man sin and death entered the world ([[@45005012|Rom 5:12]]). The New Testament calls Jesus the "last Adam" ([[@46015045|1 Cor 15:45]]).

column5: Town where the Jordan’s waters heaped up
column7: When Israel crossed the Jordan, the water flowing down stopped and rose up in a heap far off at Adam, the city beside Zarethan ([[@6003016|Josh 3:16]]).

column5: Fortified city of Naphtali
column7: It was one of the fortified cities the tribe of Naphtali received by lot ([[@6019032|Josh 19:32]]; [[@6019035-6019036|Josh 19:35-36]]).

column5: Place on Naphtali’s border
column7: It was a place on the border of the land of the tribe of Naphtali, named between the oak in Zaanannim and Jabneel ([[@6019032-6019033|Josh 19:32-33]]).

column5: Third son of Ishmael
column7: He was a son of Ishmael, and his name comes after Nebaioth and Kedar ([[@1025013|Gen 25:13]]; [[@13001029|1 Chr 1:29]]).

column5: Place some returning exiles came from
column7: Among those who returned from exile, the people who came up from Addan and other places could not prove that their families belonged to Israel ([[@15002059|Ezra 2:59]]). In Nehemiah it is written 'Addon' ([[@16007061|Neh 7:61]]).

column5: Place on Judah’s southern border
column7: It was a place along the southern border of the land of the tribe of Judah. The border passed Hezron, went up to Addar, and turned toward Karka ([[@6015001-6015003|Josh 15:1-3]]).

column5: Benjamite, son of Bela
column7: He was one of the sons of Bela, Benjamin’s firstborn ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]; [[@13008003|1 Chr 8:3]]). His brothers included Gera and Abihud.

column5: Man in Jesus’ genealogy
column7: He appears in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus. He is listed as the father of Melchi and the son of Cosam ([[@42003028|Luke 3:28]]).

column5: Chief of the Simeonites
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the tribe of Simeon ([[@13004036|1 Chr 4:36]]; [[@13004038|1 Chr 4:38]]). In Hezekiah’s time these men struck the Meunim near Gedor and took the pasture land ([[@13004039-13004041|1 Chr 4:39-41]]).

column5: Father of the priest Maasai
column7: He was the father of Maasai, a priest who returned from exile and lived in Jerusalem. Maasai was the son of Adiel and the grandson of Jahzerah ([[@13009012|1 Chr 9:12]]).

column5: Father of Azmaveth, keeper of the royal treasures
column7: He was the father of Azmaveth, who was over the king’s treasures in David’s time ([[@13027025|1 Chr 27:25]]). These men were in charge of King David’s property ([[@13027031|1 Chr 27:31]]).

column5: A family that returned from exile
column7: It was the name of a family that returned from exile, and the descendants of Adin numbered four hundred fifty-four ([[@15002015|Ezra 2:15]]). Some of them also came up with Ezra ([[@15008006|Ezra 8:6]]).

column5: Leader who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s time. His name appears along with Adonijah and Bigvai ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010016|Neh 10:16]]).

column5: Reubenite among David’s mighty men
column7: He was one of David’s mighty men, the son of Shiza the Reubenite. He was a chief of the Reubenites with thirty men under him ([[@13011042|1 Chr 11:42]]).

column5: Chief of David’s mighty men
column7: He was chief of the captains among David’s mighty men and was also called Josheb Basshebeth. He killed eight hundred men at one time ([[@10023008|2 Sam 23:8]]).

column5: Town in Judah’s lowland
column7: It was one of the towns in the lowland given to the tribe of Judah. It is named along with Shaaraim and Gederah ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]; [[@6015036|Josh 15:36]]).

column5: Father of Shaphat, keeper of the herds
column7: He was the father of Shaphat, who was over the herds in the valleys in David’s time ([[@13027029|1 Chr 27:29]]). These men were in charge of King David’s property ([[@13027031|1 Chr 27:31]]).

column5: A city destroyed along with Sodom
column7: It was a city near Sodom, Gomorrah, and Zeboiim, and its king Shinab fought alongside the other kings ([[@1014002|Gen 14:2]]). It was one of the cities the LORD overthrew in his anger, together with Sodom and Gomorrah ([[@5029023|Deut 29:23]]).

column5: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media
column7: He was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who were close to King Ahasuerus and sat first in the kingdom ([[@17001014|Esth 1:14]]).

column5: Man who had married a foreign wife
column7: He was one of the sons of Pahathmoab who had married foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010030|Ezra 10:30]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Priest of Harim’s family in Joiakim’s time
column7: He was one of the heads of the priestly families in the days of the high priest Joiakim, heading the family of Harim ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012015|Neh 12:15]]).

column5: Manassite captain who joined David at Ziklag
column7: He was one of the captains of thousands from the tribe of Manasseh who joined David as he went to Ziklag ([[@13012020|1 Chr 12:20]]).

column5: Army commander under Jehoshaphat
column7: In King Jehoshaphat’s time he was the chief of Judah’s captains of thousands, leading three hundred thousand mighty men of valor ([[@14017014|2 Chr 17:14]]).

column5: A Canaanite king captured by Judah
column7: He was the king whom the men of Judah defeated and captured at Bezek, and they cut off his thumbs and his big toes ([[@7001005-7001006|Judg 1:5-6]]). He said that God had repaid him for what he had done to seventy kings ([[@7001007|Judg 1:7]]).

column5: King of Jerusalem who fought Joshua
column7: He was the king of Jerusalem who heard that Gibeon had made peace with Israel ([[@6010001|Josh 10:1]]). He called on the kings of Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon to join him in attacking Gibeon ([[@6010003-6010004|Josh 10:3-4]]).

column5: David's fourth son, who reached for the throne
column7: He was David's fourth son, the son of Haggith ([[@10003004|2 Sam 3:4]]). When David grew old, he declared "I will be king" and prepared chariots and horsemen, and Joab and Abiathar the priest helped him ([[@11001005-11001007|1 Kgs 1:5-7]]). But Nathan and Bathsheba told David, and Solomon became king. Adonijah was afraid and took hold of the horns of the altar and was pardoned ([[@11001050-11001053|1 Kgs 1:50-53]]), but later he asked for Abishag as his wife and was put to death by Benaiah ([[@11002013-11002025|1 Kgs 2:13-25]]).

column5: Levite sent out by Jehoshaphat
column7: He was one of the Levites King Jehoshaphat sent to teach in the cities of Judah ([[@14017007-14017008|2 Chr 17:7-8]]).

column5: Leader who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s time. His name appears along with Bigvai and Adin ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010016|Neh 10:16]]).

column5: A family that returned from exile
column7: It was the name of a family that returned from exile, and the descendants of Adonikam numbered six hundred sixty-six ([[@15002013|Ezra 2:13]]). In Nehemiah the number is given as six hundred sixty-seven ([[@16007018|Neh 7:18]]).

column5: Fortified city built by Rehoboam
column7: It was one of the cities for defense that Rehoboam built to protect the land of Judah ([[@14011005|2 Chr 11:5]]; [[@14011009|2 Chr 11:9]]).

column5: Overseer of forced labor under David and Solomon
column7: He was the officer in charge of forced labor in the days of David and Solomon ([[@10020024|2 Sam 20:24]]; [[@11004006|1 Kgs 4:6]]). When Rehoboam sent him out, all Israel stoned him to death ([[@11012018|1 Kgs 12:18]]).

column5: God of the Sepharvites
column7: He was a god worshiped by the people of Sepharvaim who were brought to Samaria, and they burned their children in the fire as offerings to him ([[@12017031|2 Kgs 17:31]]).

column5: Son who killed Sennacherib
column7: A son of Sennacherib king of Assyria, he and Sharezer struck down their father with the sword while he was worshiping in the house of Nisroch, and they escaped into the land of Ararat ([[@12019037|2 Kgs 19:37]]; [[@23037038|Isa 37:38]]).

column5: Home port of Paul’s ship
column7: On his way to Rome, Paul boarded a ship of Adramyttium that was about to sail to places on the coast of Asia ([[@44027001-44027002|Acts 27:1-2]]).

column5: Sea where Paul’s ship drifted
column7: On the way to Rome, Paul’s ship was caught in a storm, and on the fourteenth night it was driven back and forth in the Adriatic Sea ([[@44027027|Acts 27:27]]).

column5: Husband of Saul's daughter Merab
column7: A Meholathite, he married Merab, Saul's daughter, who was to have been given to David ([[@9018019|1 Sam 18:19]]). He was the son of Barzillai ([[@10021008|2 Sam 21:8]]).

column5: Town in Judah's lowland, David's cave hideout
column7: It was one of the towns in the lowland given to the tribe of Judah ([[@6015033-6015035|Josh 15:33-35]]). Judah's friend Hirah was 'the Adullamite' ([[@1038012|Gen 38:12]]). David fled from Saul to the cave of Adullam, and about four hundred men who were in distress, in debt, or bitter in soul gathered to him, and he became their captain ([[@9022001-9022002|1 Sam 22:1-2]]). Later, when Rehoboam built fortified cities in the land of Judah, Adullam was one of them ([[@14011005-14011007|2 Chr 11:5-7]]).

column5: Slope on the border of Judah and Benjamin
column7: It is 'the ascent of Adummim', where the border between Judah and Benjamin passed ([[@6018017|Josh 18:17]]). Joshua 15 also mentions it ([[@6015007|Josh 15:7]]).

column5: Paralyzed man in Lydda healed by Peter
column7: He was a man in Lydda who had been bedridden for eight years because he was paralyzed ([[@44009033|Acts 9:33]]). When Peter said, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you", he got up at once ([[@44009034|Acts 9:34]]).

column5: Place where John baptized
column7: It was a place near Salim, and because there was much water there, John baptized there. People came and were baptized ([[@43003023|John 3:23]]).

column5: Prophet who foretold famine and Paul's arrest
column7: By the Spirit he foretold that a great famine would come over all the world, and it happened in the days of Claudius ([[@44011028|Acts 11:28]]). Later he bound his own feet and hands with Paul's belt and foretold that Paul would be bound in Jerusalem ([[@44021010-44021011|Acts 21:10-11]]).

column5: A king named in Balaam's prophecy
column7: He is the king Israel's king is compared to when Balaam prophesied about Israel and said, "His king shall be higher than Agag" ([[@4024007|Num 24:7]]).

column5: The Amalekite king whom Saul spared
column7: He was the king of the Amalekites in Saul's time. God commanded that Amalek be utterly destroyed, but Saul took Agag alive and spared him along with the best of the sheep and cattle ([[@9015003-9015009|1 Sam 15:3-9]]). Saul told Samuel that he had obeyed the LORD's voice and "have brought Agag the king of Amalek," but Samuel rebuked him for his disobedience ([[@9015020-9015023|1 Sam 15:20-23]]). Samuel said, "As your sword has made women childless, so your mother will be childless among women", and he cut Agag in pieces before the LORD in Gilgal ([[@9015033|1 Sam 15:33]]). Haman in the book of Esther is called "the Agagite" ([[@17003001|Esth 3:1]]).

column5: Father of Shammah, one of David's mighty men
column7: A Hararite, he was the father of Shammah, one of David's mighty men. Shammah stood and fought the Philistines when the people fled before them ([[@10023011-10023012|2 Sam 23:11-12]]).

column5: King Agrippa, who heard Paul's defense
column7: He is the 'King Agrippa' of Acts, usually taken to be Herod Agrippa II. He came to Caesarea with Bernice to greet Governor Festus and heard about Paul's case ([[@44025013|Acts 25:13]], 23). When Paul made his defense by telling of his conversion, Agrippa said, "With a little persuasion are you trying to make me a Christian?" ([[@44026028|Acts 26:28]]). He said Paul could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar ([[@44026032|Acts 26:32]]).

column5: Son of Jakeh, author of Proverbs 30
column7: The son of Jakeh, he is the man whose words make up Proverbs 30. His proverbs are introduced as spoken to Ithiel and Ucal ([[@20030001|Prov 30:1]]).

column5: Jezebel's husband, an evil king of northern Israel
column7: He was the son of Omri and reigned over Israel in Samaria for twenty-two years. He married Jezebel, daughter of the king of the Sidonians, and served Baal, doing more evil in the LORD's sight than anyone before him ([[@11016029-11016031|1 Kgs 16:29-31]]). He often clashed with the prophet Elijah, and he heard a word of judgment for killing Naboth and taking his vineyard ([[@11021019|1 Kgs 21:19]]). He was struck by an arrow and died while fighting the Syrians ([[@11022034-11022037|1 Kgs 22:34-37]]).

column5: Man who prophesied lies in Babylon
column7: The son of Kolaiah, he prophesied lies in the LORD's name ([[@24029021|Jer 29:21]]). Jeremiah said that he would die at the hand of Nebuchadnezzar and become a byword for a curse ([[@24029022|Jer 29:22]]).

column5: Son of Harum in Judah's genealogy
column7: He was the son of Harum in the genealogy of Judah's descendants. Among the families descended from Hakkoz were 'the families of Aharhel the son of Harum' ([[@13004008|1 Chr 4:8]]).

column5: Father of Eliphelet, one of David's mighty men
column7: He was the father of Eliphelet, one of David's mighty men. The list of mighty men names "Eliphelet the son of Ahasbai, the son of the Maacathite" ([[@10023008|2 Sam 23:8]]; [[@10023034|2 Sam 23:34]]).

column5: The Persian king who made Esther queen
column7: He was the king of Persia who ruled one hundred twenty-seven provinces from India to Ethiopia ([[@17001001|Esth 1:1]]). He held a great feast in the palace at Susa, and when Queen Vashti would not obey his command, he removed her and made Esther the new queen ([[@17002017|Esth 2:17]]). Taken in by Haman's scheme, he issued a decree to destroy the Jews, but after hearing Esther's plea he allowed the Jews to defend their own lives ([[@17008011|Esth 8:11]]). Scholars differ on which king of history he was, and the Ahasuerus in the book of Daniel is a different person ([[@27009001|Dan 9:1]]).

column5: The river where Ezra gathered the returning people
column7: It was the river where Ezra gathered the people who were to return from Babylon ([[@15008015|Ezra 8:15]]). There he proclaimed a fast and prayed for a safe journey, and then they set out for Jerusalem ([[@15008021|Ezra 8:21]]; [[@15008031|Ezra 8:31]]).

column5: An evil king of Judah who relied on Assyria
column7: Ahaz was the son of Jotham; he became king of Judah at twenty and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem. Unlike his forefather David, he did not do what was right in the LORD's eyes ([[@12016002|2 Kgs 16:2]]). He followed the detestable practices of the nations, even making his son pass through the fire ([[@12016003|2 Kgs 16:3]]). When Syria and Israel attacked, Isaiah told him not to be afraid ([[@23007004|Isa 7:4]]), but he sent the silver and gold of the temple and the palace to Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria and asked for his help ([[@12016007-12016008|2 Kgs 16:7-8]]).

column5: A descendant of Jonathan, son of Micah
column7: He was a descendant of Saul's son Jonathan, the son of Micah ([[@13008035|1 Chr 8:35]]). He became the father of Jehoaddah ([[@13008036|1 Chr 8:36]]).

column5: Son of Ahab, king of Israel
column7: He was the son of Ahab, and he became king of Israel in Samaria and reigned two years ([[@11022051|1 Kgs 22:51]]). He walked in the way of his father and his mother, served Baal, and provoked the LORD to anger ([[@11022052-11022053|1 Kgs 22:52-53]]). When he fell through the lattice of his upper room and became sick, he sent messengers to ask Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron, whether he would recover ([[@12001002|2 Kgs 1:2]]). Elijah told him that he would not come down from his bed but would surely die, and Ahaziah died just as the word had said ([[@12001016-12001017|2 Kgs 1:16-17]]). He is a different person from Ahaziah, the king of Judah who appears later.

column5: Son of Athaliah and king of Judah
column7: He was the son of Jehoram king of Judah and Athaliah; he became king at twenty-two and reigned one year in Jerusalem ([[@12008026|2 Kgs 8:26]]). His mother was from the house of Ahab, and he too "walked in the way of Ahab’s house" and did evil in the LORD's sight ([[@12008027|2 Kgs 8:27]]). He went to Jezreel to visit his sick uncle Joram king of Israel and was attacked along with him when Jehu rebelled. As he fled he was struck at the ascent of Gur and died at Megiddo, and his servants buried him in David's city in Jerusalem ([[@12009027-12009028|2 Kgs 9:27-28]]).

column5: Son of Abishur in Judah's genealogy
column7: He was the son born to Abishur, a descendant of Jerahmeel, by his wife Abihail, and his brother was Molid ([[@13002029|1 Chr 2:29]]).

column5: Father of Hushim
column7: He is mentioned briefly in a genealogy as the father of Hushim. The text says only, "Hushim, and the sons of Aher" ([[@13007012|1 Chr 7:12]]).

column5: Chief of the Gadites, son of Abdiel
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Gad's descendants as the grandson of Guni and the son of Abdiel. He became a chief of his fathers' houses ([[@13005015|1 Chr 5:15]]).

column5: Son of Shemer, of Asher
column7: He was the son of Shemer in the genealogy of Asher's descendants. His brothers were Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram ([[@13007032-13007034|1 Chr 7:32-34]]).

column5: A chief who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant to keep God's law in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010026|Neh 10:26]]).

column5: One of David's mighty men, son of Sharar
column7: One of David's mighty men, he was the son of Sharar the Ararite ([[@10023033|2 Sam 23:33]]). In 1 Chronicles he appears as 'the son of Sacar the Hararite' ([[@13011035|1 Chr 11:35]]).

column5: Son of Shemida, of Manasseh
column7: He was the son of Shemida in the genealogy of Manasseh's descendants. His brothers were Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam ([[@13007019|1 Chr 7:19]]).

column5: Leader of the tribe of Dan in the wilderness
column7: He was the son of Ammishaddai and the leader of the children of Dan in the wilderness ([[@4001012|Num 1:12]]; [[@4002025|Num 2:25]]). On the march he led the army of Dan, the rear guard of all the camps ([[@4010025|Num 10:25]]).

column5: Chief of the Benjamite warriors at Ziklag
column7: He was the chief of the warriors from the tribe of Benjamin who came to David while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001-13012003|1 Chr 12:1-3]]). They could use both the right hand and the left with bows and slings ([[@13012002|1 Chr 12:2]]).

column5: Asherite prince chosen to divide the land
column7: The son of Shelomi, he was the prince of the tribe of Asher chosen to divide the land of Canaan for inheritance ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034027|Num 34:27]]).

column5: A man in Benjamin's genealogy
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin's descendants. In the account of Ehud's sons it is written, "he became the father of Uzza and Ahihud" ([[@13008006-13008007|1 Chr 8:6-7]]).

column5: A scribe of King Solomon
column7: An official of King Solomon, he served as scribe along with Elihoreph, both sons of Shisha. In the same list, Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud is named as recorder ([[@11004002-11004003|1 Kgs 4:2-3]]).

column5: Prophet from Shiloh who spoke to Jeroboam
column7: He was a prophet from Shiloh. When Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, Ahijah met him on the way, tore the new garment he was wearing into twelve pieces, and told him that the LORD would give him ten tribes from Solomon's kingdom ([[@11011029-11011031|1 Kgs 11:29-31]]). When the kingdom split because Rehoboam would not listen to the people, it was this word being fulfilled ([[@11012015|1 Kgs 12:15]]). Later, when his eyes had grown dim with age, Ahijah prophesied to Jeroboam's wife, who came to him in disguise, that her child would die and that Jeroboam's house would be cut off ([[@11014004-11014012|1 Kgs 14:4-12]]). When Baasha destroyed the whole house of Jeroboam, that too happened just as the LORD had spoken through Ahijah ([[@11015029|1 Kgs 15:29]]).

column5: Father of King Baasha
column7: He was of the house of Issachar, the father of Baasha, who killed Nadab and became king of Israel ([[@11015027|1 Kgs 15:27]]; [[@11015033|1 Kgs 15:33]]).

column5: Son of Jerahmeel
column7: A son of Jerahmeel, Hezron's firstborn, his brothers were Ram, Bunah, Oren, and Ozem ([[@13002025|1 Chr 2:25]]).

column5: A man in Benjamin's genealogy
column7: He appears in the account of the family of Ehud, a descendant of Benjamin, and was carried captive to Manahath with Naaman and Gera ([[@13008006-13008007|1 Chr 8:6-7]]).

column5: One of David's mighty men, a Pelonite
column7: He is a Pelonite named in the list of the mighty men of David's armies. His name comes right after Hepher the Mecherathite ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011036|1 Chr 11:36]]).

column5: Levite over the treasuries of God's house
column7: A Levite, he was over the treasures of God's house and the treasures of the dedicated things. He appears in the record of how the Levites divided up the temple duties in David's time ([[@13026020|1 Chr 26:20]]).

column5: Son of Shaphan who protected Jeremiah
column7: He was the son of Shaphan, King Josiah's scribe. When the book of the law was found in the temple, he was one of the men the king sent to the prophetess Huldah to ask what the LORD wanted ([[@12022012-12022014|2 Kgs 22:12-14]]). In King Jehoiakim's time, when people wanted to kill Jeremiah, "the hand of Ahikam the son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah" so that he was not put to death ([[@24026024|Jer 26:24]]). His son Gedaliah became the man to whom the king of Babylon entrusted the remaining people after Jerusalem fell ([[@12025022|2 Kgs 25:22]]).

column5: Father of Jehoshaphat and Baana
column7: He was the father of Jehoshaphat, the recorder in David's time ([[@10008016|2 Sam 8:16]]). Baana, who was in charge of the region of Beth Shean under Solomon, is also called 'the son of Ahilud' ([[@11004012|1 Kgs 4:12]]).

column5: Father of Saul's wife Ahinoam
column7: He was the father of Ahinoam, King Saul's wife. The same verse also introduces Abner, the captain of Saul's army ([[@9014050|1 Sam 14:50]]).

column5: Son of Zadok who carried news to David
column7: He was the son of Zadok the priest ([[@13006008|1 Chr 6:8]]). When Absalom rebelled, he and Jonathan the son of Abiathar secretly carried news from inside Jerusalem to David ([[@10015036|2 Sam 15:36]]). After Absalom's army was defeated, he ran by the way of the plain and reached David ahead of the Cushite ([[@10018023|2 Sam 18:23]]). But when the king asked whether Absalom was all right, he could not bring himself to tell him plainly that Absalom was dead ([[@10018029|2 Sam 18:29]]).

column5: Solomon's officer over Naphtali
column7: He was the one of Solomon's twelve officers who was in charge of Naphtali. He married Solomon's daughter Basemath ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004015|1 Kgs 4:15]]).

column5: A descendant of Anak who lived in Hebron
column7: He was one of the descendants of Anak whom the spies saw in Hebron ([[@4013022|Num 13:22]]). Caleb drove him out, and he was killed when Judah attacked Hebron ([[@6015014|Josh 15:14]]; [[@7001010|Judg 1:10]]).

column5: A gatekeeper in Jerusalem after the exile
column7: He is named as a gatekeeper among those who returned from Babylon and lived in Jerusalem. He is listed with Shallum, Akkub, and Talmon ([[@13009017|1 Chr 9:17]]).

column5: Priest of Nob who helped David
column7: The son of Ahitub, he was the priest at Nob ([[@9022011|1 Sam 22:11]]). He gave David, who was fleeing from Saul, the showbread and even handed over Goliath's sword ([[@9021006-9021009|1 Sam 21:6-9]]). When Doeg the Edomite told Saul about this, Saul killed him and eighty-five priests of Nob ([[@9022018|1 Sam 22:18]]). Only his son Abiathar escaped and went to David ([[@9022020|1 Sam 22:20]]). Some see him as the same person as the priest Ahijah in 1 Samuel 14, but scholars differ.

column5: A Hittite who followed David
column7: He was a Hittite who followed David. When David asked who would go down with him into Saul's camp, he asked him along with Abishai ([[@9026006|1 Sam 26:6]]).

column5: A priest in David's time, son of Abiathar
column7: He was the son of Abiathar and served as priest with Zadok in David's time ([[@10008017|2 Sam 8:17]]). When David divided the priests into their divisions, he shared the work with Zadok ([[@13024003|1 Chr 24:3]]).

column5: Son of Elkanah, a Kohathite
column7: He was a son of Elkanah, a Levite descended from Kohath, and the brother of Amasai. His name appears in the genealogy of the Levites ([[@13006022|1 Chr 6:22]], 25).

column5: Solomon's officer over Mahanaim
column7: The son of Iddo, he was the one of Solomon's twelve officers who was in charge of Mahanaim ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004014|1 Kgs 4:14]]).

column5: Wife of King Saul
column7: She was the wife of King Saul and the daughter of Ahimaaz. The same verse names Abner the son of Ner as the captain of Saul's army ([[@9014050|1 Sam 14:50]]).

column5: Woman of Jezreel, David's wife, Amnon's mother
column7: She was a woman from Jezreel who became David's wife ([[@9025043|1 Sam 25:43]]). While David was living in Gath to escape Saul, she went with him along with Abigail ([[@9027003|1 Sam 27:3]]). She was taken captive when the Amalekites raided Ziklag, but David recovered everything and rescued his two wives ([[@9030005|1 Sam 30:5]], 18). Amnon, David's firstborn son born in Hebron, was Ahinoam's son ([[@10003002|2 Sam 3:2]]).

column5: Son of Abinadab who drove the cart carrying the ark
column7: He was a son of Abinadab who, with his brother Uzzah, drove the new cart carrying the ark of God ([[@10006003|2 Sam 6:3]]). He walked in front of the ark ([[@10006004|2 Sam 6:4]]).

column5: Son of Beriah, of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin's descendants as one of the sons of Beriah ([[@13008014-13008016|1 Chr 8:14-16]]).

column5: Son of Jeiel, the father of Gibeon
column7: He was one of the sons of Jeiel, the father of Gibeon who lived in Gibeon, and of his wife Maacah ([[@13008029|1 Chr 8:29]], 31; [[@13009035|1 Chr 9:35]], 37).

column5: Leader of the tribe of Naphtali in the wilderness
column7: He was the son of Enan and the leader of the children of Naphtali in the wilderness ([[@4001015|Num 1:15]]; [[@4002029|Num 2:29]]). On the twelfth day he brought the offering on behalf of the children of Naphtali ([[@4007078|Num 7:78]]).

column5: A son of Benjamin
column7: He was a son of Benjamin, and from him came the family of the Ahiramites ([[@4026038|Num 26:38]]). In the genealogy of Benjamin in 1 Chronicles, a third son named 'Aharah' appears ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]).

column5: Father of Oholiab
column7: He was a man of the tribe of Dan, the father of Oholiab, who helped make the tabernacle ([[@2031006|Exod 31:6]]; [[@2038023|Exod 38:23]]).

column5: Son of Bilhan, of Benjamin
column7: He was the grandson of Jediael and son of Bilhan, of Benjamin's descendants. They were heads of their fathers' households and mighty men of valor ([[@13007010-13007011|1 Chr 7:10-11]]).

column5: Solomon's officer over the household
column7: An official of King Solomon, he was over the household. In the same verse, Adoniram the son of Abda is named as over the forced labor ([[@11004006|1 Kgs 4:6]]).

column5: David's counselor who sided with Absalom
column7: He was a Gilonite and David's counselor, but when Absalom rebelled, he took Absalom's side ([[@10015012|2 Sam 15:12]]). His counsel was so highly regarded that it "was as if a man inquired at the inner sanctuary of God" ([[@10016023|2 Sam 16:23]]). David prayed that the LORD would turn his counsel into foolishness ([[@10015031|2 Sam 15:31]]). When the LORD made Absalom prefer the counsel of Hushai, Ahithophel went back to his hometown, put his house in order, and hanged himself ([[@10017014|2 Sam 17:14]], 23).

column5: Father of Ahimelech the priest of Nob
column7: He was the son of Phinehas and the brother of Ichabod ([[@9014003|1 Sam 14:3]]). Ahimelech, the priest of Nob, was his son ([[@9022009-9022011|1 Sam 22:9-11]]).

column5: Father of Zadok the priest
column7: He was the father of Zadok, the priest in David's time ([[@10008017|2 Sam 8:17]]). In the genealogy of Aaron's descendants he appears as the son of Amariah ([[@13006007-13006008|1 Chr 6:7-8]]).

column5: A man in the priestly line, father of Zadok
column7: He appears in the priestly genealogy of Aaron's descendants as the son of Amariah and the father of Zadok ([[@13006011-13006012|1 Chr 6:11-12]]). His name also appears in Ezra's genealogy ([[@15007002|Ezra 7:2]]).

column5: Town Asher did not take
column7: It was a Canaanite town in the territory of the tribe of Asher. The tribe of Asher did not drive out the inhabitants of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, and other towns ([[@7001031|Judg 1:31]]).

column5: A child of Sheshan, of Jerahmeel's line
column7: This person is recorded as a child of Sheshan, a descendant of Jerahmeel ([[@13002031|1 Chr 2:31]]). Sheshan is said to have had no sons, only daughters ([[@13002034|1 Chr 2:34]]).

column5: Father of Zabad, one of David's mighty men
column7: He was the father of Zabad, who is named in the list of David's mighty men. His name comes right after Uriah the Hittite ([[@13011010|1 Chr 11:10]]; [[@13011041|1 Chr 11:41]]).

column5: Grandson of Benjamin, ancestor of the Ahohites
column7: He was one of the sons of Bela, Benjamin's firstborn ([[@13008003-13008004|1 Chr 8:3-4]]). His descendants were called 'Ahohites,' and several men from this family appear among David's mighty men. Eleazar the son of Dodai the Ahohite was one of the three mighty men with David ([[@10023009|2 Sam 23:9]]). Zalmon the Ahohite was also on the list of David's mighty men ([[@10023028|2 Sam 23:28]]), and Dodai the Ahohite was the commander of the division for the second month in David's time ([[@13027004|1 Chr 27:4]]).

column5: Son of Jahath, of Judah
column7: The grandson of Reaiah and son of Jahath, of Judah's descendants, his brother was Lahad. They were the families of the Zorathites ([[@13004002|1 Chr 4:2]]).

column5: Son of Ashhur and Naarah
column7: He was the son born to Ashhur the father of Tekoa by his wife Naarah, and his brothers were Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari ([[@13004005-13004006|1 Chr 4:5-6]]).

column5: Friend of Abimelech king of Gerar
column7: He was a friend of Abimelech king of Gerar. Abimelech brought him, along with Phicol the captain of his army, when he came to Isaac ([[@1026026|Gen 26:26]]).

column5: Second Canaanite city Joshua attacked
column7: It was a Canaanite city east of Bethel. Abram pitched his tent between Bethel and Ai and built an altar to the LORD ([[@1012008|Gen 12:8]]). After Jericho fell, about three thousand Israelites went up to attack Ai but fled, because of the sin of Achan, who had taken some of the devoted things ([[@6007001-6007005|Josh 7:1-5]]). After the sin was dealt with, Joshua set an ambush behind the city, took Ai, and set it on fire ([[@6008019|Josh 8:19]]). People from Ai were also among those who returned from exile ([[@15002028|Ezra 2:28]]).

column5: A city of Ammon named by Jeremiah
column7: It is named along with Heshbon and Rabbah when Jeremiah prophesied about Ammon. The text says, "Ai is laid waste" ([[@24049002-24049003|Jer 49:2-3]]).

column5: Son of Zibeon, a Horite
column7: He was a son of Zibeon, a Horite who lived in the land of Edom. His brother Anah found the hot springs in the wilderness while feeding his father's donkeys ([[@1036024|Gen 36:24]]; [[@13001040|1 Chr 1:40]]).

column5: Father of Rizpah
column7: He was the father of Rizpah, Saul's concubine ([[@10003007|2 Sam 3:7]]). His daughter Rizpah guarded the bodies of her dead sons day and night ([[@10021010|2 Sam 21:10]]).

column5: A town and valley in the territory of Dan
column7: This is the place where Joshua, on the day he fought the Amorites, cried out, "Sun, stand still on Gibeon! You, moon, stop in the valley of Aijalon!" ([[@6010012|Josh 10:12]]). It was a town given to the tribe of Dan, but the Amorites forced the children of Dan into the hill country and went on living in Aijalon ([[@6019042|Josh 19:42]]; [[@7001034-7001035|Judg 1:34-35]]). In Rehoboam's time it was counted among the fortified cities in Judah and Benjamin ([[@14011010|2 Chr 11:10]]).

column5: A point on the eastern border of Canaan
column7: It is the place reached by the eastern border of Canaan that God described to Moses, as the border went down from Shepham to Riblah ([[@4034010-4034011|Num 34:10-11]]).

column5: A town in the south of Judah
column7: It was one of the towns at the far southern end of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015032|Josh 15:32]]). It became part of Simeon's share and was also given to the Levites ([[@6019007|Josh 19:7]]; [[@6021016|Josh 21:16]]).

column5: Son of Ezer, a Horite
column7: He was a son of Ezer, a Horite chief ([[@1036027|Gen 36:27]]). In 1 Chronicles his name is written 'Jaakan' ([[@13001042|1 Chr 1:42]]).

column5: The field bought with Judas' betrayal money
column7: It was the potter's field the chief priests bought with the silver Judas threw down, and it became a burial place for strangers ([[@40027005-40027008|Matt 27:5-8]]). In the local language it was called Akeldama, that is, 'field of blood' ([[@44001019|Acts 1:19]]).

column5: Son of Elioenai, of David's house
column7: He was the son of Elioenai in the genealogy of the descendants of Jeconiah the captive ([[@13003017|1 Chr 3:17]]; [[@13003024|1 Chr 3:24]]).

column5: A Levite gatekeeper after the exile
column7: He was a gatekeeper after the return from exile, named along with Shallum and Talmon ([[@13009017|1 Chr 9:17]]). His descendants also returned as gatekeepers ([[@15002042|Ezra 2:42]]).

column5: A temple servant family that returned from exile
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Akkub' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]]; [[@15002045|Ezra 2:45]]).

column5: A Levite who helped the people understand the law
column7: When Ezra read the book of the law before the people, he was one of those who helped the people understand the law as they stayed in their place ([[@16008002-16008003|Neh 8:2-3]]; [[@16008007|Neh 8:7]])

column5: An ascent on Judah's southern border
column7: It was the ascent that the southern border of the land of Judah passed through ([[@4034004|Num 34:4]]; [[@6015003|Josh 15:3]]). The border of the Amorites ran from the rock at this ascent ([[@7001036|Judg 1:36]]).

column5: Levitical town in Benjamin
column7: It was a town that the tribe of Benjamin gave to the descendants of Kohath ([[@13006060|1 Chr 6:60]]). In the same list in Joshua it appears as 'Almon' ([[@6021018|Josh 21:18]]).

column5: Son of Becher, of Benjamin
column7: He was one of the sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin. They were heads of their fathers' houses and mighty men of valor ([[@13007008-13007009|1 Chr 7:8-9]]).

column5: Descendant of Saul, son of Jehoaddah
column7: A descendant of Saul's son Jonathan, he was the son of Jehoaddah ([[@13008036|1 Chr 8:36]]). In 1 Chronicles 9 he appears as the son of Jarah ([[@13009042|1 Chr 9:42]]).

column5: Son of Simon, who carried Jesus' cross
column7: He was a son of Simon of Cyrene, the man who was forced to carry Jesus' cross. His brother was Rufus ([[@41015021|Mark 15:21]]).

column5: A member of the high priest's family
column7: He was one of those who gathered with Annas the high priest and Caiaphas when Peter and John were arrested and questioned ([[@44004006|Acts 4:6]]).

column5: Man Paul handed over to Satan
column7: Along with Hymenaeus, he had made shipwreck of the faith, and Paul delivered him to Satan so that he would be disciplined ([[@54001020|1 Tim 1:20]]). Scholars differ on whether he is the same person as Alexander the coppersmith in 2 Timothy ([[@55004014|2 Tim 4:14]]).

column5: A great port city of Egypt
column7: It was the birthplace of Apollos, who was mighty in the Scriptures ([[@44018024|Acts 18:24]]). Paul boarded a ship of Alexandria sailing for Italy ([[@44027006|Acts 27:6]]).

column5: A town received by the tribe of Asher
column7: It was one of the towns in the land the tribe of Asher received by lot according to their families, listed with Amad and Mishal ([[@6019024-6019026|Josh 19:24-26]]).

column5: The oak on Naphtali's border
column7: It is mentioned in the description of the border of the land Naphtali's descendants received. The border began at Heleph and this oak ([[@6019032-6019033|Josh 19:32-33]]).

column5: Father of Shiphi, of Simeon
column7: He was the grandfather of Ziza, a chief among Simeon's descendants. The text lists him as the son of Jedaiah and the father of Shiphi ([[@13004037-13004038|1 Chr 4:37-38]]).

column5: The oak where Deborah was buried
column7: It is the name given to the oak below Bethel under which Deborah, Rebekah's nurse, was buried ([[@1035008|Gen 35:8]]).

column5: Son of Joktan
column7: He is the first named among the sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem ([[@1010026|Gen 10:26]]; [[@13001020|1 Chr 1:20]]).

column5: Father of the apostle James
column7: He was the father of James, one of the twelve apostles. The lists of apostles call him 'James the son of Alphaeus,' which sets him apart from James the son of Zebedee ([[@40010003|Matt 10:3]]; [[@44001013|Acts 1:13]]). The Gospel of Mark also calls Levi, who was sitting at the tax office when Jesus called him, 'the son of Alphaeus' ([[@41002014|Mark 2:14]]). Scholars differ on whether the two Alphaeuses are the same man.

column5: Place for offering sacrifices and worshiping God
column7: An altar was a place where people offered sacrifices to God and worshiped him. After the flood Noah built an altar to the LORD and offered burnt offerings, and Abram also built an altar where the LORD had appeared to him ([[@1008020|Gen 8:20]]; [[@1012007|Gen 12:7]]). The tabernacle had an altar of burnt offering made of acacia wood overlaid with bronze, with horns on its four corners ([[@2027001-2027002|Exod 27:1-2]]). The altar for burning incense was made of acacia wood overlaid with pure gold and placed in front of the veil by the ark of the covenant ([[@2030001-2030003|Exod 30:1-3]], 6).

column5: A campsite in the wilderness
column7: It was where Israel camped after leaving Dophkah on their journey through the wilderness ([[@4033013|Num 33:13]]). From there they set out and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water ([[@4033014|Num 33:14]]).

column5: Edomite chief descended from Esau
column7: He was one of the chiefs of Edom who came from Esau ([[@1036040|Gen 36:40]]). In 1 Chronicles his name is written 'Aliah' ([[@13001051|1 Chr 1:51]]).

column5: Son of Shobal, a Horite
column7: He was a son of Shobal the Horite ([[@1036023|Gen 36:23]]). In 1 Chronicles his name is written 'Alian' ([[@13001040|1 Chr 1:40]]).

column5: A town received by the tribe of Asher
column7: It was one of the towns in the land the tribe of Asher received by lot according to their families, listed with Allammelech and Mishal ([[@6019024-6019026|Josh 19:24-26]]).

column5: Son of Helem, of Asher
column7: He was the son of Helem in the genealogy of Asher's descendants. His brothers were Zophah, Imna, and Shelesh ([[@13007035|1 Chr 7:35]]).

column5: A desert people who opposed Israel
column7: The Amalekites were a people descended from Amalek, Esau's grandson ([[@1036012|Gen 36:12]]). They attacked Israel at Rephidim after Israel came out of Egypt, and when Moses held up his hand Israel prevailed, but when he let it down Amalek prevailed ([[@2017011|Exod 17:11]]). God commanded that the memory of Amalek be blotted out from under the sky ([[@5025019|Deut 25:19]]). Because Saul did not fully obey the command to destroy Amalek, he was rejected as king ([[@9015023|1 Sam 15:23]]).

column5: Son of Eliphaz, grandson of Esau
column7: He was the son of Esau's son Eliphaz by his concubine Timna ([[@1036012|Gen 36:12]]). He became one of the chiefs in the land of Edom ([[@1036016|Gen 36:16]]).

column5: A town in the south of Judah
column7: It was one of the towns received by the tribe of Judah, in the South near the border of Edom ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015026|Josh 15:26]]).

column5: A mountain in the Song of Songs
column7: It is the name of a mountain the bridegroom mentions, along with Senir and Hermon, as he invites his bride to come with him ([[@22004008|Song 4:8]]).

column5: A priest in the line of Aaron
column7: In the genealogy of Aaron's descendants, he was the son of Meraioth and the father of Ahitub ([[@13006050|1 Chr 6:50]]; [[@13006052|1 Chr 6:52]]).

column5: Second son of Hebron, a Levite
column7: He was the second son of Hebron, a descendant of Kohath ([[@13023019|1 Chr 23:19]]). His name appears when the divisions of the Levites were arranged in David's time ([[@13024023|1 Chr 24:23]]).

column5: Chief priest in Jehoshaphat's time
column7: He was the chief priest in King Jehoshaphat's time, in charge of all matters of the LORD ([[@14019011|2 Chr 19:11]]).

column5: A man who distributed offerings under Hezekiah
column7: In Hezekiah's time he was one of those in the cities of the priests who were in charge of distributing the offerings to their relatives by their divisions ([[@14031014-14031015|2 Chr 31:14-15]]).

column5: An ancestor of Ezra the scribe
column7: He is an ancestor named in the genealogy of Ezra the scribe. The text traces Ezra's line back seven generations to Amariah ([[@15007001|Ezra 7:1]]; [[@15007003|Ezra 7:3]]).

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a descendant of Bani, named in the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra's time ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]; [[@15010042|Ezra 10:42]]).

column5: A priest who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the priests who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010003|Neh 10:3]]). The same name also appears in the list of priests who returned with Zerubbabel ([[@16012002|Neh 12:2]]).

column5: Ancestor of Athaiah in Jerusalem
column7: He was an ancestor of Athaiah, a man of Judah who returned from exile and lived in Jerusalem, and the text lists Athaiah as Amariah's great-grandson ([[@16011004|Neh 11:4]]).

column5: Ancestor of the prophet Zephaniah
column7: He was an ancestor of the prophet Zephaniah. Zephaniah was the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah and the great-grandson of Amariah ([[@36001001|Zeph 1:1]]).

column5: David's nephew, killed by Joab
column7: He was the son of David's sister Abigail, which made him David's nephew ([[@13002016-13002017|1 Chr 2:16-17]]). When Absalom rebelled, he made Amasa commander of the army in place of Joab ([[@10017025|2 Sam 17:25]]). After the revolt was over, David told Amasa that he would make him commander of the army instead of Joab ([[@10019013|2 Sam 19:13]]). But while they were pursuing Sheba, Joab stabbed him in the stomach with his sword by the great stone in Gibeon and killed him ([[@10020008-10020010|2 Sam 20:8-10]]).

column5: Ephraimite chief who opposed bringing in captives
column7: The son of Hadlai, he was one of the heads of the people of Ephraim. He stood against bringing in the captives taken from Judah ([[@14028012-14028013|2 Chr 28:12-13]]).

column5: Son of Elkanah, a Kohathite
column7: He was a son of Elkanah, a Levite descended from Kohath ([[@13006025|1 Chr 6:25]]). He was an ancestor of Heman the singer ([[@13006033|1 Chr 6:33]], 35).

column5: Chief of the thirty who came to David
column7: He was the chief of the thirty. When the Spirit came on him, he wished David peace, and David made them captains of the band ([[@13012018|1 Chr 12:18]]).

column5: A priest who blew the trumpet before God's ark
column7: He was one of the priests who blew the trumpets before the ark of God when it was moved ([[@13015024|1 Chr 15:24]]).

column5: Father of Mahath, who helped cleanse the temple
column7: He was the father of Mahath, a Kohathite Levite. Mahath was one of the Levites who arose to do the work of the temple in Hezekiah's time ([[@14029012|2 Chr 29:12]]).

column5: A commander who offered himself to the LORD
column7: The son of Zichri in Jehoshaphat's time, he commanded two hundred thousand mighty men of valor. The text describes him as one "who willingly offered himself to the LORD" ([[@14017016|2 Chr 17:16]]).

column5: The land by the River where Balaam lived
column7: It is the place where Balak king of Moab sent messengers to summon Balaam. The verse calls it 'the land of the children of his people,' at Pethor by the River ([[@4022005|Num 22:5]])

column5: Judah's king who grew proud after defeating Edom
column7: Amaziah was the son of Joash king of Judah; he became king at twenty-five and reigned twenty-nine years in Jerusalem ([[@12014001-12014002|2 Kgs 14:1-2]]). He killed ten thousand Edomites in the Valley of Salt and captured Sela ([[@12014007|2 Kgs 14:7]]). But he brought back the gods of Edom, set them up as his own gods, and worshiped them ([[@14025014|2 Chr 25:14]]). Afterward he picked a fight with Jehoash king of Israel and was taken captive, and the wall of Jerusalem was broken down ([[@12014013|2 Kgs 14:13]]).

column5: Father of Joshah, of Simeon
column7: He was the father of Joshah, who is named in the list of chiefs of Simeon's descendants. The families of these chiefs are said to have increased greatly ([[@13004034|1 Chr 4:34]]; [[@13004038|1 Chr 4:38]]).

column5: A Merarite Levite, son of Hilkiah
column7: An ancestor of Ethan of the descendants of Merari, he was the son of Hilkiah and the father of Hashabiah ([[@13006044-13006045|1 Chr 6:44-45]]).

column5: The priest of Bethel who tried to drive Amos out
column7: He was the priest of Bethel who reported to King Jeroboam that Amos was conspiring against the king ([[@30007010|Amos 7:10]]). He told Amos to flee to the land of Judah ([[@30007012|Amos 7:12]]).

column5: A word of response meaning 'truly, so it is'
column7: Amen is a Hebrew word meaning 'sure, true', and it is used to respond to a word or a prayer, saying 'truly, so it is'. When the curses of the law were proclaimed, all the people were to answer and say, "Amen" ([[@5027015|Deut 27:15]]). When Ezra blessed God, the people lifted up their hands and answered, "Amen, Amen", and worshiped ([[@16008006|Neh 8:6]]). Paul said that all God's promises are "Yes" in Christ, and so through him we say "Amen" to the glory of God ([[@47001020|2 Cor 1:20]]). Revelation calls Jesus "The Amen, the Faithful and True Witness" ([[@66003014|Rev 3:14]]).

column5: Descendant of Solomon's servants
column7: Among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Ami' ([[@15002055|Ezra 2:55]], 57). In Nehemiah they are written as 'the children of Amon' ([[@16007059|Neh 7:59]]).

column5: Father of the prophet Jonah
column7: From Gath Hepher, he was the father of the prophet Jonah, who announced the word that Jeroboam would restore the border of Israel ([[@12014025|2 Kgs 14:25]]). The book of Jonah begins with 'Jonah the son of Amittai' ([[@32001001|Jonah 1:1]]).

column5: The hill Joab reached chasing Abner
column7: It is the hill Joab and Abishai reached at sunset as they pursued Abner. It lay before Giah, by the way to the wilderness of Gibeon ([[@10002024|2 Sam 2:24]]).

column5: The spy from the tribe of Dan
column7: The son of Gemalli, he represented the tribe of Dan among the men Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013002|Num 13:2]]; [[@4013012|Num 13:12]]).

column5: Father of Machir of Lo Debar
column7: He was the father of Machir of Lo Debar, in whose house Mephibosheth stayed ([[@10009004|2 Sam 9:4]]). Machir helped David at Mahanaim ([[@10017027|2 Sam 17:27]]).

column5: Sixth son of Obed-Edom
column7: The sixth son of Obed-Edom, he belonged to a family of gatekeepers. The text says God blessed Obed-Edom ([[@13026004-13026005|1 Chr 26:4-5]]).

column5: Father of Elishama, chief of Ephraim
column7: He was a man of the tribe of Ephraim and the father of Elishama, the leader of Ephraim during the wilderness years ([[@4001010|Num 1:10]]). The Bible always calls Elishama "Elishama the son of Ammihud."
