Elishama was the leader of the camp of Ephraim on the west side when Israel camped ([[@4002018|Num 2:18]]), and he brought his offering on the seventh day of the dedication of the tabernacle ([[@4007048|Num 7:48]]). In the genealogy of Chronicles, Ammihud also appears as Elishama's father ([[@13007026|1 Chr 7:26]]).

column5: Father of Shemuel of Simeon
column7: He was the father of Shemuel of the tribe of Simeon. Shemuel was one of the princes chosen from each tribe to divide the land of Canaan for inheritance ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034020|Num 34:20]]).

column5: Father of Pedahel of Naphtali
column7: He was the father of Pedahel of the tribe of Naphtali. Pedahel was one of the princes chosen from each tribe to divide the land of Canaan for inheritance ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034028|Num 34:28]]).

column5: Father of Talmai king of Geshur
column7: He was the father of Talmai king of Geshur. Absalom fled to Talmai and stayed in Geshur for three years ([[@10013037-10013038|2 Sam 13:37-38]]).

column5: Father of Uthai in Jerusalem
column7: He was the father of Uthai, a descendant of Perez the son of Judah, who lived in Jerusalem after the exile. He is recorded as the son of Omri ([[@13009003-13009004|1 Chr 9:3-4]]).

column5: Father of Nahshon, father-in-law of Aaron
column7: He was a man of the tribe of Judah, the son of Ram, the father of Nahshon, and an ancestor of David ([[@8004019-8004022|Ruth 4:19-22]]). His daughter Elisheba became Aaron's wife and bore Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar ([[@2006023|Exod 6:23]]). The leader of the tribe of Judah in the wilderness was "Nahshon the son of Amminadab" ([[@4002003|Num 2:3]]). He also appears in Matthew's genealogy of Jesus ([[@40001004|Matt 1:4]]).

column5: Uzzielite chief who helped bring up the ark
column7: A chief of the sons of Uzziel, he led one hundred twelve of his brothers ([[@13015010|1 Chr 15:10]]). He was one of the Levites David called to bring up the ark of the covenant ([[@13015011-13015012|1 Chr 15:11-12]]).

column5: 'My royal people's chariots' in the Song of Songs
column7: In the Song of Songs it appears in the phrase "my royal people’s chariots." Some English Bibles translate the phrase as a personal name, Amminadib ([[@22006012|Song 6:12]]).

column5: Father of Ahiezer, leader of the tribe of Dan
column7: He was the father of Ahiezer, the leader of the children of Dan in the wilderness ([[@4001012|Num 1:12]]). His son led the army of Dan, the rear guard of all the camps, on the march ([[@4010025|Num 10:25]]).

column5: Son of the mighty man Benaiah
column7: He was the son of Benaiah, the army captain for the third month. Benaiah was a mighty man of the thirty, and Ammizabad was in his father's division ([[@13027005-13027006|1 Chr 27:5-6]]).

column5: Lot's descendants who lived east of the Jordan
column7: They were the descendants of Ben Ammi, the son born to Lot's younger daughter ([[@1019038|Gen 19:38]]). They lived east of the Jordan River, and their royal city was Rabbah ([[@10012026|2 Sam 12:26]]). They often fought with Israel, in the days of the judge Jephthah and in David's time ([[@7011004|Judg 11:4]]). In his old age Solomon even built a high place for Molech, the god the Ammonites worshiped ([[@11011007|1 Kgs 11:7]]).

column5: David's firstborn, killed by Absalom
column7: He was the firstborn son David had in Hebron, and his mother was Ahinoam of Jezreel ([[@10003002|2 Sam 3:2]]). He fell in love with his half-sister Tamar, and following the scheme of his friend Jonadab, he committed the great sin of forcing her ([[@10013014|2 Sam 13:14]]). Tamar's brother Absalom hated Amnon for this, and two years later he invited him to a sheep-shearing feast and had his servants kill him when he was drunk ([[@10013028-10013029|2 Sam 13:28-29]]). This left long-lasting sorrow and strife in David's family.

column5: Son of Shimon in Judah's genealogy
column7: He was the son of Shimon in the genealogy of Judah's descendants, and his brothers were Rinnah, Ben Hanan, and Tilon ([[@13004020|1 Chr 4:20]]).

column5: Priest who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the priests who returned in the days of Zerubbabel and Jeshua ([[@16012007|Neh 12:7]]). Later, the head of 'the family of Amok' was Eber ([[@16012020|Neh 12:20]]).

column5: City governor in Ahab's time
column7: He was the governor of the city in the time of King Ahab of Israel. Ahab had the prophet Micaiah seized and taken to Amon the governor and to Joash the king's son ([[@11022026|1 Kgs 22:26]]).

column5: Manasseh's son, a king of Judah killed by servants
column7: He was the son of Manasseh king of Judah; he became king at twenty-two and reigned two years in Jerusalem ([[@12021019|2 Kgs 21:19]]). Like his father, he did evil in the LORD's sight and served idols, but unlike his father Manasseh, he did not humble himself ([[@12021020-12021022|2 Kgs 21:20-22]]; [[@14033023|2 Chr 33:23]]). In the end his servants conspired against him and killed him in his palace, and the people of the land killed the conspirators and made his son Josiah king ([[@12021023-12021024|2 Kgs 21:23-24]]).

column5: An ancient people who lived in Canaan
column7: They were one of the peoples descended from Canaan ([[@1010016|Gen 10:16]]). God told Abram that his descendants would come back in the fourth generation, "for the iniquity of the Amorite is not yet full" ([[@1015016|Gen 15:16]]). After the Exodus, Israel defeated Sihon, the Amorite king east of the Jordan ([[@4021021-4021024|Num 21:21-24]]). In Joshua's time Israel defeated the five Amorite kings who came to attack Gibeon ([[@6010005|Josh 10:5]]).

column5: Prophet who was a herdsman from Tekoa
column7: He was a herdsman from Tekoa in Judah and a prophet who received visions about Israel in the days of Uzziah and Jeroboam ([[@30001001|Amos 1:1]]). Amaziah, the priest of Bethel, told Jeroboam that Amos was conspiring against the king, and he told Amos to flee to the land of Judah ([[@30007010-30007012|Amos 7:10-12]]). Amos answered, "I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son" ([[@30007014|Amos 7:14]]). He explained that the LORD had taken him from following the flock and told him to prophesy to Israel ([[@30007015|Amos 7:15]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, named between Mattathias and Nahum ([[@42003025|Luke 3:25]]).

column5: Father of the prophet Isaiah
column7: The father of the prophet Isaiah, he always appears in the Bible in the phrase 'Isaiah the son of Amoz' ([[@23001001|Isa 1:1]]; [[@12019002|2 Kgs 19:2]]; [[@14026022|2 Chr 26:22]]). His name looks much like that of the prophet Amos, but they are two different names. Take care not to confuse him with the prophet Amos, who was a herdsman of Tekoa. The Bible tells us nothing more about his own life.

column5: A city Paul and Silas passed through
column7: Paul and Silas passed through it, along with Apollonia, on their way to Thessalonica. In Thessalonica there was a Jewish synagogue ([[@44017001|Acts 17:1]]).

column5: A believer in Rome Paul greeted
column7: In his letter to the church in Rome, Paul greeted him, calling him "my beloved in the Lord" ([[@45016008|Rom 16:8]]).

column5: Father of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
column7: He was a son of Kohath, the son of Levi ([[@2006016-2006018|Exod 6:16-18]]). He married his father's sister Jochebed, who bore him Aaron and Moses, and he lived to be one hundred thirty-seven ([[@2006020|Exod 6:20]]). First Chronicles lists his children as Aaron, Moses, and Miriam ([[@13006003|1 Chr 6:3]]). His descendants were called 'the family of the Amramites' and formed one branch of the Levite family of Kohath ([[@4003027|Num 3:27]]).

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a descendant of Bani, named in the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra's time ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]).

column5: King of Shinar, ally of Chedorlaomer
column7: King of Shinar in Abram's time, he joined Chedorlaomer king of Elam and others in fighting five kings, including the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah ([[@1014001-1014002|Gen 14:1-2]], 9).

column5: A Merarite Levite, father of Hilkiah
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Ethan of the descendants of Merari, as the son of Bani and the father of Hilkiah ([[@13006044|1 Chr 6:44]]; [[@13006046|1 Chr 6:46]]).

column5: Ancestor of the priest Adaiah in Jerusalem
column7: He was an ancestor of Adaiah, a priest who did the work of the house in Jerusalem after the exile. The text lists Adaiah as Amzi's great-grandson ([[@16011012|Neh 11:12]]).

column5: Town in the hill country of Judah
column7: It was one of the hill country towns where Joshua destroyed the Anakim ([[@6011021|Josh 11:21]]). It later became a town of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015050|Josh 15:50]]).

column5: Son of Zibeon, father of Oholibamah
column7: He was the son of Zibeon, the son of Seir the Horite, and he found the hot springs in the wilderness while feeding the donkeys of his father Zibeon ([[@1036020|Gen 36:20]]; [[@1036024|Gen 36:24]]). His daughter Oholibamah became Esau's wife and bore him Jeush, Jalam, and Korah ([[@1036014|Gen 36:14]]). However, where Esau's wives are introduced, the text reads "Anah, the daughter of Zibeon", so scholars interpret this family relationship differently ([[@1036002|Gen 36:2]]).

column5: A town of the tribe of Issachar
column7: It was one of the towns in the land Issachar's descendants received by lot according to their families, listed with Hapharaim and Shion ([[@6019017-6019019|Josh 19:17-19]]).

column5: A man who stood at Ezra's right
column7: He was one of the men who stood at Ezra's right hand when Ezra stood on the wooden pulpit and read the book of the law ([[@16008004|Neh 8:4]]).

column5: A chief who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010022|Neh 10:22]]).

column5: Ancestor of the tall Anakim in Canaan
column7: He was the ancestor of a tall people who lived in Hebron, and the son of Arba ([[@6015013|Josh 15:13]]). The men who spied out Canaan saw Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, the children of Anak, at Hebron ([[@4013022|Num 13:22]]). Faced with them, they were afraid and said, "We were in our own sight as grasshoppers" ([[@4013033|Num 13:33]]). But later Caleb drove the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai, out of Hebron ([[@6015014|Josh 15:14]]).

column5: People descended from Mizraim
column7: They were one of the peoples descended from Mizraim, the son of Ham, and their name comes after Ludim ([[@1010013|Gen 10:13]]; [[@13001011|1 Chr 1:11]]).

column5: A god worshiped by the Sepharvites
column7: He was a god worshiped by the Sepharvites who were moved to Samaria. They burned their children in the fire to Adrammelech and Anammelech ([[@12017031|2 Kgs 17:31]]).

column5: A chief who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010026|Neh 10:26]]).

column5: Son of Elioenai, of David's house
column7: He was one of the seven sons of Elioenai in the genealogy of the descendants of Jeconiah the captive ([[@13003017|1 Chr 3:17]]; [[@13003024|1 Chr 3:24]]).

column5: Grandfather of Azariah, who repaired the wall
column7: He was the grandfather of Azariah, who repaired the wall near his own house in Nehemiah's time. Azariah was the son of Maaseiah ([[@16003023|Neh 3:23]]).

column5: A place where Benjamites lived after the exile
column7: It was one of the places where Benjamin's descendants lived after returning from exile, listed with Anathoth and Nob ([[@16011031-16011032|Neh 11:31-32]]).

column5: Sapphira's husband, who lied to the Holy Spirit
column7: With his wife Sapphira he sold a possession and kept back part of the price ([[@44005001-44005002|Acts 5:1-2]]). When Peter rebuked him, he fell down and died ([[@44005003|Acts 5:3]]; [[@44005005|Acts 5:5]]).

column5: The disciple in Damascus who laid hands on Saul
column7: He was a disciple in Damascus who, at the Lord's command, laid his hands on Saul so that he could see again ([[@44009010-44009017|Acts 9:10-17]]). Saul got up and was baptized ([[@44009018|Acts 9:18]]).

column5: High priest at Paul's trial
column7: He was the high priest who ordered those standing by to strike Paul on the mouth when Paul stood before the council ([[@44023002|Acts 23:2]]). Five days later he and the orator Tertullus brought charges against Paul before the governor ([[@44024001|Acts 24:1]]).

column5: Father of the judge Shamgar
column7: He was the father of Shamgar, the judge who killed six hundred Philistines with an ox goad ([[@7003031|Judg 3:31]]; [[@7005006|Judg 5:6]]).

column5: Jeremiah's hometown, a priests' town of Benjamin
column7: It was a town in the land of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the towns given to the priests descended from Aaron ([[@6021018|Josh 21:18]]). Instead of punishing Abiathar the priest, Solomon sent him back to his hometown of Anathoth ([[@11002026|1 Kgs 2:26]]). The prophet Jeremiah was also "one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin" ([[@24001001|Jer 1:1]]). When Babylon was invading, Jeremiah bought a field in Anathoth as God told him, showing the hope that this land would be restored ([[@24032009|Jer 32:9]]).

column5: Son of Becher, of Benjamin
column7: He was one of the sons of Becher, the son of Benjamin. They were heads of their fathers' houses and mighty men of valor ([[@13007008-13007009|1 Chr 7:8-9]]).

column5: A chief who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010019|Neh 10:19]]).

column5: Brother of Simon Peter, one of the Twelve
column7: One of Jesus' twelve apostles, he was the brother of Simon, who is called Peter ([[@40010002|Matt 10:2]]). He was one of the two who heard John and followed Jesus, and he first went to find his brother Simon, told him, "We have found the Messiah!", and brought him to Jesus ([[@43001040-43001042|John 1:40-42]]). He was a fisherman casting a net into the Sea of Galilee, and when he heard Jesus' call to make him a fisher of men, he immediately left his nets and followed him ([[@40004018-40004020|Matt 4:18-20]]). When Jesus fed a great crowd, Andrew told him about the boy who had five barley loaves and two fish ([[@43006008-43006009|John 6:8-9]]).

column5: Paul's relative and fellow prisoner
column7: He was Paul's relative and had been in prison with him. He was well known among the apostles and was in Christ before Paul ([[@45016007|Rom 16:7]]).

column5: Amorite ally of Abram
column7: The brother of Mamre and Eshcol, he was an Amorite who was an ally of Abram ([[@1014013|Gen 14:13]]). Abram made sure that those who went with him received their share of the spoils ([[@1014024|Gen 14:24]]).

column5: Spirit who serves God and carries out his will
column7: Angels are spiritual beings sent by God who carry out his will and serve him. Hebrews says that angels are "serving spirits" sent out to serve those who will inherit salvation ([[@58001014|Heb 1:14]]). The angels who went to Sodom hurried Lot along and rescued his family from destruction ([[@1019015|Gen 19:15]]). The angel Gabriel was sent to Mary in Nazareth, and an angel brought the shepherds in the fields "good news of great joy" ([[@42001026|Luke 1:26]]; [[@42002010|Luke 2:10]]).

column5: Where Uzziah built a tower
column7: It was a place in Jerusalem where King Uzziah built and fortified towers, along with the corner gate and the valley gate ([[@14026009|2 Chr 26:9]]).

column5: Son of Shemida, of Manasseh
column7: He was the son of Shemida in the genealogy of Manasseh's descendants, and his brothers were Ahian, Shechem, and Likhi ([[@13007019|1 Chr 7:19]]).

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: It was one of the towns in the hill country received by the tribe of Judah, listed with Anab and Eshtemoh ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015050|Josh 15:50]]).

column5: The prophetess who met baby Jesus in the temple
column7: She was a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel of the tribe of Asher. A widow, she never left the temple but worshiped with fasting and prayer, and she spoke about the baby Jesus to the people ([[@42002036-42002038|Luke 2:36-38]]).

column5: Caiaphas' father-in-law, a high priest
column7: He was called high priest together with Caiaphas ([[@42003002|Luke 3:2]]). After Jesus was arrested, he was first led to Annas, the father-in-law of Caiaphas ([[@43018013|John 18:13]]).

column5: A sign of being set apart as holy
column7: Pouring oil was a sign that a person or thing was set apart as holy to God. Jacob set up the stone he had used for a pillow as a pillar and poured oil on its top ([[@1028018|Gen 28:18]]). The sons who succeeded Aaron were also installed in the priesthood by anointing ([[@2029029|Exod 29:29]]), and when Samuel anointed David, the LORD's Spirit came mightily on David ([[@9016013|1 Sam 16:13]]). In the synagogue Jesus read the words "The Spirit of the Lord is on me, because he has anointed me to preach good news to the poor", and he said that this scripture had been fulfilled that day ([[@42004018|Luke 4:18]], 21).

column5: Son of Shashak, of Benjamin
column7: He was one of the sons of Shashak in the genealogy of Benjamin's descendants, named along with Hananiah, Elam, Iphdeiah, and others ([[@13008024-13008025|1 Chr 8:24-25]]).

column5: Syrian city where believers were first called Christians
column7: A great city of Syria, it is a very important place in the story of the early church. Some of those scattered because of what happened to Stephen preached the Lord Jesus here to Greeks as well ([[@44011019-44011020|Acts 11:19-20]]). Barnabas and Saul taught there for a whole year, and the Bible records, "The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch" ([[@44011026|Acts 11:26]]). The church in Antioch sent Barnabas and Saul out as missionaries ([[@44013001-44013003|Acts 13:1-3]]). It is a different place from Antioch of Pisidia.

column5: Antioch of Pisidia
column7: It was a town of Pisidia where Paul and Barnabas went into the synagogue on the Sabbath ([[@44013014|Acts 13:14]]). They were driven out by the persecution of the Jews, but later returned there ([[@44013050|Acts 13:50]]; [[@44014021|Acts 14:21]]).

column5: The faithful witness killed in Pergamum
column7: In the message to the church in Pergamum, the Lord called him "Antipas my witness, my faithful one". He was killed in the place where Satan's throne is ([[@66002012-66002013|Rev 2:12-13]]).

column5: Where Paul was taken by night
column7: When Paul was being escorted to Caesarea, the soldiers brought him there by night. From the next day on, horsemen escorted Paul ([[@44023031-44023032|Acts 23:31-32]]).

column5: Son of Hakkoz in Judah's genealogy
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah's descendants as a son of Hakkoz. The same verse also names Zobebah and the families of Aharhel ([[@13004008|1 Chr 4:8]]).

column5: A believer approved in Christ
column7: He was a believer in Rome whom Paul greeted, calling him "Apelles, the approved in Christ" ([[@45016010|Rom 16:10]]).

column5: A town where the Philistines camped
column7: It was one of the towns whose kings Joshua defeated ([[@6012018|Josh 12:18]]). The Philistines camped at Aphek when they fought against Israel ([[@9004001|1 Sam 4:1]]; [[@9029001|1 Sam 29:1]]).

column5: A town of the tribe of Asher
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Asher received ([[@6019030|Josh 19:30]]). In Judges it appears as 'Aphik', and Asher did not drive out its inhabitants ([[@7001031|Judg 1:31]]).

column5: The town where Syria was defeated by Israel
column7: It was the town Ben Hadad went up to in order to fight Israel, and when the survivors fled into it, its wall fell ([[@11020026|1 Kgs 20:26]]; [[@11020030|1 Kgs 20:30]]). Elisha said the king of Israel would strike Syria at Aphek ([[@12013017|2 Kgs 13:17]]).

column5: An ancestor of King Saul's family
column7: A Benjamite, he was an ancestor of Kish, Saul's father. The text lists Kish as Aphiah's great-great-grandson ([[@9009001|1 Sam 9:1]]).

column5: A city Paul and Silas passed through
column7: Paul and Silas passed through it, along with Amphipolis, on their way to Thessalonica. After that they came to Thessalonica, where there was a Jewish synagogue ([[@44017001|Acts 17:1]]).

column5: A worker from Alexandria, mighty in the Scriptures
column7: He was a Jew born in Alexandria, a learned man who was mighty in the Scriptures ([[@44018024|Acts 18:24]]). In Ephesus he eagerly taught the things concerning Jesus, but since he knew only the baptism of John, Priscilla and Aquila took him aside and explained the way of God to him more accurately ([[@44018025-44018026|Acts 18:25-26]]). After that he crossed over to Achaia, where he showed from the Scriptures that Jesus was the Christ and greatly helped those who had believed ([[@44018027-44018028|Acts 18:27-28]]). Paul spoke of their work together this way: "I planted. Apollos watered. But God gave the increase" ([[@46003006|1 Cor 3:6]]).

column5: Disciple appointed and sent out by Jesus
column7: Apostle means 'one who is sent'. Jesus chose twelve of his disciples and named them apostles ([[@42006013|Luke 6:13]]). When an apostle was chosen in place of Judas Iscariot, they looked for someone who had been with the Lord Jesus from the beginning and could be a witness of his resurrection ([[@44001021-44001022|Acts 1:21-22]]). Paul too was called by the risen Lord and introduced himself as "Paul, an apostle" ([[@48001001|Gal 1:1]]). The Bible says the church is built "on the foundation of the apostles and prophets", with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone ([[@49002020|Eph 2:20]]).

column5: Son of Nadab, descendant of Judah
column7: From the family of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah, he was a son of Nadab and the brother of Seled ([[@13002030|1 Chr 2:30]]). His son was Ishi ([[@13002031|1 Chr 2:31]]).

column5: A sister addressed in the letter to Philemon
column7: She was greeted together with Philemon in Paul's letter to him, as "the beloved Apphia" ([[@57001001-57001002|Phlm 1:1-2]]).

column5: Paul's co-worker who made tents
column7: He was a Jew born in Pontus who, with his wife Priscilla, worked alongside Paul. He had recently come from Italy because Emperor Claudius had ordered all Jews to leave Rome, and he met Paul in Corinth ([[@44018001-44018002|Acts 18:1-2]]). Because they had the same trade, he and Paul worked together making tents, and later he went with Paul as far as Ephesus ([[@44018003|Acts 18:3]], 18-19). In Ephesus they explained the way of God to Apollos more accurately ([[@44018026|Acts 18:26]]), and Paul thanked them because they "risked their own necks for my life" ([[@45016003-45016004|Rom 16:3-4]]).

column5: Town on Moab's border, given to Lot's descendants
column7: It was a town of Moab, located where it touched the border of Moab ([[@4021015|Num 21:15]]). God told Moses not to trouble Moab, saying, "I have given Ar to the children of Lot for a possession" ([[@5002009|Deut 2:9]]). So Israel did not take the land of Moab but had to pass by Ar, its border ([[@5002018|Deut 2:18]]). In his message about Moab, Isaiah prophesied, "in a night, Ar of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing", and 'Ar of Moab' there refers to this town ([[@23015001|Isa 15:1]]).

column5: Son of Jether, of Asher
column7: He was the son of Jether in the genealogy of Asher's descendants, and his brothers were Jephunneh and Pispa ([[@13007038|1 Chr 7:38]]).

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: It was one of the towns in the hill country received by the tribe of Judah, listed with Dumah and Eshan ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015052|Josh 15:52]]).

column5: Lowland running south from the Jordan valley
column7: It refers to the deep, low valley where the Jordan River flows and the land that runs south from it. That is why the Dead Sea was called "the sea of the Arabah, the Salt Sea" ([[@5003017|Deut 3:17]]). Moses proclaimed the words of Deuteronomy to all Israel beyond the Jordan in the wilderness, in the Arabah ([[@5001001|Deut 1:1]]). Israel passed by the children of Esau in Seir and went along the way of the Arabah by Elath and Ezion Geber ([[@5002008|Deut 2:8]]), and the Arabah is also among the lands Joshua took ([[@6012008|Josh 12:8]]).

column5: Wide desert land southeast of Israel
column7: It refers to the wide land stretching to the south and east of Israel, and to the people who lived there. In Solomon's time the kings of Arabia brought gold and silver ([[@14009014|2 Chr 9:14]]), and in Jehoshaphat's time the Arabians brought him flocks as gifts ([[@14017011|2 Chr 17:11]]). When Nehemiah was building the wall, "Geshem the Arabian" mocked the work along with Sanballat and Tobiah ([[@16002019|Neh 2:19]]). Paul says that after his conversion he went away into Arabia and then returned to Damascus ([[@48001017|Gal 1:17]]).

column5: A Canaanite town in the South
column7: It was a town of the Canaanites who lived in the South, and its king fought against Israel and took some of them captive ([[@4021001|Num 21:1]]). The king of Arad is among the kings Joshua defeated ([[@6012014|Josh 12:14]]).

column5: Son of Beriah, of Benjamin
column7: He was one of the sons of Beriah in the genealogy of Benjamin's descendants. Beriah was a head of the households of the inhabitants of Aijalon ([[@13008013|1 Chr 8:13]]; [[@13008015-13008016|1 Chr 8:15-16]]).

column5: Son of Ulla, of Asher
column7: He was the son of Ulla in the genealogy of Asher's descendants, and his brothers were Hanniel and Rizia ([[@13007039-13007040|1 Chr 7:39-40]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family that returned from exile
column7: Those who returned from exile included 'the children of Arah', seven hundred seventy-five in all ([[@15002005|Ezra 2:5]]). In Nehemiah the number is given as six hundred fifty-two ([[@16007010|Neh 7:10]]).

column5: Father of Shecaniah, Tobiah's father-in-law
column7: He was the father of Shecaniah, the father-in-law of Tobiah, who opposed Nehemiah. Tobiah was "the son-in-law of Shecaniah the son of Arah" ([[@16006018|Neh 6:18]]).

column5: A son of Shem
column7: He was a son of Shem, Noah's son ([[@1010022|Gen 10:22]]). His sons were Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash ([[@1010023|Gen 10:23]]).

column5: Grandson of Nahor, son of Kemuel
column7: He was a grandson of Nahor, Abraham's brother. Nahor's son Kemuel was Aram's father ([[@1022020-1022021|Gen 22:20-21]]).

column5: Son of Shemer, of Asher
column7: He was the son of Shemer in the genealogy of Asher's descendants, and his brothers were Ahi, Rohgah, and Jehubbah ([[@13007034|1 Chr 7:34]]).

column5: An Aramean kingdom hired by Ammon for chariots
column7: It was one of the places, along with Mesopotamia and Zobah, where the Ammonites sent silver to hire chariots and horsemen to fight David ([[@13019006|1 Chr 19:6]]).

column5: A region mentioned in the title of Psalm 60.
column7: Aram of the two rivers, is Mesopotamia (as it is rendered in [[@1024010|Gen. 24:10]]), the country enclosed between the Tigris on the east and the Euphrates on the west (Ps. 60, title); called also the “field of Aram” ([[@28012012|Hos. 12:12]], R.V.) i.e., the open country of Aram; in the Authorized Version, “country of Syria.”

column5: A region mentioned in the title of Psalm 60.
column7: (Ps. 60, title), probably the region between the Euphrates and the Orontes.

column5: Manasseh's concubine, mother of Machir
column7: She was Manasseh's concubine and bore Machir the father of Gilead. The text calls her only "his concubine the Aramitess" ([[@13007014|1 Chr 7:14]]).

column5: Son of Dishan, a Horite
column7: He was a son of Dishan, a descendant of Seir the Horite, one of the original inhabitants of the land, and he was the brother of Uz ([[@1036020|Gen 36:20]], 28; [[@13001042|1 Chr 1:42]]).

column5: The mountains where Noah's ark came to rest
column7: After the flood, on the seventeenth day of the seventh month, the ark rested on the mountains of Ararat ([[@1008004|Gen 8:4]]). The sons who killed Sennacherib escaped to the land of Ararat ([[@12019037|2 Kgs 19:37]]).

column5: The greatest man among the Anakim
column7: He was the greatest man among the Anakim. Hebron's former name, 'Kiriath Arba', came from him ([[@6014015|Josh 14:15]]). He was the father of Anak ([[@6015013|Josh 15:13]]).

column5: Herod's son who ruled Judea after him
column7: He became ruler of Judea in place of his father Herod. When Joseph heard this he was afraid, and after being warned he went to Galilee ([[@40002022|Matt 2:22]]).

column5: Paul's fellow soldier in the work
column7: He was a worker whom Paul called 'our fellow soldier' ([[@57001002|Phlm 1:2]]). Paul sent word to him to fulfill the ministry he had received in the Lord ([[@51004017|Col 4:17]]).

column5: People near Bethel, Hushai's clan
column7: They were people who lived near Bethel, toward Ataroth. The border of the descendants of Joseph is said to pass along "the border of the Archites" ([[@6016002|Josh 16:2]]). David's friend Hushai was an Archite, and when Absalom rebelled, he went to Absalom at David's request and pretended to serve him ([[@10015034|2 Sam 15:34]]; [[@10016016|2 Sam 16:16]]). Absalom and all Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel", and followed his advice, because the LORD had determined to defeat Ahithophel's good counsel ([[@10017014|2 Sam 17:14]]).

column5: A Benjamite who went to Egypt with Jacob
column7: He is named in the list of Benjamin's sons, as one of Israel's family who went down to Egypt with Jacob ([[@1046008|Gen 46:8]]; [[@1046021|Gen 46:21]]).

column5: Son of Bela, of Benjamin
column7: The son of Bela among Benjamin's descendants, he was the ancestor of the family of the Ardites. They appear as one of the families of Benjamin in the census in the wilderness ([[@4026040-4026041|Num 26:40-41]]).

column5: Son of Caleb the son of Hezron
column7: He was a son of Caleb the son of Hezron, by Azubah his wife and by Jerioth, and his brothers were Jesher and Shobab ([[@13002018|1 Chr 2:18]]).

column5: Son of Gad
column7: A son of Jacob's son Gad, he appears in the list of those who went down to Egypt with Jacob ([[@1046016|Gen 46:16]]).

column5: Hill in Athens where Paul preached
column7: It was where the people of Athens brought Paul, and Paul "stood in the middle of the Areopagus" and preached to them ([[@44017019|Acts 17:19]]; [[@44017022|Acts 17:22]]). Dionysius, one of its officials, also believed ([[@44017034|Acts 17:34]]).

column5: The king whose governor watched Damascus
column7: When Paul was in Damascus, this king's governor guarded the city to arrest him ([[@47011032|2 Cor 11:32]]).

column5: A region of towns in Bashan
column7: It was a region in the kingdom of Og in Bashan, with sixty cities ([[@5003004|Deut 3:4]]). Jair the son of Manasseh took the whole region of Argob ([[@5003014|Deut 3:14]]).

column5: A man killed with King Pekahiah
column7: He was killed along with Arieh when Pekah rebelled and killed Pekahiah king of Israel in the royal palace in Samaria ([[@12015023|2 Kgs 15:23]]; [[@12015025|2 Kgs 15:25]]).

column5: One of Haman's ten sons
column7: He was one of the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews, and was killed in the citadel of Susa ([[@17009006-17009010|Esth 9:6-10]]).

column5: One of Haman's ten sons
column7: He was one of the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews, and was killed in the citadel of Susa ([[@17009006-17009010|Esth 9:6-10]]).

column5: A man killed with King Pekahiah
column7: He was killed along with Argob when Pekah rebelled and killed Pekahiah king of Israel in the royal palace in Samaria ([[@12015023|2 Kgs 15:23]]; [[@12015025|2 Kgs 15:25]]).

column5: Father of two men Benaiah killed
column7: He was a Moabite whose two sons were killed by Benaiah, one of David's mighty men ([[@10023020|2 Sam 23:20]]; [[@13011022|1 Chr 11:22]]).

column5: A leader Ezra summoned
column7: He was one of the leaders Ezra sent for at the river that runs to Ahava, in order to bring Levites ([[@15008015-15008017|Ezra 8:15-17]]).

column5: King of Ellasar, ally of Chedorlaomer
column7: King of Ellasar in Abram's time, he joined Chedorlaomer king of Elam and others in fighting five kings, including the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah ([[@1014001-1014002|Gen 14:1-2]], 9).

column5: Captain of the Babylonian king's guard
column7: The captain of King Nebuchadnezzar's guard, he went out at the king's command to kill the wise men of Babylon ([[@27002014|Dan 2:14]]). He hurried Daniel in before the king and reported that he had found someone who could give the interpretation ([[@27002025|Dan 2:25]]).

column5: One of Haman's ten sons
column7: He was one of the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews, and was killed in the citadel of Susa ([[@17009006-17009010|Esth 9:6-10]]).

column5: A Thessalonian who traveled with Paul
column7: He was a Macedonian from Thessalonica who was seized during the riot in Ephesus ([[@44019029|Acts 19:29]]). He also boarded the ship with Paul on the way to Rome ([[@44027002|Acts 27:2]]).

column5: A man whose household Paul greeted
column7: In his letter to the church in Rome, Paul wrote, "Greet those who are of the household of Aristobulus" ([[@45016010|Rom 16:10]]).

column5: Holy chest holding God's covenant tablets
column7: The ark of the covenant was a chest made of acacia wood and overlaid inside and out with pure gold; because the tablets of the covenant that God gave were kept inside it, it is also called the ark of the Testimony ([[@2025010-2025016|Exod 25:10-16]]). On top of it were the mercy seat and two cherubim, and God said he would meet Moses there and speak with him from between the two cherubim ([[@2025022|Exod 25:22]]). When the priests carrying the ark of the covenant stepped into the Jordan, the flowing water stopped and all the people crossed on dry ground ([[@6003015-6003017|Josh 3:15-17]]). In Solomon's time it was moved into the Most Holy Place of the temple, and there was nothing in it but the two stone tablets ([[@11008009|1 Kgs 8:9]]).

column5: Descendants of Canaan
column7: They were one of the peoples descended from Canaan, the son of Ham, and their name comes after the Hivites ([[@1010015|Gen 10:15]], 17; [[@13001015|1 Chr 1:15]]).

column5: Son of Saul and Rizpah
column7: He was a son born to Saul by Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. David handed him over to the Gibeonites, and they hanged him ([[@10021008-10021009|2 Sam 21:8-9]]).

column5: Son of Rephaiah in David's family line
column7: He was the son of Rephaiah in the genealogy of the descendants of Jeconiah the captive ([[@13003017|1 Chr 3:17]]; [[@13003021|1 Chr 3:21]]).

column5: Valley east of the Jordan marking Moab's border
column7: It is a stream east of the Jordan that flows into the Dead Sea, together with its deep valley. The Bible says, "the Arnon is the border of Moab, between Moab and the Amorites" ([[@4021013|Num 21:13]]). After defeating Sihon king of the Amorites, Israel took his land "from the Arnon to the Jabbok" ([[@4021024|Num 21:24]]). After that, the valley of the Arnon became the southern border of the land given to the Reubenites and the Gadites ([[@5003016|Deut 3:16]]).

column5: Son of Gad
column7: He was a son of Gad, and in Genesis his name is written 'Arodi' ([[@1046016|Gen 46:16]]). The family of the Arodites came from him ([[@4026017|Num 26:17]]).

column5: Town east of the Jordan built by Gad
column7: It was a town east of the Jordan built by the descendants of Gad ([[@4032034|Num 32:34]]). The territory of the tribe of Gad reached to half the land of the Ammonites, as far as 'Aroer that is near Rabbah' ([[@6013025|Josh 13:25]]). The judge Jephthah struck twenty towns from Aroer to Minnith and subdued the Ammonites ([[@7011033|Judg 11:33]]). When David counted the people, the men taking the census crossed the Jordan and camped on the right side of Aroer ([[@10024005|2 Sam 24:5]]). The Bible has several towns by this name, so scholars differ on which Aroer is meant in which verse.

column5: A town on the edge of the Arnon valley
column7: It was a town on the edge of the valley of the Arnon, and the land ruled by Sihon king of Heshbon began at this Aroer ([[@6012002|Josh 12:2]]). After defeating Sihon, Israel took every high city from Aroer to Gilead ([[@5002036|Deut 2:36]]). Later the children of Gad built fortified cities, including Aroer ([[@4032034-4032036|Num 32:34-36]]). Much later, when Hazael of Syria attacked Israel, he took the land from Aroer by the valley of the Arnon to Gilead and Bashan ([[@12010032-12010033|2 Kgs 10:32-33]]).

column5: A town of Judah to which David sent plunder
column7: It was one of the places to which David sent the elders of Judah gifts from the plunder he had recovered from the Amalekites ([[@9030026|1 Sam 30:26]]; [[@9030028|1 Sam 30:28]]).

column5: Son of Shem, ancestor of Abraham
column7: He was the son of Shem, the son of Noah ([[@1010022|Gen 10:22]]). He was born when Shem was one hundred years old, two years after the flood; at thirty-five he became the father of Shelah, and after that he lived four hundred three more years and had other children ([[@1011010-1011013|Gen 11:10-13]]). From his descendants, by way of Eber and Terah, came Abram ([[@1011014-1011026|Gen 11:14-26]]). In Luke's genealogy of Jesus he is written as 'Arphaxad' ([[@42003036|Luke 3:36]]).

column5: Syrian town near Hamath, conquered by Assyria
column7: It was a Syrian town near Hamath, and in the Bible it almost always appears together with Hamath. The Rabshakeh, an officer of the king of Assyria, boasted to the people of Jerusalem, asking where the gods of Hamath and Arpad were ([[@12018028|2 Kgs 18:28]], 34). In his message to Hezekiah, the king of Assyria also asked where the kings of Hamath and Arpad were, and threatened that Jerusalem would not be saved any more than the nations Assyria had destroyed ([[@12019010-12019013|2 Kgs 19:10-13]]). Isaiah also recorded the proud words of the king of Assyria: "Isn’t Hamath like Arpad?" ([[@23010008-23010009|Isa 10:8-9]]).

column5: Persian king in the days of Ezra and Nehemiah
column7: A king of Persia who appears in the days of Ezra and Nehemiah. At first, after receiving a letter accusing the people of Jerusalem, he stopped the work of building the city ([[@15004023|Ezra 4:23]]). But in his seventh year, Ezra the scribe received the king's decree and led the people up to Jerusalem ([[@15007007|Ezra 7:7]], 21). In his twentieth year he sent his cupbearer Nehemiah to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem ([[@16002001-16002006|Neh 2:1-6]]). Scholars differ on whether all these mentions refer to the same king.

column5: A coworker Paul planned to send to Titus
column7: He was a man Paul planned to send to Titus, named along with Tychicus. Paul told Titus to hurry to Nicopolis once he arrived ([[@56003012|Titus 3:12]]).

column5: The district of Solomon's officer Ben Hesed
column7: It was the district of Ben Hesed, one of Solomon's twelve officers, who was also in charge of Socoh and all the land of Hepher ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004010|1 Kgs 4:10]]).

column5: Place where Abimelech stayed
column7: It was the place where Abimelech stayed. Meanwhile, Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem ([[@7009041|Judg 9:41]]).

column5: Coastal town that served Tyre
column7: Ezekiel sings that the inhabitants of Arvad were Tyre's rowers ([[@26027008|Ezek 27:8]]) and that the men of Arvad stood guard on Tyre's walls ([[@26027011|Ezek 27:11]]).

column5: Descendants of Canaan
column7: They were one of the peoples descended from Canaan, the son of Ham. Afterward the families of the Canaanites were spread abroad ([[@1010018|Gen 10:18]]; [[@13001016|1 Chr 1:16]]).

column5: Steward of the household under King Elah
column7: He was over the household in the time of Elah king of Israel. While Elah was getting drunk in Arza's house in Tirzah, Zimri struck and killed the king ([[@11016009-11016010|1 Kgs 16:9-10]])

column5: The third king of Judah, who removed idols
column7: Asa was the son of Abijam and the third king of Judah ([[@11015008|1 Kgs 15:8]]). He did what was right in the LORD's eyes as his forefather David had, and he removed his mother Maacah from being queen mother because she had made an Asherah image ([[@11015011-11015013|1 Kgs 15:11-13]]). When Zerah the Ethiopian invaded with a huge army, he cried out to the LORD and won the victory ([[@14014011-14014012|2 Chr 14:11-12]]). But when his feet became diseased late in life, the record says "he didn’t seek the LORD, but just the physicians" ([[@14016012|2 Chr 16:12]]). He reigned forty-one years.

column5: Father of the Levite Berechiah
column7: The son of Elkanah, he was the father of Berechiah, a Levite. Berechiah lived in the villages of the Netophathites ([[@13009014|1 Chr 9:14]]; [[@13009016|1 Chr 9:16]]).

column5: Joab's brother, a warrior killed by Abner
column7: One of the three sons of David's sister Zeruiah, he was the younger brother of Joab and Abishai ([[@13002016|1 Chr 2:16]]). The Bible says, "Asahel was as light of foot as a wild gazelle" ([[@10002018|2 Sam 2:18]]). In the battle at Gibeon he chased Abner to the end, and because he would not listen when told to turn back, Abner struck him with his spear and he died ([[@10002023|2 Sam 2:23]]). He was one of David's thirty mighty men, and later Joab killed Abner because of this ([[@10003027|2 Sam 3:27]]).

column5: A Levite sent to teach the law
column7: He was one of the Levites sent to the towns of Judah in King Jehoshaphat's time to teach the people from the book of the LORD's law ([[@14017008-14017009|2 Chr 17:8-9]]).

column5: A Levite who oversaw the offerings
column7: In Hezekiah's time he was one of the overseers, under Conaniah and Shimei, of the offerings and tithes brought to the temple ([[@14031012-14031013|2 Chr 31:12-13]]).

column5: Father of Jonathan in Ezra's time
column7: He was the father of Jonathan, who stood up against the plan to send away foreign wives in Ezra's time ([[@15010015|Ezra 10:15]]).

column5: Servant of King Josiah
column7: A servant of King Josiah, he was sent by the king with Hilkiah the priest and others to Huldah the prophetess about the book of the law that had been found ([[@12022012-12022014|2 Kgs 22:12-14]]; [[@14034020|2 Chr 34:20]]).

column5: A chief of the Simeonites
column7: He is named in the list of chiefs of Simeon's descendants. They went to the entrance of Gedor to look for pasture, and settled there in the days of Hezekiah ([[@13004036|1 Chr 4:36]]; [[@13004039-13004041|1 Chr 4:39-41]]).

column5: Son of Haggiah, a Merarite
column7: He appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Levi's son Merari. In the line that runs from Mahli, he is listed as the son of Haggiah ([[@13006029-13006030|1 Chr 6:29-30]]).

column5: Firstborn of the Shilonites in Jerusalem
column7: He was the firstborn of the Shilonites among those who lived in Jerusalem after the exile ([[@13009003|1 Chr 9:3]]; [[@13009005|1 Chr 9:5]]).

column5: Merarite chief who helped bring up the ark
column7: A chief of the sons of Merari, he led two hundred twenty of his brothers ([[@13015006|1 Chr 15:6]]). He was one of the Levites David called to bring up the ark of the covenant ([[@13015011|1 Chr 15:11]]).

column5: Father of Joah, recorder in Hezekiah's time
column7: He was the father of Joah, the recorder in the time of King Hezekiah ([[@12018018|2 Kgs 18:18]]). His son Joah tore his clothes after hearing the words of the Rabshakeh ([[@12018037|2 Kgs 18:37]]).

column5: Levite ancestor of Mattaniah
column7: He was the great-grandfather of Mattaniah, a Levite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile ([[@13009015|1 Chr 9:15]]). Mattaniah led the thanksgiving in prayer ([[@16011017|Neh 11:17]]).

column5: Levite who led worship in David's time
column7: He was the son of Berechiah, a Levite whom David appointed as a singer ([[@13015017|1 Chr 15:17]]). Together with Heman and Ethan, he led the praise, sounding cymbals of bronze aloud ([[@13015019|1 Chr 15:19]]). On the day the ark of the covenant was brought in, David appointed Asaph and his brothers to give thanks to the LORD ([[@13016007|1 Chr 16:7]]). His name is in the titles of Psalm 50 and Psalms 73-83, and in Hezekiah's time the Levites sang praises "with the words of David, and of Asaph the seer" ([[@14029030|2 Chr 29:30]]). His descendants were in charge of singing in the temple for generations.

column5: Keeper of the king's forest
column7: He was the keeper of the Persian king's forest. Nehemiah asked the king for a letter to him so that he would give timber for the gates of the citadel by the temple and for the city wall ([[@16002008|Neh 2:8]])

column5: Son of Jehallelel in Judah's genealogy
column7: He was the son of Jehallelel in the genealogy of Judah's descendants, and his brothers were Ziph, Ziphah, and Tiria ([[@13004016|1 Chr 4:16]]).

column5: Wife of Joseph, mother of Manasseh and Ephraim
column7: The daughter of Potiphera priest of On, she was given to Joseph as his wife by Pharaoh ([[@1041045|Gen 41:45]]). Before the famine came, she bore Manasseh and Ephraim to Joseph ([[@1041050|Gen 41:50]]; [[@1046020|Gen 46:20]]).

column5: A town of Judah and Simeon
column7: It was a town in the lowland of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015042|Josh 15:42]]). It became part of Simeon's share and was also given to the Levites ([[@6019007|Josh 19:7]]; [[@13006059|1 Chr 6:59]]).

column5: Son of Asaph, a singer
column7: A son of Asaph, he served in prophetic music under his father in King David's time ([[@13025002|1 Chr 25:2]]). The seventh division of singers is listed under the name 'Jesharelah' ([[@13025014|1 Chr 25:14]]).

column5: Son of Benjamin
column7: A son of Benjamin, he is recorded in 1 Chronicles as the second son ([[@1046021|Gen 46:21]]; [[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]). The family of the Ashbelites came from him ([[@4026038|Num 26:38]]).

column5: Philistine city with a temple of Dagon
column7: It was one of the five great cities of the Philistines, near the coast between Gaza and Joppa. In Joshua's time it was assigned to the tribe of Judah, but Israel never fully took it ([[@6013001-6013003|Josh 13:1-3]]; [[@6015047|Josh 15:47]]). When the Philistines put the captured ark of the covenant in the house of Dagon here, "Dagon had fallen on his face to the ground before the LORD’s ark" and the people of the city suffered a plague of tumors ([[@9005003-9005006|1 Sam 5:3-6]]). In the New Testament it is called Azotus, and Philip appeared there and preached the gospel as he went through the towns ([[@44008040|Acts 8:40]]).

column5: Jacob's son, ancestor of the tribe of Asher
column7: Asher was the son Jacob had by Zilpah, Leah's servant ([[@1035026|Gen 35:26]]). Leah named him, saying, "Happy am I" ([[@1030013|Gen 30:13]]). Jacob blessed him, saying, "Asher’s food will be rich" ([[@1049020|Gen 49:20]]). The tribe of Asher received land along the northern coast of Canaan. Anna, the prophetess who met the baby Jesus in the temple, was from the tribe of Asher ([[@42002036|Luke 2:36]]).

column5: What remains after burning; a sign of grief and repentance
column7: Ashes are the powder left after something has burned. In Egypt, when Moses tossed ashes from the furnace up toward the sky, boils broke out on people and animals ([[@2009010|Exod 9:10]]). The ashes of a burned heifer were gathered and kept, and used to make water for cleansing impurity ([[@4019009|Num 19:9]]). In times of great sorrow people put on sackcloth and covered themselves with ashes, and Mordecai did this and wailed loudly and bitterly ([[@17004001|Esth 4:1]]). After his eyes saw the Lord, Job confessed, "I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes" ([[@18042005-18042006|Job 42:5-6]]).

column5: Father of Tekoa
column7: He was the son whom Hezron's wife Abijah bore after Hezron died, and he was the father of Tekoa ([[@13002024|1 Chr 2:24]]). He had two wives, Helah and Naarah ([[@13004005|1 Chr 4:5]]).

column5: One of the five Philistine cities
column7: A Philistine city on the shore of the Mediterranean, it was one of the five cities for which the Philistines offered golden tumors ([[@9006017|1 Sam 6:17]]). Early in the time of the judges, Judah took Ashkelon and its territory ([[@7001018|Judg 1:18]]). When the Spirit of the LORD came mightily on Samson, he went down to Ashkelon and struck down thirty of its men ([[@7014019|Judg 14:19]]). The prophets foretold that Ashkelon, along with the other Philistine cities, would become desolate ([[@36002004|Zeph 2:4]]).

column5: Son of Gomer, grandson of Japheth
column7: He was a son of Gomer, the son of Noah's son Japheth, and the brother of Riphath and Togarmah ([[@1010002-1010003|Gen 10:2-3]]; [[@13001006|1 Chr 1:6]]).

column5: A kingdom called to attack Babylon
column7: It is a kingdom Jeremiah said to call together, along with Ararat and Minni, against Babylon. The kings of the Medes were also prepared against her ([[@24051027-24051028|Jer 51:27-28]]).

column5: Town in the lowland of Judah
column7: It was one of the lowland towns of the tribe of Judah. The same name appears twice, so some think it refers to two different places ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]], 43).

column5: Nebuchadnezzar's chief of the eunuchs
column7: He was the master of the eunuchs of the king of Babylon. The king ordered him to bring some of the Israelites from the royal family and the nobles ([[@27001003|Dan 1:3]]).

column5: The town where Og king of Bashan lived
column7: It was a town in the land of Bashan east of the Jordan, where Og king of Bashan lived ([[@5001004|Deut 1:4]]). Og, who was left of the remnant of the Rephaim, reigned in Ashtaroth and Edrei, and Moses attacked the people of that land and drove them out ([[@6013012|Josh 13:12]]). Later the town went to the children of Machir the son of Manasseh ([[@6013031|Josh 13:31]]), and it was given to the sons of Gershom among the Levites ([[@13006071|1 Chr 6:71]]). The name Ashtaroth is also used for the goddess of the Sidonians, also called Ashtoreth, so the context must tell them apart.

column5: Place where Chedorlaomer struck the Rephaim
column7: In Abram's time, Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him came and struck the Rephaim here. After that they also fought five kings, including the king of Sodom ([[@1014005|Gen 14:5]], 8).

column5: Son of Japhlet, of Asher
column7: He was the son of Japhlet in the genealogy of Asher's descendants, and his brothers were Pasach and Bimhal ([[@13007033|1 Chr 7:33]]).

column5: Roman province centered on Ephesus
column7: In the New Testament, Asia means a Roman province in what is now western Turkey, and its main city was Ephesus. Among the people gathered in Jerusalem at Pentecost were some from Asia ([[@44002009|Acts 2:9]]). At first the Holy Spirit kept Paul from speaking the word there ([[@44016006|Acts 16:6]]), but later he taught in Ephesus for two years, "so that all those who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks" ([[@44019010|Acts 19:10]]). The book of Revelation begins as a letter to "the seven assemblies that are in Asia" ([[@66001004|Rev 1:4]]).

column5: Ancestor of Jehu, of Simeon
column7: He was an ancestor of Jehu, a chief of Simeon's descendants, and the text lists Jehu as Asiel's great-grandson ([[@13004035|1 Chr 4:35]]).

column5: A temple servant family that returned from exile
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Asnah' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]]; [[@15002050|Ezra 2:50]]).

column5: One of Haman's ten sons
column7: He was one of the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews, and was killed in the citadel of Susa ([[@17009006-17009010|Esth 9:6-10]]).

column5: Descendant of Manasseh, ancestor of the Asrielites
column7: A descendant of Gilead of the tribe of Manasseh, he was the ancestor of the family of the Asrielites ([[@4026030-4026031|Num 26:30-31]]). When the descendants of Manasseh received their inheritance by lot, his descendants also received a share ([[@6017002|Josh 17:2]]).

column5: Son of Manasseh
column7: He was a son of Manasseh, and the text says, "Asriel, whom his concubine the Aramitess bore." She also bore Machir the father of Gilead ([[@13007014|1 Chr 7:14]])

column5: Son of Shem
column7: He was one of the sons of Noah's son Shem, and the brother of Elam, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram ([[@1010022|Gen 10:22]]; [[@13001017|1 Chr 1:17]]).

column5: A people descended from Dedan
column7: They were a people descended from Dedan, a grandson of Abraham and Keturah. They are listed with the Letushim and the Leummim ([[@1025001-1025003|Gen 25:1-3]]).

column5: Son of Korah
column7: A son of Korah the Levite, he was one of the heads of the Korahite families ([[@2006024|Exod 6:24]]). In 1 Chronicles he appears as a descendant of Kohath ([[@13006022|1 Chr 6:22]]).

column5: Son of Ebiasaph, ancestor of Samuel
column7: He was a son of Ebiasaph, a descendant of Korah ([[@13006023|1 Chr 6:23]]). In the genealogy of Heman the singer, he appears as the father of Tahath ([[@13006037|1 Chr 6:37]]).

column5: Port where Paul boarded the ship
column7: Paul went to Assos on foot while his companions went ahead by ship ([[@44020013|Acts 20:13]]). They met Paul there, took him aboard, and went on to Mitylene ([[@44020014|Acts 20:14]]).

column5: A great nation with Nineveh as its capital
column7: It was a great nation along the Hiddekel River, and Nineveh was its great city. The Hiddekel, the third river of Eden, is said to flow "in front of Assyria" ([[@1002014|Gen 2:14]]). The king of Assyria took Samaria and carried the people of northern Israel away captive ([[@12017006|2 Kgs 17:6]]). In Hezekiah's time Assyria threatened Jerusalem, but the angel of the LORD struck their camp and drove them back ([[@12019035|2 Kgs 19:35]]). The prophet Jonah went to Nineveh and proclaimed judgment ([[@32003004|Jonah 3:4]]).

column5: A believer in Rome Paul greeted
column7: He was greeted by Paul in his letter to the church in Rome, along with Phlegon, Hermes, and others ([[@45016014|Rom 16:14]]).

column5: Place of great mourning for Jacob
column7: It was a threshing floor beyond the Jordan where Joseph mourned seven days for his father Jacob ([[@1050010|Gen 50:10]]). When the people of the land saw this, they called the place Abel Mizraim ([[@1050011|Gen 50:11]]).

column5: Wife of Jerahmeel, mother of Onam
column7: She was Jerahmeel's other wife and the mother of Onam. Onam's sons were Shammai and Jada ([[@13002026|1 Chr 2:26]]; [[@13002028|1 Chr 2:28]]).

column5: Town built by the children of Gad
column7: It was one of the towns in the land east of the Jordan that the children of Reuben and Gad asked Moses for ([[@4032003|Num 32:3]]). Later the children of Gad built this town ([[@4032034|Num 32:34]]).

column5: Town on the border of Ephraim
column7: It was one of the places along the border of the descendants of Joseph, that is, the children of Ephraim. The border went down from Ataroth to Naarah and reached Jericho ([[@6016002|Josh 16:2]], 7).

column5: Town on the border of Ephraim and Benjamin
column7: It was on the eastern border of the inheritance of the children of Ephraim ([[@6016005|Josh 16:5]]). The border of the tribe of Benjamin also passed through here ([[@6018013|Josh 18:13]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family that returned from exile
column7: Those who returned from exile included 'the children of Ater, of Hezekiah', ninety-eight in all ([[@15002016|Ezra 2:16]]; [[@16007021|Neh 7:21]]).

column5: Family of gatekeepers that returned from exile
column7: Among the descendants of the gatekeepers who returned from exile were the children of Ater ([[@15002042|Ezra 2:42]]; [[@16007045|Neh 7:45]]).

column5: A chief who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010017|Neh 10:17]]).

column5: A place to which David sent plunder
column7: It was one of the places to which David sent the elders of Judah gifts from the plunder he had recovered from the Amalekites ([[@9030026|1 Sam 30:26]]; [[@9030030|1 Sam 30:30]]).

column5: A man of Judah who lived in Jerusalem
column7: A man of Judah who lived in Jerusalem after the exile, he was a descendant of Perez and the son of Uzziah ([[@16011004|Neh 11:4]]).

column5: Ahab's daughter who seized Judah's throne
column7: She was the daughter of Ahab king of Israel and the granddaughter of Omri; she became the wife of Jehoram king of Judah and led her husband in the way of Ahab ([[@12008018|2 Kgs 8:18]], 26). When her son Ahaziah died, she destroyed all the royal offspring and ruled the land herself for six years ([[@12011001-12011003|2 Kgs 11:1-3]]). But young Joash survived, hidden in the LORD's house, and when he was made king, Athaliah cried out, "Treason! Treason!" and was put to death ([[@12011014-12011016|2 Kgs 11:14-16]]).

column5: Son of Jeroham, of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin's descendants as one of the sons of Jeroham ([[@13008026-13008027|1 Chr 8:26-27]]).

column5: Father of Jeshaiah, who returned with Ezra
column7: He was the father of Jeshaiah, of the descendants of Elam, who returned with Ezra. Seventy men came back with Jeshaiah ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008007|Ezra 8:7]]).

column5: The road where the king of Arad attacked Israel
column7: The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the South, heard that Israel was coming by this road and attacked Israel ([[@4021001|Num 21:1]]).

column5: The great Greek city where Paul preached the gospel
column7: It was a famous city of Greece, and those escorting Paul brought him all the way here ([[@44017015|Acts 17:15]]). While Paul waited in Athens for Silas and Timothy, his spirit was provoked when he saw the city full of idols ([[@44017016|Acts 17:16]]). The people of Athens spent their time doing nothing else but "either to tell or to hear some new thing" ([[@44017021|Acts 17:21]]). Standing in the middle of the Areopagus, Paul pointed to an altar inscribed 'TO AN UNKNOWN GOD' and proclaimed to them the God they worshiped without knowing ([[@44017022-44017023|Acts 17:22-23]]).

column5: A descendant of Bebai who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a descendant of Bebai, named in the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra's time ([[@15010028|Ezra 10:28]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Cleansing sin and restoring peace with God
column7: Atonement means covering and washing away sin so that people are brought back into peace with God. In the Old Testament the priests made atonement with the blood of animals, and God said, "it is the blood that makes atonement by reason of the life" ([[@3017011|Lev 17:11]]). Every year on the Day of Atonement, the tenth day of the seventh month, the high priest made atonement for all the sins of the people ([[@3016030|Lev 16:30]]; [[@3023027|Lev 23:27]]). The New Testament says that Christ, "through his own blood, entered in once for all into the Holy Place, having obtained eternal redemption" ([[@58009012|Heb 9:12]]).

column5: A place in the line of Salma
column7: It is a name listed, along with Bethlehem and the Netophathites, among the descendants of Salma, a descendant of Caleb ([[@13002050-13002054|1 Chr 2:50-54]]).

column5: A town built by the Gadites
column7: It was one of the towns the Gadites built east of the Jordan, listed with Dibon, Ataroth, Aroer, and Jazer ([[@4032034-4032035|Num 32:34-35]]).

column5: Grandson of Sheshan, descendant of Judah
column7: He was the son born after Sheshan, who had no sons, gave his daughter to his Egyptian servant Jarha ([[@13002034-13002035|1 Chr 2:34-35]]). He became the father of Nathan ([[@13002036|1 Chr 2:36]]).

column5: A Gadite warrior who came to David
column7: He was the sixth of the Gadite warriors who joined David. They were trained for war and skilled with shield and spear ([[@13012008|1 Chr 12:8]]; [[@13012011|1 Chr 12:11]]).

column5: Son of Rehoboam and Maacah
column7: He was a son born to Rehoboam king of Judah by Maacah, Absalom's granddaughter. His siblings were Abijah, Ziza, and Shelomith ([[@14011020|2 Chr 11:20]])

column5: The port where Paul and Barnabas set sail
column7: It is where Paul and Barnabas went down after preaching the word in Perga. From there they sailed back to Antioch ([[@44014025-44014026|Acts 14:25-26]]).

column5: The Roman emperor when Jesus was born
column7: Because "a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that all the world should be enrolled", Joseph and Mary went to Bethlehem ([[@42002001-42002004|Luke 2:1-4]]).

column5: A valley in Aram under Amos's judgment
column7: It is a valley mentioned when Amos announced judgment on Damascus and Aram. God said he would cut off the inhabitant from it ([[@30001005|Amos 1:5]]).

column5: City of Hadad, king of Edom
column7: It was the city of Hadad the son of Bedad, one of the kings who reigned over Edom before any king reigned over Israel ([[@1036031|Gen 36:31]], 35; [[@13001046|1 Chr 1:46]]).

column5: Ancient people living around Gaza
column7: They were an ancient people who lived in villages as far as Gaza and were destroyed by the Caphtorim ([[@5002023|Deut 2:23]]). In Joshua's time the land of the Avvim still remained in the south ([[@6013003|Josh 13:3]]).

column5: A town of the tribe of Benjamin
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Benjamin received according to their families ([[@6018021|Josh 18:21]]; [[@6018023|Josh 18:23]]).

column5: A place at the end of a valley in Zechariah
column7: In Zechariah's prophecy, the valley of the mountains will reach as far as this place. Scholars differ on where it was ([[@38014005|Zech 14:5]]).

column5: Father of Shaphan the scribe
column7: He was the father of Shaphan the scribe in King Josiah's time, and the son of Meshullam ([[@12022003|2 Kgs 22:3]]). He is also mentioned in 2 Chronicles ([[@14034008|2 Chr 34:8]]).

column5: Father of Jeshua, a Levite who sealed the covenant
column7: He was the father of Jeshua, a Levite who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time. Binnui and Kadmiel are named in the same verse ([[@16010009|Neh 10:9]]).

column5: A Korahite who came to David at Ziklag
column7: He was a Korahite, one of the warriors who came to David and helped him in battle while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001|1 Chr 12:1]]; [[@13012006|1 Chr 12:6]]).

column5: Ruler of the tribe of Dan under David
column7: The son of Jeroham, he was the ruler over the tribe of Dan in David's time ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027022|1 Chr 27:22]]).

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a descendant of Bani, named in the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra's time ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]; [[@15010041|Ezra 10:41]]).

column5: A musician at the dedication of the wall
column7: He was one of those who marched with the musical instruments of David the man of God at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem ([[@16012027|Neh 12:27]]; [[@16012036|Neh 12:36]]).

column5: A priest in Solomon's time
column7: The son of Zadok, he was the priest among King Solomon's officials. He is named first in the list of Solomon's officials ([[@11004001-11004002|1 Kgs 4:1-2]]).

column5: Solomon's officer over the officers
column7: The son of Nathan, he was over the officers among King Solomon's officials. The same verse says Zabud the son of Nathan was chief minister and the king's friend ([[@11004005|1 Kgs 4:5]]).

column5: Son of Ethan, of Judah
column7: He was the son of Ethan in the genealogy of Judah's descendants. Ethan was one of the five sons of Judah's son Zerah ([[@13002006|1 Chr 2:6]]; [[@13002008|1 Chr 2:8]]).

column5: Son of Jehu, a Jerahmeelite
column7: He was a son of Jehu, from the family of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah ([[@13002038|1 Chr 2:38]]). He became the father of Helez ([[@13002039|1 Chr 2:39]]).

column5: Priest in Solomon's temple
column7: In the priestly line, he was the son of Johanan, and he served as priest in the house that Solomon built in Jerusalem ([[@13006010|1 Chr 6:10]]). He became the father of Amariah ([[@13006011|1 Chr 6:11]]).

column5: The grandfather of Ezra
column7: In the line of the high priests he was the son of Hilkiah and the father of Seraiah ([[@13006013-13006014|1 Chr 6:13-14]]). Ezra was 'the grandson of Azariah' ([[@15007001|Ezra 7:1]]).

column5: The prophet who encouraged King Asa
column7: The son of Oded, when the Spirit of God came on him, he told King Asa, "The LORD is with you while you are with him" ([[@14015001-14015002|2 Chr 15:1-2]]).

column5: High priest who stood up to King Uzziah
column7: When King Uzziah tried to burn incense in the temple, he went in after him with eighty valiant priests and stopped him ([[@14026017-14026018|2 Chr 26:17-18]]). When leprosy appeared on the king's forehead, he drove him out of the temple ([[@14026020|2 Chr 26:20]]).

column5: Ephraimite leader who urged release of captives
column7: He was the son of Johanan and one of the heads of the children of Ephraim. He stood up against those returning from the war and told them not to bring in the captives taken from Judah ([[@14028012-14028013|2 Chr 28:12-13]]).

column5: High priest in Hezekiah's time
column7: A chief priest of the house of Zadok, he told Hezekiah that the people's offerings had overflowed and there was plenty left over ([[@14031010|2 Chr 31:10]]). He was the one in charge of God's house ([[@14031013|2 Chr 31:13]]).

column5: Son of Maaseiah who repaired the wall
column7: The grandson of Ananiah and the son of Maaseiah, he repaired the wall beside his own house in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003023|Neh 3:23]]).

column5: Priest in Nehemiah's time
column7: He was one of the priests who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010002|Neh 10:2]]; [[@16010008|Neh 10:8]]). His name also appears among those who went in procession on the wall when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated ([[@16012031-16012033|Neh 12:31-33]]).

column5: Man who helped the people understand the law
column7: In Ezra’s time he was one of those who, together with the Levites, helped the people understand the law as they stood in their place ([[@16008007|Neh 8:7]]).

column5: Daniel's friend, called Abednego in Babylon
column7: He was a young man of the children of Judah who was taken to Babylon along with Daniel ([[@27001006|Dan 1:6]]). The prince of the eunuchs changed his name and called him Abednego ([[@27001007|Dan 1:7]]). With Daniel, Hananiah, and Mishael, he refused to defile himself with the king's food, and God gave these four young men knowledge and understanding ([[@27001017|Dan 1:17]]). He was thrown into the burning fiery furnace for not bowing to the golden image Nebuchadnezzar set up, but God sent his angel and rescued him along with his friends ([[@27003028|Dan 3:28]]).

column5: Reubenite, father of Bela
column7: He was of the tribe of Reuben, the grandson of Joel and the son of Shema. His son Bela lived in Aroer and reached as far as Nebo and Baal Meon ([[@13005008|1 Chr 5:8]]).

column5: Levite who played the harp
column7: He was one of the Levites in David’s time who led with harps tuned to the eight-stringed lyre ([[@13015016|1 Chr 15:16]]; [[@13015021|1 Chr 15:21]]).

column5: Father of Hoshea, ruler of Ephraim
column7: He appears in the list of rulers over the tribes in David’s time. His son Hoshea was the ruler of the children of Ephraim ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027020|1 Chr 27:20]]).

column5: Overseer of temple offerings under Hezekiah
column7: In King Hezekiah’s time he was one of the overseers of the offerings brought to the temple, serving under the Levite Conaniah and his brother Shimei ([[@14031012-14031013|2 Chr 31:12-13]]).

column5: Father of Nehemiah who repaired the wall
column7: He was the father of Nehemiah, the ruler of half the district of Beth Zur, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem. This Nehemiah is a different person from Nehemiah the governor ([[@16003016|Neh 3:16]]).

column5: Setting of Joshua's and Goliath's stories
column7: It was a town in the lowland of Judah ([[@6015035|Josh 15:35]]). Joshua struck the five Amorite kings at Gibeon and chased them as far as Azekah and Makkedah ([[@6010010|Josh 10:10]]). As they fled, the LORD threw down great hailstones from the sky on them all the way to Azekah, and more died from the hail than were killed by the sword ([[@6010011|Josh 10:11]]). In Saul's day the Philistines camped between Socoh and Azekah, and Goliath came out from that camp to challenge Israel ([[@9017001-9017004|1 Sam 17:1-4]]).

column5: Descendant of Saul, father of six sons
column7: A descendant of Saul's son Jonathan, he was the son of Eleasah ([[@13008037|1 Chr 8:37]]). He had six sons, including Azrikam ([[@13008038|1 Chr 8:38]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family that returned from exile
column7: The descendants of Azgad who returned from exile in Babylon numbered one thousand two hundred twenty-two, but Nehemiah records two thousand three hundred twenty-two ([[@15002012|Ezra 2:12]]; [[@16007017|Neh 7:17]]). Some of his descendants were also among those who came up with Ezra ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008012|Ezra 8:12]]).

column5: Leader who sealed the covenant
column7: When the people pledged in Nehemiah’s time to keep God’s law, he was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed that covenant ([[@16010014-16010015|Neh 10:14-15]]).

column5: Son of Zattu who had taken a foreign wife
column7: His name appears among the sons of Zattu, among those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010027|Ezra 10:27]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: One of David's mighty men, a Barhumite
column7: He was one of David's mighty men, a Barhumite ([[@10023031|2 Sam 23:31]]). In 1 Chronicles he appears as 'Azmaveth the Baharumite' ([[@13011033|1 Chr 11:33]]).

column5: Descendant of Saul, son of Jehoaddah
column7: A descendant of Saul's son Jonathan, he was the son of Jehoaddah ([[@13008036|1 Chr 8:36]]). In 1 Chronicles 9 he appears as the son of Jarah ([[@13009042|1 Chr 9:42]]).

column5: Father of Jeziel and Pelet, who helped David
column7: He was the father of Jeziel and Pelet, Benjamite warriors who came to help David while he was at Ziklag ([[@13012001-13012003|1 Chr 12:1-3]]).

column5: Keeper of King David’s treasures
column7: He was the son of Adiel and was over the king’s treasures in David’s time. At the same time, Jonathan the son of Uzziah was over the treasures in the fields and cities ([[@13027025|1 Chr 27:25]]).

column5: Place on the southern border of Canaan
column7: It was on the southern border of the land of Canaan, where the border turned from Azmon, passed the brook of Egypt, and ended at the sea ([[@4034004-4034005|Num 34:4-5]]). It also appears on the southern border of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015004|Josh 15:4]]).

column5: Place on Naphtali’s border
column7: It is the place where the border of the children of Naphtali turned westward. From there it went out to Hukkok ([[@6019034|Josh 19:34]]).

column5: Man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: In the genealogy of Jesus in Matthew, he is the son of Eliakim and the father of Zadok ([[@40001013-40001014|Matt 1:13-14]]).

column5: Chief of the half-tribe of Manasseh
column7: He was one of the heads of the half-tribe of Manasseh and was famous for his valor ([[@13005023-13005024|1 Chr 5:23-24]]).

column5: Father of Jeremoth, ruler of Naphtali
column7: He appears in the list of rulers over the tribes in David’s time. His son Jeremoth was the ruler of the tribe of Naphtali ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027019|1 Chr 27:19]]).

column5: Father of Seraiah
column7: He was the father of Seraiah, whom the king sent to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet ([[@24036026|Jer 36:26]]).

column5: Descendant of David’s line, son of Neariah
column7: He appears in the genealogy of David’s royal line as one of the three sons of Neariah: Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam ([[@13003023|1 Chr 3:23]]).

column5: Descendant of Saul, son of Azel
column7: He is the first named of the six sons of Azel, a descendant of Saul's son Jonathan ([[@13008038|1 Chr 8:38]]; [[@13009044|1 Chr 9:44]]).

column5: Levite descended from Merari
column7: A descendant of Merari, he was the grandfather of Shemaiah, a Levite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile ([[@13009014|1 Chr 9:14]]; [[@16011015|Neh 11:15]]).

column5: Ruler of the palace under Ahaz
column7: He was the ruler of the house in the time of Ahaz king of Judah, and he was killed by Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim ([[@14028006-14028007|2 Chr 28:6-7]]).

column5: Mother of King Jehoshaphat
column7: She was the mother of Jehoshaphat, Asa's son who became king of Judah, and the daughter of Shilhi ([[@11022041-11022042|1 Kgs 22:41-42]]; [[@14020031|2 Chr 20:31]]).

column5: Wife of Caleb son of Hezron
column7: The wife of Caleb son of Hezron, she seems to have been the mother of Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon ([[@13002018|1 Chr 2:18]]). After she died, Caleb married Ephrath ([[@13002019|1 Chr 2:19]]).

column5: Father of Paltiel, Issachar’s leader
column7: He was the father of Paltiel, the prince chosen from the tribe of Issachar to divide the land ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034026|Num 34:26]]).

column5: Leader who sealed the covenant
column7: When the people pledged in Nehemiah’s time to keep God’s law, he was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed that covenant ([[@16010014-16010017|Neh 10:14-17]]).

column5: Father of the prophet Hananiah
column7: He was the father of Hananiah, the prophet from Gibeon who spoke to Jeremiah in the LORD’s house in Zedekiah’s time ([[@24028001|Jer 28:1]]).

column5: Father of Jaazaniah, a prince
column7: He was the father of Jaazaniah, one of the princes of the people whom Ezekiel saw in a vision at the east gate of the LORD’s house ([[@26011001|Ezek 11:1]]).

column5: Reubenite, son of Reaiah
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Reuben. He was a descendant of Joel, the grandson of Micah, and the son of Reaiah ([[@13005003-13005005|1 Chr 5:3-5]]).

column5: Son of Jeiel, the father of Gibeon
column7: He was one of the sons of Jeiel, the father of Gibeon who lived in Gibeon, and of his wife Maacah ([[@13008029-13008030|1 Chr 8:29-30]]; [[@13009035-13009036|1 Chr 9:35-36]]).

column5: A king of Edom
column7: He was the son of Achbor and became king of Edom after Shaul died ([[@1036038|Gen 36:38]]). When he died, Hadar became king in his place ([[@1036039|Gen 36:39]]).

column5: Keeper of David’s olive and sycamore trees
column7: He was a Gederite who was over the olive and sycamore trees in the lowland in David’s time. He was one of the officials in charge of King David’s property ([[@13027028|1 Chr 27:28]]).

column5: Where Absalom held his sheep shearing
column7: It was a place beside Ephraim. Absalom held his sheep shearing there and invited all the king’s sons ([[@10013023|2 Sam 13:23]]).

column5: Moabite-area town built by Reuben
column7: It was a town east of the Jordan that the Reubenites built along with Nebo and renamed ([[@4032038|Num 32:38]]). In Joshua it is listed in the land of the tribe of Reuben under the name 'Beth Baal Meon' ([[@6013017|Josh 13:17]]). Later it appears as a town of Moab, and Ezekiel said that Baal Meon, one of the towns that were "the glory of the country," would be handed over to the people of the east ([[@26025009-26025010|Ezek 25:9-10]]). Many scholars think 'Beth Meon' in Jeremiah is the same place ([[@24048023|Jer 48:23]]).

column5: Hometown of a man who brought Elisha bread
column7: A man from this place brought twenty loaves of barley bread from the first fruits, along with fresh grain, to Elisha the man of God ([[@12004042|2 Kgs 4:42]]).

column5: Where Israel formed ranks against Benjamin
column7: When the men of Israel fought the Benjamites, they set themselves in array at Baal Tamar, and the men in ambush broke out of Maareh Geba ([[@7020033|Judg 20:33]]).

column5: The god of the people of Ekron
column7: He was the god of Ekron, whom the sick King Ahaziah sent messengers to inquire of ([[@12001002|2 Kgs 1:2]]). Elijah rebuked them, asking, "Is it because there is no God in Israel" that they went to inquire of him ([[@12001003|2 Kgs 1:3]]).

column5: Place facing Israel's camp by the sea
column7: God had the children of Israel camp by the sea before Pihahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, opposite Baal Zephon ([[@2014002|Exod 14:2]]). The Egyptian army pursued them all the way there ([[@2014009|Exod 14:9]]).

column5: Town in southern Judah
column7: It was one of the southern towns given to the tribe of Judah, listed among the towns near the border of Edom ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015029|Josh 15:29]]).

column5: Mountain on Judah’s northern border
column7: The northern border of Judah passed the north side of Ekron and Shikkeron and reached this mountain ([[@6015011|Josh 15:11]]).

column5: Town of the tribe of Dan
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Dan received by lot as its inheritance, named along with Eltekeh and Gibbethon ([[@6019040|Josh 19:40]]; [[@6019044|Josh 19:44]]).

column5: Town built by Solomon
column7: It was one of the towns that Solomon built, along with Gezer and Lower Beth Horon ([[@11009017-11009018|1 Kgs 9:17-18]]; [[@14008006|2 Chr 8:6]]).

column5: A town in Simeon's southern region
column7: It was a town at the edge of the inheritance the children of Simeon received by their families, also called 'Ramah of the South' ([[@6019008|Josh 19:8]]).

column5: Ammonite king who plotted against Gedaliah
column7: He was king of the children of Ammon, and he sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to take Gedaliah’s life ([[@24040014|Jer 40:14]]).

column5: Solomon’s officer over the Megiddo region
column7: He was the son of Ahilud and one of Solomon’s twelve officers. He was in charge of Taanach, Megiddo, and all Beth Shean ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004012|1 Kgs 4:12]]).

column5: Solomon’s officer over Asher
column7: He was the son of Hushai and one of Solomon’s twelve officers. He was in charge of Asher and Bealoth ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004016|1 Kgs 4:16]]).

column5: Father of Zadok who repaired the wall
column7: He was the father of Zadok, who repaired the wall of Jerusalem in Nehemiah’s time. Zadok worked on the section next to Meremoth and Meshullam ([[@16003004|Neh 3:4]]).

column5: A captain who killed Ishbosheth
column7: He was the son of Rimmon the Beerothite and a captain under Ishbosheth ([[@10004002|2 Sam 4:2]]). He and his brother Rechab killed Ishbosheth, and then David had them put to death ([[@10004006|2 Sam 4:6]]; [[@10004012|2 Sam 4:12]]).

column5: Father of Heleb, one of David's mighty men
column7: A Netophathite, he was the father of Heleb, one of David's mighty men ([[@10023029|2 Sam 23:29]]). In 1 Chronicles the son's name appears as 'Heled' ([[@13011030|1 Chr 11:30]]).

column5: Leader who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the leaders who returned from exile in Babylon with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and others ([[@15002002|Ezra 2:2]]; [[@16007007|Neh 7:7]]).

column5: Leader who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s time ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010027|Neh 10:27]]).

column5: Wife of Shaharaim the Benjamite
column7: She was one of the two wives of Shaharaim, a Benjamite. Shaharaim fathered children in the land of Moab after he had sent away Hushim and Baara ([[@13008008|1 Chr 8:8]]).

column5: Levite ancestor of Asaph
column7: He was an ancestor of Asaph, the Levite who sang in the temple, the father of Michael and the son of Malchijah ([[@13006039-13006040|1 Chr 6:39-40]]).

column5: King of Israel who killed Nadab and reigned
