column7: He was the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, and he killed Nadab king of Israel and became king. He became king over all Israel in Tirzah and reigned twenty-four years ([[@11015027-11015033|1 Kgs 15:27-33]]). He was at war with Asa king of Judah all his days, and he built up Ramah to cut off the way in and out of Judah, but he stopped when Syria attacked ([[@11015016-11015022|1 Kgs 15:16-22]]). Because he walked in the way of Jeroboam, Jehu the son of Hanani brought the word that his house would be swept away ([[@11016001-11016003|1 Kgs 16:1-3]]).

column5: The nation and capital that took Judah captive
column7: It was a great city and kingdom on the Euphrates River in southern Mesopotamia. It is the Babel in the land of Shinar where Nimrod's kingdom began ([[@1010010|Gen 10:10]]). In Nebuchadnezzar's time the Babylonian army burned Jerusalem and the temple and carried the people away captive ([[@12025008-12025011|2 Kgs 25:8-11]]). Jeremiah declared that when seventy years were completed for Babylon, God would bring his people back ([[@24029010|Jer 29:10]]). In Revelation it appears as the name of the great city that opposes God ([[@66018002|Rev 18:2]]).

column5: Village where Shimei cursed David
column7: It was a village on the road from Jerusalem to the Jordan. When Michal was sent back to David, her husband followed her, weeping, as far as Bahurim ([[@10003016|2 Sam 3:16]]). When David fled from Absalom, Shimei son of Gera, of the family of Saul's house, came out here and cursed David ([[@10016005|2 Sam 16:5]]). At the same time, Jonathan and Ahimaaz hid by going down into a well in the courtyard of a man's house in Bahurim ([[@10017018|2 Sam 17:18]]).

column5: Where the Moabites went up to weep
column7: It appears in Isaiah’s prophecy about Moab. He said the people of Moab would go up to Bayith and to the high places of Dibon to weep ([[@23015002|Isa 15:2]]).

column5: Levite who lived in Jerusalem
column7: He was one of the Levites who lived in Jerusalem, and his name appears along with Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah ([[@13009014-13009015|1 Chr 9:14-15]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Bakbuk' ([[@15002051|Ezra 2:51]]; [[@16007053|Neh 7:53]]).

column5: Levite in Jerusalem after the exile
column7: A Levite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile, he was second to Mattaniah, who led the thanksgiving ([[@16011017|Neh 11:17]]). His name also appears among the gatekeepers who guarded the storehouses at the gates ([[@16012025|Neh 12:25]]).

column5: He set out to curse Israel but blessed it
column7: He was the son of Beor, who lived at Pethor by the River ([[@4022005|Num 22:5]]). Balak king of Moab summoned him to curse Israel, but on the way the LORD opened the donkey's mouth to rebuke him ([[@4022028|Num 22:28]]). Instead, Balaam blessed Israel, speaking only the words God gave him. But later he devised the plan that led Israel to sin in the matter of Peor ([[@4031016|Num 31:16]]), and the New Testament speaks of him as one "who loved the wages of wrongdoing" and fell ([[@61002015|2 Pet 2:15]]).

column5: Father of Berodach Baladan, king of Babylon
column7: He was the father of Berodach Baladan, the king of Babylon who sent letters and a present to Hezekiah ([[@12020012|2 Kgs 20:12]]). In Isaiah the son's name appears as 'Merodach-baladan' ([[@23039001|Isa 39:1]]).

column5: Town of the tribe of Simeon
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Simeon received from within the inheritance of the children of Judah ([[@6019001-6019003|Josh 19:1-3]]).

column5: The king of Moab who tried to curse Israel
column7: Balak was the son of Zippor and was king of Moab when Israel was passing through the wilderness ([[@4022004|Num 22:4]]). Afraid after seeing what Israel had done to the Amorites, he summoned Balaam the son of Beor to curse Israel ([[@4022005-4022006|Num 22:5-6]]). But Balaam spoke only the words God gave him and instead blessed Israel three times ([[@4024010|Num 24:10]]). Later Joshua recalled this event as God's deliverance ([[@6024009-6024010|Josh 24:9-10]]).

column5: Stop on Israel's wilderness journey
column7: It was where Israel came after leaving Nahaliel on their journey through the wilderness ([[@4021019|Num 21:19]]). From there they passed through the valley in the field of Moab and reached the top of Pisgah ([[@4021020|Num 21:20]]).

column5: Town given to the tribe of Reuben
column7: One of the towns of the plain of Heshbon, it was in the land Moses gave to the tribe of Reuben ([[@6013015-6013017|Josh 13:15-17]]). Some think it is the same place as 'the high places of Baal' where Balak took Balaam ([[@4022041|Num 22:41]]).

column5: Gadite among David’s mighty men
column7: He was a Gadite whose name is in the list of David’s mighty men. He appears together with Igal the son of Nathan of Zobah ([[@10023036|2 Sam 23:36]]).

column5: Merarite ancestor of Ethan
column7: He was of the sons of Merari, an ancestor of Ethan, who served in the temple. He was the son of Shemer ([[@13006044-13006046|1 Chr 6:44-46]]).

column5: Ancestor of Uthai, of the line of Perez
column7: He was a descendant of Perez, Judah’s son, and an ancestor of Uthai, who returned from exile and lived in Jerusalem ([[@13009002-13009004|1 Chr 9:2-4]]).

column5: A family that returned from exile
column7: Among those who returned from exile, the descendants of Bani numbered six hundred forty-two ([[@15002010|Ezra 2:10]]). There were also descendants of Bani among those who had married foreign women ([[@15010029|Ezra 10:29]]).

column5: Ancestor of men who took foreign wives
column7: Among those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time were 'the sons of Bani' ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Man who had taken a foreign wife
column7: His name is in the list of those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010038|Ezra 10:38]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Father of Rehum who repaired the wall
column7: He was a Levite, the father of Rehum, who repaired a section of the wall of Jerusalem in Nehemiah’s time ([[@16003017|Neh 3:17]]).

column5: A Levite who taught the law
column7: He was a Levite who helped the people understand the law when Ezra read it ([[@16008007|Neh 8:7]]). He stood on the platform and cried out to God ([[@16009004|Neh 9:4]]).

column5: Levite who sealed the covenant
column7: When the people pledged in Nehemiah’s time to keep God’s law, he was one of the Levites who sealed that covenant ([[@16010009|Neh 10:9]]; [[@16010013|Neh 10:13]]).

column5: Leader who sealed the covenant
column7: When the people pledged in Nehemiah’s time to keep God’s law, he was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed that covenant ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]).

column5: Father of Uzzi, overseer of the Levites
column7: He was the son of Hashabiah, of the sons of Asaph, and the father of Uzzi, who became overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem ([[@16011022|Neh 11:22]]).

column5: A ceremony of faith performed with water
column7: Baptism is a ceremony performed with water. When John the Baptist baptized in the Jordan River, many people confessed their sins and were baptized ([[@40003006|Matt 3:6]]). Jesus too was baptized by John, and as he came up from the water, the heavens were opened and the Spirit of God came down on him like a dove ([[@40003016|Matt 3:16]]). The risen Jesus commanded his disciples to make disciples of all nations, "baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit", and to teach them to obey ([[@40028019-40028020|Matt 28:19-20]]). Paul said that baptism shows that we are united with Christ in his death and buried with him, so that we might walk in newness of life ([[@45006004|Rom 6:4]]).

column5: Sorcerer who opposed Paul at Paphos
column7: He was a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet whom they met at Paphos ([[@44013006|Acts 13:6]]). Also called 'Elymas', he opposed Paul and Barnabas to keep the proconsul from believing ([[@44013008|Acts 13:8]]).

column5: The prisoner released in place of Jesus
column7: At each feast the governor customarily released one prisoner, and at that time there was "a notable prisoner" named Barabbas ([[@40027015-40027016|Matt 27:15-16]]). He had been arrested for taking part in an insurrection and committing murder during it ([[@41015007|Mark 15:7]]). When Pilate asked whether to release Barabbas or Jesus, the crowds, persuaded by the chief priests and elders, asked for Barabbas ([[@40027017-40027021|Matt 27:17-21]]). In the end Barabbas was set free, and Jesus was flogged and handed over to be crucified ([[@40027026|Matt 27:26]]).

column5: Father of Elihu
column7: A Buzite of the family of Ram, he was the father of Elihu. When Job's three friends stopped answering, his son Elihu became angry with Job ([[@18032001-18032002|Job 32:1-2]], 6).

column5: Commander who defeated Sisera with Deborah
column7: He was the son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali ([[@7004006|Judg 4:6]]). When the prophet Deborah passed on the LORD's command, he answered, "If you will go with me, then I will go" ([[@7004008|Judg 4:8]]). He led ten thousand men down from Mount Tabor and pursued and defeated Sisera's army, which the LORD had routed ([[@7004015-7004016|Judg 4:15-16]]). Hebrews remembers him as one of the people of faith ([[@58011032|Heb 11:32]]).

column5: Son of Shemaiah, of David’s royal line
column7: He appears in the genealogy of David’s royal line as the grandson of Shecaniah and the son of Shemaiah ([[@13003022|1 Chr 3:22]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Barkos' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]], 53; [[@16007055|Neh 7:55]]).

column5: Levite from Cyprus and Paul's coworker
column7: He was a Levite born in Cyprus whose original name was Joses, and the apostles called him Barnabas. He sold a field and laid the money at the apostles' feet ([[@44004036-44004037|Acts 4:36-37]]). He brought the newly converted Saul to the apostles and introduced him ([[@44009027|Acts 9:27]]), and after he was sent to the church in Antioch, he brought Saul from Tarsus and they taught together ([[@44011022-44011026|Acts 11:22-26]]). Scripture says he was "a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith" ([[@44011024|Acts 11:24]]). The Holy Spirit set Barnabas and Saul apart, and they set out together on a missionary journey.

column5: One of Jesus' twelve disciples
column7: He was one of Jesus' twelve apostles, named alongside Philip ([[@40010003|Matt 10:3]]; [[@42006014|Luke 6:14]]). He was among the disciples gathered in the upper room after the Lord ascended ([[@44001013|Acts 1:13]]).

column5: Blind beggar by the road at Jericho
column7: He was the son of Timaeus, a blind beggar sitting by the road at Jericho. He immediately received his sight when Jesus said to him, "Your faith has made you well" ([[@41010046|Mark 10:46]]; [[@41010052|Mark 10:52]]).

column5: Son of Zabbai who worked hard on the wall
column7: He was the son of Zabbai, and he earnestly repaired the wall from the turning of the wall to the door of the house of Eliashib the high priest ([[@16003020|Neh 3:20]]).

column5: Priest who sealed the covenant
column7: When the people pledged in Nehemiah’s time to keep God’s law, he was one of the priests who sealed that covenant ([[@16010006|Neh 10:6]]; [[@16010008|Neh 10:8]]).

column5: Father of Maaseiah in Jerusalem
column7: He was of the children of Judah, the father of Maaseiah who lived in Jerusalem, and the son of Colhozeh ([[@16011004-16011005|Neh 11:4-5]]).

column5: Scribe who wrote down Jeremiah's words
column7: He was the grandson of Mahseiah and the son of Neriah, a scribe who stood by the prophet Jeremiah and helped him ([[@24032012|Jer 32:12]]). He wrote the LORD's words on a scroll as Jeremiah spoke them, and he read them to the people in the temple in place of Jeremiah, who was shut in ([[@24036004-24036010|Jer 36:4-10]]). When King Jehoiakim burned the scroll, he wrote down Jeremiah's words again ([[@24036032|Jer 36:32]]). After Jerusalem fell, he was taken to Egypt along with Jeremiah ([[@24043006|Jer 43:6]]).

column5: Gileadite who provided for David
column7: He was a man of Rogelim in Gilead, and when David reached Mahanaim while fleeing from Absalom, he brought food and supplies ([[@10017027-10017029|2 Sam 17:27-29]]). He was a very wealthy man of eighty, and he provided for the king while the king stayed at Mahanaim ([[@10019032|2 Sam 19:32]]). David invited him to come with him to Jerusalem, but he declined because of his age and sent Chimham in his place ([[@10019034-10019037|2 Sam 19:34-37]]). Before he died, David told Solomon to show kindness to the sons of Barzillai ([[@11002007|1 Kgs 2:7]]).

column5: Father of Adriel the Meholathite
column7: He was the father of Adriel the Meholathite. The five sons Adriel had by Saul’s daughter Merab were handed over to the Gibeonites in David’s time ([[@10021008-10021009|2 Sam 21:8-9]]).

column5: Solomon’s daughter, wife of Ahimaaz
column7: She was Solomon’s daughter. She became the wife of Ahimaaz, the one of Solomon’s twelve officers who was in charge of Naphtali ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004015|1 Kgs 4:15]]).

column5: A fertile plateau east of the Jordan
column7: Bashan is a broad, fertile land east of the Jordan River, spreading northeast of the Sea of Galilee. Before entering Canaan, Israel struck and defeated Og king of Bashan and his people ([[@5003003|Deut 3:3]]). Og was one of the last of the Rephaim and owned a huge iron bed ([[@5003011|Deut 3:11]]). Moses gave this land to the half-tribe of Manasseh ([[@4032033|Num 32:33]]). Bashan was famous for its good pastureland, and the Psalms speak of "Strong bulls of Bashan" ([[@19022012|Ps 22:12]]).

column5: A bronze basin where priests washed
column7: The basin was a bronze vessel set between the Tent of Meeting and the altar of the tabernacle and filled with water for washing ([[@2030018|Exod 30:18]]). Aaron and his sons had to wash their hands and feet with its water when they went into the Tent of Meeting or came near the altar to minister, so that they would not die ([[@2030019-2030021|Exod 30:19-21]]). The basin and its base were made from the mirrors of the women who ministered at the door of the Tent of Meeting ([[@2038008|Exod 38:8]]). In Solomon's temple there were ten bronze basins, each set on a base ([[@11007038|1 Kgs 7:38]]).

column5: Gate of Heshbon
column7: In the Song of Songs, praising the bride’s eyes, the lover says, "Your eyes are like the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bathrabbim" ([[@22007004|Song 7:4]]).

column5: Wife of Judah, mother of Er, Onan, and Shelah
column7: The daughter of Shua the Canaanite, she was taken by Judah as his wife ([[@1038002|Gen 38:2]]). She bore Judah's sons Er, Onan, and Shelah ([[@13002003|1 Chr 2:3]]).

column5: Wife of Uriah, later mother of Solomon
column7: The daughter of Eliam, she was the wife of Uriah the Hittite ([[@10011003|2 Sam 11:3]]). After David sinned with her and had Uriah killed, the prophet Nathan rebuked his sin, and David repented. Their first child died, and the son she later bore was Solomon ([[@10012024|2 Sam 12:24]]). When David was old, she went to the king with Nathan and saw to it that Solomon would take the throne ([[@11001017|1 Kgs 1:17]]). First Chronicles also calls her 'Bathshua' ([[@13003005|1 Chr 3:5]]).

column5: Wall builder who ruled part of Keilah
column7: He was the son of Henadad, ruled half the district of Keilah, and repaired the wall of Jerusalem ([[@16003018|Neh 3:18]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Bazluth' ([[@15002052|Ezra 2:52]]). In Nehemiah the name appears as 'Bazlith' ([[@16007054|Neh 7:54]]).

column5: Benjamite warrior who helped David at Ziklag
column7: He was one of the Benjamite warriors who came to help David while he was at Ziklag ([[@13012001-13012002|1 Chr 12:1-2]]; [[@13012005|1 Chr 12:5]]).

column5: Temple gate where Peter healed a lame man
column7: One of the gates of the temple in Jerusalem, it was where a man lame from birth begged every day ([[@44003002|Acts 3:2]]). Peter raised him up in the name of Jesus Christ and made him walk ([[@44003006-44003008|Acts 3:6-8]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family that returned from exile
column7: His descendants who returned from exile in Babylon numbered six hundred twenty-three ([[@15002011|Ezra 2:11]]). Descendants of Bebai were also among those who came up with Ezra ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008011|Ezra 8:11]]).

column5: Leader who sealed the covenant
column7: When the people pledged in Nehemiah’s time to keep God’s law, he was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed that covenant ([[@16010014-16010015|Neh 10:14-15]]).

column5: Son of Benjamin
column7: A son of Benjamin, he is on the list of those who went down to Egypt with Jacob ([[@1046021|Gen 46:21]]). His sons were heads of their fathers' houses and mighty men of valor ([[@13007008-13007009|1 Chr 7:8-9]]).

column5: Ancestor of the Becherite family of Ephraim
column7: When the children of Israel were counted in the wilderness, he appears among the sons of Ephraim as the ancestor of 'the family of the Becherites' ([[@4026035|Num 26:35]]).

column5: Ancestor of King Saul
column7: He was a Benjamite, the great-grandfather of Kish, Saul’s father. He appears in the genealogy as the son of Aphiah ([[@9009001|1 Sam 9:1]]).

column5: Father of Hadad, king of Edom
column7: He was the father of Hadad, king of Edom. Hadad was the one who struck Midian in the field of Moab ([[@1036035|Gen 36:35]]; [[@13001046|1 Chr 1:46]]).

column5: Manassite, son of Ulam
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Manasseh. He was the son of Ulam and a descendant of Gilead, the son of Machir ([[@13007017|1 Chr 7:17]]).

column5: Son of Bani who had taken a foreign wife
column7: He was one of the sons of Bani who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010034-15010035|Ezra 10:34-35]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Well where the LORD gave water
column7: It was a place Israel reached on the wilderness journey. It is the well where the LORD said to Moses, "Gather the people together, and I will give them water" ([[@4021016|Num 21:16]]).

column5: Place in the prophecy against Moab
column7: Isaiah prophesied that the cry of Moab would go all around its borders and its wailing would reach Beer Elim ([[@23015008|Isa 15:8]]).

column5: Spring where Hagar met the angel of the LORD
column6: the well of him that liveth and seeth me
column7: It was the well Hagar named after she met the angel of the LORD, and it lay between Kadesh and Bered ([[@1016007-1016014|Gen 16:7-14]]). Later Isaac lived near it ([[@1025011|Gen 25:11]]).

column5: Asherite, son of Zophah
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Asher as one of the sons of Zophah, the son of Helem ([[@13007035-13007037|1 Chr 7:35-37]]).

column5: Reubenite prince taken captive by Assyria
column7: He was a prince of the Reubenites and the son of Baal. He was carried away captive by Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria ([[@13005005-13005006|1 Chr 5:5-6]]).

column5: Father of Judith, Esau’s wife
column7: He was a Hittite, the father of Judith, whom Esau married when he was forty years old. This marriage grieved Isaac and Rebekah ([[@1026034-1026035|Gen 26:34-35]]).

column5: Father of the prophet Hosea
column7: He was the father of the prophet Hosea. The LORD’s word came to his son Hosea in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah ([[@28001001|Hos 1:1]]).

column5: Gibeonite town in the land of Benjamin
column7: It was one of the four Gibeonite cities that Israel reached three days after making a covenant with the Gibeonites ([[@6009016-6009017|Josh 9:16-17]]). It later became a city of the tribe of Benjamin ([[@6018025|Josh 18:25]]). The Beerothites are said to have fled to Gittaim long before and lived there ([[@10004003|2 Sam 4:3]]). Rechab and Baanah, who killed Saul's son Ishbosheth, were sons of Rimmon the Beerothite ([[@10004005-10004007|2 Sam 4:5-7]]).

column5: The patriarchs' town at Israel's southern edge
column6: the well of an oath; the seventh well
column7: This place was called Beersheba because Abraham and Abimelech swore an oath to each other over a well ([[@1021031|Gen 21:31]]). Abraham planted a tamarisk tree there and called on the name of the LORD, the Everlasting God ([[@1021033|Gen 21:33]]). Isaac also found a well here and gave it that name again ([[@1026032-1026033|Gen 26:32-33]]). Because it was the southern edge of the land of Israel, 'from Dan to Beersheba' came to mean all Israel ([[@7020001|Judg 20:1]]).

column5: The first king of Edom
column7: He was the son of Beor and reigned as king of Edom before Israel had a king, and the name of his city was Dinhabah ([[@1036032|Gen 36:32]]; [[@13001043|1 Chr 1:43]]).

column5: Firstborn son of Benjamin
column7: He was the firstborn son of Benjamin ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]). When Jacob's family went down to Egypt, his name is listed first among the sons of Benjamin ([[@1046021|Gen 46:21]]). The family of the Belaites came from him, and his sons Ard and Naaman each became the head of a family as well ([[@4026038-4026040|Num 26:38-40]]). Chronicles records that Bela's five sons were all heads of families and mighty men of valor ([[@13007007|1 Chr 7:7]]).

column5: Reubenite who lived in Aroer
column7: He was of the tribe of Reuben and the son of Azaz. He lived in Aroer, and his territory reached as far as Nebo and Baal Meon ([[@13005008|1 Chr 5:8]]).

column5: Babylonian king judged by the writing on the wall
column7: He was a king of Babylon who held a great feast for a thousand of his lords. While drinking wine, he had the gold and silver vessels brought that Nebuchadnezzar, called his father, had taken from the temple in Jerusalem, and they drank from them ([[@27005001-27005002|Dan 5:1-2]]). Then the fingers of a man's hand appeared and wrote on the wall, and Daniel explained that it meant God had brought the king's kingdom to an end ([[@27005005-27005026|Dan 5:5-26]]). That very night Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed ([[@27005030|Dan 5:30]]).

column5: Levite appointed in David’s time
column7: He was one of the Levite brothers appointed in David’s time to serve in the rank after Heman, Asaph, and Ethan ([[@13015017-13015018|1 Chr 15:17-18]]).

column5: Officer who was Solomon’s son-in-law
column7: He was one of Solomon’s twelve officers and was in charge of the height of Dor. He married Solomon’s daughter Taphath ([[@11004011|1 Kgs 4:11]]).

column5: Ancestor of the Ammonites
column7: He was the son born to Lot’s younger daughter. The Bible records that he became the father of the children of Ammon to this day ([[@1019038|Gen 19:38]]).

column5: Officer of Solomon
column7: He was one of Solomon’s twelve officers and was in charge of Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh, and Elon Beth Hanan ([[@11004009|1 Kgs 4:9]]).

column5: Solomon’s officer at Ramoth Gilead
column7: He was Solomon’s officer in Ramoth Gilead, in charge of all the towns of Jair and the region of Argob in Bashan ([[@11004013|1 Kgs 4:13]]).

column5: King of Syria in King Asa's time
column7: He was a king of Syria who lived in Damascus, the grandson of Hezion and the son of Tabrimmon ([[@11015018|1 Kgs 15:18]]). When Baasha king of Israel built Ramah to block Judah, Asa king of Judah sent him silver and gold from the treasuries of the temple and the palace and asked him to break his treaty with Baasha ([[@11015019|1 Kgs 15:19]]). Ben Hadad listened and attacked the cities of Israel, including Ijon, Dan, and the land of Naphtali ([[@11015020|1 Kgs 15:20]]). Hanani the seer rebuked Asa for relying on the king of Syria instead of the LORD ([[@14016007|2 Chr 16:7]]). Scholars differ on whether he is the same person as the Ben Hadad of Ahab's time.

column5: King of Syria in Elisha's time
column7: A king of Syria in Elisha's time, he gathered all his army and besieged Samaria ([[@12006024|2 Kgs 6:24]]). When he fell sick, he sent Hazael to Elisha to ask whether he would recover ([[@12008007-12008009|2 Kgs 8:7-9]]).

column5: Son of Hazael, king of Syria
column7: He was the son of Hazael king of Syria and became king after his father ([[@12013024|2 Kgs 13:24]]). Joash king of Israel defeated him three times and recovered the towns ([[@12013025|2 Kgs 13:25]]).

column5: Prince who taught in the towns of Judah
column7: He was one of the princes King Jehoshaphat sent in the third year of his reign to teach in the cities of Judah ([[@14017007|2 Chr 17:7]]).

column5: Son of Shimon in Judah’s genealogy
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah as one of the sons of Shimon: Amnon, Rinnah, Ben Hanan, and Tilon ([[@13004020|1 Chr 4:20]]).

column5: Solomon’s officer over Arubboth
column7: He was one of Solomon’s twelve officers and was in charge of Arubboth, Socoh, and all the land of Hepher ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004010|1 Kgs 4:10]]).

column5: Solomon’s officer over Ephraim’s hill country
column7: He was one of Solomon’s twelve officers, in charge of the hill country of Ephraim, and he provided food for the royal household one month each year ([[@11004007-11004008|1 Kgs 4:7-8]]).

column5: Son of Ishi in Judah’s genealogy
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah. The sons of Ishi are recorded as Zoheth and Ben Zoheth ([[@13004020|1 Chr 4:20]]).

column5: Son of Jehoiada, warrior for David and Solomon
column7: He was the son of Jehoiada and one of David's famous mighty men. He killed the two sons of Ariel of Moab, and he went down into a pit on a snowy day and killed a lion ([[@10023020|2 Sam 23:20]]). Under David he was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites ([[@10008018|2 Sam 8:18]]). When Adonijah tried to become king, he did not follow him but stood on Solomon's side ([[@11001008|1 Kgs 1:8]]). Solomon made him commander of the army in place of Joab ([[@11002035|1 Kgs 2:35]]).

column5: Pirathonite, one of David's mighty men
column7: A Pirathonite, he was one of David's mighty men ([[@10023030|2 Sam 23:30]]). From the tribe of Ephraim, he became the captain for the eleventh month, with twenty-four thousand men in his division ([[@13027014|1 Chr 27:14]]).

column5: Chief of the Simeonites
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the tribe of Simeon. In Hezekiah’s time these men went and settled where there was pasture for their flocks ([[@13004036|1 Chr 4:36]]; [[@13004041|1 Chr 4:41]]).

column5: A Levite musician when the ark was moved
column7: He was one of the Levites David appointed when he moved the ark of God, and he played the harp ([[@13015018-13015020|1 Chr 15:18-20]]). He served before the ark together with Asaph ([[@13016005|1 Chr 16:5]]).

column5: Father of Jehoiada
column7: He was the father of Jehoiada, who together with Abiathar came after Ahithophel in David’s time ([[@13027033-13027034|1 Chr 27:33-34]]).

column5: Grandfather of Jahaziel the Levite
column7: He was the grandfather of Jahaziel, a Levite of the sons of Asaph. The LORD’s Spirit came on Jahaziel in the middle of the assembly ([[@14020014|2 Chr 20:14]]).

column5: Overseer of temple offerings under Hezekiah
column7: In King Hezekiah’s time he was one of the overseers of the offerings brought to the temple, serving under Conaniah and his brother Shimei ([[@14031012-14031013|2 Chr 31:12-13]]).

column5: Son of Parosh who had taken a foreign wife
column7: He appears among the sons of Parosh, among those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010025|Ezra 10:25]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Son of Pahathmoab who had taken a foreign wife
column7: He appears among the sons of Pahathmoab, among those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010030|Ezra 10:30]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Son of Bani who had taken a foreign wife
column7: He appears among the sons of Bani, among those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010034-15010035|Ezra 10:34-35]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Son of Nebo who had taken a foreign wife
column7: His name appears among the sons of Nebo, among those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010043-15010044|Ezra 10:43-44]]).

column5: Father of the prince Pelatiah
column7: He was the father of Pelatiah, a prince of the people whom Ezekiel saw at the east gate of the temple ([[@26011001|Ezek 11:1]]). While Ezekiel was prophesying, his son Pelatiah died ([[@26011013|Ezek 11:13]]).

column5: Town of the tribe of Dan
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Dan received by lot as its inheritance, named along with Jehud and Gath Rimmon ([[@6019040|Josh 19:40]]; [[@6019045|Josh 19:45]]).

column5: A campsite on the wilderness journey
column7: It was where Israel camped after leaving Moseroth as they passed through the wilderness ([[@4033031-4033032|Num 33:31-32]]). Deuteronomy records that they traveled from 'Beeroth Bene Jaakan' to Moserah ([[@5010006|Deut 10:6]]).

column5: Levite who sealed the covenant
column7: When the people pledged in Nehemiah’s time to keep God’s law, he was one of the Levites who sealed that covenant ([[@16010009|Neh 10:9]]; [[@16010013|Neh 10:13]]).

column5: The youngest son of Jacob and Rachel
column7: He was the youngest of Jacob's twelve sons. His mother Rachel, dying after giving birth to him, called him 'Benoni', but Scripture records that "his father named him Benjamin" ([[@1035018|Gen 35:18]]). As Joseph's younger brother by the same mother, he was especially dear to Joseph ([[@1043029|Gen 43:29]]). From his descendants, the tribe of Benjamin, came King Saul and the apostle Paul ([[@9009001|1 Sam 9:1]]; [[@50003005|Phil 3:5]]).

column5: Benjamite, son of Bilhan
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin as the grandson of Jediael and the son of Bilhan ([[@13007006|1 Chr 7:6]]; [[@13007010|1 Chr 7:10]]).

column5: Son of Harim who had taken a foreign wife
column7: He appears among the sons of Harim, among those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010031-15010032|Ezra 10:31-32]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Man who repaired the wall across from his house
column7: In Nehemiah’s time he and Hasshub repaired the wall across from their house. He was one of those who rebuilt the wall of Jerusalem ([[@16003023|Neh 3:23]]).

column5: Man in the wall-dedication procession
column7: His name is among the company that went in procession on the wall when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated ([[@16012031-16012034|Neh 12:31-34]]).

column5: A gate of Jerusalem
column7: When Jeremiah reached this gate, he was seized by Irijah, a captain of the guard ([[@24037013|Jer 37:13]]). While King Zedekiah was sitting in this gate, Ebedmelech came out and spoke to him about Jeremiah ([[@24038007-24038008|Jer 38:7-8]]).

column5: Gate of Jerusalem
column7: In Zechariah’s prophecy, Jerusalem will be lifted up and will dwell in her place, "from Benjamin’s gate to the place of the first gate, to the corner gate" ([[@38014010|Zech 14:10]]).

column5: Levite descended from Merari
column7: A descendant of Merari the Levite, he was the son of Jaaziah ([[@13024026|1 Chr 24:26]]). He appears in the list of the divisions of the Levites made in David's time ([[@13024027|1 Chr 24:27]]).

column5: Father of Bela, king of Edom
column7: He was the father of Bela, who appears as the first king of Edom. Bela's city was Dinhabah ([[@1036032|Gen 36:32]]; [[@13001043|1 Chr 1:43]]).

column5: Father of Balaam
column7: He was the father of Balaam. Balak king of Moab sent messengers to "Balaam the son of Beor" to have him curse Israel ([[@4022004-4022005|Num 22:4-5]]). Deuteronomy says Balaam was from Pethor of Mesopotamia ([[@5023004|Deut 23:4]]). Balaam was later killed with the sword along with the five kings of Midian ([[@4031008|Num 31:8]]). 2 Peter warns that false teachers have gone astray, "having followed the way of Balaam the son of Beor" ([[@61002015|2 Pet 2:15]]).

column5: King of Sodom in Abram’s time
column7: He was king of Sodom in Abram’s time, and together with Birsha king of Gomorrah and others he fought the alliance led by Chedorlaomer ([[@1014002|Gen 14:2]]; [[@1014009|Gen 14:9]]).

column5: Benjamite warrior who helped David at Ziklag
column7: He was one of the Benjamite warriors who came to help David while he was at Ziklag ([[@13012002-13012003|1 Chr 12:2-3]]).

column5: Benjamite, son of Shimei
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin as one of the sons of Shimei: Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath ([[@13008021|1 Chr 8:21]]).

column5: A town where Paul preached the word
column7: This is where the brothers of Thessalonica sent Paul and Silas away by night, and the Jews of Thessalonica followed them there, stirring up the crowds ([[@44017010|Acts 17:10]]; [[@44017013|Acts 17:13]]). Paul’s companion Sopater came from here ([[@44020004|Acts 20:4]]).

column5: Son of Zerubbabel
column7: He appears in the genealogy of David’s royal line. His name is listed among the sons of Zerubbabel ([[@13003019-13003020|1 Chr 3:19-20]]).

column5: Father of Asaph the singer
column7: He was the son of Shimea and the father of Asaph, who served at Heman’s right hand ([[@13006039|1 Chr 6:39]]). He is also named as Asaph’s father in the list of singers the Levites appointed ([[@13015017|1 Chr 15:17]]). A Berechiah who kept the door for the ark also appears, but it is not clear whether he is the same man ([[@13015023|1 Chr 15:23]]).

column5: Levite in the villages of the Netophathites
column7: He was the son of Asa and grandson of Elkanah, a Levite who lived in the villages of the Netophathites ([[@13009014|1 Chr 9:14]]; [[@13009016|1 Chr 9:16]]).

column5: Ephraimite leader who urged release of captives
column7: He was the son of Meshillemoth and one of the heads of the children of Ephraim. He stood against bringing in the captives taken from Judah ([[@14028012-14028013|2 Chr 28:12-13]]).

column5: Father of Meshullam, who repaired the wall
column7: He was the son of Meshezabel and the father of Meshullam, who repaired the wall in Nehemiah’s day ([[@16003004|Neh 3:4]]). Tobiah’s son Jehohanan married his granddaughter, Meshullam’s daughter ([[@16006018|Neh 6:18]]).

column5: Father of the prophet Zechariah
column7: He was the father of the prophet Zechariah and the son of Iddo. In the second year of King Darius, the LORD's word came to his son Zechariah ([[@38001001|Zech 1:1]], 7).

column5: Place near Beer Lahai Roi
column7: Beer Lahai Roi, the well where Hagar met the angel of the LORD, was between Kadesh and Bered ([[@1016014|Gen 16:14]]).

column5: Descendant of Ephraim
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Ephraim as the son of Shuthelah, Ephraim’s son. His son was Tahath ([[@13007020|1 Chr 7:20]]).

column5: Asherite, son of Zophah
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Asher as one of the sons of Zophah, the son of Helem ([[@13007035-13007036|1 Chr 7:35-36]]).

column5: A son of Asher
column7: He was a son of Asher ([[@1046017|Gen 46:17]]). From him came the family of the Berites, and families also came from his sons Heber and Malchiel ([[@4026044-4026045|Num 26:44-45]]).

column5: Son of Ephraim born after a disaster
column7: He was a son born to Ephraim after Ephraim’s sons were killed by the men of Gath. He was named Beriah because trouble had come on the house ([[@13007021-13007023|1 Chr 7:21-23]]).

column5: Benjamite head of the people of Aijalon
column7: A Benjamite, he and Shema became heads of the inhabitants of Aijalon and drove out the inhabitants of Gath ([[@13008013|1 Chr 8:13]]). Michael, Ishpah, and Joha were his sons ([[@13008016|1 Chr 8:16]]).

column5: Son of Shimei, a Gershonite
column7: He was a son of Shimei, a Levite descended from Gershon ([[@13023010|1 Chr 23:10]]). Because he did not have many sons, he was counted as one family with Jeush ([[@13023011|1 Chr 23:11]]).

column5: A woman who came with King Agrippa
column7: She came to Caesarea with King Agrippa and greeted Festus ([[@44025013|Acts 25:13]]). The next day she entered the place of hearing with great pomp and listened to Paul ([[@44025023|Acts 25:23]]; [[@44026030|Acts 26:30]]).

column5: A city of Hadadezer
column7: This city of Hadadezer is called Berothai here, and from it and from Betah King David took a great quantity of bronze ([[@10008008|2 Sam 8:8]]). Some think it is the same place as the Berothah on the border of the land Ezekiel saw ([[@26047016|Ezek 47:16]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Besai' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]], 49; [[@16007052|Neh 7:52]]).

column5: Father of Meshullam, who repaired the old gate
column7: He was the father of Meshullam, who repaired the old gate with Joiada the son of Paseah in Nehemiah’s time ([[@16003006|Neh 3:6]]).

column5: The brook where two hundred of David’s men stayed
column7: When David pursued the Amalekites, two hundred men too faint to cross this brook stayed behind, and David went on with four hundred ([[@9030009-9030010|1 Sam 30:9-10]]). When he came back, he shared the plunder with those who had stayed as well ([[@9030021-9030024|1 Sam 30:21-24]]).

column5: City of Hadadezer where David took bronze
column7: It was a city of Hadadezer king of Zobah. After David struck Hadadezer, he took a great quantity of bronze from Betah and Berothai ([[@10008003|2 Sam 8:3]]; [[@10008008|2 Sam 8:8]]).

column5: Town of the tribe of Asher
column7: It was one of the towns within the border the tribe of Asher received by lot ([[@6019024-6019025|Josh 19:24-25]]).

column5: Fortified city of Naphtali
column7: It was one of the cities the children of Naphtali received ([[@6019032|Josh 19:32]]; [[@6019038|Josh 19:38]]). Naphtali did not drive out the people of Beth Anath but put them to forced labor ([[@7001033|Judg 1:33]]).

column5: Town in Judah’s hill country
column7: It was one of the towns in the hill country given to the tribe of Judah, named along with Maarath and Eltekon ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015059|Josh 15:59]]).

column5: A town on the border of Judah and Benjamin
column7: It was a place on the northern border of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015006|Josh 15:6]]). It is listed both as a town in the wilderness of Judah and as a town of the tribe of Benjamin ([[@6015061|Josh 15:61]]; [[@6018022|Josh 18:22]]).

column5: Place destroyed by Shalman
column7: Hosea said Israel’s fortresses would be destroyed "as Shalman destroyed Beth Arbel in the day of battle" ([[@28010014|Hos 10:14]]).

column5: Linen-working family of Judah
column7: Among the descendants of Shelah, Judah’s son, were "the families of the house of those who worked fine linen, of the house of Ashbea" ([[@13004021|1 Chr 4:21]]).

column5: Philistine temple where Saul’s armor was kept
column7: The Philistines put Saul’s armor "in the house of the Ashtaroth" after his death and fastened his body to the wall of Beth Shan ([[@9031010|1 Sam 31:10]]).

column5: Place near Bethel and Ai
column7: It was a place in the land of Benjamin, beside Ai on the east side of Bethel ([[@6007002|Josh 7:2]]). The northern border of the tribe of Benjamin reached 'the wilderness of Beth Aven' ([[@6018012|Josh 18:12]]). In Saul's day the Philistines camped at Michmash, east of Beth Aven, to fight against Israel ([[@9013005|1 Sam 13:5]]). Many think that Beth Aven in Hosea is a scornful name for Bethel, where idols were worshiped ([[@28004015|Hos 4:15]]).

column5: Hometown of some who returned from exile
column7: Forty-two men of Beth Azmaveth came back from exile in Babylon ([[@16007028|Neh 7:28]]). In Ezra they are listed as 'the children of Azmaveth' ([[@15002024|Ezra 2:24]]).

column5: Place where Gideon stationed men to intercept the Midianites.
column7: House of crossing, a place south of the scene of Gideon’s victory ([[@7007024|Judg. 7:24]]). It was probably the chief ford of the Jordan in that district, and may have been that by which Jacob crossed when he returned from Mesopotamia, near the Jabbok ([[@1032022|Gen. 32:22]]), and at which Jephthah slew the Ephraimites ([[@7012004|Judg. 12:4]]).

column5: Town of the Simeonites
column7: It was one of the towns where the children of Simeon lived, and it belonged to them until David’s reign ([[@13004028|1 Chr 4:28]]; [[@13004031|1 Chr 4:31]]).

column5: Where Israel chased the Philistines
column7: The men of Israel went out of Mizpah, pursued the Philistines, and struck them until they came below Beth Kar ([[@9007011|1 Sam 7:11]]).

column5: Town in Judah’s lowland
column7: It was one of the towns in the lowland given to the tribe of Judah, named along with Gederoth and Naamah ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]; [[@6015041|Josh 15:41]]).

column5: Place on Asher’s border
column7: It is the place the border of the children of Asher reached when it turned toward the sunrise ([[@6019024|Josh 19:24]]; [[@6019027|Josh 19:27]]).

column5: Syrian land in Amos’s judgment prophecy
column7: When the LORD pronounced judgment on Damascus, he said he would cut off "him who holds the scepter from the house of Eden". He said the people of Syria would go into captivity ([[@30001005|Amos 1:5]]).

column5: Where Jehu killed Ahaziah's relatives
column7: It was a place Jehu reached on his way to Samaria ([[@12010012|2 Kgs 10:12]]). There, by the pit, he killed forty-two of the brothers of Ahaziah king of Judah ([[@12010013-12010014|2 Kgs 10:13-14]]).

column5: Place on Asher’s border
column7: It was one of the places the border of the children of Asher reached after passing the valley of Iphtah El ([[@6019024|Josh 19:24]]; [[@6019027|Josh 19:27]]).

column5: Place in Micah’s prophecy
column7: Speaking of the coming judgment, Micah said, "The wailing of Beth Ezel will take from you his protection" ([[@33001011|Mic 1:11]]).

column5: Place whose 'father' was Hareph
column7: It is a name in the genealogy of Caleb’s descendants. Hareph, a son of Hur, is recorded as 'the father of Beth Gader' ([[@13002050-13002051|1 Chr 2:50-51]]).

column5: Town on the plain of Moab
column7: It was one of the towns Jeremiah named when he said judgment had come on the plain country of Moab ([[@24048021-24048023|Jer 48:21-23]]).

column5: A district of Judah
column7: In Nehemiah's time it was the district ruled by Malchijah the son of Rechab ([[@16003014|Neh 3:14]]). Warning of disaster coming from the north, Jeremiah said to raise a signal here ([[@24006001|Jer 6:1]]).

column5: Road by which Ahaziah fled
column7: Ahaziah king of Judah, fleeing from Jehu, "fled by the way of the garden house", and Jehu pursued and struck him, and Ahaziah died at Megiddo ([[@12009027|2 Kgs 9:27]]).

column5: Gadite town east of the Jordan
column7: It was a fortified town built by the children of Gad ([[@4032036|Num 32:36]]). In Joshua it appears as 'Beth Haram', a town in the valley east of the Jordan ([[@6013027|Josh 13:27]]).

column5: A town on the border of Judah and Benjamin
column7: The northern border of the tribe of Judah passed by here ([[@6015005-6015006|Josh 15:5-6]]). It was one of the cities the tribe of Benjamin received according to their families ([[@6018021|Josh 18:21]]).

column5: A town paired with Upper Beth Horon
column7: It was a town paired with Upper Beth Horon, and 1 Chronicles says that Sheerah, the daughter of Ephraim, built Lower and Upper Beth Horon ([[@13007024|1 Chr 7:24]]). After defeating the Amorite kings at Gibeon, Joshua chased them along the slopes of Beth Horon, and the LORD hurled down great hailstones on them ([[@6010010-6010011|Josh 10:10-11]]). The border of the land given to the children of Joseph passed Lower Beth Horon and reached Gezer ([[@6016001-6016003|Josh 16:1-3]]). Later Solomon built Gezer and Lower Beth Horon ([[@11009017|1 Kgs 9:17]]).

column5: Town on Ephraim’s border
column7: It was where the border of the inheritance of the children of Ephraim reached on the east ([[@6016005|Josh 16:5]]). Solomon built Upper Beth Horon into a fortified city ([[@14008005|2 Chr 8:5]]).

column5: A town on the plains of Moab
column7: It was one end of the area where Israel camped on the plains of Moab by the Jordan ([[@4033049|Num 33:49]]). It became part of the share of the children of Reuben ([[@6013020|Josh 13:20]]).

column5: Town of the tribe of Simeon
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Simeon received from within the inheritance of the children of Judah ([[@6019001|Josh 19:1]]; [[@6019006|Josh 19:6]]).

column5: Where David stopped as he fled
column7: When Absalom rebelled and the king went out, all the people followed him, and they stopped at Beth Merhak ([[@10015017|2 Sam 15:17]]).

column5: Home of the house of Millo in Shechem
column7: The men of Shechem gathered together with the house of Millo and made Abimelech king ([[@7009006|Judg 9:6]]). Jotham said that Abimelech and they would devour one another with fire ([[@7009020|Judg 9:20]]).

column5: A town of the tribe of Gad east of the Jordan
column7: It was one of the fortified cities the children of Gad built, and it is also called 'Nimrah' ([[@4032003|Num 32:3]]; [[@4032034-4032036|Num 32:34-36]]). This town in the valley east of the Jordan became part of the tribe of Gad’s share ([[@6013024-6013027|Josh 13:24-27]]).

column5: Town of the tribe of Issachar
column7: It was one of the towns the children of Issachar received by lot, named along with Remeth, Engannim, and En Haddah ([[@6019017|Josh 19:17]]; [[@6019021|Josh 19:21]]).

column5: Town in southern Judah
column7: It was a southern town given to the tribe of Judah ([[@6015027|Josh 15:27]]). Descendants of Judah who returned from exile lived here ([[@16011026|Neh 11:26]]).

column5: The place facing Moses' burial site
column7: It was a place in the land of Moab east of the Jordan, and Moses was buried "in the valley in the land of Moab opposite Beth Peor" ([[@5034006|Deut 34:6]]).

column5: Son of Eshton in Judah’s genealogy
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah as a son of Eshton. These are said to be the men of Recah ([[@13004011-13004012|1 Chr 4:11-12]]).

column5: Land of the Syrians who fought David
column7: The Ammonites hired the Syrians of this place to fight against David ([[@10010006|2 Sam 10:6]]). Laish, which the tribe of Dan took, was in the valley near it ([[@7018028|Judg 18:28]]).

column5: Town where Saul's body was hung
column7: It was a town west of the Jordan that lay within Issachar's land but belonged to Manasseh ([[@6017011|Josh 17:11]]). The Canaanites there had chariots of iron, and Manasseh did not drive out its inhabitants ([[@6017016|Josh 17:16]]; [[@7001027|Judg 1:27]]). After Saul and his sons died, the Philistines fastened their bodies to the wall of Beth Shan ([[@9031010|1 Sam 31:10]]). The valiant men of Jabesh Gilead went all night and brought the bodies back ([[@9031012|1 Sam 31:12]]).

column5: Priests' town where the ark came back
column7: It was a town on the northern border of Judah, one of the towns given to the priests ([[@6021016|Josh 21:16]]). When the Philistines sent the ark of the covenant back on a cart, the cows went straight along the road to Beth Shemesh, and the people reaping wheat in the valley saw the ark and rejoiced ([[@9006012-9006013|1 Sam 6:12-13]]). But when people who looked into the ark were struck dead, they were afraid and said, "Who is able to stand before the LORD, this holy God?" ([[@9006020|1 Sam 6:20]]). Later Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah here ([[@12014013|2 Kgs 14:13]]).

column5: Town on Issachar’s border
column7: It is a place the border of the children of Issachar reached, along with Tabor and Shahazumah ([[@6019017|Josh 19:17]]; [[@6019022|Josh 19:22]]).

column5: Fortified city of Naphtali
column7: It was one of the cities the children of Naphtali received ([[@6019032|Josh 19:32]]; [[@6019038|Josh 19:38]]). Naphtali did not drive out the people of Beth Shemesh but put them to forced labor ([[@7001033|Judg 1:33]]).

column5: Where the Midianite army fled
column7: When Gideon’s three hundred blew their trumpets, the enemy turned on one another and fled as far as Beth Shittah toward Zererah ([[@7007022|Judg 7:22]]).

column5: Town in Judah’s hill country
column7: It was one of the towns in the hill country given to the tribe of Judah, named along with Janim and Aphekah ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015053|Josh 15:53]]).

column5: People who traded horses and mules with Tyre
column7: The house of Togarmah traded with Tyre in horses, war horses, and mules ([[@26027014|Ezek 27:14]]). Ezekiel said they would come with Gog from 'the uttermost parts of the north' ([[@26038006|Ezek 38:6]]).

column5: A town of Judah built by Rehoboam
column7: It was a town in the hill country of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015058|Josh 15:58]]). Rehoboam built this city ([[@14011007|2 Chr 11:7]]).

column5: Village where Martha, Mary, and Lazarus lived
column7: A village about fifteen stadia from Jerusalem, it was where Mary, Martha, and Lazarus lived ([[@43011001|John 11:1]]; [[@43011018|John 11:18]]). Jesus raised the dead Lazarus here, and when he came again six days before the Passover, Mary poured very costly ointment on his feet and wiped his feet with her hair ([[@43012001-43012003|John 12:1-3]]). The risen Jesus led his disciples out as far as Bethany, lifted up his hands and blessed them, and was carried up into heaven ([[@42024050-42024051|Luke 24:50-51]]).

column5: The place where Jacob met God
column7: It was a city north of Jerusalem, and its original name was Luz ([[@1028019|Gen 28:19]]). Abram built an altar on the mountain east of Bethel ([[@1012008|Gen 12:8]]). Jacob had a dream here and said, "This is none other than God’s house, and this is the gate of heaven" and he named the place Bethel ([[@1028017-1028019|Gen 28:17-19]]). After the kingdom split, Jeroboam set up a golden calf here, and it became a center of idol worship ([[@11012029|1 Kgs 12:29]]).

column5: Bethel in the south of Judah
column7: It was one of the places David sent some of the plunder to when he came to Ziklag ([[@9030026-9030027|1 Sam 30:26-27]]). Some think it is the same place as 'Bethul' in Joshua ([[@6019004|Josh 19:4]]).

column5: Mountain in the Song of Songs
column7: In the Song of Songs the beloved is called to "be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether" ([[@22002017|Song 2:17]]).

column5: Pool where Jesus healed a sick man
column7: It was a pool by the sheep gate in Jerusalem, with five porches. There Jesus healed a man who had been sick for thirty-eight years ([[@43005002|John 5:2]]; [[@43005005-43005009|John 5:5-9]]).

column5: Judah's town where David and Jesus were born
column7: Bethlehem is a small town in the hill country of Judah, and its old name was Ephrath. Rachel, Jacob's wife, died on the way there and was buried ([[@1035019|Gen 35:19]]). It is where the story of Ruth and Naomi took place, and because it was David's hometown, Samuel anointed David here at Jesse's house ([[@9016001|1 Sam 16:1]], 13). The prophet Micah foretold that a ruler of Israel would come from Bethlehem ([[@33005002|Mic 5:2]]). Just as this word said, Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea ([[@40002001|Matt 2:1]]).

column5: Town of the tribe of Zebulun
column7: This is a different place from Bethlehem in Judah, one of the towns the children of Zebulun received ([[@6019010|Josh 19:10]]; [[@6019015|Josh 19:15]]).

column5: A village near the Mount of Olives
column7: When Jesus came near Jerusalem and reached Bethsphage at the Mount of Olives, he sent two disciples ahead ([[@40021001|Matt 21:1]]). It was close to Bethany ([[@41011001|Mark 11:1]]).

column5: Hometown of Peter, Andrew, and Philip
column7: It was a town by the Sea of Galilee, and Philip, Andrew, and Peter were from here ([[@43001044|John 1:44]]). Jesus took the apostles to a town called Bethsaida, and in a deserted place nearby he fed five thousand people ([[@42009010-42009017|Luke 9:10-17]]). At Bethsaida he laid his hands on the eyes of a blind man and made him see clearly ([[@41008022-41008025|Mark 8:22-25]]). But because the town did not repent even after seeing many mighty works, Jesus rebuked it, saying, "Woe to you, Bethsaida!" ([[@40011021|Matt 11:21]]).

column5: Father of Rebekah and Laban
column7: He was one of the eight sons born to Nahor, Abraham's brother, and his wife Milcah, and he became the father of Rebekah ([[@1022022-1022023|Gen 22:22-23]]). When Rebekah met Abraham's servant, she introduced herself as "the daughter of Bethuel the son of Milcah, whom she bore to Nahor" ([[@1024024|Gen 24:24]]). When the servant asked for Rebekah as a wife for Isaac, Laban and Bethuel answered, "The thing proceeds from the LORD" ([[@1024050|Gen 24:50]]). Later Isaac sent his son Jacob to Paddan Aram, to the house of his mother's father Bethuel, to find a wife ([[@1028002|Gen 28:2]]).

column5: Town in the land of Gad
column7: It is named in the border of the land Moses gave to the tribe of Gad, which reached from Heshbon to Ramath Mizpeh and Betonim ([[@6013024-6013026|Josh 13:24-26]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family that returned from exile
column7: Those who returned with Zerubbabel included 'the children of Bezai', 323 in all ([[@15002017|Ezra 2:17]]). In Nehemiah the number is given as 324 ([[@16007023|Neh 7:23]]).

column5: Leader who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s time ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010018|Neh 10:18]]).

column5: Craftsman from Judah who made the tabernacle
column7: He was the grandson of Hur and the son of Uri, of the tribe of Judah, and God called him by name for the work of making the tabernacle ([[@2031002|Exod 31:2]]). God filled him with the Spirit of God and gave him skill to work in gold, silver, and bronze, to cut stones, and to carve wood, and appointed Oholiab of the tribe of Dan to work with him ([[@2031003-2031006|Exod 31:3-6]]). Bezalel made the ark of acacia wood ([[@2037001|Exod 37:1]]), and he made all that the LORD commanded Moses ([[@2038022|Exod 38:22]]).

column5: Son of Pahathmoab who had taken a foreign wife
column7: He appears among the sons of Pahathmoab, among those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010030|Ezra 10:30]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Place where Judah struck the Canaanites
column7: Here Judah struck down ten thousand Canaanites and Perizzites ([[@7001004|Judg 1:4]]). There they found Adoni-Bezek, fought against him, and defeated him ([[@7001005|Judg 1:5]]).

column5: Where Saul counted his troops
column7: When Saul counted his troops at Bezek, the children of Israel were three hundred thousand and the men of Judah thirty thousand ([[@9011008|1 Sam 11:8]]).

column5: A city of refuge of the tribe of Reuben
column7: It was a city of refuge of the tribe of Reuben, in the wilderness on the plain ([[@5004043|Deut 4:43]]; [[@6020008|Josh 20:8]]). It was also given to the Levites ([[@6021036|Josh 21:36]]).

column5: Asherite, son of Zophah
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Asher as one of the sons of Zophah, the son of Helem ([[@13007035-13007037|1 Chr 7:35-37]]).

column5: Father of Sheba, who rebelled against David
column7: He was a Benjamite, the father of Sheba, who rebelled against David. Sheba blew the trumpet and cried, "We have no portion in David," and the men of Israel left David to follow him, but the men of Judah stayed with their king ([[@10020001-10020002|2 Sam 20:1-2]]). David sent Abishai after him, saying, "Now Sheba the son of Bichri will do us more harm than Absalom did" ([[@10020006|2 Sam 20:6]]). In the end, following the advice of a wise woman in the town where Sheba had gone, the people cut off Sheba's head and threw it out to Joab ([[@10020021-10020022|2 Sam 20:21-22]]).

column5: Jehu’s captain
column7: He was Jehu’s captain. Jehu told him to throw Joram’s body into the field of Naboth the Jezreelite ([[@12009024-12009025|2 Kgs 9:24-25]]).

column5: One of King Ahasuerus’ seven eunuchs
column7: He was one of the seven eunuchs serving in the king’s presence whom King Ahasuerus ordered to bring Queen Vashti ([[@17001010-17001011|Esth 1:10-11]]).

column5: Eunuch who plotted against King Ahasuerus
column7: One of King Ahasuerus' eunuchs who guarded the door, he plotted with Teresh to kill the king ([[@17002021|Esth 2:21]]). Mordecai's report of the plot was written down in the book of the chronicles ([[@17006002|Esth 6:2]]).

column5: Leader who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the leaders of the people of Israel who returned from exile in Babylon with Zerubbabel and Jeshua ([[@15002002|Ezra 2:2]]; [[@16007007|Neh 7:7]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family that returned from exile
column7: The descendants of Bigvai who came back from exile in Babylon numbered 2,056, though Nehemiah records 2,067 ([[@15002014|Ezra 2:14]]; [[@16007019|Neh 7:19]]). Seventy of his descendants were also among those who came up with Ezra ([[@15008014|Ezra 8:14]]).

column5: Leader who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s time ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010016|Neh 10:16]]).

column5: One of Job's three friends
column7: He was a Shuhite, one of the three friends who came to sympathize with Job and comfort him ([[@18002011|Job 2:11]]). He spoke back and forth with Job several times ([[@18008001|Job 8:1]]; [[@18018001|Job 18:1]]).

column5: Fifteenth priestly division
column7: When the priestly divisions were assigned by lot in David’s time, he was the one chosen fifteenth ([[@13024005|1 Chr 24:5]]; [[@13024014|1 Chr 24:14]]).

column5: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the priests who came back with Zerubbabel and Jeshua ([[@16012001|Neh 12:1]]; [[@16012005|Neh 12:5]]). In the days of Joiakim, the head of Bilgah’s family was Shammua ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012018|Neh 12:18]]).

column5: Rachel's servant, mother of Dan and Naphtali
column7: She was the servant whom Laban gave to his daughter Rachel as her maid ([[@1029029|Gen 29:29]]). Because Rachel could not bear children, she gave Bilhah to Jacob as a wife, and Rachel named the two sons Bilhah bore Dan and Naphtali ([[@1030001-1030008|Gen 30:1-8]]). Later Reuben slept with Bilhah, his father's concubine, and his father Israel heard about it ([[@1035022|Gen 35:22]]). In his final blessing Jacob rebuked Reuben for this, saying, "you went up to your father’s bed, then defiled it" ([[@1049004|Gen 49:4]]).

column5: Town of the Simeonites
column7: It was one of the towns where the children of Simeon lived, named along with Beersheba and Moladah. It belonged to them until David’s reign ([[@13004028-13004029|1 Chr 4:28-29]]; [[@13004031|1 Chr 4:31]]).

column5: Son of Ezer the Horite
column7: He was a son of Ezer, a Horite descended from Seir in the land of Edom. Ezer was one of the chiefs of the Horites ([[@1036021|Gen 36:21]], 27; [[@13001042|1 Chr 1:42]]).

column5: Leader who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the leaders of the people of Israel who returned from exile in Babylon with Zerubbabel and Jeshua ([[@15002002|Ezra 2:2]]; [[@16007007|Neh 7:7]]).

column5: Asherite, son of Japhlet
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Asher as one of the sons of Japhlet, the son of Heber ([[@13007032-13007033|1 Chr 7:32-33]]).

column5: Descendant of Saul, son of Moza
column7: He was the son of Moza, a descendant of Saul and Jonathan ([[@13008036-13008037|1 Chr 8:36-37]]). The same name appears in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles 9 ([[@13009043|1 Chr 9:43]]).

column5: Father of Noadiah the Levite
column7: He was the father of Noadiah, a Levite who was present when the silver, gold, and vessels were weighed in the temple in Ezra’s time ([[@15008033|Ezra 8:33]]).

column5: Son of Pahathmoab who had taken a foreign wife
column7: He appears among the sons of Pahathmoab, among those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010030|Ezra 10:30]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Man who had taken a foreign wife
column7: His name is in the list of those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010038|Ezra 10:38]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Son of Henadad who repaired the wall
column7: He was the son of Henadad, and he repaired the wall from the house of Azariah to the turning of the wall and on to the corner ([[@16003024|Neh 3:24]]).

column5: King of Gomorrah in Abram’s time
column7: He was king of Gomorrah in Abram’s time, and together with Bera king of Sodom and others he fought the alliance led by Chedorlaomer ([[@1014002|Gen 14:2]]; [[@1014009|Gen 14:9]]).

column5: Name whose 'father' was Malchiel the Asherite
column7: Malchiel, son of Beriah the son of Asher, appears in the genealogy as 'the father of Birzaith' ([[@13007030-13007031|1 Chr 7:30-31]]).

column5: Man who wrote to King Artaxerxes
column7: In the days of Artaxerxes, he wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia together with Mithredath, Tabeel, and their companions ([[@15004007|Ezra 4:7]]).

column5: An office of overseeing and caring for the church
column7: Bishop means 'one who watches over and cares for', and in the New Testament it refers to the office of overseeing and caring for the church. Paul called the elders of the church in Ephesus and told them that the Holy Spirit had made them overseers to shepherd the church of God, which he bought with his own blood ([[@44020017|Acts 20:17]], 28). An overseer had to be without reproach, the husband of one wife, temperate, and good at teaching ([[@54003001-54003002|1 Tim 3:1-2]]). Peter called Jesus the "Shepherd and Overseer of your souls" ([[@60002025|1 Pet 2:25]]).

column5: Pharaoh’s daughter whom Mered married
column7: She was the daughter of Pharaoh whom Mered of the tribe of Judah married, and her sons appear in the genealogy ([[@13004017-13004018|1 Chr 4:17-18]]).

column5: Region Abner passed through
column7: Abner and his men marched all night, crossed the Jordan, went through all Bithron, and came to Mahanaim ([[@10002029|2 Sam 2:29]]).

column5: Region in northern Asia Minor
column7: Paul and his companions tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit did not allow them ([[@44016007|Acts 16:7]]). First Peter was also written to the foreigners scattered in this region ([[@60001001|1 Pet 1:1]]).

column5: Town in southern Judah
column7: It was one of the southern towns given to the tribe of Judah, named along with Hazar Shual and Beersheba ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015028|Josh 15:28]]).

column5: One of King Ahasuerus’ seven eunuchs
column7: He was one of the seven eunuchs serving in the king’s presence whom King Ahasuerus ordered to bring Queen Vashti ([[@17001010-17001011|Esth 1:10-11]]).

column5: King Herod’s personal aide
column7: He was King Herod’s personal aide. The people of Tyre and Sidon made him their friend and asked for peace with the king ([[@44012020|Acts 12:20]]).

column5: Prominent man of Bethlehem who married Ruth
column7: He was a relative of Naomi's husband Elimelech and a man of standing in Bethlehem ([[@8002001|Ruth 2:1]]). He treated Ruth, the Moabite woman who came to glean grain, with kindness and blessed her, saying, "May the LORD repay your work, and a full reward be given to you from the LORD, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge" ([[@8002012|Ruth 2:12]]). As the kinsman-redeemer, he bought Elimelech's property before the elders at the city gate and took Ruth as his wife ([[@8004009-8004013|Ruth 4:9-13]]). Their son Obed became David's grandfather, and Boaz is also listed in Jesus' genealogy ([[@40001005|Matt 1:5]]).

column5: Descendant of Saul, son of Azel
column7: He was one of the six sons of Azel, a descendant of Saul and Jonathan. His brothers were Azrikam, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan ([[@13008038|1 Chr 8:38]]; [[@13009044|1 Chr 9:44]]).

column5: Namesake of the boundary marker 'the stone of Bohan'
column7: A descendant of Reuben, his name appears in 'the stone of Bohan', which marked the border between Judah and Benjamin ([[@6015006|Josh 15:6]]; [[@6018017|Josh 18:17]]).

column5: Place to which David sent plunder
column7: It was one of the places to which David sent plunder after returning to Ziklag ([[@9030026|1 Sam 30:26]]; [[@9030030|1 Sam 30:30]]).

column5: Rocky crag Jonathan passed
column7: It was the name of one of the rocky crags on either side of the pass by which Jonathan sought to cross over to the Philistine garrison ([[@9014004|1 Sam 14:4]]).

column5: Town in the lowland of Judah
column7: It was a town given to the tribe of Judah ([[@6015039|Josh 15:39]]). Jedidah, the mother of King Josiah, was the daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath ([[@12022001|2 Kgs 22:1]]).

column5: Important city of Edom
column7: It was an important city of Edom. Among the early kings of Edom, Jobab was the son of Zerah of Bozrah ([[@1036033|Gen 36:33]]). The prophets named Bozrah when they spoke of judgment on Edom: Isaiah said the LORD has a sacrifice in Bozrah ([[@23034006|Isa 34:6]]), and Jeremiah said Bozrah would become a waste forever ([[@24049013|Jer 49:13]]). Isaiah 63 also says, "Who is this who comes from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?" ([[@23063001|Isa 63:1]]).

column5: Bread baked from grain flour; food
column7: In the Bible, bread is food baked from grain flour, and more broadly the word can mean food in general. Melchizedek brought out bread and wine to meet Abram, and on the night of the Passover Israel ate unleavened bread, bread made without yeast ([[@1014018|Gen 14:18]]; [[@2012008|Exod 12:8]]). God fed Israel with manna in the wilderness to teach them "that man does not live by bread only, but man lives by every word that proceeds out of the LORD’s mouth" ([[@5008003|Deut 8:3]]). Jesus said, "I am the bread of life", and at the Last Supper he broke bread, gave it to his disciples, and said, "this is my body" ([[@43006035|John 6:35]]; [[@40026026|Matt 26:26]]).

column5: A section of the wall of Jerusalem
column7: It was a section of the wall of Jerusalem. In Nehemiah's time Hananiah the perfumer and others repaired Jerusalem as far as 'the wide wall' ([[@16003008|Neh 3:8]]).

column5: A stream on the southwest border of the Promised Land
column7: It was the brook that the southern border of Israel's land passed through; the border turned from Azmon, went past the brook of Egypt, and ended at the sea ([[@4034005|Num 34:5]]). The southern border of the tribe of Judah's land also reached the brook of Egypt and ended at the sea ([[@6015004|Josh 15:4]]). When Solomon held the feast, all Israel gathered "from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of Egypt", which marks the southern edge of the nation ([[@11008065|1 Kgs 8:65]]). Isaiah prophesied that the LORD would gather the children of Israel one by one, from the Euphrates to the brook of Egypt ([[@23027012|Isa 27:12]]). Scholars differ on exactly which stream it was.

column5: Brook in Amos’s prophecy
column7: Amos said the nation the LORD would raise up would afflict Israel "from the entrance of Hamath to the brook of the Arabah" ([[@30006014|Amos 6:14]]).

column5: Brook the Moabites would cross
column7: Isaiah prophesied that the people of Moab would carry the wealth they had gained and stored up across the brook of the willows ([[@23015007|Isa 15:7]]).

column5: Danite leader who divided the land
column7: He was the son of Jogli, the prince chosen from the tribe of Dan to divide the land ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034022|Num 34:22]]).

column5: Descendant of Aaron, father of Uzzi
column7: A descendant of Aaron, he was the son of Abishua and the father of Uzzi ([[@13006005|1 Chr 6:5]], 51). He was also an ancestor of Ezra the scribe ([[@15007004|Ezra 7:4]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a singer
column7: He was a son of Heman, who served as a singer in David's time ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]). The sixth lot fell to him, and he served with his sons and brothers, twelve in all ([[@13025013|1 Chr 25:13]]).

column5: Son of Jerahmeel
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah as one of the sons of Jerahmeel, Hezron’s firstborn ([[@13002025|1 Chr 2:25]]).

column5: Levite who cried out from the stairs
column7: He was one of the Levites who stood up on the stairs and cried with a loud voice to the LORD their God ([[@16009004|Neh 9:4]]).

column5: Leader who sealed the covenant
column7: When the people pledged in Nehemiah’s time to keep God’s law, he was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed that covenant ([[@16010014-16010015|Neh 10:14-15]]).

column5: Ancestor of Shemaiah the Levite
column7: He was an ancestor of Shemaiah, a Levite who lived in Jerusalem. Shemaiah was the son of Hasshub and the great-great-grandson of Bunni ([[@16011015|Neh 11:15]]).

column5: Sacrifice in which the whole offering was burned
column7: A burnt offering was a sacrifice in which the whole offering was burned on the altar and given to God. After the flood Noah built an altar and offered burnt offerings ([[@1008020|Gen 8:20]]). Abraham was told to offer Isaac as a burnt offering in the land of Moriah, but in place of his son he offered the ram God had provided ([[@1022002-1022013|Gen 22:2-13]]). Under the law a burnt offering was a male without defect, and the priest burned all of it as "a pleasant aroma to the LORD" ([[@3001003-3001009|Lev 1:3-9]]). The fire on the altar had to be kept burning without going out ([[@3006013|Lev 6:13]]).

column5: Son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother
column7: He was a son born to Abraham’s brother Nahor by Milcah, and the younger brother of Uz, the firstborn ([[@1022020-1022021|Gen 22:20-21]]).

column5: Ancestor of Abihail the Gadite
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Gad. He is recorded as the seventh-generation ancestor of Abihail, a Gadite who lived in the land of Bashan ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005014|1 Chr 5:14]]).

column5: Place that would drink the cup of wrath
column7: When Jeremiah listed the nations that would drink the cup of the LORD’s wrath, Buz appears along with Dedan and Tema ([[@24025017|Jer 25:17]]; [[@24025023|Jer 25:23]]).

column5: Father of the prophet Ezekiel
column7: He was the father of Ezekiel the priest. The LORD’s word came to Ezekiel in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar ([[@26001003|Ezek 1:3]]).

column5: The clan of Elihu
column7: This was the clan of young Elihu, who spoke to Job. Elihu was the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram ([[@18032002|Job 32:2]], 6).

column5: Town in Judah’s lowland
column7: It was one of the towns in the lowland given to the tribe of Judah, named along with Lahmam and Chitlish ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]; [[@6015040|Josh 15:40]]).

column5: Place on Asher’s border
column7: It is a place named in describing the border of the tribe of Asher. The border passed Beth Emek and Neiel and went out to Cabul on the left ([[@6019024|Josh 19:24]]; [[@6019027|Josh 19:27]]).

column5: Name Hiram gave to some towns
column7: Solomon gave Hiram king of Tyre twenty cities in the land of Galilee, but they did not please Hiram, so he called them 'the land of Cabul' ([[@11009011-11009013|1 Kgs 9:11-13]]).

column5: Mediterranean city of the Roman governor
column7: It was a large port city on the Mediterranean coast, named after the Roman emperor Caesar, and the Roman governor lived there. The centurion Cornelius lived there, and when Peter preached in his house, the Holy Spirit came on the Gentiles too ([[@44010001|Acts 10:1]], 44-45). Philip the evangelist also lived there ([[@44021008|Acts 21:8]]). Paul stood trial before the governor there and was kept in custody for two years ([[@44023033|Acts 23:33]]; [[@44024027|Acts 24:27]]).

column5: Where Peter confessed Jesus as the Christ
column7: In this region Jesus asked his disciples, 'Who do men say that I, the Son of Man, am?' ([[@40016013|Matt 16:13]]). Peter answered, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God" ([[@40016016|Matt 16:16]]).

column5: The high priest who questioned Jesus
column7: He was high priest in the year Jesus was crucified, and he was the son-in-law of Annas ([[@43018013|John 18:13]]). The chief priests and the elders of the people gathered "in the court of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas" and plotted to seize Jesus by deceit and kill him ([[@40026003-40026004|Matt 26:3-4]]). He said it was better for one man to die for the people, and John's Gospel says this was a prophecy that Jesus would die for the nation ([[@43011049-43011052|John 11:49-52]]). After Jesus was arrested, he was led to Caiaphas the high priest and questioned ([[@40026057|Matt 26:57]]).

column5: Adam and Eve's firstborn, who killed Abel
column7: The firstborn son of Adam and Eve, he worked the ground ([[@1004001-1004002|Gen 4:1-2]]). He brought an offering from the fruit of the ground, but when it was not accepted, he grew angry and killed his brother Abel in the field ([[@1004008|Gen 4:8]]). When asked where his brother was, he answered, "Am I my brother’s keeper?" ([[@1004009|Gen 4:9]]). God put a mark on him so that no one would kill him, and he lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden. The First Letter of John teaches us not to be like Cain ([[@62003012|1 John 3:12]]).

column5: Son of Arphaxad in Luke’s genealogy
column7: In the genealogy of Jesus recorded in Luke, he appears as the father of Shelah and the son of Arphaxad ([[@42003035-42003036|Luke 3:35-36]]). This name does not appear in the Old Testament genealogies.

column5: Assyrian city from Nimrod's time
column7: It was a city that Nimrod built after going into Assyria, along with Nineveh and Rehoboth Ir ([[@1010011|Gen 10:11]]). Resen lay between Nineveh and "the great city Calah" ([[@1010012|Gen 10:12]]).

column5: Wise man compared with Solomon
column7: His name appears along with Ethan, Heman, and Darda when the Bible describes how great Solomon’s wisdom was. Solomon was wiser than they, and his fame spread to all the nations around ([[@11004031|1 Kgs 4:31]]).

column5: Grandson of Judah, son of Zerah
column7: He was one of the five sons of Zerah, Judah’s son, and the brother of Zimri, Ethan, Heman, and Dara ([[@13002004|1 Chr 2:4]]; [[@13002006|1 Chr 2:6]]).

column5: Son of Jephunneh, the spy who kept faith
column7: He was the son of Jephunneh from the tribe of Judah, one of the twelve men Moses sent to spy out Canaan ([[@4013006|Num 13:6]]). The other spies were afraid, but Caleb said, "Let’s go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it!" ([[@4013030|Num 13:30]]). God said that because Caleb "has followed me fully," he would bring him into the land ([[@4014024|Num 14:24]]). Even at eighty-five he was still strong, and he received Hebron from Joshua as his inheritance ([[@6014010-6014014|Josh 14:10-14]]).

column5: Son of Hezron, a descendant of Judah
column7: He was a descendant of Judah and the son of Hezron, and by his wife Azubah he became the father of Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon ([[@13002018|1 Chr 2:18]]). 'Chelubai,' listed as a son of Hezron in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles, is also thought to refer to this Caleb ([[@13002009|1 Chr 2:9]]). After Azubah died, he married Ephrath, who bore him Hur ([[@13002019|1 Chr 2:19]]). This Hur's grandson was Bezalel, who made the tabernacle ([[@13002020|1 Chr 2:20]]). Scholars differ on whether he is the same man as Caleb the son of Jephunneh.

column5: Place where Hezron died
column7: It is where Hezron, the son of Perez, died. After Hezron died, his wife Abijah bore Ashhur, who was the father of Tekoa ([[@13002005|1 Chr 2:5]]; [[@13002024|1 Chr 2:24]]).

column5: A city in Nimrod's kingdom
column7: It was one of the cities in the land of Shinar where Nimrod's kingdom began ([[@1010010|Gen 10:10]]). Amos also mentioned Calneh ([[@30006002|Amos 6:2]]).

column5: An animal for carrying loads on long journeys
column7: The camel was used to carry loads on long journeys. Abraham's servant took ten of his master's camels and went to the city of Nahor, and there Rebekah said she would draw water for the servant's camels too until they had drunk their fill ([[@1024010|Gen 24:10]], 19). Under the law, the camel was unclean, because it chews the cud but does not have a parted hoof ([[@3011004|Lev 11:4]]). John the Baptist wore clothing made of camel's hair, and Jesus said, "it is easier for a camel to go through a needle’s eye than for a rich man to enter into God’s Kingdom" ([[@40003004|Matt 3:4]]; [[@40019024|Matt 19:24]]).

column5: Son of Ham, ancestor of the Canaanites
column7: He was the fourth son of Ham, the son of Noah ([[@1010006|Gen 10:6]]). After Ham saw his father Noah's nakedness and told his brothers, Noah said, "Canaan is cursed. He will be a servant of servants to his brothers" ([[@1009022-1009025|Gen 9:22-25]]). Canaan became the father of Sidon, his firstborn, and Heth, and he was the ancestor of many peoples such as the Jebusites, the Amorites, and the Hivites ([[@1010015-1010018|Gen 10:15-18]]). The land where his descendants spread out was called the border of the Canaanites ([[@1010019|Gen 10:19]]).

column5: The land west of the Jordan that God promised
column7: It is the land stretching from west of the Jordan River to the sea. It got its name because the descendants of Canaan, son of Ham, spread out and lived in this land ([[@1010018|Gen 10:18]]). God promised Abram, "I will give this land to your offspring" ([[@1012007|Gen 12:7]]), and Scripture calls it 'a land flowing with milk and honey' ([[@2003008|Exod 3:8]]). In Joshua's time Israel entered this land, and each tribe received its share as an inheritance ([[@6014001|Josh 14:1]]).

column5: Mother of Shaul, the son of Simeon
column7: She was the woman who bore Shaul, the son of Simeon. The Bible gives no name and calls her only 'a Canaanite woman' ([[@1046010|Gen 46:10]]; [[@2006015|Exod 6:15]]).

column5: Center of Jesus' ministry in Galilee
column7: It was a town by the Sea of Galilee in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali, and it does not appear in the Old Testament. Jesus left Nazareth and went to live there ([[@40004013|Matt 4:13]]). He taught in its synagogue on the Sabbath ([[@41001021|Mark 1:21]]) and did many things there, such as healing a centurion's servant ([[@40008005|Matt 8:5]]). But when its people did not repent even after seeing many mighty works, Jesus rebuked it, saying, "You, Capernaum, who are exalted to heaven, you will go down to Hades" ([[@40011023|Matt 11:23]]).

column5: The place the Philistines came from
column7: It was the place where the Philistines first lived and came out from; God said he had brought up "the Philistines from Caphtor" ([[@30009007|Amos 9:7]]). The Caphtorim, who came out of Caphtor, destroyed the Avvim, who lived in villages as far as Gaza, and lived in their land ([[@5002023|Deut 2:23]]). Jeremiah called it 'the isle of Caphtor' and prophesied that the Philistines left there would also perish ([[@24047004|Jer 47:4]]). Scholars differ on exactly where it was; some see it as the Mediterranean island of Crete, and others as a land near Egypt.

column5: Descendants of Mizraim
column7: They were one of the peoples descended from Mizraim ([[@1010013-1010014|Gen 10:13-14]]). The Caphtorim, who came out of Caphtor, destroyed the Avvim who lived in villages as far as Gaza and settled in their place ([[@5002023|Deut 2:23]]).

column5: Region in eastern Asia Minor
column7: In Acts, people from this region were among those gathered in Jerusalem at Pentecost ([[@44002009|Acts 2:9]]). First Peter was also written to the foreigners scattered in this region ([[@60001001|1 Pet 1:1]]).

column5: A city by the Euphrates River
column7: When Neco king of Egypt went up to fight against Carchemish by the Euphrates, Josiah went out to stop him ([[@14035020|2 Chr 35:20]]). Later the army of Pharaoh Necoh was defeated here by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon ([[@24046002|Jer 46:2]]).

column5: Eunuch of King Ahasuerus
