column7: He was one of the seven eunuchs who served in King Ahasuerus’ presence. On the seventh day of the feast, the king sent them to bring Queen Vashti ([[@17001010-17001011|Esth 1:10-11]]).

column5: Town in Judah where Nabal and Abigail lived
column7: It was a town in the hill country of Judah, near Maon and Ziph ([[@6015055|Josh 15:55]]). After striking the Amalekites, Saul came to Carmel and set up a monument for himself ([[@9015012|1 Sam 15:12]]). When Nabal, a rich man of Maon, was shearing his sheep in Carmel, David sent young men to greet him, but Nabal turned them away ([[@9025002-9025011|1 Sam 25:2-11]]). After Nabal died, his wife Abigail became David's wife ([[@9025042|1 Sam 25:42]]). It is a different place from Mount Carmel, where Elijah faced the prophets of Baal.

column5: The mountain where Elijah faced the prophets of Baal
column7: It was the mountain where Elijah had the prophets of Baal and Asherah gathered ([[@11018019-11018020|1 Kgs 18:19-20]]). Elijah went up to the top of Carmel and bowed down to pray ([[@11018042|1 Kgs 18:42]]).

column5: A son of Reuben
column7: He was a son of Reuben and one of the heads of Reuben's families ([[@1046009|Gen 46:9]]; [[@2006014|Exod 6:14]]). From him came the family of the Carmites ([[@4026006|Num 26:6]]).

column5: Father of Achan
column7: He was the son of Zabdi of the tribe of Judah and the father of Achan, who took some of the devoted things ([[@6007001|Josh 7:1]]; [[@6007018|Josh 7:18]]). In 1 Chronicles his son is called 'Achar' ([[@13002007|1 Chr 2:7]]).

column5: Man of Troas where Paul left his cloak
column7: Paul had left his cloak at Troas with Carpus. So he asked Timothy to bring the cloak when he came, along with the books, especially the parchments ([[@55004013|2 Tim 4:13]]).

column5: One of King Ahasuerus’ seven princes
column7: He was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who were close to the king and sat first in the kingdom. The king asked them what to do about Queen Vashti ([[@17001013-17001015|Esth 1:13-15]]).

column5: Descendants of Mizraim, ancestors of the Philistines
column7: They were descendants of Mizraim, and the Philistines came from the Casluhim ([[@1010013-1010014|Gen 10:13-14]]; [[@13001012|1 Chr 1:12]]).

column5: Small island Paul’s ship passed
column7: The ship carrying Paul was driven along by a stormy wind called Euroclydon, and it ran "under the lee of a small island called Clauda". There, with difficulty, they were able to secure the boat ([[@44027014-44027016|Acts 27:14-16]]).

column5: A port town near Corinth
column7: Paul had his hair cut here because of a vow when he set sail for Syria ([[@44018018|Acts 18:18]]). Phoebe, the sister Paul commended, was a servant of the church at Cenchreae ([[@45016001|Rom 16:1]]).

column5: A Roman army officer over a hundred soldiers
column7: A centurion was an officer in the Roman army who commanded a hundred soldiers. A centurion in Capernaum pleaded for his servant, who was paralyzed and tormented, saying, "Just say the word", and Jesus said he had not found so great a faith in anyone in Israel ([[@40008005-40008010|Matt 8:5-10]]). When Jesus died on the cross, the centurion and those with him who were watching Jesus confessed, "Truly this was the Son of God!" ([[@40027054|Matt 27:54]]). Cornelius, a centurion in Caesarea, was a devout man who feared God with all his household and gave many gifts to the needy ([[@44010001-44010002|Acts 10:1-2]]).

column5: Southern Babylonia, Abraham's homeland
column7: It is the region of southern Babylonia along the lower Euphrates River. Abraham's hometown, "Ur of the Chaldees", was here ([[@1011028|Gen 11:28]]). Later the Chaldeans ruled Babylon, so Chaldea became a name for Babylon itself ([[@23013019|Isa 13:19]]). The army that besieged and destroyed Jerusalem was also called the Chaldeans ([[@12025004|2 Kgs 25:4]]). The book of Daniel tells of Chaldean astrologers summoned to interpret the king's dream ([[@27002002|Dan 2:2]]).

column5: A horse-drawn cart used in war
column7: A chariot was a cart pulled by horses, used mainly in war. Pharaoh honored Joseph by having him ride in his second chariot, and at Jacob's burial, chariots and horsemen also went up with Joseph ([[@1041043|Gen 41:43]]; [[@1050009|Gen 50:9]]). Pharaoh chased Israel with six hundred chosen chariots and all the chariots of Egypt, but God cast Pharaoh's chariots and army into the sea ([[@2014007|Exod 14:7]]; [[@2015004|Exod 15:4]]). The psalmist sang, "Some trust in chariots, and some in horses, but we trust in the name of the LORD our God" ([[@19020007|Ps 20:7]]).

column5: The river where Ezekiel saw visions of God
column7: It was a river in the land of the Chaldeans, that is, Babylon ([[@26001003|Ezek 1:3]]). The captives from Judah lived by this river, and Ezekiel was among them when the heavens were opened and he saw visions of God ([[@26001001|Ezek 1:1]]). Ezekiel came to the captives at Tel Aviv who lived by the river Chebar and stayed among them seven days ([[@26003015|Ezek 3:15]]). Later he said he realized that the cherubim he saw in a vision were the living creatures he had seen by the river Chebar ([[@26010020|Ezek 10:20]]). Scholars differ on exactly which waterway it was.

column5: The king of Elam who attacked Sodom
column7: He was king of Elam, and Sodom and four other kings served him for twelve years and then rebelled ([[@1014001-1014004|Gen 14:1-4]]). After that he came out with his allied kings and struck many peoples ([[@1014005|Gen 14:5]]).

column5: Man who took a foreign wife in Ezra’s time
column7: He was one of the sons of Pahathmoab in the list of those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010030|Ezra 10:30]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Brother of Shuhah in Judah’s genealogy
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah as the brother of Shuhah. Chelub became the father of Mehir, and Mehir was the father of Eshton ([[@13004011|1 Chr 4:11]]).

column5: Father of Ezri, over the farm workers
column7: He was the father of Ezri, who was over the field workers in King David’s time. Ezri was one of those in charge of King David’s property ([[@13027026|1 Chr 27:26]]; [[@13027031|1 Chr 27:31]]).

column5: Son of Bani who took a foreign wife in Ezra’s time
column7: His name appears among the sons of Bani in the list of those who had taken foreign wives in Ezra’s time ([[@15010034-15010035|Ezra 10:34-35]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Father of the false prophet Zedekiah
column7: He was the father of the prophet Zedekiah. His son made horns of iron to predict a false victory and struck Micaiah on the cheek ([[@11022011|1 Kgs 22:11]]; [[@11022024|1 Kgs 22:24]]).

column5: Benjamite, son of Bilhan
column7: He was the grandson of Jediael, Benjamin’s son, and the son of Bilhan. His brothers included Jeush, Ehud, and Zethan ([[@13007006|1 Chr 7:6]]; [[@13007010|1 Chr 7:10]]).

column5: Levite who cried out from the stairs in Nehemiah’s time
column7: On the day in Nehemiah’s time when the children of Israel fasted and confessed their sins, he was one of the Levites who stood up on the stairs and cried with a loud voice to the LORD ([[@16009001-16009004|Neh 9:1-4]]).

column5: A Levite chief in charge of the singing
column7: He was a chief of the Levites who was skillful in singing, so he led the singing and taught the singers ([[@13015022|1 Chr 15:22]]). When David brought up the ark, he was the choir master with the singers and wore a robe of fine linen ([[@13015027|1 Chr 15:27]]).

column5: Town of the tribe of Benjamin
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Benjamin received by families, named along with Ophni and Geba ([[@6018021|Josh 18:21]]; [[@6018024|Josh 18:24]]).

column5: A town of the Gibeonites
column7: It was one of the towns of the Gibeonites ([[@6009017|Josh 9:17]]). It became a town of the tribe of Benjamin ([[@6018026|Josh 18:26]]).

column5: Son of Dishon the Horite
column7: He was a son of Dishon, a Horite descended from Seir in the land of Edom. His brothers were Hemdan, Eshban, and Ithran ([[@1036026|Gen 36:26]]; [[@13001041|1 Chr 1:41]]).

column5: A troop of soldiers who guarded King David
column7: They were a people who lived on the sea coast in the land of the Philistines, and the prophets mention them alongside the Philistines ([[@36002005|Zeph 2:5]]). In David's time Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites, and scholars see them as soldiers who guarded the king closely ([[@10008018|2 Sam 8:18]]). When David left Jerusalem, the Cherethites and the Pelethites went on before the king ([[@10015018|2 Sam 15:18]]). When Solomon was made king, they had him ride on King David's mule and brought him to Gihon ([[@11001038|1 Kgs 1:38]]).

column5: Brook where Elijah hid
column7: God told Elijah to hide by the brook Cherith, which faces the Jordan ([[@11017003|1 Kgs 17:3]]). There the ravens brought him bread and meat morning and evening ([[@11017006|1 Kgs 17:6]]).

column5: A place from which returning exiles set out
column7: It was one of the places from which people came up out of exile in Babylon ([[@15002059|Ezra 2:59]]). Some who came from here could not show whether their family and ancestry belonged to Israel ([[@16007061|Neh 7:61]]).

column5: Winged beings that guard God's holiness
column7: Cherubim are heavenly beings in the Bible who appear with God's holy presence. After the man was driven out of the Garden of Eden, God placed cherubim and a flaming sword which turned every way to guard the way to the tree of life ([[@1003024|Gen 3:24]]). Two gold cherubim with wings spread upward were made at the two ends of the mercy seat on the ark of the covenant, and cherubim were also worked into the curtains of the tabernacle ([[@2025018-2025020|Exod 25:18-20]]; [[@2026001|Exod 26:1]]). The Psalms address God as "you who sit above the cherubim" ([[@19080001|Ps 80:1]]).

column5: Place on Judah’s northern border
column7: It is a place named in describing the northern border of Judah. The border passed along "to the side of Mount Jearim (also called Chesalon) on the north" and went down to Beth Shemesh ([[@6015010|Josh 15:10]]).

column5: Son of Nahor, Abraham’s brother
column7: He was one of the eight sons born to Abraham’s brother Nahor and his wife Milcah. One of his brothers, Bethuel, became the father of Rebekah ([[@1022020-1022023|Gen 22:20-23]]).

column5: Town in southern Judah
column7: It was one of the southern towns near the border of Edom given to the tribe of Judah, named along with Eltolad and Hormah ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015030|Josh 15:30]]).

column5: A town of the tribe of Issachar
column7: It was a town within the land the tribe of Issachar received, listed with Jezreel and Shunem ([[@6019017-6019018|Josh 19:17-18]]). Some think it is the same place as 'Chisloth Tabor' on the border of Zebulun ([[@6019012|Josh 19:12]]).

column5: Son of David and Abigail
column7: He was David's second son, born in Hebron to Abigail ([[@10003003|2 Sam 3:3]]). In 1 Chronicles he appears as 'Daniel' ([[@13003001|1 Chr 3:1]]).

column5: Son of Elimelech and Naomi
column7: He was one of the two sons of Elimelech and Naomi; he went to live in the land of Moab and died there along with Mahlon ([[@8001002-8001005|Ruth 1:2-5]]). Boaz bought all that had been his from Naomi’s hand ([[@8004009|Ruth 4:9]]).

column5: Place that traded with Tyre
column7: In Ezekiel’s message about Tyre, it appears among the places that traded with Tyre, along with Haran and Asshur ([[@26027023|Ezek 27:23]]).

column5: A man who crossed the Jordan with David
column7: He was the 'servant' old Barzillai asked King David to take across with him in his place ([[@10019037|2 Sam 19:37]]). David took him along and crossed over to Gilgal ([[@10019038-10019040|2 Sam 19:38-40]]).

column5: Old name for Galilee's sea, and a town
column7: In the Old Testament the Sea of Galilee was called "the sea of Chinnereth" ([[@6013027|Josh 13:27]]). A fortified city of the same name stood in the land of the tribe of Naphtali ([[@6019035|Josh 19:35]]), and the area around it was also called Chinnereth. In Joshua it also appears under the name Chinneroth. In the New Testament the same lake is called the lake of Gennesaret, the Sea of Galilee, and the Sea of Tiberias ([[@42005001|Luke 5:1]]; [[@43006001|John 6:1]]).

column5: Island Paul sailed past
column7: After leaving Mitylene, Paul and his companions came opposite Chios the next day. After that they touched at Samos and then came to Miletus ([[@44020014-44020015|Acts 20:14-15]]).

column5: Father of Elidad, Benjamin’s leader
column7: He was the father of Elidad, the prince of the tribe of Benjamin among the leaders chosen from each tribe to divide the land of Canaan ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034021|Num 34:21]]).

column5: Town in Judah’s lowland
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Judah received in the lowland, named along with Cabbon and Lahmam ([[@6015033-6015040|Josh 15:33-40]]).

column5: Household that reported divisions at Corinth
column7: Paul heard from those of Chloe’s household that there were quarrels in the church at Corinth. The believers were divided, some saying they followed Paul and others that they followed Apollos ([[@46001011-46001012|1 Cor 1:11-12]]).

column5: Galilean town Jesus rebuked
column7: It was the town Jesus rebuked, saying, "Woe to you, Chorazin!" because it did not repent even though he had done many mighty works there ([[@40011021|Matt 11:21]]; [[@42010013|Luke 10:13]]).

column5: Herod’s steward, husband of Joanna
column7: He was Herod’s steward. His wife Joanna, together with Susanna and many other women, served Jesus and his companions from their own possessions ([[@42008001-42008003|Luke 8:1-3]]).

column5: The region of Paul's hometown, Tarsus
column7: It was a region on the southeastern coast of Asia Minor, and Paul's hometown of Tarsus was there ([[@44022003|Acts 22:3]]). In Jerusalem there was a synagogue where people from Cilicia also gathered, and some of them argued with Stephen ([[@44006009|Acts 6:9]]). After his conversion Paul went to the regions of Syria and Cilicia ([[@48001021|Gal 1:21]]), and later he traveled through Syria and Cilicia with Silas, strengthening the churches ([[@44015041|Acts 15:41]]).

column5: Cutting the foreskin as a sign of God's covenant
column7: Circumcision is the rite of cutting off a male's foreskin, the sign of the covenant God made with Abraham ([[@1017010-1017011|Gen 17:10-11]]). Israelite boys were circumcised when they were eight days old ([[@1017012|Gen 17:12]]). The Bible speaks not only of circumcision of the body but also says, "Circumcise therefore the foreskin of your heart", treating a heart turned toward God as more important ([[@5010016|Deut 10:16]]). Paul also taught that what matters is not circumcision or uncircumcision but "faith working through love" ([[@48005006|Gal 5:6]]).

column5: A pit for collecting and storing water
column7: A cistern was a place for collecting and storing water. Because springs were scarce in the land, people gathered rainwater in cisterns and used it. The law said that "a spring or a cistern in which water is gathered shall be clean", and only what touched a carcass became unclean ([[@3011036|Lev 11:36]]). God rebuked his people for forsaking him, the spring of living waters, and digging "broken cisterns that can’t hold water" ([[@24002013|Jer 2:13]]). A pit with no water was sometimes used to hold people, and Jeremiah was thrown into one that had only mud and sank in it ([[@24038006|Jer 38:6]]).

column5: Town in the wilderness of Judah
column7: It was one of the six towns the tribe of Judah received in the wilderness, named along with Nibshan and En Gedi ([[@6015061-6015062|Josh 15:61-62]]).

column5: Believer who sent greetings to Timothy
column7: At the end of Paul’s letter to Timothy, she is one of those who sent greetings to Timothy, along with Eubulus, Pudens, and Linus ([[@55004021|2 Tim 4:21]]).

column5: Roman emperor in Paul's day
column7: He was the Roman emperor during the time of the book of Acts. A man named Agabus said by the Spirit that a great famine would come over all the world, and it happened just so in the days of Claudius ([[@44011028|Acts 11:28]]). So the disciples each decided, as they were able, to send relief to the brothers living in Judea, and they sent it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul ([[@44011029-44011030|Acts 11:29-30]]). Claudius also commanded all the Jews to leave Rome, so Aquila and his wife Priscilla came from Italy to Corinth, where they met Paul ([[@44018001-44018002|Acts 18:1-2]]).

column5: Paul’s fellow worker in the gospel
column7: Paul asked the church at Philippi to help the women who had labored with him in the Good News, along with Clement and his other fellow workers. He says their names are in the book of life ([[@50004003|Phil 4:3]]).

column5: Place Paul’s ship barely reached
column7: The ship bound for Rome sailed slowly for many days and with difficulty came opposite Cnidus. The wind would not let them go further, so they sailed under the lee of Crete ([[@44027007|Acts 27:7]]).

column5: Father of Shallun, who repaired the spring gate
column7: He was the father of Shallun, the ruler of the district of Mizpah. In Nehemiah’s time Shallun repaired the spring gate and the wall of the pool of Shelah ([[@16003015|Neh 3:15]]).

column5: Grandfather of Maaseiah in Jerusalem
column7: He was the grandfather of Maaseiah, a man of Judah who lived in Jerusalem in Nehemiah’s time. Maaseiah was the son of Baruch and the grandson of Colhozeh ([[@16011004-16011005|Neh 11:4-5]]).

column5: City of the believers Paul wrote to
column7: It was where the believers lived to whom Paul sent the letter to the Colossians ([[@51001002|Col 1:2]]). Epaphras strove in prayer for the believers here ([[@51004012|Col 4:12]]).

column5: A Levite in charge of offerings under Hezekiah
column7: In Hezekiah’s day he was the Levite in charge of the offerings, the tithes, and the dedicated things ([[@14031012|2 Chr 31:12]]). His brother Shimei was second to him, and a number of Levites worked under them ([[@14031013|2 Chr 31:13]]).

column5: An offering given to God
column7: It means 'given to God'. Jesus rebuked the tradition of calling what was owed to one's parents Corban in order to avoid honoring them ([[@41007011|Mark 7:11]]).

column5: A word meaning 'given to God'
column7: Corban is a Hebrew word meaning a gift offered to God, and it appears once in the Bible, in the Gospel of Mark. Mark explains the word as meaning "given to God" ([[@41007011|Mark 7:11]]). Jesus rebuked people who taught that, even though Moses said to honor your father and mother, you no longer had to help your parents if you simply called what you would have given them Corban ([[@41007010-41007012|Mark 7:10-12]]). He said that in this way they were making void the word of God by their tradition ([[@41007013|Mark 7:13]]).

column5: Great city of Achaia where Paul founded a church
column7: It was a great city in the region of Achaia in southern Greece. Paul left Athens and came to Corinth, where he met Aquila and Priscilla and worked with them making tents, and every Sabbath he reasoned in the synagogue ([[@44018001-44018004|Acts 18:1-4]]). Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord with all his household, and many Corinthians heard, believed, and were baptized ([[@44018008|Acts 18:8]]). Paul stayed there a year and six months, teaching the word of God ([[@44018011|Acts 18:11]]). Later Paul sent a letter to "the assembly of God which is at Corinth", and that letter is 1 Corinthians ([[@46001002|1 Cor 1:2]]).

column5: Centurion of Caesarea who sent for Peter
column7: He was a centurion of what was called the Italian Regiment, living in Caesarea ([[@44010001|Acts 10:1]]). He was a devout man who feared God with all his house, gave generously to the needy, and always prayed to God ([[@44010002|Acts 10:2]]). After hearing the words of an angel of God in a vision, he sent men to Joppa to bring Simon, who was called Peter ([[@44010003-44010005|Acts 10:3-5]]). While Peter was speaking the word, the Holy Spirit fell on all who heard it, and Peter commanded that they be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ ([[@44010044-44010048|Acts 10:44-48]]).

column5: A gate in the wall of Jerusalem
column7: It was a gate in the wall of Jerusalem, and King Jehoash of Israel broke down four hundred cubits of the wall from the gate of Ephraim to this gate ([[@12014013|2 Kgs 14:13]]). Uzziah built towers here ([[@14026009|2 Chr 26:9]]).

column5: Island Paul sailed past
column7: After saying farewell to the Ephesian elders at Miletus, Paul and his companions set sail and came straight to Cos. The next day they reached Rhodes ([[@44020038|Acts 20:38]]; [[@44021001|Acts 21:1]]).

column5: Father of Addi in Luke’s genealogy
column7: In the genealogy of Jesus recorded in Luke, he appears as the father of Addi and the son of Elmodam ([[@42003028|Luke 3:28]]).

column5: God's firm promise made with people
column7: A covenant is a firm promise God made with people. After the flood God established a covenant with Noah, promising never again to destroy the earth by a flood, and gave the rainbow as its sign ([[@1009011-1009013|Gen 9:11-13]]). With Abraham he established "an everlasting covenant", promising to be the God of Abraham and his descendants, and with Israel he made a covenant by sprinkling blood ([[@1017007|Gen 17:7]]; [[@2024008|Exod 24:8]]). At the Last Supper Jesus gave the cup and said, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood" ([[@42022020|Luke 22:20]]).

column5: Midianite woman killed by Phinehas
column7: The daughter of Zur, a Midianite chief, she was killed by Phinehas along with Zimri the Simeonite ([[@4025014-4025015|Num 25:14-15]]). Because of this the plague was stopped ([[@4025008|Num 25:8]]).

column5: Paul’s co-worker who went to Galatia
column7: In his letter to Timothy, Paul reports that Crescens had gone to Galatia ([[@55004010|2 Tim 4:10]]). At that time only Luke was with Paul ([[@55004011|2 Tim 4:11]]).

column5: Corinthian synagogue ruler who believed
column7: The ruler of the synagogue in Corinth, he believed in the Lord with all his household ([[@44018008|Acts 18:8]]). He was one of the few people Paul baptized himself ([[@46001014|1 Cor 1:14]]).

column5: The wooden frame on which Jesus died
column7: The cross was a frame on which criminals were hung to die, and Jesus died on this cross. The soldiers leading Jesus away forced a man of Cyrene named Simon to carry Jesus' cross ([[@40027032|Matt 27:32]]). Jesus taught the way of a disciple, saying, "let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow me" ([[@40016024|Matt 16:24]]). Paul said, "the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are dying, but to us who are being saved it is the power of God" ([[@46001018|1 Cor 1:18]]). The Bible says that Jesus was obedient to the point of death, even death on a cross ([[@50002008|Phil 2:8]]).

column5: Execution by hanging a criminal on a cross
column7: Crucifixion was a severe punishment in which a criminal was hung on a cross to die. Jesus said beforehand that he would be handed over to the Gentiles to be crucified and would be raised on the third day ([[@40020019|Matt 20:19]]). When Pilate asked what he should do with Jesus, the crowd shouted, "Let him be crucified!" ([[@40027022|Matt 27:22]]). Jesus was crucified at a place called Golgotha along with two others, with Jesus in the middle ([[@43019017-43019018|John 19:17-18]]). Paul confessed, "I have been crucified with Christ" ([[@48002020|Gal 2:20]]).

column5: Length from the elbow to the fingertips
column7: The cubit was a unit of length based on the distance from the elbow to the fingertips. It is thought to be roughly 45 to 52 centimeters, but scholars differ on its exact length. Noah's ark was three hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high ([[@1006015|Gen 6:15]]). The ark of the covenant was two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide and high, and Solomon's temple was sixty cubits long ([[@2025010|Exod 25:10]]; [[@11006002|1 Kgs 6:2]]). Deuteronomy also speaks of "the cubit of a man" ([[@5003011|Deut 3:11]]).

column5: The land south of Egypt
column7: Cush is the name of a son of Ham ([[@1010006|Gen 10:6]]) and also of the land where his descendants lived. Gihon, the second river of Eden, is said to flow through the whole land of Cush ([[@1002013|Gen 2:13]]). In the Bible, Cush mostly refers to the region south of Egypt, but scholars differ on its exact extent. Tirhakah king of Cush came out to fight the king of Assyria ([[@12019009|2 Kgs 19:9]]), and Zerah the Cushite attacked Judah with a huge army but was defeated by King Asa ([[@14014009-14014012|2 Chr 14:9-12]]).

column5: Son of Ham, father of Nimrod
column7: He was the son of Ham, Noah's son ([[@1010006|Gen 10:6]]). His sons were Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca ([[@1010007|Gen 10:7]]). Cush also became the father of Nimrod, who "began to be a mighty one on the earth" and was a mighty hunter before the LORD ([[@1010008-1010009|Gen 10:8-9]]). The name Cush was also used for the land where his descendants lived, and Gihon, the second river of Eden, is said to flow "through the whole land of Cush" ([[@1002013|Gen 2:13]]).

column5: Benjamite mentioned in the title of Psalm 7
column7: Cush, a Benjamite, is mentioned in the title of Psalm 7, which David sang to the Lord.

column5: Place in Habakkuk’s prayer
column7: In Habakkuk’s prayer, this is where he saw "the tents of Cushan in affliction" while the dwellings of the land of Midian trembled ([[@35003007|Hab 3:7]]). Scholars differ on where it was.

column5: Great-grandfather of Jehudi
column7: He was the great-grandfather of Jehudi, who was sent to Baruch to bring Jeremiah’s scroll. Jehudi was the son of Nethaniah and the grandson of Shelemiah ([[@24036014|Jer 36:14]]).

column5: Father of the prophet Zephaniah
column7: He was the father of the prophet Zephaniah, to whom the LORD’s word came in the days of Josiah. Zephaniah was the grandson of Gedaliah and the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah ([[@36001001|Zeph 1:1]]).

column5: City whose people were moved to Samaria
column7: The king of Assyria brought people from Cuthah and other places and settled them in the cities of Samaria ([[@12017024|2 Kgs 17:24]]). The men of Cuth made the idol Nergal ([[@12017030|2 Kgs 17:30]]).

column5: Large Mediterranean island, home of Barnabas
column7: It is a large island in the eastern Mediterranean; the Kittim of the Old Testament is often taken to be this island, though some think Kittim refers to wider lands across the sea ([[@4024024|Num 24:24]]). In the New Testament it first appears as the home of Barnabas ([[@44004036|Acts 4:36]]). On their first missionary journey Paul and Barnabas went to this island and preached the word as they traveled from Salamis to Paphos, and the proconsul came to believe ([[@44013004-44013012|Acts 13:4-12]]). Later Barnabas took Mark and went there again ([[@44015039|Acts 15:39]]).

column5: North African city, home of Simon of Cyrene
column7: It was a city in North Africa, in the region of Libya. Simon, who was forced to carry Jesus' cross, was "a man of Cyrene" ([[@40027032|Matt 27:32]]; [[@41015021|Mark 15:21]]). At Pentecost there were also Jews in Jerusalem from "the parts of Libya around Cyrene" ([[@44002010|Acts 2:10]]). Later some believers from Cyrene went to Antioch and preached the Lord Jesus to the Greeks too ([[@44011020|Acts 11:20]]), and among the prophets and teachers of the church at Antioch was "Lucius of Cyrene" ([[@44013001|Acts 13:1]]).

column5: Persian king who ordered Judah's return
column7: He was the king of Persia who, in his first year after taking Babylon, issued a decree that the people of Judah could return to Jerusalem and build the temple ([[@15001001-15001002|Ezra 1:1-2]]). He also gave back the vessels of the LORD's house that Nebuchadnezzar had carried off ([[@15001007|Ezra 1:7]]). Long before this, Isaiah said that God called Cyrus "my shepherd" and would rebuild Jerusalem and the temple through him ([[@23044028|Isa 44:28]]; [[@23045001|Isa 45:1]]). He is remembered as a foreign king God used to keep his promise.

column5: Place on Zebulun’s border
column7: It was a place the border of the children of Zebulun’s inheritance passed. The border went up to Maralah, reached Dabbesheth, and reached the brook before Jokneam ([[@6019010-6019011|Josh 19:10-11]]).

column5: A Levite city in the tribe of Issachar
column7: It appears as a place on the border of the tribe of Zebulun ([[@6019012|Josh 19:12]]). It was one of the cities from the tribe of Issachar given to the Levites of the children of Gershon ([[@6021027-6021028|Josh 21:27-28]]).

column5: Region Titus went to
column7: In his letter to Timothy, Paul reports that Titus had gone to Dalmatia. At that time Demas had left Paul and gone to Thessalonica ([[@55004010|2 Tim 4:10]]).

column5: One of Haman’s ten sons
column7: He was one of the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. He was killed when the Jews struck their enemies in the citadel of Susa ([[@17009006-17009007|Esth 9:6-7]]; [[@17009010|Esth 9:10]]).

column5: Woman in Athens who believed Paul’s message
column7: Among those in Athens who heard Paul and believed was "a woman named Damaris". Dionysius the Areopagite also believed ([[@44017034|Acts 17:34]]).

column5: The capital of Syria, a very ancient city
column7: Damascus is a very ancient city and was the capital of the kingdom of Syria ([[@23007008|Isa 7:8]]). When Abram went to rescue his nephew Lot, he chased the enemy as far as the area near Damascus ([[@1014015|Gen 14:15]]). In David's time he put garrisons in Syria of Damascus, and the Syrians brought tribute to David ([[@10008006|2 Sam 8:6]]). In the New Testament, Saul was on his way to Damascus to arrest Christians when he met the risen Jesus in a light that shone from heaven ([[@44009003|Acts 9:3]]).

column5: A town at the far north of Israel
column7: It was a town at the northern edge of the land of Israel. To rescue his captured nephew Lot, Abram "pursued as far as Dan" and fought ([[@1014014|Gen 14:14]]). Its original name was Laish, but the tribe of Dan took the city and called it Dan after their forefather Dan ([[@7018029|Judg 18:29]]). The phrase 'from Dan to Beersheba' came to mean the whole land of Israel ([[@7020001|Judg 20:1]]). Jeroboam set up a golden calf here as well ([[@11012029|1 Kgs 12:29]]).

column5: Jacob's fifth son, ancestor of the tribe of Dan
column7: He was the son born to Jacob by Bilhah, Rachel's servant ([[@1035025|Gen 35:25]]). Rachel said, "God has judged me, and has also heard my voice, and has given me a son", and she named him Dan ([[@1030006|Gen 30:6]]). In his final blessing Jacob said, "Dan will judge his people, as one of the tribes of Israel" ([[@1049016|Gen 49:16]]). The descendants of Dan later attacked and took Leshem and named the town Dan after their forefather ([[@6019047|Josh 19:47]]).

column5: Descendant of Ithamar who returned with Ezra
column7: A descendant of Ithamar, he came up from Babylon with Ezra ([[@15008001-15008002|Ezra 8:1-2]]). The same name also appears in the list of priests who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010006|Neh 10:6]]).

column5: A wise prophet who served in Babylon
column7: He was one of the people of Judah, taken to Babylon when he was young. He made up his mind not to defile himself with the king's delicacies ([[@27001008|Dan 1:8]]), and with the wisdom God gave him he interpreted the king's dreams. Even after a decree forbade it, he kept praying three times a day and was thrown into the lions' den, but God sent his angel and shut the lions' mouths ([[@27006010|Dan 6:10]]; [[@27006022|Dan 6:22]]). Ezekiel named him as a righteous man alongside Noah and Job ([[@26014014|Ezek 14:14]]).

column5: Town in Judah’s hill country
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Judah received in the hill country, named along with Kiriath Sannah, which is Debir ([[@6015048-6015049|Josh 15:48-49]]).

column5: Grandson of Judah, son of Zerah
column7: He was one of the five sons of Zerah, Judah’s son, and the brother of Zimri, Ethan, Heman, and Calcol ([[@13002004|1 Chr 2:4]]; [[@13002006|1 Chr 2:6]]).

column5: Wise man compared with Solomon
column7: His name appears along with Ethan, Heman, and Calcol when the Bible describes how great Solomon’s wisdom was. Solomon is said to have been wiser than they ([[@11004030-11004031|1 Kgs 4:30-31]]).

column5: Persian king who allowed the temple rebuilding
column7: He was the king of Persia when the people who had returned from exile were rebuilding the temple. Because of enemies' opposition, work on the temple stopped until the second year of King Darius ([[@15004024|Ezra 4:24]]), and in that year Haggai and Zechariah prophesied and encouraged the people. When Governor Tattenai sent a letter about the work, Darius had the archives searched, found King Cyrus's decree, and ordered that the work on God's house not be hindered ([[@15006001-15006007|Ezra 6:1-7]]). The temple was finished "on the third day of the month Adar, which was in the sixth year of the reign of Darius the king" ([[@15006015|Ezra 6:15]]). He is considered a different person from Darius the Mede in the book of Daniel ([[@27005031|Dan 5:31]]).

column5: Persian king named in Nehemiah
column7: He is the Persian king during whose reign the heads of the Levite and priestly families were recorded ([[@16012022|Neh 12:22]]). Scholars differ on which Darius this was.

column5: The Mede who received the kingdom of Babylon
column7: He was a Mede who received the kingdom after Belshazzar the Chaldean king was killed, and he was about sixty-two years old at the time ([[@27005030-27005031|Dan 5:30-31]]). He appointed one hundred twenty local governors to rule the kingdom and set Daniel among the three presidents over them ([[@27006001-27006002|Dan 6:1-2]]). Listening to officials who were jealous of Daniel, he signed a decree ([[@27006009|Dan 6:9]]), but when Daniel came out of the lions' den alive, he issued a decree that people in all his kingdom should tremble and fear before the God of Daniel ([[@27006026|Dan 6:26]]). He is a different person from the Persian kings named Darius.

column5: Ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants
column7: Among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Darkon' ([[@15002055-15002056|Ezra 2:55-56]]; [[@16007058|Neh 7:58]]).

column5: Reubenite swallowed by the earth for opposing Moses
column7: He was the son of Eliab, a Reubenite, and together with his brother Abiram he joined Korah's company and rose up against Moses and Aaron ([[@4016001|Num 16:1]]; [[@4026009|Num 26:9]]). When Moses called for them, they refused, saying, "We won’t come up!" ([[@4016012|Num 16:12]]). Then the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them up with their households, their tents, and everything that followed them ([[@5011006|Deut 11:6]]). The Psalms also remember this: "The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan" ([[@19106017|Ps 106:17]]).

column5: Lot’s older daughter, mother of Moab
column7: She was the older of Lot’s two daughters. She bore a son and named him Moab, and he became the father of the Moabites ([[@1019036-1019037|Gen 19:36-37]]).

column5: Lot’s younger daughter, mother of Ben Ammi
column7: She was the younger of Lot’s two daughters. She bore a son and named him Ben Ammi, and he became the father of the children of Ammon ([[@1019036|Gen 19:36]]; [[@1019038|Gen 19:38]]).

column5: Wife of Caiaphas the high priest
column7: She was the wife of Caiaphas the high priest. The Bible does not give her name and says only that Annas was Caiaphas’ father-in-law ([[@43018013|John 18:13]]).

column5: Wife of Hezron, mother of Segub
column7: She was the daughter of Machir, the father of Gilead. Hezron married her when he was sixty years old, and she bore him Segub ([[@13002021|1 Chr 2:21]]).

column5: Wife of Jehohanan, Tobiah’s son
column7: She was the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah, and she was married to Jehohanan the son of Tobiah, the man who tried to make Nehemiah afraid ([[@16006018-16006019|Neh 6:18-19]]).

column5: Pharaoh’s daughter who rescued and raised baby Moses
column7: She saw the baby in a basket among the reeds by the river and had compassion on him. When the child grew, she made him her son and named him Moses ([[@2002005-2002006|Exod 2:5-6]]; [[@2002010|Exod 2:10]]).

column5: Egyptian king’s daughter who married Solomon
column7: Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh king of Egypt, took his daughter, and brought her into David’s city ([[@11003001|1 Kgs 3:1]]). Later Solomon built a house for Pharaoh’s daughter ([[@11007008|1 Kgs 7:8]]).

column5: Wife of Eleazar, mother of Phinehas
column7: Eleazar, Aaron’s son, took one of the daughters of Putiel as his wife, and she bore him Phinehas ([[@2006025|Exod 6:25]]).

column5: Sanballat’s daughter who married into the high priest’s family
column7: A son of Joiada and grandson of Eliashib the high priest became the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite. Nehemiah drove him away ([[@16013028|Neh 13:28]]).

column5: Shecaniah’s daughter who became Tobiah’s wife
column7: Tobiah the Ammonite became the son-in-law of Shecaniah the son of Arah. Because of this marriage, many in Judah were bound by oath to Tobiah ([[@16006018|Neh 6:18]]).

column5: Israel's second king, ancestor of Jesus
column7: He was the son of Jesse of Bethlehem and the great-grandson of Ruth and Boaz ([[@8004017|Ruth 4:17]]). While he was the youngest son tending sheep, Samuel anointed him, and from that day the Spirit of the LORD came mightily on him ([[@9016013|1 Sam 16:13]]). He defeated Goliath, became king after Saul, and made Jerusalem his capital. God promised, "Your throne will be established forever" ([[@10007016|2 Sam 7:16]]), and that promise carried through to Jesus Christ, who came as a descendant of David ([[@40001001|Matt 1:1]]).

column5: King of Eglon in Joshua’s time
column7: He was king of Eglon in the days of Joshua. He was one of the kings whom Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem asked for help in attacking Gibeon ([[@6010003-6010005|Josh 10:3-5]]).

column5: Town in Judah, once called Kiriath Sepher
column7: A town in the land of Judah, its original name was Kiriath Sepher ([[@6015015|Josh 15:15]]). Joshua and all Israel attacked Debir, captured its king and the city, and utterly destroyed them ([[@6010038-6010039|Josh 10:38-39]]). Later, when Caleb promised his daughter Achsah as wife to whoever took Kiriath Sepher, Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's brother, took the city and married Achsah ([[@6015016-6015017|Josh 15:16-17]]). Debir later became one of the towns given to the descendants of Aaron the priest ([[@6021013-6021015|Josh 21:13-15]]).

column5: A place on Judah’s northern border
column7: This was a place that Judah’s northern border passed through. The border went up from the Valley of Achor to Debir and on northward ([[@6015007|Josh 15:7]]).

column5: Rebekah’s nurse
column7: She was Rebekah’s nurse. When she died she was buried under the oak below Bethel, and people called that tree Allon Bacuth ([[@1035008|Gen 35:8]]).

column5: Prophetess and judge of Israel
column7: She was the wife of Lappidoth, a prophetess and a judge of Israel. She sat under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the children of Israel came to her for judgment ([[@7004004-7004005|Judg 4:4-5]]). Deborah called Barak and told him to attack Sisera, the commander of the army of Jabin, a Canaanite king, and when Barak said he would not go unless she went with him, she went with him ([[@7004006-7004009|Judg 4:6-9]]). After the victory she sang with Barak and said of herself, "Until I arose a mother in Israel" ([[@7005007|Judg 5:7]]). After that the land had rest forty years ([[@7005031|Judg 5:31]]).

column5: A region where crowds followed Jesus
column7: Large crowds from Decapolis also followed Jesus ([[@40004025|Matt 4:25]]). After the man who had been possessed by demons was healed, he told in this region the great things Jesus had done for him ([[@41005018-41005020|Mark 5:18-20]]).

column5: Grandson of Cush, son of Raamah
column7: He was a descendant of Noah's son Ham. He was a son of Raamah, the son of Cush, and the brother of Sheba ([[@1010006-1010007|Gen 10:6-7]]; [[@13001009|1 Chr 1:9]]).

column5: Grandson of Abraham and Keturah
column7: He was a son of Jokshan, whom Keturah, Abraham’s concubine, bore, and a brother of Sheba. That makes him Abraham’s grandson ([[@13001032|1 Chr 1:32]]).

column5: Arabian people and land known for trade
column7: It is the name of the people descended from Dedan, the son of Raamah and grandson of Cush, and also of the land in Arabia where they lived ([[@1010007|Gen 10:7]]). In his message about Arabia, Isaiah called out to the "caravans of Dedanites" ([[@23021013|Isa 21:13]]). Ezekiel says the men of Dedan traded with Tyre in goods such as ivory and ebony ([[@26027015|Ezek 27:15]]). Jeremiah and Ezekiel prophesied that when God judged Edom, the disaster would reach as far as Dedan ([[@24049008|Jer 49:8]]; [[@26025013|Ezek 25:13]]).

column5: A group that accused the people of Jerusalem
column7: They were one of the groups that joined Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe when they wrote a letter to King Artaxerxes accusing the people of Jerusalem ([[@15004008-15004009|Ezra 4:8-9]]).

column5: One of Solomon’s twelve officers
column7: He was one of the twelve officers Solomon appointed to provide food for the king’s household. He was in charge of Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh, and Elon Beth Hanan ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004009|1 Kgs 4:9]]).

column5: Son of Elioenai in David’s royal line
column7: In the family line of Jeconiah the captive, he was one of the seven sons of Elioenai the son of Neariah ([[@13003017|1 Chr 3:17]]; [[@13003023-13003024|1 Chr 3:23-24]]).

column5: Priest of the twenty-third division
column7: When the priestly divisions were assigned by lot in David’s time, he was the one chosen twenty-third ([[@13024005|1 Chr 24:5]]; [[@13024018|1 Chr 24:18]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family with no proof of lineage
column7: He was the ancestor of 'the children of Delaiah', who returned from exile but could not show that their family belonged to Israel ([[@15002059-15002060|Ezra 2:59-60]]; [[@16007062|Neh 7:62]]).

column5: Father of Shemaiah, who tried to deceive Nehemiah
column7: He was the grandson of Mehetabel and the father of Shemaiah. Shemaiah urged Nehemiah to go into God’s house, within the temple, and hide there ([[@16006010|Neh 6:10]]).

column5: Official who pleaded for the scroll
column7: A prince in King Jehoiakim's time, he was the son of Shemaiah ([[@24036012|Jer 36:12]]). He pleaded with the king not to burn Jeremiah's scroll, but the king would not listen ([[@24036025|Jer 36:25]]).

column5: Woman who betrayed Samson to the Philistines
column7: She was a woman who lived in the valley of Sorek, and Samson loved her ([[@7016004|Judg 16:4]]). The lords of the Philistines promised that each of them would give her eleven hundred pieces of silver if she found out where Samson's great strength came from ([[@7016005|Judg 16:5]]). Even after being deceived three times, Delilah pressed him with her words every day, and at last Samson told her the whole truth, that he was a Nazirite and no razor had ever touched his head ([[@7016015-7016017|Judg 16:15-17]]). Delilah made him sleep on her knees and called a man to shave off the seven locks of his hair, and his strength left him, and the Philistines seized him and put out his eyes ([[@7016019-7016021|Judg 16:19-21]]).

column5: Paul’s co-worker who later left him
column7: As Paul’s fellow worker, he sent greetings to the Colossians and to Philemon ([[@51004014|Col 4:14]]; [[@57001024|Phlm 1:24]]). But later, "having loved this present world," he left Paul and went to Thessalonica ([[@55004010|2 Tim 4:10]]).

column5: A silversmith in Ephesus
column7: He was a silversmith in Ephesus who made silver shrines of Artemis and brought no little business to the craftsmen ([[@44019024|Acts 19:24]]). Fearing that Paul’s preaching would bring their trade into disrepute, he gathered the workmen and stirred them up ([[@44019025-44019027|Acts 19:25-27]]).

column5: Roman silver coin, a worker's daily wage
column7: The denarius was a Roman silver coin in New Testament times. As in the parable where the landowner agreed with the workers for "a denarius a day", it was an ordinary laborer's daily wage ([[@40020002|Matt 20:2]]). When Jesus was tested over paying taxes, he asked them to show him a denarius and said, "Give therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s" ([[@40022019-40022021|Matt 22:19-21]]). The good Samaritan gave two denarii to the innkeeper and asked him to take care of the injured man ([[@42010035|Luke 10:35]]).

column5: A town of Lycaonia
column7: It was a town of Lycaonia where Paul and Barnabas fled from Iconium ([[@44014006|Acts 14:6]]). The day after Paul was stoned at Lystra, he went to Derbe with Barnabas ([[@44014019-44014020|Acts 14:19-20]]).

column5: Father of Eliasaph, leader of the tribe of Gad
column7: He was the father of Eliasaph, the leader of the children of Gad in the wilderness ([[@4001014|Num 1:14]]; [[@4007042|Num 7:42]]). In Numbers 2 he is called 'Reuel' ([[@4002014|Num 2:14]]).

column5: An evil spirit who opposes God and people
column7: The word devil means 'slanderer', and the devil is an evil spirit who opposes God and leads people into sin. Jesus was tempted by the devil in the wilderness, but he drove him back with the word of God ([[@40004001-40004011|Matt 4:1-11]]). Jesus said of the devil, "he is a liar, and the father of lies" ([[@43008044|John 8:44]]). Peter said that the devil prowls around like a roaring lion, looking for someone to devour, so we must be sober and watchful ([[@60005008|1 Pet 5:8]]). Revelation says that the devil who deceived people will in the end be thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur ([[@66020010|Rev 20:10]]).

column5: Father of Gomer, Hosea’s wife
column7: He was the father of Gomer, whom the prophet Hosea married as the LORD told him. Gomer bore Hosea a son ([[@28001002-28001003|Hos 1:2-3]]).

column5: A camp on the wilderness journey
column7: Israel set out from Dibon Gad and camped here, then left and camped in the mountains of Abarim before Nebo ([[@4033046-4033047|Num 33:46-47]]). Some think it is the same place as 'Beth Diblathaim' in the word against Moab ([[@24048022|Jer 48:22]]).

column5: A Moabite town north of the Arnon
column7: It was a town in the land of Moab east of the Jordan, and the song Israel sang after defeating Sihon king of the Amorites says, "Heshbon has perished even to Dibon" ([[@4021030|Num 21:30]]). The children of Gad built Dibon, and the book of Joshua lists Dibon in the land Moses gave to the tribe of Reuben ([[@4032034|Num 32:34]]; [[@6013015-6013017|Josh 13:15-17]]). Later it became a town of Moab again, and Isaiah prophesied that the people of Moab would go up to the high places of Dibon to weep ([[@23015002|Isa 15:2]]).

column5: A place where people of Judah lived in Nehemiah’s time
column7: In Nehemiah’s time some of the children of Judah lived in Dibon and its towns, as well as in Kiriath Arba and Jekabzeel ([[@16011025|Neh 11:25]]).

column5: A man of Dan, father of Shelomith
column7: He was a man of the tribe of Dan and the father of Shelomith. Shelomith’s son fought in the camp and blasphemed the name of the LORD and cursed ([[@3024010-3024011|Lev 24:10-11]]).

column5: Son of Joktan
column7: He was one of the sons of Joktan, the son of Eber, a descendant of Shem ([[@1010025-1010027|Gen 10:25-27]]; [[@13001021|1 Chr 1:21]]).

column5: A town in Judah’s lowland
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Judah received in the lowland, listed with Mizpah and Joktheel ([[@6015033-6015038|Josh 15:33-38]]).

column5: A Levite city in the tribe of Zebulun
column7: It was one of the cities from the tribe of Zebulun given to the Levites of the children of Merari ([[@6021034-6021035|Josh 21:34-35]]). Some think it is the same place as 'Rimmono' in 1 Chronicles ([[@13006077|1 Chr 6:77]]).

column5: A town in the south of Judah
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Judah received in the South, near the border of Edom, listed with Kinah and Adadah ([[@6015021-6015022|Josh 15:21-22]]).

column5: Daughter of Jacob and Leah
column7: She was the daughter born to Jacob and Leah ([[@1030021|Gen 30:21]]). While Jacob's family was staying in the land of Shechem, Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite took Dinah and violated her ([[@1034002|Gen 34:2]]). Then Dinah's brothers Simeon and Levi took their swords, came upon the city, and killed all the males ([[@1034025|Gen 34:25]]). Jacob feared that trouble would come on him because of this, and before he died he rebuked the fierce anger of these two sons ([[@1034030|Gen 34:30]]; [[@1049005-1049007|Gen 49:5-7]]).

column5: A group that accused the people of Jerusalem
column7: They were one of the groups that joined Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe when they wrote a letter to King Artaxerxes accusing the people of Jerusalem ([[@15004008-15004009|Ezra 4:8-9]]).

column5: City of Bela, king of Edom
column7: It was the city of Bela the son of Beor, who reigned in the land of Edom before any king reigned over Israel ([[@1036031-1036032|Gen 36:31-32]]; [[@13001043|1 Chr 1:43]]).

column5: A member of the Areopagus who believed in Athens
column7: He heard Paul in Athens and believed. The Bible calls him "Dionysius the Areopagite" ([[@44017034|Acts 17:34]]).

column5: A man who refused to welcome the elder and his companions
column7: In the church, "Diotrephes, who loves to be first among them," refused to welcome the elder who wrote the letter and his companions. He even threw out of the church those who wanted to welcome the brothers ([[@64001009-64001010|3 John 1:9-10]]).

column5: A Horite chief among the sons of Seir
column7: He was a chief of the Horites among the sons of Seir in the land of Edom ([[@1036021|Gen 36:21]]). His children were Uz and Aran ([[@1036028|Gen 36:28]]).

column5: A Horite chief among the sons of Seir
column7: He was a chief of the Horites among the sons of Seir in the land of Edom ([[@1036021|Gen 36:21]]; [[@1036030|Gen 36:30]]). Among Anah's children there was also a Dishon of the same name ([[@1036025|Gen 36:25]]).

column5: Son of Anah the Horite
column7: He was a child of Anah the son of Zibeon, and a brother of Oholibamah. Anah was the one who found the hot springs in the wilderness while he was feeding his father’s donkeys ([[@1036024-1036025|Gen 36:24-25]]).

column5: An oak near Shechem
column7: When Abimelech attacked Shechem, Gaal saw a company of soldiers coming "by the way of the oak of Meonenim" ([[@7009035-7009037|Judg 9:35-37]]).

column5: A place near where Moses spoke to Israel
column7: It is named along with Paran, Hazeroth, and others in describing the place where Moses spoke to Israel in the wilderness, in the Arabah beyond the Jordan ([[@5001001|Deut 1:1]]).

column5: Son of Javan
column7: He was a grandson of Noah's son Japheth. A son of Japheth's son Javan, he was the brother of Elishah, Tarshish, and Kittim ([[@1010002|Gen 10:2]], 4; [[@13001007|1 Chr 1:7]]).

column5: Father of the prophet Eliezer
column7: A man of Mareshah, he was the father of Eliezer, who prophesied that Jehoshaphat’s ships would be wrecked because he had joined with Ahaziah ([[@14020037|2 Chr 20:37]]).

column5: Grandfather of the judge Tola
column7: A man of Issachar, he was the grandfather of Tola, who arose after Abimelech to save Israel. Tola was the son of Puah, the son of Dodo ([[@7010001|Judg 10:1]]).

column5: Father of Eleazar, one of David’s mighty men
column7: He was an Ahohite, the father of Eleazar, one of David’s three mighty men ([[@13011012|1 Chr 11:12]]). In 2 Samuel he is called 'Dodai' ([[@10023009|2 Sam 23:9]]).

column5: Father of Elhanan, one of David's mighty men
column7: A man of Bethlehem, he was the father of Elhanan, one of David's thirty mighty men ([[@10023024|2 Sam 23:24]]; [[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]).

column5: The Edomite who killed the priests
column7: He was an Edomite, the chief of Saul's herdsmen ([[@9021007|1 Sam 21:7]]). He reported to Saul about Ahimelech, who had helped David, and killed eighty-five priests ([[@9022009|1 Sam 22:9]]; [[@9022018|1 Sam 22:18]]).

column5: An animal for carrying loads and riding
column7: The donkey was an animal that carried loads and that people rode, and it appears very often in the Bible. Saul set out with a servant to look for the donkeys his father Kish had lost ([[@9009003|1 Sam 9:3]]). There was also the time the LORD opened the mouth of Balaam's donkey, and the donkey spoke to Balaam ([[@4022028|Num 22:28]]). Zechariah foretold that the King would come lowly and riding on the colt of a donkey, and this word was fulfilled when Jesus had a donkey and a colt brought to him and sat on them ([[@38009009|Zech 9:9]]; [[@40021005-40021007|Matt 21:5-7]]).

column5: A campsite in the wilderness
column7: It was where Israel camped after leaving the wilderness of Sin. From Dophkah they set out and camped at Alush ([[@4033012-4033013|Num 33:12-13]]).

column5: A town Manasseh could not drive out
column7: It was a Canaanite town on the heights to the west ([[@6011002|Josh 11:2]]). It belonged to Manasseh, but they could not drive out its inhabitants ([[@6017011|Josh 17:11]]; [[@7001027|Judg 1:27]]).

column5: The town where Elisha was staying
column7: When the king of Syria tried to capture Elisha, Elisha was in Dothan, and the Syrian army came by night and surrounded the city ([[@12006013-12006014|2 Kgs 6:13-14]]). Dothan was also where Joseph found his brothers ([[@1037017|Gen 37:17]]).

column5: A well Nehemiah passed by night
column7: Nehemiah went out by night through the Valley Gate, past the jackal’s well, to the Dung Gate, inspecting the broken-down walls of Jerusalem ([[@16002013|Neh 2:13]]).

column5: An offering of poured-out wine
column7: A drink offering was an offering made to God by pouring out something such as wine. Jacob set up a pillar of stone in the place where God had spoken with him, and he poured out a drink offering on it and poured oil on it ([[@1035014|Gen 35:14]]). The law said that when a lamb was offered as a burnt offering, a fourth part of a hin of wine was to be offered as a drink offering along with the fine flour and oil ([[@2029040|Exod 29:40]]). Paul compared his own life to a drink offering poured out on the sacrifice of the believers' faith, saying he would rejoice even if he were poured out that way, and he also said that the time of his departure was near ([[@50002017|Phil 2:17]]; [[@55004006|2 Tim 4:6]]).

column5: Felix’s Jewish wife
column7: She was the wife of Felix and a Jewish woman. She came with Felix and heard Paul speak about faith in Christ Jesus ([[@44024024|Acts 24:24]]).

column5: Son of Ishmael
column7: He was one of the twelve sons of Abraham's son Ishmael. These sons became twelve princes according to their tribes ([[@1025014|Gen 25:14]], 16; [[@13001030|1 Chr 1:30]]).

column5: A town in Judah’s hill country
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Judah received in the hill country, listed with Arab and Eshan ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015052|Josh 15:52]]).

column5: A place named in Isaiah’s warning
column7: In the message that begins "The burden of Dumah", someone calls to the watchman out of Seir, asking, "what of the night?" ([[@23021011-23021012|Isa 21:11-12]]).

column5: A gate in the wall of Jerusalem
column7: It was a gate of Jerusalem that Nehemiah passed when he inspected the wall at night ([[@16002013|Neh 2:13]]). Malchijah the son of Rechab repaired this gate ([[@16003014|Neh 3:14]]).

column5: The plain where Nebuchadnezzar set up a gold image
column7: This is the plain in the province of Babylon where King Nebuchadnezzar set up an image of gold sixty cubits high and six cubits wide ([[@27003001|Dan 3:1]]).

column5: Land east of Israel and its peoples
column7: It is a word for the direction of the sunrise, that is, the land to the east of Israel. On his way to his uncle Laban, Jacob came to "the land of the children of the east" ([[@1029001|Gen 29:1]]). In the time of the judges, the 'children of the east,' along with the Midianites and Amalekites, came up against Israel every time they had sown and destroyed the produce of the land ([[@7006003-7006004|Judg 6:3-4]]). They were as many as locusts, but God drove them back through Gideon ([[@7007012|Judg 7:12]]; [[@7008010|Judg 8:10]]). Job too was called "the greatest of all the children of the east" ([[@18001003|Job 1:3]]).

column5: The eastern gate of Jerusalem
column7: Among those who repaired the wall in Nehemiah’s time was Shemaiah the son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the east gate ([[@16003029|Neh 3:29]]).

column5: Son of Shobal the Horite
column7: He was a son of Shobal, a Horite descended from Seir in the land of Edom ([[@1036020|Gen 36:20]], 23). In 1 Chronicles, too, he appears as a son of Shobal ([[@13001040|1 Chr 1:40]]).

column5: The mountain where the curses of the law were declared
column7: It was the mountain facing Mount Gerizim, and Moses commanded that when they entered Canaan they should set the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal ([[@5011029|Deut 11:29]]). He also told them that after crossing the Jordan they should set up large stones on Mount Ebal, coat them with plaster, and write the words of the law on them ([[@5027004-5027008|Deut 27:4-8]]). Joshua did as he was told and built an altar to the LORD on Mount Ebal ([[@6008030|Josh 8:30]]), and the people heard the words of the law with half of them standing in front of Mount Gerizim and half in front of Mount Ebal ([[@6008033-6008034|Josh 8:33-34]]).

column5: Father of Gaal, who opposed Abimelech
column7: He was the father of Gaal, who rose against Abimelech in Shechem ([[@7009026|Judg 9:26]]). His son Gaal stirred up the men of Shechem, saying, "Who is Abimelech" ([[@7009028|Judg 9:28]]).

column5: A descendant of Adin who returned with Ezra
column7: He was the head of the descendants of Adin who came up from Babylon with Ezra, and the son of Jonathan. Fifty men came with him ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008006|Ezra 8:6]]).

column5: Ethiopian eunuch who rescued Jeremiah from the pit
column7: He was a eunuch in the royal palace of Judah, an Ethiopian. When he heard that Jeremiah had been thrown into a muddy pit, he went to the king and told him that Jeremiah would die of hunger there ([[@24038007-24038009|Jer 38:7-9]]). At the king's command he took thirty men, let rags and worn-out clothes down by ropes, had Jeremiah put them under his armpits, and pulled him out ([[@24038010-24038013|Jer 38:10-13]]). Because he trusted in God, the LORD promised that on the day Jerusalem fell he would not die by the sword but would be saved ([[@24039016-24039018|Jer 39:16-18]]).

column5: The stone of help Samuel set up
column7: This is where Israel camped to fight the Philistines ([[@9004001|1 Sam 4:1]]). Later Samuel set up a stone and named it Ebenezer, saying, "The LORD helped us until now" ([[@9007012|1 Sam 7:12]]).

column5: Descendant of Shem, father of Peleg and Joktan
column7: Eber was a descendant of Noah's son Shem and the son of Shelah ([[@1011014|Gen 11:14]]). The Bible introduces Shem as "the father of all the children of Eber", giving Eber's family special notice ([[@1010021|Gen 10:21]]). Eber had two sons, Peleg and Joktan, and it is recorded that in Peleg's days "the earth was divided" ([[@1010025|Gen 10:25]]). He also appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus ([[@42003035|Luke 3:35]]). Some scholars think the name 'Hebrew' comes from Eber.

column5: A Gadite who lived in Bashan
column7: He was one of seven relatives among the clans of the descendants of Gad who lived in the land of Bashan ([[@13005011-13005013|1 Chr 5:11-13]]). They were recorded in the genealogies in the days of Jotham and Jeroboam ([[@13005017|1 Chr 5:17]]).

column5: Son of Elpaal of Benjamin
column7: He was a son of Elpaal of the tribe of Benjamin, and a brother of Misham and Shemed ([[@13008012|1 Chr 8:12]]). One of these brothers built Ono and Lod with their towns.

column5: Son of Shashak of Benjamin
column7: His name appears among the sons of Shashak in the genealogy of Benjamin. These men were heads of families who lived in Jerusalem ([[@13008022-13008028|1 Chr 8:22-28]]).

column5: Head of the priestly family of Amok under Joiakim
column7: In the days of Joiakim, he was the head of the family of Amok among the heads of priestly families ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012020|Neh 12:20]]).

column5: A town of Issachar
column7: It was one of the towns in the land that the tribe of Issachar received by lot, listed with Rabbith and Kishion ([[@6019017-6019020|Josh 19:17-20]]).

column5: Korah's descendant, ancestor of a gatekeeper family
column7: He was a Levite descended from Korah ([[@13006037|1 Chr 6:37]]). Shallum the son of Kore, who guarded the gates of the tabernacle, was his descendant ([[@13009019|1 Chr 9:19]]).

column5: The Median palace where Cyrus’s decree was found
column7: When King Darius had a search made for the decree, a scroll was found in the palace at Achmetha (Ecbatana) in the province of Media. In it was King Cyrus’s decree that the temple should be built ([[@15006001-15006003|Ezra 6:1-3]]).

column5: Where God placed the first man in a garden
column7: Eden is where the LORD God planted a garden in the east and put the first man he had made ([[@1002008|Gen 2:8]]). In the middle of the garden stood the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil, and a river flowing out of Eden watered the garden and from there divided into four rivers ([[@1002009-1002010|Gen 2:9-10]]). Among them the rivers Hiddekel and Euphrates are named, but scholars differ on the exact location ([[@1002014|Gen 2:14]]). After the man sinned, God sent him out of the garden and placed cherubim and a flaming sword to guard the way to the tree of life ([[@1003024|Gen 3:24]]).

column5: Land of the children of Eden, destroyed by Assyria
column7: When the king of Assyria listed the nations his fathers had destroyed, he named the children of Eden who were in Telassar ([[@12019010-12019012|2 Kgs 19:10-12]]; [[@23037012|Isa 37:12]]). Eden also appears among the places that traded with Tyre ([[@26027023|Ezek 27:23]]).

column5: A Levite who cleansed the temple under Hezekiah
column7: He was the son of Joah, a Gershonite. In Hezekiah’s day he was one of the Levites who arose with their brothers to cleanse the LORD’s house ([[@14029012|2 Chr 29:12]]; [[@14029015|2 Chr 29:15]]).

column5: A Levite who distributed offerings under Hezekiah
column7: In Hezekiah’s day he served under Kore, who was over the offerings, and was one of those who gave portions to their brothers by divisions in the cities of the priests ([[@14031014-14031015|2 Chr 31:14-15]]).

column5: A town in the south of Judah
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Judah received in the South, near the border of Edom. It is listed with Kabzeel and Jagur ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]).

column5: Son of Beriah of Benjamin
column7: His name appears among the sons of Beriah in the genealogy of Benjamin ([[@13008015-13008016|1 Chr 8:15-16]]). These men were heads of families who lived in Jerusalem ([[@13008028|1 Chr 8:28]]).

column5: Son of Mushi, a Merarite
column7: A Levite descended from Merari, he was one of the three sons of Mushi. His brothers were Mahli and Jerimoth ([[@13023021|1 Chr 23:21]], 23; [[@13024030|1 Chr 24:30]]).

column5: The nation founded by Esau's descendants
column7: It is another name for Esau, Jacob's older brother, and the name of his descendants' nation. Because Esau asked for the red stew, it is recorded, "Therefore his name was called Edom" ([[@1025030|Gen 25:30]]). Esau, that is Edom, lived in the hill country of Seir ([[@1036008|Gen 36:8]]). At the Exodus the king of Edom refused to let Israel pass through his land ([[@4020021|Num 20:21]]). Obadiah rebuked Edom for the violence it did to its brother Jacob ([[@31001010|Obad 1:10]]).

column5: Where Moses defeated Og king of Bashan
column7: It was one of the towns east of the Jordan where Og king of Bashan reigned ([[@6013012|Josh 13:12]]). When Israel went up by the way of Bashan, Og came out with all his people to fight them at Edrei ([[@4021033|Num 21:33]]). The LORD told Moses not to fear Og and delivered him into Moses' hand, and Israel took possession of his land ([[@4021034-4021035|Num 21:34-35]]). This land later went to the children of Machir the son of Manasseh ([[@6013031|Josh 13:31]]).

column5: Wife of David, mother of Ithream
column7: A wife of David, she bore his sixth son, Ithream, in Hebron ([[@10003005|2 Sam 3:5]]; [[@13003003|1 Chr 3:3]]).

column5: A place named in Isaiah’s warning to Moab
column7: It is a place in Moab mentioned in Isaiah’s message against Moab, which says the wailing reaches "to Eglaim" ([[@23015008|Isa 15:8]]).

column5: Town of Moab
column7: In the prophecy about Moab, it appears as a place to which Moab's nobles flee ([[@23015005|Isa 15:5]]). It also appears in Jeremiah ([[@24048034|Jer 48:34]]).

column5: A lowland town of Judah destroyed by Joshua
column7: It was a Canaanite town in the lowland of Judah, later included in the list of towns of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015039|Josh 15:39]]). Debir king of Eglon answered the call of Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem and attacked Gibeon with four other kings ([[@6010003-6010005|Josh 10:3-5]]). After striking Lachish, Joshua went on to Eglon, took the city, and utterly destroyed everyone in it ([[@6010034-6010035|Josh 10:34-35]]). It shares only its name with Eglon, the king of Moab in the time of the judges.

column5: A king of Moab who oppressed Israel
column7: He was the king of Moab whom the LORD strengthened against Israel ([[@7003012|Judg 3:12]]). Israel served him for eighteen years, and the LORD raised up Ehud as their savior ([[@7003014-7003015|Judg 3:14-15]]).

column5: A son of Ham
column7: He was a son of Ham, Noah's son, and in these verses he is called Mizraim ([[@1010006|Gen 10:6]]). His sons included Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, and Naphtuhim ([[@1010013|Gen 10:13]]).

column5: A great nation where Israel lived as slaves
column7: It was a great nation southwest of Israel. Abram once went down there to escape a famine ([[@1012010|Gen 12:10]]), and in Joseph's time Jacob's whole household moved there to live. Later the children of Israel became slaves there, and God brought them out after sending many plagues ([[@2012051|Exod 12:51]]). God revealed himself as "the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage" ([[@2020002|Exod 20:2]]).

column5: The sea of Egypt named by Isaiah
column7: Isaiah prophesied that the LORD would "utterly destroy the tongue of the Egyptian sea" and strike the River so that people could cross over in sandals ([[@23011015|Isa 11:15]]).

column5: Left-handed judge who killed King Eglon
column7: He was the son of Gera, a Benjamite, and a left-handed judge of Israel ([[@7003015|Judg 3:15]]). After Israel had served Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years, the LORD raised him up as a savior ([[@7003014-7003015|Judg 3:14-15]]). Ehud strapped a double-edged sword a cubit long under his clothing on his right thigh, went in, drew the sword with his left hand, and stabbed the king ([[@7003016|Judg 3:16]], 21). Afterward he held the fords of the Jordan and struck down about ten thousand Moabites, and the land had rest for eighty years ([[@7003028-7003030|Judg 3:28-30]]).

column5: Son of Bilhan of Benjamin
column7: He was a grandson of Jediael the son of Benjamin, and a son of Bilhan. He is a different person from Ehud the judge ([[@13007006|1 Chr 7:6]]; [[@13007010|1 Chr 7:10]]).

column5: Grandson of Jerahmeel, son of Ram
column7: He was a son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah, and a brother of Maaz and Jamin ([[@13002025|1 Chr 2:25]]; [[@13002027|1 Chr 2:27]]).

column5: Northernmost of the five Philistine cities
column7: It was the northernmost of the five great cities of the Philistines. It fell within the border of Judah and was later assigned to the land of the tribe of Dan ([[@6019043|Josh 19:43]]), but it went back into the hands of the Philistines. When the ark of the covenant came to Ekron after Ashdod and Gath, the people cried out in fear that it had been brought to kill them ([[@9005010|1 Sam 5:10]]). In Elijah's time, when Ahaziah king of Israel fell sick, he sent messengers to inquire of "Baal Zebub, the god of Ekron" and was rebuked for it ([[@12001002-12001003|2 Kgs 1:2-3]]). Zephaniah prophesied that "Ekron will be rooted up" ([[@36002004|Zeph 2:4]]).

column5: A place by the wilderness reached by Chedorlaomer
column7: Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him struck the Horites in Mount Seir and went as far as El Paran, which is by the wilderness ([[@1014005-1014006|Gen 14:5-6]]).

column5: Father of Shimei, Solomon’s officer
column7: He was the father of Shimei, one of Solomon’s twelve officers, who was in charge of Benjamin ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004018|1 Kgs 4:18]]).

column5: Chief of Edom
column7: He was one of the chiefs of Edom who came from Esau. The chiefs were named according to their families and their places ([[@1036040-1036041|Gen 36:40-41]]; [[@13001052|1 Chr 1:52]]).

column5: Son of Baasha, king of Israel
column7: He was the son of Baasha who became king of Israel in Tirzah and reigned two years ([[@11016008|1 Kgs 16:8]]). While he was drunk, his servant Zimri killed him ([[@11016009-11016010|1 Kgs 16:9-10]]).

column5: Father of Hoshea, Israel's last king
column7: He was the father of Hoshea, the last king of Israel. His son Hoshea killed Pekah, became king, and reigned in Samaria nine years ([[@12015030|2 Kgs 15:30]]; [[@12017001|2 Kgs 17:1]]).

column5: A Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem
column7: He was one of the descendants of Benjamin who returned from exile and lived in Jerusalem, the son of Uzzi and grandson of Michri ([[@13009003|1 Chr 9:3]]; [[@13009007-13009008|1 Chr 9:7-8]]).

column5: The valley where David killed Goliath
column7: This is the valley where Saul and the men of Israel camped and lined up against the Philistines ([[@9017002|1 Sam 17:2]]). David killed Goliath the Philistine here ([[@9021009|1 Sam 21:9]]).

column5: Son of Shem
column7: A son of Noah's son Shem, his name comes first among Shem's sons. His brothers were Asshur, Arpachshad, Lud, and Aram ([[@1010022|Gen 10:22]]; [[@13001017|1 Chr 1:17]]).

column5: Ancient kingdom east of Babylon
column7: It was a kingdom named after Elam the son of Shem, in the hill country east of Babylon ([[@1010022|Gen 10:22]]). In Abraham's time Chedorlaomer king of Elam came to make war together with several other kings ([[@1014001|Gen 14:1]]). Daniel saw a vision in the citadel of Susa in Elam ([[@27008002|Dan 8:2]]), and the prophets also spoke of judgment and restoration for Elam. At Pentecost, Elamites too heard the mighty works of God in their own language in Jerusalem ([[@44002009|Acts 2:9]]).

column5: Son of Shashak of Benjamin
column7: His name appears among the sons of Shashak in the genealogy of Benjamin. These men were heads of families who lived in Jerusalem ([[@13008024-13008028|1 Chr 8:24-28]]).

column5: A gatekeeper in David’s time
column7: He was the fifth son of Meshelemiah of the Korahites and was counted among the divisions of the temple gatekeepers ([[@13026001-13026003|1 Chr 26:1-3]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family that returned from Babylon
column7: It is the name of the ancestor of one of the families that returned from captivity in Babylon. The descendants of Elam who came back with Zerubbabel numbered one thousand two hundred fifty-four ([[@15002007|Ezra 2:7]]; [[@16007012|Neh 7:12]]). Among those who came up with Ezra were also Jeshaiah of the sons of Elam and seventy men with him ([[@15008007|Ezra 8:7]]). Shecaniah, one of the sons of Elam, confessed the sin of marrying foreign wives and said, "there is hope for Israel" ([[@15010002|Ezra 10:2]]).

column5: A leader who sealed the covenant under Nehemiah
column7: In Nehemiah’s time his name appears among the chiefs of the people who made a sure covenant and sealed it ([[@16009038|Neh 9:38]]; [[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]).

column5: A man present at the wall’s dedication
column7: He was one of those who stood in God’s house with the companies giving thanks when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated ([[@16012040-16012042|Neh 12:40-42]]).

column5: A descendant of Pashhur who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Pashhur in the list of priests who had married foreign women ([[@15010018|Ezra 10:18]]; [[@15010022|Ezra 10:22]]).

column5: Son of Shaphan who carried Jeremiah’s letter
column7: He was the son of Shaphan. When King Zedekiah sent him to Babylon, Jeremiah entrusted to him the letter he was sending to the captives ([[@24029001-24029003|Jer 29:1-3]]).

column5: A port town on the Red Sea
column7: It was a place Israel passed by in the wilderness, together with Ezion Geber ([[@5002008|Deut 2:8]]). Azariah king of Judah built Elath and restored it to Judah ([[@12014022|2 Kgs 14:22]]).

column5: Son of Midian
column7: He was one of the five sons of Midian, the son of Abraham and Keturah ([[@1025001-1025002|Gen 25:1-2]], 4; [[@13001033|1 Chr 1:33]]).

column5: Elder who prophesied in the camp
column7: One of the seventy elders Moses gathered, he did not go out to the Tent, yet the Spirit rested on him and he prophesied in the camp ([[@4011024-4011026|Num 11:24-26]]). Moses said he wished that the LORD would make all his people prophets ([[@4011029|Num 11:29]]).

column5: Older leader who guided the people
column7: An elder was an older person with wisdom and authority who led the people. After God called Moses, Moses first gathered the elders of Israel and passed on God's words to them ([[@2003016|Exod 3:16]]). In the wilderness God had seventy of the people's elders gathered to stand with Moses at the Tent of Meeting ([[@4011016|Num 11:16]]). The early church also appointed elders in every church, and elders were to care for God's flock not under compulsion but willingly ([[@44014023|Acts 14:23]]; [[@60005002|1 Pet 5:2]]).

column5: An Ephraimite killed by the men of Gath
column7: A descendant of Ephraim, he went down to take the livestock of the men of Gath and was killed by the men born in that land. His father Ephraim mourned many days ([[@13007021-13007022|1 Chr 7:21-22]]).

column5: A man in Ephraim’s genealogy
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Ephraim as the son of Tahath. His son was also named Tahath ([[@13007020|1 Chr 7:20]]).

column5: A town in Moab built by the Reubenites
column7: It was a town built by the children of Reuben ([[@4032037|Num 32:37]]). Isaiah said that at Moab's judgment Heshbon and Elealeh would cry out ([[@23015004|Isa 15:4]]).

column5: Descendant of Judah, son of Helez
column7: A descendant of Judah, he was the son of Helez and the father of Sismai. He appears in the genealogy of Judah in 1 Chronicles ([[@13002039-13002040|1 Chr 2:39-40]]).

column5: A descendant in Saul’s family
column7: In the genealogy of Saul’s family he appears as the son of Raphah, and his son was Azel ([[@13008037|1 Chr 8:37]]). In 1 Chronicles 9 his father’s name is given as 'Rephaiah' ([[@13009043|1 Chr 9:43]]).

column5: Aaron's son, high priest after Aaron
column7: He was the third son of Aaron and Elisheba ([[@2006023|Exod 6:23]]). After his older brothers Nadab and Abihu died for offering strange fire, he served as priest together with his younger brother Ithamar ([[@4003004|Num 3:4]]). When Aaron died on Mount Hor, Eleazar received Aaron's garments and became high priest ([[@4020028|Num 20:28]]). Together with Joshua he divided the land of Canaan among the tribes ([[@6014001|Josh 14:1]]).

column5: Son of Abinadab who kept the LORD’s ark
column7: The men of Kiriath Jearim brought the LORD’s ark into Abinadab’s house and consecrated his son Eleazar to keep the ark ([[@9007001|1 Sam 7:1]]).

column5: One of David's three mighty men
column7: The son of Dodai the Ahohite, he was one of David's three mighty men ([[@10023009|2 Sam 23:9]]). He struck the Philistines until his hand froze to the sword ([[@10023010|2 Sam 23:10]]).

column5: Son of Mahli, a descendant of Merari
column7: He was the son of Mahli, a descendant of Merari ([[@13023021|1 Chr 23:21]]). He died with no sons, only daughters, so the sons of his brother Kish married them ([[@13023022|1 Chr 23:22]]).

column5: A man present when the temple vessels were weighed
column7: He was the son of Phinehas. He was there when Ezra’s company arrived in Jerusalem and weighed out the silver, the gold, and the vessels ([[@15008032-15008033|Ezra 8:32-33]]).

column5: A descendant of Parosh who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Parosh in the list of those who had married foreign women ([[@15010025|Ezra 10:25]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A man present at the wall’s dedication
column7: He was one of those who stood in God’s house with the companies giving thanks when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated ([[@16012040-16012042|Neh 12:40-42]]).

column5: Man who killed Lahmi, Goliath's brother
column7: The son of Jaare-Oregim the Bethlehemite, he killed Lahmi, the brother of Goliath of Gath, in a battle with the Philistines ([[@10021019|2 Sam 21:19]]). In 1 Chronicles he appears as 'the son of Jair' ([[@13020005|1 Chr 20:5]]).

column5: One of David's thirty mighty men
column7: The son of Dodo of Bethlehem, he was one of David's thirty mighty men ([[@10023024|2 Sam 23:24]]; [[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]).

column5: Priest of Shiloh who judged forty years
column7: He was the priest when God's ark was at Shiloh. When Hannah prayed silently in the temple, he at first thought she was drunk, but later he blessed her, saying, "Go in peace" ([[@9001017|1 Sam 1:17]]). His two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were wicked, and because Eli did not restrain them, God said he would judge his house ([[@9003013|1 Sam 3:13]]). When he heard the news that God's ark had been captured, he fell backward from his seat, broke his neck, and died. He had judged Israel for forty years ([[@9004018|1 Sam 4:18]]).

column5: Leader of the tribe of Zebulun in the wilderness
column7: He was the son of Helon and the leader of the children of Zebulun in the wilderness ([[@4001009|Num 1:9]]; [[@4002007|Num 2:7]]). On the third day he brought the offering on behalf of the children of Zebulun ([[@4007024|Num 7:24]]).

column5: Father of Dathan and Abiram
column7: He was the son of Pallu, a descendant of Reuben ([[@4026008|Num 26:8]]). Dathan and Abiram, who rose up against Moses with Korah, were his sons ([[@4016001|Num 16:1]]).

column5: Jesse's firstborn, David's oldest brother
column7: He was Jesse's firstborn son, and when Samuel saw him he thought he was the one the LORD would anoint, but he was not chosen ([[@9016006-9016007|1 Sam 16:6-7]]). Before Goliath, he grew angry at David and scolded him, saying, "you have come down that you might see the battle" ([[@9017028|1 Sam 17:28]]).

column5: A Gadite warrior who joined David
column7: He was the third of the Gadite warriors who came to David while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001|1 Chr 12:1]]; [[@13012008-13012009|1 Chr 12:8-9]]).

column5: A Levite musician in David’s time
