column7: He was one of the Levites appointed next after the singers when David brought up the ark ([[@13015018|1 Chr 15:18]]). He was assigned to play a stringed instrument set to Alamoth ([[@13015020|1 Chr 15:20]]).

column5: A son of David born in Jerusalem
column7: He was one of the sons born to David in Jerusalem ([[@10005013-10005016|2 Sam 5:13-16]]). In 1 Chronicles 14 he is called 'Beeliada' ([[@13014007|1 Chr 14:7]]).

column5: Father of Rezon, Solomon’s adversary
column7: He was the father of Rezon, whom God raised up as an adversary to Solomon. Rezon had fled from Hadadezer king of Zobah ([[@11011023|1 Kgs 11:23]]).

column5: A mighty warrior of Benjamin under Jehoshaphat
column7: In Jehoshaphat’s time he was a mighty man of valor from Benjamin who led two hundred thousand men armed with bow and shield ([[@14017017|2 Chr 17:17]]).

column5: One of David's mighty men, a Shaalbonite
column7: A Shaalbonite, he is named on the list of David's mighty men ([[@10023032|2 Sam 23:32]]; [[@13011033|1 Chr 11:33]]).

column5: Palace administrator under King Hezekiah
column7: He was the son of Hilkiah and was over the household in King Hezekiah's time ([[@12018018|2 Kgs 18:18]]). When the Assyrian Rabshakeh threatened Jerusalem, he went out with Shebna the scribe and others to hear him, then came to Hezekiah with his clothes torn and told him what was said ([[@12018037|2 Kgs 18:37]]). Hezekiah sent him, covered with sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah ([[@12019002|2 Kgs 19:2]]). Isaiah prophesied that God would call "my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah" in place of Shebna and entrust him with the key of David's house ([[@23022015-23022022|Isa 22:15-22]]).

column5: A priest with a trumpet at the wall’s dedication
column7: He was one of the priests who held trumpets when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated with thanksgiving in Nehemiah’s time ([[@16012040-16012041|Neh 12:40-41]]).

column5: Father of Jonan in Luke’s genealogy
column7: In the genealogy of Jesus recorded in Luke, he appears as the father of Jonan and the son of Melea ([[@42003030-42003031|Luke 3:30-31]]).

column5: Father of Bathsheba
column7: He was the father of Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah the Hittite ([[@10011003|2 Sam 11:3]]). In 1 Chronicles he appears as 'Ammiel' ([[@13003005|1 Chr 3:5]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men, son of Ahithophel
column7: He appears in the list of David’s mighty men and was the son of Ahithophel the Gilonite ([[@10023008|2 Sam 23:8]]; [[@10023034|2 Sam 23:34]]).

column5: Leader of the tribe of Gad in the wilderness
column7: He was the son of Deuel and the leader of the children of Gad in the wilderness ([[@4001014|Num 1:14]]). On the sixth day he brought the offering on behalf of the children of Gad ([[@4007042|Num 7:42]]).

column5: Chief of the Gershonite clan
column7: He was the son of Lael and the prince of the Gershonite clan of the Levites. The Gershonites were in charge of the tabernacle, the tent, its covering, and other things ([[@4003024-4003025|Num 3:24-25]]).

column5: Son of Elioenai in David’s royal line
column7: In the family line of Jeconiah the captive, he was one of the seven sons of Elioenai the son of Neariah ([[@13003017|1 Chr 3:17]]; [[@13003023-13003024|1 Chr 3:23-24]]).

column5: Priest of the eleventh division
column7: When the priestly divisions were assigned by lot in David’s time, he was the one chosen eleventh ([[@13024005|1 Chr 24:5]]; [[@13024012|1 Chr 24:12]]).

column5: Father of Jehohanan
column7: When Ezra was grieving over the problem of foreign wives, he went into the room of Jehohanan the son of Eliashib and neither ate bread nor drank water ([[@15010006|Ezra 10:6]]).

column5: A singer who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears as a singer in the list of those who had married foreign women ([[@15010024|Ezra 10:24]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Zattu who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Zattu in the list of those who had married foreign women ([[@15010027|Ezra 10:27]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Bani in the list of those who had married foreign women ([[@15010034-15010036|Ezra 10:34-36]]).

column5: High priest in Nehemiah's time
column7: The high priest in Nehemiah's time, he built the sheep gate with his brothers the priests ([[@16003001|Neh 3:1]]). The door of his house is also mentioned in the record of the wall repairs ([[@16003020|Neh 3:20]]).

column5: High priest in Nehemiah’s time
column7: He was the high priest in Nehemiah’s day, and with his brothers the priests he built the sheep gate ([[@16003001|Neh 3:1]]). One of his grandsons, a son of Joiada, became the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite, and Nehemiah drove him away ([[@16013028|Neh 13:28]]).

column5: Priest who gave Tobiah a room
column7: A priest in charge of the rooms of God's house, he was allied with Tobiah ([[@16013004|Neh 13:4]]). When Nehemiah learned that he had prepared a room for Tobiah in the courts of God's house, he set it right ([[@16013007-16013008|Neh 13:7-8]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a singer
column7: He was a son of Heman, who served as a singer in David's time ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]). The twentieth lot fell to him, and he served in that turn ([[@13025027|1 Chr 25:27]]).

column5: Benjamin’s leader in dividing the land
column7: Among the leaders chosen from each tribe to divide the land of Canaan, he was the leader for the tribe of Benjamin, the son of Chislon ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034021|Num 34:21]]).

column5: Seventh son of Meshelemiah
column7: He was the seventh son of Meshelemiah of the Korahites and was counted among the divisions of the temple gatekeepers in David’s time ([[@13026001-13026003|1 Chr 26:1-3]]).

column5: A descendant of Pahathmoab who returned with Ezra
column7: He was the head of the descendants of Pahathmoab who came up from Babylon with Ezra, and the son of Zerahiah. Two hundred men came with him ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008004|Ezra 8:4]]).

column5: A leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh
column7: He was one of the heads of the half-tribe of Manasseh, who lived from Bashan to Mount Hermon, and was among the "mighty men of valor, famous men" ([[@13005023-13005024|1 Chr 5:23-24]]).

column5: Son of Shimei of Benjamin
column7: His name appears among the sons of Shimei in the genealogy of Benjamin. These men were heads of families who lived in Jerusalem ([[@13008020-13008021|1 Chr 8:20-21]]; [[@13008028|1 Chr 8:28]]).

column5: Son of Shashak of Benjamin
column7: His name appears among the sons of Shashak in the genealogy of Benjamin. These men were heads of families who lived in Jerusalem ([[@13008022-13008028|1 Chr 8:22-28]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men, a Mahavite
column7: He was a Mahavite named in the list of David’s mighty men ([[@13011010|1 Chr 11:10]]; [[@13011046|1 Chr 11:46]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men
column7: His name appears with Obed and Jaasiel at the end of the list of David’s mighty men ([[@13011010|1 Chr 11:10]]; [[@13011047|1 Chr 11:47]]).

column5: A Gadite warrior who joined David
column7: He was the seventh of the Gadite warriors who came to David while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001|1 Chr 12:1]]; [[@13012008-13012011|1 Chr 12:8-11]]).

column5: Chief of the sons of Hebron
column7: A chief of the Levite sons of Hebron, he led eighty of his brothers ([[@13015009|1 Chr 15:9]]). He was one of the Levite leaders David called together to bring up the ark of the covenant ([[@13015011-13015012|1 Chr 15:11-12]]).

column5: A Levite overseeing offerings under Hezekiah
column7: In Hezekiah’s time he was one of those who oversaw the offerings and tithes brought to the temple, serving under the Levite Conaniah and his brother Shimei ([[@14031012-14031013|2 Chr 31:12-13]]).

column5: Son of Shimei of Benjamin
column7: His name appears among the sons of Shimei in the genealogy of Benjamin. These men were heads of families who lived in Jerusalem ([[@13008020-13008021|1 Chr 8:20-21]]; [[@13008028|1 Chr 8:28]]).

column5: The man of Damascus Abram called his heir
column7: Childless Abram said that "Eliezer of Damascus" would inherit his estate ([[@1015002|Gen 15:2]]). God said that one who would come from Abram’s own body would be his heir ([[@1015004|Gen 15:4]]).

column5: Son of Moses
column7: He was the son of Moses and Zipporah, named so because Moses said, "My father’s God was my help and delivered me from Pharaoh’s sword" ([[@2018002-2018004|Exod 18:2-4]]). His son was Rehabiah ([[@13023017|1 Chr 23:17]]).

column5: Son of Becher of Benjamin
column7: He was one of the nine sons of Becher the son of Benjamin, a head of his father’s house and a mighty man of valor ([[@13007006|1 Chr 7:6]]; [[@13007008-13007009|1 Chr 7:8-9]]).

column5: A priest who blew a trumpet before the ark
column7: He was one of the priests who blew trumpets before God’s ark when David brought the ark of the covenant up from the house of Obed-Edom ([[@13015024-13015025|1 Chr 15:24-25]]).

column5: Ruler of Reuben in David’s time
column7: He was the son of Zichri, and among those over the tribes of Israel in David’s time he was the ruler of the Reubenites ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]).

column5: A man who prophesied against Jehoshaphat
column7: He was the son of Dodavahu of Mareshah. When Jehoshaphat joined with wicked King Ahaziah, he prophesied that the LORD would destroy his ships, and the ships were wrecked ([[@14020035-14020037|2 Chr 20:35-37]]).

column5: A leader Ezra sent for
column7: He was one of the leaders Ezra sent for at the river that runs to Ahava when he found that none of the sons of Levi were there ([[@15008015-15008016|Ezra 8:15-16]]).

column5: A priest who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the priests who had married foreign women, as one of the brothers of Jeshua the son of Jozadak ([[@15010018|Ezra 10:18]]).

column5: A Levite who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the Levites in the list of those who had married foreign women ([[@15010023|Ezra 10:23]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Harim who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Harim in the list of those who had married foreign women ([[@15010031|Ezra 10:31]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: An ancestor in Luke’s genealogy
column7: He is one of the ancestors in the genealogy of Jesus recorded in Luke, the son of Jorim ([[@42003029|Luke 3:29]]).

column5: Solomon’s scribe
column7: He was a son of Shisha and, with Ahijah, a scribe for King Solomon. He appears in the list of Solomon’s officials ([[@11004002-11004003|1 Kgs 4:2-3]]).

column5: Grandfather of Elkanah, Samuel’s father
column7: He was the son of Tohu and the grandfather of Elkanah the Ephraimite ([[@9001001|1 Sam 1:1]]). In 1 Chronicles he is called 'Eliel' ([[@13006034|1 Chr 6:34]]).

column5: A captain of thousands from Manasseh who joined David
column7: He was one of the captains of thousands from the tribe of Manasseh who joined David as he went to Ziklag ([[@13012020|1 Chr 12:20]]).

column5: A gatekeeper descended from Obed-Edom
column7: He was one of the grandsons of Obed-Edom and a relative of Elzabad the son of Shemaiah. He was a valiant man ([[@13026007-13026008|1 Chr 26:7-8]]).

column5: David’s brother, ruler of Judah
column7: He was one of David’s brothers, and among those over the tribes of Israel in David’s time he was the ruler of Judah ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027018|1 Chr 27:18]]).

column5: Young man who spoke to Job and his friends
column7: He was the son of Barachel the Buzite, of the family of Ram ([[@18032002|Job 32:2]]). He became angry because Job justified himself rather than God, and because the three friends condemned Job without finding an answer ([[@18032002-18032003|Job 32:2-3]]). He waited patiently until the older men had finished speaking, and then he began, "I am young, and you are very old" ([[@18032006|Job 32:6]]). Elihu's speech runs from Job 32 to 37, and after it the LORD spoke to Job out of the whirlwind ([[@18038001|Job 38:1]]).

column5: The Tishbite prophet in King Ahab's time
column7: He was a prophet, a Tishbite who lived in Gilead. He told King Ahab that no rain would fall for years ([[@11017001|1 Kgs 17:1]]). While he was hiding by a brook, ravens brought him bread and meat ([[@11017006|1 Kgs 17:6]]). When he confronted the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, fire fell from heaven, and the people cried out, "The LORD, he is God!" ([[@11018039|1 Kgs 18:39]]). After a chariot of fire and horses of fire appeared, he went up into heaven by a whirlwind ([[@12002011|2 Kgs 2:11]]).

column5: Son of Jeroham of Benjamin
column7: He appears among the sons of Jeroham in the genealogy of Benjamin. These men were heads of families who lived in Jerusalem ([[@13008027-13008028|1 Chr 8:27-28]]).

column5: A descendant of Harim who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Harim in the list of those who had married foreign women ([[@15010021|Ezra 10:21]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Elam who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Elam in the list of those who had married foreign women ([[@15010026|Ezra 10:26]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men, a Harodite
column7: He was a Harodite named in the list of David’s mighty men, listed alongside Shammah, another Harodite ([[@10023008|2 Sam 23:8]]; [[@10023025|2 Sam 23:25]]).

column5: Place of twelve springs and seventy palm trees
column7: It was where Israel camped after coming out of Egypt, and there were twelve springs of water and seventy palm trees there ([[@2015027|Exod 15:27]]; [[@4033009|Num 33:9]]).

column5: Naomi's husband, a man of Bethlehem in Judah
column7: He lived in Bethlehem of Judah in the days when the judges ruled, and he was Naomi's husband. When famine came to the land, he took his wife and his two sons, Mahlon and Chilion, and went to live in the country of Moab ([[@8001001-8001002|Ruth 1:1-2]]). Elimelech died there, and later his two sons, who had married Moabite women, also died, leaving only Naomi ([[@8001003-8001005|Ruth 1:3-5]]). Later his relative Boaz bought from Naomi everything that had belonged to Elimelech and took Mahlon's wife Ruth as his wife ([[@8002001|Ruth 2:1]]; [[@8004009-8004010|Ruth 4:9-10]]).

column5: Descendant of David, son of Neariah
column7: A descendant of David, he was the son of Neariah ([[@13003023|1 Chr 3:23]]). He had seven sons, including Hodaviah ([[@13003024|1 Chr 3:24]]).

column5: A Simeonite leader in Hezekiah’s time
column7: He was one of the leaders of the descendants of Simeon. In the days of Hezekiah they went to find pasture for their flocks and settled there ([[@13004036|1 Chr 4:36]]; [[@13004038-13004041|1 Chr 4:38-41]]).

column5: Son of Becher of Benjamin
column7: He was one of the nine sons of Becher the son of Benjamin, a head of his father’s house and a mighty man of valor ([[@13007006|1 Chr 7:6]]; [[@13007008-13007009|1 Chr 7:8-9]]).

column5: A descendant of Pashhur who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Pashhur in the list of priests who had married foreign women ([[@15010018|Ezra 10:18]]; [[@15010022|Ezra 10:22]]).

column5: A descendant of Zattu who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Zattu in the list of those who had married foreign women ([[@15010027|Ezra 10:27]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A priest with a trumpet at the wall’s dedication
column7: He was one of the priests who held trumpets when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated with thanksgiving in Nehemiah’s time ([[@16012040-16012041|Neh 12:40-41]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men, son of Ur
column7: He appears in the list of David’s mighty men and was the son of Ur ([[@13011010|1 Chr 11:10]]; [[@13011035|1 Chr 11:35]]).

column5: Esau's firstborn, ancestor of Edomite chiefs
column7: He was the son Esau had by his wife Adah ([[@1036004|Gen 36:4]]). His sons were Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz, and by his concubine Timna he had Amalek ([[@1036011-1036012|Gen 36:11-12]]). The Bible calls him "Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau", and from him came many chiefs in the land of Edom, including chief Teman ([[@1036015-1036016|Gen 36:15-16]]).

column5: Temanite, one of Job's three friends
column7: He was a Temanite, a friend who came with Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite to comfort Job when they heard of the great disaster that had come on him ([[@18002011|Job 2:11]]). He was the first of the three friends to answer, and he tried to correct Job, saying, "Remember, now, who ever perished, being innocent?" ([[@18004001|Job 4:1]], 7). After that he answered Job two more times ([[@18015001|Job 15:1]]; [[@18022001|Job 22:1]]). In the end the LORD was angry with the three friends because they had not spoken of him what was right as Job had, and when Job prayed for them, the LORD accepted Job ([[@18042007-18042010|Job 42:7-10]]).

column5: Levite who played the harp before the ark
column7: He was a Levite David appointed in the second rank ([[@13015018|1 Chr 15:18]]). He was given the task of leading with harps ([[@13015021|1 Chr 15:21]]).

column5: A son of David born in Jerusalem
column7: His name comes last among the sons born to David in Jerusalem ([[@10005013-10005016|2 Sam 5:13-16]]). He also appears in the lists of David’s sons in 1 Chronicles ([[@13003008|1 Chr 3:8]]; [[@13014007|1 Chr 14:7]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men, son of Ahasbai
column7: He appears in the list of David’s mighty men and was the son of Ahasbai and grandson of the Maacathite ([[@10023008|2 Sam 23:8]]; [[@10023034|2 Sam 23:34]]).

column5: Son of Eshek in the family line of Saul
column7: He appears as the third son of Eshek in the Benjamite genealogy that traces the descendants of Saul and Jonathan ([[@13008033|1 Chr 8:33]]; [[@13008039|1 Chr 8:39]]).

column5: A descendant of Adonikam who returned with Ezra
column7: He was one of the descendants of Adonikam who came up from Babylon with Ezra, bringing sixty men along with Jeuel and Shemaiah ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008013|Ezra 8:13]]).

column5: A descendant of Hashum who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Hashum in the list of those who had married foreign women ([[@15010033|Ezra 10:33]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: The prophet who succeeded Elijah
column7: Elisha was the son of Shaphat of Abel Meholah. When Elijah called him by throwing his mantle on him as he plowed, he slaughtered his oxen, fed the people, and followed Elijah ([[@11019019-11019021|1 Kgs 19:19-21]]). As Elijah was taken up to heaven by a whirlwind, Elisha asked for a double portion of his spirit, and he took up the mantle that had fallen ([[@12002009-12002013|2 Kgs 2:9-13]]). After that he did many miracles, such as raising the Shunammite woman's dead son and healing the Syrian commander Naaman ([[@12004032-12004035|2 Kgs 4:32-35]]; [[@12005014|2 Kgs 5:14]]).

column5: Son of Javan
column7: He was a grandson of Noah's son Japheth. A son of Japheth's son Javan, his name comes before those of his brothers ([[@1010002|Gen 10:2]], 4; [[@13001007|1 Chr 1:7]]).

column5: Leader of the tribe of Ephraim, son of Ammihud
column7: He was the son of Ammihud and the leader who represented the tribe of Ephraim during the wilderness years ([[@4001010|Num 1:10]]). He was the leader of the army of Ephraim camped on the west side when Israel set up camp, and he also led Ephraim's army on the march ([[@4002018|Num 2:18]]; [[@4010022|Num 10:22]]). When the leaders brought their offerings one each day in turn, Elishama brought his on the seventh day ([[@4007048|Num 7:48]]). According to the genealogy in Chronicles, his son was Nun and his grandson was Joshua, which makes him Joshua's grandfather ([[@13007026-13007027|1 Chr 7:26-27]]).

column5: A son of David born in Jerusalem
column7: He was one of the sons born to David in Jerusalem ([[@10005013-10005016|2 Sam 5:13-16]]). He also appears in the lists of David’s sons in 1 Chronicles ([[@13003008|1 Chr 3:8]]; [[@13014007|1 Chr 14:7]]).

column5: Grandfather of Ishmael, who killed Gedaliah
column7: A member of the royal family, he was the grandfather of Ishmael, who struck down Gedaliah at Mizpah. Ishmael's father was Nethaniah ([[@12025025|2 Kgs 25:25]]; [[@24041001|Jer 41:1]]).

column5: Son of Jekamiah in Judah’s genealogy
column7: He appears near the end of the genealogy of Judah’s descendants. Shallum became the father of Jekamiah, and Jekamiah became the father of Elishama ([[@13002041|1 Chr 2:41]]).

column5: A priest Jehoshaphat sent to teach the law
column7: He was a priest whom King Jehoshaphat sent with Levites to teach from the book of the LORD’s law in the cities of Judah ([[@14017008-14017009|2 Chr 17:8-9]]).

column5: A scribe in Jehoiakim’s time
column7: He was a scribe in Jehoiakim’s day, and Baruch read Jeremiah’s scroll while the princes were gathered in his room ([[@24036012-24036015|Jer 36:12-15]]). The princes laid up the scroll in Elishama’s room ([[@24036020-24036021|Jer 36:20-21]]).

column5: A captain of hundreds in covenant with Jehoiada
column7: He was the son of Zichri and one of the captains of hundreds who entered into a covenant with Jehoiada in the seventh year. They went around Judah and gathered the Levites and the heads of families ([[@14023001-14023002|2 Chr 23:1-2]]).

column5: Aaron’s wife
column7: She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; she became Aaron’s wife and bore him Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar ([[@2006023|Exod 6:23]]).

column5: A son of David born in Jerusalem
column7: He was one of the sons born to David in Jerusalem ([[@10005013-10005015|2 Sam 5:13-15]]). He also appears in the list of David’s sons in 1 Chronicles ([[@13014005|1 Chr 14:5]]).

column5: Man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Matthew. He was the son of Achim and the father of Eleazar ([[@40001014-40001015|Matt 1:14-15]]).

column5: Wife of Zacharias, mother of John the Baptist
column7: She was a descendant of Aaron and the wife of Zacharias, a priest of the division of Abijah ([[@42001005|Luke 1:5]]). The two of them were righteous before God, but Elizabeth was barren, so they had no child and were well along in years ([[@42001006-42001007|Luke 1:6-7]]). An angel told Zacharias that his wife would bear him a son and that he should name him John ([[@42001013|Luke 1:13]]). When Mary came and greeted her, the baby leaped in Elizabeth's womb, and Elizabeth, filled with the Holy Spirit, cried out, "Blessed are you among women" ([[@42001041-42001042|Luke 1:41-42]]).

column5: A chief of the Kohathite families
column7: He was the son of Uzziel and became the chief of the families of the Kohathites ([[@4003030|Num 3:30]]). In Leviticus he appears as 'Elzaphan', and Moses called him to carry his dead relatives out of the camp ([[@3010004|Lev 10:4]]).

column5: Zebulun’s leader in dividing the land
column7: Among the leaders chosen from each tribe to divide the land of Canaan, he was the leader for the tribe of Zebulun, the son of Parnach ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034025|Num 34:25]]).

column5: Leader of the tribe of Reuben in the wilderness
column7: He was the son of Shedeur and the leader of the children of Reuben in the wilderness ([[@4001005|Num 1:5]]; [[@4002010|Num 2:10]]). On the fourth day he brought the offering on behalf of the children of Reuben ([[@4007030|Num 7:30]]).

column5: Son of Korah
column7: He was a grandson of Izhar the Levite and a son of Korah. Along with his brothers Assir and Abiasaph, he was a head of the Korahite families ([[@2006021|Exod 6:21]], 24).

column5: Father of Samuel
column7: He was an Ephraimite who lived in Ramathaim Zophim in the hill country of Ephraim, the son of Jeroham ([[@9001001|1 Sam 1:1]]). He had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah; Peninnah had children but Hannah had none, and every year he went up to Shiloh to sacrifice to the LORD of Armies ([[@9001002-9001003|1 Sam 1:2-3]]). When Hannah grieved because she had no children, he comforted her, saying, "Am I not better to you than ten sons?" ([[@9001008|1 Sam 1:8]]). The LORD remembered Hannah, and the prophet Samuel was born to Elkanah and Hannah ([[@9001019-9001020|1 Sam 1:19-20]]).

column5: Father of Amasai, a Kohathite
column7: A Levite descended from Kohath, he was the father of Amasai and Ahimoth ([[@13006025|1 Chr 6:25]]). In Heman's genealogy he appears as the son of Joel ([[@13006036|1 Chr 6:36]]).

column5: Kohathite, son of Mahath
column7: A Levite descended from Kohath, he appears in Heman's genealogy as the son of Mahath ([[@13006035|1 Chr 6:35]]). His line continues through Zophai and Nahath ([[@13006026|1 Chr 6:26]]).

column5: Grandfather of the Levite Berechiah
column7: He was the grandfather of Berechiah, a Levite who lived there after the return from exile. Berechiah was the son of Asa and grandson of Elkanah, and he lived in the villages of the Netophathites ([[@13009014-13009016|1 Chr 9:14-16]]).

column5: A Korahite who joined David at Ziklag
column7: He was a Korahite, one of the warriors who came to David and helped him in battle while he was hiding at Ziklag from Saul ([[@13012001|1 Chr 12:1]]; [[@13012006|1 Chr 12:6]]).

column5: A doorkeeper for the ark
column7: When David brought up the ark of the covenant, he and Berechiah served as doorkeepers for the ark ([[@13015023|1 Chr 15:23]]; [[@13015025|1 Chr 15:25]]).

column5: King Ahaz’s second-in-command
column7: He was second only to the king in the days of Ahaz king of Judah. He was killed, along with the king’s son Maaseiah, by Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim ([[@14028001|2 Chr 28:1]]; [[@14028007|2 Chr 28:7]]).

column5: Hometown of the prophet Nahum
column7: Nahum is introduced as 'the Elkoshite.' The book of Nahum begins, "A revelation about Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite" ([[@34001001|Nah 1:1]]).

column5: Kingdom ruled by Arioch
column7: Arioch king of Ellasar, along with Chedorlaomer and others, fought against the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah ([[@1014001|Gen 14:1]], 9).

column5: Ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy
column7: A man in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke. He is listed as Cosam's father, and his own father is Er ([[@42003028|Luke 3:28]]).

column5: Father of Jeribai and Joshaviah, David's warriors
column7: Father of Jeribai and Joshaviah, who are in the list of David's mighty men. The two sons are listed with Eliel the Mahavite and Ithmah the Moabite ([[@13011046|1 Chr 11:46]]).

column5: Maternal grandfather of King Jehoiachin
column7: A man of Jerusalem, the father of Nehushta, King Jehoiachin's mother. Jehoiachin became king at eighteen and reigned three months ([[@12024008|2 Kgs 24:8]]).

column5: An official in Jehoiakim’s time
column7: He was the son of Achbor, whom King Jehoiakim sent to Egypt to bring Uriah back ([[@24026022-24026023|Jer 26:22-23]]). Later he pleaded with the king not to burn the scroll, but the king would not listen ([[@24036025|Jer 36:25]]).

column5: Esau's Hittite father-in-law
column7: He was a Hittite whose daughter became Esau's wife ([[@1026034|Gen 26:34]]). In Genesis 36 his daughter appears as 'Adah' ([[@1036002|Gen 36:2]]).

column5: Son of Zebulun
column7: A son of Zebulun, he went down to Egypt with Jacob ([[@1046014|Gen 46:14]]). The family of the Elonites came from him ([[@4026026|Num 26:26]]).

column5: City of the tribe of Dan
column7: One of the cities in the inheritance the tribe of Dan received by lot; it is listed with Timnah and Ekron ([[@6019040|Josh 19:40]]; [[@6019043|Josh 19:43]]).

column5: Judge from Zebulun
column7: A Zebulunite, he became judge of Israel and judged for ten years ([[@7012011|Judg 12:11]]). When he died he was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun ([[@7012012|Judg 12:12]]).

column5: Place under Solomon's officer Ben Deker
column7: A place under Ben Deker, one of the twelve officers Solomon set over all Israel; it is listed with Makaz, Shaalbim, and Beth Shemesh ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004009|1 Kgs 4:9]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Shaharaim
column7: In the genealogy of Benjamin he is a son born to Shaharaim by his wife Hushim ([[@13008008-13008011|1 Chr 8:8-11]]). Among his sons were those who built Ono and Lod with its towns ([[@13008012|1 Chr 8:12]]).

column5: Son of David born in Jerusalem
column7: He was one of the sons born to David in Jerusalem ([[@13014005|1 Chr 14:5]]). In 1 Chronicles 3 he appears as 'Eliphelet' ([[@13003006|1 Chr 3:6]]).

column5: Town of Dan, given to the Levites
column7: It was a town given to the tribe of Dan ([[@6019044|Josh 19:44]]). Later it was given to the Levites along with its pasture lands ([[@6021023|Josh 21:23]]).

column5: City in Judah's hill country
column7: One of the hill-country cities the tribe of Judah received; it is listed with Maarath and Beth Anoth ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015059|Josh 15:59]]).

column5: Town of Judah and Simeon
column7: It was a southern town of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015030|Josh 15:30]]). It is also among the towns the tribe of Simeon received from within Judah's inheritance ([[@6019001|Josh 19:1]], 4).

column5: Benjaminite who helped David at Ziklag
column7: One of the Benjaminite warriors who came and helped David in battle while he was hiding from Saul at Ziklag ([[@13012001-13012002|1 Chr 12:1-2]]; [[@13012005|1 Chr 12:5]]).

column5: Gadite warrior who came to David
column7: The ninth among the Gadite warriors who came over to David at the stronghold in the wilderness ([[@13012008|1 Chr 12:8]]; [[@13012012|1 Chr 12:12]]).

column5: Gatekeeper descended from Obed-Edom
column7: A descendant of Obed-Edom listed among the divisions of gatekeepers; he was the son of Shemaiah. He and his brothers are described as able men ([[@13026006-13026008|1 Chr 26:6-8]]).

column5: City of the tribe of Benjamin
column7: One of the cities the tribe of Benjamin received according to their families; it is listed with Jericho and Beth Hoglah ([[@6018021|Josh 18:21]]).

column5: A great people who lived in Moab before
column7: They were a people struck by Chedorlaomer and his allied kings at Shaveh Kiriathaim ([[@1014005|Gen 14:5]]). They were a great, numerous, and tall people who once lived in the land of Moab, and the Moabites called them 'Emim' ([[@5002010-5002011|Deut 2:10-11]]).

column5: Village where the risen Jesus walked with two disciples
column7: A village sixty stadia from Jerusalem. As two disciples were walking there, the risen Jesus came near and went with them ([[@42024013-42024015|Luke 24:13-15]]).

column5: Where Saul visited a medium
column7: It was one of the holdings of Manasseh within the land of Issachar and Asher ([[@6017011|Josh 17:11]]). Saul disguised himself and went to a woman with a familiar spirit at En Dor ([[@9028007-9028008|1 Sam 28:7-8]]).

column5: City in Judah's lowland
column7: One of the lowland cities the tribe of Judah received; it is listed with Zanoah and Tappuah ([[@6015033-6015034|Josh 15:33-34]]).

column5: A Levite city in the tribe of Issachar
column7: It was one of the cities the tribe of Issachar received ([[@6019021|Josh 19:21]]). It was also one of the cities from the tribe of Issachar given to the Levites of the children of Gershon ([[@6021027-6021029|Josh 21:27-29]]).

column5: City of the tribe of Issachar
column7: One of the cities in the land the children of Issachar received by lot; it is listed with Remeth and Engannim ([[@6019017|Josh 19:17]]; [[@6019021|Josh 19:21]]).

column5: Spring at Lehi where Samson drank
column6: spring of the one who called
column7: The spring that came out when Samson, very thirsty, called on the LORD and God split the hollow place in Lehi. That is why it was named En Hakkore ([[@7015018-7015019|Judg 15:18-19]]).

column5: Fortified city of the tribe of Naphtali
column7: One of the fortified cities Naphtali's descendants received; it is listed with Kedesh and Edrei ([[@6019035|Josh 19:35]]; [[@6019037|Josh 19:37]]).

column5: A spring near Jerusalem
column7: It was a spring on the border between the lands of Judah and Benjamin ([[@6015007|Josh 15:7]]; [[@6018016|Josh 18:16]]). Adonijah held a feast near here by the stone of Zoheleth when he tried to become king ([[@11001009|1 Kgs 1:9]]).

column5: Spring on the border of Judah and Benjamin
column7: It was the waters along which the border of the tribe of Judah passed ([[@6015007|Josh 15:7]]). It also appears on the border of the tribe of Benjamin ([[@6018017|Josh 18:17]]).

column5: Place where Tamar waited for Judah
column7: It was a place on the way to Timnah, and Tamar covered her face and sat at the gate of Enaim ([[@1038014|Gen 38:14]]). Judah's friend asked the people of this place about the woman ([[@1038020-1038021|Gen 38:20-21]]).

column5: City in Judah's lowland
column7: One of the lowland cities the tribe of Judah received; it is listed with En Gannim and Tappuah ([[@6015033-6015034|Josh 15:33-34]]).

column5: Father of Ahira, leader of the tribe of Naphtali
column7: He was the father of Ahira, the leader of the children of Naphtali in the wilderness ([[@4001015|Num 1:15]]). His son brought the offering on behalf of the children of Naphtali on the twelfth day ([[@4007078|Num 7:78]]).

column5: Place by the river in Ezekiel's vision
column7: In Ezekiel's vision of the river flowing in and healing the sea water, the shore from En Gedi to En Eglaim will be a place for spreading nets ([[@26047009-26047010|Ezek 47:9-10]]).

column5: Spring in Judah's wilderness, David's refuge
column7: It was a town in the wilderness of Judah, one of the places given to the tribe of Judah ([[@6015062|Josh 15:62]]). It was also called Hazazon Tamar ([[@14020002|2 Chr 20:2]]). David stayed in the strongholds of En Gedi while fleeing from Saul, and Saul came after him when he heard that David was in the wilderness of En Gedi ([[@9023029|1 Sam 23:29]]; [[@9024001|1 Sam 24:1]]). The Song of Songs sings of "a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi" ([[@22001014|Song 1:14]]).

column5: Son of Cain
column7: Son of Cain; Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch. Enoch became the father of Irad ([[@1004017-1004018|Gen 4:17-18]]).

column5: The man who walked with God and was taken
column7: He was the son Jared fathered at the age of one hundred sixty-two ([[@1005018|Gen 5:18]]). After becoming the father of Methuselah at sixty-five, Enoch walked with God for three hundred years, and the Bible says, "Enoch walked with God, and he was not found, for God took him" ([[@1005021-1005024|Gen 5:21-24]]). Hebrews says that by faith Enoch "was taken away, so that he wouldn’t see death," and that he was well pleasing to God ([[@58011005|Heb 11:5]]). Jude calls him "Enoch, the seventh from Adam," and says that he prophesied ([[@65001014|Jude 1:14]]).

column5: Son of Seth, grandson of Adam
column7: He was the son of Seth and the grandson of Adam. Speaking of the time he was born, the Bible says, "At that time men began to call on the LORD’s name" ([[@1004026|Gen 4:26]]). Enosh became the father of Kenan at ninety, lived nine hundred five years, and died ([[@1005009-1005011|Gen 5:9-11]]). His name also appears between Seth and Adam in Luke's genealogy of Jesus ([[@42003038|Luke 3:38]]).

column5: Paul's beloved, first fruits to Christ
column7: Someone Paul asked the church in Rome to greet. Paul called him "Epaenetus, my beloved, who is the first fruits of Achaia to Christ" ([[@45016005|Rom 16:5]]).

column5: Paul’s co-worker who brought the gospel to Colossae
column7: He was "Epaphras our beloved fellow servant," from whom the Colossians learned the gospel, a faithful servant of Christ ([[@51001007|Col 1:7]]). While imprisoned with Paul, he was always striving in prayer for the Colossians ([[@51004012|Col 4:12]]; [[@57001023|Phlm 1:23]]).

column5: The man the Philippian church sent to Paul
column7: He was the messenger sent by the Philippian church, and Paul called him "my brother, fellow worker, fellow soldier" ([[@50002025|Phil 2:25]]). Through him Paul received what the Philippians had sent ([[@50004018|Phil 4:18]]).

column5: Son of Midian
column7: He is the first named of the five sons of Midian, the son of Abraham and Keturah ([[@1025001-1025002|Gen 25:1-2]], 4; [[@13001033|1 Chr 1:33]]).

column5: A unit for measuring grain
column7: The ephah was a unit for measuring amounts of grain or flour. The omer used when gathering manna in the wilderness was one tenth of an ephah ([[@2016036|Exod 16:36]]). When Ruth gleaned in Boaz's field until evening and beat out what she had gleaned, it was about an ephah of barley ([[@8002017|Ruth 2:17]]). The prophet Amos rebuked merchants who made the ephah small and cheated with false balances ([[@30008005|Amos 8:5]]). The same word, 'Ephah', also appears as a person's name, such as a son of Midian ([[@1025004|Gen 25:4]]).

column5: Caleb's concubine in Judah's genealogy
column7: Caleb's concubine in Judah's genealogy, who bore Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran also became the father of Gazez ([[@13002046|1 Chr 2:46]]).

column5: Son of Jahdai
column7: A son of Jahdai in the genealogy of Caleb's family; he was a brother of Regem, Jothan, Geshan, Pelet, and Shaaph ([[@13002047|1 Chr 2:47]]).

column5: Place known for its young camels
column7: Isaiah prophesied that the dromedaries of Midian and Ephah would fill Zion, and that all from Sheba would bring gold and frankincense ([[@23060006|Isa 60:6]]).

column5: Netophathite whose sons went to Gedaliah
column7: A Netophathite whose sons, along with other army captains, came to Gedaliah, the governor at Mizpah ([[@24040007-24040008|Jer 40:7-8]]).

column5: Son of Midian
column7: He was one of the five sons of Midian, the son of Abraham and Keturah ([[@1025001-1025002|Gen 25:1-2]], 4; [[@13001033|1 Chr 1:33]]).

column5: Son of Ezrah
column7: Son of Ezrah in Judah's genealogy, and a brother of Jether, Mered, and Jalon. His name appears only in this verse ([[@13004017|1 Chr 4:17]]).

column5: Head of a family in half of Manasseh
column7: One of the heads of the half-tribe of Manasseh, described as a famous mighty man of valor ([[@13005023-13005024|1 Chr 5:23-24]]).

column5: Philistine camp in the story of Goliath
column7: The Philistines camped at Ephesdammim, between Socoh and Azekah ([[@9017001|1 Sam 17:1]]). In 1 Chronicles it appears as 'Pasdammim' ([[@13011013|1 Chr 11:13]]).

column5: Great city of Asia Minor where Paul stayed long
column7: It was a great city in western Asia Minor. When Paul first came there, he reasoned with the Jews in the synagogue ([[@44018019|Acts 18:19]]). When he came back, he stayed two years, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus, and all who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord ([[@44019009-44019010|Acts 19:9-10]]). Because of the silversmith Demetrius, a great uproar also broke out, with crowds shouting, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!" ([[@44019024-44019029|Acts 19:24-29]]). Paul sent the letter of Ephesians to this church, and it is the first of the seven churches in Revelation ([[@66002001|Rev 2:1]]).

column5: Holy outer garment worn by priests
column7: The ephod was a holy garment worn by priests. The high priest's ephod was skillfully woven of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, and fine twined linen ([[@2028006|Exod 28:6]]). On its two shoulders were stones engraved with the names of the sons of Israel, so that Aaron would bear them as a memorial before the LORD ([[@2028012|Exod 28:12]]). The boy Samuel served before the LORD wearing a linen ephod, and David, wearing a linen ephod, danced before the LORD with all his might ([[@9002018|1 Sam 2:18]]; [[@10006014|2 Sam 6:14]]).

column5: Father of Hanniel, a prince of Manasseh
column7: Father of Hanniel, the prince of the tribe of Manasseh given the task of dividing the land of Canaan ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034023|Num 34:23]]).

column5: Joseph's second son; the tribe of Ephraim
column7: He was the second son born to Joseph in Egypt. Joseph named him, saying, "For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction" ([[@1041052|Gen 41:52]]). When Jacob gave his blessing, he laid his right hand on the head of Ephraim, the younger, putting him ahead of his older brother Manasseh ([[@1048014|Gen 48:14]]). The tribe of Ephraim was powerful among the northern tribes, and in the prophets the name was also used for all of northern Israel ([[@28011008|Hos 11:8]]).

column5: Town near the wilderness where Jesus stayed
column7: Jesus no longer walked openly among the Jews, but went to a town called Ephraim near the wilderness and stayed there with his disciples ([[@43011054|John 11:54]]).

column5: A gate in the wall of Jerusalem
column7: It was a gate in the wall of Jerusalem, and Jehoash king of Israel captured Amaziah king of Judah and broke down four hundred cubits of the wall from this gate to the Corner Gate ([[@12014013|2 Kgs 14:13]]). In Nehemiah's time the people made booths in the square of this gate ([[@16008016|Neh 8:16]]).

column5: Wife of Caleb son of Hezron, mother of Hur
column7: She was the wife of Caleb the son of Hezron. After his wife Azubah died, Caleb married Ephrath, and Ephrath bore him Hur ([[@13002018-13002019|1 Chr 2:18-19]]). Chronicles also calls her 'Ephrathah' and introduces Hur as "the firstborn of Ephrathah, the father of Bethlehem" ([[@13002050|1 Chr 2:50]]; [[@13004004|1 Chr 4:4]]). Hur became the father of Uri, and Uri became the father of Bezalel ([[@13002020|1 Chr 2:20]]). An old name of Bethlehem was also Ephrath ([[@1035019|Gen 35:19]]), and scholars differ on how she is connected with this name.

column5: The Hittite who sold Abraham the field of Machpelah
column7: He was the son of Zohar the Hittite and owned the field with the cave of Machpelah ([[@1023008|Gen 23:8]]). When Abraham looked for a place to bury Sarah, Ephron offered to give him the field and the cave, but Abraham said he would pay the price of the field ([[@1023011-1023013|Gen 23:11-13]]). Abraham weighed out four hundred shekels of silver for Ephron, as he had named, and bought the field and the cave ([[@1023016|Gen 23:16]]). When Abraham died, he too was buried in this cave of Machpelah in the field of Ephron ([[@1025009|Gen 25:9]]).

column5: Mountain on the border of Judah and Benjamin
column7: It was a mountain on the northern border of the tribe of Judah. The border ran from the spring of the waters of Nephtoah to the cities of Mount Ephron and reached Baalah, that is, Kiriath Jearim ([[@6015009|Josh 15:9]]).

column5: Judah’s firstborn son
column7: He was Judah’s firstborn, and Judah took Tamar as a wife for him ([[@1038006|Gen 38:6]]). He was wicked in the LORD’s sight, so the LORD killed him ([[@1038007|Gen 38:7]]).

column5: Descendant of Shelah son of Judah
column7: A descendant of Shelah son of Judah, called 'the father of Lecah.' The same verse also mentions Laadah the father of Mareshah and the families of the house of linen workers ([[@13004021|1 Chr 4:21]]).

column5: Ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy
column7: A man in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke. He is listed as the father of Elmodam, and his own father is named Jose ([[@42003028-42003029|Luke 3:28-29]]).

column5: Ancestor of the Eranite family
column7: A descendant of Shuthelah son of Ephraim, from whom the family of the Eranites came. His name appears in the census of Israel in the wilderness ([[@4026035-4026037|Num 26:35-37]]).

column5: A co-worker of Paul
column7: Paul sent him to Macedonia along with Timothy ([[@44019022|Acts 19:22]]). Paul told Timothy, "Erastus remained at Corinth" ([[@55004020|2 Tim 4:20]]).

column5: City in Nimrod's kingdom
column7: It was one of the cities in the land of Shinar where the kingdom of Nimrod, the son of Cush, began, and it is named with Babel, Accad, and Calneh ([[@1010008|Gen 10:8]], 10).

column5: Son of Gad
column7: A son of Gad, he went down to Egypt with Jacob ([[@1046016|Gen 46:16]]). The family of the Erites came from him ([[@4026016|Num 26:16]]).

column5: King of Assyria after Sennacherib
column7: He became king in place of Sennacherib king of Assyria after Sennacherib was killed by his sons ([[@12019036-12019037|2 Kgs 19:36-37]]). The enemies of Judah and Benjamin said he had brought them there ([[@15004001-15004002|Ezra 4:1-2]]).

column5: Isaac's firstborn son, ancestor of the Edomites
column7: He was the first to be born of the twins of Isaac and Rebekah. At birth he came out "red all over, like a hairy garment" so they named him Esau ([[@1025025|Gen 25:25]]). He was a skilled hunter, but he sold his birthright to his younger brother Jacob for bread and lentil stew ([[@1025033-1025034|Gen 25:33-34]]). Later, when he also lost his father's blessing, he hated Jacob, but long afterward they met again, embraced, and wept ([[@1033004|Gen 33:4]]). His descendants became the Edomites, who lived in the hill country of Seir ([[@1036009|Gen 36:9]]).

column5: The hill country of Edom, judged in Obadiah
column7: It refers to the hill country of Edom, the descendants of Esau. Obadiah prophesied that on that day the LORD would destroy understanding from the mountain of Esau ([[@31001008-31001009|Obad 1:8-9]]).

column5: Well dug by Isaac's servants
column7: A well Isaac's servants dug in the valley of Gerar. When the herdsmen of Gerar argued, claiming the water as theirs, Isaac named it Esek because of the quarrel ([[@1026019-1026020|Gen 26:19-20]]).

column5: City in Judah's hill country
column7: One of the hill-country cities the tribe of Judah received; it is listed with Arab and Dumah ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015052|Josh 15:52]]).

column5: Son of Dishon the Horite
column7: He was a son of Dishon, a Horite descended from Seir in the land of Edom. His brothers were Hemdan, Ithran, and Cheran ([[@1036026|Gen 36:26]]; [[@13001041|1 Chr 1:41]]).

column5: Amorite ally of Abram
column7: The brother of Mamre and Aner, he was an ally of Abram ([[@1014013|Gen 14:13]]). Abram let him take his own share of the spoils ([[@1014024|Gen 14:24]]).

column5: Where the spies cut a huge grape cluster
column7: It is the valley where the men spying out Canaan cut off a branch with a single cluster of grapes and carried it on a pole between two of them. It was called the valley of Eshcol because of the cluster they cut there ([[@4013023-4013024|Num 13:23-24]]).

column5: A town in the story of Samson
column7: It was a town in the lowland of Judah ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]), which later became part of the inheritance of the tribe of Dan ([[@6019041|Josh 19:41]]). In Mahaneh Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol, the LORD's Spirit began to move Samson ([[@7013025|Judg 13:25]]). After Samson died, his brothers and all his father's house took his body and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the burial place of his father Manoah ([[@7016031|Judg 16:31]]). This is also where the children of Dan sent out five men to explore new land.

column5: Priestly town in the hill country of Judah
column7: It was a town in the hill country of Judah, which appears in Joshua 15 under the name 'Eshtemoh' ([[@6015048-6015050|Josh 15:48-50]]). This town and its pasture lands were among the towns given to the descendants of Aaron the priest ([[@6021013-6021014|Josh 21:13-14]]; [[@13006057|1 Chr 6:57]]). When David returned to Ziklag, he sent some of the plunder taken from the LORD's enemies as a gift to the elders of Judah, including those in Eshtemoa ([[@9030026-9030028|1 Sam 30:26-28]]).

column5: Descendant of Judah, son of Mehir
column7: He was a descendant of Judah and the son of Mehir ([[@13004011|1 Chr 4:11]]). He became the father of Beth Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah, and these were the men of Recah ([[@13004012|1 Chr 4:12]]).

column5: Ancestor of Jesus in Luke's genealogy
column7: A man in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke. He is listed as Nahum's father, and his own father is Naggai ([[@42003025|Luke 3:25]]).

column5: The Jewish queen of Persia who saved her people
column7: Esther was a young Jewish woman also called Hadassah; she lost her parents and was raised by her cousin Mordecai ([[@17002007|Esth 2:7]]). King Ahasuerus made her queen in place of Vashti ([[@17002017|Esth 2:17]]). When Haman set out to destroy all the Jews, she resolved to fast for three days and then go to the king against the law, saying, "if I perish, I perish" ([[@17004016|Esth 4:16]]). In the end Haman's plot was exposed, the Jews were saved, and the Feast of Purim began in memory of this ([[@17009026|Esth 9:26]]).

column5: Rock where Samson stayed
column7: After striking the Philistines with a great slaughter, Samson went down and lived in the cave in Etam’s rock ([[@7015008|Judg 15:8]]). Three thousand men of Judah came here looking for him ([[@7015011|Judg 15:11]]).

column5: Town of the descendants of Simeon
column7: It was one of the five towns where the descendants of Simeon lived ([[@13004032|1 Chr 4:32]]). The genealogy of Judah also mentions 'the sons of the father of Etam' ([[@13004003|1 Chr 4:3]]).

column5: City of Judah built by Rehoboam
column7: One of the cities Rehoboam built to defend the land of Judah; it is listed with Bethlehem and Tekoa ([[@14011005-14011006|2 Chr 11:5-6]]).

column5: Place on Zebulun's border
column7: A place along the border of the land Zebulun's descendants received. The border passed Gath Hepher, reached Ethkazin, and went out to Rimmon ([[@6019010|Josh 19:10]]; [[@6019013|Josh 19:13]]).

column5: An Exodus camp at the wilderness edge
column7: It was where the children of Israel camped after Succoth when they left Egypt, described as Etham "in the edge of the wilderness" ([[@2013020|Exod 13:20]]; [[@4033006|Num 33:6]]).

column5: Ezrahite famous for his wisdom
column7: An Ezrahite, he was famous for his wisdom, but Solomon was wiser than he was ([[@11004030-11004031|1 Kgs 4:30-31]]).

column5: Grandson of Judah, son of Zerah
column7: He was a son of Zerah, the son of Judah ([[@13002004|1 Chr 2:4]], 6). He was the father of Azariah ([[@13002008|1 Chr 2:8]]).

column5: King of Sidon, father of Jezebel
column7: King of the Sidonians and father of Jezebel, who became King Ahab's wife. Ahab married Jezebel and served Baal ([[@11016030-11016031|1 Kgs 16:30-31]]).

column5: Town of Judah and Simeon
column7: It was a town given to the tribe of Judah ([[@6015042|Josh 15:42]]). It is also among the towns of the tribe of Simeon ([[@6019007|Josh 19:7]]).

column5: Son of Ashhur and Helah
column7: A son born to Helah, wife of Ashhur the father of Tekoa; he was a brother of Zereth and Izhar ([[@13004005|1 Chr 4:5]]; [[@13004007|1 Chr 4:7]]).

column5: Man who sent greetings to Timothy
column7: A man who, at the end of Paul's letter to Timothy, sent greetings to Timothy along with Pudens, Linus, and Claudia ([[@55004021|2 Tim 4:21]]).

column5: Mother of Timothy
column7: The mother of Timothy. Paul said the sincere faith in Timothy lived first in his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice ([[@55001005|2 Tim 1:5]]).

column5: Woman of the church in Philippi
column7: A woman of the church in Philippi. Paul urged Euodia and Syntyche "to think the same way in the Lord" ([[@50004002|Phil 4:2]]).

column5: The great river at the promised land's edge
column7: It is the fourth of the four rivers that flowed out of Eden ([[@1002014|Gen 2:14]]). God promised to give Abram the land "from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates" ([[@1015018|Gen 15:18]]). In the Bible, 'the great river' usually means this river ([[@6001004|Josh 1:4]]). In Revelation the sixth bowl is poured out on this river ([[@66016012|Rev 16:12]]).

column5: Young man who fell and was revived at Troas
column7: A young man in Troas who fell asleep while listening to Paul's teaching, fell from the third floor, and was taken up dead. Paul embraced him and said, "his life is in him", and the people brought him in alive ([[@44020006|Acts 20:6]]; [[@44020009-44020012|Acts 20:9-12]]).

column5: The first woman, Adam's wife
column7: Adam named his wife Eve because she would be "the mother of all the living" ([[@1003020|Gen 3:20]]). Eve gave birth to Cain, and Paul pointed to the way the serpent deceived her as a warning ([[@1004001|Gen 4:1]]; [[@47011003|2 Cor 11:3]]).

column5: Midianite king killed by Israel
column7: He was one of the five kings of Midian killed when Israel fought against Midian ([[@4031008|Num 31:8]]). In Joshua he appears as one of the princes of Sihon ([[@6013021|Josh 13:21]]).

column5: Babylonian king who freed Jehoiachin
column7: A king of Babylon, in the year he began to reign he released Jehoiachin king of Judah from prison ([[@12025027|2 Kgs 25:27]]; [[@24052031|Jer 52:31]]).

column5: Father of Naarai, one of David's warriors
column7: Father of Naarai in the list of David's mighty men. Hezro the Carmelite also appears in the same verse ([[@13011037|1 Chr 11:37]]).

column5: Son of Gad
column7: A son of Gad, he went down to Egypt with Jacob ([[@1046016|Gen 46:16]]). He seems to be the same person as 'Ozni', who appears in the same place in the genealogy in Numbers ([[@4026016|Num 26:16]]).

column5: Grandson of Benjamin, son of Bela
column7: One of the five sons of Bela, Benjamin's son; with his brothers he was a head of their fathers' house and a mighty man of valor ([[@13007006-13007007|1 Chr 7:6-7]]).

column5: Priest and prophet of the exile
column7: A priest, the son of Buzi, he received the LORD's word by the river Chebar in the land of the Chaldeans ([[@26001003|Ezek 1:3]]). His life became a sign to the people ([[@26024024|Ezek 24:24]]).

column5: Stone where David waited for Jonathan
column7: Jonathan told David to go down after three days to the place where he had hidden and stay by the stone Ezel. He said he would shoot three arrows on its side ([[@9020019-9020020|1 Sam 20:19-20]]).

column5: A town in southern Judah given to Simeon
column7: It was one of the towns of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015029|Josh 15:29]]), and it was also a town the tribe of Simeon received within the inheritance of the children of Judah ([[@6019001-6019003|Josh 19:1-3]]).

column5: A Horite chief among the sons of Seir
column7: He was a chief of the Horites among the sons of Seir in the land of Edom ([[@1036021|Gen 36:21]]). His children were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan ([[@1036027|Gen 36:27]]).

column5: Father of Hushah
column7: The father of Hushah in Judah's genealogy, descended from Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah the father of Bethlehem ([[@13004004|1 Chr 4:4]]).

column5: Ephraimite killed by the men of Gath
column7: A descendant of Ephraim who went down with Elead to take the livestock of the men of Gath and was killed. Their father Ephraim mourned many days ([[@13007021-13007022|1 Chr 7:21-22]]).

column5: Chief of the Gadites who came to David
column7: The chief of the Gadite warriors who came over to David at the stronghold in the wilderness ([[@13012008-13012009|1 Chr 12:8-9]]).

column5: Ruler of Mizpah who repaired the wall
column7: Son of Jeshua and ruler of Mizpah. He repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall across from the ascent to the armory ([[@16003019|Neh 3:19]]).

column5: Man who stood at the wall's dedication
column7: One of those who stood in God's house when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated; his name appears with Maaseiah and Shemaiah ([[@16012040|Neh 12:40]]; [[@16012042|Neh 12:42]]).

column5: Red Sea port where Solomon built ships
column7: It was a place where Israel camped while passing through the wilderness ([[@4033035|Num 33:35]]). It lay on the shore of the Red Sea in the land of Edom, near Eloth, and King Solomon built ships there ([[@11009026|1 Kgs 9:26]]). Those ships went to Ophir and brought back four hundred and twenty talents of gold ([[@11009028|1 Kgs 9:28]]). Later Jehoshaphat also built ships to go for gold, but they were wrecked at Ezion Geber and never sailed ([[@11022048|1 Kgs 22:48]]).

column5: Hometown of Adino, David's warrior
column7: Among David's mighty men, the chief of the captains was also called 'Adino the Eznite.' He killed eight hundred men at one time ([[@10023008|2 Sam 23:8]]).

column5: Scribe and priest skilled in the law
column7: He was a priest descended from Aaron and a scribe skilled in the law of Moses ([[@15007006|Ezra 7:6]]). In the time of Artaxerxes king of Persia, he led a group of people from Babylon up to Jerusalem. The Bible says he "had set his heart to seek the LORD’s law, and to do it, and to teach statutes and ordinances in Israel" ([[@15007010|Ezra 7:10]]). When he heard that the people had married foreigners, he tore his garment and mourned and prayed ([[@15009003|Ezra 9:3]]). In Nehemiah's time he read the book of the law before the assembly from early morning until midday ([[@16008002-16008003|Neh 8:2-3]]).

column5: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the priests who came back with Zerubbabel and Jeshua ([[@16012001|Neh 12:1]]). In the days of Joiakim, the head of Ezra’s family was Meshullam ([[@16012012-16012013|Neh 12:12-13]]).

column5: A man in Judah's genealogy
column7: A man in Judah's genealogy, the father of Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. The wife of his son Mered bore Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah ([[@13004017|1 Chr 4:17]]).

column5: Overseer of David's farm workers
column7: Son of Chelub; among those in charge of King David's property, he was over the workers who tilled the fields ([[@13027026|1 Chr 27:26]]; [[@13027031|1 Chr 27:31]]).

column5: Harbor of Crete where Paul's ship stopped
column7: The place Paul's ship, bound for Rome, reached with difficulty after sailing along the coast of Crete; it was near the city of Lasea ([[@44027007-44027008|Acts 27:7-8]]).

column5: Believing and trusting God and his word
column7: Faith means holding God and his word to be true and relying on them. Hebrews says, "faith is assurance of things hoped for, proof of things not seen", and it says that without faith it is impossible to please God ([[@58011001|Heb 11:1]], 6). To the centurion who said his servant would be healed by just a word from him, Jesus said, "I haven’t found so great a faith, not even in Israel" ([[@40008008-40008010|Matt 8:8-10]]). Paul said that we have been saved by grace through faith, and that this is the gift of God ([[@49002008|Eph 2:8]]).

column5: Going without food to humble oneself before God
column7: Fasting means going without food for a time to humble oneself and pray before God. Israel gathered at Mizpah and fasted, confessing, "We have sinned against the LORD" ([[@9007006|1 Sam 7:6]]). Before going in to the king, Esther asked the Jews in Susa to fast for her for three days, night and day ([[@17004016|Esth 4:16]]). Jesus fasted forty days and forty nights, and he taught that when we fast we should not do it to be seen by people but to be seen by our Father who is in secret ([[@40004002|Matt 4:2]]; [[@40006016-40006018|Matt 6:16-18]]).

column5: Barnabas's father, not named
column7: The Bible tells us nothing about Barnabas's father. Paul introduces Mark as "Mark the cousin of Barnabas" ([[@51004010|Col 4:10]]).

column5: Conaniah's father, not named
column7: The Bible does not give this man's name. His son Conaniah the Levite was in charge of the offerings in Hezekiah's time, and Conaniah's brother Shimei was second ([[@14031012|2 Chr 31:12]]).

column5: Elizabeth's father, not named
column7: The Bible does not give this man's name. His daughter Elizabeth was the wife of the priest Zacharias and is described as a descendant of Aaron ([[@42001005|Luke 1:5]]).

column5: Timothy's maternal grandfather, not named
column7: The Bible does not give this man's name. Paul speaks only of the faith of Timothy's grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice ([[@55001005|2 Tim 1:5]]).

column5: Jeremiah's grandfather, not named
column7: Jeremiah was the son of Hilkiah, but the Bible does not give the name of Hilkiah's father ([[@24001001|Jer 1:1]]). Jeremiah had an uncle named Shallum ([[@24032007|Jer 32:7]]).

column5: Hodiah's father, not named
column7: The Bible does not give this man's name. This verse introduces the father of Keilah and Eshtemoa as "sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham" ([[@13004019|1 Chr 4:19]]).

column5: Father of Martha, Mary, and Lazarus
column7: The Bible does not give this man's name. Martha and Mary of Bethany were sisters, and Lazarus was their brother ([[@42010038-42010039|Luke 10:38-39]]; [[@43011001-43011002|John 11:1-2]]).

column5: Mamre's father, not named
column7: The Bible does not give this man's name. Mamre the Amorite was a brother of Eshcol and Aner, and an ally of Abram ([[@1014013|Gen 14:13]]).

column5: Father of Nathan and Joel, not named
column7: The Bible does not give this man's name. In the list of David's mighty men, his son Joel appears as 'the brother of Nathan' ([[@13011038|1 Chr 11:38]]).

column5: Father of Pharaoh's queen, not named
column7: The Bible does not give this man's name. His daughter Tahpenes was Pharaoh's queen, and Pharaoh gave Tahpenes's sister to Hadad as his wife ([[@11011019|1 Kgs 11:19]]).

column5: Timothy's Greek father
column7: The Bible does not give this man's name. Timothy's mother was a Jewish believer, and the text says only that "his father was a Greek" ([[@44016001|Acts 16:1]]).

column5: Israel's festivals appointed by God
column7: The feasts were holy festivals appointed by God that Israel kept every year ([[@3023002|Lev 23:2]]). Three times a year all the men of Israel were to appear before the LORD at the place God chose: at the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Booths ([[@5016016|Deut 16:16]]). Besides these there were the day of remembrance with trumpet blasts on the first day of the seventh month and the Day of Atonement on the tenth day of the seventh month ([[@3023024-3023028|Lev 23:24-28]]). At the Feast of Booths the people lived in temporary shelters for seven days and remembered how God had brought them out of Egypt ([[@3023042-3023043|Lev 23:42-43]]).

column5: Governor of Judea who held Paul prisoner
column7: He was the Roman governor of Judea, and when Paul was sent to Caesarea, Felix heard the charges against him ([[@44023024|Acts 23:24]]; [[@44024001|Acts 24:1]]). Felix, with his Jewish wife Drusilla, sent for Paul and heard him speak about faith in Christ Jesus ([[@44024024|Acts 24:24]]). When Paul reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix was terrified and sent him away, saying, "Go your way for this time" ([[@44024025|Acts 24:25]]). He often sent for Paul, hoping Paul would give him money, and when Festus succeeded him two years later, he left Paul in prison to gain favor with the Jews ([[@44024026-44024027|Acts 24:26-27]]).

column5: Roman governor who sent Paul to Caesar
column7: Porcius Festus was the Roman governor of Judea who succeeded Felix ([[@44024027|Acts 24:27]]). After taking office he tried Paul at Caesarea, and when, wanting to win favor with the Jews, he asked Paul whether he would be tried in Jerusalem, Paul appealed to Caesar ([[@44025009-44025012|Acts 25:9-12]]). When Paul made his defense before King Agrippa, Festus shouted, "Paul, you are crazy!" ([[@44026024|Acts 26:24]]). In the end he sent Paul to Rome.

column5: A fruit tree commonly grown in Israel
column7: The fig tree was a fruit tree commonly grown in the land of Israel. After Adam and Eve sinned, they knew that they were naked, and they sewed fig leaves together to make coverings ([[@1003007|Gen 3:7]]). The men who spied out Canaan brought back pomegranates and figs along with a cluster of grapes ([[@4013023|Num 13:23]]). It is recorded that in Solomon's time the people "lived safely, every man under his vine and under his fig tree" ([[@11004025|1 Kgs 4:25]]). Jesus told a fig tree that had only leaves and no fruit that it would never bear fruit again, and the tree soon withered ([[@40021019|Matt 21:19]]).

column5: Offering God the first of the harvest
column7: First fruits were the earliest produce gathered from the land, brought first to the house of God and offered there ([[@2023019|Exod 23:19]]). At harvest time a sheaf of the first grain was brought to the priest and waved before the LORD ([[@3023010-3023011|Lev 23:10-11]]). Proverbs says, "Honor the LORD with your substance, with the first fruits of all your increase" ([[@20003009|Prov 3:9]]). The New Testament calls Christ, who rose from the dead, "the first fruit of those who are asleep" ([[@46015020|1 Cor 15:20]]).

column5: The Fish Gate in Jerusalem's wall
column7: It was a gate in the wall of Jerusalem, rebuilt by the sons of Hassenaah in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003003|Neh 3:3]]). It is also mentioned in 2 Chronicles ([[@14033014|2 Chr 33:14]]).

column5: Where David's and Absalom's armies fought
column7: The place where David's army fought against Israel, who followed Absalom. Israel was defeated there, and twenty thousand men died that day ([[@10018006-10018007|2 Sam 18:6-7]]).

column5: Corinthian believer who visited Paul
column7: He came to Paul with Stephanas and Achaicus ([[@46016017|1 Cor 16:17]]). Paul said that they had refreshed his spirit ([[@46016018|1 Cor 16:18]]).

column5: Where believers from Rome met Paul
column7: When the brothers in Rome heard about Paul, they came as far as the Market of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet him. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage ([[@44028015|Acts 28:15]]).

column5: Gate guarded when Joash was crowned
column7: The gate where Jehoiada, when making the king's son king, stationed a third of the priests and Levites who came on duty on the Sabbath ([[@14023003-14023005|2 Chr 23:3-5]]).

column5: A gate in the wall of Jerusalem
column7: Nehemiah passed by this gate, also called the spring gate, when he inspected the wall by night ([[@16002014|Neh 2:14]]). Shallun the son of Colhozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, repaired this gate ([[@16003015|Neh 3:15]]).

column5: A fragrant spice offered to God
column7: Frankincense is a fragrant spice, and it was one of the ingredients of the holy incense offered to God ([[@2030034|Exod 30:34]]). For a meal offering, oil was poured on the fine flour and frankincense put on it, and the priest burned all the frankincense on the altar ([[@3002001-3002002|Lev 2:1-2]]). Isaiah foretold that people from Sheba would come bringing gold and frankincense and would proclaim the praises of the LORD ([[@23060006|Isa 60:6]]). The wise men from the east offered the child Jesus gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh ([[@40002011|Matt 2:11]]).

column5: Son of Ebed who stood against Abimelech
column7: He was the son of Ebed, and when he came to Shechem with his brothers, the men of Shechem put their trust in him ([[@7009026|Judg 9:26]]). He stirred up the people, saying, "Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him?" ([[@7009028|Judg 9:28]]). When Zebul, the ruler of the city, heard this, he was angry and secretly sent word to Abimelech ([[@7009030-7009031|Judg 9:30-31]]). Gaal led the men of Shechem out to fight Abimelech but was chased and fled, and Zebul drove Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem ([[@7009039-7009041|Judg 9:39-41]]).

column5: A mountain in Ephraim near Joshua's burial place
column7: It was a mountain in the hill country of Ephraim, and Joshua was buried at Timnath Serah, north of this mountain ([[@6024030|Josh 24:30]]; [[@7002009|Judg 2:9]]).

column5: Benjaminite who lived in Jerusalem
column7: A man named with Sallai among the Benjaminites who returned from exile and lived in Jerusalem ([[@16011007-16011008|Neh 11:7-8]]).

column5: Where Pilate sat on the judgment seat
column7: The place where Pilate brought Jesus out and sat down on the judgment seat. It was called "The Pavement", and in Hebrew "Gabbatha" ([[@43019013|John 19:13]]).

column5: Jacob's son, ancestor of the tribe of Gad
column7: Gad was the son Jacob had by Zilpah, Leah's servant. Leah named him, saying, "How fortunate!" ([[@1030011|Gen 30:11]]). Before he died, Jacob blessed him, saying, "A troop will press on Gad, but he will press on their heel" ([[@1049019|Gen 49:19]]). The children of Gad had a great deal of livestock ([[@4032001|Num 32:1]]), and together with the children of Reuben they received land east of the Jordan as their inheritance ([[@4032033|Num 32:33]]). The prophet Gad of David's time is a different person.

column5: Prophet and seer of King David
column7: A prophet in David's time, he told David to go into the land of Judah when David was in the stronghold hiding from Saul ([[@9022005|1 Sam 22:5]]). After David counted the people, Gad, as 'David's seer', brought him the LORD's word to choose one of three punishments ([[@10024011-10024013|2 Sam 24:11-13]]). He then told David to build an altar on the Jebusite's threshing floor. He recorded the acts of David, and the order for Levites to play cymbals, harps, and lyres in the LORD's house was set by his command and Nathan's ([[@13029029|1 Chr 29:29]]; [[@14029025|2 Chr 29:25]]).

column5: Spy from the tribe of Manasseh
column7: Son of Susi, chosen from the tribe of Manasseh among the men Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013011|Num 13:11]]; [[@4013016|Num 13:16]]).

column5: Spy from the tribe of Zebulun
column7: Son of Sodi, chosen from the tribe of Zebulun among the men Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013010|Num 13:10]]; [[@4013016|Num 13:16]]).

column5: Father of King Menahem of Israel
column7: He was the father of Menahem king of Israel. Menahem killed Shallum, became king, and reigned ten years in Samaria ([[@12015014|2 Kgs 15:14]], 17).

column5: Son of Nahor's concubine Reumah
column7: A son born to Reumah, the concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother; he was a brother of Tebah, Tahash, and Maacah ([[@1022023-1022024|Gen 22:23-24]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Gahar' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]], 47; [[@16007049|Neh 7:49]]).

column5: Macedonian seized in the Ephesus riot
column7: A Macedonian who traveled with Paul. When a riot broke out in Ephesus, he was seized along with Aristarchus and rushed into the theater ([[@44019028-44019029|Acts 19:28-29]]).

column5: Man of Derbe who traveled with Paul
column7: One of those who went with Paul as far as Asia when he returned through Macedonia; he was from Derbe ([[@44020003-44020004|Acts 20:3-4]]).

column5: Corinthian who hosted Paul and the church
column7: He was host to Paul and to the whole church ([[@45016023|Rom 16:23]]). He was one of the few people Paul baptized himself in Corinth ([[@46001014|1 Cor 1:14]]).

column5: Recipient of 3 John
column7: The man to whom 3 John was written. The elder called him "Gaius the beloved" and prayed that he would prosper in all things, even as his soul prospers ([[@64001001-64001002|3 John 1:1-2]]).

column5: Levite who lived in Jerusalem
column7: His name appears as one of the Levites among those who lived in Jerusalem ([[@13009003|1 Chr 9:3]]; [[@13009014-13009015|1 Chr 9:14-15]]).

column5: Levite descended from Jeduthun
column7: He was a Levite descended from Jeduthun ([[@13009016|1 Chr 9:16]]). He was the grandfather of Abda, who lived in Jerusalem after the exile ([[@16011017|Neh 11:17]]).

column5: The region of the churches Paul wrote to
column7: It was a region in central Asia Minor. When the Holy Spirit kept Paul from speaking the word in Asia, he went through the region of Phrygia and Galatia ([[@44016006|Acts 16:6]]), and later he went through it again in order, strengthening all the disciples ([[@44018023|Acts 18:23]]). Paul sent a letter "to the assemblies of Galatia", and this is the book of Galatians ([[@48001002|Gal 1:2]]). In that letter Paul rebuked them for being swayed by a different teaching, saying, "Foolish Galatians" ([[@48003001|Gal 3:1]]).

column5: The northern region where Jesus mainly worked
column7: It is a region in the north of Israel, lying along the Sea of Galilee. Isaiah prophesied that God would make glorious "Galilee of the nations" ([[@23009001|Isa 9:1]]). Jesus grew up in Nazareth in Galilee and went about all Galilee teaching and healing the sick ([[@40004023|Matt 4:23]]). Several disciples, such as Peter and Andrew, were also fishermen from Galilee ([[@40004018|Matt 4:18]]).

column5: Village in Benjamin, home of Palti
column7: It was the home of Palti, to whom Saul gave David's wife Michal ([[@9025044|1 Sam 25:44]]). The name also appears in Isaiah ([[@23010030|Isa 10:30]]).

column5: Proconsul of Achaia
column7: When he was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews brought Paul before the judgment seat, but he drove them away, saying he did not want to be a judge of such matters ([[@44018012-44018016|Acts 18:12-16]]). He did not care even when Sosthenes was beaten ([[@44018017|Acts 18:17]]).

column5: Men who guarded the towers of Tyre
column7: People spoken of in the lament over Tyre: "valiant men were in your towers." They hung their shields on the walls all around and perfected Tyre's beauty ([[@26027011|Ezek 27:11]]).

column5: Leader of the tribe of Manasseh in the wilderness
column7: He was the son of Pedahzur and the leader of the children of Manasseh in the wilderness ([[@4001010|Num 1:10]]; [[@4002020|Num 2:20]]). On the eighth day he brought the offering on behalf of the children of Manasseh ([[@4007054|Num 7:54]]).

column5: Respected Pharisee and teacher of the law
column7: A Pharisee and teacher of the law honored by all the people, he advised the council to leave the apostles alone ([[@44005034|Acts 5:34]], 38). Paul learned the law under him ([[@44022003|Acts 22:3]]).

column5: Twenty-second priestly division
column7: The one chosen twenty-second when the divisions of Aaron's descendants were assigned by lot ([[@13024001|1 Chr 24:1]]; [[@13024017|1 Chr 24:17]]).

column5: One of David's mighty men, an Ithrite
column7: An Ithrite, he is named on the list of David's mighty men. He appears next to Ira, who was also an Ithrite ([[@10023038|2 Sam 23:38]]; [[@13011040|1 Chr 11:40]]).

column5: Hill the measuring line reaches
column7: Speaking of the days when Jerusalem would be rebuilt, God said the measuring line would go straight out to the hill Gareb and turn toward Goah ([[@24031038-24031039|Jer 31:38-39]]).

column5: People of the father of Keilah
column7: Judah's genealogy mentions "the fathers of Keilah the Garmite". They are listed among the sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham ([[@13004019|1 Chr 4:19]]).

column5: Son of Eliphaz, a chief of Edom
column7: He was a son of Eliphaz, Esau’s son ([[@1036011|Gen 36:11]]). He was one of the chiefs who came from Eliphaz in the land of Edom ([[@1036016|Gen 36:16]]).

column5: A Philistine city, Goliath's hometown
column7: Gath was one of the five cities of the Philistines ([[@9006017|1 Sam 6:17]]). When the Philistines moved the captured ark of God there, the LORD struck the people of the city, and tumors broke out on them ([[@9005008-9005009|1 Sam 5:8-9]]). Goliath, the giant who fought David, was from Gath ([[@9017004|1 Sam 17:4]]). When David was fleeing from Saul, he even took refuge with Achish, king of Gath ([[@9021010|1 Sam 21:10]]).

column5: Hometown of the prophet Jonah
column7: It was a place on the border of the tribe of Zebulun ([[@6019013|Josh 19:13]]). The prophet Jonah, the son of Amittai, was from Gath Hepher ([[@12014025|2 Kgs 14:25]]).

column5: A Levite city in the tribe of Dan
column7: It was one of the cities the tribe of Dan received ([[@6019045|Josh 19:45]]). It was also one of the cities from the tribe of Dan given to the Levites ([[@6021023-6021024|Josh 21:23-24]]).

column5: One of the five Philistine cities
column7: It was an ancient city on the Mediterranean coast, named at the southern border of the land of Canaan ([[@1010019|Gen 10:19]]). It was one of the cities ruled by the five lords of the Philistines. In Gaza, Samson pulled up the doors of the city gate, bar and all, at midnight and carried them away, and later, after he was captured, he ground at the mill in the prison of Gaza ([[@7016001-7016003|Judg 16:1-3]]; [[@7016021|Judg 16:21]]). In the New Testament an angel of the Lord sent Philip to "the way that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza" and on that road Philip shared the gospel with an Ethiopian eunuch ([[@44008026|Acts 8:26]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Gazzam' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]], 48; [[@16007051|Neh 7:51]]).

column5: The valley of craftsmen
column7: Joab became the father of Ge Harashim, for they were craftsmen ([[@13004014|1 Chr 4:14]]). After the exile, descendants of Benjamin lived in 'the valley of craftsmen' ([[@16011035|Neh 11:35]]).

column5: Priests' town of the tribe of Benjamin
column7: It was a town of the tribe of Benjamin, one of the towns given to the priests ([[@6021017|Josh 21:17]]). In Saul's time Jonathan struck the garrison of the Philistines that was in Geba ([[@9013003|1 Sam 13:3]]). Asa king of Judah took the stones and timber Baasha had been using to build Ramah and built Geba and Mizpah ([[@11015022|1 Kgs 15:22]]). Because it lay at the northern edge of Judah, "from Geba to Beersheba" was used to mean the whole land of Judah ([[@12023008|2 Kgs 23:8]]).

column5: The town of the Gebalites, who cut stone
column7: In Joshua's time 'the land of the Gebalites' was among the lands not yet taken ([[@6013005|Josh 13:5]]). The Gebalites cut the stones for Solomon's temple, and in the Psalms Gebal is among those plotting against Israel ([[@11005018|1 Kgs 5:18]]; [[@19083007|Ps 83:7]]).

column5: One of Solomon's twelve officers
column7: Son of Uri, the officer of Solomon who alone was in charge of the land of Gilead, once the country of Sihon and Og ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004019|1 Kgs 4:19]]).

column5: Place that fled as Assyria's king came
column7: In the prophecy picturing the king of Assyria advancing toward Jerusalem, Isaiah says, "The inhabitants of Gebim flee for safety" ([[@23010028|Isa 10:28]]; [[@23010031|Isa 10:31]]).

column5: Governor of Judah appointed by Babylon
column7: He was the grandson of Shaphan and the son of Ahikam. After Jerusalem fell, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon appointed him to govern the people left in the land of Judah ([[@12025022|2 Kgs 25:22]]). Jeremiah also went to him at Mizpah and lived among the people ([[@24040006|Jer 40:6]]). Gedaliah told the people not to be afraid and to serve the king of Babylon, but he was struck down with the sword by Ishmael, a man of the royal family ([[@24041002|Jer 41:2]]). Second Kings also tells how he was killed at Mizpah ([[@12025025|2 Kgs 25:25]]).

column5: Son of Jeduthun, a singer
column7: A son of Jeduthun, he played the harp under his father, giving thanks and praise to the LORD ([[@13025003|1 Chr 25:3]]). The second lot fell to him, and he served in that turn ([[@13025009|1 Chr 25:9]]).

column5: Priest who married a foreign woman
column7: One of the priests in Ezra's time who had married foreign women; he was of the sons of Jeshua and pledged to put away his wife ([[@15010018-15010019|Ezra 10:18-19]]).

column5: Son of Pashhur who heard Jeremiah
column7: Son of Pashhur, one of those who heard the words Jeremiah spoke to the people. These princes told the king to put Jeremiah to death ([[@24038001|Jer 38:1]]; [[@24038004|Jer 38:4]]).

column5: Grandfather of the prophet Zephaniah
