column7: Grandfather of the prophet Zephaniah. Zephaniah was the son of Cushi, the grandson of Gedaliah, the great-grandson of Amariah, and the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah ([[@36001001|Zeph 1:1]]).

column5: A town in the lowland of Judah
column7: It was one of the lowland towns the tribe of Judah received ([[@6015033-6015036|Josh 15:33-36]]). Among the mighty men who came to David was 'Jozabad the Gederathite' ([[@13012004|1 Chr 12:4]]).

column5: Town in the lowland of Judah
column7: It was a lowland town given to the tribe of Judah ([[@6015041|Josh 15:41]]). In Ahaz's time the Philistines took it and lived there ([[@14028018|2 Chr 28:18]]).

column5: City in Judah's lowland
column7: One of the lowland cities the tribe of Judah received; it is listed with Gederah ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]; [[@6015036|Josh 15:36]]).

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: It was a town in the hill country of the tribe of Judah, listed with Halhul and Beth Zur ([[@6015058|Josh 15:58]]). In Judah's genealogy, Jered is named as 'the father of Gedor' ([[@13004018|1 Chr 4:18]]).

column5: Where the Simeonites found pasture
column7: The leaders of the Simeonites went to the entrance of Gedor, on the east side of the valley, to seek pasture for their flocks, and found rich, good pasture ([[@13004024|1 Chr 4:24]]; [[@13004038-13004040|1 Chr 4:38-40]]).

column5: Son of Jeiel, the father of Gibeon
column7: He was one of the sons of Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, and Maacah ([[@13008029-13008031|1 Chr 8:29-31]]; [[@13009035-13009037|1 Chr 9:35-37]]).

column5: Elisha's servant, struck with leprosy for greed
column7: Gehazi was the servant of the prophet Elisha. He told Elisha that the Shunammite woman had no son, and when the boy died he went ahead with Elisha's staff and laid it on the child's face ([[@12004014|2 Kgs 4:14]]; [[@12004031|2 Kgs 4:31]]). After the Syrian commander Naaman was healed, Gehazi secretly ran after him, got silver and clothing from him with a lie, and hid them in the house. When Elisha rebuked him and said, "the leprosy of Naaman will cling to you and to your offspring forever", Gehazi at once became leprous ([[@12005020-12005027|2 Kgs 5:20-27]]). Later he also told the king about the great things Elisha had done ([[@12008004-12008005|2 Kgs 8:4-5]]).

column5: Father of Ammiel, the spy from Dan
column7: Father of Ammiel, chosen from the tribe of Dan among the men Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013012|Num 13:12]]; [[@4013016|Num 13:16]]).

column5: Son of Hilkiah who carried Jeremiah's letter
column7: Son of Hilkiah, sent by King Zedekiah to the king of Babylon. Along with Elasah, he carried the letter Jeremiah sent to the exiles ([[@24029001-24029003|Jer 29:1-3]]).

column5: Son of Shaphan, a scribe under Jehoiakim
column7: He was a scribe, the son of Shaphan, and Baruch read Jeremiah's words to the people from his room ([[@24036010|Jer 36:10]]). He begged the king not to burn the scroll, but the king would not listen ([[@24036025|Jer 36:25]]).

column5: Peoples other than Israel
column7: Gentiles means all the peoples who are not Jews. In the Old Testament, too, God promised to make his servant "a light to the nations" so that his salvation would reach to the end of the earth ([[@23049006|Isa 49:6]]). The circumcised believers who came with Peter were amazed to see the Holy Spirit poured out on the Gentiles as well ([[@44010045|Acts 10:45]]). Paul taught that through the gospel the Gentiles are "fellow heirs and fellow members of the body" and share in the promise in Christ Jesus ([[@49003006|Eph 3:6]]).

column5: A descendant of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the list of Benjamin’s sons when Jacob’s family went down to Egypt ([[@1046021|Gen 46:21]]). In 1 Chronicles he appears as a son of Bela, Benjamin’s firstborn ([[@13008003|1 Chr 8:3]]). The judge Ehud was called 'the son of Gera' ([[@7003015|Judg 3:15]]).

column5: Father of Shimei, who cursed David
column7: He was a Benjamite, the father of Shimei, who cursed David during Absalom's rebellion ([[@10016005|2 Sam 16:5]]; [[@10019016|2 Sam 19:16]]).

column5: Grandson of Benjamin, son of Bela
column7: One of the sons of Bela, Benjamin's firstborn; he is listed with Addar and Abihud ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]; [[@13008003|1 Chr 8:3]]).

column5: Man in the account of Ehud's family
column7: A name in the account of Ehud's sons. The text records, "Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera, who carried them captive" ([[@13008006-13008007|1 Chr 8:6-7]]).

column5: Place ruled by Abimelech, a Philistine king
column7: It is named together with Gaza in describing the southern border of the land of Canaan ([[@1010019|Gen 10:19]]). While staying in Gerar, Abraham said that his wife Sarah was his sister, and Abimelech king of Gerar took Sarah ([[@1020001-1020002|Gen 20:1-2]]). When a famine came, Isaac also went to Gerar, to Abimelech king of the Philistines ([[@1026001|Gen 26:1]]). Isaac farmed in that land and "reaped in the same year one hundred times what he planted", and the LORD blessed him ([[@1026012|Gen 26:12]]).

column5: Where Jesus healed a demon-possessed man
column7: It was a region on the other side of the Sea of Galilee, where Jesus healed a man possessed by demons ([[@41005001-41005002|Mark 5:1-2]]; [[@42008026-42008027|Luke 8:26-27]]). Matthew calls this region 'the country of the Gadarenes' ([[@40008028|Matt 8:28]]).

column5: The mountain where the blessing was proclaimed
column7: Moses said that when they entered Canaan they were to proclaim the blessing on Mount Gerizim ([[@5011029|Deut 11:29]]). Jotham called out to the men of Shechem from the top of this mountain ([[@7009007|Judg 9:7]]).

column5: Son of Moses and Zipporah
column7: He was the son Moses had by Zipporah in Midian. Moses named him Gershom, saying, "I have lived as a foreigner in a foreign land" ([[@2002021-2002022|Exod 2:21-22]]). Later Moses' father-in-law Jethro brought Zipporah and her two sons, Gershom and Eliezer, to Moses in the wilderness ([[@2018002-2018004|Exod 18:2-4]]). In David's time Shebuel, a descendant of Gershom, became a chief and was put in charge of the treasuries ([[@13023015-13023016|1 Chr 23:15-16]]; [[@13026024|1 Chr 26:24]]). Judges says that "Jonathan, the son of Gershom, the son of Moses" became a priest for the tribe of Dan ([[@7018030|Judg 18:30]]).

column5: Descendant of Phinehas who came with Ezra
column7: One of the family heads who came up from Babylon with Ezra in the reign of King Artaxerxes; he was from the descendants of Phinehas ([[@15008001-15008002|Ezra 8:1-2]]).

column5: Levi's firstborn son, ancestor of the Gershonites
column7: Gershon was the firstborn of Levi's three sons. He went down to Egypt with Jacob and had two sons, Libni and Shimei ([[@2006017|Exod 6:17]]). In the wilderness the Gershonite families camped behind the tabernacle, on the west side ([[@4003023|Num 3:23]]), and they were in charge of the tabernacle, the tent, its covering, and the screens and hangings ([[@4003025-4003026|Num 3:25-26]]). After entering Canaan, they received thirteen cities from the tribes of Issachar, Asher, and Naphtali and from the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan ([[@6021006|Josh 21:6]]).

column5: Place near Bethlehem where Johanan stayed
column7: After Gedaliah was killed, Johanan and the remnant of the people set out for Egypt and stayed at this place near Bethlehem ([[@24041016-24041017|Jer 41:16-17]]).

column5: Son of Jahdai
column7: A son of Jahdai in the genealogy of Caleb's family; he was a brother of Regem, Jothan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph ([[@13002047|1 Chr 2:47]]).

column5: The Arabian who opposed Nehemiah
column7: He was an Arabian who, with Sanballat and Tobiah, mocked and hindered the rebuilding of Jerusalem's wall ([[@16002019|Neh 2:19]]; [[@16006001-16006002|Neh 6:1-2]]). In Nehemiah 6 he is also called 'Gashmu' ([[@16006006|Neh 6:6]]).

column5: Small Syrian kingdom, home of Absalom's mother
column7: It was a small kingdom of Syrians east of the Jordan, north of Bashan near Mount Hermon ([[@5003014|Deut 3:14]]). Israel did not drive out the Geshurites, so they went on living among Israel ([[@6013013|Josh 13:13]]). David married Maacah, the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur, and she bore Absalom ([[@10003003|2 Sam 3:3]]). After killing Amnon, Absalom fled to his grandfather in Geshur and stayed there three years ([[@10013037-10013038|2 Sam 13:37-38]]).

column5: Son of Aram
column7: He was a grandson of Noah's son Shem. A son of Shem's son Aram, he was the brother of Uz, Hul, and Mash ([[@1010022-1010023|Gen 10:22-23]]).

column5: Where Jesus prayed
column6: a very fat or plentiful vale
column7: It was the place where Jesus went with his disciples to pray ([[@40026036|Matt 26:36]]). There he prayed, "not what I desire, but what you desire" ([[@40026039|Matt 26:39]]).

column5: Spy from the tribe of Gad
column7: Son of Machi, chosen from the tribe of Gad among the men Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013015-4013016|Num 13:15-16]]).

column5: Canaanite city Joshua struck
column7: It was an ancient Canaanite city. Horam king of Gezer came up to help Lachish and was defeated by Joshua ([[@6010033|Josh 10:33]]). But the descendants of Ephraim did not drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer ([[@6016010|Josh 16:10]]), and the city is also on the list of towns given to the Levites. David pursued the Philistines as far as Gezer, and later Pharaoh king of Egypt captured the city and gave it as a gift to his daughter, Solomon's wife ([[@10005025|2 Sam 5:25]]; [[@11009016|1 Kgs 9:16]]).

column5: Place Joab reached chasing Abner
column7: As Joab and Abishai pursued Abner, the sun went down when they reached the hill of Ammah, which lies before Giah by the way of the wilderness of Gibeon ([[@10002024|2 Sam 2:24]]).

column5: A Levite town of the tribe of Dan
column7: It was a town of the tribe of Dan that was given to the Levites ([[@6019044|Josh 19:44]]; [[@6021023|Josh 21:23]]). Nadab king of Israel was killed by Baasha while he was besieging this place, which belonged to the Philistines ([[@11015027|1 Kgs 15:27]]).

column5: A name in Caleb's genealogy
column7: Sheva, born to Caleb's concubine Maacah, is called 'the father of Machbena and the father of Gibea' ([[@13002048-13002049|1 Chr 2:48-49]]).

column5: Town in the hill country of Judah
column7: It was one of the hill country towns given to the tribe of Judah, named with Kain and Timnah ([[@6015057|Josh 15:57]]). The Bible also mentions other places with the same name.

column5: A town of Benjamin, Saul's hometown
column7: Gibeah means 'hill', and it was a town in the land of Benjamin. In the time of the judges, a terrible thing happened there: wicked men of the town abused a Levite's concubine until she died ([[@7019022-7019026|Judg 19:22-26]]). Because of this, war broke out between the tribes of Israel and Benjamin, and the tribe of Benjamin was nearly wiped out ([[@7020046-7020048|Judg 20:46-48]]). King Saul's home was here, so it was also called "Gibeah of Saul" ([[@9010026|1 Sam 10:26]]; [[@9011004|1 Sam 11:4]]).

column5: Hill of God with a Philistine garrison
column7: The place where the Philistine garrison was. Samuel told Saul that in the city there he would meet a band of prophets coming down and prophesying ([[@9010001|1 Sam 10:1]]; [[@9010005|1 Sam 10:5]]).

column5: A Hivite city that made peace with Joshua
column7: Gibeon was a large city in the land of Benjamin where Hivites lived. When they heard that Jericho and Ai had fallen, they disguised themselves as people from a far country and made a peace covenant with Joshua ([[@6009003-6009015|Josh 9:3-15]]). Israel realized they had been deceived, but because of their oath they let them live and made them woodcutters and water carriers ([[@6009021|Josh 9:21]]). When five Amorite kings attacked Gibeon, Joshua went to help, and that day the sun and moon stood still ([[@6010012-6010013|Josh 10:12-13]]). Solomon met God in a dream at Gibeon ([[@11003005|1 Kgs 3:5]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a singer
column7: He was a son of Heman, who served as a singer in David's time ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]). The twenty-second lot fell to him, and he served in that turn ([[@13025029|1 Chr 25:29]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Giddel' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]], 47; [[@16007049|Neh 7:49]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of Solomon's servants
column7: Among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Giddel' ([[@15002055-15002056|Ezra 2:55-56]]; [[@16007058|Neh 7:58]]).

column5: The judge of Israel who defeated Midian
column7: Gideon was the son of Joash the Abiezrite, of the tribe of Manasseh. While he was threshing wheat in a winepress to hide it from the Midianites, he met the angel of the LORD and was called ([[@7006011|Judg 6:11]]). He tore down the altar of Baal at his father's house and was given the name Jerub-Baal ([[@7006032|Judg 6:32]]). After confirming God's will with the sign of the fleece ([[@7006037|Judg 6:37]]), he and three hundred men took trumpets, pitchers, and torches, shouted, "The sword of the LORD and of Gideon!" and defeated the great army of Midian ([[@7007020|Judg 7:20]]).

column5: Father of Abidan, leader of the tribe of Benjamin
column7: He was the father of Abidan, the leader of the children of Benjamin in the wilderness ([[@4001011|Num 1:11]]). His son brought the offering on behalf of the children of Benjamin on the ninth day ([[@4007060|Num 7:60]]).

column5: Place reached chasing the Benjamites
column7: In the battle of Gibeah, Israel followed hard after the Benjamites fleeing toward the wilderness, reached Gidom, and killed two thousand of them ([[@7020043-7020045|Judg 20:43-45]]).

column5: Second river of Eden; spring by Jerusalem
column7: The Bible mentions two places called Gihon. One is the second of the four rivers into which the river flowing out of Eden divided, and it is said to flow around the whole land of Cush ([[@1002010|Gen 2:10]], 13). The other is a spring near Jerusalem, where, at David's command, Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed Solomon as king ([[@11001033-11001034|1 Kgs 1:33-34]], 38-39, 45). Hezekiah stopped the upper spring of Gihon and brought its water straight down to the west side of the City of David ([[@14032030|2 Chr 32:30]]).

column5: Musician at the wall's dedication
column7: A brother of Zechariah the trumpeter at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall; he played the musical instruments of David the man of God ([[@16012035-16012036|Neh 12:35-36]]).

column5: The mountain where Saul died
column7: This is where Saul gathered all Israel and camped to fight the Philistines ([[@9028004|1 Sam 28:4]]). The Philistines killed Saul on Gilboa, and David mourned, crying, "You mountains of Gilboa" ([[@10021012|2 Sam 21:12]]; [[@10001021|2 Sam 1:21]]).

column5: Mountain where Saul and his sons died
column7: It is where King Saul gathered all Israel and camped to fight the Philistines ([[@9028004|1 Sam 28:4]]). In that battle the men of Israel fled before the Philistines and fell dead on Mount Gilboa, and the next day the Philistines found Saul and his three sons dead on Mount Gilboa ([[@9031001|1 Sam 31:1]], 8). When David heard the news, he lamented over Saul and Jonathan, singing, "You mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew or rain on you" ([[@10001017|2 Sam 1:17]], 21).

column5: The hill country east of the Jordan
column7: It is a mountainous region east of the Jordan River. When Jacob fled from Laban, he headed for the mountain of Gilead ([[@1031021|Gen 31:21]]), and the two men piled up a heap of stones as a witness between them ([[@1031047-1031048|Gen 31:47-48]]). Moses gave this land to the children of Gad and the children of Reuben ([[@4032029|Num 32:29]]). It was famous for its balm that healed wounds, and Jeremiah lamented, "Is there no balm in Gilead?" ([[@24008022|Jer 8:22]]).

column5: Grandson of Manasseh, son of Machir
column7: He was the grandson of Manasseh, Joseph's son, and the son of Machir ([[@4026029|Num 26:29]]; [[@13007017|1 Chr 7:17]]). From him came the families of Iezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Shemida, and Hepher ([[@4026030-4026032|Num 26:30-32]]). Hepher's son Zelophehad had no sons, only daughters, and these daughters were Gilead's great-granddaughters ([[@4027001|Num 27:1]]). He is a different person from Gilead, the name of the land east of the Jordan.

column5: Father of the judge Jephthah
column7: He was the man who fathered the judge Jephthah by a prostitute ([[@7011001|Judg 11:1]]). When the sons his wife bore him grew up, they drove Jephthah out ([[@7011002|Judg 11:2]]).

column5: A man in Gad's genealogy
column7: A man in the genealogy of Abihail of the tribe of Gad; he was the son of Michael and the father of Jaroah ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005014|1 Chr 5:14]]).

column5: Israel's first camp after crossing the Jordan
column7: Gilgal was the place where Israel first camped after crossing the Jordan River, on the east side of Jericho ([[@6004019|Josh 4:19]]). Joshua set up here the twelve stones taken from the Jordan ([[@6004020|Josh 4:20]]). The LORD said, "I have rolled away the reproach of Egypt from you" so this place was named Gilgal ([[@6005009|Josh 5:9]]). Later it was one of the places Samuel visited each year as he judged Israel, and it was also where the people made Saul king ([[@9011015|1 Sam 11:15]]). Scholars differ on whether every Gilgal in the Bible is the same place.

column5: Place where Elijah and Elisha stayed
column7: Before Elijah was taken up to heaven, he set out with Elisha from Gilgal ([[@12002001|2 Kgs 2:1]]). During a famine, Elisha had stew cooked here for the sons of the prophets ([[@12004038|2 Kgs 4:38]]).

column5: Ahithophel’s hometown
column7: It was one of the towns in the hill country of Judah ([[@6015048-6015051|Josh 15:48-51]]). David’s counselor Ahithophel came from here, and when Absalom rebelled, he sent for him from Giloh ([[@10015012|2 Sam 15:12]]).

column5: Judean city taken by the Philistines
column7: One of the cities in Judah's lowland and the South that the Philistines invaded and took in Ahaz's time, along with its villages ([[@14028018-14028019|2 Chr 28:18-19]]).

column5: Father of Tibni
column7: He was the father of Tibni. The people of Israel were divided in two, with half following Tibni and half following Omri, and Tibni died and Omri became king ([[@11016021-11016022|1 Kgs 16:21-22]]).

column5: A priest who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the priests who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s day ([[@16010006|Neh 10:6]]; [[@16010008|Neh 10:8]]). In the days of Joiakim, the head of Ginnethon’s family was Meshullam ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012016|Neh 12:16]]).

column5: One of seven nations living in Canaan
column7: They were a people descended from Canaan, listed in the genealogy alongside the Jebusites and the Amorites ([[@1010015-1010016|Gen 10:15-16]]). When God made his covenant with Abram, he named the Girgashites among the peoples of the land he would give to Abram's descendants ([[@1015021|Gen 15:21]]). They were one of seven nations greater and mightier than Israel, and God said he would drive them out before Israel ([[@5007001|Deut 7:1]]). The Bible does not say exactly where they lived, so it is hard to know.

column5: People David raided
column7: A people David raided, along with the Geshurites and Amalekites, while he lived in the land of the Philistines ([[@9027007-9027008|1 Sam 27:7-8]]).

column5: Leader of the temple servants
column7: A leader of the temple servants who lived in Ophel in Nehemiah's time; he was over them together with Ziha ([[@16011021|Neh 11:21]]).

column5: Place where the Beerothites fled
column7: It was where the Beerothites fled and stayed ([[@10004003|2 Sam 4:3]]). After the exile, descendants of Benjamin lived here ([[@16011033|Neh 11:33]]).

column5: Hometown of Hashem, David's warrior
column7: The list of David's mighty men includes "the sons of Hashem the Gizonite". Gizonite points to where Hashem came from ([[@13011034|1 Chr 11:34]]).

column5: Where the measuring line turns
column7: Speaking of the days when Jerusalem would be rebuilt, God said the measuring line would reach the hill Gareb and turn toward Goah ([[@24031038-24031039|Jer 31:38-39]]).

column5: Grandson of Joel, a Reubenite
column7: A man in the genealogy of Reuben's descendants; he was the son of Shemaiah son of Joel, and the father of Shimei ([[@13005003-13005004|1 Chr 5:3-4]]).

column5: King of the land of Magog in Ezekiel's prophecy
column7: He is the leader of the enemy who comes to attack God's people in Ezekiel 38-39. The Bible calls him "Gog, of the land of Magog, the prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal" ([[@26038002|Ezek 38:2]]). God said that in the latter days he would bring Gog against the land of Israel, and in this way show his holiness before the eyes of the nations ([[@26038016|Ezek 38:16]]). Gog and his multitude would perish and be buried in a valley in the land of Israel, which would be called 'The valley of Hamon Gog' ([[@26039011|Ezek 39:11]]). Revelation also has a scene where Satan deceives the nations in the four corners of the earth, "Gog and Magog," and gathers them for war, and scholars differ on whom Gog actually refers to ([[@66020007-66020008|Rev 20:7-8]]).

column5: The nation ruled by Tidal
column7: It was the nation ruled by Tidal, one of the kings allied with Chedorlaomer ([[@1014001|Gen 14:1]]; [[@1014009|Gen 14:9]]). Among the kings Joshua struck was also 'the king of Goiim in Gilgal' ([[@6012023|Josh 12:23]]).

column5: A city of refuge in Bashan
column7: It was a city in Bashan, a city of refuge for manslayers, set aside for the tribe of Manasseh ([[@5004043|Deut 4:43]]; [[@6020008|Josh 20:8]]). It was given to the Levites, the descendants of Gershon ([[@6021027|Josh 21:27]]).

column5: The place where Jesus was crucified
column7: Golgotha is the name of the place where Jesus was crucified. The Gospels explain the name as "The place of a skull" ([[@40027033|Matt 27:33]]; [[@41015022|Mark 15:22]]). Carrying his own cross, Jesus went out to this place near the city, and there he was crucified along with two others ([[@43019017-43019020|John 19:17-20]]). Hebrews says that Jesus "suffered outside of the gate" ([[@58013012|Heb 13:12]]). Scholars differ on its exact location.

column5: Place where Jesus was crucified
column7: It was the place called 'The Skull', where Jesus was crucified ([[@42023033|Luke 23:33]]). In Hebrew it is called Golgotha ([[@43019017|John 19:17]]).

column5: Philistine giant struck down by David
column7: He was a man of Gath, a champion who came out of the Philistine camp to challenge Israel. He was six cubits and a span tall, wore a bronze helmet and a coat of mail, and the shaft of his spear was like a weaver's beam ([[@9017004-9017007|1 Sam 17:4-7]]). David went out to him "in the name of the LORD of Armies," slung a stone that struck him in the forehead, then drew Goliath's own sword, killed him, and cut off his head ([[@9017045|1 Sam 17:45]], 49-51). His sword was later kept by Ahimelech the priest at Nob and was given to David when he was fleeing from Saul ([[@9021001|1 Sam 21:1]], 9).

column5: A son of Japheth
column7: He was a son of Japheth, Noah's son ([[@1010002|Gen 10:2]]). His sons were Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah ([[@1010003|Gen 10:3]]).

column5: Wife of the prophet Hosea
column7: Daughter of Diblaim, the woman Hosea took as his wife at God's word. She bore Jezreel, Lo-Ruhamah, and another son ([[@28001002-28001004|Hos 1:2-4]]; [[@28001006|Hos 1:6]]; [[@28001008|Hos 1:8]]).

column5: City destroyed along with Sodom
column7: Gomorrah was a city in the plain of the Jordan, and in the Bible it nearly always appears together with Sodom ([[@1013010|Gen 13:10]]). The LORD said that "the cry of Sodom and Gomorrah is great" and that "their sin is very grievous" ([[@1018020|Gen 18:20]]). In the end the LORD rained sulfur and fire from the sky and destroyed the two cities ([[@1019024|Gen 19:24]]). After that, Sodom and Gomorrah were often used as an example of the judgment that awaits the ungodly ([[@61002006|2 Pet 2:6]]).

column5: The land in Egypt where Jacob's family lived
column7: It was the land in Egypt where Joseph wanted his father Jacob and his brothers to live, close to him ([[@1045010|Gen 45:10]]). Pharaoh gave them the land of Goshen, saying to let them dwell in "the best of the land" ([[@1047006|Gen 47:6]]). The Bible says that Israel got possessions there, and "were fruitful, and multiplied exceedingly" ([[@1047027|Gen 47:27]]). When plagues fell on Egypt, God set apart the land of Goshen so that there were no swarms of flies there ([[@2008022|Exod 8:22]]).

column5: The land of Goshen in southern Canaan
column7: Joshua struck the land from Kadesh Barnea to Gaza, and all the country of Goshen as far as Gibeon ([[@6010041|Josh 10:41]]). There is also a Goshen among the towns of the hill country of Judah ([[@6015048-6015051|Josh 15:48-51]]).

column5: The good news of salvation through Jesus Christ
column7: Gospel means 'good news', and it refers to the joyful news of the salvation God has accomplished through Jesus Christ. Long ago Isaiah sang that the feet of him "who brings good news" and proclaims salvation are beautiful ([[@23052007|Isa 52:7]]). In Galilee Jesus preached, "Repent, and believe in the Good News" ([[@41001015|Mark 1:15]]). Paul said the gospel is "the power of God for salvation for everyone who believes", and he taught that at its heart is this: Christ died for our sins, was buried, and was raised on the third day ([[@45001016|Rom 1:16]]; [[@46015003-46015004|1 Cor 15:3-4]]).

column5: A place where Israelite captives were taken
column7: It was one of the places where the king of Assyria settled the Israelites he carried away after taking Samaria ([[@12017006|2 Kgs 17:6]]). The king of Assyria boasted that his fathers had destroyed Gozan ([[@12019012|2 Kgs 19:12]]).

column5: God's love and favor freely given
column7: Grace is the love and favor that God freely gives to people who do not deserve it. The Bible says, "Noah found favor in the LORD’s eyes" ([[@1006008|Gen 6:8]]). The Gospel of John says, "Grace and truth were realized through Jesus Christ" ([[@43001017|John 1:17]]). Paul said that we have been saved by that grace through faith, and when he was weak he heard the Lord say, "My grace is sufficient for you" ([[@49002008|Eph 2:8]]; [[@47012009|2 Cor 12:9]]).

column5: The Mediterranean, western border of the Promised Land
column7: This is today's Mediterranean Sea, the sea that formed the western border of the Promised Land ([[@4034006|Num 34:6]]). God told Joshua that their land would reach from the wilderness and Lebanon to the Euphrates River, and "to the great sea toward the going down of the sun" ([[@6001004|Josh 1:4]]). Because the Philistines lived along its coast, it was also called 'the sea of the Philistines' ([[@2023031|Exod 23:31]]). In Ezekiel's vision it also appears as the western border of the new land ([[@26047020|Ezek 47:20]]).

column5: Greece, called Javan in the Old Testament
column7: This is the land of today's Greece. The Old Testament name 'Javan' is also usually taken to mean Greece; Javan appears in the genealogy as one of the sons of Noah's son Japheth ([[@1010002|Gen 10:2]]). In Joel the LORD rebuked Tyre, Sidon, and Philistia for selling the children of Judah and Jerusalem to 'the sons of the Greeks' ([[@29003004-29003006|Joel 3:4-6]]). In Daniel's vision the shaggy male goat stood for "the king of Greece" ([[@27008021|Dan 8:21]]). After Paul went through Macedonia encouraging the disciples, he came to Greece and stayed three months ([[@44020001-44020003|Acts 20:1-3]]).

column5: Gate where the dedication procession stopped
column7: When the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated, one of the thanksgiving companies passed the sheep gate and stood still at the gate of the guard ([[@16012038-16012039|Neh 12:38-39]]).

column5: Son of Naphtali
column7: He was a son of Naphtali, Jacob’s son ([[@1046024|Gen 46:24]]). The family of the Gunites came from him ([[@4026048|Num 26:48]]).

column5: Grandfather of Ahi, a Gadite chief
column7: A man in the genealogy of Gad's descendants; Ahi, who became chief, was Guni's grandson and Abdiel's son ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005015|1 Chr 5:15]]).

column5: Ascent where Ahaziah was struck
column7: Jehu pursued Ahaziah king of Judah and struck him at the ascent of Gur near Ibleam. Ahaziah fled to Megiddo and died there ([[@12009027|2 Kgs 9:27]]).

column5: Home of Arabians Uzziah defeated
column7: God helped Uzziah against the Philistines, the Arabians who lived in Gur Baal, and the Meunim ([[@14026007|2 Chr 26:7]]).

column5: Son of Ashhur and Naarah
column7: A son born to Naarah, wife of Ashhur the father of Tekoa; he was a brother of Ahuzzam, Hepher, and Temeni ([[@13004005-13004006|1 Chr 4:5-6]]).

column5: Priestly family missing from the records
column7: It was a priestly family that returned from exile, but because they could not find their names in the genealogical records, they could not serve as priests ([[@15002061-15002062|Ezra 2:61-62]]). In Nehemiah it appears as 'Hobaiah' ([[@16007063|Neh 7:63]]).

column5: Prophet who wrote the book of Habakkuk
column7: He was the prophet who gave us the book of Habakkuk ([[@35001001|Hab 1:1]]). His prayer is found in Habakkuk 3 ([[@35003001|Hab 3:1]]).

column5: Grandfather of Jaazaniah the Rechabite
column7: Grandfather of Jaazaniah of the Rechabites. Jeremiah brought Jaazaniah, the son of Jeremiah and grandson of Habazziniah, and the whole house of the Rechabites into the LORD's house ([[@24035003-24035004|Jer 35:3-4]]).

column5: A river where Israelite captives were taken
column7: The king of Assyria took Samaria, carried Israel away captive, and placed them on the Habor, the river of Gozan, among other places ([[@12017006|2 Kgs 17:6]]). The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh were also carried away here ([[@13005026|1 Chr 5:26]]).

column5: Father of Nehemiah
column7: He was Nehemiah's father, and the book of Nehemiah begins with 'the words of Nehemiah the son of Hacaliah' ([[@16001001|Neh 1:1]]). The list of those who sealed the covenant also names 'Nehemiah the governor, the son of Hacaliah' ([[@16010001|Neh 10:1]]).

column5: A hill where David hid
column7: The Ziphites told Saul that David was hiding in the strongholds in the woods on the hill of Hachilah ([[@9023019|1 Sam 23:19]]). Saul camped by the road on the hill of Hachilah ([[@9026001-9026003|1 Sam 26:1-3]]).

column5: Father of Jehiel
column7: Father of Jehiel, who in David's time was with the king's sons. Jonathan, David's uncle, also appears in the same verse ([[@13027032|1 Chr 27:32]]).

column5: Family of Jashobeam, one of David's mighty men
column7: Jashobeam, the chief of David's mighty men, is called 'the son of a Hachmonite' ([[@13011011|1 Chr 11:11]]). In 2 Samuel he appears as 'a Tahchemonite' ([[@10023008|2 Sam 23:8]]).

column5: Son of Ishmael
column7: He was one of the twelve sons of Abraham's son Ishmael. These sons became twelve princes according to their tribes ([[@1025015-1025016|Gen 25:15-16]]; [[@13001030|1 Chr 1:30]]).

column5: An Edomite king who defeated Midian
column7: He was the son of Bedad, the king of Edom who followed Husham. He struck Midian in the field of Moab, and the name of his city was Avith ([[@1036035|Gen 36:35]]; [[@13001046|1 Chr 1:46]]).

column5: A king of Edom
column7: He was a king of Edom who reigned after Baal Hanan died; his city was Pai and his wife was Mehetabel ([[@13001050|1 Chr 1:50]]). In Genesis he is called 'Hadar' ([[@1036039|Gen 36:39]]).

column5: An Edomite who became Solomon’s adversary
column7: He was of the royal family of Edom, and the LORD raised him up as an adversary to Solomon ([[@11011014|1 Kgs 11:14]]). In Egypt he found favor with Pharaoh and married the sister of Queen Tahpenes ([[@11011019|1 Kgs 11:19]]).

column5: Place in the valley of Megiddo
column7: Zechariah prophesied that on that day there would be a great mourning in Jerusalem, like the mourning of Hadadrimmon in the valley of Megiddo ([[@38012010-38012011|Zech 12:10-11]]).

column5: King of Zobah defeated by David
column7: He was the son of Rehob and king of Zobah. When he tried to win back his power toward the Euphrates River, he was badly defeated by David, and the Syrians of Damascus that came to help him was also defeated ([[@10008003-10008005|2 Sam 8:3-5]]). David took the shields of gold carried by his servants and a great quantity of bronze from his towns ([[@10008007-10008008|2 Sam 8:7-8]]). Later he fought again to help Ammon but was defeated, and the kings who served him made peace with Israel ([[@10010019|2 Sam 10:19]]). Rezon, Solomon's adversary, was a man who had fled from Hadadezer ([[@11011023|1 Kgs 11:23]]).

column5: City in Judah's lowland
column7: One of the lowland cities the tribe of Judah received; it is listed with Zenan and Migdal Gad ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]; [[@6015037|Josh 15:37]]).

column5: The place where the dead go down
column7: Hades is a word for the place where the dead go down. Thinking Joseph was dead, Jacob wept and said, "I will go down to Sheol to my son, mourning" ([[@1037035|Gen 37:35]]). Jesus said that Capernaum "will go down to Hades", and he said of the church he would build on the rock, "the gates of Hades will not prevail against it" ([[@40011023|Matt 11:23]]; [[@40016018|Matt 16:18]]). Peter said that David foresaw the resurrection of Christ and spoke of how his soul was not left in Hades and his flesh did not see decay ([[@44002031|Acts 2:31]]).

column5: A town people returned to after the exile
column7: Listed with Lod and Ono, it was a place whose people came back from exile in Babylon ([[@15002033|Ezra 2:33]]). It was one of the places where the children of Benjamin lived after the exile ([[@16011031-16011034|Neh 11:31-34]]).

column5: Father of Amasa, an Ephraimite leader
column7: Father of Amasa. Amasa was one of the heads of the Ephraimites, and he stood against bringing in the captives taken from Judah ([[@14028012-14028013|2 Chr 28:12-13]]).

column5: Son of Joktan
column7: He was one of the sons of Joktan, the son of Eber, a descendant of Shem ([[@1010025-1010027|Gen 10:25-27]]; [[@13001021|1 Chr 1:21]]).

column5: Land the LORD's word was against
column7: Zechariah prophesied, "The LORD’s word is against the land of Hadrach, and will rest upon Damascus" ([[@38009001|Zech 9:1]]).

column5: City of the tribe of Benjamin
column7: One of the cities the Benjaminites received according to their families; it is listed with Zelah and the Jebusite city, that is, Jerusalem ([[@6018028|Josh 18:28]]).

column5: Ancestor of returning temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Hagab' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]]; [[@15002046|Ezra 2:46]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Hagabah' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]], 45; [[@16007048|Neh 7:48]]).

column5: Sarah's Egyptian servant, mother of Ishmael
column7: She was Sarai's Egyptian servant, whom Sarai, being unable to have children, gave to her husband Abram as a wife ([[@1016001-1016003|Gen 16:1-3]]). After Hagar conceived, she despised her mistress, and when she was treated harshly she fled, but by a spring on the way to Shur she met the LORD's angel and was told to go back ([[@1016004-1016009|Gen 16:4-9]]). Hagar called the LORD who spoke to her "a God who sees", and she bore Abram a son, Ishmael ([[@1016013-1016015|Gen 16:13-15]]). Later she was sent away with her son and wandered in the wilderness of Beersheba, but God opened her eyes so that she saw a well of water ([[@1021014-1021019|Gen 21:14-19]]).

column5: Prophet who urged the rebuilding of the temple
column7: He was a prophet who, after the return from exile in Babylon, prophesied to the people of Judah together with Zechariah the son of Iddo ([[@15005001|Ezra 5:1]]). In the second year of King Darius he received the word of the LORD and brought it to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the high priest ([[@37001001|Hag 1:1]]). He rebuked the people, saying, "Is it a time for you yourselves to dwell in your paneled houses, while this house lies waste?", and urged them to build the temple ([[@37001004|Hag 1:4]]). Through the preaching of Haggai and Zechariah, the elders of Judah built and prospered and at last finished the temple ([[@15006014|Ezra 6:14]]).

column5: Father of the overseer Zabdiel
column7: Father of Zabdiel. In Nehemiah's list of those living in Jerusalem, his son Zabdiel was overseer of one hundred twenty-eight mighty men of valor ([[@16011014|Neh 11:14]]).

column5: Son of Gad
column7: A son of Gad, Jacob's son, listed among those who went down to Egypt with Jacob ([[@1046008|Gen 46:8]]; [[@1046016|Gen 46:16]]).

column5: Levite descended from Merari
column7: A man in the genealogy of the Levites descended from Merari; he was the son of Shimea and the father of Asaiah ([[@13006029-13006030|1 Chr 6:29-30]]).

column5: David's wife, mother of Adonijah
column7: She was a wife of David and bore Adonijah, David's fourth son ([[@10003004|2 Sam 3:4]]). Her son Adonijah exalted himself and tried to become king ([[@11001005|1 Kgs 1:5]]).

column5: Father of Mibhar, one of David's mighty men
column7: He appears just once in the list of David's mighty men, as "Mibhar the son of Hagri" ([[@13011038|1 Chr 11:38]]). The Bible tells us nothing more about Hagri himself. Because the name is similar to the 'Hagrites' who fought the Reubenites in Saul's time, some think he came from that people, but scholars differ ([[@13005010|1 Chr 5:10]]). Among those in charge of King David's property there was also "Jaziz the Hagrite" ([[@13027030-13027031|1 Chr 27:30-31]]).

column5: Father of Johanan
column7: Father of Johanan, of the sons of Azgad, who came up from Babylon with Ezra. With Johanan were one hundred ten men ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008012|Ezra 8:12]]).

column5: Seventh priestly division
column7: The one chosen seventh when the divisions of Aaron's descendants were assigned by lot ([[@13024001|1 Chr 24:1]]; [[@13024010|1 Chr 24:10]]).

column5: Priestly family missing from the records
column7: It was a priestly family that returned from exile, but because they could not find their names in the genealogical records, they could not serve as priests ([[@15002061-15002062|Ezra 2:61-62]]).

column5: Grandfather of Meremoth, who repaired the wall
column7: He was the grandfather of Meremoth, who repaired two sections of the wall of Jerusalem in Nehemiah's time. Meremoth was the son of Uriah ([[@16003004|Neh 3:4]], 21).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Hakupha' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]], 51; [[@16007053|Neh 7:53]]).

column5: A place where Israelite captives were taken
column7: The king of Assyria took Samaria and placed the captured Israelites in Halah, on the Habor, and in other places ([[@12017006|2 Kgs 17:6]]; [[@12018011|2 Kgs 18:11]]). The Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh were also carried away here ([[@13005026|1 Chr 5:26]]).

column5: Southern limit of the land Joshua conquered
column7: Joshua conquered the land from Mount Halak, which goes up to Seir, to the foot of Mount Hermon ([[@6011017|Josh 11:17]]; [[@6012007|Josh 12:7]]).

column5: City in Judah's hill country
column7: One of the hill-country cities the tribe of Judah received; it is listed with Beth Zur and Gedor ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015058|Josh 15:58]]).

column5: City of the tribe of Asher
column7: A city within the border of the land the tribe of Asher received; it is listed with Helkath, Beten, and Achshaph ([[@6019024-6019025|Josh 19:24-25]]).

column5: Pillared hall of Solomon's palace
column7: A hall built with pillars when Solomon built his own palace; it was fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide ([[@11007001|1 Kgs 7:1]]; [[@11007006|1 Kgs 7:6]]).

column5: A shout of praise meaning 'praise the LORD'
column7: Hallelujah is a Hebrew word meaning 'praise the LORD', and it is a shout of praise to God. Several psalms begin with this shout of praise, and Psalm 106 too begins, "Praise the LORD! Give thanks to the LORD" ([[@19106001|Ps 106:1]]). The last psalm ends, "Let everything that has breath praise the LORD! Praise the LORD!" ([[@19150006|Ps 150:6]]). In Revelation a great multitude in heaven praised God, saying, "Hallelujah! Salvation, power, and glory belong to our God", and a voice was also heard saying, "Hallelujah! For the Lord our God, the Almighty, reigns!" ([[@66019001|Rev 19:1]], 6).

column5: Father of Shallum
column7: He was the father of Shallum, the ruler of half the district of Jerusalem, who repaired the wall with his daughters ([[@16003012|Neh 3:12]]). Among those who sealed the covenant there is also a 'Hallohesh' ([[@16010024|Neh 10:24]]).

column5: One of Noah's three sons, father of Canaan
column7: He was one of the three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, whom Noah fathered after he was five hundred years old ([[@1005032|Gen 5:32]]). After the flood, Ham saw his father's nakedness and went out and told his two brothers, and when Noah awoke from his wine he said that Ham's son Canaan would be cursed ([[@1009022-1009025|Gen 9:22-25]]). The sons of Ham were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan, and his descendants became many peoples ([[@1010006|Gen 10:6]]). A psalm speaks of Egypt this way: "Jacob lived in the land of Ham" ([[@19105023|Ps 105:23]]).

column5: Where Chedorlaomer struck the Zuzim
column7: The place where Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him, coming out in the fourteenth year, struck the Zuzim after striking the Rephaim in Ashteroth Karnaim ([[@1014005|Gen 14:5]]).

column5: The Persian official who tried to destroy the Jews
column7: Haman was the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, and King Ahasuerus set him above all the princes ([[@17003001|Esth 3:1]]). When Mordecai would not bow to him, he plotted to destroy all the Jews, Mordecai's people, throughout the king's whole kingdom ([[@17003006|Esth 3:6]]). But Queen Esther exposed his plot before the king, saying, "An adversary and an enemy, even this wicked Haman!" ([[@17007006|Esth 7:6]]). In the end he was hanged on the gallows he had set up for Mordecai ([[@17007010|Esth 7:10]]).

column5: A great Syrian city beyond Israel's northern border
column7: Hamath was a great city and kingdom in Syria, north of Israel. When the Bible describes the northern border of Canaan, the phrase "the entrance of Hamath" often appears ([[@4034008|Num 34:8]]). When David defeated Hadadezer, Toi king of Hamath sent his son Joram to greet and bless David ([[@10008009-10008010|2 Sam 8:9-10]]). Amos called this city "Hamath the great" ([[@30006002|Amos 6:2]]), and later the king of Assyria moved people from Hamath to live in the towns of Samaria ([[@12017024|2 Kgs 17:24]]).

column5: A people descended from Canaan
column7: They were one of the peoples descended from Canaan, the grandson of Noah through Ham. Afterward the families of the Canaanites were spread abroad ([[@1010018|Gen 10:18]]; [[@13001016|1 Chr 1:16]]).

column5: A fortified town of Naphtali
column7: It was one of the fortified cities in the land the tribe of Naphtali received by lot, listed with Ziddim, Zer, and Rakkath ([[@6019032|Josh 19:32]]; [[@6019035|Josh 19:35]]).

column5: Father of the house of Rechab
column7: The families of scribes who lived at Jabez were Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab ([[@13002055|1 Chr 2:55]]).

column5: Father of Haman
column7: He was an Agagite, the father of Haman ([[@17003001|Esth 3:1]]). The king took off his ring and gave it to his son Haman, 'the Jews' enemy' ([[@17003010|Esth 3:10]]).

column5: Title given to Jerahmeel and Malchijah
column7: In Hebrew 'hammelech' means 'the king', and these verses call two men "the king’s son" ([[@24036026|Jer 36:26]]; [[@24038006|Jer 38:6]]). They are Jerahmeel, who was ordered to arrest Baruch and Jeremiah, and Malchijah, the owner of the dungeon Jeremiah was thrown into.

column5: Woman in Manasseh's genealogy
column7: A woman in the genealogy of Manasseh's descendants, called 'his sister'; she bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah ([[@13007017-13007018|1 Chr 7:17-18]]).

column5: Son of Mishma, a Simeonite
column7: Son of Mishma in the genealogy of Simeon's descendants; he was the father of Zaccur and the grandfather of Shimei ([[@13004024-13004026|1 Chr 4:24-26]]).

column5: Valley where Gog's multitude will be buried
column7: Ezekiel prophesied that the valley where Gog and his multitude would be buried would be called 'The valley of Hamon Gog' ([[@26039011|Ezek 39:11]]; [[@26039015|Ezek 39:15]]).

column5: Name of a city in Ezekiel's prophecy
column7: In the prophecy about burying Gog's multitude to cleanse the land, it says, "Hamonah will also be the name of a city" ([[@26039016|Ezek 39:16]]).

column5: Hivite man, father of Shechem
column7: Hamor was a Hivite, the father of Shechem, the prince of the land ([[@1034002|Gen 34:2]]). Jacob bought the field where he had pitched his tent in front of the city of Shechem from the sons of Hamor ([[@1033019|Gen 33:19]]). Later, after Shechem disgraced Jacob's daughter Dinah, Hamor asked for her as a wife for his son, but Simeon and Levi attacked the city and killed Hamor and Shechem ([[@1034025-1034026|Gen 34:25-26]]). The children of Israel buried the bones of Joseph, which they had brought from Egypt, in this land that Jacob had bought from the sons of Hamor ([[@6024032|Josh 24:32]]).

column5: Grandson of Judah, son of Perez
column7: He was a son of Perez, Judah’s son ([[@1046012|Gen 46:12]]). The family of the Hamulites came from him ([[@4026021|Num 26:21]]).

column5: Mother of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah
column7: She was the daughter of Jeremiah of Libnah and the mother of Jehoahaz king of Judah ([[@12023031|2 Kgs 23:31]]). She was also the mother of King Zedekiah ([[@12024018|2 Kgs 24:18]]).

column5: Jeremiah's cousin who sold him a field in Anathoth
column7: He was the son of Shallum, Jeremiah's uncle, and asked Jeremiah to buy his field in Anathoth ([[@24032007-24032008|Jer 32:7-8]]). Jeremiah weighed out seventeen shekels of silver and bought the field ([[@24032009|Jer 32:9]]).

column5: Son of Shashak, a Benjaminite
column7: One of the sons of Shashak in the Benjamite genealogy; he is listed with Abdon and Zichri ([[@13008023-13008025|1 Chr 8:23-25]]).

column5: Descendant of Saul, son of Azel
column7: He was one of the six sons of Azel, a descendant of Saul and Jonathan. His brothers were Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, and Obadiah ([[@13008038|1 Chr 8:38]]; [[@13009044|1 Chr 9:44]]).

column5: One of David's mighty men
column7: Son of Maacah in the list of David's mighty men. His name appears with Joshaphat the Mithnite ([[@13011043|1 Chr 11:43]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Hanan' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]], 46; [[@16007049|Neh 7:49]]).

column5: Levite who helped the people understand the law
column7: When Ezra read the law, he was one of those who helped the people understand it ([[@16008007|Neh 8:7]]). He is also on the list of Levites who sealed the covenant ([[@16010010|Neh 10:10]]).

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: One of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah's time who sealed the covenant to keep God's law ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010022|Neh 10:22]]).

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: One of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah's time who sealed the covenant to keep God's law; he is listed with Ahiah and Anan ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010026|Neh 10:26]]).

column5: Son of Zaccur, in charge of the storehouses
column7: Grandson of Mattaniah and son of Zaccur. Nehemiah, finding him faithful, set him next to the treasurers to distribute to their brothers ([[@16013013|Neh 13:13]]).

column5: Son of Igdaliah, the man of God
column7: Son of Igdaliah, called 'the man of God.' Jeremiah brought the Rechabites into the room of Hanan's sons in the LORD's house ([[@24035004|Jer 35:4]]).

column5: The seer who rebuked King Asa
column7: He was a seer who rebuked Asa king of Judah for relying on the king of Syria, and he was put in prison for it ([[@14016007-14016010|2 Chr 16:7-10]]). He was the father of the prophet Jehu ([[@11016001|1 Kgs 16:1]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a singer
column7: He was a son of Heman, who served as a singer in David's time ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]). The eighteenth lot fell to him, and he served in that turn ([[@13025025|1 Chr 25:25]]).

column5: Son of Immer who married a foreign woman
column7: One of those in Ezra's time who had married foreign women; he was of the sons of Immer ([[@15010018-15010020|Ezra 10:18-20]]).

column5: Brother of Nehemiah
column7: Nehemiah's brother, he came from Judah and told him how things stood in Jerusalem ([[@16001002-16001003|Neh 1:2-3]]). Later Nehemiah put him in charge of Jerusalem ([[@16007002|Neh 7:2]]).

column5: Musician at the wall's dedication
column7: A brother of Zechariah the trumpeter at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall; he played the musical instruments of David the man of God ([[@16012035-16012036|Neh 12:35-36]]).

column5: Son of Zerubbabel
column7: He was a son of Zerubbabel of the house of David. He had a brother, Meshullam, and a sister, Shelomith, and he was the father of Pelatiah and Jeshaiah ([[@13003019|1 Chr 3:19]], 21).

column5: Son of Shashak, a Benjaminite
column7: One of the sons of Shashak in the Benjamite genealogy; he is listed with Elam and Anthothijah ([[@13008024-13008025|1 Chr 8:24-25]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a singer
column7: He was a son of Heman, who served as a singer in David's time ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]). The sixteenth lot fell to him, and he served in that turn ([[@13025023|1 Chr 25:23]]).

column5: Captain of King Uzziah
column7: One of King Uzziah's captains; Uzziah's fighting men were under his hand and went out to war by bands ([[@14026011|2 Chr 26:11]]).

column5: Son of Bebai who married a foreign woman
column7: One of the Israelites in Ezra's time who had married foreign women; he was of the sons of Bebai ([[@15010025|Ezra 10:25]]; [[@15010028|Ezra 10:28]]).

column5: Perfumer who repaired the wall
column7: A perfumer who repaired Jerusalem's wall in Nehemiah's time; the work reached as far as the wide wall ([[@16003008|Neh 3:8]]).

column5: Son of Shelemiah who repaired the wall
column7: Son of Shelemiah, he repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall with Hanun in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003030|Neh 3:30]]).

column5: Fortress governor put in charge of Jerusalem
column7: The governor of the fortress, whom Nehemiah put in charge of Jerusalem along with his brother Hanani. He was faithful and feared God more than most ([[@16007002|Neh 7:2]]).

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: One of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah's time who sealed the covenant to keep God's law ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010023|Neh 10:23]]).

column5: Head of Jeremiah's family in Joiakim's day
column7: One of the heads of priestly families in the days of Joiakim son of Jeshua; he headed the family of Jeremiah ([[@16012010|Neh 12:10]]; [[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]).

column5: Priest with a trumpet at the wall's dedication
column7: A priest who held a trumpet at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall, along with Eliakim, Maaseiah, and others ([[@16012041|Neh 12:41]]).

column5: False prophet who opposed Jeremiah
column7: He was the son of Azzur from Gibeon, a prophet who spoke in the house of the LORD in the fourth year of King Zedekiah ([[@24028001|Jer 28:1]]). He said that within two years the temple vessels and the captives taken to Babylon would be brought back ([[@24028003-24028004|Jer 28:3-4]]). Then he took the yoke off Jeremiah's neck and broke it, but the LORD said that in place of the wooden yoke an iron yoke had been made ([[@24028010|Jer 28:10]], 13). Jeremiah rebuked him, saying, "The LORD has not sent you," and told him he would die that year, and Hananiah died in the seventh month of that same year ([[@24028015-24028017|Jer 28:15-17]]).

column5: Father of Zedekiah, a prince
column7: Father of Zedekiah, one of the princes gathered in the scribe's room in the king's house in Jehoiakim's time ([[@24036009|Jer 36:9]]; [[@24036012|Jer 36:12]]).

column5: Grandfather of Irijah, captain of the guard
column7: Grandfather of Irijah, the captain of the guard who seized Jeremiah. Irijah was the son of Shelemiah and the grandson of Hananiah ([[@24037013|Jer 37:13]]).

column5: Daniel's friend, called Shadrach in Babylon
column7: He was a young man of the children of Judah who was taken to Babylon along with Daniel, and the prince of the eunuchs changed his name to Shadrach ([[@27001007|Dan 1:7]]). When King Nebuchadnezzar was about to kill the wise men because of his dream, Daniel told Hananiah and his friends so they would ask the God of heaven for mercy ([[@27002017-27002018|Dan 2:17-18]]). When he was accused of not bowing to the golden image, he and his friends declared, "But if not, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods" ([[@27003018|Dan 3:18]]). When God delivered them from the fiery furnace, even the king praised their God ([[@27003028|Dan 3:28]]).

column5: Place the envoys reached
column7: In the prophecy rebuking the people who sought refuge in the shadow of Egypt, Isaiah says, "their princes are at Zoan, and their ambassadors have come to Hanes" ([[@23030001-23030004|Isa 30:1-4]]).

column5: Samuel's mother, a woman of prayer
column7: She was one of Elkanah's two wives; the other wife, Peninnah, had children, but Hannah had none ([[@9001002|1 Sam 1:2]]). Hannah prayed and made a vow that if the LORD gave her a son, "then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life," and no razor would touch his head ([[@9001011|1 Sam 1:11]]). God heard her prayer and she gave birth to Samuel, and after the child was weaned she gave him to the LORD as she had promised ([[@9001020-9001028|1 Sam 1:20-28]]). Afterward the LORD visited Hannah, and she bore three more sons and two daughters ([[@9002021|1 Sam 2:21]]).

column5: Place on Zebulun's northern border
column7: A place the border of Zebulun's land reached as it turned around on the north ([[@6019010|Josh 19:10]]; [[@6019014|Josh 19:14]]).

column5: Manasseh prince who helped divide the land
column7: Son of Ephod, he was the prince of the tribe of Manasseh among the princes chosen from each tribe to divide the land of Canaan as an inheritance ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034023|Num 34:23]]).

column5: Son of Ulla, of the tribe of Asher
column7: Son of Ulla in Asher's genealogy; he was a brother of Arah and Rizia ([[@13007039-13007040|1 Chr 7:39-40]]).

column5: Son of Midian
column7: He was one of the five sons of Midian, the son of Abraham and Keturah ([[@1025001-1025002|Gen 25:1-2]], 4; [[@13001033|1 Chr 1:33]]).

column5: A son of Reuben
column7: He was a son of Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, and one of the heads of Reuben's families ([[@1046009|Gen 46:9]]; [[@2006014|Exod 6:14]]). From him came the family of the Hanochites ([[@4026005|Num 26:5]]).

column5: Ammonite king who shamed David's envoys
column7: He was the son of Nahash, king of the Ammonites, and became king after his father died ([[@10010001-10010002|2 Sam 10:1-2]]). To repay the kindness Nahash had shown him, David sent his servants to comfort Hanun ([[@10010002|2 Sam 10:2]]). But Hanun listened to his princes and treated them as spies sent to search out the city, so he shaved off half their beards, cut their garments off at the buttocks, and sent them away ([[@10010003-10010004|2 Sam 10:3-4]]). After that the Ammonites hired the Syrians to fight, but they fled before Abishai and went into the city ([[@10010006|2 Sam 10:6]], 14).

column5: Man who repaired the valley gate
column7: With the inhabitants of Zanoah he repaired the valley gate and set up its doors, and repaired a thousand cubits of the wall as far as the dung gate ([[@16003013|Neh 3:13]]).

column5: Sixth son of Zalaph, who repaired the wall
column7: The sixth son of Zalaph, he repaired a section of the wall with Hananiah son of Shelemiah in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003030|Neh 3:30]]).

column5: Eighteenth priestly division
column7: The one chosen eighteenth when the divisions of Aaron's descendants were assigned by lot ([[@13024001|1 Chr 24:1]]; [[@13024015|1 Chr 24:15]]).

column5: Place where Assyria took captives
column7: One of the places to which Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria carried away the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh ([[@13005026|1 Chr 5:26]]).

column5: A campsite in the wilderness
column7: It was where Israel camped after leaving Mount Shepher ([[@4033024|Num 33:24]]). From Haradah they set out and camped at Makheloth ([[@4033025|Num 33:25]]).

column5: Son of Terah, father of Lot
column7: He was a son of Terah and a brother of Abram and Nahor, and he became the father of Lot ([[@1011027|Gen 11:27]]). He died in Ur of the Chaldees before his father Terah, and he was the father of Milcah and Iscah ([[@1011028-1011029|Gen 11:28-29]]).

column5: Mesopotamian city where Abram and Jacob stayed
column7: Haran was a city in Mesopotamia. Terah left Ur of the Chaldees with his son Abram, his grandson Lot, and Sarai to go to Canaan, but when they reached Haran they settled there, and he died there ([[@1011031-1011032|Gen 11:31-32]]). Following the LORD's word, Abram left Haran for Canaan at the age of seventy-five ([[@1012004|Gen 12:4]]). Later Jacob fled from his brother Esau to Haran, where his uncle Laban lived, and stayed there a long time ([[@1027043|Gen 27:43]]; [[@1028010|Gen 28:10]]). Scholars differ on the meaning of the name.

column5: Son of Shimei, a Gershonite
column7: Son of Shimei of the Gershonite family of Levi; he was a brother of Shelomoth and Haziel ([[@13023007|1 Chr 23:7]]; [[@13023009|1 Chr 23:9]]).

column5: A family that produced some of David’s mighty men
column7: Shammah, one of David’s mighty men, was the son of Agee the Hararite ([[@10023011|2 Sam 23:11]]). Ahiam the son of Sacar the Hararite was also one of David’s mighty men ([[@13011035|1 Chr 11:35]]).

column5: Eunuch of King Ahasuerus
column7: He was one of the seven eunuchs who served in the presence of King Ahasuerus ([[@17001010|Esth 1:10]]). He told the king about the gallows Haman had set up for Mordecai, and Haman was hanged on it ([[@17007009-17007010|Esth 7:9-10]]).

column5: Father of Beth Gader
column7: A son of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah, among Caleb's descendants, and the father of Beth Gader. He is listed with Salma the father of Bethlehem ([[@13002050-13002051|1 Chr 2:50-51]]).

column5: Father of Uzziel
column7: Father of Uzziel, who repaired the wall in Nehemiah's time. The text introduces his son as "Uzziel the son of Harhaiah, goldsmiths" ([[@16003008|Neh 3:8]]).

column5: Grandfather of Shallum, Huldah's husband
column7: He was the grandfather of Shallum, the husband of Huldah the prophetess ([[@12022014|2 Kgs 22:14]]). In 2 Chronicles he appears as 'Hasrah' ([[@14034022|2 Chr 34:22]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Harhur' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]], 51; [[@16007053|Neh 7:53]]).

column5: The name of a priestly division
column7: It was the third of the priestly divisions chosen by lot in David's time ([[@13024008|1 Chr 24:8]]). Among those who returned from exile, the descendants of Harim numbered one thousand seventeen ([[@15002039|Ezra 2:39]]).

column5: Family that returned from exile
column7: It was one of the families that returned from exile in Babylon with Zerubbabel, and 'the children of Harim' numbered 320 ([[@15002032|Ezra 2:32]]; [[@16007035|Neh 7:35]]).

column5: Father of Malchijah, who repaired the wall
column7: Father of Malchijah, who repaired a section of the wall and the tower of the furnaces with Hasshub son of Pahathmoab in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003011|Neh 3:11]]).

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: One of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah's time who sealed the covenant to keep God's law ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010027|Neh 10:27]]).

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: One of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah's time who sealed the covenant to keep God's law ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010019|Neh 10:19]]).

column5: Place they would be cast into, in Amos
column7: Amos prophesied that those like the cows of Bashan in Samaria would go out through the breaks in the wall and cast themselves into Harmon ([[@30004001-30004003|Amos 4:1-3]]).

column5: Son of Zophah, of the tribe of Asher
column7: Son of Zophah in Asher's genealogy; he was a brother of Suah, Shual, Beri, and Imrah ([[@13007036|1 Chr 7:36]]).

column5: Spring where Gideon camped
column7: Gideon and the people with him camped beside the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian was to the north of them ([[@7007001|Judg 7:1]]).

column5: Descendant of Shobal
column7: He was from the family of Caleb, a descendant of Judah. Haroeh appears as a descendant of Shobal, the father of Kiriath Jearim ([[@13002050|1 Chr 2:50]], 52).

column5: Where Sisera lived
column7: It was where Sisera, the commander of the army of Jabin king of Canaan, lived ([[@7004002|Judg 4:2]]). Barak pursued Sisera’s army as far as Harosheth of the Gentiles and struck them all with the sword ([[@7004016|Judg 4:16]]).

column5: A stringed instrument played by hand
column7: The harp was an instrument played by plucking it with the hand. The Bible first introduces Jubal, a descendant of Cain, as "the father of all who handle the harp and pipe" ([[@1004021|Gen 4:21]]). When the evil spirit came on Saul, David played the harp, and then Saul was refreshed and was well ([[@9016023|1 Sam 16:23]]). The Psalms call us to give thanks to the LORD and sing praises with the harp ([[@19033002|Ps 33:2]]). The people taken captive to Babylon wept as they remembered Zion and hung up their harps on the willows ([[@19137001-19137002|Ps 137:1-2]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Harsha' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]], 52; [[@16007054|Neh 7:54]]).

column5: Father of Aharhel
column7: A man in Judah's genealogy, the father of Aharhel. Hakkoz is said to have become the father of Anub, Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel son of Harum ([[@13004008|1 Chr 4:8]]).

column5: Father of Jedaiah, who repaired the wall
column7: Father of Jedaiah, who repaired the wall across from his own house in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003010|Neh 3:10]]).

column5: Origin of Shephatiah, who came to David
column7: Among the warriors who came and helped David in battle while he was at Ziklag was 'Shephatiah the Haruphite' ([[@13012001|1 Chr 12:1]]; [[@13012005|1 Chr 12:5]]).

column5: Maternal grandfather of King Amon
column7: A man of Jotbah, the father of Meshullemeth, the mother of King Amon son of King Manasseh ([[@12021018-12021019|2 Kgs 21:18-19]]).

column5: Member of Zerubbabel's family
column7: One of five men listed with Zerubbabel's children in the genealogy of the descendants of Jeconiah the captive ([[@13003017|1 Chr 3:17]]; [[@13003019-13003020|1 Chr 3:19-20]]).

column5: Merarite Levite, son of Amaziah
column7: A Levite of the sons of Merari, the son of Amaziah and the father of Malluch. He is listed among the ancestors of Ethan, who was in charge of singing ([[@13006044-13006045|1 Chr 6:44-45]]).

column5: Levite descended from Merari
column7: He was the great-grandfather of Shemaiah, a Levite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile, and a descendant of Merari ([[@13009014|1 Chr 9:14]]; [[@16011015|Neh 11:15]]).

column5: Son of Jeduthun, a singer
column7: A son of Jeduthun, he played the harp under his father and gave praise ([[@13025003|1 Chr 25:3]]). The twelfth lot fell to him, and he served in that turn ([[@13025019|1 Chr 25:19]]).

column5: Leader of the Hebronites in David's day
column7: One of the Hebronites; with his brothers, one thousand seven hundred men of valor, he had the oversight of Israel west of the Jordan, for all the business of the LORD and the service of the king ([[@13026030|1 Chr 26:30]]).

column5: Ruler over the Levites in David's day
column7: Son of Kemuel; in David's time he was the ruler over the Levites among those in charge of Israel's tribes ([[@13027016-13027017|1 Chr 27:16-17]]).

column5: Chief of the Levites in Josiah's day
column7: One of the chiefs of the Levites in King Josiah's time. With the other chiefs he gave the Levites five thousand sheep and five hundred cattle for the Passover offerings ([[@14035009|2 Chr 35:9]]).

column5: A man who returned with Ezra
column7: He was brought along with Jeshaiah of the sons of Merari when Ezra was looking for Levites by the river Ahava ([[@15008018-15008019|Ezra 8:18-19]]). His name also appears among the twelve chiefs of the priests whom Ezra set apart ([[@15008024|Ezra 8:24]]).

column5: Ruler of half of Keilah who repaired the wall
column7: Ruler of half the district of Keilah; in Nehemiah's time he repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall for his district ([[@16003017|Neh 3:17]]).

column5: Grandfather of Uzzi, overseer of the Levites
column7: A descendant of Asaph and grandfather of Uzzi, who became overseer of the Levites living in Jerusalem. Uzzi was the son of Bani, and Bani was the son of Hashabiah ([[@16011022|Neh 11:22]]).

column5: Head of Hilkiah's family in Joiakim's day
column7: One of the heads of priestly families in the days of Joiakim; he headed the family of Hilkiah ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012021|Neh 12:21]]).

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: One of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah's time who sealed the covenant to keep God's law ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010025|Neh 10:25]]).

column5: Father of Hattush, who repaired the wall
column7: Father of Hattush, who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall next to Jedaiah son of Harumaph in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003010|Neh 3:10]]).

column5: Levite who called the people to bless God
column7: A Levite who, with Jeshua, Kadmiel, and others, said to the people, "Stand up and bless the LORD your God from everlasting to everlasting!" ([[@16009005|Neh 9:5]]).

column5: Man who stood beside Ezra at the reading
column7: One of those who stood on the left of Ezra the scribe as he stood on the wooden pulpit and read the book of the law ([[@16008003-16008004|Neh 8:3-4]]).

column5: A campsite in the wilderness
column7: It was where Israel camped after leaving Mithkah. From Hashmonah they set out and camped at Moseroth ([[@4033029-4033030|Num 33:29-30]]).

column5: Descendant of David in Zerubbabel's family
column7: A man in the genealogy of David's royal line, recorded after Zerubbabel's children as one of five, along with Ohel, Berechiah, and others ([[@13003019-13003020|1 Chr 3:19-20]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family that returned from exile
column7: The descendants of Hashum who came back from exile in Babylon numbered 223, though Nehemiah records 328 ([[@15002019|Ezra 2:19]]; [[@16007022|Neh 7:22]]).

column5: Man who stood beside Ezra at the reading
column7: One of those who stood on the left of Ezra the scribe as he stood on the wooden pulpit and read the book of the law ([[@16008003-16008004|Neh 8:3-4]]).

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: One of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah's time who sealed the covenant to keep God's law ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010018|Neh 10:18]]).

column5: Levite descended from Merari
column7: He was the father of Shemaiah, a Levite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile, and a descendant of Merari ([[@13009014|1 Chr 9:14]]; [[@16011015|Neh 11:15]]).

column5: Son of Pahathmoab who repaired the wall
column7: Son of Pahathmoab, he repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall and the tower of the furnaces with Malchijah son of Harim in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003011|Neh 3:11]]).

column5: Man who repaired the wall across from his house
column7: In Nehemiah's time he repaired, with Benjamin, the section of Jerusalem's wall across from their house ([[@16003023|Neh 3:23]]).

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: One of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah's time who sealed the covenant to keep God's law ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010023|Neh 10:23]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Hasupha' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]]; [[@16007046|Neh 7:46]]).

column5: A palace eunuch who attended Esther
column7: He was a eunuch the king had appointed to attend Esther. At Esther's command he went to Mordecai to find out what was happening and brought back his words ([[@17004005-17004006|Esth 4:5-6]]; [[@17004009|Esth 4:9]]).

column5: Son of Othniel, of the tribe of Judah
column7: A man in Judah's genealogy, the son of Othniel son of Kenaz ([[@13004013|1 Chr 4:13]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of temple servants
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile were 'the children of Hatipha' ([[@15002054|Ezra 2:54]]; [[@16007056|Neh 7:56]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of returning gatekeepers
column7: Among the gatekeepers who came back from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Hatita' ([[@15002042|Ezra 2:42]]; [[@16007045|Neh 7:45]]).

column5: A family among the descendants of Solomon’s servants
column7: Among the descendants of Solomon’s servants who came back from exile were 'the children of Hattil' ([[@15002055-15002057|Ezra 2:55-57]]). They also appear in Nehemiah’s list ([[@16007059|Neh 7:59]]).

column5: Son of Shemaiah, of David's royal line
column7: A man in the genealogy of David's royal line, one of the six sons of Shemaiah son of Shecaniah ([[@13003022|1 Chr 3:22]]).

column5: Descendant of David who returned with Ezra
column7: In the list of those who came up from Babylon with Ezra, he appears as the representative of the sons of David ([[@15008001-15008002|Ezra 8:1-2]]).

column5: Son of Hashabneiah who repaired the wall
column7: Son of Hashabneiah, he repaired the section of Jerusalem's wall next to Jedaiah son of Harumaph in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003010|Neh 3:10]]).

column5: A priest who sealed the covenant
column7: His name is among those who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s day ([[@16010004|Neh 10:4]]). Hattush also appears in the list of priests who came back with Zerubbabel and Jeshua ([[@16012001-16012002|Neh 12:1-2]]).

column5: A region on Israel’s northeast border in Ezekiel
column7: It is a place on the border of the land of Israel that Ezekiel saw. The northern border ran to Hazer Hatticon by the border of Hauran, and the eastern border was the Jordan, between Hauran, Damascus, Gilead, and the land of Israel ([[@26047016|Ezek 47:16]]; [[@26047018|Ezek 47:18]]).

column5: Land encircled by the Pishon from Eden
column7: The land the Pishon flowed around, the first of the four rivers that flowed out of Eden. The Bible says the gold of that land is good, and bdellium and onyx stone are also there ([[@1002011-1002012|Gen 2:11-12]]).

column5: Grandson of Ham, son of Cush
column7: He was one of the sons of Cush, Ham’s son, a brother of Seba, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca ([[@1010007|Gen 10:7]]; [[@13001009|1 Chr 1:9]]).

column5: A descendant of Shem, son of Joktan
column7: He was one of the sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem, and a brother of Ophir and Jobab ([[@1010029|Gen 10:29]]; [[@13001023|1 Chr 1:23]]).

column5: A land where Ishmael’s descendants lived
column7: The descendants of Ishmael lived from Havilah to Shur, which is before Egypt ([[@1025018|Gen 25:18]]). Saul struck the Amalekites from Havilah as far as Shur ([[@9015007|1 Sam 15:7]]).

column5: The villages won by Jair son of Manasseh
column7: Jair the son of Manasseh took the villages of Gilead and called them Havvoth Jair ([[@4032041|Num 32:41]]; [[@5003014|Deut 3:14]]). The towns in Gilead held by the judge Jair were also called by this name ([[@7010003-7010004|Judg 10:3-4]]).

column5: Man who followed Ben Hadad as king of Syria
column7: He was an officer of Ben Hadad king of Syria. God told Elijah to anoint Hazael to be king over Syria ([[@11019015|1 Kgs 19:15]]). When the sick Ben Hadad sent him to Elisha, Elisha wept, foreseeing the evil Hazael would do to the children of Israel ([[@12008012|2 Kgs 8:12]]). The next day Hazael covered the king's face with a cloth dipped in water so that he died, and he became king in his place ([[@12008015|2 Kgs 8:15]]), and after that he oppressed Israel for a long time ([[@12013022|2 Kgs 13:22]]).

column5: Ancestor of Maaseiah, who lived in Jerusalem
column7: Great-grandfather of Maaseiah, a man of Judah who lived in Jerusalem. Maaseiah was the son of Baruch and the grandson of Colhozeh ([[@16011004-16011005|Neh 11:4-5]]).

column5: Place on Canaan's southern border
column7: A place on the southern border of the land of Canaan that Israel was to receive; the border passed south of Kadesh Barnea, went to Hazar Addar, and on to Azmon ([[@4034004|Num 34:4]]).

column5: A place on Israel's northern border
column7: It was the point reached by the northern border of Israel that the LORD laid out ([[@4034009-4034010|Num 34:9-10]]). In Ezekiel it appears as 'Hazar Enon' ([[@26047017|Ezek 47:17]]).

column5: City in the south of Judah
column7: One of the southern cities the tribe of Judah received; it is listed with Heshmon and Beth Pelet ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015027|Josh 15:27]]).

column5: A town in southern Judah where Simeon lived
column7: It was one of the southern towns of the tribe of Judah, and the children of Simeon also lived there ([[@6015028|Josh 15:28]]; [[@13004028|1 Chr 4:28]]).

column5: City given to the tribe of Simeon
column7: One of the cities the tribe of Simeon received by lot within the inheritance of Judah's descendants; it is listed with Ziklag and Beth Marcaboth ([[@6019001|Josh 19:1]]; [[@6019005|Josh 19:5]]).

column5: City where the Simeonites lived
column7: One of the cities where the Simeonites lived. These cities belonged to them until King David's reign ([[@13004028|1 Chr 4:28]]; [[@13004031|1 Chr 4:31]]).

column5: A descendant of Shem, son of Joktan
column7: He was one of the sons of Joktan, Eber’s son, a descendant of Shem ([[@1010025-1010026|Gen 10:25-26]]; [[@13001020|1 Chr 1:20]]).

column5: Place on Israel's border in Ezekiel's vision
column7: A place on the border of the land of Israel in Ezekiel's vision; it is said to be by the border of Hauran ([[@26047016|Ezek 47:16]]).

column5: Villages of the Avvim, as far as Gaza
column7: The Caphtorim, who came out of Caphtor, destroyed the Avvim who lived in villages as far as Gaza and lived in their place ([[@5002023|Deut 2:23]]).

column5: A place where Israel stayed in the wilderness
column7: It was where the people of Israel stayed after leaving Kibroth Hattaavah ([[@4011035|Num 11:35]]). From there they set out and camped in the wilderness of Paran ([[@4012016|Num 12:16]]).

column5: Son of Shimei, a Gershonite
column7: A Gershonite descendant of Levi, one of the three sons of Shimei. They were heads of the fathers' households of Ladan ([[@13023007|1 Chr 23:7]]; [[@13023009|1 Chr 23:9]]).

column5: Son of Nahor, Abraham's brother
column7: One of the eight sons Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother ([[@1022022-1022023|Gen 22:22-23]]).

column5: Great city in northern Canaan
column7: It was a great city in northern Canaan. Jabin king of Hazor gathered many kings to fight Israel, but Joshua took Hazor, which "used to be the head of all those kingdoms", killed its king, and burned the city ([[@6011001-6011011|Josh 11:1-11]]). In the time of the judges, Jabin, a Canaanite king who reigned in Hazor, had nine hundred chariots of iron and cruelly oppressed the children of Israel for twenty years ([[@7004002-7004003|Judg 4:2-3]]). Later Solomon raised forced labor to build Hazor ([[@11009015|1 Kgs 9:15]]). In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria took Hazor and carried its people captive to Assyria ([[@12015029|2 Kgs 15:29]]).

column5: City in the south of Judah
column7: One of the southern cities of the tribe of Judah toward the border of Edom; it is listed with Kedesh and Ithnan ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015023|Josh 15:23]]).

column5: Southern Judean town also called Kerioth Hezron
column7: A place in the list of Judah's southern cities; the text says "Kerioth Hezron (also called Hazor)" ([[@6015025|Josh 15:25]]).

column5: City where Benjaminites lived in Nehemiah's day
column7: One of the cities where the Benjaminites lived in Nehemiah's time; it is listed with Ramah and Gittaim ([[@16011031|Neh 11:31]]; [[@16011033|Neh 11:33]]).

column5: Kingdoms attacked by Nebuchadnezzar
column7: It appears in the word about Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon struck ([[@24049028|Jer 49:28]]). Hazor was told it would become a home for jackals, desolate forever ([[@24049033|Jer 49:33]]).

column5: City in the south of Judah
column7: One of the southern cities the tribe of Judah received. It is listed with Kerioth Hezron ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015025|Josh 15:25]]).

column5: Woman in Judah's genealogy
column7: A woman in Judah's genealogy, the sister of Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash, the sons of the father of Etam ([[@13004003|1 Chr 4:3]]).

column5: Grandson of Asher, son of Beriah
column7: He was a son of Beriah, the son of Asher ([[@1046017|Gen 46:17]]). From him came the family of the Heberites ([[@4026045|Num 26:45]]).

column5: A Kenite, husband of Jael
column7: He was a Kenite descended from Hobab, Moses’ brother-in-law, who separated from his people and pitched his tent near Kedesh ([[@7004011|Judg 4:11]]). His wife Jael killed Sisera ([[@7004021|Judg 4:21]]).

column5: Father of Soco in Judah's genealogy
column7: A man in Judah's genealogy. The text says, "His wife the Jewess bore Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Soco," and the father of Zanoah ([[@13004018|1 Chr 4:18]]).

column5: Son of Elpaal, a Benjaminite
column7: A man in the Benjamite genealogy, one of the sons of Elpaal ([[@13008017-13008018|1 Chr 8:17-18]]).

column5: An old name for the people of Israel
column7: Hebrews is an old name for the people of Israel. The Bible first uses it when it calls Abram "Abram, the Hebrew" ([[@1014013|Gen 14:13]]). It was mostly used when other nations spoke of the Israelites, or when Israelites introduced themselves to other nations ([[@32001009|Jonah 1:9]]). The apostle Paul also called himself "a Hebrew of Hebrews" ([[@50003005|Phil 3:5]]). In the early church, Jewish believers who spoke Hebrew were called 'the Hebrews' to distinguish them from the Greek-speaking Jews ([[@44006001|Acts 6:1]]).

column5: Ancient Judean hill town where the patriarchs were buried
column7: Hebron is a very old town in the hill country of Judah, and its old name was Kiriath Arba. Abram moved his tent to the oaks of Mamre here and built an altar to the LORD ([[@1013018|Gen 13:18]]). Abraham buried his wife Sarah here in the cave of the field of Machpelah ([[@1023019|Gen 23:19]]). Joshua gave this town to Caleb as his inheritance ([[@6014013|Josh 14:13]]). After Saul died, David was anointed in Hebron and became king of Judah ([[@10002004|2 Sam 2:4]]).

column5: Son of Kohath, grandson of Levi
