column7: He was one of the four sons of Kohath, the son of Levi ([[@2006018|Exod 6:18]]). His descendants were called 'the family of the Hebronites' and formed one branch of the Kohathite family ([[@4003027|Num 3:27]]). When David gathered the Levites to bring up the ark of the LORD, among the sons of Hebron were Eliel the chief and eighty of his brothers ([[@13015003-13015009|1 Chr 15:3-9]]). In David's time Hashabiah and seventeen hundred of his relatives, mighty men of the Hebronites, were in charge west of the Jordan for the work of the LORD and the service of the king ([[@13026030|1 Chr 26:30]]).

column5: A descendant of Judah, son of Mareshah
column7: In the genealogy of Caleb, the brother of Jerahmeel, he appears as the son of Mareshah ([[@13002042|1 Chr 2:42]]). His sons were Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema ([[@13002043|1 Chr 2:43]]).

column5: Where Jacob sent Joseph to his brothers
column7: The place from which Jacob sent Joseph to see whether it was well with his brothers and the flock. From there Joseph went to Shechem ([[@1037014|Gen 37:14]]).

column5: The eunuch in charge of King Ahasuerus’s women
column7: He was the eunuch in charge of the women in King Ahasuerus’s day. The young women gathered in Susa were put in his care, and when Esther went in to the king, she asked for nothing but what Hegai advised ([[@17002008|Esth 2:8]]; [[@17002015|Esth 2:15]]).

column5: Wife of Ashhur, father of Tekoa
column7: She was one of the two wives of Ashhur the father of Tekoa ([[@13004005|1 Chr 4:5]]). Her sons were Zereth, Izhar, and Ethnan ([[@13004007|1 Chr 4:7]]).

column5: Where David defeated the Syrian army
column7: It was where the Syrians from beyond the River, whom Hadadezer brought out, gathered. David gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, came to Helam, and fought them there ([[@10010016-10010017|2 Sam 10:16-17]]).

column5: City Asher did not drive out
column7: One of the cities whose inhabitants the tribe of Asher did not drive out. So the Asherites lived among the Canaanites of the land ([[@7001031-7001032|Judg 1:31-32]]).

column5: Place known for fine wine
column7: A place in Ezekiel's lament over Tyre; Damascus traded with Tyre in the wine of Helbon and white wool ([[@26027018|Ezek 27:18]]).

column5: A man who returned from Babylon
column7: He was one of those who came back from Babylon, and Zechariah was told to take silver and gold from them and make crowns ([[@38006010-38006011|Zech 6:10-11]]). In verse 14 he is called 'Helem' ([[@38006014|Zech 6:14]]).

column5: A Netophathite, one of David’s mighty men
column7: He was the son of Baanah the Netophathite and one of David’s mighty men ([[@10023029|2 Sam 23:29]]). In 1 Chronicles he is called 'Heled' ([[@13011030|1 Chr 11:30]]).

column5: Army guarding the walls of Tyre
column7: A word in the lament over Tyre, which says, "The men of Arvad with your army were on your walls all around" ([[@26027011|Ezek 27:11]]).

column5: A descendant of Manasseh, son of Gilead
column7: He was a descendant of Gilead, Manasseh’s grandson, and the family of the Helekites came from him ([[@4026030|Num 26:30]]). When the land of Canaan was divided, the children of Helek also received an inheritance by lot ([[@6017002|Josh 17:2]]).

column5: Place on Naphtali's border
column7: The place where the border of the land Naphtali's descendants received began; it is listed with the oak in Zaanannim ([[@6019032-6019033|Josh 19:32-33]]).

column5: A Paltite, one of David’s mighty men
column7: He was a Paltite and one of David’s mighty men ([[@10023026|2 Sam 23:26]]). As one of the children of Ephraim, he became captain for the seventh month, with twenty-four thousand in his division ([[@13027010|1 Chr 27:10]]).

column5: Man above Joseph in Luke's genealogy
column7: The man recorded above Joseph in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke. The text says Jesus was "the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli" ([[@42003023|Luke 3:23]]).

column5: Head of Meraioth's family in Joiakim's day
column7: One of the heads of priestly families in the days of Joiakim; he headed the family of Meraioth ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012015|Neh 12:15]]).

column5: A Levite city in the tribe of Asher
column7: It was a town within the border of the land the tribe of Asher received ([[@6019024-6019025|Josh 19:24-25]]). It was also one of the cities from the tribe of Asher given to the Levites ([[@6021030-6021031|Josh 21:30-31]]).

column5: Where young men fell together at Gibeon
column7: The place by the pool of Gibeon where twelve young men on Abner's side and twelve on Joab's side thrust their swords into one another and fell down together. So that place was called Helkath Hazzurim ([[@10002013-10002016|2 Sam 2:13-16]]).

column5: The place of eternal punishment for the judged
column7: Hell is the place of punishment where those who come under God's judgment go. Jesus called hell "the unquenchable fire", and he solemnly warned that if your hand causes you to sin, it is better to cut it off ([[@41009043|Mark 9:43]]). He also taught that we should not fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul; rather, "fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna" ([[@40010028|Matt 10:28]]). He said that whoever calls his brother a fool will be in danger of the fire of hell, and he rebuked the hypocritical scribes and Pharisees, asking how they would escape the judgment of hell ([[@40005022|Matt 5:22]]; [[@40023033|Matt 23:33]]).

column5: Father of Eliab, leader of the tribe of Zebulun
column7: He was the father of Eliab, the leader of the children of Zebulun in the wilderness ([[@4001009|Num 1:9]]). His son brought the offering on behalf of the children of Zebulun on the third day ([[@4007024|Num 7:24]]).

column5: A descendant of Seir the Horite, son of Lotan
column7: He was one of the children of Lotan, Seir’s son ([[@1036022|Gen 36:22]]). In 1 Chronicles he is called 'Homam' ([[@13001039|1 Chr 1:39]]).

column5: A wise man compared with Solomon
column7: He was one of the men Solomon’s wisdom was compared with, a son of Mahol. Solomon is said to have been wiser than Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Darda ([[@11004031|1 Kgs 4:31]]).

column5: Son of Zerah, son of Judah
column7: One of the five sons of Zerah son of Judah. His brothers were Zimri, Ethan, Calcol, and Dara ([[@13002006|1 Chr 2:6]]).

column5: A Levite in charge of praise in David's day
column7: He was a Levite of the Kohathites, the son of Joel and grandson of Samuel ([[@13006033|1 Chr 6:33]]). In David's time he was appointed as a singer along with Asaph and Ethan, and he sounded the bronze cymbals aloud ([[@13015017-13015019|1 Chr 15:17-19]]). The Bible calls him "the king’s seer in the words of God" and says that God gave Heman fourteen sons and three daughters ([[@13025005|1 Chr 25:5]]). In Solomon's time, when the ark of the covenant was brought into the temple, he stood with Asaph and Jeduthun, dressed in fine linen and holding instruments ([[@14005012|2 Chr 5:12]]).

column5: A Horite, son of Dishon
column7: He was one of the children of Dishon the Horite ([[@1036026|Gen 36:26]]). In 1 Chronicles he is called 'Hamran' ([[@13001041|1 Chr 1:41]]).

column5: A city conquered by Assyria
column7: It was one of the places the Assyrian king’s officer named, saying their gods had not saved their cities ([[@12018033-12018034|2 Kgs 18:33-34]]). The king of Assyria asked Hezekiah where the king of Hena was ([[@12019013|2 Kgs 19:13]]).

column5: Ancestor of a Levite family that oversaw temple work
column7: After the return from exile, the sons of Henadad, along with other Levites, oversaw the work on God’s house ([[@15003009|Ezra 3:9]]). Binnui, of the sons of Henadad, sealed the covenant ([[@16010009|Neh 10:9]]).

column5: Father of Bavvai, who repaired the wall
column7: Father of Bavvai, who ruled half the district of Keilah and repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003018|Neh 3:18]]).

column5: Father of Binnui, who repaired the wall
column7: Father of Binnui, who repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall from the house of Azariah to the corner in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003024|Neh 3:24]]).

column5: Father of Zelophehad
column7: He was a son of Gilead, a descendant of Manasseh, and from him came the family of the Hepherites ([[@4026030-4026032|Num 26:30-32]]). He was the father of Zelophehad, who had only five daughters ([[@4026033|Num 26:33]]; [[@4027001|Num 27:1]]).

column5: A Canaanite city whose king Joshua struck
column7: Among the Canaanite kings Joshua struck and destroyed was the king of Hepher ([[@6012017|Josh 12:17]]). In Solomon’s day, Ben Hesed was in charge of Socoh and all the land of Hepher ([[@11004010|1 Kgs 4:10]]).

column5: Son of Ashhur, the father of Tekoa
column7: A man in Judah's genealogy, a son born to Ashhur the father of Tekoa and his wife Naarah ([[@13004005-13004006|1 Chr 4:5-6]]).

column5: One of David's mighty men, a Mecherathite
column7: A Mecherathite listed among the mighty men of David's armies ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011036|1 Chr 11:36]]).

column5: Mother of King Manasseh of Judah
column7: The mother of Manasseh king of Judah. Manasseh became king at twelve and reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem ([[@12021001|2 Kgs 21:1]]).

column5: Ascent Gideon returned from
column7: The name that appears when Gideon, who had captured Zebah and Zalmunna, the two kings of Midian, "returned from the battle from the ascent of Heres" ([[@7008012-7008013|Judg 8:12-13]]).

column5: Levite who lived in Jerusalem
column7: A man in the list of Levites, named with Bakbakkar, Galal, and Mattaniah. They lived in Jerusalem ([[@13009014-13009015|1 Chr 9:14-15]]; [[@13009034|1 Chr 9:34]]).

column5: Forest in Judah where David hid
column7: The forest David came to after the prophet Gad told him not to stay in the stronghold but to go into the land of Judah ([[@9022005|1 Sam 22:5]]).

column5: Man of Asia who turned away from Paul
column7: A man Paul named along with Phygelus when he said that all who were in Asia had turned away from him ([[@55001015|2 Tim 1:15]]).

column5: High mountain on Israel's northern border
column7: It is a high mountain at the northern end of the land east of the Jordan. Israel took land from the two kings of the Amorites "from the valley of the Arnon to Mount Hermon" ([[@5003008|Deut 3:8]]). The Sidonians called this mountain Sirion, and the Amorites called it Senir ([[@5003009|Deut 3:9]]). Hivites lived below it ([[@6011003|Josh 11:3]]). A psalm compares the goodness of brothers living together in unity to "the dew of Hermon" ([[@19133003|Ps 133:3]]).

column5: King of Judea when Jesus was born
column7: He was the king who ruled when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea ([[@40002001|Matt 2:1]]). When the wise men from the east came looking for the one born King of the Jews, King Herod and all Jerusalem were troubled, and Herod secretly called the wise men and asked them exactly when the star had appeared ([[@40002003-40002007|Matt 2:3-7]]). An angel of the Lord told Joseph that Herod would seek the child to kill him, so Joseph took the child and his mother by night and left for Egypt ([[@40002013-40002014|Matt 2:13-14]]). When Herod saw that the wise men had tricked him, he was furious and killed all the boys two years old and under in Bethlehem and all its surrounding area ([[@40002016|Matt 2:16]]).

column5: Tetrarch of Galilee in Jesus' time
column7: He was Herod the tetrarch, who ruled Galilee during Jesus' ministry ([[@40014001|Matt 14:1]]). When John rebuked him for marrying Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, Herod put John in prison and later sent men to behead him ([[@40014003-40014010|Matt 14:3-10]]). Jesus called him "that fox" ([[@42013032|Luke 13:32]]). During Jesus' trial Pilate sent Jesus to him, and Herod and his soldiers treated Jesus with contempt and mocked him before sending him back to Pilate ([[@42023007-42023011|Luke 23:7-11]]).

column5: King who killed James and imprisoned Peter
column7: He is the King Herod of Acts 12, usually identified as Herod Agrippa I. To harm some members of the church, he killed James the brother of John with the sword, and when he saw that this pleased the Jews, he arrested Peter too and put him in prison ([[@44012001-44012004|Acts 12:1-4]]). But an angel of the Lord led Peter out of the prison, and Herod questioned the guards and ordered them put to death ([[@44012007-44012010|Acts 12:7-10]], 19). Later, when he put on his royal robes and gave a speech to the people, they shouted, "The voice of a god, and not of a man!" and because he did not give the glory to God, an angel of the Lord struck him and he was eaten by worms and died ([[@44012021-44012023|Acts 12:21-23]]).

column5: A Jewish group that supported Herod's family
column7: The Herodians were a group of Jews who supported the rule of Herod's family and thought it right to submit to Rome. When Jesus healed a man with a withered hand on the Sabbath, the Pharisees immediately plotted with the Herodians about how to destroy Jesus ([[@41003005-41003006|Mark 3:5-6]]). Later the Pharisees sent their disciples along with the Herodians to ask, "Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?" ([[@40022016-40022017|Matt 22:16-17]]). Jesus knew their wickedness and answered that they should give to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's ([[@40022018-40022021|Matt 22:18-21]]).

column5: Herod's wife who brought about John the Baptist's death
column7: She was the wife of Herod the tetrarch, and she had first been the wife of Herod's brother Philip. When Herod married her, John the Baptist rebuked him, saying, "It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife", and Herod put John in prison. Herodias held a grudge against John and wanted to kill him ([[@41006017-41006019|Mark 6:17-19]]). At Herod's birthday feast her daughter danced, and the king swore to give her whatever she asked, and Herodias told her daughter, "The head of John the Baptizer" ([[@41006021-41006024|Mark 6:21-24]]). In the end John was beheaded in the prison ([[@40014010-40014011|Matt 14:10-11]]).

column5: Paul's relative in Rome
column7: A man Paul named in his letter to the church in Rome: "Greet Herodion, my kinsman" ([[@45016011|Rom 16:11]]).

column5: One of Solomon's twelve officers
column7: One of the twelve officers Solomon set to provide food for the royal household. He was in charge of Arubboth and over Socoh and all the land of Hepher ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004010|1 Kgs 4:10]]).

column5: The royal city of Sihon, king of the Amorites
column7: Heshbon was a town east of the Jordan River and the royal city of Sihon, king of the Amorites ([[@4021026|Num 21:26]]). Israel defeated Sihon and took Heshbon and its villages ([[@4021025|Num 21:25]]). After that the children of Reuben rebuilt the town ([[@4032037|Num 32:37]]), and it became one of the towns given to the Levites ([[@6021039|Josh 21:39]]). Later it became a town of Moab and also appears in Isaiah's prophecies.

column5: City in the south of Judah
column7: One of the southern cities the tribe of Judah received; it is listed with Hazar Gaddah and Beth Pelet ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015027|Josh 15:27]]).

column5: Son of Canaan, ancestor of the Hittites
column7: He was a son of Canaan and the ancestor of the Hittites ([[@1010015|Gen 10:15]]). In Abraham's time his descendants, the Hittites, lived near Hebron. To bury Sarah, Abraham paid Ephron the Hittite four hundred shekels of silver for a field and its cave ([[@1023016|Gen 23:16]]). When Esau married Hittite women, it brought grief to Isaac and Rebekah ([[@1026034-1026035|Gen 26:34-35]]). Uriah, one of David's warriors, was also a Hittite ([[@10011003|2 Sam 11:3]]).

column5: A road on the northern border in Ezekiel
column7: It is a place on the northern border of the land of Israel that Ezekiel saw. The border ran from the great sea by the way of Hethlon to the entrance of Zedad ([[@26047015|Ezek 47:15]]; [[@26048001|Ezek 48:1]]).

column5: A king of Judah who trusted in God
column7: He was the son of Ahaz and became king of Judah ([[@12016020|2 Kgs 16:20]]). He removed the high places and broke in pieces the bronze serpent Moses had made, and Scripture says "He trusted in the LORD, the God of Israel" so that no king of Judah before or after him was like him ([[@12018004-12018005|2 Kgs 18:4-5]]). When the king of Assyria threatened Jerusalem, he prayed to the LORD ([[@12019015|2 Kgs 19:15]]). When he became sick and was about to die, he prayed again and was given fifteen more years of life ([[@12020005-12020006|2 Kgs 20:5-6]]).

column5: Ancestor of the children of Ater who returned
column7: Among those who came back from Babylon were ninety-eight of 'the children of Ater, of Hezekiah' ([[@15002016|Ezra 2:16]]; [[@16007021|Neh 7:21]]). He is a different person from Hezekiah king of Judah.

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: One of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah's time who sealed the covenant to keep God's law; he is listed with Ater and Azzur ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010017|Neh 10:17]]).

column5: Ancestor of the prophet Zephaniah
column7: The prophet Zephaniah is recorded as his great-great-grandson. Zephaniah was the son of Cushi, the grandson of Gedaliah, and the great-grandson of Amariah ([[@36001001|Zeph 1:1]]).

column5: Grandfather of Ben Hadad, king of Syria
column7: Grandfather of Ben Hadad king of Syria and father of Tabrimmon. Asa king of Judah sent silver and gold to Ben Hadad, who lived at Damascus ([[@11015018|1 Kgs 15:18]]).

column5: Seventeenth priestly division in David's day
column7: The one chosen seventeenth when the priestly divisions were assigned by lot in David's time ([[@13024005|1 Chr 24:5]]; [[@13024015|1 Chr 24:15]]).

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: One of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah's time who sealed the covenant to keep God's law ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010020|Neh 10:20]]).

column5: A Carmelite, one of David’s mighty men
column7: He was one of David’s mighty men, a Carmelite ([[@10023035|2 Sam 23:35]]). He also appears in the list in 1 Chronicles ([[@13011037|1 Chr 11:37]]).

column5: A son of Reuben
column7: He was a son of Reuben, Jacob's firstborn, and one of the heads of Reuben's families ([[@1046009|Gen 46:9]]; [[@2006014|Exod 6:14]]). From him came the family of the Hezronites ([[@4026006|Num 26:6]]).

column5: Son of Perez, ancestor of David
column7: He was one of the two sons of Perez son of Judah, and his name is on the list of Jacob's family when they went down to Egypt ([[@1046008-1046012|Gen 46:8-12]]). His descendants were called 'the family of the Hezronites' and formed one branch of the tribe of Judah ([[@4026021|Num 26:21]]). The genealogy in Ruth goes on, "Hezron became the father of Ram", and from this line David was at last born ([[@8004019-8004022|Ruth 4:19-22]]). His name also appears in Jesus' genealogy in Matthew ([[@40001003|Matt 1:3]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men, from the brooks of Gaash
column7: He was one of David’s mighty men and lived by the brooks of Gaash ([[@10023030|2 Sam 23:30]]). In 1 Chronicles he is called 'Hurai' ([[@13011032|1 Chr 11:32]]).

column5: Bethelite who rebuilt Jericho
column7: A Bethelite who rebuilt Jericho; he laid its foundation at the cost of his firstborn Abiram and set up its gates at the cost of his youngest son Segub. It happened according to the LORD's word spoken by Joshua ([[@11016034|1 Kgs 16:34]]).

column5: Home of believers Epaphras labored for
column7: A place mentioned in the letter to the church in Colossae. Paul testified that Epaphras, who came from among the Colossians, had great zeal for them and for those in Laodicea and Hierapolis ([[@51004012-51004013|Col 4:12-13]]).

column5: The chief of the priests
column7: The high priest was the chief among the priests, and Aaron was the first to hold this office. He was anointed with the anointing oil and wore holy garments, and on the pure gold plate on the front of his turban were engraved the words "HOLY TO THE LORD" ([[@3021010|Lev 21:10]]; [[@2028036|Exod 28:36]]). Only the high priest went into the Most Holy Place, once a year, with blood, to make atonement for his own sins and the errors of the people ([[@58009007|Heb 9:7]]). Hebrews calls Jesus "a great high priest" who has passed through the heavens ([[@58004014|Heb 4:14]]).

column5: Father of Eliakim, palace official under Hezekiah
column7: He was the father of Eliakim, who was in charge of the palace under King Hezekiah. When the Assyrian Rabshakeh came to threaten Jerusalem, "Eliakim the son of Hilkiah, who was over the household" went out to meet him with Shebnah the scribe and Joah the recorder ([[@12018017-12018018|2 Kgs 18:17-18]]). Through Isaiah, God said he would call "my servant Eliakim the son of Hilkiah" and put the government into his hand ([[@23022020-23022021|Isa 22:20-21]]). The Bible says nothing more about Hilkiah himself.

column5: High priest who found the book of the law
column7: He was the high priest in the time of King Josiah. While the temple was being repaired, he said, "I have found the book of the law in the LORD’s house" and gave the book to Shaphan the scribe ([[@12022008|2 Kgs 22:8]]). At the king's command he went to the prophetess Huldah to ask what the LORD wanted ([[@12022014|2 Kgs 22:14]]), and he brought out of the temple the vessels made for Baal and the Asherah, and they were burned ([[@12023004|2 Kgs 23:4]]). Ezra the scribe was his descendant ([[@15007001|Ezra 7:1]]).

column5: Merarite Levite, father of Amaziah
column7: A Levite of the sons of Merari and the father of Amaziah. He is listed among the ancestors of Ethan, who was in charge of singing ([[@13006044-13006045|1 Chr 6:44-45]]).

column5: Second son of Hosah, a gatekeeper
column7: The second son of Hosah, of the sons of Merari, and one of the chiefs of the divisions of gatekeepers who served in the LORD's house in David's time ([[@13026010-13026012|1 Chr 26:10-12]]).

column5: Man who stood beside Ezra at the reading
column7: One of those who stood on the right of Ezra the scribe as he stood on the wooden pulpit and read the book of the law ([[@16008003-16008004|Neh 8:3-4]]).

column5: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jeshua ([[@16012007|Neh 12:7]]). In the days of Joiakim, the head of Hilkiah’s family was Hashabiah ([[@16012021|Neh 12:21]]).

column5: Father of the prophet Jeremiah
column7: One of the priests at Anathoth in the land of Benjamin and the father of the prophet Jeremiah. The book of Jeremiah begins, "The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah" ([[@24001001|Jer 1:1]]).

column5: Father of the judge Abdon
column7: He was a Pirathonite, the father of Abdon, who judged Israel. His son Abdon was buried in Pirathon when he died ([[@7012013|Judg 12:13]]; [[@7012015|Judg 12:15]]).

column5: Judah’s friend, an Adullamite
column7: He was the Adullamite whom Judah visited after leaving his brothers ([[@1038001|Gen 38:1]]). Later Judah went up to his sheep shearers at Timnah with his friend Hirah ([[@1038012|Gen 38:12]]).

column5: King of Tyre who helped David and Solomon
column7: He was king of the coastal city of Tyre. He sent David cedar trees, carpenters, and masons to help build his palace ([[@10005011|2 Sam 5:11]]). In Solomon's time he also sent cedar and cypress timber for the temple and the palace, and the two of them made a treaty together ([[@11005010-11005012|1 Kgs 5:10-12]]). When Solomon gave him twenty towns in the land of Galilee, he was not pleased and called them "the land of Cabul" ([[@11009011-11009013|1 Kgs 9:11-13]]). In 2 Chronicles he is also called Huram ([[@14002003|2 Chr 2:3]]), and he is a different person from Hiram the craftsman who made the bronze furnishings for the temple.

column5: The craftsman from Tyre who made Solomon's temple furnishings
column7: He was a craftsman King Solomon brought from Tyre, the son of a widow of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre ([[@11007013-11007014|1 Kgs 7:13-14]]). He made all the vessels of the LORD's house out of bright bronze ([[@11007045|1 Kgs 7:45]]).

column5: People who lived in the land of Canaan
column7: The Hivites were a people listed among the descendants of Canaan ([[@1010017|Gen 10:17]]). Shechem and his father Hamor, who appear in the story of Dinah, were Hivites ([[@1034002|Gen 34:2]]). In Joshua's time the people of Gibeon were also Hivites, and they pretended to have come from far away so they could make a treaty with Israel ([[@6009007|Josh 9:7]]). They also lived below Mount Hermon ([[@6011003|Josh 11:3]]), and since they were not all driven out, they remained in the land until Solomon's time.

column5: Son of Elpaal, a Benjaminite
column7: A man in the Benjamite genealogy, one of the sons of Elpaal ([[@13008017-13008018|1 Chr 8:17-18]]).

column5: Son of Neariah, of David's royal line
column7: A man in the genealogy of David's royal line, one of the three sons of Neariah. His brothers were Elioenai and Azrikam ([[@13003023|1 Chr 3:23]]).

column5: A Midianite of Moses’ in-laws
column7: He was the son of Reuel the Midianite, and Moses asked him to come along with them ([[@4010029|Num 10:29]]). Judges calls him Moses’ brother-in-law and says Heber the Kenite was one of his descendants ([[@7004011|Judg 4:11]]).

column5: Place near Damascus where Abram pursued the enemy
column7: The place to which Abram pursued the band that had taken his nephew Lot captive, after striking them by night; it lay on the left hand of Damascus ([[@1014014-1014015|Gen 14:14-15]]).

column5: Son of Zophah, a descendant of Asher
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Asher’s descendants as one of the sons of Zophah ([[@13007036-13007037|1 Chr 7:36-37]]).

column5: Son of Elioenai, of David’s royal line
column7: He appears in the genealogy of David’s royal line as one of the seven sons of Elioenai ([[@13003024|1 Chr 3:24]]).

column5: A family head of the half-tribe of Manasseh
column7: He was one of the family heads of the half-tribe of Manasseh, who spread out from Bashan to Mount Hermon, and he was a famous man of valor ([[@13005023-13005024|1 Chr 5:23-24]]).

column5: Ancestor of Sallu, a Benjamite in Jerusalem
column7: He was the grandfather of Sallu, one of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem. Sallu was the son of Meshullam ([[@13009003|1 Chr 9:3]]; [[@13009007|1 Chr 9:7]]).

column5: A Levite family that returned from exile
column7: Among the Levites who came back from exile in Babylon were seventy-four of the children of Hodaviah, that is, of Jeshua and Kadmiel ([[@15002040|Ezra 2:40]]). In Nehemiah the name is given as 'Hodevah' ([[@16007043|Neh 7:43]]).

column5: Wife of Shaharaim the Benjamite
column7: She was the wife of Shaharaim, a descendant of Benjamin, and in the land of Moab she bore Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam, and others ([[@13008008-13008009|1 Chr 8:8-9]]).

column5: A name in the genealogy of Judah
column7: This is a name in the genealogy of Judah’s descendants. The text says that "The sons of the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham" were the fathers of Keilah and Eshtemoa ([[@13004019|1 Chr 4:19]]).

column5: A Levite who helped the people understand the law
column7: He was one of the Levites who helped the people understand the law when Ezra read it ([[@16008007|Neh 8:7]]). His name also appears among the Levites who sealed the covenant ([[@16010010|Neh 10:10]]).

column5: A Levite who sealed the covenant under Nehemiah
column7: He was one of the Levites in Nehemiah’s time who set their seal on the covenant to keep God’s law ([[@16010009|Neh 10:9]]; [[@16010013|Neh 10:13]]).

column5: A leader who sealed the covenant under Nehemiah
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah’s time who set their seal on the covenant to keep God’s law ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010018|Neh 10:18]]).

column5: A daughter of Zelophehad
column7: She was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh ([[@4026033|Num 26:33]]). With her sisters she came to Moses to ask for her father's inheritance ([[@4027001|Num 27:1]]).

column5: King of Hebron who fought Joshua
column7: He was king of Hebron, who was summoned by Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem and went up with the other Amorite kings to attack Gibeon, which had made peace with Israel ([[@6010003-6010005|Josh 10:3-5]]).

column5: A Levite city in the hill country of Judah
column7: It was one of the towns in the hill country of Judah ([[@6015048-6015051|Josh 15:48-51]]). It was also a city given to the children of Aaron, and in 1 Chronicles it is called 'Hilen' ([[@6021013-6021015|Josh 21:13-15]]; [[@13006058|1 Chr 6:58]]).

column5: A town in Jeremiah’s prophecy against Moab
column7: This town appears in Jeremiah’s message about Moab as one of the towns of the plain on which judgment came ([[@24048001|Jer 48:1]]; [[@24048021|Jer 48:21]]).

column5: The holy room before the Most Holy Place
column7: The Holy Place is the front room of the tabernacle, separated from the Most Holy Place by a veil. God commanded that the veil be hung, saying, "The veil shall separate the holy place from the most holy for you" ([[@2026033|Exod 26:33]]). In the Holy Place stood the lampstand and the table for the show bread ([[@58009002|Heb 9:2]]), and the priests went into this first tabernacle continually to serve ([[@58009006|Heb 9:6]]). Solomon's temple was laid out the same way. Elsewhere in the Bible, 'the holy place' or 'the sanctuary' can also mean the whole tabernacle or temple.

column5: Son of Eli, a wicked priest
column7: He was one of Eli's two sons and a priest of the LORD at Shiloh ([[@9001003|1 Sam 1:3]]). He died along with Phinehas on the day the ark of God was captured ([[@9004011|1 Sam 4:11]]).

column5: Pharaoh of Egypt in Zedekiah's time
column7: He was the king of Egypt in the time of Zedekiah king of Judah, and his name appears once in the Bible, as "Pharaoh Hophra king of Egypt" ([[@24044030|Jer 44:30]]). When the Babylonian army was besieging Jerusalem, Pharaoh's army came out of Egypt and the Chaldeans withdrew for a while ([[@24037005|Jer 37:5]]). Jeremiah prophesied that this army would soon go back to its own land, Egypt ([[@24037007|Jer 37:7]]). The Pharaoh of this time is usually taken to be Hophra, and God said he would give him into the hand of his enemies just as he had given Zedekiah to Nebuchadnezzar.

column5: A place where Israel camped in the wilderness
column7: It was one of the places where the people of Israel camped as they passed through the wilderness. They came from Bene Jaakan and camped here, then went on to Jotbathah ([[@4033032-4033033|Num 33:32-33]]).

column5: The mountain on Edom's border where Aaron died
column7: It was the mountain that the whole congregation of Israel reached after leaving Kadesh on their journey through the wilderness, and it lay on the border of the land of Edom ([[@4020022-4020023|Num 20:22-23]]). At the LORD's command Moses took off Aaron's garments and put them on his son Eleazar, and the Bible says, "Aaron died there on the top of the mountain" ([[@4020028|Num 20:28]]). It was the first day of the fifth month in the fortieth year after the children of Israel came out of Egypt, and Aaron was one hundred twenty-three years old ([[@4033038-4033039|Num 33:38-39]]). The whole congregation mourned for Aaron thirty days ([[@4020029|Num 20:29]]).

column5: King of Gezer who came to help Lachish
column7: He was king of Gezer, who came up to help Lachish and was defeated by Joshua. Joshua struck him and his people until no one was left ([[@6010033|Josh 10:33]]).

column5: A fortified city of the tribe of Naphtali
column7: It was one of the cities the descendants of Naphtali received by lot, listed with Migdal El and Beth Anath ([[@6019032|Josh 19:32]]; [[@6019038|Josh 19:38]]).

column5: The wood in the wilderness of Ziph where David hid
column7: It was the wood in the wilderness of Ziph where David stayed while fleeing from Saul ([[@9023015|1 Sam 23:15]]). Jonathan came to David there and strengthened him to rely on God ([[@9023016|1 Sam 23:16]]).

column5: A people who lived in Seir before Esau's descendants
column7: They were a people who lived in the hill country of Seir before the descendants of Esau came in. In Abraham's time the kings allied with Chedorlaomer struck "the Horites in their Mount Seir" ([[@1014006|Gen 14:6]]). Genesis calls them "the inhabitants of the land" and lists the names of chiefs who were the sons of Seir, such as Lotan, Shobal, and Zibeon ([[@1036020-1036030|Gen 36:20-30]]). Later the descendants of Esau destroyed the Horites and lived in their land in their place ([[@5002012|Deut 2:12]]; [[@5002022|Deut 2:22]]).

column5: Father of Shaphat, the spy from Simeon
column7: He was the father of Shaphat, who represented the tribe of Simeon among the twelve men Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013002|Num 13:2]]; [[@4013005|Num 13:5]]).

column5: A town Israel destroyed and named
column7: It was a town in the south of Canaan. After the spies returned, Israel disobeyed the LORD's word and went up to the top of the mountain, but they were beaten by the Amalekites and the Canaanites and driven back as far as Hormah ([[@4014040-4014045|Num 14:40-45]]). Later, when the king of Arad attacked Israel, Israel made a vow to the LORD and utterly destroyed those cities, and they named the place Hormah ([[@4021001-4021003|Num 21:1-3]]). Judges says that Judah, together with his brother Simeon, utterly destroyed the Canaanites of Zephath and named the city Hormah ([[@7001017|Judg 1:17]]). Hormah became one of the towns the tribe of Simeon received within Judah's inheritance ([[@6019001-6019004|Josh 19:1-4]]).

column5: A town of Moab
column7: It was a town of Moab, and Isaiah said a cry of destruction would be raised on the way to Horonaim ([[@23015005|Isa 15:5]]). Jeremiah also said, "The sound of a cry from Horonaim" ([[@24048003|Jer 48:3]]).

column5: A name used for Sanballat
column7: This word describes Sanballat, who was displeased with Nehemiah’s work ([[@16002010|Neh 2:10]]). Sanballat the Horonite, together with Tobiah and Geshem, mocked the building of the wall ([[@16002019|Neh 2:19]]).

column5: A gate in the wall of Jerusalem
column7: It was one of the gates of the city of Jerusalem. In Nehemiah’s day, above the horse gate, the priests repaired the wall, each one across from his own house ([[@16003028|Neh 3:28]]). Jeremiah said the land as far as "the corner of the horse gate toward the east" would be holy to the LORD ([[@24031040|Jer 31:40]]).

column5: A place on the border of Asher
column7: It was a place the border of Asher’s land passed through; the border turned from Tyre to Hosah and ended at the sea by the region of Achzib ([[@6019029|Josh 19:29]]).

column5: A gatekeeper of the sons of Merari
column7: He was a descendant of Merari who was appointed a gatekeeper in David's time ([[@13016038|1 Chr 16:38]]). His sons and brothers numbered thirteen ([[@13026010-13026011|1 Chr 26:10-11]]).

column5: A shout of praise meaning 'save us now'
column7: Hosanna means 'save us now', and it became a joyful shout of praise. The Psalms too have the prayer "Save us now, we beg you, LORD!" along with a song that he who comes in the LORD's name is blessed ([[@19118025-19118026|Ps 118:25-26]]). When Jesus entered Jerusalem, the crowds shouted, "Hosanna to the son of David!" ([[@40021009|Matt 21:9]]). People went out to meet him carrying palm branches, and in the temple the children also shouted the same words ([[@43012013|John 12:13]]; [[@40021015|Matt 21:15]]).

column5: A prophet who spoke to northern Israel
column7: He was the son of Beeri, a prophet who received the LORD’s word in the days of Uzziah through Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and of Jeroboam, king of Israel ([[@28001001|Hos 1:1]]). Paul quoted from Hosea’s writings ([[@45009025|Rom 9:25]]).

column5: He followed the procession at the wall’s dedication
column7: When the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated in Nehemiah’s time and the thanksgiving choirs marched on top of the wall, he followed behind them with half of the princes of Judah ([[@16012031-16012032|Neh 12:31-32]]).

column5: Father of Jezaniah and Azariah
column7: He was the father of Jezaniah, a captain of the forces in Jeremiah’s day ([[@24042001|Jer 42:1]]). Azariah, who called Jeremiah’s words false, was also 'the son of Hoshaiah' ([[@24043002|Jer 43:2]]).

column5: Son of Jeconiah the captive
column7: He appears in the genealogy of David’s royal line as one of the sons of Jeconiah, who was taken captive ([[@13003017-13003018|1 Chr 3:17-18]]).

column5: The last king of northern Israel
column7: He was the son of Elah, and he attacked and killed Pekah the son of Remaliah and reigned in his place ([[@12015030|2 Kgs 15:30]]). He reigned nine years in Samaria and did evil in the LORD's sight, though not like the kings before him ([[@12017001-12017002|2 Kgs 17:1-2]]). He paid tribute to Shalmaneser king of Assyria, but when he sent messengers to So king of Egypt and stopped paying tribute, the king of Assyria put him in prison ([[@12017003-12017004|2 Kgs 17:3-4]]). In the ninth year of Hoshea, Samaria fell and the people of Israel were carried away captive to Assyria ([[@12017006|2 Kgs 17:6]]).

column5: Officer over Ephraim in David’s time
column7: The son of Azaziah, he was the officer over the descendants of Ephraim among those who ruled the tribes of Israel in David’s time ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027020|1 Chr 27:20]]).

column5: A leader who sealed the covenant under Nehemiah
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah’s time who set their seal on the covenant to keep God’s law ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010023|Neh 10:23]]).

column5: A descendant of Asher, son of Heber
column7: He was one of the sons of Heber, Asher’s grandson, a brother of Japhlet and Shomer, and his sister was Shua ([[@13007031-13007032|1 Chr 7:31-32]]).

column5: Father of Shama and Jeiel, David’s mighty men
column7: An Aroerite, he was the father of Shama and Jeiel, who appear in the list of David’s mighty men ([[@13011044|1 Chr 11:44]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a temple singer
column7: He was one of the sons of Heman, who served in song in David’s day ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]). When lots were cast, the twenty-first lot fell to him, and he served with his sons and brothers, twelve in all ([[@13025028|1 Chr 25:28]]).

column5: Great palace Solomon built of cedar
column7: It was a palace Solomon built from the wood of Lebanon, one hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high. Cedar pillars stood in four rows, with cedar beams laid on top of them ([[@11007002-11007003|1 Kgs 7:2-3]]). Solomon kept three hundred small shields made of beaten gold in this palace, and all the vessels of this palace were of pure gold ([[@11010017|1 Kgs 10:17]], 21). Some think that "the armor in the house of the forest" that Isaiah mentions also refers to this palace, but scholars differ ([[@23022008|Isa 22:8]]).

column5: A giant of Gath with six fingers and six toes
column7: He was a man of great stature who appeared when there was war at Gath, with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four in all, and he was born to the giant ([[@10021020|2 Sam 21:20]]). Jonathan the son of Shimei, David’s brother, killed him ([[@10021021|2 Sam 21:21]]).

column5: A place on the border of Naphtali
column7: It was a place the border of Naphtali’s land passed through; the border went out from Aznoth Tabor and reached Hukkok ([[@6019034|Josh 19:34]]).

column5: Grandson of Shem, son of Aram
column7: He was one of the sons of Aram, Shem’s son, a brother of Uz, Gether, and Mash ([[@1010022-1010023|Gen 10:22-23]]; [[@13001017|1 Chr 1:17]]).

column5: A prophetess in King Josiah’s time
column7: She was a prophetess who lived in the second quarter of Jerusalem in King Josiah’s day, the wife of Shallum, the keeper of the wardrobe. Hilkiah the priest and others went to her to ask about the book of the law ([[@12022014|2 Kgs 22:14]]; [[@14034022|2 Chr 34:22]]).

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: It was one of the hill-country towns the tribe of Judah received, listed with Kiriath Arba, that is, Hebron ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015054|Josh 15:54]]).

column5: Priest of the thirteenth division in David’s time
column7: When the priests’ divisions were assigned by lot in David’s time, he was the one chosen thirteenth ([[@13024005|1 Chr 24:5]]; [[@13024013|1 Chr 24:13]]).

column5: Son of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the list of Benjamin’s sons when Jacob’s family went down to Egypt ([[@1046021|Gen 46:21]]). Some think he is the same as Hupham, from whom the family of the Huphamites came in Numbers ([[@4026039|Num 26:39]]).

column5: Brother of Shuppim and of Maacah
column7: In the genealogy of 1 Chronicles, Shuppim and Huppim are listed as 'the sons of Ir' ([[@13007012|1 Chr 7:12]]). Machir the son of Manasseh married Maacah, the sister of Huppim and Shuppim ([[@13007015|1 Chr 7:15]]).

column5: Moses' helper, grandfather of Bezalel
column7: He went up to the top of the hill with Moses and Aaron when Israel fought Amalek at Rephidim ([[@2017008-2017010|Exod 17:8-10]]). When Moses' hands grew tired, Aaron and Hur held up his hands, one on one side and one on the other, so that they did not come down until sunset ([[@2017012|Exod 17:12]]). When Moses went up the mountain of God, Hur stayed with Aaron beside the elders so that anyone with a dispute could come to them ([[@2024013-2024014|Exod 24:13-14]]). Bezalel, who built the tabernacle, was "the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah" ([[@2031002|Exod 31:2]]).

column5: A king of Midian killed by Israel
column7: He was one of the five kings of Midian whom Israel killed ([[@4031008|Num 31:8]]). In Joshua, Hur is listed among 'the chiefs of Midian' ([[@6013021|Josh 13:21]]).

column5: Solomon’s officer over the hill country of Ephraim
column7: He was one of the twelve officers Solomon appointed to provide food for the royal household, and he was in charge of the hill country of Ephraim ([[@11004007-11004008|1 Kgs 4:7-8]]).

column5: Father of Rephaiah, who repaired the wall
column7: He was the father of Rephaiah, who ruled half the district of Jerusalem in Nehemiah’s time and repaired a section of the wall ([[@16003009|Neh 3:9]]).

column5: Father of Abihail, a descendant of Gad
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Gad’s descendants as the father of Abihail and the son of Jaroah ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005014|1 Chr 5:14]]).

column5: Husband of Hammolecheth, father of Ishhod
column7: The Bible does not give the name of Hammolecheth’s husband. The genealogy of Manasseh’s descendants only says that his wife Hammolecheth bore Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah ([[@13007018|1 Chr 7:18]]).

column5: Father of John called Mark
column7: The Bible does not give the name of the father of John who was called Mark. After Peter was freed from prison, he went to the house of Mary, John’s mother, where many people were gathered and praying ([[@44012012|Acts 12:12]]).

column5: Father of Mehetabel, queen of Edom
column7: The Bible does not give this man’s name. Mehetabel, the wife of Hadar king of Edom, is described as "the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab" ([[@1036039|Gen 36:39]]).

column5: Father of Jozacar, who killed Joash
column7: The Bible does not give this man’s name. Jozacar, the son of his wife Shimeath, was one of the servants who struck down Joash king of Judah ([[@12012020-12012021|2 Kgs 12:20-21]]).

column5: Father of Joab and Abishai
column7: The Bible does not give the name of Zeruiah’s husband. Zeruiah’s sons were three brothers: Abishai, Joab, and Asahel ([[@13002016|1 Chr 2:16]]; [[@9026006|1 Sam 26:6]]).

column5: A name in Judah’s genealogy, with Ezer as its father
column7: This name appears in the genealogy of Judah’s descendants, and the text calls Ezer "the father of Hushah." They were descendants of Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah ([[@13004004|1 Chr 4:4]]).

column5: David's friend who defeated Absalom's counsel
column7: An Archite, he was David's friend and was called 'the king's friend' ([[@13027033|1 Chr 27:33]]). When Absalom rebelled and David fled, Hushai came out to meet David with his clothes torn and earth on his head ([[@10015032|2 Sam 15:32]]). David sent him back to the city to stay near Absalom and defeat the counsel of Ahithophel ([[@10015034|2 Sam 15:34]]). When Hushai gave advice different from Ahithophel's, Absalom and all Israel said, "The counsel of Hushai the Archite is better than the counsel of Ahithophel", and followed it, because the LORD meant to bring evil on Absalom ([[@10017014|2 Sam 17:14]]).

column5: A king of Edom from the land of the Temanites
column7: He was from the land of the Temanites and became king of Edom after Jobab ([[@1036034|Gen 36:34]]; [[@13001045|1 Chr 1:45]]).

column5: The clan of some of David's mighty men
column7: Sibbecai and Mebunnai, among David's mighty men, were Hushathites ([[@10021018|2 Sam 21:18]]; [[@10023027|2 Sam 23:27]]). Sibbecai was the commander of the division for the eighth month ([[@13027011|1 Chr 27:11]]).

column5: Son of Dan
column7: He appears as Dan’s son when Jacob’s family went down to Egypt ([[@1046023|Gen 46:23]]). Some think he is the same as Shuham, from whom came the family of the Shuhamites among the sons of Dan in Numbers ([[@4026042|Num 26:42]]).

column5: Named with the sons of Aher in Benjamin’s line
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants, and the text mentions him only in the words "Hushim, and the sons of Aher" ([[@13007012|1 Chr 7:12]]).

column5: Wife of Shaharaim, a Benjamite
column7: She was the wife of Shaharaim, a descendant of Benjamin, and Shaharaim sent away Hushim and Baara ([[@13008008|1 Chr 8:8]]). By Hushim, Shaharaim became the father of Abitub and Elpaal ([[@13008011|1 Chr 8:11]]).

column5: A man who shipwrecked his faith
column7: He was a man Paul mentioned to Timothy, whom Paul delivered to Satan along with Alexander ([[@54001020|1 Tim 1:20]]). Together with Philetus, he spread error about the truth ([[@55002017-55002018|2 Tim 2:17-18]]).

column5: Small plant used in cleansing rites
column7: Hyssop was a small plant used in cleansing rites to dip into blood or water and sprinkle it. At the first Passover the Israelites dipped a bunch of hyssop in the blood in the basin and struck the lintel and both doorposts with it ([[@2012022|Exod 12:22]]). Hyssop was also used, together with cedar wood and scarlet, to cleanse someone healed of leprosy ([[@3014004-3014006|Lev 14:4-6]]). In his repentance David prayed, "Purify me with hyssop" ([[@19051007|Ps 51:7]]). Scholars differ on exactly which plant it was.

column5: A son of David born in Jerusalem
column7: He was one of the sons born to David in Jerusalem ([[@10005013-10005015|2 Sam 5:13-15]]). He also appears in the lists of David’s sons in 1 Chronicles ([[@13003006|1 Chr 3:6]]; [[@13014005|1 Chr 14:5]]).

column5: Town of Manasseh in Issachar's territory
column7: It was a town of the tribe of Manasseh within the land of Issachar and Asher ([[@6017011|Josh 17:11]]). But the people of Manasseh did not drive out the inhabitants of Ibleam, and the Canaanites kept living in that land ([[@7001027|Judg 1:27]]). Later Jehu chased Ahaziah king of Judah and struck him at the ascent of Gur near Ibleam, and Ahaziah fled to Megiddo and died there ([[@12009027|2 Kgs 9:27]]). Some take 'Bileam,' which was given to the descendants of Kohath in Chronicles, to be the same place ([[@13006070|1 Chr 6:70]]).

column5: Son of Jeroham, a Benjamite in Jerusalem
column7: The son of Jeroham, he was one of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem. He is listed with Elah the son of Uzzi, the grandson of Michri ([[@13009003|1 Chr 9:3]]; [[@13009008|1 Chr 9:8]]).

column5: Ancestor of Meshullam, a Benjamite in Jerusalem
column7: He was the great-grandfather of Meshullam, one of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem. Meshullam was the son of Shephatiah and the grandson of Reuel ([[@13009008|1 Chr 9:8]]).

column5: Son of Jaaziah, a descendant of Merari
column7: He was a Levite descended from Merari, one of the sons born to Jaaziah. These too cast lots in the presence of King David ([[@13024026-13024027|1 Chr 24:26-27]]; [[@13024031|1 Chr 24:31]]).

column5: Son of Tola, a descendant of Issachar
column7: He was a son of Tola the son of Issachar, one of the heads of Tola’s family and among the mighty men of valor in their generations ([[@13007001-13007002|1 Chr 7:1-2]]).

column5: A judge of Israel from Bethlehem
column7: He was a man of Bethlehem who judged Israel after Jephthah ([[@7012008|Judg 12:8]]). When he died, he was buried at Bethlehem ([[@7012010|Judg 12:10]]).

column5: Son of Phinehas, born the day the ark was taken
column7: He was the son born to Phinehas’ wife on the day God’s ark was taken and her father-in-law and husband died. His mother named him Ichabod, saying, "The glory has departed from Israel!" ([[@9004021|1 Sam 4:21]]).

column5: City where Paul preached and was persecuted
column7: It is the city Paul and Barnabas went to after they were driven out of Antioch and shook the dust off their feet ([[@44013050-44013051|Acts 13:50-51]]). When the two apostles spoke in the Jewish synagogue, a great number of Jews and Greeks believed, but when a crowd tried to stone them, they fled to Lystra and Derbe in Lycaonia ([[@44014001|Acts 14:1]], 5-6). After that, Jews who came from Antioch and Iconium stirred up the crowds in Lystra, and they stoned Paul ([[@44014019|Acts 14:19]]). Paul reminded Timothy of the persecution he suffered in Iconium and said the Lord had delivered him out of them all ([[@55003011|2 Tim 3:11]]).

column5: A town of the tribe of Zebulun
column7: It was one of the twelve towns the descendants of Zebulun received by lot, listed with Shimron and Bethlehem ([[@6019010|Josh 19:10]]; [[@6019015|Josh 19:15]]).

column5: Descendant of the father of Etam, in Judah’s genealogy
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah’s descendants and, with Jezreel and Ishma, is called a son of the father of Etam ([[@13004003|1 Chr 4:3]]).

column5: Father of Ahinadab, Solomon’s officer
column7: He was the father of Ahinadab, who was in charge of Mahanaim, one of the twelve officers Solomon appointed to provide food for the royal household ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004014|1 Kgs 4:14]]).

column5: A Levite descended from Gershom
column7: In the genealogy of Gershom, Levi’s son, he appears as the son of Joah, and his son was Zerah ([[@13006020-13006021|1 Chr 6:20-21]]).

column5: Officer over half of Manasseh in Gilead under David
column7: The son of Zechariah, he was the officer over the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead in David’s time ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027021|1 Chr 27:21]]).

column5: A seer in the days of Solomon and Rehoboam
column7: He was a seer, and the acts of Solomon were recorded in his visions concerning Jeroboam the son of Nebat ([[@14009029|2 Chr 9:29]]). The acts of Rehoboam and Abijah were also recorded in his writings ([[@14012015|2 Chr 12:15]]; [[@14013022|2 Chr 13:22]]).

column5: Grandfather of the prophet Zechariah
column7: He was the grandfather of the prophet Zechariah and the father of Berechiah ([[@38001001|Zech 1:1]]). The book of Ezra calls Zechariah 'the son of Iddo' ([[@15005001|Ezra 5:1]]).

column5: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the priests who came back with Zerubbabel and Jeshua ([[@16012004|Neh 12:4]]). In the days of Joiakim, the head of Iddo’s family was Zechariah ([[@16012016|Neh 12:16]]).

column5: One of the regions crowds came from to Jesus
column7: When they heard of the great things Jesus was doing, great crowds came to him from Judea and Jerusalem, from around Tyre and Sidon, and other places, and some came from Idumaea as well ([[@41003007-41003008|Mark 3:7-8]]).

column5: The spy from the tribe of Issachar
column7: The son of Joseph, he represented the tribe of Issachar among the twelve men Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013002|Num 13:2]]; [[@4013007|Num 13:7]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men, son of Nathan of Zobah
column7: The son of Nathan of Zobah, he appears in the list of David’s mighty men. His name is listed with Bani the Gadite ([[@10023036|2 Sam 23:36]]).

column5: Son of Shemaiah, of David’s royal line
column7: He appears in the genealogy of David’s royal line as one of the six sons of Shemaiah, the son of Shecaniah ([[@13003022|1 Chr 3:22]]).

column5: Father of Hanan, the man of God
column7: He was the father of Hanan, the man of God. Jeremiah brought the Rechabites into 'the room of the sons of Hanan' in the LORD’s house ([[@24035004|Jer 35:4]]).

column5: A town in the south of Judah
column7: It was one of the southern towns the tribe of Judah received, listed with Baalah and Ezem ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015029|Josh 15:29]]).

column5: A town in northern Naphtali
column7: It was an Israelite town that Ben Hadad king of Syria struck and captured ([[@11015020|1 Kgs 15:20]]). In Pekah's time Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria took this place ([[@12015029|2 Kgs 15:29]]).

column5: Father of Ira, one of David’s mighty men
column7: He was a Tekoite and the father of Ira, one of David’s mighty men ([[@10023026|2 Sam 23:26]]). His son Ira was captain for the sixth month ([[@13027009|1 Chr 27:9]]).

column5: The farthest point of Paul’s preaching
column7: Paul says that, traveling all around from Jerusalem as far as Illyricum, he had fully preached the Good News of Christ ([[@45015019|Rom 15:19]]).

column5: Father of the prophet Micaiah
column7: He was the father of the prophet Micaiah. The king of Israel hated Micaiah the son of Imlah because he prophesied only evil about him ([[@11022008|1 Kgs 22:8]]; [[@14018007|2 Chr 18:7]]).

column5: Ancestor of a priestly family in Jerusalem after the exile
column7: He appears as an ancestor in the genealogy of Maasai, a priest who lived in Jerusalem ([[@13009012|1 Chr 9:12]]). In the same list in Nehemiah he is the ancestor of Amashsai ([[@16011013|Neh 11:13]]).

column5: The name of a priestly division
column7: It was the sixteenth of the priestly divisions chosen by lot in David's time ([[@13024014|1 Chr 24:14]]). The descendants of Immer who returned from exile numbered one thousand fifty-two ([[@15002037|Ezra 2:37]]).

column5: A place in Babylon from which exiles came up
column7: Among those who came back from exile were some who came up from Immer, but they could not show whether their family and ancestry belonged to Israel ([[@15002059|Ezra 2:59]]; [[@16007061|Neh 7:61]]).

column5: Father of Zadok, who repaired the wall
column7: He was the father of Zadok, who in Nehemiah’s time repaired the part of the Jerusalem wall across from his own house ([[@16003029|Neh 3:29]]).

column5: Son of Helem, a descendant of Asher
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Asher’s descendants as one of the sons of Helem ([[@13007035|1 Chr 7:35]]; [[@13007040|1 Chr 7:40]]).

column5: Son of Asher, ancestor of the Imnites
column7: A son of Asher, he was the ancestor of the family of the Imnites. His brothers included Ishvi and Beriah ([[@4026044|Num 26:44]]; [[@13007030|1 Chr 7:30]]).

column5: Father of Kore, in charge of offerings under Hezekiah
column7: He was the father of Kore, the Levite gatekeeper at the east gate who was in charge of the freewill offerings to God in King Hezekiah’s time ([[@14031014|2 Chr 31:14]]).

column5: Son of Zophah, a descendant of Asher
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Asher’s descendants as one of the sons of Zophah ([[@13007036|1 Chr 7:36]]; [[@13007040|1 Chr 7:40]]).

column5: Ancestor of Uthai, a man of Judah in Jerusalem
column7: He was the great-grandfather of Uthai, a descendant of Perez the son of Judah, who lived in Jerusalem. Uthai was the son of Ammihud and the grandson of Omri ([[@13009003-13009004|1 Chr 9:3-4]]).

column5: Father of Zaccur, who built the wall
column7: He was the father of Zaccur, who in Nehemiah’s time built the part of the Jerusalem wall next to the men of Jericho ([[@16003002|Neh 3:2]]).

column5: Holy incense burned in the holy place
column7: Incense was a fragrant blend of spices, burned on the altar of incense in the holy place. God had them mix sweet spices, gum resin, onycha, and galbanum with frankincense to make holy incense ([[@2030034-2030035|Exod 30:34-35]]). Aaron burned incense every morning when he tended the lamps and every evening when he lit them, and no other incense was to be burned on that altar ([[@2030007-2030009|Exod 30:7-9]]). The psalmist said, "Let my prayer be set before you like incense", and Revelation also speaks of incense together with the prayers of the saints ([[@19141002|Ps 141:2]]; [[@66008003-66008004|Rev 8:3-4]]).

column5: The far eastern land ruled by King Ahasuerus
column7: King Ahasuerus reigned from India to Ethiopia, over one hundred twenty-seven provinces ([[@17001001|Esth 1:1]]). The decree for the Jews was also sent to every province from India to Ethiopia ([[@17008009|Esth 8:9]]).

column5: Son of Shashak, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants and, with Penuel, was a son of Shashak. They were family heads who lived in Jerusalem ([[@13008025|1 Chr 8:25]]; [[@13008028|1 Chr 8:28]]).

column5: A town in the lowland of Judah
column7: It was one of the lowland towns the tribe of Judah received, listed with Ashnah and Nezib ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]; [[@6015043|Josh 15:43]]).

column5: A valley on the border of Zebulun and Asher
column7: It is the valley where the northern border of the tribe of Zebulun ended ([[@6019014|Josh 19:14]]). The border of the tribe of Asher also reached this valley on the north ([[@6019027|Josh 19:27]]).

column5: Father of Shuppim and Huppim
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants, and the text names "Shuppim, Huppim, the sons of Ir" ([[@13007012|1 Chr 7:12]]).

column5: A place whose father was Tehinnah
column7: This name appears in the genealogy of Judah, which says Eshton became the father of Tehinnah, the father of Ir Nahash. These were all the men of Recah ([[@13004012|1 Chr 4:12]]).

column5: The Jairite who became David’s chief minister
column7: A Jairite, he became chief minister to David. He appears in the list of David’s officials along with Joab, Benaiah, Zadok, Abiathar, and others ([[@10020023-10020026|2 Sam 20:23-26]]).

column5: A Tekoite, one of David’s mighty men
column7: He was the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite and one of David’s mighty men ([[@10023026|2 Sam 23:26]]). He became captain for the sixth month, with twenty-four thousand in his division ([[@13027009|1 Chr 27:9]]).

column5: An Ithrite, one of David’s mighty men
column7: He was one of David’s mighty men, an Ithrite. His name is listed next to Gareb, another Ithrite ([[@10023038|2 Sam 23:38]]; [[@13011040|1 Chr 11:40]]).

column5: A chief of Edom descended from Esau
column7: He was one of the chiefs of Edom descended from Esau, the last name in the list of chiefs ([[@1036043|Gen 36:43]]; [[@13001054|1 Chr 1:54]]).

column5: Grandson of Benjamin, son of Bela
column7: He was one of the five sons of Bela the son of Benjamin, a head of his family and a mighty man of valor ([[@13007006-13007007|1 Chr 7:6-7]]).

column5: The captain of the guard who seized Jeremiah
column7: He was the son of Shelemiah and the captain of the guard at Benjamin’s gate. He seized Jeremiah, claiming he was defecting to the Chaldeans, and brought him to the princes ([[@24037013-24037014|Jer 37:13-14]]).

column5: A town of the tribe of Benjamin
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Benjamin received by families, listed with Rekem and Taralah ([[@6018021|Josh 18:21]]; [[@6018027|Josh 18:27]]).

column5: Descendant of Caleb son of Jephunneh
column7: A descendant of Caleb the son of Jephunneh, his name is listed with Elah and Naam. He is recorded in the genealogy of Judah’s descendants ([[@13004001|1 Chr 4:1]]; [[@13004015|1 Chr 4:15]]).

column5: Abraham's son of promise
column7: He was the son born to Abraham and Sarah, just as God had promised. God said, "You shall call his name Isaac" and promised to establish his covenant with him ([[@1017019|Gen 17:19]]). Abraham was a hundred years old when Isaac was born, and Sarah said that God had made her laugh ([[@1021005-1021006|Gen 21:5-6]]). When Abraham was about to offer him as a burnt offering, God provided a ram ([[@1022013|Gen 22:13]]). Later he married Rebekah and became the father of Esau and Jacob.

column5: A prophet under four kings of Judah
column7: He was the son of Amoz and prophesied about Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah ([[@23001001|Isa 1:1]]). When he heard the Lord's voice, he answered, "Here I am. Send me!" ([[@23006008|Isa 6:8]]). When Assyria threatened Jerusalem, he brought King Hezekiah the LORD's word not to be afraid ([[@12019006|2 Kgs 19:6]]). His prophecies are often quoted in the New Testament ([[@40008017|Matt 8:17]]).

column5: Daughter of Haran, sister of Milcah
column7: She was the daughter of Haran, Abram’s brother. Haran the son of Terah was the father of Milcah, Nahor’s wife, and also the father of Iscah ([[@1011027|Gen 11:27]]; [[@1011029|Gen 11:29]]).

column5: Son of Saul, king of Israel for two years
column7: He was the son of Saul; after Saul died, Abner the commander of the army took him to Mahanaim and made him king over all Israel. He was forty years old when he became king and reigned two years, while the house of Judah followed David ([[@10002008-10002010|2 Sam 2:8-10]]). When he rebuked Abner over his father's concubine Rizpah, Abner sent messengers to David to make a covenant with him ([[@10003007-10003012|2 Sam 3:7-12]]). When Ishbosheth heard that Abner had died in Hebron, he lost heart ([[@10004001|2 Sam 4:1]]). In the end Rechab and Baanah the Beerothites killed him while he was taking his midday rest and brought his head to David, but David put those two men to death instead ([[@10004005-10004012|2 Sam 4:5-12]]).

column5: Ancestor of Eshtemoa
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah’s descendants as a son born to Mered. He is called the father of Eshtemoa ([[@13004017|1 Chr 4:17]]).

column5: Son of Abraham and Keturah
column7: He was one of the six sons born to Abraham by Keturah, the wife he took later ([[@1025001-1025002|Gen 25:1-2]]; [[@13001032|1 Chr 1:32]]).

column5: Son of the giant who tried to kill David
column7: One of the sons of the giant, he carried a bronze spear weighing three hundred shekels and tried to kill David. Abishai the son of Zeruiah struck him down and killed him ([[@10021016-10021017|2 Sam 21:16-17]]).

column5: Son of Hammolecheth
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Manasseh’s descendants as a son born to Hammolecheth. His brothers were Abiezer and Mahlah ([[@13007018|1 Chr 7:18]]).

column5: Father of Zoheth and Ben Zoheth
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah’s descendants, and the text says, "The sons of Ishi: Zoheth, and Ben Zoheth" ([[@13004020|1 Chr 4:20]]).

column5: Father of Simeonite captains who went to Mount Seir
column7: A descendant of Simeon, his sons Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel led five hundred men to Mount Seir and struck the remaining Amalekites ([[@13004042-13004043|1 Chr 4:42-43]]).

column5: A family head of the half-tribe of Manasseh
column7: He was one of the family heads of the half-tribe of Manasseh, who spread out from Bashan to Mount Hermon, and he was a famous man of valor ([[@13005023-13005024|1 Chr 5:23-24]]).

column5: Descendant of the father of Etam, in Judah’s genealogy
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah’s descendants and, with Jezreel and Idbash, is called a son of the father of Etam ([[@13004003|1 Chr 4:3]]).

column5: Son of Abraham and Hagar
column7: He was the son Abraham had by Hagar, Sarai's servant. The LORD's angel told Hagar, "You shall call his name Ishmael, because the LORD has heard your affliction" ([[@1016011|Gen 16:11]]). He was born when Abram was eighty-six years old ([[@1016016|Gen 16:16]]). God promised that he would become the father of twelve princes and a great nation ([[@1017020|Gen 17:20]]). Because he mocked Isaac, he had to leave home with his mother, but God did not abandon him ([[@1021009-1021014|Gen 21:9-14]]).

column5: Royal descendant who killed Governor Gedaliah
column7: He was the grandson of Elishama, of the royal family, and the son of Nethaniah. After Jerusalem fell, people told Gedaliah that Baalis king of Ammon had sent Ishmael to kill him, but Gedaliah did not believe them ([[@24040014|Jer 40:14]]). In the seventh month, while eating bread with Gedaliah at Mizpah, Ishmael and ten men struck him down with the sword ([[@24041001-24041002|Jer 41:1-2]]). He took the remaining people captive and set out for Ammon, but when Johanan pursued him, he escaped with eight men to the children of Ammon ([[@24041015|Jer 41:15]]). He is a different person from Ishmael the son of Abraham.

column5: A Benjamite in the genealogy of Saul’s family
column7: He appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Jonathan, Saul’s son, as one of the six sons of Azel, the son of Eleasah ([[@13008037-13008038|1 Chr 8:37-38]]; [[@13009044|1 Chr 9:44]]).

column5: Father of Zebadiah in Jehoshaphat’s time
column7: He was the father of Zebadiah, who was put in charge of all the king’s matters in King Jehoshaphat’s time ([[@14019011|2 Chr 19:11]]).

column5: A captain who made a covenant with Jehoiada
column7: The son of Jehohanan, he was a captain of hundreds. He was one of those who made a covenant with Jehoiada the priest in the seventh year ([[@14023001|2 Chr 23:1]]).

column5: A priest of Pashhur’s line who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Pashhur, among the priests who had married foreign women ([[@15010018|Ezra 10:18]]; [[@15010022|Ezra 10:22]]).

column5: A Gibeonite who helped David at Ziklag
column7: A Gibeonite, he was one of the mighty men who came to help David when he was at Ziklag. He is called "a mighty man among the thirty and a leader of the thirty" ([[@13012001|1 Chr 12:1]]; [[@13012004|1 Chr 12:4]]).

column5: Officer over Zebulun in David’s time
column7: The son of Obadiah, he was the officer over Zebulun among those who ruled the tribes of Israel in David’s time ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027019|1 Chr 27:19]]).

column5: Son of Elpaal, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants as one of the sons of Elpaal ([[@13008018|1 Chr 8:18]]).

column5: Son of Beriah, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants and, with Michael and Joha, was a son of Beriah ([[@13008016|1 Chr 8:16]]).

column5: Son of Shashak, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants as one of the sons of Shashak ([[@13008022|1 Chr 8:22]]; [[@13008025|1 Chr 8:25]]).

column5: Grandson of Jacob, son of Asher
column7: He was one of the sons of Asher, Jacob’s son, a brother of Imnah, Ishvi, and Beriah ([[@1046017|Gen 46:17]]; [[@13007030|1 Chr 7:30]]).

column5: Son of Asher
column7: He was a son of Asher, Jacob’s son ([[@1046017|Gen 46:17]]). The family of the Ishvites came from him ([[@4026044|Num 26:44]]).

column5: Overseer of temple offerings under Hezekiah
column7: In King Hezekiah’s time he was one of those who looked after the temple offerings and tithes under Conaniah and his brother Shimei ([[@14031012-14031013|2 Chr 31:12-13]]).

column5: Jacob's new name, ancestor of the twelve tribes
column7: This is the new name Jacob, son of Isaac, received after wrestling until daybreak near the ford of the Jabbok. The man told Jacob, "you have fought with God and with men, and have prevailed" ([[@1032028|Gen 32:28]]). The people descended from Jacob's twelve sons were all called the 'children of Israel', and they became the twelve tribes of Israel ([[@1049028|Gen 49:28]]). After the kingdom split in two, the name was also used for the northern kingdom of the ten tribes ([[@11012020|1 Kgs 12:20]]).

column5: Son of Jacob and Leah, ancestor of Issachar's tribe
column7: Issachar was the fifth son Jacob had by Leah. Leah named him, saying, "God has given me my hire" ([[@1030018|Gen 30:18]]). Jacob compared him to "a strong donkey, lying down between the saddlebags" ([[@1049014|Gen 49:14]]). The tribe of Issachar received its inheritance in Canaan by the fourth lot ([[@6019017|Josh 19:17]]). In David's time its men were known for understanding the times and knowing what Israel ought to do ([[@13012032|1 Chr 12:32]]).

column5: Seventh son of Obed-Edom
column7: The seventh son of Obed-Edom, he appears among the divisions of gatekeepers in David’s time. The text says God blessed Obed-Edom ([[@13026004-13026005|1 Chr 26:4-5]]).

column5: Son of Izrahiah, a descendant of Issachar
column7: A descendant of Issachar, he was a son of Izrahiah the son of Uzzi. All of them were chief men ([[@13007003|1 Chr 7:3]]).

column5: A Korahite who helped David at Ziklag
column7: A Korahite, he was one of the mighty men who came to help David when he was at Ziklag ([[@13012001|1 Chr 12:1]]; [[@13012006|1 Chr 12:6]]).

column5: Second son of Uzziel, a descendant of Kohath
column7: A descendant of Kohath the son of Levi, he is listed among the sons of Uzziel after Micah the chief ([[@13023012|1 Chr 23:12]]; [[@13023020|1 Chr 23:20]]).

column5: A Levite chief in David’s time, son of Rehabiah
column7: When the divisions of the Levites were arranged in David’s day, he appears as the chief among the sons of Rehabiah ([[@13024021|1 Chr 24:21]]).

column5: A descendant of Harim who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Harim, among those who had married foreign women ([[@15010031|Ezra 10:31]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Land where Rome was, today's Italy
column7: It is the land of present-day Italy, where Rome was. Cornelius, a centurion who lived in Caesarea, belonged to a unit called the 'Italian Regiment' ([[@44010001|Acts 10:1]]). Aquila and his wife Priscilla had recently come from Italy when Claudius ordered all Jews to leave Rome, and they met Paul in Corinth ([[@44018001-44018002|Acts 18:1-2]]). Paul was sent to Italy by ship as a prisoner ([[@44027001|Acts 27:1]]), and Hebrews includes the greeting, "The Italians greet you" ([[@58013024|Heb 13:24]]).

column5: Aaron's fourth son, a priest
column7: He was the fourth son born to Aaron and Elisheba ([[@2006023|Exod 6:23]]). He was set apart as a priest with his brothers, and after Nadab and Abihu died for offering strange fire, he and Eleazar carried on the priest's office in the presence of their father ([[@4003004|Num 3:4]]). In the wilderness he oversaw the work of the Gershonites and the Merarites at the Tent of Meeting ([[@4004028|Num 4:28]], 33). When the priests were divided into divisions in David's time, the descendants of Ithamar were given eight divisions ([[@13024004|1 Chr 24:4]]).

column5: Ancestor of Sallu, a Benjamite in Jerusalem
column7: He was an ancestor six generations back of Sallu, one of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem. Sallu was the son of Meshullam and the grandson of Joed ([[@16011007|Neh 11:7]]).

column5: A town of the tribe of Dan
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Dan received by lot, listed with Shaalabbin and Aijalon ([[@6019040|Josh 19:40]]; [[@6019042|Josh 19:42]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men, a Moabite
column7: A Moabite, he appears in the list of the mighty men of David’s armies ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011046|1 Chr 11:46]]).

column5: A town in the south of Judah
column7: It was one of the southern towns the tribe of Judah received, listed with Kedesh and Hazor ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015023|Josh 15:23]]).

column5: A Horite, son of Dishon
column7: He was one of the children of Dishon, a descendant of Seir the Horite, and a brother of Hemdan, Eshban, and Cheran ([[@1036026|Gen 36:26]]; [[@13001041|1 Chr 1:41]]).

column5: A descendant of Asher, son of Zophah
column7: He was one of the sons of Zophah, a descendant of Asher, listed in the genealogy with Bezer, Hod, Shamma, and Shilshah ([[@13007036-13007037|1 Chr 7:36-37]]).

column5: David’s sixth son
column7: He was the sixth son born to David in Hebron, by David’s wife Eglah ([[@10003005|2 Sam 3:5]]; [[@13003003|1 Chr 3:3]]).

column5: A clan from Kiriath Jearim
column7: They were one of the families of Kiriath Jearim. David’s mighty men Ira and Gareb are also called Ithrites ([[@13002053|1 Chr 2:53]]; [[@13011040|1 Chr 11:40]]).

column5: The Gittite who stayed with David
column7: He was a man of Gath, and during Absalom's rebellion David told him to go back, but he followed David, saying, "whether for death or for life, your servant will be there also" ([[@10015019-10015021|2 Sam 15:19-21]]). Later he commanded a third of the army ([[@10018002|2 Sam 18:2]]).

column5: A man of Gibeah, one of David’s mighty men
column7: He was one of David’s mighty men, the son of Ribai of Gibeah of the children of Benjamin ([[@10023029|2 Sam 23:29]]). In 1 Chronicles he is called 'Ithai' ([[@13011031|1 Chr 11:31]]).

column5: A town conquered by Assyria
column7: The king of Assyria moved people from this place and settled them in the towns of Samaria ([[@12017024|2 Kgs 17:24]]). The Avvites made Nibhaz and Tartak and worshiped them ([[@12017031|2 Kgs 17:31]]).

column5: Where Israel camped facing Moab
column7: It was where Israel camped after setting out from Oboth, in the wilderness before Moab, toward the sunrise ([[@4021011|Num 21:11]]; [[@4033044|Num 33:44]]).

column5: A wilderness camp of Israel
column7: It was one of the places where the Israelites stopped while passing through the wilderness; they traveled from Iyim and camped at Dibon Gad ([[@4033045|Num 33:45]]).

column5: Son of Kohath and father of Korah
column7: He was a grandson of Levi and the second son of Kohath, the brother of Amram, Hebron, and Uzziel ([[@2006018|Exod 6:18]]). His sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri ([[@2006021|Exod 6:21]]). His descendants formed 'the family of the Izharites,' one branch of the Kohathite families ([[@4003027|Num 3:27]]). His son Korah is well known for later gathering a group and rising up against Moses and Aaron ([[@4016001|Num 16:1]]).

column5: Son of Helah, in Judah’s genealogy
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah’s descendants as a son born to Helah, the wife of Ashhur ([[@13004005|1 Chr 4:5]]; [[@13004007|1 Chr 4:7]]).

column5: Son of Elpaal, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants as one of the sons of Elpaal ([[@13008018|1 Chr 8:18]]).

column5: A descendant of Parosh who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Parosh, among those who had married foreign women ([[@15010025|Ezra 10:25]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A family head of the Simeonites
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Simeon’s descendants as one of the princes of their families ([[@13004036|1 Chr 4:36]]; [[@13004038|1 Chr 4:38]]).

column5: A family among the descendants of Solomon’s servants
column6: ascending; a little doe or goat
column7: Among the descendants of Solomon’s servants who came back from exile were 'the children of Jaalah' ([[@15002055-15002056|Ezra 2:55-56]]; [[@16007058|Neh 7:58]]).

column5: Father of Elhanan, who killed Goliath’s brother
column7: He was a Bethlehemite, the father of Elhanan, who killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath of Gath ([[@10021019|2 Sam 21:19]]). In 1 Chronicles, Elhanan is called 'the son of Jair' ([[@13020005|1 Chr 20:5]]).

column5: Son of Jeroham, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants as one of the sons of Jeroham ([[@13008027|1 Chr 8:27]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men, the Mezobaite
column7: The Mezobaite, he is named at the end of the list of the mighty men of David’s armies ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011047|1 Chr 11:47]]).

column5: Officer over Benjamin in David’s time
column7: The son of Abner, he was the officer over Benjamin among those who ruled the tribes of Israel in David’s time ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027021|1 Chr 27:21]]).

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Bani, among those who had married foreign women ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]; [[@15010037|Ezra 10:37]]).

column5: A Rechabite, grandson of Habazziniah
column7: The grandson of Habazziniah and son of Jeremiah, he was a Rechabite. The prophet Jeremiah brought him and the whole house of the Rechabites into the LORD’s house and offered them wine ([[@24035003-24035005|Jer 35:3-5]]).

column5: Son of Shaphan, an elder holding a censer
column7: The son of Shaphan, he stood among the seventy elders of the house of Israel that Ezekiel saw in a vision, with a censer in his hand ([[@26008010-26008011|Ezek 8:10-11]]).

column5: Son of Azzur, a prince who gave wicked counsel
column7: The son of Azzur, he was one of the twenty-five men Ezekiel saw at the east gate of the LORD’s house. They were princes of the people, and they were said to give wicked counsel in the city ([[@26011001-26011002|Ezek 11:1-2]]).

column5: A Levite descended from Merari
column7: He was a descendant of Merari, listed in the divisions of the Levites in David’s day. From him came Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri ([[@13024026-13024027|1 Chr 24:26-27]]).

column5: A Levite who played the harp in David’s time
column7: He was one of the Levites of the second rank appointed when David brought up the ark ([[@13015018|1 Chr 15:18]]). He played a stringed instrument set to Alamoth, and in verse 20 he is called 'Aziel' ([[@13015020|1 Chr 15:20]]).

column5: Father of those who live in tents and keep livestock
column7: He was the son of Lamech and Adah. He became the father of those who live in tents and keep livestock, and his brother was Jubal ([[@1004019-1004021|Gen 4:19-21]]).

column5: River east of the Jordan where Jacob wrestled
column7: It is a river that flows down from the east side of the Jordan. Jacob led his family across the ford of the Jabbok at night, and then, left alone, he wrestled with a man until daybreak ([[@1032022-1032024|Gen 32:22-24]]). Israel defeated Sihon king of the Amorites and took his land from the Arnon to the Jabbok ([[@4021024|Num 21:24]]). The river Jabbok was the border of the Ammonites, and it is also named as the edge of the land given to the Reubenites and Gadites ([[@5003016|Deut 3:16]]).

column5: Gileadite town that remembered Saul to the end
column7: It was a town in Gilead east of the Jordan, usually called 'Jabesh Gilead.' In the time of the judges it was punished for not coming to the assembly at Mizpah ([[@7021008-7021012|Judg 21:8-12]]). When Nahash the Ammonite besieged the town, Saul gathered an army and rescued it ([[@9011001-9011011|1 Sam 11:1-11]]). Remembering that kindness, the men of Jabesh traveled all night after Saul's death to take his body and bury it ([[@9031011-9031013|1 Sam 31:11-13]]).

column5: Father of Shallum, who became king
column7: He was the father of Shallum, who killed Zechariah king of Israel and became king ([[@12015008-12015010|2 Kgs 15:8-10]]). His son Shallum reigned for a month in Samaria ([[@12015013|2 Kgs 15:13]]).

column5: A place where families of scribes lived
