column7: It was the place where families of scribes lived, such as the Tirathites, the Shimeathites, and the Sucathites. They were Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab ([[@13002055|1 Chr 2:55]]).

column5: An honorable man whose prayer was answered
column7: He was more honorable than his brothers, and his mother named him Jabez because she bore him in pain. When he prayed that God would enlarge his border and keep him from harm, God granted what he asked ([[@13004009-13004010|1 Chr 4:9-10]]).

column5: King of Hazor who fought Joshua
column7: He was king of Hazor; when he heard about Israel, he camped at the waters of Merom with Jobab king of Madon and many other kings ([[@6011001|Josh 11:1]]; [[@6011005|Josh 11:5]]). Joshua took Hazor and struck its king with the sword ([[@6011010|Josh 11:10]]).

column5: A Canaanite king who reigned in Hazor
column7: He was a Canaanite king who reigned in Hazor, and the commander of his army was Sisera ([[@7004002|Judg 4:2]]). On that day God subdued Jabin before the children of Israel ([[@7004023|Judg 4:23]]).

column5: A town on Judah’s northern border
column7: It was a place on the border of the tribe of Judah. The border went from the north side of Ekron past Shikkeron and Mount Baalah to Jabneel, and it ended at the sea ([[@6015011|Josh 15:11]]).

column5: A place on the border of Naphtali
column7: It was one of the places the border of the land Naphtali’s descendants received by lot passed through ([[@6019032-6019033|Josh 19:32-33]]).

column5: A Gadite who lived in Bashan
column7: He was a descendant of Gad who lived in the land of Bashan, one of seven brothers of their family ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005013|1 Chr 5:13]]).

column5: A son of Simeon
column7: He was a son of Simeon, Jacob's son ([[@1046010|Gen 46:10]]; [[@2006015|Exod 6:15]]). From him came the family of the Jachinites ([[@4026012|Num 26:12]]).

column5: A priest who lived in Jerusalem after the exile
column7: He was one of the priests who returned from exile and lived in Jerusalem, and his name appears with Jedaiah ([[@13009010|1 Chr 9:10]]; [[@16011010|Neh 11:10]]).

column5: Priest of the twenty-first division
column7: When the priests’ divisions were assigned by lot, he was the one chosen twenty-first ([[@13024007|1 Chr 24:7]]; [[@13024017|1 Chr 24:17]]).

column5: Father of Joseph, Mary’s husband
column7: In Matthew’s genealogy of Jesus, he was the son of Matthan. It continues, "Jacob became the father of Joseph, the husband of Mary" ([[@40001015-40001016|Matt 1:15-16]]).

column5: A descendant of Judah, son of Onam
column7: He was the son of Onam, a descendant of Jerahmeel, and the brother of Shammai ([[@13002028|1 Chr 2:28]]). His sons were Jether and Jonathan ([[@13002032|1 Chr 2:32]]).

column5: A descendant of Nebo who married a foreign wife
column7: A descendant of Nebo, he was on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010043-15010044|Ezra 10:43-44]]).

column5: A leader who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah’s time who set their seal on the covenant ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010021|Neh 10:21]]).

column5: A descendant of Jeshua, son of Jonathan
column7: He was a descendant of Jeshua and the son of Jonathan ([[@16012010-16012011|Neh 12:10-11]]). The heads of the Levite families were recorded in the days of Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua ([[@16012022|Neh 12:22]]).

column5: A Meronothite who repaired the wall
column7: A Meronothite, he worked with Melatiah the Gibeonite and the men of Gibeon and Mizpah to repair a section of the wall ([[@16003007|Neh 3:7]]).

column5: Wife of Heber the Kenite, who killed Sisera
column7: She was the wife of Heber the Kenite. When Sisera, the army commander of Jabin king of Hazor, lost the battle and fled to her on foot, Jael welcomed him into her tent and covered him with a rug ([[@7004017-7004018|Judg 4:17-18]]). When Sisera, worn out, fell into a deep sleep, she drove a tent peg into his temple and killed him, and she showed him to Barak, who had come after him ([[@7004021-7004022|Judg 4:21-22]]). This happened just as Deborah had said, that the LORD would sell Sisera into a woman's hand ([[@7004009|Judg 4:9]]). The song of Deborah and Barak praises her: "Jael shall be blessed above women, the wife of Heber the Kenite" ([[@7005024|Judg 5:24]]).

column5: A town of Judah near the border of Edom
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Judah received, among the cities in the South near the border of Edom ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]).

column5: A descendant of Gershon, son of Shimei
column7: When the Levites were counted in David’s day, he was the chief among the sons of Shimei ([[@13023010-13023011|1 Chr 23:10-11]]).

column5: Son of Shelomoth, a descendant of Izhar
column7: In the list of Levi’s descendants he appears as the son of Shelomoth, of the Izharites ([[@13024020|1 Chr 24:20]]; [[@13024022|1 Chr 24:22]]).

column5: Overseer of temple repairs under Josiah
column7: A Levite descended from Merari, he oversaw the work of repairing the LORD’s house with Obadiah in Josiah’s time ([[@14034008|2 Chr 34:8]]; [[@14034012|2 Chr 34:12]]).

column5: Where Sihon king of the Amorites fought Israel
column7: It was a place east of the Jordan toward the wilderness, where Sihon king of the Amorites, refusing to let Israel pass through his land, gathered his people and fought at Jahaz. Israel struck them with the edge of the sword and took their land from the Arnon to the Jabbok ([[@4021023-4021024|Num 21:23-24]]). Jahaz became part of the inheritance of the tribe of Reuben ([[@6013015-6013018|Josh 13:15-18]]), and it was also one of the towns given from it to the Levites of the family of Merari ([[@6021034-6021036|Josh 21:34-36]]). In his warning against Moab, Isaiah said that Heshbon cries out with Elealeh and their voice "is heard even to Jahaz" ([[@23015004|Isa 15:4]]).

column5: A warrior who came to David at Ziklag
column7: He was one of the warriors from the tribe of Benjamin who came to David and helped him in battle while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001-13012002|1 Chr 12:1-2]]; [[@13012004|1 Chr 12:4]]).

column5: Priest who blew trumpets before the ark
column7: In David’s time he and Benaiah, the priests, served "with trumpets continually, before the ark of the covenant of God" ([[@13016006|1 Chr 16:6]]).

column5: A descendant of Kohath, Hebron’s third son
column7: He was a grandson of Kohath son of Levi, and the third son of Hebron ([[@13023012|1 Chr 23:12]]; [[@13023019|1 Chr 23:19]]; [[@13024023|1 Chr 24:23]]).

column5: A Levite who prophesied in Jehoshaphat’s time
column7: He was a Levite, the son of Zechariah of the sons of Asaph, and the LORD’s Spirit came on him ([[@14020014|2 Chr 20:14]]). He told Judah not to be afraid because of this great multitude ([[@14020015|2 Chr 20:15]]).

column5: Father of one who came with Ezra
column7: He was of the descendants of Shecaniah, and his son came up from Babylon with Ezra along with three hundred men ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008005|Ezra 8:5]]).

column5: A man in Caleb’s line, father of Regem and others
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah that includes Caleb’s descendants, and he was the father of Regem, Jothan, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph ([[@13002047|1 Chr 2:47]]).

column5: A family head of the half-tribe of Manasseh
column7: He was a family head of the half-tribe of Manasseh, who spread out from Bashan to Mount Hermon, and he was a famous man of valor ([[@13005023-13005024|1 Chr 5:23-24]]).

column5: An ancestor in the genealogy of Gad
column7: He was an ancestor of Abihail, a descendant of Gad who lived in Bashan, and he was the son of Buz ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005014|1 Chr 5:14]]).

column5: Grandson of Jacob, son of Zebulun
column7: He was one of Zebulun’s sons and went with Jacob’s family to Egypt ([[@1046014|Gen 46:14]]). The family of the Jahleelites came from him ([[@4026026|Num 26:26]]).

column5: Son of Tola, a descendant of Issachar
column7: He was a son of Tola the son of Issachar, and his brothers included Uzzi, Rephaiah, and Jeriel. They were heads of their father Tola’s house and mighty men of valor ([[@13007001-13007002|1 Chr 7:1-2]]).

column5: Son of Naphtali
column7: His name comes first among the sons of Naphtali, Jacob’s son ([[@1046024|Gen 46:24]]). In Numbers the family of the Jahzeelites came from him ([[@4026048|Num 26:48]]).

column5: A man who opposed Ezra’s plan
column7: The son of Tikvah, he stood up with Jonathan the son of Asahel against the proposal to deal with the matter of those who had married foreign women ([[@15010014-15010015|Ezra 10:14-15]]).

column5: Grandfather of Maasai the priest
column7: He was the grandfather of Maasai, a priest who lived in Jerusalem; he was the son of Meshullam and the father of Adiel ([[@13009010|1 Chr 9:10]]; [[@13009012|1 Chr 9:12]]).

column5: A descendant of Manasseh who took towns in Gilead
column7: He was a son of Manasseh who took villages and called them Havvoth Jair ([[@4032041|Num 32:41]]). He took the whole region of Argob and called Bashan by his own name ([[@5003014|Deut 3:14]]).

column5: The villages of Jair in Bashan
column7: This was a place within the land Moses gave to the half-tribe of Manasseh, referring to all the villages of Jair in Bashan, sixty cities ([[@6013029-6013030|Josh 13:29-30]]).

column5: A judge who led Israel for 22 years
column7: He was a Gileadite who judged Israel for twenty-two years ([[@7010003|Judg 10:3]]). When he died, he was buried in Kamon ([[@7010005|Judg 10:5]]).

column5: Father of Mordecai
column7: A Benjamite, he was the father of Mordecai, a Jew who lived in the citadel of Susa. Mordecai is introduced as the grandson of Shimei and great-grandson of Kish ([[@17002005|Esth 2:5]]).

column5: A synagogue ruler who asked Jesus to save his daughter
column7: He was a ruler of the synagogue who fell at Jesus’ feet and begged him to come to his house ([[@41005022|Mark 5:22]]; [[@42008041|Luke 8:41]]). Jesus raised his daughter from the dead ([[@41005041-41005042|Mark 5:41-42]]).

column5: Father of Agur
column7: He was the father of Agur, whose words are recorded in Proverbs 30. Agur spoke these sayings to Ithiel and Ucal ([[@20030001|Prov 30:1]]).

column5: Son of Shimei, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He was one of the sons of Shimei in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants ([[@13008019|1 Chr 8:19]]; [[@13008021|1 Chr 8:21]]).

column5: Priest of the twelfth division
column7: When the priests’ divisions were assigned by lot, he was the one chosen twelfth ([[@13024007|1 Chr 24:7]]; [[@13024012|1 Chr 24:12]]).

column5: Son of Esau and Oholibamah
column7: He was the son born to Esau's wife Oholibamah in the land of Canaan ([[@1036005|Gen 36:5]]). He later became a chief of Edom ([[@1036018|Gen 36:18]]).

column5: Son of Ezrah, in Judah’s genealogy
column7: He was a son of Ezrah in the genealogy of Judah’s descendants, and his brothers were Jether, Mered, and Epher ([[@13004001|1 Chr 4:1]]; [[@13004017|1 Chr 4:17]]).

column5: A man who opposed Moses
column7: He is named with Jannes as one who opposed Moses. Paul compared those who oppose the truth to these men ([[@55003008|2 Tim 3:8]]).

column5: Son of Zebedee, one of the twelve apostles
column7: He was the son of Zebedee and the brother of John, a fisherman on the Sea of Galilee. He was mending nets in a boat when Jesus called him, and he followed him. Jesus gave James and John the name "Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder" ([[@41003017|Mark 3:17]]). With Peter and John he went up the mountain where Jesus was transfigured, and he was also close to Jesus in Gethsemane ([[@40017001|Matt 17:1]]; [[@41014033|Mark 14:33]]). Later King Herod "killed James, the brother of John, with the sword" ([[@44012002|Acts 12:2]]).

column5: Son of Alphaeus, one of the Twelve
column7: He was one of Jesus' twelve apostles, called "James the son of Alphaeus" to set him apart from James the son of Zebedee, who had the same name ([[@40010003|Matt 10:3]]; [[@41003018|Mark 3:18]]). His name also appears among the apostles gathered in the upper room after Jesus went up to heaven ([[@44001013|Acts 1:13]]). Among the women near the cross was Mary the mother of 'James the less' ([[@41015040|Mark 15:40]]), and scholars differ on whether this James the less is the same man as James the son of Alphaeus. The Bible tells nothing more about what he did.

column5: The Lord's brother, leader of the Jerusalem church
column7: He was one of Jesus' brothers; people spoke of "his brothers James, Joses, Simon, and Judas" ([[@40013055|Matt 13:55]]). In Jerusalem Paul called him 'James, the Lord's brother' ([[@48001019|Gal 1:19]]). In the Jerusalem church he was regarded, together with Cephas and John, as a pillar ([[@48002009|Gal 2:9]]). At the Jerusalem council he gave the opinion that they should not trouble the Gentiles who were turning to God ([[@44015013-44015019|Acts 15:13-19]]).

column5: Father of the apostle Judas
column7: He was the father of Judas, one of the twelve Jesus chose as apostles. This Judas is a different person from Judas Iscariot ([[@42006013|Luke 6:13]]; [[@42006016|Luke 6:16]]).

column5: A son of Simeon
column7: He was a son of Simeon, Jacob's son ([[@1046010|Gen 46:10]]; [[@2006015|Exod 6:15]]). From him came the family of the Jaminites ([[@4026012|Num 26:12]]).

column5: Son of Ram, Jerahmeel’s firstborn
column7: He was the son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel, who was the firstborn of Hezron; his brothers were Maaz and Eker ([[@13002025|1 Chr 2:25]]; [[@13002027|1 Chr 2:27]]).

column5: He helped the people understand the law
column7: In Ezra’s time he was one of those who, together with the Levites, helped the people understand the law ([[@16008007-16008008|Neh 8:7-8]]).

column5: A Simeonite leader in Hezekiah’s time
column7: He was one of the leaders of Simeon’s descendants, among those who in Hezekiah’s time destroyed the Meunim and settled in their land ([[@13004034|1 Chr 4:34]]; [[@13004038|1 Chr 4:38]]; [[@13004041|1 Chr 4:41]]).

column5: A Gadite leader in Bashan
column7: He was one of the leaders of Gad’s descendants who lived in the land of Bashan, and his name comes after Joel and Shapham ([[@13005011-13005012|1 Chr 5:11-12]]).

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: It was one of the hill-country towns the tribe of Judah received, listed with Beth Tappuah and Aphekah ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015053|Josh 15:53]]).

column5: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke’s genealogy
column7: He is an ancestor in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus, the son of Joseph and the father of Melchi ([[@42003024|Luke 3:24]]).

column5: A man who opposed Moses
column7: He is named with Jambres as one who opposed Moses. Paul compared those who oppose the truth to these men ([[@55003008|2 Tim 3:8]]).

column5: A town on the border of Ephraim
column7: It was a place on the border of the children of Ephraim. The border passed along the east of Janoah, then went down from Janoah to Ataroth and Naarah and reached Jericho ([[@6016006-6016007|Josh 16:6-7]]).

column5: An Israelite town taken by Assyria
column7: It was one of the towns that Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria came and took in the days of Pekah king of Israel ([[@12015029|2 Kgs 15:29]]).

column5: One of Noah's three sons
column7: He was one of Noah's sons Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and he went into the ark with his father and brothers at the time of the flood and was saved ([[@1007013|Gen 7:13]]). When his father Noah was drunk with wine and lay uncovered in his tent, Japheth and Shem laid a garment on their shoulders, walked in backward, and covered him ([[@1009021-1009023|Gen 9:21-23]]). Then Noah blessed him, saying, "May God enlarge Japheth. Let him dwell in the tents of Shem" ([[@1009027|Gen 9:27]]). From his descendants the peoples of many nations spread out and settled in the coastlands ([[@1010002-1010005|Gen 10:2-5]]).

column5: King of Lachish who fought Joshua
column7: He was king of Lachish, one of the five Amorite kings who, summoned by Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem, went to attack Gibeon ([[@6010003|Josh 10:3]]; [[@6010005|Josh 10:5]]). Joshua struck these kings and put them to death ([[@6010026|Josh 10:26]]).

column5: A place on the border of Zebulun
column7: It was a place the border of Zebulun’s inheritance passed through; the border went up from Daberath to Japhia ([[@6019010|Josh 19:10]]; [[@6019012|Josh 19:12]]).

column5: A son of David born in Jerusalem
column7: He was one of the sons born to David in Jerusalem ([[@10005013-10005015|2 Sam 5:13-15]]). He also appears in the lists of David’s sons in 1 Chronicles ([[@13003007|1 Chr 3:7]]; [[@13014006|1 Chr 14:6]]).

column5: A descendant of Asher, son of Heber
column7: He was the son of Heber, a descendant of Asher, and the brother of Hotham and Shomer ([[@13007032|1 Chr 7:32]]). His sons were Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath ([[@13007033|1 Chr 7:33]]).

column5: Ancestor before the Flood, father of Enoch
column7: He was a descendant of Seth who lived before the Flood. Mahalalel became the father of Jared at sixty-five ([[@1005015|Gen 5:15]]). Jared became the father of Enoch at one hundred sixty-two, and after that he lived eight hundred years and had other children ([[@1005018-1005019|Gen 5:18-19]]). He lived nine hundred sixty-two years and then died ([[@1005020|Gen 5:20]]). His name also appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus ([[@42003037|Luke 3:37]]).

column5: An Egyptian servant who married Sheshan’s daughter
column7: He was the Egyptian servant of Sheshan, who had no sons, only daughters. Sheshan gave him his daughter as a wife, and he became the father of Attai ([[@13002034-13002035|1 Chr 2:34-35]]).

column5: A leader Ezra sent for
column7: He was one of the chief men Ezra sent for and sent to Iddo at Casiphia, to bring back ministers for the house of God ([[@15008016-15008017|Ezra 8:16-17]]).

column5: A priest who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a priest among the descendants of Jeshua who had married a foreign woman. They pledged to put away their wives and offered a ram as a guilt offering ([[@15010018-15010019|Ezra 10:18-19]]).

column5: Lowland town of Judah conquered by Joshua
column7: It was a town in the land of Canaan in Joshua's time, and its king Piram, summoned by Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem, attacked Gibeon with four other Amorite kings ([[@6010003-6010005|Josh 10:3-5]]). But Joshua brought these five kings out of the cave, struck them down, and hanged them on trees ([[@6010023-6010026|Josh 10:23-26]]). After this Jarmuth became one of the lowland towns given to the tribe of Judah ([[@6015033-6015035|Josh 15:33-35]]), and some of the people of Judah who returned from exile lived there ([[@16011025|Neh 11:25]], 29).

column5: A town of Issachar given to the Levites
column7: It was one of the towns from the tribe of Issachar given to the descendants of Gershon, a Levite family ([[@6021027-6021029|Josh 21:27-29]]).

column5: An ancestor in the genealogy of Gad
column7: He was an ancestor of Abihail, a descendant of Gad who lived in Bashan, and he was the son of Gilead ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005014|1 Chr 5:14]]).

column5: The book of Jashar, a record of old songs
column7: 'The book of Jashar' is an ancient book known only by name in the Bible. The sun standing still and David’s song of the bow are said to be written in it ([[@6010013|Josh 10:13]]; [[@10001018|2 Sam 1:18]]).

column5: Father of Jonathan, one of David’s mighty men
column7: He was the father of Jonathan, one of David’s mighty men ([[@10023032|2 Sam 23:32]]). The same list in 1 Chronicles has 'the sons of Hashem the Gizonite' ([[@13011034|1 Chr 11:34]]).

column5: Chief of David’s mighty men
column7: He was the son of a Hachmonite and chief of the thirty, who lifted up his spear against three hundred and killed them at one time ([[@13011011|1 Chr 11:11]]). The captain of the division for the first month was also Jashobeam, the son of Zabdiel ([[@13027002|1 Chr 27:2]]).

column5: A Korahite who came to David at Ziklag
column7: A Korahite, he was one of the warriors who came to David and helped him in battle while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001|1 Chr 12:1]]; [[@13012006|1 Chr 12:6]]).

column5: Son of Issachar
column7: He was one of the four sons of Issachar ([[@13007001|1 Chr 7:1]]). The family of the Jashubites came from him ([[@4026023-4026024|Num 26:23-24]]). Some think he is the same as 'Iob' in Genesis ([[@1046013|Gen 46:13]]).

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: A descendant of Bani, he was on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010029|Ezra 10:29]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: The man who welcomed Paul in Thessalonica
column7: He was the man in Thessalonica who received Paul and his companions into his house, and the Jews attacked his house and dragged him before the city officials ([[@44017005-44017007|Acts 17:5-7]]).

column5: Fourth son of Meshelemiah the gatekeeper
column7: The fourth son of Meshelemiah the Korahite, he was among the divisions of the gatekeepers. The firstborn was Zechariah ([[@13026001-13026002|1 Chr 26:1-2]]).

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: It was a town in the hill country of Judah that was given to the descendants of Aaron the priest ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6021013-6021014|Josh 21:13-14]]). It was one of the places to which David sent a share of the plunder ([[@9030026-9030027|1 Sam 30:26-27]]).

column5: Son of Japheth, ancestor of the Greeks
column7: Javan was the fourth son of Japheth, Noah's son ([[@1010002|Gen 10:2]]). His sons were Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim ([[@1010004|Gen 10:4]]). In Hebrew, Javan is the name used for Greece, both the land and its people, so his descendants are thought to have become the Greeks. In the prophets the name also appears as 'Javan' ([[@26027013|Ezek 27:13]]), but in a few places, such as the book of Daniel, it is translated 'Greece'. The "king of Greece" in Daniel's vision is also this name in the original text ([[@27008021|Dan 8:21]]).

column5: Town of Gilead east of the Jordan
column7: It was an Amorite town east of the Jordan; Moses sent men to spy it out, and Israel took its villages ([[@4021032|Num 21:32]]). Because the land of Jazer and the land of Gilead were good for livestock, the descendants of Reuben and Gad asked for that land ([[@4032001|Num 32:1]]). Later Jazer became one of the towns given to the Levites of the family of Merari ([[@6021034-6021039|Josh 21:34-39]]). Grieving over what would happen to Moab, Isaiah said, "I will weep with the weeping of Jazer" ([[@23016009|Isa 16:9]]).

column5: The Hagrite in charge of David’s flocks
column7: A Hagrite, he was in charge of the flocks among King David’s property. At the same time Jehdeiah the Meronothite was in charge of the donkeys ([[@13027030-13027031|1 Chr 27:30-31]]).

column5: A descendant of Gershom, son of Zerah
column7: In the genealogy of Gershom, Levi’s son, he appears as the son of Zerah, the last name in that line ([[@13006020-13006021|1 Chr 6:20-21]]).

column5: Father of Zechariah the witness
column7: He was the father of Zechariah, who in the book of Isaiah is called a faithful witness along with Uriah the priest ([[@23008002|Isa 8:2]]).

column5: The Canaanite people who lived in Jerusalem before David
column7: The Jebusites were a people descended from Canaan ([[@1010016|Gen 10:16]]), and they lived in Jebus, the old name for Jerusalem ([[@7019010|Judg 19:10]]). They were one of the peoples living in the land God promised to give Israel. The children of Judah could not drive them out, so they lived together for a long time ([[@6015063|Josh 15:63]]). After David became king, he struck the Jebusites and took the stronghold of Zion, and it was called the city of David ([[@10005006-10005007|2 Sam 5:6-7]]).

column5: Mother of Azariah (Uzziah), king of Judah
column7: She was the mother of Azariah king of Judah, a woman of Jerusalem ([[@12015001-12015002|2 Kgs 15:1-2]]). In 2 Chronicles she is named as Uzziah’s mother, 'Jechiliah' ([[@14026003|2 Chr 26:3]]).

column5: Ancestor of Ziza, a Simeonite
column7: He was the son of Shimri in the genealogy of Simeon’s descendants, and the great-grandfather of Ziza, a family leader ([[@13004024|1 Chr 4:24]]; [[@13004037|1 Chr 4:37]]).

column5: A priest who lived in Jerusalem after the exile
column7: He was a priest who returned from exile and lived in Jerusalem ([[@13009010|1 Chr 9:10]]). The book of Nehemiah records him as 'Jedaiah the son of Joiarib' ([[@16011010|Neh 11:10]]).

column5: Head of a priestly division
column7: When the priestly divisions were assigned by lot in David’s day, the second lot fell to him ([[@13024003-13024007|1 Chr 24:3-7]]). Among the priests who came back from exile were 973 of the children of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua ([[@15002036|Ezra 2:36]]).

column5: He repaired the wall across from his house
column7: The son of Harumaph, he repaired the part of the wall across from his own house in Nehemiah’s time ([[@16003010|Neh 3:10]]).

column5: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the priests and their brothers in the days of Jeshua ([[@16012007|Neh 12:7]]). In the days of Joiakim, the head of Jedaiah’s family was Nethanel ([[@16012021|Neh 12:21]]).

column5: A returned exile who brought silver and gold for crowns
column7: He was one of those who came back from Babylon, and Zechariah was told to take silver and gold from them and make crowns ([[@38006010-38006011|Zech 6:10-11]]). The crowns were to be kept in the LORD’s temple as a memorial to them ([[@38006014|Zech 6:14]]).

column5: Son of Benjamin
column7: He was a son of Benjamin ([[@13007006|1 Chr 7:6]]). His descendants who were able to go out to war numbered seventeen thousand two hundred ([[@13007010-13007011|1 Chr 7:10-11]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men, son of Shimri
column7: The son of Shimri, he appears in the list of David’s mighty men along with his brother Joha the Tizite ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011045|1 Chr 11:45]]).

column5: A Manassite captain of thousands who joined David
column7: He was one of those from the tribe of Manasseh who joined David as he went to Ziklag, and he was a captain of thousands of Manasseh ([[@13012020|1 Chr 12:20]]).

column5: Second son of Meshelemiah the gatekeeper
column7: The second son of Meshelemiah the Korahite, he was among the divisions of the gatekeepers. The firstborn was Zechariah ([[@13026001-13026002|1 Chr 26:1-2]]).

column5: Mother of King Josiah
column7: She was the mother of King Josiah and the daughter of Adaiah of Bozkath. Josiah became king at eight years old ([[@12022001|2 Kgs 22:1]]).

column5: Levite musician in charge of praise under David
column7: A Levite musician appointed by David, he was put in charge, with Asaph and Heman, of songs giving thanks to the LORD ([[@13016041|1 Chr 16:41]]). His sons played the harp and sang spiritual songs, giving thanks and praise to the LORD ([[@13025003|1 Chr 25:3]]). Second Chronicles also calls him 'Jeduthun the king's seer' ([[@14035015|2 Chr 35:15]]). Many scholars think he is the same person as the musician Ethan, but this is not certain ([[@13015017|1 Chr 15:17]]).

column5: Ancestor of Levites in Jerusalem after the exile
column7: He appears as the great-grandfather of Obadiah, a Levite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile ([[@13009016|1 Chr 9:16]]). In Nehemiah, Abda is listed as a great-grandson of Jeduthun ([[@16011017|Neh 11:17]]).

column5: Father of Ziph, Ziphah, and others
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah’s descendants as the father of Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel ([[@13004001|1 Chr 4:1]]; [[@13004016|1 Chr 4:16]]).

column5: Father of Azariah, a descendant of Merari
column7: He was the father of Azariah, a descendant of Merari. Azariah was one of the Levites who cleansed the LORD’s house in Hezekiah’s time ([[@14029012|2 Chr 29:12]]; [[@14029015|2 Chr 29:15]]).

column5: A Levite, son of Shubael
column7: In the list of Levi’s descendants he appears as the son of Shubael, the son of Amram. These too cast lots in the presence of King David, just like the descendants of Aaron ([[@13024020|1 Chr 24:20]]; [[@13024031|1 Chr 24:31]]).

column5: The man in charge of David’s donkeys
column7: A Meronothite, he was in charge of the donkeys among King David’s property. At the same time Obil the Ishmaelite was in charge of the camels ([[@13027030-13027031|1 Chr 27:30-31]]).

column5: Priest of the twentieth division
column7: When the priests’ divisions were assigned by lot, he was the one chosen twentieth ([[@13024007|1 Chr 24:7]]; [[@13024016|1 Chr 24:16]]).

column5: Chief of Gershonite Levites in David's time
column7: He was a descendant of Gershon the son of Levi and the chief among the sons of Ladan ([[@13023007-13023008|1 Chr 23:7-8]]). In 1 Chronicles 26 he appears under the name 'Jehieli,' and his sons, Zetham and Joel his brother, were in charge of the treasuries of the LORD's house ([[@13026021-13026022|1 Chr 26:21-22]]). In David's time, when the people gave offerings for the temple, those who had precious stones gave them to the treasury of the LORD's house "under the hand of Jehiel the Gershonite" ([[@13029008|1 Chr 29:8]]).

column5: A Levite musician in David’s time
column7: He was one of the Levites appointed next after the singers when David brought up the ark ([[@13015018|1 Chr 15:18]]). He was assigned to play a stringed instrument set to Alamoth ([[@13015020|1 Chr 15:20]]).

column5: Attendant to David’s sons
column7: The son of Hachmoni, he is recorded in David’s time as one who "was with the king’s sons" ([[@13027032|1 Chr 27:32]]).

column5: Son of King Jehoshaphat
column7: He was a son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah and a brother of Jehoram. Azariah, Zechariah, Michael, and Shephatiah were also his brothers ([[@14021002|2 Chr 21:2]]).

column5: He looked after offerings under Hezekiah
column7: In King Hezekiah’s time he was in charge of looking after the offerings brought to God’s house, under Conaniah the Levite and his brother Shimei ([[@14031012-14031013|2 Chr 31:12-13]]).

column5: A ruler of God’s house in Josiah’s time
column7: In Josiah’s time he was one of the rulers of God’s house along with Hilkiah and Zechariah, and they gave the priests two thousand six hundred small livestock and three hundred cattle for the Passover offerings ([[@14035007-14035008|2 Chr 35:7-8]]).

column5: Father of Obadiah, who came with Ezra
column7: A descendant of Joab, he was the father of Obadiah, who came up from Babylon with Ezra along with two hundred eighteen men ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008009|Ezra 8:9]]).

column5: Father of Shecaniah
column7: A descendant of Elam, he was the father of Shecaniah, who confessed to Ezra the sin of marrying foreign women ([[@15010002|Ezra 10:2]]).

column5: A priest of Harim’s line who married a foreign wife
column7: A descendant of Harim, he was on the list of priests who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010018|Ezra 10:18]]; [[@15010021|Ezra 10:21]]).

column5: A descendant of Elam who married a foreign wife
column7: A descendant of Elam, he was on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010026|Ezra 10:26]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: An Ephraimite leader who stopped the captives
column7: The son of Shallum, he was one of the heads of the descendants of Ephraim. He stood against those returning from the war and told them not to bring in the captives ([[@14028012-14028013|2 Chr 28:12-13]]).

column5: Mother of Amaziah, king of Judah
column7: She was the mother of Amaziah king of Judah, the son of Joash, and she was from Jerusalem ([[@12014001-12014002|2 Kgs 14:1-2]]; [[@14025001|2 Chr 25:1]]).

column5: Son of Jehu, king of northern Israel
column7: The son of Jehu king of Israel, he succeeded his father and reigned in Samaria for seventeen years ([[@12010035|2 Kgs 10:35]]; [[@12013001|2 Kgs 13:1]]). He followed the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat and did evil in the LORD's sight, and so Israel suffered for a long time under Hazael and Benhadad, kings of Syria ([[@12013002-12013003|2 Kgs 13:2-3]]). When he pleaded with the LORD, the LORD listened and gave Israel a savior ([[@12013004-12013005|2 Kgs 13:4-5]]). He is a different person from Jehoahaz king of Judah.

column5: Son of Josiah who ruled Judah three months
column7: After King Josiah died at Megiddo, the people anointed his son Jehoahaz and made him king ([[@12023030|2 Kgs 23:30]]). He became king at twenty-three, reigned three months in Jerusalem, and did evil in the LORD's sight ([[@12023031-12023032|2 Kgs 23:31-32]]). Pharaoh Necoh imprisoned him at Riblah in the land of Hamath and made Josiah's other son Eliakim king under the name Jehoiakim, and Jehoahaz was taken to Egypt and died there ([[@12023033-12023034|2 Kgs 23:33-34]]). Under the name 'Shallum,' Jeremiah prophesied that he would never come back ([[@24022011-24022012|Jer 22:11-12]]).

column5: Sixth son of Meshelemiah the gatekeeper
column7: The sixth son of Meshelemiah the Korahite, he was among the divisions of the gatekeepers. The firstborn was Zechariah ([[@13026001-13026003|1 Chr 26:1-3]]).

column5: A captain over two hundred eighty thousand
column7: He was a captain of Judah’s army in King Jehoshaphat’s time, with two hundred eighty thousand men under him ([[@14017014-14017015|2 Chr 17:14-15]]; [[@14017019|2 Chr 17:19]]).

column5: Father of Ishmael, captain of hundreds
column7: He was the father of Ishmael, a captain of hundreds. Ishmael was one of the captains of hundreds who made a covenant with Jehoiada in the seventh year ([[@14023001|2 Chr 23:1]]).

column5: Son of Eliashib
column7: He was the son of Eliashib. Ezra went into his room and mourned over the trespass of the exiles, eating no bread and drinking no water ([[@15010006|Ezra 10:6]]).

column5: A descendant of Bebai who married a foreign wife
column7: A descendant of Bebai, he was on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010028|Ezra 10:28]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Son of Tobiah
column7: The son of Tobiah, he married the daughter of Meshullam the son of Berechiah. This was one reason many in Judah were sworn to Tobiah ([[@16006018|Neh 6:18]]).

column5: Priestly head of the family of Amariah
column7: In the days of Joiakim he was one of the heads of the priestly families, the head of the family of Amariah ([[@16012012-16012013|Neh 12:12-13]]).

column5: A man at the dedication of the wall
column7: He was present with Maaseiah, Shemaiah, and others at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem ([[@16012027|Neh 12:27]]; [[@16012042|Neh 12:42]]).

column5: King of Judah taken captive to Babylon
column7: He was the son of Jehoiakim; he became king at eighteen and reigned three months in Jerusalem ([[@12024008|2 Kgs 24:8]]). When Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon attacked Jerusalem, he went out with his mother and his officials and surrendered, and he was carried captive to Babylon ([[@12024012-12024015|2 Kgs 24:12-15]]). In the thirty-seventh year of his captivity, Evilmerodach king of Babylon released him from prison and let him eat before the king for the rest of his life ([[@12025027-12025029|2 Kgs 25:27-29]]). In the Bible he is also called Jeconiah and Coniah, and his name appears in Jesus' genealogy ([[@40001012|Matt 1:12]]).

column5: Father of Benaiah, David's mighty man
column7: He was the father of Benaiah, one of David's mighty men. In the Bible he usually appears only in the phrase "Benaiah the son of Jehoiada" ([[@10008018|2 Sam 8:18]]). His family was a family of valiant men from Kabzeel ([[@10023020|2 Sam 23:20]]). 1 Chronicles calls him "Jehoiada the chief priest" and so shows that he came from a priestly family ([[@13027005|1 Chr 27:5]]). He lived in David's time, long before the priest Jehoiada who made Joash king, and the two are different people.

column5: Priest who made young Joash king
column7: He was the priest when Athaliah killed the royal offspring and ruled Judah. His wife Jehoshabeath hid young Joash and saved his life ([[@14022011|2 Chr 22:11]]). In the seventh year Jehoiada made a covenant with the captains over hundreds, made Joash king, and had Athaliah put to death ([[@12011004-12011016|2 Kgs 11:4-16]]). Joash did what was right in the LORD's eyes as long as Jehoiada the priest instructed him ([[@12012002|2 Kgs 12:2]]). He died at one hundred thirty years old and was buried among the kings in the City of David ([[@14024015-14024016|2 Chr 24:15-16]]).

column5: Counselor after Ahithophel
column7: The son of Benaiah, he and Abiathar succeeded Ahithophel, who had been the king’s counselor ([[@13027033-13027034|1 Chr 27:33-34]]).

column5: Priest before Zephaniah
column7: He was the priest who served before Zephaniah. A letter sent by Shemaiah the Nehelamite said that the LORD had made Zephaniah the son of Maaseiah priest in place of Jehoiada, to be an officer in the LORD’s house ([[@24029024-24029026|Jer 29:24-26]]).

column5: Josiah's son, made king by the king of Egypt
column7: Jehoiakim was a son of Josiah, and his original name was Eliakim. Pharaoh Necoh, king of Egypt, made him king and changed his name to Jehoiakim ([[@12023034|2 Kgs 23:34]]). He became king at twenty-five and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem, but he did evil in the LORD's sight ([[@12023036-12023037|2 Kgs 23:36-37]]). He served Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon for three years and then rebelled ([[@12024001|2 Kgs 24:1]]). He was also the king who cut up the scroll of Jeremiah's prophecies with a knife and burned it in the fire ([[@24036023|Jer 36:23]]).

column5: Priest of the first division
column7: When the priests’ divisions were assigned by lot, he was the one chosen first. The one chosen second was Jedaiah ([[@13024007|1 Chr 24:7]]).

column5: A Levite sent out by Jehoshaphat
column7: He was one of the Levites King Jehoshaphat sent to the cities of Judah to teach the people from the book of the LORD’s law ([[@14017007-14017009|2 Chr 17:7-9]]).

column5: Priestly head of the family of Shemaiah
column7: In the days of Joiakim he was one of the heads of the priestly families, the head of the family of Shemaiah ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012018|Neh 12:18]]).

column5: Son of Jehoshaphat and king of Judah
column7: He was the eldest son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah; he became king at thirty-two and reigned eight years in Jerusalem. He married Ahab's daughter and did evil, for he "walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did Ahab’s house" ([[@12008016-12008018|2 Kgs 8:16-18]]). After taking the throne he killed his brothers with the sword ([[@14021004|2 Chr 21:4]]), and in his time Edom and Libnah revolted against Judah ([[@12008022|2 Kgs 8:22]]). In the end he died of a disease of the bowels; no one was sorry to see him go, and he was not buried in the tombs of the kings ([[@14021018-14021020|2 Chr 21:18-20]]).

column5: A priest sent out by Jehoshaphat
column7: He was a priest King Jehoshaphat sent with the Levites to the cities of Judah to teach the people ([[@14017007-14017009|2 Chr 17:7-9]]).

column5: Recorder under David and Solomon
column7: He was the son of Ahilud and became recorder in the time of King David ([[@10008016|2 Sam 8:16]]). He was also recorder in Solomon's time ([[@11004003|1 Kgs 4:3]]).

column5: Solomon’s officer over Issachar
column7: The son of Paruah, he was in charge of Issachar as one of the twelve officers Solomon appointed ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004017|1 Kgs 4:17]]).

column5: Asa's son, a good king of Judah
column7: He was the son of Asa and became king of Judah ([[@11015024|1 Kgs 15:24]]). He sent princes, Levites, and priests with the book of the LORD's law to go through the cities of Judah and teach the people ([[@14017007-14017009|2 Chr 17:7-9]]). He once went out to battle at Ramoth Gilead together with Ahab, king of Israel ([[@11022004|1 Kgs 22:4]]). When Moab and Ammon invaded, he fasted and prayed, and when the singers began to praise, the LORD defeated the enemy ([[@14020003|2 Chr 20:3]], 21-22).

column5: Father of King Jehu
column7: He was the son of Nimshi and the father of Jehu, who became king of Israel ([[@12009002|2 Kgs 9:2]]; [[@12009014|2 Kgs 9:14]]). He is a different person from Jehoshaphat king of Judah.

column5: Daughter of King Joram who hid Joash
column7: She was the daughter of King Joram and the sister of Ahaziah. When Athaliah destroyed all the royal offspring, she took Joash the son of Ahaziah away and hid him in a bedroom ([[@12011001-12011002|2 Kgs 11:1-2]]).

column5: A servant who killed King Joash
column7: He was the son of Shomer, one of the servants who struck down and killed Joash king of Judah ([[@12012021|2 Kgs 12:21]]). In 2 Chronicles he is called the son of Shimrith the Moabitess ([[@14024026|2 Chr 24:26]]).

column5: Second son of Obed-Edom
column7: The second son of Obed-Edom, he appears in the passage about the divisions of the gatekeepers ([[@13026001|1 Chr 26:1]]; [[@13026004|1 Chr 26:4]]).

column5: A commander of 180,000 under Jehoshaphat
column7: He was a commander who served King Jehoshaphat; listed after Eliada, he led one hundred eighty thousand men ready for war ([[@14017017-14017019|2 Chr 17:17-19]]).

column5: Father of Joshua the high priest
column7: He appears in the genealogy of the Levite priestly family as the son of Seraiah ([[@13006014|1 Chr 6:14]]). When the LORD carried Judah and Jerusalem away by the hand of Nebuchadnezzar, he too went into captivity ([[@13006015|1 Chr 6:15]]). His son Jeshua built the altar of God with Zerubbabel after the return from exile, and the book of Ezra writes his father's name as 'Jozadak' ([[@15003002|Ezra 3:2]]). The prophet Haggai called his son "Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest" ([[@37001001|Hag 1:1]]).

column5: The prophet who rebuked Baasha and Jehoshaphat
column7: He was a prophet, the son of Hanani, who rebuked Baasha king of Israel ([[@11016001-11016007|1 Kgs 16:1-7]]). He also rebuked Jehoshaphat king of Judah for helping the wicked ([[@14019002|2 Chr 19:2]]).

column5: The king of Israel who destroyed Ahab's house
column7: Jehu was the son of Jehoshaphat, the grandson of Nimshi. God told Elijah to anoint him king over Israel ([[@11019016|1 Kgs 19:16]]), and later a young man sent by Elisha poured oil on his head ([[@12009006|2 Kgs 9:6]]). He killed King Joram and Jezebel, destroyed the house of Ahab, and wiped out Baal from Israel ([[@12010028|2 Kgs 10:28]]). But he did not turn away from the sin of worshiping the golden calves at Bethel and Dan ([[@12010029|2 Kgs 10:29]]).

column5: A Simeonite family head
column7: The son of Joshibiah, he appears in the list of the leaders of Simeon’s descendants. In Hezekiah’s time they destroyed the Meunim and settled in their land ([[@13004035|1 Chr 4:35]]; [[@13004038|1 Chr 4:38]]; [[@13004041|1 Chr 4:41]]).

column5: An Anathothite who came to David at Ziklag
column7: An Anathothite, he was one of the warriors from the tribe of Benjamin who came to David and helped him in battle while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001-13012003|1 Chr 12:1-3]]).

column5: Son of Shemer, a descendant of Asher
column7: He was a son of Shemer, the son of Heber of Asher’s descendants, and his brothers were Ahi, Rohgah, and Aram ([[@13007032|1 Chr 7:32]]; [[@13007034|1 Chr 7:34]]).

column5: A man Zedekiah sent to Jeremiah
column7: He was the son of Shelemiah, whom King Zedekiah sent to Jeremiah to ask for prayer ([[@24037003|Jer 37:3]]). In chapter 38 he is called 'Jucal' ([[@24038001|Jer 38:1]]).

column5: A town of the tribe of Dan
column7: It was a town in the inheritance the tribe of Dan received by lot ([[@6019040|Josh 19:40]]; [[@6019045|Josh 19:45]]).

column5: The man who read Jeremiah’s scroll before the king
column7: He was the son of Nethaniah, whom the princes sent to Baruch to bring the scroll ([[@24036014|Jer 36:14]]). As he read it before the king, the king cut the scroll and threw it into the fire in the brazier ([[@24036021-24036023|Jer 36:21-23]]).

column5: Mother of Jered, Heber, and Jekuthiel
column7: She is the woman in the genealogy of Judah called "His wife the Jewess," who bore Jered the father of Gedor, Heber the father of Soco, and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah ([[@13004018|1 Chr 4:18]]).

column5: A descendant of Heman who cleansed the temple
column7: A descendant of Heman, he was a Levite who joined his brothers in cleansing the LORD’s house in Hezekiah’s time ([[@14029012|2 Chr 29:12]]; [[@14029014-14029015|2 Chr 29:14-15]]).

column5: A family head of the Reubenites
column7: He was among the brothers of Beerah, the prince of the Reubenites, and became a chief by their families and genealogy ([[@13005006-13005007|1 Chr 5:6-7]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men
column7: He appears in the list of David’s mighty men alongside Shama, the son of Hotham the Aroerite ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011044|1 Chr 11:44]]).

column5: A Levite musician and doorkeeper in David’s time
column7: He was one of the Levites appointed when David brought up the ark, and he is listed as a doorkeeper ([[@13015018|1 Chr 15:18]]). He was assigned to lead with a harp tuned to the eight-stringed lyre ([[@13015021|1 Chr 15:21]]).

column5: Great-grandfather of Jahaziel
column7: He was the great-grandfather of Jahaziel the Levite. In Jehoshaphat’s time the LORD’s Spirit came on this Jahaziel ([[@14020014|2 Chr 20:14]]).

column5: Scribe of Uzziah’s army
column7: He was a scribe in King Uzziah’s time who, with Maaseiah the officer, counted the number of the fighting men ([[@14026011|2 Chr 26:11]]).

column5: A Levite chief who gave Passover offerings
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the Levites, and in Josiah’s time he and the other chiefs gave Passover offerings to the Levites ([[@14035007|2 Chr 35:7]]; [[@14035009|2 Chr 35:9]]).

column5: A descendant of Nebo who married a foreign wife
column7: A descendant of Nebo, he was on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010043-15010044|Ezra 10:43-44]]).

column5: A place where people of Judah lived
column7: It was a place where some of the people of Judah lived with its villages in Nehemiah’s time, listed with Kiriath Arba and Dibon ([[@16011025|Neh 11:25]]).

column5: A descendant of Kohath, Hebron’s fourth son
column7: He was a grandson of Kohath son of Levi, and the fourth son of Hebron ([[@13023012|1 Chr 23:12]]; [[@13023019|1 Chr 23:19]]; [[@13024023|1 Chr 24:23]]).

column5: Son of Jeconiah the captive
column7: He was one of the sons of Jeconiah, who was taken captive, and his name is listed with Shealtiel, Malchiram, Pedaiah, and others ([[@13003017-13003018|1 Chr 3:17-18]]).

column5: Ancestor of Zanoah
column7: In the genealogy of Judah he was a son of the woman called "His wife the Jewess," and the father of Zanoah. His name is listed with Jered and Heber ([[@13004018|1 Chr 4:18]]).

column5: Job’s first daughter
column7: She was the first of the three daughters born to Job after the LORD blessed the latter part of his life ([[@18042012-18042014|Job 42:12-14]]).

column5: A son of Simeon
column7: He was a son of Simeon, Jacob's son ([[@1046010|Gen 46:10]]; [[@2006015|Exod 6:15]]). In Numbers and 1 Chronicles he appears as 'Nemuel' ([[@4026012|Num 26:12]]; [[@13004024|1 Chr 4:24]]).

column5: Gileadite judge who defeated Ammon
column7: He was a Gileadite and a mighty man of valor, but because he was the son of a prostitute, his brothers drove him out, and he lived in the land of Tob. When the children of Ammon attacked, the elders of Gilead brought him back and made him their head ([[@7011001-7011011|Judg 11:1-11]]). Before going to battle, he vowed that if he came back in peace, he would offer as a burnt offering whoever first came out of the door of his house to meet him, and it was his only child, his daughter, who came out dancing with tambourines ([[@7011030-7011035|Judg 11:30-35]]). He judged Israel for six years ([[@7012007|Judg 12:7]]), and Hebrews names him among the people of faith ([[@58011032|Heb 11:32]]).

column5: Kenizzite, father of Caleb
column7: He was the father of Caleb, the spy from the tribe of Judah, and he was a Kenizzite ([[@4013006|Num 13:6]]; [[@4032012|Num 32:12]]). In the Bible he almost always appears in the phrase 'Caleb the son of Jephunneh.' When ten spies spread a bad report, his son Caleb, together with Joshua, followed the LORD completely, and they were the only two of the wilderness generation to enter Canaan ([[@4014030|Num 14:30]]). Caleb later received Hebron as his inheritance ([[@6014014|Josh 14:14]]).

column5: Son of Jether, a descendant of Asher
column7: He was a son of Jether in the genealogy of Asher’s descendants, and his brothers were Pispa and Ara. This genealogy records the heads of Asher’s families ([[@13007038|1 Chr 7:38]]; [[@13007040|1 Chr 7:40]]).

column5: A descendant of Shem, son of Joktan
column7: He was one of the sons of Joktan, Eber’s son, a descendant of Shem ([[@1010025-1010026|Gen 10:25-26]]; [[@13001020|1 Chr 1:20]]).

column5: Firstborn of Hezron, a descendant of Judah
column7: He was the firstborn of Hezron, the grandson of Judah. His sons were Ram, Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah, and by another wife, Atarah, he had Onam ([[@13002025-13002026|1 Chr 2:25-26]]). His descendants, the Jerahmeelites, lived in the south of Judah, and David told Achish the Philistine king that he had raided the South of the Jerahmeelites ([[@9027010|1 Sam 27:10]]). Later, at Ziklag, David also sent some of the plunder recovered from the Amalekites to the cities of the Jerahmeelites ([[@9030026-9030029|1 Sam 30:26-29]]).

column5: A Levite, son of Kish
column7: He appears in the list of Levi’s descendants as the son of Kish. Kish was the son of Mahli, the son of Merari ([[@13023021|1 Chr 23:21]]; [[@13024020|1 Chr 24:20]]; [[@13024029|1 Chr 24:29]]).

column5: The king’s son ordered to arrest Jeremiah
column7: He was the king’s son, who was ordered by the king to arrest Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet, but the LORD hid them ([[@24036026|Jer 36:26]]).

column5: Ancestor of Gedor
column7: In the genealogy of Judah he was a son of the woman called "His wife the Jewess," and the father of Gedor. His name is listed with Heber and Jekuthiel ([[@13004018|1 Chr 4:18]]).

column5: A descendant of Hashum who married a foreign wife
column7: A descendant of Hashum, he was on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010033|Ezra 10:33]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Father of Hamutal, from Libnah
column7: He was from Libnah, the father of Hamutal, who was the mother of Jehoahaz and Zedekiah, kings of Judah ([[@12023031|2 Kgs 23:31]]; [[@12024018|2 Kgs 24:18]]). He is a different person from the prophet Jeremiah.

column5: A family head of the half-tribe of Manasseh
column7: He was a family head of the half-tribe of Manasseh, who spread out from Bashan to Mount Hermon, and he was a famous man of valor ([[@13005023-13005024|1 Chr 5:23-24]]).

column5: A warrior who came to David at Ziklag
column7: He was one of the warriors from the tribe of Benjamin who came to David and helped him in battle while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001-13012002|1 Chr 12:1-2]]; [[@13012004|1 Chr 12:4]]).

column5: Fifth of the Gadites who joined David
column7: He was the fifth of the Gadite warriors who joined David at the stronghold in the wilderness ([[@13012008|1 Chr 12:8]]; [[@13012010|1 Chr 12:10]]).

column5: Tenth of the Gadites who joined David
column7: He was the tenth of the Gadite warriors who joined David at the stronghold in the wilderness ([[@13012008|1 Chr 12:8]]; [[@13012013|1 Chr 12:13]]).

column5: A prophet in Judah's last days
column7: He was the son of Hilkiah, a priest from Anathoth in the land of Benjamin ([[@24001001|Jer 1:1]]). He composed a lament when King Josiah died ([[@14035025|2 Chr 35:25]]). He cried out that Judah would fall to Babylon if it did not repent, and for this he was even beaten and imprisoned ([[@24037015|Jer 37:15]]). Even so, he brought God's word of hope that he would "make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and with the house of Judah" ([[@24031031|Jer 31:31]]).

column5: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the priests who returned from exile with Zerubbabel and Jeshua ([[@16012001|Neh 12:1]]). In Joiakim's time the head of Jeremiah's family was Hananiah ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]).

column5: Father of Jaazaniah the Rechabite
column7: He was the son of Habazziniah and the father of Jaazaniah. The prophet Jeremiah brought this Jaazaniah and the whole house of the Rechabites into the LORD’s house ([[@24035003-24035004|Jer 35:3-4]]).

column5: Son of Becher, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He was one of the sons of Becher the son of Benjamin, and his brothers included Zemirah, Joash, and Eliezer ([[@13007006|1 Chr 7:6]]; [[@13007008|1 Chr 7:8]]).

column5: Son of Beriah, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants as a son of Beriah. Beriah was a family head of the inhabitants of Aijalon who drove out the inhabitants of Gath ([[@13008013-13008014|1 Chr 8:13-14]]; [[@13008016|1 Chr 8:16]]).

column5: A descendant of Elam who married a foreign wife
column7: A descendant of Elam, he was on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010026|Ezra 10:26]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Zattu who married a foreign wife
column7: A descendant of Zattu, he was on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010027|Ezra 10:27]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: A descendant of Bani, he was on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010029|Ezra 10:29]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Kohath, Hebron’s firstborn
column7: He was a grandson of Kohath son of Levi, Hebron’s firstborn and the chief ([[@13023012|1 Chr 23:12]]; [[@13023019|1 Chr 23:19]]; [[@13024023|1 Chr 24:23]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men
column7: He appears in the list of David’s mighty men as "Jeribai, and Joshaviah, the sons of Elnaam" ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011046|1 Chr 11:46]]).

column5: The first Canaanite city Israel brought down
column7: It was a city west of the Jordan River, across from the plains of Moab. It was also called 'the city of palm trees' ([[@5034003|Deut 34:3]]). Rahab the prostitute hid the spies Joshua sent ([[@6002001|Josh 2:1]]). When the people of Israel heard the trumpet and gave a great shout, the wall fell down ([[@6006020|Josh 6:20]]). Jesus, too, passed through Jericho and met Zacchaeus, a chief tax collector ([[@42019001-42019002|Luke 19:1-2]]).

column5: Son of Tola, a descendant of Issachar
column7: He was a son of Tola the son of Issachar, and his brothers included Uzzi, Rephaiah, and Jahmai. They were heads of their father Tola’s house and mighty men of valor ([[@13007001-13007002|1 Chr 7:1-2]]).

column5: Chief of the Hebronites
column7: He was the chief of the Hebronites. In the fortieth year of David’s reign, mighty men of valor were found among his clan at Jazer of Gilead ([[@13026031|1 Chr 26:31]]).

column5: Son of Bela, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He was a son of Bela the son of Benjamin, a head of his family and a mighty man of valor. His brothers were Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, and Iri ([[@13007006-13007007|1 Chr 7:6-7]]).

column5: A warrior who came to David at Ziklag
column7: He was one of the warriors from the tribe of Benjamin who came to David and helped him in battle while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001-13012002|1 Chr 12:1-2]]; [[@13012005|1 Chr 12:5]]).

column5: A descendant of Merari, son of Mushi
column7: He was one of the three sons of Mushi, Merari’s son, and is called Jeremoth there ([[@13023023|1 Chr 23:23]]). In chapter 24 he is called 'Jerimoth' ([[@13024030|1 Chr 24:30]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a temple singer
column7: He was one of the sons of Heman, who served in song in David’s day ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]). He is the 'Jeremoth' to whom the fifteenth lot fell ([[@13025022|1 Chr 25:22]]).

column5: Officer over the tribe of Naphtali
column7: The son of Azriel, he was the officer over the tribe of Naphtali among those who ruled the tribes of Israel ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027019|1 Chr 27:19]]).

column5: Son of David, father of Mahalath
column7: He was a son of David, and his daughter Mahalath became Rehoboam’s wife. Mahalath’s mother was Abihail the daughter of Eliab ([[@14011018|2 Chr 11:18]]).

column5: He looked after offerings under Hezekiah
column7: In King Hezekiah’s time he was in charge of looking after the offerings brought to God’s house, under Conaniah the Levite and his brother Shimei ([[@14031012-14031013|2 Chr 31:12-13]]).

column5: A woman who bore Caleb sons
column7: She was a woman by whom Caleb the son of Hezron had children, and her name is listed with his wife Azubah ([[@13002018|1 Chr 2:18]]).

column5: The first king of northern Israel
column7: He was the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite, and a servant of Solomon ([[@11011026|1 Kgs 11:26]]). The prophet Ahijah told him God's word that God would give him ten tribes ([[@11011031|1 Kgs 11:31]]). After Solomon died, he became king of northern Israel ([[@11012020|1 Kgs 12:20]]). But to keep the people from going up to Jerusalem, he made two golden calves and set them in Bethel and Dan, and this became the sin that later kings followed ([[@11012028-11012029|1 Kgs 12:28-29]]).

column5: Son of Joash and king of northern Israel
column7: He was the son of Joash king of Israel, often called Jeroboam II to tell him apart from Jeroboam the son of Nebat. He reigned forty-one years in Samaria, but he did evil in the LORD's sight and did not turn from the sins of the earlier Jeroboam ([[@12014023-12014024|2 Kgs 14:23-24]]). Even so, as the prophet Jonah had said, God used him to restore Israel's border from the entrance of Hamath to the sea of the Arabah ([[@12014025|2 Kgs 14:25]]). The prophets Amos and Hosea spoke God's word in his time ([[@30001001|Amos 1:1]]; [[@28001001|Hos 1:1]]).

column5: Grandfather of Samuel
column7: He was the father of Elkanah the Ephraimite ([[@9001001|1 Sam 1:1]]). The genealogy in 1 Chronicles reads "the son of Elkanah, the son of Jeroham" ([[@13006034|1 Chr 6:34]]).

column5: Father of Jaareshiah and others
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants as the father of Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]; [[@13008027|1 Chr 8:27]]).

column5: Father of Ibneiah
column7: He was the father of Ibneiah, one of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem. This list records those who lived in Jerusalem ([[@13009003|1 Chr 9:3]]; [[@13009007-13009008|1 Chr 9:7-8]]).

column5: Father of Adaiah the priest
column7: He was the father of Adaiah, a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the exile. His line goes back to Pashhur and Malchijah ([[@13009012|1 Chr 9:12]]; [[@16011012|Neh 11:12]]).

column5: Father of Joelah and Zebadiah
column7: Of Gedor, he was the father of Joelah and Zebadiah, who came to David at Ziklag and helped him in battle ([[@13012001|1 Chr 12:1]]; [[@13012007|1 Chr 12:7]]).

column5: Father of Azarel, officer over Dan
column7: He was the father of Azarel, the officer over the tribe of Dan. Azarel was one of those who ruled the tribes of Israel ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027022|1 Chr 27:22]]).

column5: Father of Azariah, captain of hundreds
column7: He was the father of Azariah, a captain of hundreds. Azariah was one of the captains of hundreds who made a covenant with Jehoiada in the seventh year ([[@14023001|2 Chr 23:1]]).

column5: The wilderness where Jehoshaphat met the enemy
column7: When Moab and the people of Ammon came to attack Jehoshaphat, this is where Jahaziel said they would find the enemy "at the end of the valley, before the wilderness of Jeruel" ([[@14020001|2 Chr 20:1]]; [[@14020016|2 Chr 20:16]]).

column5: The holy city David made his capital
column7: This city became the capital of Israel. Many people think it is the Salem that Melchizedek ruled ([[@1014018|Gen 14:18]]). The Jebusites originally lived there, and it is recorded that "David took the stronghold of Zion. This is David’s city" ([[@10005007|2 Sam 5:7]]). Solomon built the temple here and brought the ark of the covenant into it ([[@11008001|1 Kgs 8:1]]). The Psalms sing, "Pray for the peace of Jerusalem" ([[@19122006|Ps 122:6]]).

column5: Wives and concubines David took in Jerusalem
column7: These were the additional wives and concubines David took in Jerusalem after he came from Hebron. More sons and daughters were born to him by them ([[@10005013|2 Sam 5:13]]).

column5: Mother of Jotham, king of Judah
column7: She was the mother of Jotham king of Judah, Uzziah’s son, and the daughter of Zadok ([[@12015032-12015033|2 Kgs 15:32-33]]; [[@14027001|2 Chr 27:1]]).

column5: Son of Hananiah
column7: He was a son of Hananiah, the son of Zerubbabel, in the genealogy of David’s descendants, and his brother was Pelatiah ([[@13003019|1 Chr 3:19]]; [[@13003021|1 Chr 3:21]]).

column5: Son of Jeduthun, a temple singer
column7: He was a son of Jeduthun and gave thanks and praised the LORD with the harp ([[@13025003|1 Chr 25:3]]). The eighth lot fell to him, and he served with his sons and brothers, twelve in all ([[@13025015|1 Chr 25:15]]).

column5: A descendant of Elam who came with Ezra
column7: The son of Athaliah, a descendant of Elam, he came up from Babylon with Ezra along with seventy men ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008007|Ezra 8:7]]).

column5: A Merarite who came to Ezra
column7: He was a descendant of Merari brought from Casiphia to serve in the house of God, and he came with Hashabiah along with twenty of his brothers and their sons ([[@15008017-15008019|Ezra 8:17-19]]).

column5: Ancestor of Sallu, a Benjamite
column7: He was an ancestor of Sallu, one of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem; Sallu was his descendant seven generations later ([[@16011004|Neh 11:4]]; [[@16011007|Neh 11:7]]).

column5: A town taken by Abijah
column7: It was a town that Abijah king of Judah took when he pursued Jeroboam, and it was taken along with Bethel and Ephron, together with their villages ([[@14013001|2 Chr 13:1]]; [[@14013019|2 Chr 13:19]]).

column5: Priest of the fourteenth division
column7: When the priests’ divisions were assigned by lot, he was the one chosen fourteenth ([[@13024007|1 Chr 24:7]]; [[@13024013|1 Chr 24:13]]).

column5: Son of Caleb
column7: He was one of the sons born to Caleb the son of Hezron, and his brothers were Shobab and Ardon ([[@13002018|1 Chr 2:18]]).

column5: The desert north of the hill of Hachilah in Ziph
column7: The hill of Hachilah and the wilderness of Maon, David's hiding places that the Ziphites reported to Saul, lay south of this desert ([[@9023019|1 Sam 23:19]]; [[@9023024|1 Sam 23:24]]). In these verses the place name is translated simply as 'the desert'.

column5: An ancestor in the genealogy of Gad
column7: He was an ancestor of Abihail, a descendant of Gad who lived in Bashan, and he was the son of Jahdo ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005014|1 Chr 5:14]]).

column5: A Simeonite family head
column7: He appears in the list of the leaders of Simeon’s descendants. In Hezekiah’s time they destroyed the Meunim and settled in their land ([[@13004036|1 Chr 4:36]]; [[@13004038|1 Chr 4:38]]; [[@13004041|1 Chr 4:41]]).

column5: The ninth priestly division
column7: It was the ninth of the priestly divisions chosen by lot in David's time ([[@13024011|1 Chr 24:11]]). The 'children of Jedaiah, of the house of Jeshua' who returned from exile numbered nine hundred seventy-three ([[@15002036|Ezra 2:36]]).

column5: He served in the priests’ cities
column7: In Hezekiah’s time he served under Kore in the cities of the priests, in charge of distributing to his brothers by their divisions ([[@14031014-14031015|2 Chr 31:14-15]]).

column5: A branch of the family of Pahathmoab
column7: He is the Jeshua in 'the children of Pahathmoab, of the children of Jeshua and Joab', who came back from exile ([[@15002006|Ezra 2:6]]; [[@16007011|Neh 7:11]]).

column5: A leading Levite among those who returned from exile
column7: He was one of the leaders of the Levites who returned from exile in Babylon. The children of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the children of Hodaviah, numbered seventy-four ([[@15002040|Ezra 2:40]]). When work on the temple began, Jeshua, with his sons and brothers, oversaw the workmen in God's house ([[@15003009|Ezra 3:9]]). When Ezra read the book of the law, he helped the people understand the law ([[@16008007|Neh 8:7]]), and he stood on the stairs, cried out loudly to the LORD, and called the people to bless God ([[@16009004-16009005|Neh 9:4-5]]). He is a different person from Jeshua the high priest, the son of Jozadak.

column5: Father of Jozabad the Levite
column7: He was the father of Jozabad the Levite. Jozabad was present when the silver, the gold, and the vessels were weighed in the house of God in Ezra’s time ([[@15008033|Ezra 8:33]]).

column5: Father of Ezer, who repaired the wall
column7: He was the father of Ezer. His son Ezer repaired a section of the wall across from the armory at the turning of the wall ([[@16003019|Neh 3:19]]).

column5: A place where people of Judah lived
column7: It was one of the places where the people of Judah lived in Nehemiah’s time, listed with Moladah and Beth Pelet ([[@16011025-16011026|Neh 11:25-26]]).

column5: Son of Kadmiel, a chief of the Levites
column7: The son of Kadmiel, he was a chief of the Levites. He praised the Lord section by section, according to the commandment of David the man of God ([[@16012024|Neh 12:24]]).

column5: A Simeonite family head
column7: He appears in the list of the leaders of Simeon’s descendants. In Hezekiah’s time they destroyed the Meunim and settled in their land ([[@13004036|1 Chr 4:36]]; [[@13004038|1 Chr 4:38]]; [[@13004041|1 Chr 4:41]]).

column5: The father of King David
column7: Jesse was a man of Bethlehem, the son of Obed, who was the son of Ruth and Boaz ([[@8004017|Ruth 4:17]]). God sent Samuel to his house to choose a king from among his sons ([[@9016001|1 Sam 16:1]]), and David, the youngest of his eight sons, was anointed ([[@9016013|1 Sam 16:13]]). Isaiah prophesied the Messiah who would come from David's family, saying, "A shoot will come out of the stock of Jesse" ([[@23011001|Isa 11:1]]).

column5: The Son of God, Savior of the world
column7: He is the Savior who came to this earth as the Son of God. The angel announced, "You shall name him Jesus, for it is he who shall save his people from their sins" ([[@40001021|Matt 1:21]]). Jesus was born in Bethlehem, the town of David, and went about all Galilee preaching the Good News of the Kingdom and healing the sick ([[@40004023|Matt 4:23]]). He died on the cross for our sins and rose again on the third day ([[@46015003-46015004|1 Cor 15:3-4]]). Peter proclaimed that God has made this Jesus "both Lord and Christ" ([[@44002036|Acts 2:36]]).

column5: Gideon’s firstborn son
column7: He was Gideon’s firstborn son; he was told to kill Zebah and Zalmunna, but because he was still young, he was afraid and did not draw his sword ([[@7008020-7008021|Judg 8:20-21]]).

column5: Father of Amasa
column7: He was an Ishmaelite, the father of Amasa, who was born to Abigail, David's sister ([[@13002016-13002017|1 Chr 2:16-17]]; [[@11002005|1 Kgs 2:5]]). In 2 Samuel he appears as 'Ithra' ([[@10017025|2 Sam 17:25]]).

column5: Son of Ezrah, in Judah’s genealogy
column7: He was a son of Ezrah in the genealogy of Judah’s descendants, and his brothers were Mered, Epher, and Jalon ([[@13004001|1 Chr 4:1]]; [[@13004017|1 Chr 4:17]]).

column5: A chief of Edom descended from Esau
column7: He was one of the chiefs of Edom descended from Esau, listed after chiefs Timna and Alvah ([[@1036040|Gen 36:40]]; [[@13001051|1 Chr 1:51]]).

column5: Moses' father-in-law, priest of Midian
column7: A priest of Midian, he was Moses' father-in-law. While keeping the flock of his father-in-law Jethro, Moses came to Horeb, the mountain of God ([[@2003001|Exod 3:1]]). After Israel came out of Egypt, Jethro brought Moses' wife Zipporah and their two sons to Moses where he was camped at the mountain of God ([[@2018002-2018005|Exod 18:2-5]]). When he heard from Moses what the LORD had done, he confessed, "Now I know that the LORD is greater than all gods", and offered a burnt offering to God ([[@2018011-2018012|Exod 18:11-12]]). Seeing Moses judge the people alone, he also advised him to appoint rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties, and tens, and Moses did as he said ([[@2018021-2018024|Exod 18:21-24]]).

column5: Son of Ishmael
column7: He was one of the sons of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, a brother of Hadad, Tema, and Naphish ([[@1025013-1025015|Gen 25:13-15]]; [[@13001031|1 Chr 1:31]]).

column5: A people fought by Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh
column7: The sons of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh made war with the Hagrites, Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab ([[@13005018-13005019|1 Chr 5:18-19]]).

column5: A descendant of Zerah who lived in Jerusalem
column7: A descendant of Zerah, he lived in Jerusalem with six hundred ninety of his brothers ([[@13009003|1 Chr 9:3]]; [[@13009006|1 Chr 9:6]]).

column5: A descendant of Elizaphan who cleansed the temple
column7: A descendant of Elizaphan, he was one of the Levites who cleansed the LORD’s house in Hezekiah’s time ([[@14029012-14029013|2 Chr 29:12-13]]; [[@14029015|2 Chr 29:15]]).

column5: A descendant of Adonikam who came with Ezra
column7: He was among the last of the descendants of Adonikam, and he came up from Babylon with Ezra along with sixty men ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008013|Ezra 8:13]]).

column5: Son of Esau and Oholibamah
column7: He was the son born to Esau's wife Oholibamah in the land of Canaan ([[@1036005|Gen 36:5]]). He later became a chief of Edom ([[@1036018|Gen 36:18]]).

column5: Son of Bilhan, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He was a grandson of Jediael the son of Benjamin and a son of Bilhan, and his brothers included Ehud and Chenaanah ([[@13007006|1 Chr 7:6]]; [[@13007010|1 Chr 7:10]]).

column5: Second son of Eshek
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants as the second son of Eshek. The firstborn was Ulam and the third was Eliphelet ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]; [[@13008039|1 Chr 8:39]]).

column5: A descendant of Gershon, son of Shimei
column7: He was one of the sons of Shimei ([[@13023010|1 Chr 23:10]]). Because he did not have many sons, he was counted as one family together with Beriah ([[@13023011|1 Chr 23:11]]).

column5: Son of Rehoboam and Mahalath
column7: He was a son Rehoboam had by Mahalath, the daughter of David’s son Jerimoth, and his brothers were Shemariah and Zaham ([[@14011018-14011019|2 Chr 11:18-19]]).

column5: Son of Shaharaim and Hodesh
column7: He was a son Shaharaim had by his wife Hodesh in the land of Moab, and he was a family head ([[@13008008-13008010|1 Chr 8:8-10]]).

column5: An army captain who came to Gedaliah
column7: He was one of the army captains who went to Mizpah and came to Gedaliah after Jerusalem fell, the son of the Maacathite ([[@24040008|Jer 40:8]]). In 2 Kings he appears as 'Jaazaniah' ([[@12025023|2 Kgs 25:23]]).

column5: Ahab's queen who spread Baal worship
column7: She was the daughter of Ethbaal king of the Sidonians; she became the wife of Ahab king of Israel, and Ahab came to serve Baal ([[@11016031|1 Kgs 16:31]]). Jezebel killed the LORD's prophets, and after the events on Mount Carmel she threatened to take Elijah's life ([[@11018004|1 Kgs 18:4]]; [[@11019002|1 Kgs 19:2]]). She also set up false witnesses to have Naboth killed so she could take his vineyard. In the end, in Jehu's time, she was thrown down from a window and died, and as Elijah had said, the dogs ate her flesh ([[@12009033-12009036|2 Kgs 9:33-36]]).

column5: Son of Naphtali
column7: He was a son of Naphtali, Jacob’s son ([[@1046024|Gen 46:24]]). The family of the Jezerites came from him ([[@4026049|Num 26:49]]).

column5: A warrior who came to David at Ziklag
column7: The son of Azmaveth, he was one of the warriors from the tribe of Benjamin who came to David and helped him in battle while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001-13012003|1 Chr 12:1-3]]).

column5: Overseer of the singers at the wall’s dedication
column7: He was the overseer of the singers who sang loudly at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem ([[@16012027|Neh 12:27]]; [[@16012042|Neh 12:42]]).

column5: Hometown of Ahinoam, David's wife
column7: It was a town in the hill country of Judah ([[@6015056|Josh 15:56]]). David's wife Ahinoam was called 'the Jezreelitess,' and many scholars think she came from this Jezreel in Judah ([[@9025043|1 Sam 25:43]]; [[@9027003|1 Sam 27:3]]). Ahinoam was taken captive by the Amalekites along with Abigail ([[@9030005|1 Sam 30:5]]), but David pursued them and rescued his two wives ([[@9030018|1 Sam 30:18]]). It is a different place from the town of the same name in the Valley of Jezreel to the north.

column5: A town in Issachar, site of Ahab's palace
column7: Jezreel was a town given to the tribe of Issachar ([[@6019018|Josh 19:18]]). The palace of Ahab, king of northern Israel, was here, and Naboth's vineyard was next to it ([[@11021001|1 Kgs 21:1]]). After praying for rain on Mount Carmel, Elijah tucked his cloak into his belt and ran ahead of Ahab all the way to Jezreel ([[@11018046|1 Kgs 18:46]]). Later Jehu came here and had Jezebel, who was looking out of a window, thrown down ([[@12009030-12009033|2 Kgs 9:30-33]]). There was also a town of the same name in the hill country of Judah, and many scholars think David's wife Ahinoam came from there.

column5: Where news came of Saul and Jonathan’s death
column7: This is the place from which the news of Saul and Jonathan’s death came. At that time Mephibosheth, who was five years old, fell as his nurse fled with him and became lame ([[@10004004|2 Sam 4:4]]).

column5: A man in Judah’s genealogy, son of the father of Etam
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah’s descendants as one of the sons of the father of Etam ([[@13004001|1 Chr 4:1]]; [[@13004003|1 Chr 4:3]]).

column5: A northern valley where Midian camped
column7: The Canaanites living here had chariots of iron ([[@6017016|Josh 17:16]]). In Gideon’s day the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the children of the east crossed the Jordan and camped in this valley ([[@7006033|Judg 6:33]]).

column5: Son of Nahor and Milcah
column7: He was one of the eight sons that Nahor, Abraham’s brother, had by his wife Milcah ([[@1022022-1022023|Gen 22:22-23]]).

column5: David's nephew and army commander
column7: He was the son of Zeruiah, David's sister, and a brother of Abishai and Asahel ([[@13002016|1 Chr 2:16]]). Throughout David's reign he was commander of the army and led many battles ([[@10008016|2 Sam 8:16]]). But he deceived and killed Abner to avenge his brother ([[@10003027|2 Sam 3:27]]), and against the king's request he also killed Absalom ([[@10018014|2 Sam 18:14]]). In Solomon's time he was put to death by Benaiah.

column5: Son of Seraiah, father of Ge Harashim
column7: He was the son of Seraiah the son of Kenaz, and the father of Ge Harashim. His descendants were craftsmen ([[@13004013-13004014|1 Chr 4:13-14]]).

column5: A branch of the family of Pahathmoab
column7: He is the Joab in 'the children of Pahathmoab, of the children of Jeshua and Joab', who came back from exile ([[@15002006|Ezra 2:6]]; [[@16007011|Neh 7:11]]). He is a different person from Joab, David’s army commander.

column5: Ancestor of a family who came with Ezra
column7: From the descendants of Joab, Obadiah the son of Jehiel came up from Babylon with Ezra along with two hundred eighteen men ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008009|Ezra 8:9]]).

column5: Recorder under King Hezekiah, son of Asaph
column7: He was the son of Asaph, the recorder who kept the records of the kingdom under King Hezekiah. When the Rabshakeh, sent by the king of Assyria, came against Jerusalem, Joah went out to meet him with Eliakim, who was over the palace, and Shebnah the scribe ([[@12018017-12018018|2 Kgs 18:17-18]]). They asked him to speak in Aramaic so that the people on the wall would not understand, but the Rabshakeh only threatened them more loudly ([[@12018026-12018028|2 Kgs 18:26-28]]). The three men tore their clothes, went to Hezekiah, and told him the Rabshakeh's words ([[@12018037|2 Kgs 18:37]]; [[@23036022|Isa 36:22]]).

column5: A descendant of Gershom, son of Zimmah
column7: In the genealogy of Gershom, Levi’s son, he appears as the son of Zimmah, and his son was Iddo ([[@13006020-13006021|1 Chr 6:20-21]]).

column5: Third son of Obed-Edom
column7: The third son of Obed-Edom, he appears in the passage about the divisions of the gatekeepers ([[@13026001|1 Chr 26:1]]; [[@13026004|1 Chr 26:4]]).

column5: Sent by Josiah to repair the temple
column7: The son of Joahaz, he was sent by Josiah with Shaphan and Maaseiah to repair the LORD’s house ([[@14034008|2 Chr 34:8]]).

column5: Father of Joah, whom Josiah sent
column7: He was the father of Joah. In the eighteenth year of his reign, Josiah sent Joah to repair the LORD’s house ([[@14034008|2 Chr 34:8]]).

column5: An ancestor of Jesus in Luke’s genealogy
column7: He is an ancestor in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus, the son of Rhesa. Above Rhesa come Zerubbabel and Shealtiel ([[@42003027|Luke 3:27]]).

column5: A woman who served Jesus, wife of Chuzas
column7: She was the wife of Chuzas, Herod’s steward, and she served Jesus and his followers from her own possessions ([[@42008003|Luke 8:3]]). She was one of the women who told the apostles the news of Jesus’ resurrection ([[@42024010|Luke 24:10]]).

column5: Gideon's father, an Abiezrite
column7: He was an Abiezrite and the father of the judge Gideon. When the angel of the LORD sat under the oak at Ophrah that belonged to Joash, his son Gideon was threshing wheat in the winepress ([[@7006011|Judg 6:11]]). When Gideon tore down Baal's altar, the men of the town demanded that he hand over his son, but Joash protected him, saying, "If he is a god, let him contend for himself" ([[@7006030-7006031|Judg 6:30-31]]). Gideon died at a good old age and was buried in the tomb of his father Joash ([[@7008032|Judg 8:32]]).

column5: A king’s son in charge of Micaiah under Ahab
column7: He was 'Joash the king’s son', to whom the king of Israel had the prophet Micaiah taken ([[@11022026|1 Kgs 22:26]]; [[@14018025|2 Chr 18:25]]).

column5: King of Judah who was crowned at seven
column7: He was the son of Ahaziah king of Judah. When Athaliah was killing the princes, his aunt Jehosheba secretly took him away and hid him, saving his life ([[@12011002|2 Kgs 11:2]]). At seven he became king with the help of Jehoiada the priest and reigned forty years in Jerusalem ([[@14024001|2 Chr 24:1]]). As long as Jehoiada lived, he did what was right in the LORD's eyes and set out to repair the temple ([[@14024002-14024005|2 Chr 24:2-5]]). But after Jehoiada died he served idols, and when Jehoiada's son Zechariah rebuked him for it, he had him stoned to death in the temple court ([[@14024017-14024022|2 Chr 24:17-22]]).

column5: Son of Jehoahaz and king of Israel
column7: He was the son of Jehoahaz king of Israel and reigned sixteen years in Samaria ([[@12013010|2 Kgs 13:10]]). He did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam, but when Elisha fell sick with the illness he would die of, Joash went to him and wept, saying, "My father, my father, the chariots of Israel and its horsemen!" ([[@12013014|2 Kgs 13:14]]).
