At Elisha's word he struck the ground with the arrows only three times, and just as Elisha said, he defeated Ben Hadad three times and won back the towns his father had lost ([[@12013018-12013019|2 Kgs 13:18-19]], 25). He fought Amaziah king of Judah, captured him at Beth Shemesh, and broke down the wall of Jerusalem ([[@12014013|2 Kgs 14:13]]).

column5: A descendant of Shelah son of Judah
column7: He was one of the descendants of Shelah the son of Judah, a name recorded from ancient records ([[@13004021-13004022|1 Chr 4:21-22]]).

column5: Son of Becher, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He was one of the sons of Becher the son of Benjamin, and his brothers included Zemirah, Eliezer, and Jeremoth ([[@13007006|1 Chr 7:6]]; [[@13007008|1 Chr 7:8]]).

column5: A warrior who came to David at Ziklag
column7: The son of Shemaah the Gibeathite, he was next after Ahiezer among the warriors from the tribe of Benjamin who came to David and helped him in battle while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001-13012003|1 Chr 12:1-3]]).

column5: Keeper of David’s oil storehouses
column7: He was in charge of the cellars of oil among King David’s property. At the same time Baal Hanan was in charge of the olive trees and sycamore trees in the lowland ([[@13027028|1 Chr 27:28]]; [[@13027031|1 Chr 27:31]]).

column5: A man who kept his faith through great suffering
column7: Job was a man who lived in the land of Uz, and he "was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil" ([[@18001001|Job 1:1]]). Through Satan's testing he lost his wealth and his children all at once, yet he fell to the ground and blessed the name of the LORD ([[@18001021|Job 1:21]]). After painful sores broke out on his body and he had a long debate with his friends, he heard God speak, and God restored his fortunes and gave him twice as much as before ([[@18042010|Job 42:10]]). James tells us to remember Job's perseverance and the outcome the Lord gave him ([[@59005011|Jas 5:11]]).

column5: A descendant of Shem, son of Joktan
column7: He was one of the sons of Joktan, Eber’s son, a brother of Ophir and Havilah ([[@1010029|Gen 10:29]]; [[@13001023|1 Chr 1:23]]).

column5: Son of Zerah of Bozrah, a king of Edom
column7: He was the son of Zerah of Bozrah and became king of Edom after Bela ([[@1036033|Gen 36:33]]; [[@13001044|1 Chr 1:44]]).

column5: King of Madon who fought Joshua
column7: He was king of Madon, one of the kings who camped with Jabin king of Hazor at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel ([[@6011001|Josh 11:1]]; [[@6011005|Josh 11:5]]).

column5: Son of Shaharaim and Hodesh
column7: He was a son Shaharaim had by his wife Hodesh in the land of Moab, and his brothers were Zibia, Mesha, and Malcam ([[@13008008-13008009|1 Chr 8:8-9]]).

column5: Son of Elpaal, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants, recorded as a son of Elpaal along with Ishmerai and Izliah ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]; [[@13008018|1 Chr 8:18]]).

column5: Mother of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
column7: She was a daughter of Levi who became the wife of Amram and bore Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam ([[@2006020|Exod 6:20]]; [[@4026059|Num 26:59]]).

column5: A man in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus. He is listed as the father of Joseph and the son of Joanan ([[@42003026-42003027|Luke 3:26-27]]).

column5: Ancestor of Sallu, a Benjamite in Jerusalem
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Sallu, a descendant of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile. Sallu was the son of Meshullam and the grandson of Joed ([[@16011007|Neh 11:7]]).

column5: Samuel's firstborn son
column7: He was Samuel's firstborn son and became a judge in Beersheba along with his younger brother Abijah ([[@9008002|1 Sam 8:2]]). But he did not walk in his father's ways; he took bribes and perverted justice ([[@9008003|1 Sam 8:3]]).

column5: A family head of the Simeonites
column7: His name is in the genealogy of Simeon’s descendants, and everyone on this list was a prince in his family ([[@13004035|1 Chr 4:35]]; [[@13004038|1 Chr 4:38]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Reuben
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Reuben’s descendants. His son was Shemaiah, followed by Gog and Shimei ([[@13005003-13005004|1 Chr 5:3-4]]).

column5: Great-grandfather of Bela, who lived in Aroer
column7: A descendant of Reuben, he was the great-grandfather of Bela, who lived in Aroer and as far as Nebo and Baal Meon. Bela was the son of Azaz and the grandson of Shema ([[@13005008|1 Chr 5:8]]).

column5: A Gadite chief in Bashan
column7: He was the chief of the descendants of Gad, who lived in the land of Bashan beside the Reubenites. Next to him was Shapham ([[@13005011-13005012|1 Chr 5:11-12]]).

column5: Son of Izrahiah, a descendant of Issachar
column7: He was a grandson of Uzzi of Issachar’s descendants and a son of Izrahiah. Along with Michael, Obadiah, and Isshiah, all of them were chief men ([[@13007003|1 Chr 7:3]]).

column5: Brother of Nathan, one of David’s mighty men
column7: The brother of Nathan, he appears in the list of David’s mighty men. His name is listed with Mibhar the son of Hagri ([[@13011038|1 Chr 11:38]]).

column5: A chief of the sons of Gershom in David’s time
column7: When David brought up the ark, he was the chief of the sons of Gershom, with one hundred thirty of his brothers ([[@13015007|1 Chr 15:7]]). David called him to bring up the ark ([[@13015011-13015012|1 Chr 15:11-12]]).

column5: A descendant of Gershon, son of Ladan
column7: He was one of the sons of Ladan, a descendant of Gershon ([[@13023008|1 Chr 23:8]]). Zetham son of Jehieli and Joel his brother were over the treasures of the LORD’s house, and some think this is the same man ([[@13026022|1 Chr 26:22]]).

column5: Officer over the half-tribe of Manasseh
column7: He was one of the officers over the tribes of Israel in David’s time; the son of Pedaiah, he was the officer over the half-tribe of Manasseh ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027020|1 Chr 27:20]]).

column5: A Levite who cleansed the temple under Hezekiah
column7: He was a Levite, the son of Azariah of the Kohathites. In King Hezekiah’s time he arose with the other Levites and cleansed the LORD’s house ([[@14029012|2 Chr 29:12]]; [[@14029015|2 Chr 29:15]]).

column5: A descendant of Nebo who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a descendant of Nebo on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010043-15010044|Ezra 10:43-44]]).

column5: Overseer of the Benjamites in Jerusalem
column7: The son of Zichri, he was the overseer of the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile ([[@16011007|Neh 11:7]]; [[@16011009|Neh 11:9]]).

column5: The prophet who wrote the book of Joel
column7: He was the son of Pethuel, a prophet who received the LORD’s word ([[@29001001|Joel 1:1]]). At Pentecost, Peter said that what happened that day was what had been spoken through the prophet Joel ([[@44002016-44002017|Acts 2:16-17]]).

column5: A warrior who came to David at Ziklag
column7: He was a son of Jeroham of Gedor. He was one of the warriors who came to help David while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001|1 Chr 12:1]]; [[@13012007|1 Chr 12:7]]).

column5: A Korahite who came to David at Ziklag
column7: A Korahite, he was one of the warriors who came to help David while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001|1 Chr 12:1]]; [[@13012006|1 Chr 12:6]]).

column5: A town built by the children of Gad
column7: It was one of the towns the children of Gad built ([[@4032034-4032035|Num 32:34-35]]). Gideon went up by the way of those who lived in tents east of Jogbehah and struck the Midianite army ([[@7008011|Judg 8:11]]).

column5: Father of Bukki, prince of Dan
column7: He was the father of Bukki, the prince of the tribe of Dan who was given the task of dividing the land of Canaan ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034022|Num 34:22]]).

column5: Son of Beriah, a descendant of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin’s descendants, recorded as a son of Beriah along with Michael and Ishpah ([[@13008016|1 Chr 8:16]]).

column5: The Tizite, one of David’s mighty men
column7: The Tizite, he appears in the list of David’s mighty men. He was the brother of Jediael the son of Shimri ([[@13011045|1 Chr 11:45]]).

column5: Army captain of Judah after Jerusalem fell
column7: He was the son of Kareah, one of the army captains who gathered to Gedaliah, the governor Babylon appointed after Jerusalem fell ([[@24040008|Jer 40:8]]). He warned Gedaliah ahead of time that Ishmael meant to kill him, but Gedaliah did not believe him ([[@24040013-24040016|Jer 40:13-16]]). After Gedaliah was killed, Johanan recovered the people Ishmael was carrying away ([[@24041016|Jer 41:16]]). But he did not obey the LORD's word not to go to Egypt, and he went down to Egypt, taking even Jeremiah with him ([[@24043004-24043007|Jer 43:4-7]]).

column5: Son of Elioenai, of David’s royal line
column7: He appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Jeconiah, who was taken captive, as one of the seven sons of Elioenai ([[@13003017|1 Chr 3:17]]; [[@13003024|1 Chr 3:24]]).

column5: In the priestly line, son of Azariah
column7: In the priestly line of the descendants of Levi, he was the son of Azariah ([[@13006009|1 Chr 6:9]]). His son Azariah served as priest in the house Solomon built ([[@13006010|1 Chr 6:10]]).

column5: A warrior who came to David at Ziklag
column7: He was one of the warriors who came to help David while he was hiding at Ziklag. He appears in the list of Saul’s relatives from the tribe of Benjamin, who used bows and slings ([[@13012002|1 Chr 12:2]]; [[@13012004|1 Chr 12:4]]).

column5: A Gadite warrior who joined David
column7: He was the eighth of the Gadite warriors who joined David. They were men trained for war who could handle shield and spear ([[@13012008|1 Chr 12:8]]; [[@13012012|1 Chr 12:12]]).

column5: Father of Azariah, an Ephraimite leader
column7: He was the father of Azariah, a head of the descendants of Ephraim, who stood up over the matter of the captives taken from Judah in King Ahaz’s time ([[@14028008|2 Chr 28:8]]; [[@14028012|2 Chr 28:12]]).

column5: A descendant of Azgad who returned with Ezra
column7: The son of Hakkatan, he was a descendant of Azgad who came up from Babylon with Ezra. With him were one hundred ten men ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008012|Ezra 8:12]]).

column5: Son of Eliashib
column7: He was the son of Eliashib, and the heads of the Levite families were written in the book of the chronicles up to his days ([[@16012022-16012023|Neh 12:22-23]]).

column5: John the Baptizer, who prepared the way for Jesus
column7: He was the son of the priest Zacharias and of Elizabeth ([[@42001013|Luke 1:13]]). In the wilderness of Judea he cried out, "Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand!" ([[@40003001-40003002|Matt 3:1-2]]). He baptized people in the Jordan River and baptized Jesus too ([[@40003013|Matt 3:13]]). When he saw Jesus, he testified, "Behold, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world!" ([[@43001029|John 1:29]]). Later he rebuked Herod for his wrongdoing, was thrown into prison, and was put to death.

column5: Son of Zebedee, one of Jesus' twelve apostles
column7: John was the son of Zebedee and the brother of James, and Jesus called him while he was mending nets in a boat ([[@40004021|Matt 4:21]]). Jesus gave these brothers the name Boanerges, which means "Sons of Thunder" ([[@41003017|Mark 3:17]]). He stayed close to Jesus, and with Peter and James he went up a high mountain and saw Jesus transfigured ([[@40017001|Matt 17:1]]). After Jesus rose from the dead, John went up to the temple with Peter and preached the gospel ([[@44003001|Acts 3:1]]). He is a different person from John the Baptizer, who had the same name.

column5: Father of Simon Peter
column7: He was the father of Simon Peter, and in these verses his name appears as Jonah. Jesus called Peter "Simon the son of Jonah" ([[@43001042|John 1:42]]; [[@43021015|John 21:15]]).

column5: A John present when the apostles were questioned
column7: He was present with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, and Alexander when they stood the apostles in the middle and questioned them. He is a different person from the apostle John ([[@44004005-44004007|Acts 4:5-7]]).

column5: Son of Paseah, who repaired the old gate
column7: He was the son of Paseah. In Nehemiah’s time he and Meshullam the son of Besodeiah repaired the old gate and set up its doors, its bolts, and its bars ([[@16003006|Neh 3:6]]).

column5: Son of Eliashib, of the high priest's family
column7: He was the son of Eliashib the high priest and the father of Jonathan ([[@16012010-16012011|Neh 12:10-11]]). One of his sons became Sanballat's son-in-law, so Nehemiah chased him away ([[@16013028|Neh 13:28]]).

column5: Son of Jeshua, grandson of Jozadak
column7: He was the son of Jeshua and the grandson of Jozadak ([[@16012010|Neh 12:10]]; [[@16012026|Neh 12:26]]). A list of the heads of the priestly families in his days was recorded ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]).

column5: A priest after the exile
column7: He was a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile, called 'Jehoiarib' in 1 Chronicles ([[@13009010|1 Chr 9:10]]). The book of Nehemiah records the priest Jedaiah as 'the son of Joiarib' ([[@16011010|Neh 11:10]]).

column5: A teacher Ezra sent for
column7: He was one of the men Ezra sent for when he found there were no Levites at the river that runs to Ahava. The Bible calls him a teacher ([[@15008015-15008016|Ezra 8:15-16]]).

column5: Ancestor of Maaseiah, a man of Judah in Jerusalem
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Maaseiah, a descendant of Judah who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile, as Maaseiah’s ancestor five generations back ([[@16011004-16011005|Neh 11:4-5]]).

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: It was one of the hill-country towns the tribe of Judah received, listed with Jezreel and Zanoah ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015056|Josh 15:56]]).

column5: A descendant of Shelah son of Judah
column7: This name appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Shelah the son of Judah. The Bible says these records are ancient ([[@13004021-13004022|1 Chr 4:21-22]]).

column5: A town at Carmel, a Levite town in Zebulun
column7: It was the town of 'the king of Jokneam in Carmel', whom Joshua struck down ([[@6012022|Josh 12:22]]). Later it was given from the tribe of Zebulun to the Levites of the sons of Merari ([[@6021034|Josh 21:34]]).

column5: Son of Abraham and Keturah
column7: He was a son born to Abraham by his concubine Keturah ([[@1025002|Gen 25:2]]). He became the father of Sheba and Dedan ([[@1025003|Gen 25:3]]).

column5: Son of Eber, brother of Peleg
column7: He was one of the two sons born to Eber, a descendant of Shem, and the brother of Peleg ([[@1010025|Gen 10:25]]). He had thirteen sons, from Almodad, Sheleph, and Hazarmaveth to Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab ([[@1010026-1010029|Gen 10:26-29]]; [[@13001020-13001023|1 Chr 1:20-23]]). His descendants lived from Mesha toward Sephar, the mountain of the east ([[@1010030|Gen 10:30]]). Some think these descendants were the ancestors of various Arabian peoples, but scholars differ on exactly where they lived.

column5: A town in the lowland of Judah
column7: It was one of the lowland towns the tribe of Judah received, listed with Dilean and Mizpah ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]; [[@6015038|Josh 15:38]]).

column5: David's nephew, Amnon's crafty friend
column7: He was the son of David's brother Shimeah and a friend of Amnon. The Bible says he was "a very subtle man" ([[@10013003|2 Sam 13:3]]). When Amnon was lovesick over Absalom's sister Tamar, Jonadab told him to lie in bed and pretend to be sick, and then ask the king to send Tamar to him ([[@10013004-10013005|2 Sam 13:4-5]]). Later, when a report reached David that Absalom had killed all the king's sons, Jonadab told him, "Amnon only is dead", explaining that Absalom had determined to do this because of what happened to Tamar ([[@10013030-10013032|2 Sam 13:30-32]]).

column5: Son of Rechab, ancestor of the Rechabites
column7: He was the son of Rechab and the ancestor of the Rechabites. Jehu met him, took his hand, and had him ride in his chariot to see his zeal for the LORD ([[@12010015-12010016|2 Kgs 10:15-16]]), and they went into the house of Baal together ([[@12010023|2 Kgs 10:23]]). Jonadab commanded his descendants not to drink wine, not to build houses, and to live in tents all their days, and his descendants kept this command ([[@24035006-24035010|Jer 35:6-10]]). God pointed to their obedience to rebuke the people of Judah, who would not listen to his words ([[@24035014|Jer 35:14]]). In 2 Kings 10 he is also called 'Jehonadab.'

column5: Prophet who called Nineveh to repent
column7: He was the son of Amittai from Gath Hepher, a prophet of Israel in the days of King Jeroboam ([[@12014025|2 Kgs 14:25]]). God told him to go to Nineveh, but he ran away toward Tarshish, was swallowed by a huge fish, and "was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights" ([[@32001017|Jonah 1:17]]). When he was called again and went to Nineveh and cried out, the people repented, and God did not send the disaster he had spoken of ([[@32003004-32003010|Jonah 3:4-10]]). Jesus compared Jonah's time in the belly of the fish with the time the Son of Man would spend in the heart of the earth ([[@40012040|Matt 12:40]]).

column5: A man in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus. He is listed as the father of Joseph and the son of Eliakim ([[@42003030|Luke 3:30]]).

column5: Son of Gershom, who became priest for Dan
column7: He was the grandson of Moses and the son of Gershom. When the descendants of Dan set up the engraved image, he and his sons became priests to the tribe of Dan until the day of the captivity ([[@7018030|Judg 18:30]]).

column5: King Saul's son, David's friend
column7: He was King Saul's son ([[@13008033|1 Chr 8:33]]). He was a brave man; taking only the young man who carried his armor, he crossed over to a Philistine garrison, saying, "there is no restraint on the LORD to save by many or by few" ([[@9014006|1 Sam 14:6]]). Because "he loved him as his own soul" he made a covenant with David ([[@9018003|1 Sam 18:3]]), and he protected David when his father tried to kill him. When he died in the battle at Gilboa, David mourned him with a song ([[@10001026|2 Sam 1:26]]).

column5: Son of the priest Abiathar who helped David
column7: He was the son of Abiathar the priest. When Absalom rebelled, David sent Jonathan back to Jerusalem with Ahimaaz the son of Zadok, so they could bring him news from the city ([[@10015027|2 Sam 15:27]], 36). The two stayed by En Rogel, and when a boy reported them to Absalom, they hid in a well at a man's house in Bahurim, then went safely to David and told him of Ahithophel's plan ([[@10017017-10017021|2 Sam 17:17-21]]). Near the end of David's life, he brought Adonijah the news that King David had made Solomon king ([[@11001042-11001043|1 Kgs 1:42-43]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men
column7: He was one of David’s mighty men, a son of Jashen ([[@10023032|2 Sam 23:32]]). In 1 Chronicles he is listed as 'Jonathan the son of Shagee the Hararite' ([[@13011034|1 Chr 11:34]]).

column5: A descendant of Judah, son of Jada
column7: He was the son of Jada, a descendant of Jerahmeel ([[@13002032|1 Chr 2:32]]). His sons were Peleth and Zaza ([[@13002033|1 Chr 2:33]]).

column5: Son of Uzziah, over David’s storehouses
column7: The son of Uzziah, he was in charge of the treasures in the fields, cities, villages, and towers in King David’s time ([[@13027025|1 Chr 27:25]]).

column5: Father of Ebed, who returned with Ezra
column7: He was the father of Ebed, a descendant of Adin who came up from Babylon with Ezra. With Ebed were fifty men ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008006|Ezra 8:6]]).

column5: A man who opposed dealing with foreign wives
column7: He was the son of Asahel. In Ezra’s time, when the matter of marriages to foreign women was being dealt with, he stood up with Jahzeiah the son of Tikvah against it ([[@15010015|Ezra 10:15]]).

column5: Priestly head of the family of Malluchi
column7: In the days of Joiakim the high priest, he was one of the heads of the priestly families, the head of the family of Malluchi ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012014|Neh 12:14]]).

column5: Ancestor of Zechariah the trumpeter
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Zechariah, a priest’s son who held a trumpet at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem. Zechariah was the son of Jonathan, the son of Shemaiah ([[@16012035|Neh 12:35]]).

column5: A scribe whose house became a prison
column7: He was a scribe whose house the princes had made into a prison, and they beat Jeremiah and locked him up there ([[@24037015|Jer 37:15]]). Jeremiah pleaded not to be sent back to that house, fearing he would die there ([[@24037020|Jer 37:20]]).

column5: Son of Kareah who went to Gedaliah at Mizpah
column7: He was one of the two sons of Kareah, and with his brother Johanan he was among the army captains who came to Gedaliah the governor at Mizpah ([[@24040007-24040008|Jer 40:7-8]]).

column5: Mediterranean port near Jerusalem
column7: It was a port city on the Mediterranean coast; cedars from Lebanon were tied into rafts and floated by sea to this port, then carried up to Jerusalem ([[@14002016|2 Chr 2:16]]; [[@15003007|Ezra 3:7]]). Jonah went down to Joppa to flee from the presence of the LORD and boarded a ship going to Tarshish ([[@32001003|Jonah 1:3]]). In the New Testament Peter raised Tabitha from the dead here, and he stayed many days in the house of Simon the tanner ([[@44009040|Acts 9:40]], 43). After seeing a vision there, he went to Cornelius in Caesarea.

column5: Ancestor of a family that returned from exile
column7: One hundred twelve of 'the children of Jorah' came back from Babylon ([[@15002018|Ezra 2:18]]). In the same place in Nehemiah, they are listed as 'the children of Hariph' ([[@16007024|Neh 7:24]]).

column5: A Gadite who lived in Bashan
column7: He was one of seven brothers of the families of Gad’s descendants who lived in the land of Bashan. They were all sons of Abihail ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005013-13005014|1 Chr 5:13-14]]).

column5: Son of Toi, king of Hamath
column7: He was the son of Toi king of Hamath; when David defeated Hadadezer, he came to greet David, bringing vessels of silver, gold, and bronze ([[@10008009-10008010|2 Sam 8:9-10]]). In 1 Chronicles he is called 'Hadoram' ([[@13018010|1 Chr 18:10]]).

column5: Son of Ahab, king of northern Israel
column7: The son of Ahab, he was king over Israel in Samaria for twelve years. His name is also written 'Jehoram'; he removed the pillar of Baal his father had made, but he did not turn away from the sins of Jeroboam ([[@12003001-12003003|2 Kgs 3:1-3]]). When the king of Moab rebelled, he went out to fight Moab with Jehoshaphat king of Judah and the king of Edom ([[@12003007-12003009|2 Kgs 3:7-9]]). Later, while he was recovering in Jezreel from wounds he received fighting Hazael king of Syria, Jehu rebelled ([[@12009014-12009015|2 Kgs 9:14-15]]). An arrow shot by Jehu pierced his heart and he died, and his body was thrown into the field of Naboth the Jezreelite ([[@12009024-12009025|2 Kgs 9:24-25]]).

column5: Ancestor of Shelomoth, keeper of the treasuries
column7: A descendant of Eliezer the son of Moses, he was the son of Jeshaiah. His descendant Shelomoth and his brothers were in charge of all the treasuries of the dedicated things ([[@13026025-13026026|1 Chr 26:25-26]]).

column5: The river that flows north to south through Israel
column7: It is the river that flows through the land of Israel from the north down to the Salt Sea. Lot saw that the plain of the Jordan was well-watered and chose it ([[@1013010|Gen 13:10]]). In Joshua's time the people crossed on dry ground while the priests carrying the ark of the covenant stood in the middle of the Jordan ([[@6003017|Josh 3:17]]). The Syrian commander Naaman dipped himself seven times in this river and was made clean ([[@12005014|2 Kgs 5:14]]), and Jesus too was baptized by John here ([[@40003013|Matt 3:13]]).

column5: A man in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus. He is listed as the father of Eliezer and the son of Matthat ([[@42003029|Luke 3:29]]).

column5: A name whose father is recorded as Raham
column7: This name appears in the genealogy of Caleb’s descendants. It records that Shema the son of Hebron became the father of Raham, and Raham was the father of Jorkeam ([[@13002043-13002044|1 Chr 2:43-44]]).

column5: A man in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus. He is listed as the father of Semein and the son of Judah ([[@42003026|Luke 3:26]]).

column5: Jacob's son, prime minister of Egypt
column7: He was the firstborn son of Jacob and Rachel. Rachel named him, saying, "May the LORD add another son to me" ([[@1030024|Gen 30:24]]). Hated by his brothers, he was sold as a slave into Egypt, but he interpreted Pharaoh's dreams and became the ruler over all the land of Egypt ([[@1041041|Gen 41:41]]). He saved his family during a great famine and told his brothers, "you meant evil against me, but God meant it for good" ([[@1050020|Gen 50:20]]).

column5: Father of Igal, the spy from Issachar
column7: He was the father of Igal, who represented the tribe of Issachar among the twelve men sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013002|Num 13:2]]; [[@4013007|Num 13:7]]).

column5: Son of Asaph, a temple singer
column7: He was one of the sons of Asaph, assigned to prophesy in song ([[@13025002|1 Chr 25:2]]). When lots were cast for the divisions, the first lot fell to him ([[@13025009|1 Chr 25:9]]).

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a descendant of Bani on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]; [[@15010042|Ezra 10:42]]).

column5: Priestly head of the family of Shebaniah
column7: In the days of Joiakim the high priest, he was one of the heads of the priestly families, the head of the family of Shebaniah ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012014|Neh 12:14]]).

column5: Mary's husband, the carpenter of Nazareth
column7: He was a descendant of David and the husband of Mary, and he lived in Nazareth of Galilee ([[@42002004|Luke 2:4]]). The Bible calls him "a righteous man". When he learned that Mary was pregnant, he planned to end the engagement quietly, but after hearing the angel of the Lord in a dream, he took Mary as his wife ([[@40001019-40001024|Matt 1:19-24]]). When Herod tried to kill the child Jesus, he took the child and his mother and fled to Egypt as the angel of the Lord told him ([[@40002013-40002014|Matt 2:13-14]]). People called Jesus "the carpenter’s son" ([[@40013055|Matt 13:55]]).

column5: Man of Arimathaea who buried Jesus
column7: He was from Arimathaea, a town of the Jews, a rich man and a respected member of the council who was waiting for God's Kingdom ([[@40027057|Matt 27:57]]; [[@41015043|Mark 15:43]]). He was a good and righteous man who had not agreed with the council's decision and action, and he was a disciple of Jesus, though secretly because he feared the Jews ([[@42023050-42023051|Luke 23:50-51]]; [[@43019038|John 19:38]]). After Jesus died, he boldly went to Pilate and asked for the body, and with Nicodemus he wrapped Jesus' body in linen cloths with spices ([[@41015043|Mark 15:43]]; [[@43019039-43019040|John 19:39-40]]). Then he laid it in his own new tomb cut in the rock and rolled a large stone against the door of the tomb ([[@40027059-40027060|Matt 27:59-60]]).

column5: A man in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus. He is listed as the father of Jannai and the son of Mattathias ([[@42003024-42003025|Luke 3:24-25]]).

column5: A man in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus. He is listed as the father of Judah and the son of Jonan ([[@42003030|Luke 3:30]]).

column5: Barsabbas, put forward for Judas’s place
column7: He was called Barsabbas and was also known as Justus. He was put forward with Matthias to take the place of Judas Iscariot, and when they drew lots, Matthias was chosen ([[@44001023|Acts 1:23]]; [[@44001026|Acts 1:26]]).

column5: A brother of Jesus
column7: He was one of the brothers of Jesus named by the people of Jesus’ hometown. His brothers were James, Joses, Simon, and Judas ([[@40013055|Matt 13:55]]; [[@41006003|Mark 6:3]]).

column5: Brother of James the less
column7: Among the women watching Jesus’ crucifixion from afar was "Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses" ([[@41015040|Mark 15:40]]). Matthew also names her as the mother of James and Joses ([[@40027056|Matt 27:56]]).

column5: A family head of the Simeonites
column7: The son of Amaziah, he was a leader whose name is in the genealogy of Simeon’s descendants. In Hezekiah’s time they took over the pastureland at the entrance of Gedor ([[@13004034|1 Chr 4:34]]; [[@13004039-13004041|1 Chr 4:39-41]]).

column5: The Mithnite, one of David’s mighty men
column7: The Mithnite, he appears in the list of David’s mighty men. Just before him comes Hanan the son of Maacah ([[@13011043|1 Chr 11:43]]).

column5: Priest who blew a trumpet before God’s ark
column7: He was one of the priests who blew the trumpets before God’s ark when David brought it up ([[@13015024|1 Chr 15:24]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men
column7: He appears in the list of David’s mighty men, and his name is listed with Jeribai; the two are called the sons of Elnaam ([[@13011046|1 Chr 11:46]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a temple singer
column7: He was one of the sons of Heman, who served in song in David’s day ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]). The seventeenth lot fell to him, and he served with his sons and brothers, twelve in all ([[@13025024|1 Chr 25:24]]).

column5: Father of Jehu the Simeonite
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Simeon’s descendants as the father of Jehu, a leader. He was the son of Seraiah and the grandson of Asiel ([[@13004035|1 Chr 4:35]]).

column5: The leader who led the people after Moses
column7: He was the son of Nun, of the tribe of Ephraim, and his original name was Hoshea ([[@4013008|Num 13:8]]; [[@4013016|Num 13:16]]). He served at Moses' side and led the army in the battle against Amalek ([[@2017009|Exod 17:9]]). After Moses died, he led the people across the Jordan into the land of Canaan. At the end, he made this pledge before the people: "as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD" ([[@6024015|Josh 24:15]]).

column5: Owner of a field in Beth Shemesh
column7: He was a man of Beth Shemesh, and the cart carrying the LORD’s ark back from the Philistines came into his field and stopped where there was a great stone ([[@9006014|1 Sam 6:14]]). That stone remained in his field for a long time ([[@9006018|1 Sam 6:18]]).

column5: Governor of the city in Josiah’s time
column7: He was governor of the city in King Josiah’s time. The high places of the gates that the king broke down were at the entrance of the gate of Joshua the governor, on the left side of the city gate ([[@12023008|2 Kgs 23:8]]).

column5: High priest of the returning exiles
column7: He was the son of Jozadak, the high priest who led the people back from exile in Babylon together with Zerubbabel. After they returned, they first built God's altar and offered burnt offerings as written in the law of Moses ([[@15003002|Ezra 3:2]]). Work on the temple stopped because of the enemies' opposition, but he and Zerubbabel rose up and began building again, with God's prophets helping them ([[@15005002|Ezra 5:2]]). The books of Haggai and Zechariah call the same man "Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest" ([[@37001001|Hag 1:1]]; [[@38003001|Zech 3:1]]).

column5: Son of Eliezer, a distant ancestor of Jesus
column7: He is a man of this name in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus. He is listed as the father of Er and the son of Eliezer ([[@42003028-42003029|Luke 3:28-29]]).

column5: Judah's reforming king who found the Law book
column7: Josiah was the son of Amon; he became king of Judah at eight years old and reigned thirty-one years in Jerusalem ([[@12022001|2 Kgs 22:1]]). When the high priest Hilkiah found the book of the law while the temple was being repaired, Josiah heard its words, tore his clothes, and repented ([[@12022008-12022011|2 Kgs 22:8-11]]). After that he got rid of the idols and high places and kept a great Passover such as had not been kept since the days of the judges ([[@12023021-12023023|2 Kgs 23:21-23]]). Long before, a man of God had named him in a prophecy against the altar at Bethel, and that prophecy was fulfilled at this time ([[@11013002|1 Kgs 13:2]]).

column5: Owner of the house where returned exiles stayed
column7: He was the son of Zephaniah, and Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who had come back from Babylon, went into his house ([[@38006010|Zech 6:10]]). In verse 14 he is called 'Hen the son of Zephaniah' ([[@38006014|Zech 6:14]]).

column5: Father of one who came with Ezra
column7: Among the descendants of Shelomith who came up from Babylon with Ezra was the son of Josiphiah. With him were one hundred sixty men ([[@15008010|Ezra 8:10]]).

column5: Hometown of King Amon’s mother
column7: This place is connected with Meshullemeth, the mother of Amon king of Judah. Meshullemeth was the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah ([[@12021019|2 Kgs 21:19]]).

column5: A wilderness camp with many brooks
column7: It was where Israel camped in the wilderness after leaving Hor Haggidgad ([[@4033033|Num 33:33]]). Deuteronomy describes it as "a land of brooks of water" ([[@5010007|Deut 10:7]]).

column5: Gideon's youngest son
column7: He was the youngest son of Jerubbaal (Gideon), who survived by hiding when Abimelech killed his seventy brothers ([[@7009005|Judg 9:5]]). He called out to the men of Shechem from the top of Mount Gerizim and then fled to Beer ([[@7009007|Judg 9:7]]; [[@7009021|Judg 9:21]]).

column5: Son of Uzziah and king of Judah
column7: He was the son of Uzziah (Azariah) king of Judah. When his father lived in a separate house because of leprosy, Jotham ruled the land as the king's son ([[@12015005|2 Kgs 15:5]]). He became king at twenty-five and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem; he did what was right in the LORD's eyes and built the upper gate of the LORD's house, but he did not take away the high places ([[@12015033-12015035|2 Kgs 15:33-35]]). He defeated the children of Ammon, and the Bible says, "Jotham became mighty, because he ordered his ways before the LORD his God" ([[@14027006|2 Chr 27:6]]). The prophet Isaiah also prophesied in his time ([[@23001001|Isa 1:1]]).

column5: A man in Caleb’s line, son of Jahdai
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Caleb’s descendants, recorded as a son of Jahdai along with Regem, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph ([[@13002047|1 Chr 2:47]]).

column5: A Gederathite who came to David at Ziklag
column7: A Gederathite, he was one of the warriors who came to help David while he was hiding at Ziklag ([[@13012001|1 Chr 12:1]]; [[@13012004|1 Chr 12:4]]).

column5: A Levite who looked after offerings under Hezekiah
column7: In King Hezekiah’s time he was one of those who looked after the offerings and tithes brought into the temple, under Conaniah and Shimei ([[@14031012-14031013|2 Chr 31:12-13]]).

column5: A Levite chief who gave Passover offerings
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the Levites in King Josiah’s time, and with the other chiefs he gave five thousand small livestock and five hundred cattle as Passover offerings ([[@14035009|2 Chr 35:9]]).

column5: A Levite present when temple gifts were weighed
column7: He was the son of Jeshua the Levite. He was present when the silver, the gold, and the vessels brought by Ezra’s company were weighed and handed over in the house of God ([[@15008033|Ezra 8:33]]).

column5: A descendant of Pashhur who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a descendant of Pashhur on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010022|Ezra 10:22]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A Levite who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a Levite on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010023|Ezra 10:23]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: He helped the people understand the law
column7: When Ezra read the book of the law, he was one of those who, together with the Levites, helped the people standing in their place understand the law ([[@16008007-16008008|Neh 8:7-8]]).

column5: A Levite chief over the outside work of God’s house
column7: A chief of the Levites, he and Shabbethai had oversight of the outward business of God’s house. He appears in the list of those who lived in Jerusalem ([[@16011003|Neh 11:3]]; [[@16011016|Neh 11:16]]).

column5: A servant who killed King Joash
column7: He was the son of Shimeath, one of the servants who struck down and killed Joash king of Judah ([[@12012021|2 Kgs 12:21]]). In 2 Chronicles he is called 'Zabad', the son of Shimeath the Ammonitess ([[@14024026|2 Chr 24:26]]).

column5: Father of Jeshua the priest
column7: He was the father of Jeshua the priest ([[@15003002|Ezra 3:2]]). In Ezra’s time the list of priests who had married foreign women includes members of Jeshua’s family, "the son of Jozadak, and his brothers" ([[@15010018|Ezra 10:18]]).

column5: Father of all who play the harp and pipe
column7: He was the son of Lamech and Adah and the brother of Jabal. The Bible calls him "the father of all who handle the harp and pipe" ([[@1004020-1004021|Gen 4:20-21]]).

column5: The year of freedom that came every fifty years
column7: The Jubilee was the fiftieth year, which came after seven sabbatical years had passed. On the Day of Atonement, the tenth day of the seventh month, a loud trumpet was sounded to announce the Jubilee, and liberty was proclaimed to all the inhabitants of the land ([[@3025009-3025010|Lev 25:9-10]]). In the Jubilee year no one sowed, and land that had been sold went back to its original owner, so that each person returned to his own property and family ([[@3025011|Lev 25:11]]; [[@3025013|Lev 25:13]]). Behind this lies the truth that God is the real owner of the land, as he said, "the land is mine" ([[@3025023|Lev 25:23]]).

column5: Jacob's fourth son; the tribe and kingdom of Judah
column7: He was the fourth son born to Jacob and Leah. Leah named him Judah, saying, "This time I will praise the LORD" ([[@1029035|Gen 29:35]]). In his last blessing Jacob said, "The scepter will not depart from Judah" ([[@1049010|Gen 49:10]]), and King David did indeed come from the tribe of Judah. After the kingdom split in two, the southern kingdom that followed David's house was called Judah ([[@11012020|1 Kgs 12:20]]).

column5: A Levite who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a Levite on the list of those who had married foreign women in Ezra’s time ([[@15010023|Ezra 10:23]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Son of Hassenuah, second over the city
column7: He was the son of Hassenuah. Among the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile, he was second over the city after Joel the overseer ([[@16011007|Neh 11:7]]; [[@16011009|Neh 11:9]]).

column5: He followed the procession at the wall’s dedication
column7: When the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated and the thanksgiving choirs marched on top of the wall, he was one of those who followed behind them ([[@16012031-16012034|Neh 12:31-34]]).

column5: He played David’s instruments at the wall’s dedication
column7: At the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem he was one of Zechariah’s brothers, and he took part in the procession with the musical instruments of David the man of God ([[@16012035-16012036|Neh 12:35-36]]).

column5: A man in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in Luke’s genealogy of Jesus. He is listed as the father of Simeon and the son of Joseph ([[@42003030|Luke 3:30]]).

column5: The apostle Judas, not Iscariot
column7: He was one of the twelve apostles, and John calls him 'Judas (not Iscariot)' ([[@43014022|John 14:22]]). Luke records him as "Judas the son of James", and many consider him the same person as the Thaddaeus named by Matthew and Mark ([[@42006016|Luke 6:16]]; [[@40010003|Matt 10:3]]).

column5: Disciple who betrayed Jesus
column7: He was the son of Simon Iscariot and one of Jesus' twelve disciples ([[@43006071|John 6:71]]). He kept the disciples' money box but used to steal what was put into it ([[@43012006|John 12:6]]). He went to the chief priests and agreed to hand Jesus over for thirty pieces of silver, and in Gethsemane he led a crowd to Jesus and betrayed him ([[@40026014-40026016|Matt 26:14-16]], 47-49). When Jesus was condemned, Judas felt remorse, threw the silver into the sanctuary, went away, and took his own life ([[@40027003-40027005|Matt 27:3-5]]).

column5: A Galilean who rose up at the time of the census
column7: He was a man Gamaliel gave as an example in the council. He rose up in the days of the enrollment and drew people after him, but he perished and all who followed him were scattered ([[@44005034|Acts 5:34]]; [[@44005037|Acts 5:37]]).

column5: A man with a house on Straight Street in Damascus
column7: He had a house on the street called Straight in Damascus. The Lord sent Ananias to this man’s house to look for Saul of Tarsus ([[@44009011|Acts 9:11]]).

column5: Judas called Barsabbas, a prophet
column7: He was 'Judas called Barsabbas', whom the Jerusalem church sent to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas ([[@44015022|Acts 15:22]]). Being a prophet, he and Silas encouraged the brothers and strengthened them ([[@44015032|Acts 15:32]]).

column5: Brother of Jesus, writer of the letter of Jude
column7: His was one of the names the people of Jesus’ hometown listed as Jesus’ brothers ([[@40013055|Matt 13:55]]). The writer of the letter of Jude introduced himself as "Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James" ([[@65001001|Jude 1:1]]).

column5: The southern region around Jerusalem
column7: Judea is a name that comes from 'Judah', and after the return from exile it was used for the land around Jerusalem. In Jesus' time it was the southern region that, together with Galilee and Samaria, made up Palestine, and it was ruled by a Roman governor ([[@42003001|Luke 3:1]]). Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea ([[@40002001|Matt 2:1]]), and John preached repentance in the wilderness of Judea ([[@40003001|Matt 3:1]]). The risen Jesus told his disciples they would be his witnesses "in Jerusalem, in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost parts of the earth" ([[@44001008|Acts 1:8]]).

column5: Esau’s wife, daughter of Beeri the Hittite
column7: She was the daughter of Beeri the Hittite. Esau took her as his wife when he was forty years old, along with Basemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite ([[@1026034|Gen 26:34]]).

column5: A believer in Rome whom Paul greeted
column7: When Paul sent greetings to the believers in Rome, he named her along with Philologus ([[@45016015|Rom 16:15]]).

column5: The centurion who escorted Paul to Rome
column7: He was a centurion of the Augustan band, put in charge of Paul and other prisoners sailing for Italy ([[@44027001|Acts 27:1]]). At Sidon he treated Paul kindly and allowed him to go to his friends and be cared for ([[@44027003|Acts 27:3]]).

column5: Paul’s relative and fellow prisoner
column7: A relative of Paul, Junia had been in prison with Paul along with Andronicus. They were notable among the apostles and were in Christ before Paul ([[@45016007|Rom 16:7]]).

column5: A man of Zerubbabel’s family
column7: He appears in the genealogy of David’s royal line among the descendants of Zerubbabel, recorded as one of five along with Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, and Hasadiah ([[@13003019-13003020|1 Chr 3:19-20]]).

column5: God declaring believers righteous
column7: Justification means God declaring a person righteous. In the law God said, "I will not justify the wicked" ([[@2023007|Exod 23:7]]). Yet the New Testament says that though all have sinned, people are "justified freely by his grace through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus" ([[@45003023-45003024|Rom 3:23-24]]). This comes by faith, not by the works of the law ([[@45003028|Rom 3:28]]). So those who have been justified by faith have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ ([[@45005001|Rom 5:1]]).

column5: Owner of the house next to the synagogue in Corinth
column7: He was Justus, a man in Corinth who worshiped God. When the Jews opposed Paul, he left the synagogue and moved to Justus’s house next door to it ([[@44018006-44018007|Acts 18:6-7]]).

column5: Jesus called Justus, Paul’s fellow worker
column7: He was Jesus who is called Justus, who sent greetings to the church in Colossae. Paul says that among those of the circumcision, these were his only fellow workers for God’s Kingdom and had been a comfort to him ([[@51004011|Col 4:11]]).

column5: A Levite city in the hill country of Judah
column7: It was one of the hill-country towns the tribe of Judah received ([[@6015055|Josh 15:55]]). Later it was given, with its pasture lands, to the descendants of Levi ([[@6021016|Josh 21:16]]).

column5: A town in southern Judah, Benaiah’s home
column7: It was a town in the south of Judah near the border of Edom ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]). David’s mighty man Benaiah was the grandson of "a valiant man of Kabzeel" ([[@10023020|2 Sam 23:20]]).

column5: Place in the wilderness of Zin, Kadesh Barnea
column7: It was a place in the wilderness south of Israel, also called Kadesh Barnea. The spies Moses sent came back to Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran and gave their report, showing the fruit of the land ([[@4013026|Num 13:26]]). The people of Israel stayed near here for a long time, and Miriam died and was buried here ([[@4020001|Num 20:1]]). The "waters of Meribah of Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin" where the people quarreled because they had no water are also here ([[@4027014|Num 27:14]]). From Kadesh, Moses asked the king of Edom to let Israel pass through his land ([[@4020014|Num 20:14]]).

column5: A Levite who returned from exile
column7: He was a Levite who returned from exile in Babylon. The children of Jeshua and Kadmiel, of the children of Hodaviah, numbered seventy-four ([[@15002040|Ezra 2:40]]). When work on the temple began, Kadmiel and his sons oversaw the workmen in God's house ([[@15003009|Ezra 3:9]]). In Nehemiah's time he stood on the stairs, cried out to the LORD, and called the people to bless God ([[@16009004-16009005|Neh 9:4-5]]), and his name is also among those who sealed the covenant ([[@16010001-16010009|Neh 10:1-9]]).

column5: A people in the land promised to Abram’s offspring
column7: They were one of the peoples living in the land God promised to give Abram’s offspring when he made a covenant with him ([[@1015018-1015019|Gen 15:18-19]]).

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: It was one of the hill-country towns the tribe of Judah received, listed with Gibeah and Timnah ([[@6015057|Josh 15:57]]).

column5: Priestly family head of Sallai in Joiakim's day
column7: He was one of the heads of the priestly families in the days of the high priest Joiakim, the head of the family of Sallai ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012020|Neh 12:20]]).

column5: Where the judge Jair was buried
column7: This is the place where Jair the Gileadite, who judged Israel for twenty-two years, died and was buried ([[@7010003|Judg 10:3]]; [[@7010005|Judg 10:5]]).

column5: A brook on the border of Ephraim and Manasseh
column7: It is the brook along which the border between Ephraim and Manasseh ran. South of the brook was Ephraim’s land, and north of it was Manasseh’s ([[@6016008|Josh 16:8]]; [[@6017009|Josh 17:9]]).

column5: A town on the border of Asher
column7: It was a town on the border of the tribe of Asher, listed with Ebron, Rehob, and Hammon, and that border reached as far as great Sidon ([[@6019028|Josh 19:28]]).

column5: Father of Johanan and Jonathan
column7: He was the father of Johanan and Jonathan, army captains who were active after Jerusalem fell ([[@24040008|Jer 40:8]]). The Bible tells nothing about him, and he always appears with a son's name, as in 'Johanan the son of Kareah' ([[@12025023|2 Kgs 25:23]]). His son Johanan warned Governor Gedaliah ahead of time about Ishmael's plot, and after Gedaliah was killed he recovered the people Ishmael was carrying away ([[@24040015|Jer 40:15]]; [[@24041016|Jer 41:16]]). But later he did not obey the LORD's word and led the people down to Egypt.

column5: A place on Judah's southern border
column7: This was a place on the southern border of the land of the tribe of Judah. The border passed Hezron and Addar and then turned toward Karka ([[@6015001|Josh 15:1]]; [[@6015003|Josh 15:3]]).

column5: Where Gideon struck Zebah and Zalmunna
column7: This is where Zebah and Zalmunna, the two kings of Midian, were staying with what was left of their army. Gideon struck the enemy army there and captured the two kings ([[@7008010-7008012|Judg 8:10-12]]).

column5: A Levite city in Naphtali
column7: It was one of the three cities from the tribe of Naphtali given to the Levite descendants of Gershon ([[@6021027|Josh 21:27]]; [[@6021032|Josh 21:32]]).

column5: Son of Ishmael and the tribe descended from him
column7: He is the son listed after Nebaioth, the firstborn, among the sons of Ishmael ([[@1025013|Gen 25:13]]). His descendants became a tribe living in tents, and the psalmist lamented, "Woe is me, that I live in Meshech, that I dwell among the tents of Kedar!" ([[@19120005|Ps 120:5]]). Isaiah prophesied that within a year "all the glory of Kedar will fail" ([[@23021016|Isa 21:16]]). Jeremiah also brought a message about Kedar, which Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon would attack ([[@24049028|Jer 49:28]]).

column5: Son of Ishmael
column7: His name comes last among the sons of Ishmael ([[@1025015|Gen 25:15]]; [[@13001031|1 Chr 1:31]]). The sons of Ishmael became twelve princes according to their nations ([[@1025016|Gen 25:16]]).

column5: A Levite town of the tribe of Reuben
column7: From this wilderness Moses sent messengers to Sihon king of Heshbon ([[@5002026|Deut 2:26]]). It was a town of the tribe of Reuben that was given to the Levites ([[@6013018|Josh 13:18]]; [[@6021037|Josh 21:37]]).

column5: A city of refuge in Naphtali, Barak's hometown
column7: Among the Canaanite kings whom Joshua defeated was "the king of Kedesh" ([[@6012022|Josh 12:22]]). Kedesh was in Galilee in the hill country of Naphtali, and it was set apart as a city of refuge where anyone who killed a person unintentionally could flee ([[@6020007-6020009|Josh 20:7-9]]). Barak received Deborah's call in "Kedesh Naphtali," and he summoned ten thousand men of Zebulun and Naphtali to Kedesh ([[@7004006-7004010|Judg 4:6-10]]). In the days of Pekah king of Israel, Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria captured Kedesh and carried its people captive to Assyria ([[@12015029|2 Kgs 15:29]]).

column5: A place where Israel camped in the wilderness
column7: It was a place where the people of Israel camped as they passed through the wilderness. They came from Rissah and camped here, then went on to Mount Shepher ([[@4033022-4033023|Num 33:22-23]]).

column5: Town of Judah David rescued from the Philistines
column7: It was a town in the lowland of Judah ([[@6015044|Josh 15:44]]). When the Philistines attacked Keilah and robbed the threshing floors, David inquired of the LORD, went down, struck them with a great slaughter, and saved the town ([[@9023001-9023005|1 Sam 23:1-5]]). But the LORD told him that the men of Keilah would hand him over to Saul ([[@9023012|1 Sam 23:12]]). So David and his men, about six hundred, left Keilah and went wherever they could go ([[@9023013|1 Sam 23:13]]).

column5: A Levite who had married a foreign wife
column7: He was a Levite in Ezra's time who had married a foreign woman. The Bible calls him "Kelaiah (also called Kelita)" ([[@15010023|Ezra 10:23]]).

column5: A Levite who helped the people understand the law
column7: He was one of the Levites who helped the people understand the law when Ezra read it ([[@16008007|Neh 8:7]]). He also appears in the list of Levites who sealed the covenant ([[@16010010|Neh 10:10]]).

column5: Son of Nahor, father of Aram
column7: He was the son of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and Milcah. The Bible calls him the father of Aram ([[@1022020-1022021|Gen 22:20-21]]).

column5: Ephraimite leader who helped divide the land
column7: The son of Shiphtan, he was the leader of the tribe of Ephraim chosen to help divide the land of Canaan ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034024|Num 34:24]]).

column5: Father of Hashabiah, ruler over the Levites
column7: He was the father of Hashabiah, who in David's time was the ruler over the Levites among the officers in charge of the tribes of Israel ([[@13027016-13027017|1 Chr 27:16-17]]).

column5: Son of Enosh, ancestor before the Flood
column7: He was Seth's grandson and the son of Enosh, an ancestor who lived before the Flood. Enosh became the father of Kenan at ninety ([[@1005009|Gen 5:9]]). Kenan became the father of Mahalalel at seventy, and after that he lived eight hundred forty years and had other children ([[@1005012-1005013|Gen 5:12-13]]). He lived nine hundred ten years and then died ([[@1005014|Gen 5:14]]). His name also appears among Adam's descendants in the genealogy of Chronicles ([[@13001002|1 Chr 1:2]]).

column5: A town of Gilead taken by Nobah
column7: Nobah, a descendant of Manasseh, took Kenath and its villages and called it Nobah after his own name ([[@4032042|Num 32:42]]). Later Geshur and Aram took this place ([[@13002023|1 Chr 2:23]]).

column5: A descendant of Esau, a chief of Edom
column7: He was a son of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn ([[@1036011|Gen 36:11]]). He became one of the chiefs among Esau's descendants ([[@1036015|Gen 36:15]]).

column5: Father of the judge Othniel
column7: He was the father of Othniel, Israel's first judge. The Bible introduces Othniel as "Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb" ([[@6015017|Josh 15:17]]). Caleb is also called 'the son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite,' so Kenaz seems to be a name connected with Caleb's family ([[@4032012|Num 32:12]]). The LORD's Spirit came on Othniel, and he defeated Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia ([[@7003009-7003010|Judg 3:9-10]]). Scholars differ on exactly how Kenaz and Caleb were related.

column5: A descendant of Caleb son of Jephunneh
column7: His name appears in the family line of Caleb the son of Jephunneh, together with Iru, Elah, Naam, and the descendants of Elah ([[@13004015|1 Chr 4:15]]).

column5: A people friendly toward Israel
column7: They were a people living in the land of Canaan, the first named among the peoples whose land God promised to give to Abram's descendants ([[@1015019|Gen 15:19]]). A Kenite was related to Moses by marriage, and his descendants went up with the children of Judah and lived in the south of Arad ([[@7001016|Judg 1:16]]). When Saul attacked the Amalekites, he remembered how the Kenites had shown kindness to Israel at the Exodus and let them leave first ([[@9015006|1 Sam 15:6]]). In Deborah's song, Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite is called blessed above other women ([[@7005024|Judg 5:24]]).

column5: A people in the land promised to Abram
column7: They were one of the peoples living in the land God promised to give Abram's offspring when he made his covenant with him ([[@1015018-1015019|Gen 15:18-19]]).

column5: Job's third daughter
column7: She was the third of the daughters born to Job after the LORD blessed the latter part of his life. In all the land there were no women as beautiful as Job's daughters ([[@18042014-18042015|Job 42:14-15]]).

column5: A southern town of Judah, also Hazor
column7: It was one of the southern towns of the tribe of Judah, toward the border of Edom. The Bible says "Kerioth Hezron (also called Hazor)" ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015025|Josh 15:25]]).

column5: A family of temple servants who returned from exile
column7: Among the temple servants who came back from exile were 'the children of Keros' ([[@15002043-15002044|Ezra 2:43-44]]; [[@16007047|Neh 7:47]]).

column5: Abraham's later wife
column7: She was the wife Abraham took later ([[@1025001|Gen 25:1]]), and she bore Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. In 1 Chronicles she is called 'Abraham's concubine' ([[@13001032|1 Chr 1:32]]).

column5: Job's second daughter
column7: She was the second of the daughters born to Job after the LORD blessed the latter part of his life. Job gave his daughters an inheritance just as he did their brothers ([[@18042014-18042015|Job 42:14-15]]).

column5: Where the people who craved were buried
column7: It was called 'Kibroth Hattaavah' because there they buried the people who had craved meat in the wilderness ([[@4011034|Num 11:34]]). From there Israel traveled on to Hazeroth ([[@4011035|Num 11:35]]).

column5: A Levite city in the land of Ephraim
column7: It was a city from the tribe of Ephraim given to the Levites of the children of Kohath ([[@6021020-6021022|Josh 21:20-22]]). In the same place in 1 Chronicles, 'Jokmeam' appears ([[@13006068|1 Chr 6:68]]).

column5: Brook east of Jerusalem
column7: It is the brook east of Jerusalem that runs between the city and the Mount of Olives. When David fled from Absalom, he crossed this brook with all the people and headed toward the wilderness ([[@10015023|2 Sam 15:23]]). King Asa cut down the idol his mother Maacah had made and burned it by the brook Kidron, and King Josiah also brought the Asherah out of the temple and burned it at the brook Kidron ([[@11015013|1 Kgs 15:13]]; [[@12023006|2 Kgs 23:6]]). When Jesus had finished speaking, he went with his disciples across the brook Kidron to a garden ([[@43018001|John 18:1]]).

column5: A town at Judah's far south
column7: It was one of the southern towns of the tribe of Judah toward the border of Edom, listed with Dimonah and Adadah ([[@6015021-6015022|Josh 15:21-22]]).

column5: A main road through Edom and the Amorite land
column7: Israel asked the king of Edom to let them pass, going only along the king’s highway ([[@4020017|Num 20:17]]). They told Sihon king of the Amorites that they would also go only by that road ([[@4021021-4021022|Num 21:21-22]]).

column5: Valley where Absalom's monument stood
column7: This is where the pillar stood that Absalom set up in his own name, lamenting that he had no son to keep his name in memory. That pillar was called Absalom's monument ([[@10018018|2 Sam 18:18]]).

column5: Important city of Moab
column7: It was an important city of Moab. When the armies of Israel and Judah attacked Moab, the other towns were all torn down, but the stones of Kir Hareseth were left ([[@12003025|2 Kgs 3:25]]). Isaiah prophesied, "in a night Kir of Moab is laid waste, and brought to nothing", and mourned for Kir Heres ([[@23015001|Isa 15:1]]; [[@23016011|Isa 16:11]]). Jeremiah also calls it Kir Heres ([[@24048031|Jer 48:31]]). Many scholars think 'Kir of Moab' and Kir Hareseth are the same place, but views differ somewhat.

column5: The land where Assyria deported the Syrians
column7: It was the place to which the king of Assyria carried away the people of Damascus after taking the city ([[@12016009|2 Kgs 16:9]]). Amos prophesied that the people of Syria would go into captivity to Kir ([[@30001005|Amos 1:5]]).

column5: Where Balak took Balaam
column7: This is the place where Balak king of Moab went with Balaam. There Balak sacrificed cattle and sheep and sent portions to Balaam and those with him ([[@4022039-4022040|Num 22:39-40]]).

column5: Town where the ark stayed twenty years
column7: It was a town on the border between Judah and Benjamin, and at first it was one of the cities of the Gibeonites ([[@6009017|Josh 9:17]]). It was also called Baalah or Kiriath Baal ([[@6015009|Josh 15:9]], 60). The people of this town brought the ark of the covenant, which had come back from the land of the Philistines, into Abinadab's house, and the Bible says, "From the day that the ark stayed in Kiriath Jearim, the time was long—for it was twenty years" ([[@9007001-9007002|1 Sam 7:1-2]]). Later David went up there with all Israel to bring the ark to Jerusalem ([[@13013006|1 Chr 13:6]]).

column5: A town east of the Jordan built by the Reubenites
column7: It was a town east of the Jordan. There is a record that in Abraham's time Chedorlaomer struck "the Emim in Shaveh Kiriathaim" ([[@1014005|Gen 14:5]]). The children of Reuben built Kiriathaim along with Heshbon and Elealeh, and gave new names to the towns ([[@4032037-4032038|Num 32:37-38]]). In Jeremiah's time it appears as a town of Moab, and Jeremiah prophesied Moab's ruin, saying, "Kiriathaim is disappointed. It is taken" ([[@24048001|Jer 48:1]]). Ezekiel also named Kiriathaim as one of the glorious towns on Moab's frontier ([[@26025009|Ezek 25:9]]).

column5: A Levite city in Naphtali
column7: It was one of the cities from the tribe of Naphtali given to the Levite descendants of Gershom ([[@13006062|1 Chr 6:62]]; [[@13006076|1 Chr 6:76]]).

column5: Father of Saul, Israel's first king
column7: He was a man of standing from the tribe of Benjamin, the son of Abiel ([[@9009001|1 Sam 9:1]]). When his donkeys were lost, he sent his son Saul with a servant to look for them ([[@9009003|1 Sam 9:3]]). Later the bones of Saul and Jonathan were buried in the tomb of Kish at Zela in the land of Benjamin ([[@10021014|2 Sam 21:14]]). Paul too said in a sermon that God gave Israel "Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin" as king ([[@44013021|Acts 13:21]]).

column5: A descendant of Merari, son of Mahli
column7: He was a son of Mahli, Merari’s son ([[@13023021|1 Chr 23:21]]). When his brother Eleazar died leaving only daughters, the sons of Kish married them ([[@13023022|1 Chr 23:22]]).

column5: Levite who cleansed the temple under Hezekiah
column7: He was the son of Abdi, of the descendants of Merari. In King Hezekiah's time he rose up with the other Levites and cleansed the LORD's house ([[@14029012|2 Chr 29:12]]; [[@14029015|2 Chr 29:15]]).

column5: Great-grandfather of Mordecai
column7: He was the great-grandfather of Mordecai, a Benjamite who lived in the citadel of Susa. Mordecai was the son of Jair and the grandson of Shimei ([[@17002005|Esth 2:5]]).

column5: A descendant of Merari, father of Ethan
column7: He was a descendant of Merari and the father of Ethan, a temple singer ([[@13006044|1 Chr 6:44]]). In chapter 15 he is called 'Kushaiah' ([[@13015017|1 Chr 15:17]]).

column5: A Levite city in the tribe of Issachar
column7: It was one of the cities the tribe of Issachar received ([[@6019020|Josh 19:20]]). It was also one of the cities from the tribe of Issachar given to the Levites of the children of Gershon ([[@6021027-6021028|Josh 21:27-28]]).

column5: The river where Sisera was defeated
column7: It was the river where the LORD drew Sisera's army and delivered it into Barak's hand ([[@7004007|Judg 4:7]]; [[@7005021|Judg 5:21]]). Elijah brought the prophets of Baal down to the brook Kishon and killed them ([[@11018040|1 Kgs 18:40]]).

column5: A town Zebulun did not drive out
column7: It was a town whose inhabitants the tribe of Zebulun did not drive out, so the Canaanites lived among them and became subject to forced labor ([[@7001030|Judg 1:30]]). Some think it is the same place as 'Kattath' in Joshua ([[@6019015|Josh 19:15]]).

column5: Grandson of Japheth, son of Javan
column7: He was a grandson of Noah’s son Japheth, one of the sons of Javan ([[@1010004|Gen 10:4]]; [[@13001007|1 Chr 1:7]]).

column5: The people of Koa named by Ezekiel
column7: Koa was one of the peoples Ezekiel named, along with the Babylonians, the Chaldeans, Pekod, and Shoa, among those who would come against Oholibah ([[@26023022-26023023|Ezek 23:22-23]]).

column5: Levi's second son, ancestor of the Kohathites
column7: Kohath was the second son of Levi and the brother of Gershon and Merari ([[@1046011|Gen 46:11]]). He went down to Egypt with Jacob and lived one hundred thirty-three years ([[@2006018|Exod 6:18]]). His son Amram became the father of Aaron and Moses ([[@2006020|Exod 6:20]]). In the wilderness the Kohathites were given the task of carrying the holy furnishings after Aaron and his sons had covered them, and they were warned not to touch the holy things ([[@4004015|Num 4:15]]).

column5: Ancestor of Sallu, a Benjamite in Jerusalem
column7: He appears in the family line of Sallu, a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile, as Sallu's great-great-grandfather ([[@16011007|Neh 11:7]]).

column5: Father of the false prophet Ahab
column7: He was the father of Ahab, who prophesied lies in the LORD's name among the exiles in Babylon ([[@24029021|Jer 29:21]]).

column5: Son of Esau and Oholibamah
column7: He was the son born to Esau's wife Oholibamah in the land of Canaan ([[@1036005|Gen 36:5]]). He later became a chief of Edom ([[@1036018|Gen 36:18]]).

column5: An Edomite chief descended from Eliphaz
column7: He was one of the Edomite chiefs descended from Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn. These were the descendants of Adah ([[@1036015-1036016|Gen 36:15-16]]).

column5: A Levite who rebelled against Moses and Aaron
column7: Korah was a great-grandson of Levi and the son of Izhar ([[@4016001|Num 16:1]]). Along with Dathan and Abiram of the tribe of Reuben and two hundred fifty leaders of the congregation, he rose up against Moses and Aaron and challenged them, saying, "You take too much on yourself" ([[@4016002-4016003|Num 16:2-3]]). Then the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them, and the two hundred fifty men offering incense were burned up by fire that came out from the LORD ([[@4016032-4016035|Num 16:32-35]]). But the sons of Korah did not die ([[@4026011|Num 26:11]]), and from their descendants came those who sang praise in the temple.

column5: Son of Hebron, a descendant of Caleb
column7: He appears in the family line of Caleb as a son of Hebron. His brothers were Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema ([[@13002042-13002043|1 Chr 2:42-43]]).

column5: Father of Shallum, a Korahite gatekeeper
column7: He was the son of Ebiasaph, a Korahite, and the father of Shallum, who kept the doors of the tabernacle ([[@13009019|1 Chr 9:19]]). The gatekeeper Meshelemiah was also 'the son of Kore' ([[@13026001|1 Chr 26:1]]).

column5: Levite gatekeeper over the freewill offerings
column7: The son of Imnah, he was a Levite who kept the east gate. In Hezekiah's time he was put in charge of the freewill offerings and distributed the LORD's offerings and the most holy things ([[@14031014|2 Chr 31:14]]).

column5: A man in the family line of Judah
column7: He appears in the family line of the descendants of Judah. He became the father of Anub, Zobebah, and the families of Aharhel the son of Harum ([[@13004001|1 Chr 4:1]]; [[@13004008|1 Chr 4:8]]).

column5: Father of Mareshah, a descendant of Shelah
column7: A descendant of Shelah the son of Judah, he is recorded as the father of Mareshah. The same verse also mentions Er the father of Lecah ([[@13004021|1 Chr 4:21]]).

column5: Rebekah's brother, father of Leah and Rachel
column7: Laban was the son of Bethuel the Syrian, who lived in Paddan Aram, and he was Rebekah's brother ([[@1028005|Gen 28:5]]). He welcomed his nephew Jacob, who had fled from Esau, but after Jacob served seven years for Rachel, Laban deceived him by giving him Leah instead ([[@1029025|Gen 29:25]]). He also changed Jacob's wages ten times, but God protected Jacob ([[@1031007|Gen 31:7]]). When Jacob left, the two of them piled up a heap of stones as a witness between them and made a covenant ([[@1031044-1031048|Gen 31:44-48]]).

column5: Near where Moses proclaimed God's words
column7: This name appears with Paran, Tophel, Hazeroth, and Dizahab in describing where Moses spoke to Israel in the wilderness of the Arabah beyond the Jordan ([[@5001001|Deut 1:1]]).

column5: Fortified city in the lowland of Judah
column6: a place that cannot be taken
column7: It was a city in the low hill country of western Judah. In Joshua's time the king of Lachish attacked Gibeon with other Amorite kings and was defeated, and Israel took the city ([[@6010032|Josh 10:32]]). Rehoboam king of Judah made it a fortified city ([[@14011009|2 Chr 11:9]]), and the king of Assyria stayed there when he attacked Judah ([[@12018014|2 Kgs 18:14]]). When the Babylonian army invaded, Lachish and Azekah were the places of which it is said "these alone remained of the cities of Judah as fortified cities" ([[@24034007|Jer 34:7]]).

column5: A man in the family line of Ephraim
column7: He appears in the family line of the descendants of Ephraim. His son was Ammihud, and next came Elishama. Joshua came from this family ([[@13007026-13007027|1 Chr 7:26-27]]).

column5: Father of Eliasaph, Gershonite leader
column7: He was the father of Eliasaph, the leader of the Gershonite families. The Gershonite families camped behind the tabernacle, on the west side ([[@4003023-4003024|Num 3:23-24]]).

column5: Son of Jahath, of the Zorathite families
column7: He appears in the family line of Judah as a son of Jahath. These were the families of the Zorathites ([[@13004002|1 Chr 4:2]]).

column5: A town in Judah's lowland
column7: It was one of the lowland towns that the tribe of Judah received, listed with Cabbon and Chitlish ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]; [[@6015040|Josh 15:40]]).

column5: Brother of Goliath
column7: He was the brother of Goliath of Gath, and the staff of his spear was like a weaver’s beam. Elhanan killed him in a war with the Philistines ([[@10021019|2 Sam 21:19]]; [[@13020005|1 Chr 20:5]]).

column5: Father of Palti, Michal’s husband
column7: He was of Gallim, the father of Palti, to whom Saul gave David’s wife Michal ([[@9025044|1 Sam 25:44]]). In 2 Samuel his son’s name appears as Paltiel ([[@10003015|2 Sam 3:15]]).

column5: A place called out as Assyria approached
column7: Isaiah called out to this place, along with Gallim and Anathoth, as he described the Assyrian king's march toward Jerusalem ([[@23010028|Isa 10:28]]; [[@23010030|Isa 10:30]]).

column5: A town on Naphtali's border
column7: This was a place on the border of the land the descendants of Naphtali received. The border ran past Jabneel to Lakkum and ended at the Jordan ([[@6019032-6019033|Josh 19:32-33]]).

column5: A descendant of Cain with two wives
column7: He was a descendant of Cain, the son of Methushael, and he took two wives, Adah and Zillah ([[@1004018-1004019|Gen 4:18-19]]). He said to his wives, "If Cain will be avenged seven times, truly Lamech seventy-seven times" ([[@1004023-1004024|Gen 4:23-24]]).

column5: Son of Methuselah, father of Noah
column7: He was a descendant of Seth, the son Methuselah had at one hundred eighty-seven ([[@1005025|Gen 5:25]]). Lamech had a son at one hundred eighty-two and named him Noah, saying that because the LORD had cursed the ground, "This one will comfort us in our work" ([[@1005028-1005029|Gen 5:28-29]]). He lived seven hundred seventy-seven years and then died ([[@1005031|Gen 5:31]]). There is another Lamech among Cain's descendants, so the two should not be confused.

column5: City in Asia, church rebuked for lukewarmness
column7: It was a city in Asia Minor, the home of one of the seven churches ([[@66001011|Rev 1:11]]). Paul said he struggled for those at Laodicea as well as the church at Colossae, and he asked that the letter to the Colossians also be read in the church of the Laodiceans ([[@51002001|Col 2:1]]; [[@51004016|Col 4:16]]). The Lord rebuked the church at Laodicea, saying, "because you are lukewarm" ([[@66003016|Rev 3:16]]). They said they were rich, but they did not know that they were really poor, blind, and naked ([[@66003017|Rev 3:17]]).

column5: Husband of the prophetess Deborah
column7: He was the husband of Deborah, the prophetess who judged Israel. The Bible introduces Deborah as "the wife of Lappidoth" ([[@7004004|Judg 4:4]]).

column5: A city of Crete near Fair Havens
column7: This was a city near a place called Fair Havens, which Paul's ship reached as it sailed along the coast of Crete on the way to Rome ([[@44027007-44027008|Acts 27:7-8]]).

column5: The far edge of Canaan's territory
column7: This place appears as the far end of the territory of the Canaanites. The border ran past Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim to Lasha ([[@1010019|Gen 10:19]]).

column5: A royal city struck by Joshua
column7: The king of Lassharon is listed among the kings Joshua and the children of Israel struck and destroyed west of the Jordan ([[@6012007|Josh 12:7]]; [[@6012018|Josh 12:18]]).

column5: The beggar in the parable of the rich man
column7: He was the beggar in Jesus' parable who lay at the rich man's gate, covered with sores ([[@42016020|Luke 16:20]]). He died and was carried by the angels to Abraham's bosom ([[@42016022|Luke 16:22]]).

column5: Brother of Martha and Mary, raised from the dead
column7: The brother of Mary and Martha of Bethany, he was someone Jesus loved ([[@43011001-43011005|John 11:1-5]]). When he fell sick and died, Jesus said, "Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep", and went to wake him ([[@43011011|John 11:11]]). When he had been dead four days, Jesus cried with a loud voice in front of the tomb, "Lazarus, come out!", and the man who had died came out with his hands and feet bound with strips of cloth ([[@43011039-43011044|John 11:39-44]]). Because many Jews came to believe in Jesus through this, the chief priests plotted to kill Lazarus as well ([[@43012010-43012011|John 12:10-11]]).

column5: Laban's older daughter, Jacob's first wife
column7: She was Laban's older daughter and Rachel's older sister. Scripture says, "Leah’s eyes were weak, but Rachel was beautiful in form and attractive" ([[@1029017|Gen 29:17]]). Jacob worked for Rachel, but Laban brought Leah to him in the evening, so Leah became Jacob's wife first ([[@1029023-1029025|Gen 29:23-25]]). Jacob loved Rachel more, but the LORD opened Leah's womb, and she gave birth to Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah ([[@1029031-1029035|Gen 29:31-35]]). Later she also gave birth to Issachar and Zebulun and a daughter, Dinah ([[@1030017-1030021|Gen 30:17-21]]).

column5: What makes dough rise
column7: Leaven is something put into dough to make it rise. Israel had to remove leaven from their houses for seven days and eat unleavened bread, and no leaven could be put into a meal offering to the LORD ([[@2012015|Exod 12:15]]; [[@3002011|Lev 2:11]]). Jesus compared the Kingdom of Heaven to leaven that a woman hid in three measures of meal until it was all leavened ([[@40013033|Matt 13:33]]). He also said, "Beware of the yeast of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy", comparing the Pharisees' hypocrisy to leaven ([[@42012001|Luke 12:1]]).

column5: A family of temple servants who returned from exile
column7: Among the temple servants who came back from exile were 'the children of Lebanah' ([[@15002043-15002045|Ezra 2:43-45]]; [[@16007047-16007048|Neh 7:47-48]]).

column5: The northern mountains famous for their cedars
column7: Lebanon is a long range of high mountains stretching across the north of Israel. When God described the borders of the land he would give Israel, Lebanon was included ([[@6001004|Josh 1:4]]). Moses begged to cross the Jordan and see that fine mountain and Lebanon ([[@5003025|Deut 3:25]]). Its cedars were excellent timber, so Solomon asked Hiram king of Tyre for cedars of Lebanon and built the temple with them ([[@11005006|1 Kgs 5:6]]). The Psalms sing that the righteous will grow "like a cedar in Lebanon" ([[@19092012|Ps 92:12]]).

column5: Mountain where the Hivites lived
column7: Among the nations the LORD left in order to test Israel were the Hivites who lived on Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon to the entrance of Hamath ([[@7003001-7003003|Judg 3:1-3]]).

column5: A valley below Mount Hermon
column7: It was the northern edge of the land Joshua conquered; he struck as far as Baal Gad in the valley of Lebanon under Mount Hermon ([[@6011017|Josh 11:17]]; [[@6012007|Josh 12:7]]).

column5: A town at Judah's far south
column7: It was one of the southern towns of the tribe of Judah toward the border of Edom, listed with Ziklag, Madmannah, and Sansannah ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015031|Josh 15:31]]).

column5: A landmark for finding Shiloh
column7: This place is mentioned in describing the location of Shiloh, where the LORD's feast was held. Shiloh was north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and east of the highway that goes up from Bethel to Shechem ([[@7021019|Judg 21:19]]).

column5: A name linked with Er, descendant of Shelah
column7: This name appears in the family line of the descendants of Shelah the son of Judah. Er, a descendant of Shelah, is recorded as the father of Lecah ([[@13004021|1 Chr 4:21]]).

column5: The name a host of demons gave themselves
column7: Legion is a word for a large unit of the Roman army, and it is the name the demon-possessed man gave himself. In the country of the Gadarenes, when Jesus asked the man with an unclean spirit his name, he answered, "My name is Legion, for we are many" ([[@41005001|Mark 5:1]], 9). Luke explains that this was because many demons had entered into him ([[@42008030|Luke 8:30]]). When Jesus gave them permission, the demons entered a herd of pigs, and the herd of about two thousand drowned in the sea. The man was then sitting there, clothed and in his right mind ([[@41005013|Mark 5:13]], 15).

column5: Grandson of Ham, son of Mizraim
column7: They were among the descendants of Mizraim, Ham’s son, listed with the Ludim and the Anamim ([[@1010006|Gen 10:6]]; [[@1010013|Gen 10:13]]; [[@13001011|1 Chr 1:11]]).

column5: Where Samson struck down the Philistines
column7: It was where the Philistines camped in Judah, and here Samson struck down the Philistines with the jawbone of a donkey ([[@7015009|Judg 15:9]]; [[@7015014-7015016|Judg 15:14-16]]). God made a spring burst out at this place ([[@7015019|Judg 15:19]]).

column5: A king taught by his mother
column7: Proverbs 31 is the words of King Lemuel, the teaching his mother gave him ([[@20031001|Prov 31:1]]). His mother told him that wine and strong drink are not fitting for kings ([[@20031004|Prov 31:4]]).

column5: Serious skin disease regarded as unclean
column7: In the Bible, leprosy refers to a serious skin disease that made a person unclean. When someone had a disease on the skin, he was brought to the priest to be examined and declared clean or unclean ([[@3013002-3013003|Lev 13:2-3]]). A leper had to wear torn clothes, cry out, "Unclean! Unclean!", and live alone outside the camp ([[@3013045-3013046|Lev 13:45-46]]). Jesus touched a leper, said, "Be made clean", and healed him ([[@40008003|Matt 8:3]]). Scholars differ on whether this disease in the Bible is exactly the same as today's Hansen's disease.

column5: A people descended from Dedan
column7: This was a people descended from Dedan, the son of Jokshan, whom Abraham's later wife Keturah bore to him ([[@1025001-1025003|Gen 25:1-3]]).

column5: A people descended from Dedan
column7: This was a people descended from Dedan, the son of Jokshan, whom Abraham's later wife Keturah bore to him. They are listed with the Letushim ([[@1025001-1025003|Gen 25:1-3]]).

column5: Jacob's third son, ancestor of the tribe of Levi
column7: He was the third son born to Jacob and Leah. Leah named him Levi, saying, "Now this time my husband will be joined to me" ([[@1029034|Gen 29:34]]). Over the matter of his sister Dinah, he and Simeon killed the men of the city of Shechem ([[@1034025|Gen 34:25]]).
