His descendants, the tribe of Levi, received no land as an inheritance but were given the work of serving at the tabernacle and its offerings ([[@4003006|Num 3:6]]; [[@5018001|Deut 18:1]]).

column5: A man in Jesus' genealogy in Luke
column7: He appears in Jesus' genealogy in the Gospel of Luke. His name comes in the generation before Matthat and after Melchi ([[@42003024|Luke 3:24]]).

column5: A man in Jesus' genealogy in Luke
column7: He appears in Jesus' genealogy in the Gospel of Luke. His name comes in the generation before Matthat and after Simeon ([[@42003029-42003030|Luke 3:29-30]]).

column5: Levi's descendant serving at the tabernacle and temple
column7: Levites were the descendants of Levi, Jacob's son; in a broad sense the word refers to the whole tribe of Levi. God chose the Levites in place of Israel's firstborn to assist Aaron the priest and take charge of the work of the Tent of Meeting ([[@4003006-4003012|Num 3:6-12]]). Instead of an inheritance of land they received Israel's tithes, and they lived in forty-eight towns scattered among the lands of the tribes ([[@4018021|Num 18:21]]; [[@6021041|Josh 21:41]]). Aaron's descendants became priests, and the other Levites served in the temple and helped with the work of purification ([[@13023028|1 Chr 23:28]]).

column5: A place where Israel camped in the wilderness
column7: It was a place where the people of Israel camped as they passed through the wilderness. They came from Rimmon Perez and camped here, then went on to Rissah ([[@4033020-4033021|Num 33:20-21]]).

column5: A Canaanite town Joshua struck, later a priests' town
column7: A Canaanite town in the southern lowland; Joshua struck it and its king and destroyed them ([[@6010029-6010030|Josh 10:29-30]]). It later became part of Judah and was one of the towns given to the priests, the descendants of Aaron ([[@6021013|Josh 21:13]]). In the days of Jehoram king of Judah, Libnah even revolted ([[@12008022|2 Kgs 8:22]]). When Sennacherib king of Assyria attacked Judah, he fought here ([[@12019008|2 Kgs 19:8]]).

column5: Grandson of Levi, son of Gershon
column7: He was a grandson of Levi and one of the two sons of Gershon, and his brother was Shimei ([[@2006017|Exod 6:17]]). From him came the family of the Libnites, part of the Levite clan of the Gershonites ([[@4003021|Num 3:21]]). In the wilderness the sons of Gershon were in charge of the tabernacle, the tent, its covering, the screens, and similar things ([[@4003025-4003026|Num 3:25-26]]). The genealogy in 1 Chronicles says his son was Jahath ([[@13006020|1 Chr 6:20]]).

column5: Son of Mahli, a descendant of Merari
column7: He appears in the family line of Merari the son of Levi. He was the son of Mahli, and his son was Shimei ([[@13006029|1 Chr 6:29]]).

column5: North African land west of Egypt
column7: It was a land in North Africa, west of Egypt. Among the people gathered in Jerusalem at Pentecost were those from "the parts of Libya around Cyrene" ([[@44002010|Acts 2:10]]). In the Old Testament the people of this region seem to be called 'Lubim,' and the seer Hanani reminded King Asa that because he relied on the LORD he had defeated "the Ethiopians and the Lubim" with their huge army ([[@14016008|2 Chr 16:8]]). Daniel contains the prophecy, "The Libyans and the Ethiopians will follow his steps" ([[@27011043|Dan 11:43]]). Scholars differ on which Old Testament names refer to this land.

column5: Son of Shemida, of Manasseh
column7: He appears in the family line of Manasseh, recorded as a son of Shemida along with Ahian, Shechem, and Aniam ([[@13007019|1 Chr 7:19]]).

column5: A believer who greeted Timothy
column7: At the end of Paul's letter to Timothy, he was one of those who sent greetings to Timothy, along with Eubulus, Pudens, and Claudia ([[@55004021|2 Tim 4:21]]).

column5: Son of Hosea
column7: This is the name the LORD gave to the son born to Hosea and Gomer. The name carries the words "you are not my people" ([[@28001008-28001009|Hos 1:8-9]]).

column5: Where Mephibosheth lived
column7: It was the place where Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, lived in the house of Machir the son of Ammiel. David sent for him and brought him from there ([[@10009004-10009005|2 Sam 9:4-5]]).

column5: Hosea’s daughter, a name with a message
column7: She was the daughter Hosea’s wife Gomer bore, and God gave her this name to show that he would no longer have mercy on the house of Israel ([[@28001006|Hos 1:6]]).

column5: Benjamite town, the Lydda of the New Testament
column7: It is a town named in the genealogy of Benjamin, where the record says that the sons of Elpaal "built Ono and Lod, with its towns" ([[@13008012|1 Chr 8:12]]). Among those who returned from Babylon were the people of Lod, Hadid, and Ono, and after the return the descendants of Benjamin lived in Lod ([[@15002033|Ezra 2:33]]; [[@16011031|Neh 11:31]], 35). In the New Testament it was called Lydda, and there Peter healed Aeneas, who had been bedridden and paralyzed for eight years ([[@44009033-44009034|Acts 9:33-34]]).

column5: Grandmother of Timothy
column7: She was Timothy's grandmother. Paul says that sincere faith lived first in Lois and Eunice and is in Timothy too ([[@55001005|2 Tim 1:5]]).

column5: The bread and cup that remember Jesus' death
column7: The Lord's Supper is the holy meal the church shares together, remembering the bread and cup Jesus gave on the night he was betrayed. Paul rebuked the Corinthian church because when they gathered, each one ate his own supper first, so that one was hungry and another was drunk, and he told them, "it is not the Lord’s supper that you eat" ([[@46011020-46011021|1 Cor 11:20-21]]). The Lord Jesus took bread, gave thanks, broke it, and said, "Do this in memory of me" ([[@46011023-46011024|1 Cor 11:23-24]]). So Paul said that every time we eat this bread and drink this cup, we proclaim the Lord's death until he comes ([[@46011026|1 Cor 11:26]]).

column5: Abraham's nephew, rescued from Sodom
column7: He was the son of Haran and Abraham's nephew ([[@1011027|Gen 11:27]]). He came to Canaan with Abraham, but because they had so much livestock that their herdsmen quarreled, he chose the well-watered plain of the Jordan and moved his tent as far as Sodom ([[@1013010-1013012|Gen 13:10-12]]). When God destroyed Sodom, the angels took him by the hand and led him out of the city, and his wife, who looked back, became a pillar of salt ([[@1019016-1019026|Gen 19:16-26]]). Peter called him "righteous Lot" ([[@61002007|2 Pet 2:7]]).

column5: A son of Seir the Horite
column7: He was a son of Seir the Horite, the native people of that land ([[@1036020|Gen 36:20]]). He was one of the chiefs of the Horites ([[@1036029|Gen 36:29]]).

column5: Something drawn to decide matters or divide shares
column7: Lots were something drawn to decide a matter or to divide up shares. Under the law, Aaron was to cast lots for the two goats, setting one apart for the LORD and the other for the scapegoat ([[@3016008|Lev 16:8]]). Joshua cast lots before the LORD in Shiloh and divided the land among the tribes ([[@6018010|Josh 18:10]]). The Bible says, "The lot is cast into the lap, but its every decision is from the LORD" ([[@20016033|Prov 16:33]]). After Jesus went up to heaven, the disciples drew lots and added Matthias to the eleven apostles ([[@44001026|Acts 1:26]]).

column5: A prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch
column7: He was from Cyrene, and with Barnabas, Saul, and others he was a prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch ([[@44013001|Acts 13:1]]).

column5: Son of Shem, brother of Elam and Aram
column7: He was the son of Noah's son Shem and the brother of Elam, Asshur, Arpachshad, and Aram ([[@1010022|Gen 10:22]]; [[@13001017|1 Chr 1:17]]). In the prophets, 'Lud' appears as the name of a people: Isaiah spoke of "Lud, who draw the bow," and Ezekiel said men of Lud served as soldiers in the army of Tyre ([[@23066019|Isa 66:19]]; [[@26027010|Ezek 27:10]]). Scholars differ on whether this people descended from Lud the son of Shem or is connected with the 'Ludim' whose father was Mizraim the son of Ham ([[@1010013|Gen 10:13]]).

column5: Grandson of Ham, son of Mizraim
column7: They were among the descendants of Mizraim, Ham’s son, listed with the Anamim and the Lehabim ([[@1010006|Gen 10:6]]; [[@1010013|Gen 10:13]]; [[@13001011|1 Chr 1:11]]).

column5: An ascent in Moab
column7: It appears in the prophecies of judgment on Moab, which say the Moabites go up the ascent of Luhith weeping ([[@23015005|Isa 15:5]]; [[@24048005|Jer 48:5]]).

column5: Paul's coworker, the beloved physician
column7: He was the coworker Paul called 'Luke the beloved physician' ([[@51004014|Col 4:14]]; [[@57001024|Phlm 1:24]]). While Paul was in prison, he wrote, "Only Luke is with me" ([[@55004011|2 Tim 4:11]]).

column5: A city built in the land of the Hittites
column7: Luz was also the old name of Bethel. The man who showed the way into the city of Bethel went to the land of the Hittites, built a city, and named it Luz ([[@7001023-7001026|Judg 1:23-26]]).

column5: The region of Lystra and Derbe
column7: It was the region Paul and Barnabas fled to from Iconium, where the two cities of Lystra and Derbe were ([[@44014006|Acts 14:6]]). The crowd there shouted in the language of Lycaonia ([[@44014011|Acts 14:11]]).

column5: The region where Myra stood
column7: This was the region where the city of Myra stood, which Paul's ship reached on the way to Rome after sailing across the sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia ([[@44027005|Acts 27:5]]).

column5: A seller of purple who believed at Philippi
column7: She was a seller of purple from the city of Thyatira, and the Lord opened her heart to listen to what Paul said ([[@44016014|Acts 16:14]]). After Paul and Silas came out of prison, they met the brothers at Lydia’s house ([[@44016040|Acts 16:40]]).

column5: Tetrarch of Abilene
column7: He was tetrarch of Abilene in the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar. At that time the word of God came to John, the son of Zacharias, in the wilderness ([[@42003001-42003002|Luke 3:1-2]]).

column5: The commanding officer who protected Paul
column7: He was Claudius Lysias, the commanding officer who wrote a letter about Paul to Governor Felix ([[@44023025-44023026|Acts 23:25-26]]). Felix put off the case, saying he would decide it when Lysias the commanding officer came down ([[@44024022|Acts 24:22]]).

column5: City in Lycaonia where Paul was stoned
column7: It was a city in Lycaonia where Paul and Barnabas came to preach the Good News after escaping persecution in Iconium ([[@44014006-44014007|Acts 14:6-7]]). When Paul made a man who had been lame from birth stand up, the crowd said the gods had come down in human form, called Barnabas 'Jupiter' and Paul 'Mercury,' and tried to offer sacrifices to them ([[@44014008-44014013|Acts 14:8-13]]). But Jews who came from Antioch and Iconium stirred up the crowd, and they stoned Paul and dragged him out of the city, thinking he was dead ([[@44014019|Acts 14:19]]). When Paul came to Lystra again, there was a disciple there named Timothy, who was well spoken of by the brothers ([[@44016001-44016002|Acts 16:1-2]]).

column5: Son of Nahor's concubine Reumah
column7: Maacah was one of the sons borne by Reumah, the concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother, listed with Tebah, Gaham, and Tahash ([[@1022024|Gen 22:24]]).

column5: Northern land east of the Jordan, near Geshur
column7: This was a land and its people near Geshur, toward Mount Hermon and Bashan ([[@6012005|Josh 12:5]]). Its name is also written 'Maacath'; Jair the son of Manasseh took all the region of Argob as far as the border of the Geshurites and the Maacathites ([[@5003014|Deut 3:14]]). Because the children of Israel did not drive out the Geshurites and the Maacathites, they lived among Israel for a long time ([[@6013013|Josh 13:13]]). In David's time the Ammonites hired the king of Maacah with a thousand men, along with Syrians, to fight David ([[@10010006|2 Sam 10:6]]).

column5: David’s wife, mother of Absalom
column7: She was the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur and the mother of Absalom, the third son born to David in Hebron ([[@10003003|2 Sam 3:3]]; [[@13003002|1 Chr 3:2]]).

column5: Rehoboam's wife, mother of King Abijah
column7: She was a descendant of Absalom, and she became the wife of Rehoboam king of Judah and bore Abijah ([[@14011020|2 Chr 11:20]]). Of all his many wives and concubines, Rehoboam loved Maacah most, and he made her son Abijah chief among his brothers ([[@14011021-14011022|2 Chr 11:21-22]]). Kings records Maacah, the mother of King Abijam, as 'the daughter of Abishalom' ([[@11015002|1 Kgs 15:2]]). In King Asa's time Maacah made an abominable image for an Asherah, so Asa removed her from being queen mother and burned the image ([[@11015013|1 Kgs 15:13]]).

column5: Concubine of Caleb
column7: She was Caleb's concubine and bore Sheber and Tirhanah. She also bore Shaaph the father of Madmannah, and Sheva the father of Machbena and of Gibea ([[@13002048-13002049|1 Chr 2:48-49]]).

column5: Wife of Machir, son of Manasseh
column7: She was the sister of Huppim and Shuppim and became the wife of Machir ([[@13007015|1 Chr 7:15]]). She bore a son named Peresh, and his brother was Sheresh ([[@13007016|1 Chr 7:16]]).

column5: Wife of Jeiel, father of Gibeon
column7: She was the wife of Jeiel the father of Gibeon, who lived in Gibeon ([[@13008029|1 Chr 8:29]]; [[@13009035|1 Chr 9:35]]). Saul came from their descendants ([[@13009036|1 Chr 9:36]]; [[@13009039|1 Chr 9:39]]).

column5: Father of Hanan, one of David's mighty men
column7: He was the father of Hanan, who appears in the list of David's mighty men. Hanan is listed alongside Joshaphat the Mithnite ([[@13011043|1 Chr 11:43]]).

column5: Father of Shephatiah, ruler of the Simeonites
column7: He was the father of Shephatiah, who in David's time was the ruler over the Simeonites among the officers in charge of the tribes of Israel ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]).

column5: A son of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a descendant of Bani listed among those in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Played David's instruments at the wall dedication
column7: At the dedication of Jerusalem's wall he was one of Zechariah's brothers, marching in the procession with the musical instruments of David the man of God ([[@16012035-16012036|Neh 12:35-36]]).

column5: A town in Judah's hill country
column7: It was one of the hill-country towns that the tribe of Judah received, listed with Beth Anoth and Eltekon ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015059|Josh 15:59]]).

column5: Where Israel's ambush broke out
column7: This is the place where Israel's ambush lay hidden and then broke out when Israel fought against Benjamin ([[@7020029|Judg 20:29]]; [[@7020033|Judg 20:33]]).

column5: A priest in Jerusalem after the exile
column7: He was the son of Adiel, a priest descended from Immer who lived in Jerusalem after the exile ([[@13009012|1 Chr 9:12]]). In Nehemiah he is called 'Amashsai' ([[@16011013|Neh 11:13]]).

column5: A Levite who played the harp in David’s time
column7: He was one of the Levites of the second rank appointed when David brought up the ark ([[@13015018|1 Chr 15:18]]). He was assigned to play a stringed instrument set to Alamoth ([[@13015020|1 Chr 15:20]]).

column5: Captain who joined Jehoiada's covenant
column7: The son of Adaiah, he was a captain of hundreds. In the seventh year, when Jehoiada strengthened himself, he made a covenant with him together with the other captains ([[@14023001|2 Chr 23:1]]).

column5: Officer who counted Uzziah's soldiers
column7: He was an officer in King Uzziah's time who, with Jeiel the scribe, made the count of the fighting men ([[@14026011|2 Chr 26:11]]).

column5: King's son killed by Zichri
column7: He was the king's son who was killed by Zichri, a mighty man of Ephraim, when Israel attacked Judah in the days of King Ahaz of Judah ([[@14028006-14028007|2 Chr 28:6-7]]).

column5: City governor sent to repair the temple
column7: He was the governor of the city in King Josiah's time. The king sent him with Shaphan and Joah to repair the house of the LORD ([[@14034008|2 Chr 34:8]]).

column5: Priest of Jeshua's family with a foreign wife
column7: He was a priest of the descendants of Jeshua who had married a foreign woman. These men pledged to put away their wives and offered a guilt offering ([[@15010018-15010019|Ezra 10:18-19]]).

column5: A son of Harim who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a descendant of Harim listed among those in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010021|Ezra 10:21]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A son of Pashhur who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a descendant of Pashhur listed among those in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010022|Ezra 10:22]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A son of Pahathmoab who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a descendant of Pahathmoab listed among those in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010030|Ezra 10:30]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Father of Azariah, who repaired the wall
column7: He was the son of Ananiah. In Nehemiah's time his son Azariah repaired the part of the wall beside his own house ([[@16003023|Neh 3:23]]).

column5: Stood at Ezra's right as the law was read
column7: He was one of the men who stood at the right hand of Ezra the scribe as Ezra stood on a wooden pulpit and read the law ([[@16008004|Neh 8:4]]).

column5: Helped the people understand the law
column7: When Ezra read the book of the law, he was one of those who, with the Levites, helped the people understand the law ([[@16008007-16008008|Neh 8:7-8]]).

column5: A chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: He appears in the list of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010025|Neh 10:25]]).

column5: A man of Judah living in Jerusalem
column7: He was a descendant of Judah who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile. He was the son of Baruch and a seventh-generation descendant of the Shilonite ([[@16011004-16011005|Neh 11:4-5]]).

column5: Ancestor of Sallu, a Benjamite in Jerusalem
column7: He appears in the family line of Sallu, a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile, as Sallu's great-great-great-grandfather ([[@16011007|Neh 11:7]]).

column5: Priest with a trumpet at the wall dedication
column7: He was one of the priests who stood in God's house with trumpets at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall ([[@16012040-16012041|Neh 12:40-41]]).

column5: Stood with others at the wall dedication
column7: He was one of those who stood with the trumpet-bearing priests at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall. At that time the singers sang loudly ([[@16012041-16012042|Neh 12:41-42]]).

column5: Father of Zephaniah the priest
column7: He was the father of Zephaniah, whom King Zedekiah sent to Jeremiah ([[@24021001|Jer 21:1]]; [[@24037003|Jer 37:3]]). Zephaniah was called 'the son of Maaseiah the priest' ([[@24029025|Jer 29:25]]).

column5: Father of the false prophet Zedekiah
column7: He was the father of Zedekiah, who prophesied lies in the LORD's name among the exiles in Babylon ([[@24029021|Jer 29:21]]).

column5: Son of Shallum, keeper of the temple threshold
column7: The son of Shallum, he was a keeper of the threshold at the temple. The room where Jeremiah brought the Rechabites was above Maaseiah's room ([[@24035003-24035004|Jer 35:3-4]]).

column5: A man in Jesus' genealogy in Luke
column7: He appears in Jesus' genealogy in the Gospel of Luke. His name comes in the generation before Naggai and after Mattathias ([[@42003025-42003026|Luke 3:25-26]]).

column5: Son of Ram, Jerahmeel's firstborn
column7: He appears in the family line of Judah as a son of Ram, the firstborn of Jerahmeel ([[@13002025|1 Chr 2:25]]; [[@13002027|1 Chr 2:27]]).

column5: The twenty-fourth priestly division
column7: His is the name drawn twenty-fourth when the priests descended from Aaron were divided into divisions by lot in David's time ([[@13024005|1 Chr 24:5]]; [[@13024018|1 Chr 24:18]]).

column5: A priest who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the priests who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s day ([[@16010008|Neh 10:8]]). Some think he belongs to the same family as 'Maadiah', a priest who returned with Zerubbabel ([[@16012005|Neh 12:5]]).

column5: Northern Greek region Paul crossed to after a vision
column7: It was a Roman province in the north of Greece. In a vision at night Paul saw a man of Macedonia begging him to "Come over into Macedonia and help us" and he set out for there at once ([[@44016009-44016010|Acts 16:9-10]]). Philippi was the first city of that district of Macedonia ([[@44016012|Acts 16:12]]), and the gospel also reached Thessalonica and Berea. Even in deep poverty, the churches of Macedonia gave generously with overflowing joy for the believers in Jerusalem ([[@47008001-47008002|2 Cor 8:1-2]]).

column5: A Gadite warrior who came to David
column7: He was the eleventh of the Gadite warriors who came over to David. These were men trained for war who could handle shield and spear ([[@13012008|1 Chr 12:8]]; [[@13012013|1 Chr 12:13]]).

column5: Name with Sheva recorded as its father
column7: This name appears in the family line of Caleb. Sheva, born to Caleb's concubine Maacah, is recorded as the father of Machbena and Gibea ([[@13002048-13002049|1 Chr 2:48-49]]).

column5: Father of Geuel, the spy from Gad
column7: He was the father of Geuel, the representative of the tribe of Gad among the twelve men sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013002|Num 13:2]]; [[@4013015|Num 13:15]]).

column5: Manasseh's firstborn and father of Gilead
column7: He was the firstborn son of Manasseh the son of Joseph, and while Joseph was still alive, Machir's children were raised on Joseph's knees ([[@1050023|Gen 50:23]]). He became the father of Gilead and the ancestor of the family of the Machirites ([[@4026029|Num 26:29]]). The descendants of Machir took Gilead and drove out the Amorites there, and Moses gave Gilead to Machir ([[@4032039-4032040|Num 32:39-40]]). The Song of Deborah also says, "Governors come down out of Machir" ([[@7005014|Judg 5:14]]).

column5: A man of Lo Debar who cared for Mephibosheth
column7: He was the son of Ammiel who lived in Lo Debar, and Jonathan’s son Mephibosheth was in his house ([[@10009004-10009006|2 Sam 9:4-6]]). When David came to Mahanaim, he brought food along with Barzillai and others ([[@10017027-10017029|2 Sam 17:27-29]]).

column5: A son of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a descendant of Bani listed among those in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]; [[@15010040|Ezra 10:40]]).

column5: Family burial place at Hebron bought by Abraham
column7: It was a field in front of Mamre, that is, Hebron, with a cave in it. When Sarah died, Abraham weighed out four hundred shekels of silver to Ephron the Hittite, bought this field and cave, and buried Sarah there ([[@1023016-1023019|Gen 23:16-19]]). When Abraham died, his sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him there too ([[@1025009|Gen 25:9]]). Jacob said that Abraham and Sarah, Isaac and Rebekah, and Leah were buried there and asked to be buried there himself, and his sons did as he said ([[@1049029-1049031|Gen 49:29-31]]; [[@1050013|Gen 50:13]]).

column5: Son of Japheth
column7: He was one of the sons of Japheth, Noah’s son, a brother of Gomer, Magog, and Javan ([[@1010002|Gen 10:2]]; [[@13001005|1 Chr 1:5]]).

column5: A town in southern Judah
column7: It was one of the towns in the south of Judah near the border of Edom ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015031|Josh 15:31]]). Its name appears with Ziklag and Sansannah.

column5: Name with Shaaph recorded as its father
column7: This name appears in the family line of Caleb. Shaaph, born to Caleb's concubine Maacah, is recorded as the father of Madmannah ([[@13002048-13002049|1 Chr 2:48-49]]).

column5: A place in Moab under judgment
column7: This place appears in Jeremiah's message about Moab and received the warning, "You also, Madmen, will be brought to silence. The sword will pursue you." ([[@24048001-24048002|Jer 48:1-2]]).

column5: A place that fled before Assyria
column7: This place appears where Isaiah describes the Assyrian king's march toward Jerusalem, saying, "Madmenah is a fugitive" ([[@23010028|Isa 10:28]]; [[@23010031|Isa 10:31]]).

column5: A Canaanite city whose king Joshua struck
column7: Among the kings Jabin king of Hazor called together was Jobab king of Madon ([[@6011001|Josh 11:1]]). The king of Madon is in the list of kings Joshua struck and destroyed ([[@6012019|Josh 12:19]]).

column5: Land by the Sea of Galilee where Jesus sailed
column7: This is where Jesus went by boat after feeding the four thousand and sending the crowds away ([[@40015039|Matt 15:39]]). Mark, telling the same event, calls it "the region of Dalmanutha" ([[@41008010|Mark 8:10]]). It seems to have been on the west shore of the Sea of Galilee, and many think it was the same place as Magdala, the hometown of Mary Magdalene, or near it. Still, scholars differ on its exact location.

column5: Descendants of Magbish who returned
column7: This name appears in the list of those who returned from exile in Babylon. The descendants of Magbish numbered one hundred fifty-six ([[@15002030|Ezra 2:30]]).

column5: A chief of Edom descended from Esau
column7: He was one of the chiefs of Edom descended from Esau, listed just before chief Iram ([[@1036043|Gen 36:43]]; [[@13001054|1 Chr 1:54]]).

column5: Son of Japheth
column7: He was one of the sons of Japheth, Noah’s son, a brother of Gomer, Madai, and Javan ([[@1010002|Gen 10:2]]; [[@13001005|1 Chr 1:5]]).

column5: The land of Gog in Ezekiel’s prophecy
column7: Ezekiel prophesied against Gog of the land of Magog ([[@26038002|Ezek 38:2]]). The LORD said he would send fire on Magog, and 'Gog and Magog' also appear in Revelation ([[@26039006|Ezek 39:6]]; [[@66020008|Rev 20:8]]).

column5: A leader of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: In Nehemiah’s time his name appears among the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010020|Neh 10:20]]).

column5: Son of Kenan, ancestor before the Flood
column7: He was a descendant of Seth, the son Kenan had at seventy ([[@1005012|Gen 5:12]]). Mahalalel became the father of Jared at sixty-five, and after that he lived eight hundred thirty years and had other children ([[@1005015-1005016|Gen 5:15-16]]). He lived eight hundred ninety-five years and then died ([[@1005017|Gen 5:17]]). His name also appears in the genealogies of Chronicles and Luke ([[@13001002|1 Chr 1:2]]; [[@42003037|Luke 3:37]]).

column5: An ancestor of Athaiah, who lived in Jerusalem after the exile
column7: Among the children of Judah who lived in Jerusalem after the exile, Athaiah of the children of Perez is listed as a descendant of Mahalalel five generations down ([[@16011004|Neh 11:4]]).

column5: Daughter of Ishmael, wife of Esau
column7: She was the daughter of Abraham's son Ishmael and the sister of Nebaioth, and she became Esau's wife. When Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan did not please his father Isaac, he took Mahalath as a wife in addition to the wives he already had ([[@1028008-1028009|Gen 28:8-9]]). Some take the woman called "Basemath, Ishmael’s daughter, sister of Nebaioth" in Genesis 36 to be the same person as Mahalath ([[@1036003|Gen 36:3]]). This Basemath bore Reuel to Esau ([[@1036004|Gen 36:4]]).

column5: Rehoboam’s wife, daughter of Jerimoth
column7: She was the daughter of Jerimoth the son of David, and she became Rehoboam’s wife. Her mother was Abihail, the daughter of Eliab the son of Jesse ([[@14011018|2 Chr 11:18]]).

column5: Town east of the Jordan, David's refuge
column7: A place east of the Jordan, named by Jacob when he met the angels of God and said, "This is God’s army" ([[@1032002|Gen 32:2]]). It later became a Levitical town in the tribe of Gad ([[@6021038|Josh 21:38]]). After Saul died, Abner brought Ishbosheth here and made him king ([[@10002008|2 Sam 2:8]]). When Absalom rebelled, David fled to Mahanaim, and people like Barzillai fed him and helped him ([[@10017027|2 Sam 17:27]]).

column5: A place between Zorah and Eshtaol
column7: It was a place between Zorah and Eshtaol, where the LORD’s Spirit first began to move Samson ([[@7013025|Judg 13:25]]). The place behind Kiriath Jearim where the Danites camped was also called Mahaneh Dan ([[@7018012|Judg 18:12]]).

column5: A Netophathite, one of David’s mighty men
column7: He was a Netophathite and one of David’s mighty men ([[@10023028|2 Sam 23:28]]). Of the Zerahites, he became captain for the tenth month, with twenty-four thousand in his division ([[@13027013|1 Chr 27:13]]).

column5: A Levite who cleansed the temple under Hezekiah
column7: He was the son of Amasai, of the Kohathites. In Hezekiah’s day he was one of the Levites who arose, gathered their brothers, sanctified themselves, and cleansed the LORD’s house ([[@14029012|2 Chr 29:12]]; [[@14029015|2 Chr 29:15]]).

column5: A Levite overseeing offerings under Hezekiah
column7: In Hezekiah’s time he was one of the overseers under Conaniah, who was in charge of the offerings and tithes, and his brother Shimei ([[@14031012-14031013|2 Chr 31:12-13]]).

column5: The people of David’s warrior Eliel
column7: The list of David’s mighty men includes "Eliel the Mahavite" ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011046|1 Chr 11:46]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a temple singer
column7: He was one of the sons of Heman, who served in song in David’s day ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]). The twenty-third lot fell to him, and he served with his sons and brothers, twelve in all ([[@13025030|1 Chr 25:30]]).

column5: Isaiah’s son, a name with a message
column7: It was the name the LORD told Isaiah to write on a large tablet ([[@23008001|Isa 8:1]]). When Isaiah’s wife bore a son, the LORD told him to call his name Maher Shalal Hash Baz ([[@23008003|Isa 8:3]]).

column5: A daughter of Zelophehad
column7: She was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh ([[@4026033|Num 26:33]]). With her sisters she came to Moses to ask for her father's inheritance ([[@4027001|Num 27:1]]).

column5: A child of Hammolecheth
column7: The name appears among the children of Hammolecheth in the genealogy of Gilead of the tribe of Manasseh ([[@13007017-13007018|1 Chr 7:17-18]]).

column5: Son of Merari, ancestor of the Mahlite family
column7: He was the son of Merari, the son of Levi, and his brother was Mushi ([[@4003020|Num 3:20]]). Exodus also names him among the sons of Merari ([[@2006019|Exod 6:19]]). His descendants formed the family of the Mahlites, which together with the family of the Mushites made up the families of Merari ([[@4003033|Num 3:33]]). 1 Chronicles names Eleazar and Kish as the sons of Mahli; Eleazar died without sons and had only daughters, so the sons of Kish married them ([[@13023021-13023022|1 Chr 23:21-22]]).

column5: Grandson of Merari, son of Mushi
column7: He was a grandson of Merari son of Levi, and the son of Mushi ([[@13023023|1 Chr 23:23]]; [[@13024030|1 Chr 24:30]]). He also appears in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles 6 ([[@13006047|1 Chr 6:47]]).

column5: Son of Elimelech and Naomi, Ruth's husband
column7: He was the son of Elimelech and Naomi of Bethlehem, and he died in the land of Moab ([[@8001002|Ruth 1:2]]; [[@8001005|Ruth 1:5]]). Boaz took 'Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon' as his wife ([[@8004010|Ruth 4:10]]).

column5: Father of Heman the wise man
column7: He was the father of Heman, named among "the sons of Mahol" when Solomon’s wisdom is compared with others. Solomon was wiser than they were ([[@11004031|1 Kgs 4:31]]).

column5: Grandfather of Baruch and Seraiah
column7: He was the father of Neriah and the grandfather of Baruch, to whom Jeremiah gave the deed of purchase ([[@24032012|Jer 32:12]]). Seraiah, the chief quartermaster, was also 'the grandson of Mahseiah' ([[@24051059|Jer 51:59]]).

column5: A place under Solomon’s officer Ben Deker
column7: It was one of the places under Ben Deker, one of the twelve officers Solomon appointed to provide food ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004009|1 Kgs 4:9]]).

column5: A place where Israel camped in the wilderness
column7: It was a place where the people of Israel camped as they passed through the wilderness. They came from Haradah and camped here, then went on to Tahath ([[@4033025-4033026|Num 33:25-26]]).

column5: Canaanite town where five kings hid in a cave
column7: It was a Canaanite town conquered by Joshua. When the armies of the five Amorite kings who had gathered against Gibeon were defeated, Joshua chased them as far as Azekah and Makkedah ([[@6010005|Josh 10:5]], 10). The five kings fled and hid in the cave at Makkedah, and Joshua had the mouth of the cave blocked with large stones and guarded ([[@6010016-6010018|Josh 10:16-18]]). After the battle he brought the kings out, put them to death, hung them on five trees, and then threw them into that cave, and that same day he also took the town of Makkedah ([[@6010026-6010028|Josh 10:26-28]]). The king of Makkedah also appears in the list of kings Joshua defeated ([[@6012016|Josh 12:16]]).

column5: The prophet of the book of Malachi
column7: The book of Malachi begins with the words "A revelation, the LORD’s word to Israel by Malachi" ([[@39001001|Mal 1:1]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Shaharaim
column7: In the genealogy of Benjamin, he was one of the sons Shaharaim had by his wife Hodesh in the land of Moab ([[@13008008-13008009|1 Chr 8:8-9]]).

column5: A son of King Saul
column7: He was a son of King Saul ([[@9014049|1 Sam 14:49]]), and he died in battle against the Philistines along with Jonathan and Abinadab ([[@9031002|1 Sam 31:2]]).

column5: Father of Pashhur
column7: He was the father of Pashhur, whom King Zedekiah sent to Jeremiah ([[@24021001|Jer 21:1]]). In Jeremiah 38 his son Pashhur is with the princes who wanted Jeremiah put to death ([[@24038001-24038004|Jer 38:1-4]]).

column5: Grandson of Asher, son of Beriah
column7: He was a son of Beriah, Asher’s son ([[@1046017|Gen 46:17]]). The family of the Malchielites came from him, and he was the father of Birzaith ([[@4026045|Num 26:45]]; [[@13007031|1 Chr 7:31]]).

column5: A Gershonite ancestor of Asaph
column7: In the genealogy of Asaph, the Levite singer, he is the son of Ethni and the father of Baaseiah. He was a descendant of Gershom ([[@13006039-13006043|1 Chr 6:39-43]]).

column5: Ancestor of Adaiah the priest
column7: He was an ancestor of Adaiah, a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the exile, and his name comes at the end of that genealogy ([[@13009012|1 Chr 9:12]]; [[@16011012|Neh 11:12]]).

column5: The fifth priestly division
column7: When the divisions of Aaron’s descendants were assigned by lot in David’s time, he was the one chosen fifth ([[@13024007-13024009|1 Chr 24:7-9]]).

column5: A descendant of Harim who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Harim who had married foreign women ([[@15010031|Ezra 10:31]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Son of Harim who repaired the wall
column7: He was the son of Harim, and with Hasshub the son of Pahathmoab he repaired a section of Jerusalem’s wall and the tower of the furnaces ([[@16003011|Neh 3:11]]).

column5: Son of Rechab who repaired the Dung Gate
column7: The son of Rechab, ruler of the district of Beth Haccherem, he repaired the Dung Gate, built it, and set up its doors, bolts, and bars ([[@16003014|Neh 3:14]]).

column5: A goldsmith who repaired the wall
column7: He was a goldsmith who repaired the section opposite the gate of Hammiphkad, as far as the ascent of the corner ([[@16003031|Neh 3:31]]).

column5: A man who stood beside Ezra at the reading of the law
column7: He was one of those who stood on the left of Ezra the scribe when Ezra read the book of the law from a wooden pulpit ([[@16008003-16008004|Neh 8:3-4]]).

column5: A priest who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the priests whose names were set down when the people made a sure covenant, wrote it, and sealed it ([[@16009038|Neh 9:38]]; [[@16010003|Neh 10:3]]; [[@16010008|Neh 10:8]]).

column5: A man who stood in the temple at the wall’s dedication
column7: He was one of those who stood in God’s house with the companies giving thanks when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated ([[@16012040|Neh 12:40]]; [[@16012042|Neh 12:42]]).

column5: Son of Jeconiah
column7: In the genealogy of David’s royal house, his name appears among the sons of Jeconiah, the king of Judah who was taken captive ([[@13003017-13003018|1 Chr 3:17-18]]).

column5: The servant whose ear Peter cut off
column7: He was the high priest’s servant, and Simon Peter drew his sword and cut off his right ear ([[@43018010|John 18:10]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a temple singer
column7: He was one of the sons of Heman, who served in song in David’s day ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]). The nineteenth lot fell to him, and he served with his sons and brothers, twelve in all ([[@13025026|1 Chr 25:26]]).

column5: A Merarite ancestor of Ethan
column7: Among the singers David appointed, he appears in the genealogy of Ethan, a descendant of Merari, as the son of Hashabiah and the father of Abdi ([[@13006031|1 Chr 6:31]]; [[@13006044-13006045|1 Chr 6:44-45]]).

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Bani who had married foreign women ([[@15010029|Ezra 10:29]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Harim who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Harim who had married foreign women ([[@15010031-15010032|Ezra 10:31-32]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the priests who came back with Zerubbabel and Jeshua ([[@16012001-16012002|Neh 12:1-2]]). The name also appears among those who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s day ([[@16010004|Neh 10:4]]).

column5: A leader of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: In Nehemiah’s time his name appears among the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010027|Neh 10:27]]).

column5: The island Paul’s company reached after the shipwreck
column7: After the ship bound for Rome broke apart, everyone escaped safely to land, and the island was called Malta ([[@44027044|Acts 27:44]]; [[@44028001|Acts 28:1]]).

column5: Money and wealth, which cannot be served along with God
column7: Mammon is a word meaning 'wealth, money', and Jesus spoke of it as if it were a master that people serve. Jesus taught, "You can’t serve both God and Mammon" ([[@40006024|Matt 6:24]]). He also said, "make for yourselves friends by means of unrighteous mammon" ([[@42016009|Luke 16:9]]), and asked who would entrust true riches to someone who has not been faithful with unrighteous mammon ([[@42016011|Luke 16:11]]). Luke also records the saying that just as no servant can serve two masters, you cannot serve both God and Mammon ([[@42016013|Luke 16:13]]).

column5: The oaks at Hebron where Abraham stayed
column7: It was a place in Hebron, where Abram moved his tent and lived "by the oaks of Mamre," and built an altar to the LORD ([[@1013018|Gen 13:18]]). Genesis 14 also mentions Mamre the Amorite, an ally of Abram ([[@1014013|Gen 14:13]]). The LORD appeared to Abraham by the oaks of Mamre ([[@1018001|Gen 18:1]]). Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field of Machpelah before Mamre, and the Bible adds, "that is, Hebron" ([[@1023019|Gen 23:19]]).

column5: An Amorite ally of Abram
column7: He was an Amorite, the brother of Eshcol and Aner, and an ally of Abram. Abram lived by his oaks ([[@1014013|Gen 14:13]]).

column5: A prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch
column7: He was one of the prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch, and "the foster brother of Herod the tetrarch" ([[@44013001|Acts 13:1]]).

column5: Son of Shobal the Horite
column7: He was a son of Shobal, a descendant of Seir the Horite ([[@1036020|Gen 36:20]]; [[@1036023|Gen 36:23]]). The same name appears in the genealogy in 1 Chronicles ([[@13001040|1 Chr 1:40]]).

column5: Where the people of Geba were carried captive
column7: The sons of Ehud, a Benjamite, were heads of the families of the people of Geba, and they were carried captive to Manahath ([[@13008006|1 Chr 8:6]]).

column5: Joseph's firstborn son; the tribe of Manasseh
column7: He was the firstborn son born to Joseph in Egypt. Joseph named him, saying, "God has made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house" ([[@1041051|Gen 41:51]]). Jacob took Manasseh and Ephraim as his own sons, but when he blessed them he put the younger, Ephraim, first ([[@1048005|Gen 48:5]], 14). His descendants, the tribe of Manasseh, received land divided between the east and west sides of the Jordan ([[@6013029|Josh 13:29]]; [[@6017001|Josh 17:1]]).

column5: King of Judah who reigned fifty-five years
column7: He was the son of Hezekiah; he became king at twelve and reigned fifty-five years in Jerusalem ([[@12021001|2 Kgs 21:1]]). He rebuilt the high places his father had destroyed and raised up altars for Baal ([[@12021003|2 Kgs 21:3]]), and he shed a great deal of innocent blood ([[@12021016|2 Kgs 21:16]]). According to 2 Chronicles, after he was captured by the Assyrian army and taken to Babylon, he humbled himself greatly before God in his distress and prayed, and God brought him back to Jerusalem ([[@14033011-14033013|2 Chr 33:11-13]]). He is a different person from Manasseh the son of Joseph.

column5: A descendant of Pahathmoab who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Pahathmoab who had married foreign women ([[@15010030|Ezra 10:30]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Hashum who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Hashum who had married foreign women ([[@15010033|Ezra 10:33]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Food God sent down in the wilderness
column7: Manna was the food God sent down from heaven while the people of Israel lived in the wilderness. After the dew was gone, there was something small, round, and like frost on the ground, and when the people saw it they asked one another, "What is it?" ([[@2016014-2016015|Exod 16:14-15]]). It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey, and the people ate manna for forty years until they came to the border of Canaan ([[@2016031|Exod 16:31]]; [[@2016035|Exod 16:35]]). Speaking about the manna, Jesus said, "I am the bread of life" ([[@43006035|John 6:35]]).

column5: Samson's father, from the tribe of Dan
column7: He was a man of the tribe of Dan who lived in Zorah, and his wife was unable to have children ([[@7013002|Judg 13:2]]). When the LORD's angel told his wife she would bear a son, Manoah prayed that he would be taught how to raise the child ([[@7013003-7013008|Judg 13:3-8]]). When the angel went up toward the sky in the flame of the altar, Manoah was afraid and said, "We shall surely die, because we have seen God" ([[@7013020-7013022|Judg 13:20-22]]). After Samson died, he was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol in the burial place of his father Manoah ([[@7016031|Judg 16:31]]).

column5: A large outer garment worn over other clothes
column7: A mantle was a large garment worn over other clothes. Boaz had Ruth spread out her mantle and hold it, and he measured six measures of barley into it ([[@8003015|Ruth 3:15]]). Elijah went to Elisha, who was plowing, and threw his mantle over him, and after saying goodbye to his parents, Elisha followed Elijah and served him ([[@11019019-11019021|1 Kgs 19:19-21]]). After Elijah went up to heaven, Elisha took the mantle that had fallen from Elijah and struck the waters of the Jordan, and the waters divided this way and that ([[@12002013-12002014|2 Kgs 2:13-14]]).

column5: Father of Achish, king of Gath
column7: He was the father of Achish king of Gath, to whom David went over with his six hundred men ([[@9027002|1 Sam 27:2]]). In 1 Kings the king is called 'Achish, son of Maacah' ([[@11002039|1 Kgs 2:39]]).

column5: A town in Judah's hill country, home of Nabal
column7: It was a town in the hill country of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015055|Josh 15:55]]). David stayed in the wilderness of Maon while fleeing from Saul, and the rich man Nabal was also from Maon ([[@9023024|1 Sam 23:24]]; [[@9025002|1 Sam 25:2]]).

column5: A wilderness place named for its bitter water
column7: It was where Israel camped after crossing the sea and going three days’ journey into the wilderness of Etham ([[@4033008|Num 33:8]]). Its water was bitter and they could not drink it, so it was named Marah ([[@2015023|Exod 15:23]]).

column5: A place on Zebulun’s border
column7: It is where the border of the inheritance Zebulun received by lot went up westward, to Maralah. From there it reached Dabbesheth ([[@6019010-6019011|Josh 19:10-11]]).

column5: Fortified town in the lowland of Judah
column7: It was one of the lowland towns given to the tribe of Judah ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]], 44). Rehoboam built Mareshah and several other towns to defend the land of Judah ([[@14011005-14011008|2 Chr 11:5-8]]). In King Asa's day, when Zerah the Ethiopian came to Mareshah with an army of a million troops and three hundred chariots, Asa cried out to the LORD, and the LORD defeated the Ethiopians ([[@14014009-14014012|2 Chr 14:9-12]]). Eliezer, who prophesied against Jehoshaphat, was also from Mareshah ([[@14020037|2 Chr 20:37]]).

column5: Son of Mesha, father of Hebron
column7: In Judah’s genealogy he appears as the son of Mesha, Caleb’s firstborn, and is called 'the father of Hebron' ([[@13002042|1 Chr 2:42]]).

column5: A person or town with Laadah as its 'father'
column7: Among the descendants of Shelah the son of Judah is "Laadah the father of Mareshah". The text alone does not make clear whether Mareshah was a person or a town ([[@13004021|1 Chr 4:21]]).

column5: John Mark, co-worker of Paul and Peter
column7: He was known as "John who was called Mark," and many people gathered to pray at the house of his mother Mary ([[@44012012|Acts 12:12]]). He went with Paul and Barnabas on their missionary journey but left them in Pamphylia, and because of this Paul and Barnabas later had a sharp disagreement and parted ways ([[@44015037-44015039|Acts 15:37-39]]). Years later Paul asked Timothy to bring Mark, saying, "he is useful to me for service" ([[@55004011|2 Tim 4:11]]). Peter also called him "Mark, my son" ([[@60005013|1 Pet 5:13]]), and he is traditionally known as the writer of the Gospel of Mark.

column5: A town named by Micah
column7: Micah’s prophecy says that "the inhabitant of Maroth waits anxiously for good". This was because disaster had come down to the gate of Jerusalem ([[@33001012|Mic 1:12]]).

column5: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media
column7: He was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who were close to the king and sat first in the kingdom ([[@17001013-17001014|Esth 1:13-14]]).

column5: Sister of Mary and Lazarus
column7: A woman who lived in Bethany, she was the sister of Lazarus ([[@43011001|John 11:1]]). When she welcomed Jesus into her home, her sister Mary sat at the Lord's feet listening to his word, while Martha was distracted with much serving. Jesus called her, "Martha, Martha", and told her that "one thing is needed" ([[@42010038-42010042|Luke 10:38-42]]). After Lazarus died, she went out first to meet Jesus when she heard he was coming, and confessed, "I have come to believe that you are the Christ, God’s Son, he who comes into the world" ([[@43011020-43011027|John 11:20-27]]). Later, when a dinner was given for Jesus in Bethany, she served there too ([[@43012002|John 12:2]]).

column5: Mother of Jesus and wife of Joseph
column7: She was a virgin who lived in Nazareth of Galilee, pledged to be married to Joseph, a descendant of David ([[@42001027|Luke 1:27]]). When the angel Gabriel told her she would bear a son, she obeyed, saying, "Behold, the servant of the Lord; let it be done to me according to your word" ([[@42001038|Luke 1:38]]). She conceived by the Holy Spirit and gave birth to Jesus, and when Jesus was crucified, she stood by his cross ([[@43019025|John 19:25]]). After Jesus went up to heaven, she joined the disciples with one accord and kept on in prayer ([[@44001014|Acts 1:14]]).

column5: Sister of Martha and Lazarus
column7: She was the sister of Lazarus of Bethany, and Martha's sister ([[@43011001-43011002|John 11:1-2]]). When Jesus came to their home she sat at his feet and listened to his word, and Jesus said, "Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her" ([[@42010039-42010042|Luke 10:39-42]]). After Lazarus died, she came to Jesus, fell at his feet, and wept, saying, "Lord, if you would have been here, my brother wouldn’t have died" ([[@43011032-43011033|John 11:32-33]]). Six days before the Passover she poured a pound of very costly ointment of nard on Jesus' feet and wiped his feet with her hair ([[@43012001-43012003|John 12:1-3]]).

column5: Mother of John Mark
column7: She was the mother of John who was called Mark. When Peter came to her house after escaping from prison, many people were gathered there praying ([[@44012011-44012012|Acts 12:11-12]]).

column5: A hard worker in the church at Rome
column7: In his greetings to the church at Rome, Paul wrote of "Mary, who labored much for us" ([[@45016006|Rom 16:6]]).

column5: Freed from seven demons, first resurrection witness
column7: She was a woman from whom Jesus had cast out seven demons, and with other women she supported Jesus and his followers out of her own means ([[@42008002-42008003|Luke 8:2-3]]). When Jesus was crucified, she stood by the cross, and she also watched where Jesus was laid in the tomb ([[@43019025|John 19:25]]; [[@41015047|Mark 15:47]]). Early on the first day of the week she went to the tomb and saw that the stone had been taken away, and while she was weeping outside the tomb, she met the risen Jesus. Mark says that after Jesus rose, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene ([[@43020001|John 20:1]], 11-16; [[@41016009|Mark 16:9]]). She went and told the disciples "that she had seen the Lord" ([[@43020018|John 20:18]]).

column5: Grandson of Shem, son of Aram
column7: He was one of the sons of Aram, Shem’s son ([[@1010023|Gen 10:23]]). In the same place in 1 Chronicles, 'Meshech' appears ([[@13001017|1 Chr 1:17]]).

column5: Hometown of Samlah, king of Edom
column7: It was the home of 'Samlah of Masrekah', who became king after Hadad king of Edom died ([[@1036036|Gen 36:36]]; [[@13001047|1 Chr 1:47]]).

column5: Son of Ishmael
column7: He was one of the sons of Ishmael, Abraham’s son ([[@1025013-1025014|Gen 25:13-14]]; [[@13001030|1 Chr 1:30]]).

column5: Where the people tested the LORD
column7: It was the place at Rephidim where the people quarreled over water and tested the LORD, so it was called 'Massah' or 'Meribah' ([[@2017007|Exod 17:7]]). Moses told the people not to tempt the LORD "as you tempted him in Massah" ([[@5006016|Deut 6:16]]).

column5: Parent of Mehetabel, queen of Edom
column7: Mehetabel, the wife of Hadar king of Edom, is introduced as "the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab" ([[@1036039|Gen 36:39]]; [[@13001050|1 Chr 1:50]]).

column5: The Benjamite family Saul came from
column7: It was the family chosen from the tribe of Benjamin when Samuel was choosing a king. From that family Saul the son of Kish was chosen ([[@9010020-9010021|1 Sam 10:20-21]]).

column5: A priest of Baal
column7: He was a priest of Baal who was killed before the altars when all the people tore down the house of Baal in Jehoiada’s day ([[@12011018|2 Kgs 11:18]]; [[@14023017|2 Chr 23:17]]).

column5: Father of Shephatiah
column7: He was the father of Shephatiah, who heard the words Jeremiah spoke to the people. Afterward the princes told the king that Jeremiah should be put to death ([[@24038001|Jer 38:1]]; [[@24038004|Jer 38:4]]).

column5: A stop on Israel’s wilderness journey
column7: The people of Israel came from the wilderness to Mattanah, and from Mattanah they went on to Nahaliel ([[@4021018-4021019|Num 21:18-19]]).

column5: A descendant of Asaph who led the thanksgiving
column7: He was a descendant of Asaph, the son of Mica ([[@13009015|1 Chr 9:15]]). He was the leader who began the thanksgiving in prayer ([[@16011017|Neh 11:17]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a temple singer
column7: He was one of the sons of Heman and was given the ninth turn in the service of praise. With his sons and brothers there were twelve in all ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]; [[@13025016|1 Chr 25:16]]).

column5: An Asaphite ancestor of Jahaziel
column7: He was of the sons of Asaph, and Jahaziel, the Levite on whom the LORD’s Spirit came, is listed as his great-great-grandson ([[@14020014|2 Chr 20:14]]).

column5: A descendant of Asaph who arose under Hezekiah
column7: He was a descendant of Asaph among the Levites who arose in Hezekiah’s time to cleanse the LORD’s house ([[@14029012-14029013|2 Chr 29:12-13]]; [[@14029015|2 Chr 29:15]]).

column5: A descendant of Elam who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Elam who had married foreign women ([[@15010026|Ezra 10:26]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Zattu who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Zattu who had married foreign women ([[@15010027|Ezra 10:27]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Pahathmoab who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Pahathmoab who had married foreign women ([[@15010030|Ezra 10:30]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Bani who had married foreign women ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]; [[@15010037|Ezra 10:37]]).

column5: A Levite descended from Asaph
column7: He was a descendant of Asaph and the great-grandfather of Uzzi, who became overseer of the Levites living in Jerusalem ([[@16011022|Neh 11:22]]).

column5: Grandfather of Hanan, a storehouse keeper
column7: He was the grandfather of Hanan, whom Nehemiah placed next to those in charge of the storehouses. Hanan was the son of Zaccur ([[@16013013|Neh 13:13]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke. He is listed as the father of Menan and the son of Nathan ([[@42003031|Luke 3:31]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke. He is listed as the father of Joseph and the son of Amos ([[@42003024-42003025|Luke 3:24-25]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke. He is listed as the father of Maath and the son of Semein ([[@42003026|Luke 3:26]]).

column5: A descendant of Hashum who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Hashum who had married foreign women ([[@15010033|Ezra 10:33]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Hashum who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Hashum who had married foreign women ([[@15010033|Ezra 10:33]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Bani who had married foreign women ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]; [[@15010037|Ezra 10:37]]).

column5: Head of the priestly family of Joiarib
column7: In the days of Joiakim, he was the head of the family of Joiarib among the heads of priestly families ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012019|Neh 12:19]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke. He is listed as the father of Heli and the son of Levi ([[@42003023-42003024|Luke 3:23-24]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke. He is listed as the father of Jorim and the son of Levi ([[@42003029|Luke 3:29]]).

column5: Tax collector and one of Jesus' twelve apostles
column7: He was one of Jesus' twelve apostles. He was sitting at the tax office when he heard Jesus say, "Follow me", and he got up and followed him ([[@40009009|Matt 9:9]]). Mark tells the same story and calls him 'Levi the son of Alphaeus' ([[@41002014|Mark 2:14]]). Levi held a great feast for Jesus in his house, and many tax collectors and others were reclining with them ([[@42005029|Luke 5:29]]). In the list of apostles he is called 'Matthew the tax collector' ([[@40010003|Matt 10:3]]), and the church has long held that he wrote the Gospel of Matthew.

column5: The apostle chosen to replace Judas Iscariot
column7: He was put forward with Joseph as a replacement for Judas Iscariot, and when lots were drawn, he was counted with the eleven apostles ([[@44001023|Acts 1:23]]; [[@44001026|Acts 1:26]]).

column5: A Levite in charge of the baking in pans
column7: He was a Levite, the firstborn of Shallum the Korahite, and he was in charge of the things baked in pans. He appears in the list of Levite family heads who lived in Jerusalem ([[@13009031|1 Chr 9:31]]; [[@13009034|1 Chr 9:34]]).

column5: A Levite musician in David's time
column7: He was one of the Levites David appointed when he moved the ark of God, and he led with the harp ([[@13015018-13015021|1 Chr 15:18-21]]).

column5: A descendant of Nebo who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Nebo who had married foreign women ([[@15010043-15010044|Ezra 10:43-44]]).

column5: A man who stood beside Ezra at the reading of the law
column7: He was one of those who stood on the right of Ezra the scribe when Ezra read the book of the law from a wooden pulpit ([[@16008003-16008004|Neh 8:3-4]]).

column5: A place in Dan’s inheritance
column7: It was one of the places in the inheritance the tribe of Dan received by lot, listed with Rakkon and the border opposite Joppa ([[@6019040|Josh 19:40]]; [[@6019046|Josh 19:46]]).

column5: An offering made of grain flour
column7: The meal offering was an offering of grain rather than of animals. It was offered as fine flour with oil poured on it and frankincense put on it, and the priest burned a handful of it on the altar as a memorial ([[@3002001-3002002|Lev 2:1-2]]). The rest went to Aaron and his sons, and it was "a most holy part of the offerings of the LORD made by fire" ([[@3002003|Lev 2:3]]). No yeast or honey could be put in a meal offering, and it had to be seasoned with the salt of the covenant ([[@3002011|Lev 2:11]], 13). When a lamb was offered in the morning and in the evening, a meal offering and a drink offering were offered with it too ([[@2029041|Exod 29:41]]).

column5: A place belonging to the Sidonians
column7: In Joshua’s time, when the land still left to be taken is described, "Mearah that belongs to the Sidonians" is named ([[@6013001-6013002|Josh 13:1-2]]; [[@6013004|Josh 13:4]]).

column5: The people of David’s warrior Hepher
column7: The list of David’s mighty men includes "Hepher the Mecherathite" ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011036|1 Chr 11:36]]).

column5: A town where people of Judah lived after the exile
column7: Some of the children of Judah who returned from exile lived in Ziklag and in Meconah and its towns ([[@16011025|Neh 11:25]]; [[@16011028|Neh 11:28]]).

column5: An elder who prophesied in the camp
column7: He was one of the elders whose names were written down; he and Eldad stayed in the camp instead of going to the Tent of Meeting, but the Spirit rested on them and they prophesied in the camp ([[@4011026-4011027|Num 11:26-27]]).

column5: Son of Abraham and Keturah
column7: He was one of the six sons born to Abraham by Keturah, the wife he took later, a brother of Jokshan and Midian ([[@1025001-1025002|Gen 25:1-2]]; [[@13001032|1 Chr 1:32]]).

column5: A town on the plain of Moab
column7: It was a town in the land of Moab mentioned in the song passed down about Heshbon ([[@4021030|Num 21:30]]). The plain around it became part of the share of the children of Reuben ([[@6013016|Josh 13:16]]).

column5: People who formed a great kingdom with Persia
column7: Media was a people who lived east of Assyria, and also their kingdom. After the king of Assyria took Samaria, he carried the Israelites away and placed them "in the cities of the Medes" ([[@12017006|2 Kgs 17:6]]). Later Media joined with Persia to form one kingdom, so the phrase "Persia and Media" often appears in the book of Esther ([[@17001003|Esth 1:3]]). Daniel explained that the kingdom of Babylon would be divided and given to the Medes and Persians, and later Darius the Mede received the kingdom ([[@27005028|Dan 5:28]]; [[@27005031|Dan 5:31]]).

column5: Fortress town on the plain of Jezreel
column7: An important town at the edge of the plain of Jezreel; the king of Megiddo was among the Canaanite kings Joshua defeated ([[@6012021|Josh 12:21]]). The tribe of Manasseh could not drive out its people. Deborah's song also tells of a battle "by the waters of Megiddo" ([[@7005019|Judg 5:19]]). Solomon built up this city ([[@11009015|1 Kgs 9:15]]). King Josiah went out against Pharaoh Necoh king of Egypt and died at Megiddo ([[@12023029|2 Kgs 23:29]]).

column5: Wife of Hadar, king of Edom
column7: She was the wife of Hadar king of Edom, the daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Mezahab ([[@1036039|Gen 36:39]]; [[@13001050|1 Chr 1:50]]).

column5: An ancestor of Shemaiah
column7: Shemaiah, who urged Nehemiah to hide in God’s house, is called "the son of Delaiah the son of Mehetabel" ([[@16006010|Neh 6:10]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family of returning temple servants
column7: He was the ancestor of 'the children of Mehida', among the temple servants who came back from exile in Babylon ([[@15002052|Ezra 2:52]]; [[@16007054|Neh 7:54]]).

column5: Son of Chelub, father of Eshton
column7: He was the son of Chelub, the brother of Shuhah, and the father of Eshton. He appears in the genealogy of Judah ([[@13004001|1 Chr 4:1]]; [[@13004011|1 Chr 4:11]]).

column5: The people of Adriel, Saul’s son-in-law
column7: Adriel, the husband of Saul’s daughter Merab, was called a Meholathite ([[@9018019|1 Sam 18:19]]). He was the son of Barzillai ([[@10021008|2 Sam 21:8]]).

column5: A eunuch who served King Ahasuerus
column7: He was one of the seven eunuchs serving in the king’s presence whom the king ordered, on the seventh day of the feast, to bring Queen Vashti ([[@17001010-17001011|Esth 1:10-11]]).

column5: A Gibeonite who repaired the wall
column7: He was a Gibeonite who, together with Jadon the Meronothite and the men of Gibeon and Mizpah, repaired the wall ([[@16003007|Neh 3:7]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke. He is listed as the father of Levi and the son of Jannai ([[@42003024|Luke 3:24]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke. He is listed as the father of Neri and the son of Addi ([[@42003027-42003028|Luke 3:27-28]]).

column5: King of Salem, priest of God Most High
column7: He was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. When Abram returned from defeating Chedorlaomer and the kings who were with him, Melchizedek brought out bread and wine ([[@1014017-1014018|Gen 14:17-18]]). He blessed Abram, and Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of all he had gained ([[@1014019-1014020|Gen 14:19-20]]). The Psalms say, "You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek" ([[@19110004|Ps 110:4]]). Pointing to these words, Hebrews teaches that Jesus has become a high priest forever after the order of Melchizedek ([[@58006020|Heb 6:20]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke. He is listed as the father of Eliakim and the son of Menan ([[@42003030-42003031|Luke 3:30-31]]).

column5: Son of Micah, a descendant of Saul
column7: He was one of the four sons of Micah, a descendant of Saul. Micah was the son of Merib-baal, Jonathan’s son ([[@13008034-13008035|1 Chr 8:34-35]]; [[@13009041|1 Chr 9:41]]).

column5: The official in charge of Daniel and his friends
column7: He was the man the chief of the eunuchs appointed over Daniel and his three friends. He agreed to Daniel’s request, tested them for ten days, and gave them vegetables ([[@27001011-27001016|Dan 1:11-16]]).

column5: An ancient great city in northern Egypt
column7: It was a great ancient city on the Nile in northern Egypt. Isaiah said that the princes of Memphis were deceived and caused Egypt to go astray ([[@23019013|Isa 19:13]]). In Jeremiah's time people of Judah lived here too ([[@24044001|Jer 44:1]]), and Jeremiah prophesied that Memphis would become a desolation, burned up and without inhabitant ([[@24046019|Jer 46:19]]). Ezekiel also declared that God would cause the images to cease from Memphis ([[@26030013|Ezek 30:13]]).

column5: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media
column7: He was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who were next to King Ahasuerus ([[@17001014|Esth 1:14]]). He told the king that Queen Vashti had done wrong, and the king did as he said ([[@17001016|Esth 1:16]]; [[@17001021|Esth 1:21]]).

column5: King of Israel who killed Shallum and took the throne
column7: He was the son of Gadi, and he went up from Tirzah to Samaria, killed Shallum, and became king of Israel in his place ([[@12015014|2 Kgs 15:14]]). He was so cruel that when Tiphsah would not open its gates, he attacked it and even ripped open the pregnant women ([[@12015016|2 Kgs 15:16]]). He reigned ten years in Samaria and did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam ([[@12015017-12015018|2 Kgs 15:17-18]]). When Pul king of Assyria invaded, Menahem gave him a thousand talents of silver collected from the wealthy men of Israel so that he would turn back ([[@12015019-12015020|2 Kgs 15:19-20]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: Menan appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke. He is listed as the father of Melea and the son of Mattatha ([[@42003031|Luke 3:31]]).

column5: A group among Shobal’s descendants
column7: In Judah’s genealogy, "half of the Menuhoth" are counted among the descendants of Shobal the father of Kiriath Jearim ([[@13002052|1 Chr 2:52]]).

column5: Father of Ophrah
column7: His name appears in the genealogy of Judah as the father of Ophrah. Just before him are listed Othniel and Seraiah, the sons of Kenaz ([[@13004013-13004014|1 Chr 4:13-14]]).

column5: A Levite town of the tribe of Reuben
column7: It was one of the towns Moses gave to the tribe of Reuben ([[@6013015-6013018|Josh 13:15-18]]). Later it was given from the tribe of Reuben to the Levites ([[@6021036-6021037|Josh 21:36-37]]; [[@13006079|1 Chr 6:79]]).

column5: Jonathan's son, Saul's grandson who was lame
column7: He was the son of Saul's son Jonathan. He was five years old when news came that Saul and Jonathan had died, and as his nurse picked him up and fled in a hurry, he fell and became lame ([[@10004004|2 Sam 4:4]]). For Jonathan's sake David gave him back all of Saul's land and said, "You will eat bread at my table continually" ([[@10009007|2 Sam 9:7]]). Later his servant Ziba slandered him, but when David returned he told the king he had been deceived, and David told him to divide the land with Ziba ([[@10019024-10019029|2 Sam 19:24-29]]). Because of the oath he had sworn by the LORD with Jonathan, David cared for him to the end ([[@10021007|2 Sam 21:7]]).

column5: Son of Saul and Rizpah
column7: He was one of the two sons whom Rizpah the daughter of Aiah bore to Saul. The Gibeonites hanged him on the mountain before the LORD ([[@10021008-10021009|2 Sam 21:8-9]]).

column5: Saul's older daughter
column7: She was Saul's older daughter ([[@9014049|1 Sam 14:49]]). Saul said he would give her to David, but when the time came he gave her as a wife to Adriel the Meholathite ([[@9018017|1 Sam 18:17]]; [[@9018019|1 Sam 18:19]]).

column5: Head of the priestly family of Seraiah
column7: In the days of Joiakim, he was the head of the family of Seraiah among the heads of priestly families. Seraiah was a priest who had returned with Zerubbabel ([[@16012001|Neh 12:1]]; [[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]).

column5: Priest in Eleazar's line, father of Amariah
column7: He was a member of the priestly family descended from Eleazar the son of Aaron. He was the son of Zerahiah and the father of Amariah ([[@13006006-13006007|1 Chr 6:6-7]]). His name is also on the list of Aaron's descendants in 1 Chronicles 6 and in Ezra's genealogy ([[@13006052|1 Chr 6:52]]; [[@15007003|Ezra 7:3]]). A Meraioth also appears in the genealogy of Azariah, the ruler of God's house, and scholars differ on whether he is the same man ([[@13009011|1 Chr 9:11]]).

column5: Levi's third son, ancestor of the Merarites
column7: Merari was the third son of Levi and the brother of Gershon and Kohath. He went down to Egypt with Jacob and had two sons, Mahli and Mushi ([[@2006019|Exod 6:19]]). In the wilderness the Merarites camped on the north side of the tabernacle ([[@4003035|Num 3:35]]), and they were given the task of carrying the tabernacle's boards, bars, pillars, and sockets ([[@4004031|Num 4:31]]). After entering Canaan, they received twelve cities from the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun ([[@6021007|Josh 21:7]]).

column5: Pure gold cover on the ark of the covenant
column7: The mercy seat was the pure gold cover over the ark of the covenant. It was two and a half cubits long and a cubit and a half wide, and two cherubim made of gold stood at its two ends with their wings spread upward, covering the mercy seat. God said he would meet Moses between those two cherubim and speak with him ([[@2025017-2025022|Exod 25:17-22]]). The high priest made atonement by sprinkling the blood of a bull with his finger before the mercy seat seven times ([[@3016014|Lev 16:14]]). Hebrews also looks back on this, speaking of the "cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat" ([[@58009005|Heb 9:5]]).

column5: A man of Judah, son of Ezrah
column7: He was the son of Ezrah, and he married Bithiah, Pharaoh’s daughter, who bore Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah ([[@13004017-13004018|1 Chr 4:17-18]]).

column5: Priest who kept temple treasures and repaired the wall
column7: He was the son of Uriah the priest. After Ezra's company arrived in Jerusalem from Babylon, the silver, the gold, and the vessels were weighed in the house of God and placed in Meremoth's hands ([[@15008032-15008033|Ezra 8:32-33]]). In Nehemiah's time he took part in repairing the wall of Jerusalem, and one section he repaired ran from the door of Eliashib's house to the end of that house ([[@16003004|Neh 3:4]], 21). A Meremoth also appears among those who sealed the covenant and among the priests who returned with Zerubbabel, but scholars differ on whether he is the same man ([[@16010005|Neh 10:5]]; [[@16012003|Neh 12:3]]).

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Bani who had married foreign women ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]; [[@15010036|Ezra 10:36]]).

column5: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media
column7: He was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who were close to the king and sat first in the kingdom ([[@17001013-17001014|Esth 1:13-14]]).

column5: Where Israel quarreled
column7: At Rephidim the people had no water, so they quarreled with Moses and tested the LORD, and the place was called 'Massah' and 'Meribah' ([[@2017001-2017007|Exod 17:1-7]]). The Psalms say not to harden your heart "as at Meribah" ([[@19095008|Ps 95:8]]).

column5: Where Moses struck the rock twice
column7: It is the name of a place where the people of Israel quarreled over water. At Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin there was no water, and when the people quarreled with Moses, God told him to command the rock to give water, but Moses struck the rock twice with his rod ([[@4020001-4020011|Num 20:1-11]]). God said that because Moses and Aaron had not believed and had not shown his holiness, they would not lead the people into the Promised Land, and this water was called the waters of Meribah ([[@4020012-4020013|Num 20:12-13]]). Earlier, the place at Rephidim where water came out of the rock was also called 'Massah' or 'Meribah' ([[@2017007|Exod 17:7]]). A psalm speaks of this, saying, "They angered him also at the waters of Meribah" ([[@19106032|Ps 106:32]]).

column5: The king of Babylon who sent envoys to Hezekiah
column7: He was the son of Baladan and king of Babylon. When he heard that Hezekiah had been sick and had recovered, he sent letters and a present ([[@23039001|Isa 39:1]]). In 2 Kings he appears as 'Berodach Baladan' ([[@12020012|2 Kgs 20:12]]).

column5: The waters where Joshua struck an alliance
column7: Joshua came suddenly upon the Canaanite kings who had gathered and camped at the waters of Merom ([[@6011005|Josh 11:5]]; [[@6011007|Josh 11:7]]).

column5: A person from Meronoth
column7: This refers to someone from Meronoth. Jehdeiah, who was over David’s donkeys, and Jadon, who repaired the wall in Nehemiah’s day, were Meronothites ([[@13027030|1 Chr 27:30]]; [[@16003007|Neh 3:7]]).

column5: A place cursed for not helping the LORD
column7: The song of Deborah and Barak says, "Curse Meroz". This was because its people did not come to help the LORD ([[@7005001|Judg 5:1]]; [[@7005023|Judg 5:23]]).

column5: The edge of the land where Joktan’s descendants lived
column7: The sons of Joktan lived in the land stretching from Mesha toward Sephar, the mountain of the east ([[@1010029-1010030|Gen 10:29-30]]).

column5: The king of Moab who rebelled against Israel
column7: He was a king of Moab who bred sheep, and he supplied the king of Israel with a hundred thousand lambs and the wool of a hundred thousand rams. After Ahab died, he rebelled against the king of Israel ([[@12003004-12003005|2 Kgs 3:4-5]]).

column5: Caleb’s firstborn, father of Ziph
column7: He was the firstborn of Caleb, the brother of Jerahmeel, and is called 'the father of Ziph.' His son was Mareshah, 'the father of Hebron' ([[@13002042|1 Chr 2:42]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Shaharaim
column7: In the genealogy of Benjamin, he was one of the sons Shaharaim had by his wife Hodesh in the land of Moab ([[@13008008-13008009|1 Chr 8:8-9]]).

column5: Son of Japheth
column7: He was one of the sons of Japheth, Noah’s son, a brother of Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, and Tiras ([[@1010002|Gen 10:2]]; [[@13001005|1 Chr 1:5]]).

column5: A distant nation descended from Japheth
column7: It was a distant nation that also bore the name of one of Japheth's sons ([[@1010002|Gen 10:2]]). The psalmist sang of the sorrow of having to "live in Meshech," and it also appears as a nation that traded with Tyre ([[@19120005|Ps 120:5]]; [[@26027013|Ezek 27:13]]).

column5: Nations that went down to the pit
column7: In the lament over the multitude of Egypt, they appear among the uncircumcised who were slain by the sword. In the land of the living they had spread terror ([[@26032018|Ezek 32:18]]; [[@26032026|Ezek 32:26]]).

column5: A Levite gatekeeper in David's time
column7: He was the son of Kore of the Korahites and was among the divisions of the gatekeepers ([[@13026001|1 Chr 26:1]]). His son Zechariah became gatekeeper of the Tent of Meeting ([[@13009021|1 Chr 9:21]]).

column5: Grandfather of Meshullam, who repaired the wall
column7: Meshullam, who repaired the wall, is called "the son of Berechiah, the son of Meshezabel". Meshullam took charge of one section of the wall in Nehemiah’s time ([[@16003004|Neh 3:4]]).

column5: A leader of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: In Nehemiah’s time his name appears among the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010021|Neh 10:21]]).

column5: Father of Pethahiah
column7: He was a descendant of Zerah the son of Judah and the father of Pethahiah, who served at the king’s hand in all matters concerning the people ([[@16011024|Neh 11:24]]).

column5: Ancestor of a priest in Jerusalem after the exile
column7: He was an ancestor of Maasai, a priest who lived in Jerusalem, and the father of Meshullam ([[@13009012|1 Chr 9:12]]). In Nehemiah he appears as 'Meshillemoth' ([[@16011013|Neh 11:13]]).

column5: Father of Berechiah, a leader of Ephraim
column7: He was the father of Berechiah, one of the leaders of the children of Ephraim. Berechiah was one of those who stood up against the men coming back from the war ([[@14028012|2 Chr 28:12]]).

column5: A Simeonite leader in Hezekiah’s time
column7: He was a leader named in the genealogy of Simeon’s descendants. In the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, these men struck the Meunim, destroyed them completely, and settled in their place ([[@13004034|1 Chr 4:34]]; [[@13004038-13004041|1 Chr 4:38-41]]).

column5: Grandfather of Shaphan the scribe
column7: In King Josiah’s time, Shaphan the scribe is called "the son of Azaliah the son of Meshullam" ([[@12022003|2 Kgs 22:3]]).

column5: Son of Zerubbabel
column7: In the genealogy of David’s royal house he was a son of Zerubbabel, named with Hananiah and their sister Shelomith ([[@13003019|1 Chr 3:19]]).

column5: A Gadite who lived in Bashan
column7: He was one of seven relatives among the clans of the descendants of Gad who lived in the land of Bashan ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005013|1 Chr 5:13]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Elpaal
column7: In the genealogy of Benjamin he was one of the sons of Elpaal, named with Zebadiah, Hizki, and Heber ([[@13008017-13008018|1 Chr 8:17-18]]).

column5: Father of Sallu, who lived in Jerusalem
column7: He was the father of Sallu, a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile. He was the son of Hodaviah and the grandson of Hassenuah ([[@13009003|1 Chr 9:3]]; [[@13009007|1 Chr 9:7]]).

column5: Son of Shephatiah, who lived in Jerusalem
column7: He was a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem, the son of Shephatiah and the grandson of Reuel ([[@13009003|1 Chr 9:3]]; [[@13009008|1 Chr 9:8]]).

column5: Great-grandfather of Maasai the priest
column7: He was the son of Meshillemith and the great-grandfather of Maasai, a priest who lived in Jerusalem after the exile. The family descended from Immer ([[@13009012|1 Chr 9:12]]).

column5: A Levite overseer in Josiah’s time
column7: He was a Levite of the Kohathites who oversaw the work when Josiah repaired the LORD’s house ([[@14034008|2 Chr 34:8]]; [[@14034012|2 Chr 34:12]]).

column5: A leader Ezra sent for
column7: He was one of the leaders Ezra sent for when he found none of the sons of Levi at the river that runs to Ahava ([[@15008015-15008016|Ezra 8:15-16]]).

column5: A man who supported those opposing the foreign-wives plan
column7: When Jonathan and Jahzeiah stood up against sending away the foreign wives, he and Shabbethai the Levite helped them ([[@15010015|Ezra 10:15]]).

column5: A descendant of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Bani who had married foreign women ([[@15010029|Ezra 10:29]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Son of Berechiah, who repaired the wall
column7: He was the son of Berechiah and repaired the wall of Jerusalem in Nehemiah’s day ([[@16003004|Neh 3:4]]; [[@16003030|Neh 3:30]]). Tobiah’s son Jehohanan married his daughter ([[@16006018|Neh 6:18]]).

column5: Son of Besodeiah who repaired the Old Gate
