column7: The son of Besodeiah, he and Joiada the son of Paseah repaired the Old Gate and set up its doors ([[@16003006|Neh 3:6]]).

column5: A man who stood beside Ezra at the reading of the law
column7: He was one of those who stood on the left of Ezra the scribe when Ezra read the book of the law from a wooden pulpit ([[@16008003-16008004|Neh 8:3-4]]).

column5: A priest who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s time
column7: He was one of those who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s day, and those listed with him were all 'priests' ([[@16010007-16010008|Neh 10:7-8]]).

column5: A leader of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: In Nehemiah’s time his name appears among the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010020|Neh 10:20]]).

column5: Father of Sallu, who lived in Jerusalem
column7: He was the father of Sallu, a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile, and the son of Joed ([[@16011007|Neh 11:7]]).

column5: Head of the priestly family of Ezra
column7: In the days of Joiakim, he was the head of the family of Ezra among the heads of priestly families. Joiakim was the son of Jeshua, the grandson of Jozadak ([[@16012012-16012013|Neh 12:12-13]]; [[@16012026|Neh 12:26]]).

column5: Head of the priestly family of Ginnethon
column7: In the days of Joiakim, he was the head of the family of Ginnethon among the heads of priestly families ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012016|Neh 12:16]]).

column5: A gatekeeper who guarded the storehouses
column7: He was one of the gatekeepers who kept watch by turns at the storehouses of the gates. He lived in the days of Joiakim, Nehemiah, and Ezra ([[@16012025-16012026|Neh 12:25-26]]).

column5: Mother of King Amon
column7: She was the mother of Amon king of Judah and the daughter of Haruz of Jotbah. Amon became king at twenty-two and reigned two years in Jerusalem ([[@12021019|2 Kgs 21:19]]).

column5: Land between the Euphrates and the Tigris
column7: It is a name for the land between two great rivers. Abraham's servant went to Mesopotamia to find a wife for Isaac and came to the city of Nahor ([[@1024010|Gen 24:10]]). Balaam, whom the Ammonites and Moabites hired to curse Israel, was also from Pethor of Mesopotamia ([[@5023003-5023004|Deut 23:3-4]]). In the time of the judges, Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia ruled Israel for eight years, and Othniel defeated him ([[@7003008|Judg 3:8]], 10). Among the people gathered in Jerusalem at Pentecost were also people from Mesopotamia ([[@44002009|Acts 2:9]]).

column5: The Savior anointed by God, the Messiah
column7: Christ means 'anointed one' and is the same title as the Hebrew word 'Messiah'. John's Gospel also explains that the Messiah is, "being interpreted, Christ" ([[@43001041|John 1:41]]). In the Old Testament priests, prophets, and kings were set apart by anointing, and Daniel speaks of an Anointed One who would come in the future ([[@27009025|Dan 9:25]]). When the Samaritan woman said she knew the Messiah was coming, Jesus said, "I am he, the one who speaks to you" ([[@43004025-43004026|John 4:25-26]]). Peter confessed to Jesus, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God" ([[@40016016|Matt 16:16]]).

column5: Son of Enoch, the longest-lived man
column7: He was the son Enoch had at sixty-five ([[@1005021|Gen 5:21]]). After Methuselah was born, Enoch walked with God for three hundred years ([[@1005022|Gen 5:22]]). Methuselah became the father of Lamech at one hundred eighty-seven, and Lamech was the father of Noah ([[@1005025|Gen 5:25]], 28-29). He lived nine hundred sixty-nine years and then died, the longest life of anyone whose age the Bible records ([[@1005027|Gen 5:27]]).

column5: A family of temple servants who returned from exile
column7: Among the temple servants who came back from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Meunim' ([[@15002050|Ezra 2:50]]; [[@16007052|Neh 7:52]]).

column5: A people who attacked Jehoshaphat
column7: They came with the children of Moab and the children of Ammon to fight against Jehoshaphat king of Judah ([[@14020001|2 Chr 20:1]]). In Uzziah’s day, God helped Judah against the Meunim ([[@14026007|2 Chr 26:7]]).

column5: Grandfather of the wife of Hadar, king of Edom
column7: Mezahab was the grandfather of Mehetabel, the wife of Hadar king of Edom. Mehetabel was the daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Mezahab ([[@1036039|Gen 36:39]]).

column5: The people of David’s warrior Jaasiel
column7: The list of David’s mighty men includes "Jaasiel the Mezobaite" ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011047|1 Chr 11:47]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men, son of Hagri
column7: He was the son of Hagri, named in the list of David’s mighty men. His name stands next to Joel the brother of Nathan ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011038|1 Chr 11:38]]).

column5: Son of Ishmael
column7: He was one of the sons of Ishmael, listed after Nebaioth, Kedar, and Adbeel ([[@1025013|Gen 25:13]]; [[@13001029|1 Chr 1:29]]).

column5: A Simeonite, son of Shallum
column7: In the genealogy of Simeon he was the son of Shallum, the son of Shaul, and the father of Mishma ([[@13004024-13004025|1 Chr 4:24-25]]).

column5: A chief of Edom descended from Esau
column7: He was one of the chiefs of Edom descended from Esau, listed after chief Kenaz and chief Teman ([[@1036040|Gen 36:40]]; [[@1036042|Gen 36:42]]).

column5: A descendant of Asaph, father of Mattaniah
column7: He was the son of Zichri and grandson of Asaph, the father of Mattaniah, a Levite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile ([[@13009015|1 Chr 9:15]]). In Nehemiah he appears as the son of Zabdi ([[@16011017|Neh 11:17]]).

column5: A Levite who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the Levites whose names were set down when the people made a sure covenant and sealed it ([[@16009038|Neh 9:38]]; [[@16010009|Neh 10:9]]; [[@16010011|Neh 10:11]]).

column5: A descendant of Asaph, ancestor of Uzzi
column7: He was a descendant of Asaph and the great-great-grandfather of Uzzi, who became overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem and was in charge of the work of God’s house ([[@16011022|Neh 11:22]]).

column5: Ephraimite who set up a shrine at home
column7: He was a man who lived in the hill country of Ephraim. He took eleven hundred pieces of silver from his mother and then gave them back, and his mother used the silver to have an idol made, which was kept in Micah's house ([[@7017002-7017004|Judg 17:2-4]]). Micah set up a shrine, made an ephod and teraphim, made a wandering young Levite his priest, and said he knew the LORD would bless him ([[@7017013|Judg 17:13]]). But the men of the tribe of Dan carried off his idol and his priest ([[@7018027|Judg 18:27]]). The Bible sums up that time with the words "Everyone did that which was right in his own eyes" ([[@7017006|Judg 17:6]]).

column5: Son of Mephibosheth
column7: He was the young son of Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son ([[@10009012|2 Sam 9:12]]). In 1 Chronicles, Merib-baal is said to have fathered Micah ([[@13008034|1 Chr 8:34]]).

column5: A descendant of Joel of Reuben
column7: In the genealogy of Joel of the tribe of Reuben, he was the son of Shimei and the father of Reaiah. His descendant Beerah was carried away captive by Tilgath Pilneser king of Assyria ([[@13005004-13005006|1 Chr 5:4-6]]).

column5: A Levite chief, son of Uzziel
column7: He was the son of Uzziel, a Levite, and he was the chief; his brother was Isshiah ([[@13023020|1 Chr 23:20]]; [[@13024025|1 Chr 24:25]]).

column5: A prophet from Moresheth
column7: He was a man of Morasheth who received the LORD’s word in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah ([[@33001001|Mic 1:1]]). He prophesied that Zion would be plowed like a field ([[@24026018|Jer 26:18]]).

column5: Prophet who foretold Ahab's death
column7: He was the son of Imlah, a prophet in the time of King Ahab. Ahab hated Micaiah because "he does not prophesy good concerning me, but evil" ([[@11022008|1 Kgs 22:8]]). When Ahab and Jehoshaphat were about to go up against Ramoth Gilead, the other prophets said they would win, but Micaiah said, "what the LORD says to me, that I will speak" and prophesied that Israel would be scattered like sheep without a shepherd ([[@11022014-11022017|1 Kgs 22:14-17]]). For this he was struck on the cheek and put in prison, but Ahab was hit by an arrow in that battle and died ([[@11022024-11022027|1 Kgs 22:24-27]], 34-37).

column5: Father of Achbor, an official of Josiah
column7: He was the father of Achbor, one of the officials King Josiah sent along with Hilkiah and others ([[@12022012|2 Kgs 22:12]]). In 2 Chronicles he appears in the phrase 'Abdon the son of Micah' ([[@14034020|2 Chr 34:20]]).

column5: A prince Jehoshaphat sent to teach
column7: He was one of the princes Jehoshaphat sent in the third year of his reign to teach in the cities of Judah ([[@14017007|2 Chr 17:7]]).

column5: A priest with a trumpet
column7: He was one of the priests who held trumpets with the companies giving thanks when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated ([[@16012040-16012041|Neh 12:40-41]]).

column5: Son of Gemariah, grandson of Shaphan
column7: The grandson of Shaphan and son of Gemariah, he heard the words of Jeremiah that Baruch read aloud and reported them to the officials ([[@24036011|Jer 36:11]]; [[@24036013|Jer 36:13]]).

column5: Father of Sethur, the spy from Asher
column7: His son Sethur, of the tribe of Asher, was one of the men sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013002|Num 13:2]]; [[@4013013|Num 13:13]]).

column5: A Gadite who lived in Bashan
column7: He was one of seven relatives among the clans of the descendants of Gad who lived in the land of Bashan ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005013|1 Chr 5:13]]).

column5: An ancestor of Abihail of Gad
column7: In the genealogy of Gad, Abihail is listed as his great-great-grandson. He was the son of Jeshishai and the father of Gilead ([[@13005014|1 Chr 5:14]]).

column5: A Levite ancestor of Asaph
column7: In the genealogy of Asaph, the Levite singer, he is the son of Baaseiah and the father of Shimea ([[@13006039-13006040|1 Chr 6:39-40]]).

column5: A chief of Issachar
column7: From the family of Tola of Issachar, he was the grandson of Uzzi and the son of Izrahiah. All five of them were chief men ([[@13007001-13007003|1 Chr 7:1-3]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Beriah
column7: He was one of the sons of Beriah in the genealogy of Benjamin. His name appears with Ishpah and Joha ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]; [[@13008016|1 Chr 8:16]]).

column5: A captain of thousands who joined David at Ziklag
column7: He was one of the captains of thousands from the tribe of Manasseh who joined David as he went to Ziklag ([[@13012020|1 Chr 12:20]]).

column5: Father of Omri, ruler of Issachar
column7: He was the father of Omri, the ruler of Issachar among those over the tribes of Israel in David’s time ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027018|1 Chr 27:18]]).

column5: Son of Jehoshaphat
column7: He was a son of Jehoshaphat king of Judah and a brother of Jehoram. When Jehoram had taken the throne and strengthened himself, he killed all his brothers with the sword ([[@14021002|2 Chr 21:2]]; [[@14021004|2 Chr 21:4]]).

column5: Father of Zebadiah, who came up with Ezra
column7: Among the descendants of Shephatiah who came up from Babylon with Ezra was "Zebadiah the son of Michael", with eighty men ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008008|Ezra 8:8]]).

column5: The archangel who helps God's people
column7: When the one who appeared to Daniel was held back by the prince of Persia, Michael came to help as 'one of the chief princes' ([[@27010013|Dan 10:13]]). He is called "the great prince who stands for the children of your people", and Jude calls him 'the archangel' ([[@27012001|Dan 12:1]]; [[@65001009|Jude 1:9]]).

column5: Saul's younger daughter and David's wife
column7: She was Saul's younger daughter, who loved David and became his wife ([[@9018027|1 Sam 18:27]]). When Saul tried to kill David, she let David down through the window so he could escape ([[@9019012|1 Sam 19:12]]). After that Saul gave Michal to Palti, but after David became king he took her back. When God's ark came into David's city, she despised David as he danced, and the Bible says she had no children to the day of her death ([[@10006016|2 Sam 6:16]], 23).

column5: Town in Benjamin where Jonathan struck the Philistines
column7: Saul stayed with two thousand men in Michmash and the hill country of Bethel, and later the Philistines came up with thirty thousand chariots and six thousand horsemen and camped at Michmash ([[@9013002-9013005|1 Sam 13:2-5]]). Then Jonathan climbed up to the Philistine garrison with his armor bearer and struck them, and that day Israel struck the Philistines from Michmash to Aijalon ([[@9014013|1 Sam 14:13]]; [[@9014031|1 Sam 14:31]]). After the return from exile, the descendants of Benjamin lived from Geba onward, at Michmash, Aija, and Bethel ([[@16011031|Neh 11:31]]).

column5: A place on the border of Ephraim and Manasseh
column7: It was a place on the north side of Ephraim's border ([[@6016006|Josh 16:6]]). The border of Manasseh also reached Michmethath, which faces Shechem ([[@6017007|Josh 17:7]]).

column5: Grandfather of the Benjamite Elah
column7: Elah, a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem, is called "Elah the son of Uzzi, the son of Michri" ([[@13009008|1 Chr 9:8]]).

column5: A town in the wilderness of Judah
column7: It was a town in the wilderness among the inheritance of the tribe of Judah, listed with Beth Arabah and Secacah ([[@6015020|Josh 15:20]]; [[@6015061|Josh 15:61]]).

column5: Son of Abraham and Keturah
column7: He was a son Abraham had by Keturah ([[@1025001-1025002|Gen 25:1-2]]). His sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah ([[@1025004|Gen 25:4]]).

column5: Descendants of Midian, son of Abraham
column7: It refers to the descendants of Midian, the son of Abraham and Keturah, and the land where they lived ([[@1025002|Gen 25:2]]). Moses fled from Pharaoh and stayed in the land of Midian ([[@2002015|Exod 2:15]]). In the time of the judges, the LORD gave Israel into the hand of Midian for seven years ([[@7006001|Judg 6:1]]). Gideon defeated the Midianites with the three hundred men who lapped the water ([[@7007007|Judg 7:7]]).

column5: A fortified town of Naphtali
column7: It was one of the fortified cities the tribe of Naphtali received ([[@6019032|Josh 19:32]]; [[@6019035-6019038|Josh 19:35-38]]).

column5: A town in Judah’s lowland
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Judah received in the lowland, listed with Zenan and Hadashah ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]; [[@6015037|Josh 15:37]]).

column5: Place near the Red Sea where Israel camped
column7: When Israel came out of Egypt, God turned them back and had them camp by the sea "before Pihahiroth, between Migdol and the sea" ([[@2014002|Exod 14:2]]; [[@4033007|Num 33:7]]). In Jeremiah's time Jews also lived at Migdol in the land of Egypt, and the word of God about them came to Jeremiah ([[@24044001|Jer 44:1]]). Ezekiel spoke of the whole land of Egypt with the words "from the tower of Seveneh", where "tower" is the Hebrew word migdol ([[@26029010|Ezek 29:10]]; [[@26030006|Ezek 30:6]]). Scholars differ on whether the Migdol of the Exodus and the Migdol of the prophets are the same place.

column5: A place on the outskirts of Gibeah
column7: It was a place on the outskirts of Gibeah, where Saul stayed with about six hundred people ([[@9014002|1 Sam 14:2]]). Isaiah said the king of Assyria would pass through Migron ([[@23010028|Isa 10:28]]).

column5: The sixth priestly division
column7: When the divisions of Aaron’s descendants were assigned by lot in David’s time, he was the one chosen sixth ([[@13024007-13024009|1 Chr 24:7-9]]).

column5: A descendant of Parosh who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time his name appears among the descendants of Parosh who had married foreign women ([[@15010025|Ezra 10:25]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A priest who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the priests who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s day ([[@16010007-16010008|Neh 10:7-8]]). He also appears in the list of priests who returned with Zerubbabel ([[@16012001|Neh 12:1]]; [[@16012005|Neh 12:5]]).

column5: Son of Jeiel, father of Gibeon
column7: He was a Benjamite, one of the sons of Jeiel the father of Gibeon, and he became the father of Shimeam ([[@13009035-13009038|1 Chr 9:35-38]]). His family lived in Jerusalem near their relatives ([[@13008032|1 Chr 8:32]]).

column5: Ruler in the division of the second month
column7: In David’s time he was the ruler of the division of the second month, under Dodai the Ahohite, its commander. That division numbered twenty-four thousand ([[@13027004|1 Chr 27:4]]).

column5: A Levite harpist in David's time
column7: He was one of the Levites appointed in David's time, who led the music with harps tuned to the eight-stringed lyre ([[@13015018|1 Chr 15:18]]; [[@13015021|1 Chr 15:21]])

column5: A musician at the wall’s dedication
column7: He was one of Zechariah’s relatives who played the musical instruments of David the man of God when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated ([[@16012035-16012036|Neh 12:35-36]]).

column5: Wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother
column7: She was the wife of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and bore eight sons ([[@1022020-1022023|Gen 22:20-23]]). She was Rebekah's grandmother ([[@1024015|Gen 24:15]]).

column5: A daughter of Zelophehad
column7: She was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh ([[@4026033|Num 26:33]]). With her sisters she came to Moses to ask for her father's inheritance ([[@4027001|Num 27:1]]).

column5: Where Paul called the Ephesian elders
column7: Paul stopped here on his way to Jerusalem and sent to Ephesus to call the elders of the church ([[@44020015-44020017|Acts 20:15-17]]). Paul left Trophimus sick at Miletus ([[@55004020|2 Tim 4:20]]).

column5: Fortification in the City of David
column7: It seems to have been a fortification in the City of David in Jerusalem. After David took the stronghold of Jerusalem, he built the city all around from the Millo inward ([[@10005009|2 Sam 5:9]]; [[@13011008|1 Chr 11:8]]). Solomon used forced labor to build the Millo, along with the LORD's house and his own palace ([[@11009015|1 Kgs 9:15]], 24). When Hezekiah repaired the broken-down wall, he strengthened the Millo in the City of David ([[@14032005|2 Chr 32:5]]). Scholars differ on its exact shape and location.

column5: A man who distributed portions in the priests’ cities
column7: In Hezekiah’s day he served under Kore in the cities of the priests and was one of those who gave portions to their brothers by divisions ([[@14031014-14031015|2 Chr 31:14-15]]).

column5: A priest with a trumpet
column7: He was one of the priests who held trumpets with the companies giving thanks when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated ([[@16012040-16012041|Neh 12:40-41]]).

column5: A kingdom summoned against Babylon
column7: It is named with Ararat and Ashkenaz as one of the kingdoms called together to attack Babylon ([[@24051027|Jer 51:27]]; [[@24051029|Jer 51:29]]).

column5: A town in the land of Ammon
column7: Jephthah struck twenty cities, from Aroer all the way to Minnith ([[@7011033|Judg 11:33]]). Ezekiel mentioned 'wheat of Minnith' among the goods traded with Tyre ([[@26027017|Ezek 27:17]]).

column5: Sister of Moses and Aaron, a prophetess
column7: She was the daughter of Amram and Jochebed, and the sister of Aaron and Moses ([[@4026059|Num 26:59]]). After the crossing of the sea, "Miriam the prophetess" took a tambourine and danced with the women, singing, "Sing to the LORD" ([[@2015020-2015021|Exod 15:20-21]]). But when she and Aaron spoke against Moses, she was struck with leprosy and shut outside the camp for seven days ([[@4012001-4012015|Num 12:1-15]]). Miriam died at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin and was buried there ([[@4020001|Num 20:1]]).

column5: A child of Mered
column7: In Judah’s genealogy the name appears among the children born to Mered the son of Ezrah ([[@13004017|1 Chr 4:17]]).

column5: Son of Shaharaim, a family head
column7: He was one of the sons Shaharaim had by his wife Hodesh in the land of Moab, and he was a head of a family ([[@13008008-13008010|1 Chr 8:8-10]]).

column5: A place named in the message against Moab
column7: In the message against Moab, along with Nebo and Kiriathaim, it says, "Misgab is put to shame and broken down" ([[@24048001|Jer 48:1]]).

column5: Son of Uzziel, a Levite
column6: who is asked for or lent
column7: The son of Aaron's uncle Uzziel, he and Elzaphan obeyed Moses and carried the bodies of Nadab and Abihu out of the camp ([[@2006022|Exod 6:22]]; [[@3010004|Lev 10:4]]).

column5: A man who stood beside Ezra at the reading of the law
column7: He was one of those who stood on the left of Ezra the scribe when Ezra read the book of the law from a wooden pulpit ([[@16008003-16008004|Neh 8:3-4]]).

column5: Daniel's friend, called Meshach in Babylon
column7: He was a young man of the children of Judah who was taken to Babylon along with Daniel, and his Babylonian name was Meshach ([[@27001007|Dan 1:7]]). At Daniel's request, he and his friends ate vegetables for ten days, and their faces looked healthier than those of the young men who ate the king's food. The king found their wisdom and understanding ten times better than that of all the magicians and enchanters in his realm ([[@27001015-27001020|Dan 1:15-20]]). Later the king put them over the affairs of the province of Babylon ([[@27002049|Dan 2:49]]). When they were thrown into the fiery furnace for not bowing to the golden image, the king saw four men walking in the middle of the fire ([[@27003025|Dan 3:25]]).

column5: A Levite city in the tribe of Asher
column7: It was one of the cities the tribe of Asher received ([[@6019026|Josh 19:26]]). It was also one of the cities from the tribe of Asher given to the Levites, and in 1 Chronicles it is called 'Mashal' ([[@6021030|Josh 21:30]]; [[@13006074|1 Chr 6:74]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Elpaal
column7: In the genealogy of Benjamin he was one of the sons of Elpaal, named with Eber and Shemed ([[@13008012|1 Chr 8:12]]).

column5: Son of Ishmael
column7: He was one of the sons of Ishmael, Abraham's son by Hagar, and a brother of Dumah and Massa ([[@1025012-1025014|Gen 25:12-14]]; [[@13001030|1 Chr 1:30]]).

column5: Descendant of Simeon, son of Mibsam
column7: A descendant of Shaul the son of Simeon, he was the son of Mibsam and the father of Hammuel ([[@13004024-13004026|1 Chr 4:24-26]]).

column5: A Gadite warrior who joined David
column7: He is named fourth among the Gadite warriors who joined David at the stronghold in the wilderness ([[@13012008|1 Chr 12:8]]; [[@13012010|1 Chr 12:10]]).

column5: One of the families of Kiriath Jearim
column7: They were one of the families of Kiriath Jearim. From them came the Zorathites and the Eshtaolites ([[@13002053|1 Chr 2:53]]).

column5: A leader who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the leaders who came back from exile with Zerubbabel ([[@15002002|Ezra 2:2]]). In Nehemiah he is called 'Mispereth' ([[@16007007|Neh 7:7]]).

column5: A place near Sidon
column7: Joshua chased the allied Canaanite forces as far as great Sidon and Misrephoth Maim ([[@6011008|Josh 11:8]]). The land from Lebanon to this place belonged to the Sidonians ([[@6013006|Josh 13:6]]).

column5: A camp in the wilderness
column7: In the wilderness the Israelites left Terah and camped at Mithkah, then left Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah ([[@4033028-4033029|Num 33:28-29]]).

column5: The people of David’s warrior Joshaphat
column7: The list of David’s mighty men includes "Joshaphat the Mithnite" ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011043|1 Chr 11:43]]).

column5: Cyrus’s treasurer
column7: He was the treasurer through whom Cyrus king of Persia brought out the vessels of the LORD’s house and counted them out to Sheshbazzar ([[@15001007-15001008|Ezra 1:7-8]]).

column5: A man who wrote to Artaxerxes
column7: In the days of Artaxerxes, he wrote to Artaxerxes king of Persia together with Bishlam, Tabeel, and their companions ([[@15004007|Ezra 4:7]]).

column5: A place Paul’s company stopped
column7: After Paul met his companions at Assos and came aboard, they went there together. From there they sailed past Chios and Samos and came to Miletus ([[@44020014-44020015|Acts 20:14-15]]).

column5: A hill named in the Psalms
column7: In his despair, the psalmist said, "I remember you from the land of the Jordan, the heights of Hermon, from the hill Mizar" ([[@19042006|Ps 42:6]]).

column5: A town of Benjamin where Israel gathered to pray
column7: Mizpah means 'watchtower', and it was a town in the land of Benjamin ([[@6018026|Josh 18:26]]). In the time of the judges, the whole congregation of Israel gathered here to decide a serious matter ([[@7020001|Judg 20:1]]). Samuel gathered the people at Mizpah to fast and confess their sin, and then the LORD defeated the Philistines for them ([[@9007005-9007011|1 Sam 7:5-11]]). It was also here that Saul was chosen as king before the people Samuel had gathered ([[@9010017-9010024|1 Sam 10:17-24]]). There are other places with the same name, so scholars differ on its exact location.

column5: A town in Judah’s lowland
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Judah received in the lowland, listed with Dilean and Joktheel ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]; [[@6015038|Josh 15:38]]).

column5: Land of Mizpah below Mount Hermon
column7: After winning at the waters of Merom, Joshua chased the enemy eastward as far as the valley of Mizpah ([[@6011008|Josh 11:8]]). Hivites lived in the land of Mizpah below Mount Hermon ([[@6011003|Josh 11:3]]).

column5: Grandson of Esau, a chief of Edom
column7: He was a son of Reuel, Esau’s son, and a descendant of Esau’s wife Basemath ([[@1036013|Gen 36:13]]). He was one of the chiefs in the land of Edom ([[@1036017|Gen 36:17]]).

column5: An early disciple who hosted Paul’s company
column7: He was a man of Cyprus and an early disciple. When Paul’s company went up to Jerusalem, some disciples from Caesarea brought him along, since they were to stay at his house ([[@44021015-44021016|Acts 21:15-16]]).

column5: A nation east of the Dead Sea, Ruth's homeland
column7: It was a nation on the high plateau east of the Dead Sea. Its ancestor was Moab, the son born to Lot's older daughter ([[@1019037|Gen 19:37]]). Balak king of Moab feared Israel and sent for Balaam to curse them ([[@4022004-4022006|Num 22:4-6]]). Moses died in the land of Moab ([[@5034005|Deut 34:5]]), and Ruth, David's great-grandmother, was a Moabite woman ([[@8001004|Ruth 1:4]]).

column5: Plains east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho
column7: These are the plains across the Jordan opposite Jericho, where the children of Israel camped before they entered Canaan ([[@4022001|Num 22:1]]). Here Moses and Eleazar the priest counted the children of Israel again ([[@4026063|Num 26:63]]). From these plains Moses went up Mount Nebo to the top of Pisgah, and the LORD showed him all the land of Gilead as far as Dan ([[@5034001|Deut 34:1]]). After Moses died, the children of Israel wept for him in the plains of Moab for thirty days ([[@5034008|Deut 34:8]]).

column5: A town in southern Judah where Simeon lived
column7: It was a southern town of the tribe of Judah that the children of Simeon received as their inheritance ([[@6015026|Josh 15:26]]; [[@6019002|Josh 19:2]]).

column5: Son of Abishur
column7: In Judah’s genealogy he was the son Abishur’s wife Abihail bore him, and a brother of Ahban. Abishur was the son of Shammai ([[@13002028-13002029|1 Chr 2:28-29]]).

column5: A leader who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the leaders who came back from exile in Babylon with Zerubbabel ([[@15002002|Ezra 2:2]]; [[@16007007|Neh 7:7]]).

column5: A Benjamite Jew who raised Esther
column7: Mordecai was a Jew of the tribe of Benjamin who lived in Susa, the royal city of Persia ([[@17002005|Esth 2:5]]). He raised Esther, his uncle's orphaned daughter, as his own daughter ([[@17002007|Esth 2:7]]). When the king's servants bowed down to Haman, he would not bow or pay him homage, and this earned him Haman's hatred ([[@17003002|Esth 3:2]]). After saving the Jews together with Esther, he rose to the place next to King Ahasuerus and looked after his people ([[@17010003|Esth 10:3]]).

column5: The oak in the land of Shechem
column7: It was the place of the oak of Moreh at Shechem, which Abram reached as he passed through the land of Canaan ([[@1012006|Gen 12:6]]). It was near Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal ([[@5011029-5011030|Deut 11:29-30]]).

column5: The hill by the valley where Midian camped
column7: When Gideon camped beside the spring of Harod, the camp of Midian was in the valley by 'the hill of Moreh' ([[@7007001|Judg 7:1]]).

column5: Hometown of the prophet Micah
column7: It was the hometown of the prophet Micah, who was called 'Micah the Morashtite' ([[@33001001|Mic 1:1]]; [[@24026018|Jer 26:18]]). The book of Micah mentions 'Moresheth Gath' ([[@33001014|Mic 1:14]]).

column5: Where Isaac was offered; the temple site
column7: It is the land where God told Abraham to take Isaac ([[@1022002|Gen 22:2]]). Solomon built the LORD's house on Mount Moriah in Jerusalem ([[@14003001|2 Chr 3:1]]).

column5: A place Zephaniah called to wail
column7: Zephaniah cried out, "Wail, you inhabitants of Maktesh". This was because those loaded with silver were cut off ([[@36001011|Zeph 1:11]]).

column5: The place where Aaron died and was buried
column7: It was where the children of Israel came after leaving Beeroth Bene Jaakan, and there Aaron died and was buried ([[@5010006|Deut 10:6]]).

column5: A camp in the wilderness
column7: In the wilderness the Israelites left Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth, then left Moseroth and camped at Bene Jaakan ([[@4033030-4033031|Num 33:30-31]]).

column5: The prophet who led Israel out of Egypt
column7: He was born into a Levite family and raised as the son of the daughter of Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Pharaoh's daughter named him Moses, saying, "Because I drew him out of the water" ([[@2002010|Exod 2:10]]). God sent him to Pharaoh to bring the children of Israel out of Egypt ([[@2003010|Exod 3:10]]). He received the law in the wilderness of Sinai and passed it on to the people, and Scripture says he was the one "whom the LORD knew face to face" ([[@5034010|Deut 34:10]]).

column5: Innermost room of the tabernacle and temple
column7: It was the innermost room of the tabernacle and the temple. A veil hung inside the tent divided the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place, and in the Most Holy Place the ark of the covenant was kept with the mercy seat on top of it ([[@2026033-2026034|Exod 26:33-34]]). In Solomon's temple the priests carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD into the Most Holy Place, under the wings of the cherubim ([[@11008006|1 Kgs 8:6]]). The high priest could go in there only once a year, with blood ([[@58009007|Heb 9:7]]). Hebrews teaches that Christ entered the holy place once for all, not with the blood of goats and calves but with his own blood, and obtained eternal redemption ([[@58009012|Heb 9:12]]).

column5: Peter’s mother-in-law, healed of a fever by Jesus
column7: She was Simon Peter’s mother-in-law, and she lay sick with a fever ([[@40008014|Matt 8:14]]; [[@41001030|Mark 1:30]]). Jesus touched her hand, and the fever left her; she got up and served him ([[@40008015|Matt 8:15]]).

column5: Son of Caleb and his concubine Ephah
column7: He was a son born to Ephah, Caleb’s concubine, named with Haran and Gazez. He belongs to the genealogy of Caleb of the tribe of Judah ([[@13002046|1 Chr 2:46]]).

column5: Son of Zimri, of Saul's family
column7: He was one of the descendants of Saul's son Jonathan, the son of Zimri and the father of Binea ([[@13008036-13008037|1 Chr 8:36-37]]).

column5: A town of Benjamin
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Benjamin received, listed with Mizpeh and Chephirah ([[@6018021|Josh 18:21]]; [[@6018026|Josh 18:26]]).

column5: Son of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the list of Benjamin’s sons when Jacob’s family went down to Egypt ([[@1046021|Gen 46:21]]). Some think he is the same as Shephupham, from whom the family of the Shuphamites came in Numbers ([[@4026039|Num 26:39]]).

column5: Son of Merari, ancestor of the Mushite family
column7: He was the son of Merari, the son of Levi ([[@13006047|1 Chr 6:47]]). In Exodus he appears with his brother Mahli among the heads of the Levites ([[@2006019|Exod 6:19]]). His descendants formed the family of the Mushites, which together with the family of the Mahlites made up the families of Merari ([[@4003033|Num 3:33]]). 1 Chronicles names three sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth ([[@13023023|1 Chr 23:23]]).

column5: A tiny seed; a picture of small things growing great
column7: The mustard seed is a very small seed, and the Bible always speaks of it because it is so small. Jesus compared the Kingdom of Heaven to a grain of mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his field ([[@40013031|Matt 13:31]]). He said that this seed is smaller than all seeds, but when it is grown it becomes a tree, and the birds of the air come and lodge in its branches ([[@40013032|Matt 13:32]]). He also said that if you have "faith as a grain of mustard seed", you can tell this mountain to move, and it will move ([[@40017020|Matt 17:20]]).

column5: A gate of Jerusalem
column7: In Nehemiah’s time Malchijah the goldsmith made repairs "opposite the gate of Hammiphkad" ([[@16003031|Neh 3:31]]).

column5: The city where Paul’s company changed ships
column7: It is a city of Lycia that Paul’s company reached on the way to Rome. There the centurion found a ship of Alexandria and put them on board ([[@44027005-44027006|Acts 27:5-6]]).

column5: A precious spice used in perfume and burial
column7: Myrrh is a precious, fragrant spice. The Ishmaelite traders whom Joseph's brothers saw were on their way down to Egypt with camels carrying spices, balm, and myrrh ([[@1037025|Gen 37:25]]). Myrrh was one of the fine spices used to make the holy anointing oil ([[@2030023-2030025|Exod 30:23-25]]). The wise men from the east offered myrrh as a gift to the child Jesus, and after Jesus died, Nicodemus brought a mixture of myrrh and aloes weighing about a hundred pounds ([[@40002011|Matt 2:11]]; [[@43019039|John 19:39]]).

column5: A region of Asia Minor Paul passed through
column7: When Paul and his companions came opposite Mysia, they tried to go into Bithynia, but the Spirit of Jesus did not allow them, so they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas ([[@44016007-44016008|Acts 16:7-8]]).

column5: Son of Caleb
column7: He was one of the sons of Caleb the son of Jephunneh, named with Iru and Elah, and Kenaz ([[@13004015|1 Chr 4:15]]).

column5: Sister of Tubal Cain
column7: She was the sister of Tubal Cain, whom Zillah, Lamech’s wife, bore. Tubal Cain was the forger of every cutting instrument of bronze and iron ([[@1004019|Gen 4:19]]; [[@1004022|Gen 4:22]]).

column5: A town in Judah’s lowland
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Judah received in the lowland, listed with Gederoth, Beth Dagon, and Makkedah ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]; [[@6015041|Josh 15:41]]).

column5: Mother of King Rehoboam
column7: She was an Ammonite woman, the mother of Rehoboam king of Judah, Solomon’s son ([[@11014021|1 Kgs 14:21]]; [[@11014031|1 Kgs 14:31]]).

column5: Son of Benjamin
column7: He was one of the sons of Benjamin, listed among Israel's family who went down to Egypt with Jacob ([[@1046008|Gen 46:8]]; [[@1046021|Gen 46:21]]).

column5: Son of Bela, ancestor of the Naamites
column7: The son of Benjamin's son Bela, he was the ancestor of the family of the Naamites ([[@4026040|Num 26:40]]; [[@13008003-13008004|1 Chr 8:3-4]]).

column5: Syrian commander healed through Elisha's word
column7: He was the commander of the army of the king of Syria, a mighty man of valor, but he was a leper ([[@12005001|2 Kgs 5:1]]). A little girl taken captive from Israel said that the prophet in Samaria could heal him, and so he went to find Elisha ([[@12005002-12005009|2 Kgs 5:2-9]]). At first he was angry at what Elisha told him, but when he finally dipped himself seven times in the Jordan, the Bible says "his flesh was restored like the flesh of a little child, and he was clean" ([[@12005011-12005014|2 Kgs 5:11-14]]). Jesus said that of the many lepers in Elisha's time, not one was cleansed "except Naaman, the Syrian" ([[@42004027|Luke 4:27]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Ehud
column7: In the genealogy of Benjamin, his name appears with Ahijah and Gera among the sons of Ehud, who were heads of families of the people of Geba ([[@13008006-13008007|1 Chr 8:6-7]]).

column5: The people of Job's friend Zophar
column7: It is the term used for Zophar, one of Job's three friends ([[@18002011|Job 2:11]]). The book of Job introduces his words with "Zophar, the Naamathite, answered" ([[@18011001|Job 11:1]]).

column5: Wife of Ashhur, the father of Tekoa
column7: She was one of the two wives of Ashhur the father of Tekoa, and she bore Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari ([[@13004005-13004006|1 Chr 4:5-6]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men, son of Ezbai
column7: He was the son of Ezbai, named in the list of David’s mighty men. His name stands next to Hezro the Carmelite ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011037|1 Chr 11:37]]).

column5: A place on Ephraim's eastern border
column7: It was a place at the eastern edge of the land of Ephraim's descendants ([[@13007028|1 Chr 7:28]]). In Joshua it is called 'Naarah' ([[@6016007|Josh 16:7]]).

column5: Abigail's husband, a rich man who insulted David
column7: He was a man of Maon and very rich, with three thousand sheep and a thousand goats in Carmel, but he was described as "surly and evil in his doings" ([[@9025002-9025003|1 Sam 25:2-3]]). When David, who had protected his shepherds in the wilderness, asked for food, Nabal insulted him, saying, "Who is David? Who is the son of Jesse?" ([[@9025010|1 Sam 25:10]]). His wife Abigail wisely went out to meet David and prevented disaster, but when Nabal heard of it his heart sank, and about ten days later the LORD struck him and he died ([[@9025037-9025038|1 Sam 25:37-38]]).

column5: Jezreelite killed by Ahab for his vineyard
column7: He was a man of Jezreel whose vineyard was next to King Ahab's palace ([[@11021001|1 Kgs 21:1]]). When Ahab asked for the vineyard, he refused, saying, "May the LORD forbid me, that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you!" ([[@11021003|1 Kgs 21:3]]). Then Queen Jezebel set up false witnesses and had Naboth stoned to death ([[@11021013|1 Kgs 21:13]]). God sent Elijah to announce judgment on Ahab's house, and that word was fulfilled in Jehu's time ([[@12009026|2 Kgs 9:26]]).

column5: The threshing floor where Uzzah grabbed the ark
column7: At the threshing floor of Nacon the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the ark of God ([[@10006006|2 Sam 6:6]]). In 1 Chronicles it is called 'Chidon's threshing floor' ([[@13013009|1 Chr 13:9]]).

column5: Aaron's firstborn, a priest who offered strange fire
column7: He was the firstborn of Aaron's sons ([[@4003002|Num 3:2]]). At Mount Sinai he went up with Moses, Aaron, his brother Abihu, and seventy of the elders of Israel, and saw the God of Israel ([[@2024009-2024010|Exod 24:9-10]]). With his father Aaron and his brothers, he was called to serve God as a priest ([[@2028001|Exod 28:1]]). But with Abihu he put "strange fire", which the LORD had not commanded, in his censer and offered incense, and fire came out from before the LORD and devoured them ([[@3010001-3010002|Lev 10:1-2]]).

column5: Son of Jeroboam, king of Israel
column7: He was the son of Jeroboam who became king of Israel and reigned two years ([[@11015025|1 Kgs 15:25]]). While he was besieging Gibbethon, Baasha conspired against him and killed him ([[@11015027|1 Kgs 15:27]]).

column5: Son of Shammai, of Judah
column7: A son of Shammai among the descendants of Jerahmeel, he was the father of Seled and Appaim ([[@13002028|1 Chr 2:28]]; [[@13002030|1 Chr 2:30]]).

column5: Son of a Gibeonite, a Benjamite
column7: He was one of the sons of a Benjamite who lived in Gibeon, a brother of Abdon, Zur, Kish, and Baal ([[@13008030|1 Chr 8:30]]; [[@13009036|1 Chr 9:36]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke. He is listed as the father of Esli and the son of Maath ([[@42003025-42003026|Luke 3:25-26]]).

column5: A Levite city in the tribe of Zebulun
column7: It was one of the cities the tribe of Zebulun received, called Nahalal in Joshua, and it was given to the Levites of the children of Merari ([[@6019015|Josh 19:15]]; [[@6021034-6021035|Josh 21:34-35]]). In Judges it appears as 'Nahalol' ([[@7001030|Judg 1:30]]).

column5: Brother of Hodiah’s wife
column7: Judah’s genealogy mentions "the wife of Hodiah, the sister of Naham". Her sons were the fathers of Keilah and Eshtemoa ([[@13004019|1 Chr 4:19]]).

column5: A man who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of those who came back from exile with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, and others ([[@16007007|Neh 7:7]]).

column5: Joab's armor bearer
column7: A Beerothite, he was armor bearer to Joab the son of Zeruiah and one of David's mighty men ([[@10023037|2 Sam 23:37]]; [[@13011039|1 Chr 11:39]]).

column5: Ammonite king who attacked Jabesh Gilead
column7: An Ammonite, he told the people of Jabesh Gilead he would make a treaty with them only if all their right eyes were gouged out ([[@9011002|1 Sam 11:2]]). When he came against them, the people asked for a king ([[@9012012|1 Sam 12:12]]).

column5: King of Ammon, father of Hanun
column7: He was king of the children of Ammon, a man who had shown kindness to David ([[@10010002|2 Sam 10:2]]). When he died, David sent messengers to his son Hanun to comfort him ([[@13019001-13019002|1 Chr 19:1-2]]).

column5: Parent of Abigail
column7: Abigail, the mother of Amasa, Absalom’s army commander, is called "Abigail the daughter of Nahash". Abigail was the sister of Zeruiah, Joab’s mother ([[@10017025|2 Sam 17:25]]).

column5: Father of Shobi of Rabbah
column7: He was the father of Shobi of Rabbah of the children of Ammon, who came to David when David reached Mahanaim ([[@10017027|2 Sam 17:27]]).

column5: Grandson of Esau, a chief of Edom
column7: He was a son of Reuel, Esau’s son, and a descendant of Esau’s wife Basemath ([[@1036013|Gen 36:13]]). He was one of the chiefs in the land of Edom ([[@1036017|Gen 36:17]]).

column5: A Levite overseeing offerings under Hezekiah
column7: In Hezekiah’s time he was one of the overseers under Conaniah, who was in charge of the offerings and tithes, and his brother Shimei ([[@14031012-14031013|2 Chr 31:12-13]]).

column5: The spy from the tribe of Naphtali
column7: He was the son of Vophsi, chosen from the tribe of Naphtali among the men sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013002|Num 13:2]]; [[@4013014|Num 13:14]]).

column5: Son of Serug, grandfather of Abraham
column7: He was a descendant of Shem, the son Serug had at thirty ([[@1011022|Gen 11:22]]). Nahor became the father of Terah at twenty-nine, and after that he lived one hundred nineteen years and had other children ([[@1011024-1011025|Gen 11:24-25]]). Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran, so this Nahor was Abraham's grandfather and a different man from Abraham's brother Nahor ([[@1011026|Gen 11:26]]). His name also appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus ([[@42003034|Luke 3:34]]).

column5: Abraham's brother, Rebekah's grandfather
column7: He was the son of Terah and the brother of Abram and Haran ([[@1011026|Gen 11:26]]). Nahor married Milcah, the daughter of his brother Haran ([[@1011029|Gen 11:29]]). Milcah bore Nahor eight sons, and one of them, Bethuel, became the father of Rebekah ([[@1022020-1022023|Gen 22:20-23]]). Abraham's servant went to "the city of Nahor" in Mesopotamia to find a wife for Isaac, and there he met Rebekah ([[@1024010-1024015|Gen 24:10-15]]). Abraham's grandfather was also named Nahor, but he was a different person.

column5: Leader of the tribe of Judah in the wilderness
column7: He was the son of Amminadab of the tribe of Judah, and when the people were counted in the wilderness, he was appointed head of the tribe of Judah ([[@4001004-4001007|Num 1:4-7]]). When the altar was dedicated, the one who brought his offering on the first day was "Nahshon the son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah" ([[@4007011-4007012|Num 7:11-12]]). His sister Elisheba became the wife of Aaron ([[@2006023|Exod 6:23]]). Nahshon's name also appears in the genealogy of Jesus ([[@40001004|Matt 1:4]]).

column5: The prophet who spoke about Nineveh
column7: He was an Elkoshite, and the book of Nahum begins with the words "A revelation about Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite" ([[@34001001|Nah 1:1]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke. He is listed as the father of Amos and the son of Esli ([[@42003025|Luke 3:25]]).

column5: The town where Jesus raised a widow’s son
column7: It is the town Jesus went to with his disciples and a great crowd. Near its gate he raised a widow’s only son from the dead ([[@42007011-42007015|Luke 7:11-15]]).

column5: Where David stayed with Samuel at Ramah
column7: It was the place where David stayed with Samuel after fleeing from Saul to Ramah ([[@9019018|1 Sam 19:18]]). When Saul heard of it, he sent men to 'Naioth in Ramah' ([[@9019019|1 Sam 19:19]]).

column5: The mother-in-law of Ruth
column7: She was the wife of Elimelech of Bethlehem, and when famine came she moved to the country of Moab with her husband and her two sons, Mahlon and Chilion ([[@8001002|Ruth 1:2]]). There she lost her husband and both sons, and she returned home with her daughter-in-law Ruth ([[@8001022|Ruth 1:22]]). At that time she poured out her sorrow, saying, "Don’t call me Naomi. Call me Mara" ([[@8001020|Ruth 1:20]]). Later, when Ruth married Boaz and gave birth to Obed, Naomi held the baby in her arms and cared for him ([[@8004016|Ruth 4:16]]).

column5: The three heights Manasseh held in Issachar and Asher
column7: After listing what Manasseh held in Issachar and Asher, the verse speaks of "three heights" ([[@6017011|Josh 17:11]]). Scholars differ on which places are meant.

column5: Son of Ishmael
column7: He was one of the sons of Ishmael ([[@1025015|Gen 25:15]]). Later the sons of Reuben, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh fought and won against the Hagrites, Naphish, and others ([[@13005018-13005020|1 Chr 5:18-20]]).

column5: Jacob's son, ancestor of the tribe of Naphtali
column7: Naphtali was the son Jacob had by Bilhah, Rachel's servant ([[@1035025|Gen 35:25]]). Rachel named him, saying, "I have wrestled with my sister with mighty wrestlings, and have prevailed" ([[@1030008|Gen 30:8]]). Jacob blessed him by comparing him to "a doe set free" ([[@1049021|Gen 49:21]]). The tribe of Naphtali received land in northern Galilee, and when Jesus lived in Capernaum in the region of Zebulun and Naphtali, Isaiah's prophecy was fulfilled ([[@40004013-40004016|Matt 4:13-16]]).

column5: Descendants of Mizraim
column7: They were one of the peoples descended from Mizraim, the son of Noah's son Ham, listed with the Ludim, Anamim, and Lehabim ([[@1010013|Gen 10:13]]; [[@13001011|1 Chr 1:11]]).

column5: A man whose household received greetings
column7: Paul told the church at Rome to greet "them of the household of Narcissus, who are in the Lord" ([[@45016011|Rom 16:11]]).

column5: A very costly perfumed ointment
column7: Nard is a very costly perfumed ointment. When Jesus was eating at the house of Simon the leper in Bethany, a woman broke an alabaster jar of pure nard and poured it over Jesus' head ([[@41014003|Mark 14:3]]). Some people scolded the woman, saying this ointment could have been sold for more than three hundred denarii and given to the poor ([[@41014004-41014005|Mark 14:4-5]]). The Gospel of John records that Mary poured a pound of pure nard on Jesus' feet and wiped them with her hair, and the house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment ([[@43012003|John 12:3]]). The Song of Songs also speaks of this perfume spreading its fragrance ([[@22001012|Song 1:12]]).

column5: Son of David and Bathshua
column7: He was a son born to David in Jerusalem, a child of Bathshua ([[@13003005|1 Chr 3:5]]). The genealogy of Jesus in Luke passes through him to David ([[@42003031|Luke 3:31]]).

column5: Prophet in the days of David and Solomon
column7: He was a prophet in the time of King David. When David wanted to build a house for God's ark, Nathan brought him God's word that God would raise up David's offspring and make his kingdom secure forever ([[@10007012-10007017|2 Sam 7:12-17]]). When David sinned in the matter of Bathsheba, Nathan told him a parable about a rich man and a poor man and then told him, "You are the man!" ([[@10012001-10012007|2 Sam 12:1-7]]). When Adonijah tried to make himself king, Nathan and Bathsheba told David, and Solomon was anointed king ([[@11001011-11001034|1 Kgs 1:11-34]]).

column5: Father of Igal, one of David's mighty men
column7: A man of Zobah, he was the father of Igal, one of David's mighty men ([[@10023036|2 Sam 23:36]]). In 1 Chronicles the mighty man Joel is called 'the brother of Nathan' ([[@13011038|1 Chr 11:38]]).

column5: A leader Ezra sent for
column7: He was one of the leaders Ezra sent for when he found none of the sons of Levi at the river that runs to Ahava ([[@15008015-15008016|Ezra 8:15-16]]).

column5: A man who had married a foreign wife
column7: His name appears in the list of those in Ezra’s time who had married foreign women ([[@15010039|Ezra 10:39]]). He is counted among the descendants of Bani ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]).

column5: An officer in Josiah’s time whose room was near the LORD’s house
column7: He was an officer whose room was near the entrance of the LORD’s house. The horses the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun stood near his room until they were taken away ([[@12023011|2 Kgs 23:11]]).

column5: Man of Cana in Galilee, disciple of Jesus
column7: He was a disciple who came to Jesus through Philip. When Philip told him they had found Jesus of Nazareth, the one Moses and the prophets wrote about, he first said, "Can any good thing come out of Nazareth?" ([[@43001045-43001046|John 1:45-46]]). When Jesus saw him, he said, "an Israelite indeed, in whom is no deceit!" and when Jesus said he had seen him under the fig tree, Nathanael confessed that Jesus was the Son of God and the King of Israel ([[@43001047-43001049|John 1:47-49]]). When the risen Jesus appeared to the disciples at the Sea of Tiberias, "Nathanael of Cana in Galilee" was there with them ([[@43021001-43021002|John 21:1-2]]).

column5: The town in Galilee where Jesus grew up
column7: Nazareth was a town in Galilee, the place where the angel Gabriel appeared to Mary ([[@42001026-42001027|Luke 1:26-27]]). After returning from Egypt, Jesus grew up here, and so he was called 'Jesus of Nazareth' ([[@40002023|Matt 2:23]]). When Jesus read from Isaiah in the synagogue of his hometown and spoke, the people were filled with anger and tried to drag him to a cliff outside the town ([[@42004016-42004029|Luke 4:16-29]]). The name does not appear in the Old Testament.

column5: One set apart to God by a special vow
column7: A Nazirite was someone who made a special vow and set himself apart to the LORD. Both men and women could make this vow ([[@4006002|Num 6:2]]). During the vow they did not drink wine or strong drink or eat anything from the grapevine, let no razor touch their head, and did not go near a dead body ([[@4006003-4006006|Num 6:3-6]]). Samson was a Nazirite dedicated to God from the womb ([[@7013005|Judg 13:5]]). When the days of the vow were completed, the Nazirite shaved his head at the door of the Tent of Meeting and put the hair on the fire under the peace offering ([[@4006018|Num 6:18]]).

column5: A place on Zebulun's border
column7: It was a place on the border of the land given to Zebulun's descendants, where the border went out at Rimmon, which stretches to Neah ([[@6019013|Josh 19:13]]).

column5: Where Paul sailed from Troas
column7: It is the place Paul’s company reached the day after they set sail from Troas and passed Samothrace ([[@44016011|Acts 16:11]]).

column5: Son of Shemaiah, of David's royal line
column7: One of the sons of Shemaiah in David's royal line, he was the father of Elioenai, Hizkiah, and Azrikam ([[@13003022-13003023|1 Chr 3:22-23]]).

column5: A Simeonite captain who went to Mount Seir
column7: A son of Ishi, he became one of the captains of five hundred men of Simeon who went to Mount Seir ([[@13004042|1 Chr 4:42]]). There they struck the remnant of the Amalekites ([[@13004043|1 Chr 4:43]]).

column5: A leader of the people who sealed the covenant under Nehemiah
column7: In Nehemiah’s time Nobai was one of the chiefs of the people who made a covenant to keep God’s law and sealed it ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010019|Neh 10:19]]).

column5: Ishmael's firstborn son
column7: He was Ishmael's firstborn ([[@1025013|Gen 25:13]]). Mahalath, whom Esau took as a wife, was the sister of Nebaioth ([[@1028009|Gen 28:9]]).

column5: A place where Benjamites lived after the exile
column7: It was one of the places where the children of Benjamin lived after returning from exile ([[@16011031|Neh 11:31]]; [[@16011034|Neh 11:34]]).

column5: Father of Jeroboam, northern Israel's first king
column7: Nebat was the father of Jeroboam, the first king of northern Israel. Jeroboam was an Ephraimite of Zeredah, and his mother Zeruah was a widow ([[@11011026|1 Kgs 11:26]]). In the Bible he almost always appears only in the phrase "Jeroboam the son of Nebat" ([[@11012002|1 Kgs 12:2]]). Many later kings are said again and again to have walked in 'the way of Jeroboam the son of Nebat,' so the phrase came to mean the path that led Israel into sin ([[@11016026|1 Kgs 16:26]]).

column5: Moabite-area town built by Reuben
column7: It was a town east of the Jordan, one of the places the Reubenites and Gadites asked for because it was good land for livestock ([[@4032003-4032004|Num 32:3-4]]). The Reubenites built Nebo and Baal Meon and changed their names ([[@4032038|Num 32:38]]). Mount Nebo, with the same name, is where Moses went up and looked out over the promised land ([[@5034001|Deut 34:1]]). Later, in their prophecies about Moab, Isaiah and Jeremiah wailed over Nebo and spoke of its ruin ([[@23015002|Isa 15:2]]; [[@24048001|Jer 48:1]]).

column5: Hometown of some who returned from exile
column7: Fifty-two of the children of Nebo came back from exile in Babylon ([[@15002029|Ezra 2:29]]; [[@16007033|Neh 7:33]]). Some of his descendants had taken foreign wives ([[@15010043-15010044|Ezra 10:43-44]]).

column5: Mountain where Moses viewed the promised land
column7: It is a mountain in the Abarim range in the land of Moab, across from Jericho. God told Moses to go up the mountains of Abarim to Mount Nebo and look at the land of Canaan that he was giving to the Israelites as their possession ([[@5032049|Deut 32:49]]). Moses went up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, to the top of Pisgah, and the LORD showed him the land ([[@5034001|Deut 34:1]]). Then, as the LORD had said, he died in the land of Moab and was buried in the valley opposite Beth Peor, and no one knows where his grave is to this day ([[@5034005-5034006|Deut 34:5-6]]).

column5: A Babylonian chief officer who sat in Jerusalem’s middle gate
column7: When Jerusalem fell, he was one of the princes of the king of Babylon who came and sat in the middle gate, and he was the chief officer (the Rabsaris) ([[@24039003|Jer 39:3]]).

column5: The king of Babylon who brought down Judah
column7: He was the king of Babylon who attacked Judah and carried its people away captive. He first came up in Jehoiakim's time and made Judah serve him ([[@12024001|2 Kgs 24:1]]). An army led by his servant Nebuzaradan burned the city of Jerusalem and the temple ([[@12025008-12025011|2 Kgs 25:8-11]]). When Daniel interpreted his dream, he honored Daniel ([[@27002048|Dan 2:48]]). After he was humbled for his pride, he praised the King of heaven and exalted God ([[@27004037|Dan 4:37]]).

column5: The Babylonian chief officer who freed Jeremiah
column7: He was the chief officer (the Rabsaris) of the king of Babylon. With Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard and others, he sent and took Jeremiah out of the court of the guard and entrusted him to Gedaliah ([[@24039013-24039014|Jer 39:13-14]]).

column5: Babylonian captain of the guard who burned Jerusalem
column7: He was the captain of the guard of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. In Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year he came to Jerusalem, burned the LORD's house, the king's house, and the houses of the city, and broke down the walls ([[@12025008-12025010|2 Kgs 25:8-10]]). He carried the remaining people away to Babylon, but he left the poor in the land of Judah and gave them vineyards and fields ([[@24039009-24039010|Jer 39:9-10]]). Following the king's order, he freed Jeremiah, who was being taken away in chains, and let him decide for himself where to go ([[@24039011-24039012|Jer 39:11-12]]; [[@24040001-24040004|Jer 40:1-4]]).

column5: King of Egypt in the days of King Josiah
column7: He was the king of Egypt in the days of King Josiah, and he went up to the river Euphrates to fight against the king of Assyria ([[@12023029|2 Kgs 23:29]]). When Josiah went out to stop him, Neco sent messengers saying he had not come against him, but Josiah would not listen, fought in the valley of Megiddo, was hit by archers, and was brought back to Jerusalem, where he died ([[@14035021-14035024|2 Chr 35:21-24]]). After that Pharaoh Necoh put Josiah's son Jehoahaz in bonds at Riblah so that he could not reign, and he made Eliakim king and changed his name to Jehoiakim ([[@12023033-12023034|2 Kgs 23:33-34]]). Later Pharaoh Necoh's army was defeated at Carchemish by Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon ([[@24046002|Jer 46:2]]).

column5: Son of Jeconiah the captive
column7: He was one of the sons of Jeconiah, the king of Judah who was taken captive, and a brother of Shealtiel, Malchiram, and others ([[@13003017-13003018|1 Chr 3:17-18]]).

column5: The dry land south of Judah
column7: The land often called 'the South', the Negev, is the dry land south of the hill country of Judah. After Abram came into Canaan, he traveled on, still going toward the South ([[@1012009|Gen 12:9]]). Isaac also lived in the South for a time ([[@1024062|Gen 24:62]]). The spies Moses sent went up into Canaan by way of the South ([[@4013017|Num 13:17]]). It is a land of little rain, where streambeds run dry and then flow again when the rain comes, so a psalm prays for the captives to be brought back "like the streams in the Negev" ([[@19126004|Ps 126:4]]).

column5: A title for the false prophet Shemaiah
column7: This is the name given to the false prophet Shemaiah ([[@24029024|Jer 29:24]]). Because he prophesied though the LORD had not sent him and made the people trust in a lie, the LORD said he would punish him and his offspring ([[@24029031-24029032|Jer 29:31-32]]).

column5: A leader who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the leaders who came back from exile in Babylon with Zerubbabel ([[@15002002|Ezra 2:2]]; [[@16007007|Neh 7:7]]).

column5: The governor who rebuilt Jerusalem's walls
column7: He was the son of Hacaliah and was in the palace at Susa in the time of Artaxerxes king of Persia ([[@16001001|Neh 1:1]]). As governor, he joined Ezra in telling the people not to mourn ([[@16008009|Neh 8:9]]).

column5: Son of Azbuk who repaired the wall
column7: He was the son of Azbuk and ruler of half the district of Beth Zur. He repaired the wall of Jerusalem as far as the place opposite the tombs of David ([[@16003016|Neh 3:16]]).

column5: Mother of King Jehoiachin
column7: She was the mother of Jehoiachin king of Judah and the daughter of Elnathan of Jerusalem. Jehoiachin became king at eighteen ([[@12024008|2 Kgs 24:8]]).

column5: A temple servant family that returned from exile
column7: He was the ancestor of 'the children of Nekoda' among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon ([[@15002048|Ezra 2:48]]; [[@16007050|Neh 7:50]]).

column5: A family that could not prove its ancestry
column7: He was the ancestor of 'the children of Nekoda,' who returned from exile but could not show that their family and descent were of Israel ([[@15002059-15002060|Ezra 2:59-60]]).

column5: Son of Eliab of Reuben
column7: He was a son of Eliab the son of Pallu, of the tribe of Reuben. He was a brother of Dathan and Abiram, who joined Korah’s company ([[@4026008-4026009|Num 26:8-9]]).

column5: Son of Izhar, a Kohathite
column7: He was a son of Izhar, the son of Kohath and grandson of Levi. He was a brother of Korah and Zichri ([[@2006018|Exod 6:18]]; [[@2006021|Exod 6:21]]).

column5: A son of David born in Jerusalem
column7: He was one of the sons born to David in Jerusalem ([[@10005013-10005015|2 Sam 5:13-15]]). He also appears in the lists of David’s sons in 1 Chronicles ([[@13003007|1 Chr 3:7]]; [[@13014006|1 Chr 14:6]]).

column5: People on the earth before the Flood
column7: They were people on the earth in those days before the Flood. The same verse says that the children born when God’s sons came in to men’s daughters were "the mighty men who were of old, men of renown" ([[@1006004|Gen 6:4]]).

column5: A spring on the border of Judah and Benjamin
column7: It was a spring on the border between the lands of Judah and Benjamin. The border reached the spring of the waters of Nephtoah ([[@6015009|Josh 15:9]]; [[@6018015|Josh 18:15]]).

column5: A temple servant family that returned from exile
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Nephisim' ([[@15002050|Ezra 2:50]]). In Nehemiah the name is 'Nephushesim' ([[@16007052|Neh 7:52]]).

column5: Father of Abner and uncle of Saul
column7: He was the father of Abner, the commander of Saul's army. The Bible introduces Abner as "the son of Ner, Saul’s uncle" ([[@9014050|1 Sam 14:50]]). Saul's father Kish and Ner both belonged to the family of Abiel ([[@9014051|1 Sam 14:51]]). In the Bible Abner is often called 'Abner the son of Ner' ([[@9026014|1 Sam 26:14]]; [[@10002008|2 Sam 2:8]]). The genealogy in 1 Chronicles records the relationship a little differently, so scholars explain it in different ways.

column5: A believer in Rome whom Paul greeted
column7: He was one of those Paul greeted when he wrote to the church at Rome. He is named together with his sister ([[@45016015|Rom 16:15]]).

column5: The Babylonian king’s Rabmag
column7: When Jerusalem fell, he was one of the princes of the king of Babylon who sat in the middle gate, and he was the Rabmag ([[@24039003|Jer 39:3]]). He was one of those who had Jeremiah taken out of the court of the guard ([[@24039013-24039014|Jer 39:13-14]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Luke. In that genealogy he is listed just above Shealtiel, as his father ([[@42003027|Luke 3:27]]).

column5: Father of Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe
column7: He was the son of Mahseiah and the father of Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe ([[@24032012|Jer 32:12]]). He appears in the Bible mostly in the phrase "Baruch the son of Neriah," and Baruch wrote down Jeremiah's words on a scroll ([[@24036004|Jer 36:4]]). Seraiah, the chief quartermaster who went to Babylon with King Zedekiah, was also "the son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah" ([[@24051059|Jer 51:59]]).

column5: The Caesar to whom Paul appealed
column7: Paul said the charges against him were not true and declared, "I appeal to Caesar!" ([[@44025011|Acts 25:11]]). Among those who sent greetings to the believers in Philippi were "those who are of Caesar’s household" ([[@50004022|Phil 4:22]]).

column5: A place where potters lived
column7: It was where some of the descendants of Judah who were potters lived. There they lived with the king and did his work ([[@13004023|1 Chr 4:23]]).

column5: Leader of the tribe of Issachar in the wilderness
column7: He was the son of Zuar and the leader of the children of Issachar in the wilderness ([[@4001008|Num 1:8]]; [[@4002005|Num 2:5]]). On the second day he brought the offering on behalf of the children of Issachar ([[@4007018|Num 7:18]]).

column5: Jesse’s fourth son, David’s brother
column7: He was Jesse’s fourth son and an older brother of David. He is listed after Eliab, Abinadab, and Shimea ([[@13002013-13002014|1 Chr 2:13-14]]).

column5: A priest who blew a trumpet before God’s ark
column7: When David brought up God’s ark, he was one of the priests who blew trumpets before the ark ([[@13015024-13015025|1 Chr 15:24-25]]).

column5: Father of Shemaiah the scribe
column7: He was a Levite and the father of Shemaiah the scribe, who wrote down the names of the priestly divisions ([[@13024006|1 Chr 24:6]]).

column5: Fifth son of Obed-Edom
column7: He was the fifth son of Obed-Edom, listed in the divisions of the Korahite gatekeepers. Obed-Edom’s firstborn was Shemaiah ([[@13026001|1 Chr 26:1]]; [[@13026004|1 Chr 26:4]]).

column5: A prince Jehoshaphat sent to teach
column7: He was one of the princes King Jehoshaphat sent to teach in the cities of Judah ([[@14017007|2 Chr 17:7]]; [[@14017009|2 Chr 17:9]]).

column5: A chief of the Levites in Josiah’s time
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the Levites in Josiah’s time. He gave the Levites sheep and cattle for the Passover offerings ([[@14035009|2 Chr 35:9]]).

column5: A priest of Pashhur’s family who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra’s time he was a descendant of Pashhur among the priests who had married foreign women ([[@15010018|Ezra 10:18]]; [[@15010022|Ezra 10:22]]).

column5: Head of the family of Jedaiah under Joiakim
column7: In the days of Joiakim he was one of the heads of priestly families, the head of the family of Jedaiah ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012021|Neh 12:21]]).

column5: A musician at the wall’s dedication
column7: He was one of Zechariah’s relatives who played the musical instruments of David when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated ([[@16012035-16012036|Neh 12:35-36]]).

column5: Father of Ishmael, who killed Gedaliah
column7: He was the son of Elishama of the royal family and the father of Ishmael, who killed Governor Gedaliah ([[@12025025|2 Kgs 25:25]]). Jeremiah also names him as Ishmael's father ([[@24040008|Jer 40:8]]). The Bible tells nothing of his own deeds and mostly introduces him through the name "Ishmael the son of Nethaniah". His son Ishmael killed Gedaliah while eating bread with him at Mizpah ([[@24041001-24041002|Jer 41:1-2]]), and later fled to the children of Ammon ([[@24041015|Jer 41:15]]).

column5: Son of Asaph, a singer
column7: A son of Asaph, he prophesied in song under the king's order and was given the fifth turn in the service of praise ([[@13025002|1 Chr 25:2]]; [[@13025012|1 Chr 25:12]]).

column5: A Levite Jehoshaphat sent out
column7: He was one of the Levites King Jehoshaphat sent with the princes through Judah to teach the law ([[@14017008-14017009|2 Chr 17:8-9]]).

column5: Father of Jehudi, son of Shelemiah
column7: He was the father of Jehudi, whom the princes sent to Baruch. He was the son of Shelemiah and the grandson of Cushi ([[@24036014|Jer 36:14]]).

column5: A village of Judah near Bethlehem
column7: It was a village of Judah thought to lie near Bethlehem. In the genealogy of 1 Chronicles, Bethlehem and the Netophathites appear together among the descendants of Salma ([[@13002054|1 Chr 2:54]]). Among David's mighty men were Maharai and Heleb, both from Netophah ([[@10023028-10023029|2 Sam 23:28-29]]). Maharai later became the commander of the tenth division of David's army, serving in the tenth month ([[@13027013|1 Chr 27:13]]). Among those who returned from exile in Babylon were fifty-six men of Netophah ([[@15002022|Ezra 2:22]]).

column5: A gate of the LORD's house
column7: It was a gate of the LORD's house. The princes of Judah sat at the entrance of this gate, and Baruch read Jeremiah's words from a room beside it ([[@24026010|Jer 26:10]]; [[@24036010|Jer 36:10]]).

column5: A temple servant ancestor who returned from exile
column7: He was the ancestor of 'the children of Neziah' among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon ([[@15002054|Ezra 2:54]]; [[@16007056|Neh 7:56]]).

column5: A town in Judah’s lowland
column7: It was a town in the lowland, part of the inheritance the tribe of Judah received according to their families ([[@6015020|Josh 15:20]]; [[@6015043|Josh 15:43]]).

column5: A town in the wilderness of Judah
column7: It was one of the towns in the wilderness that the tribe of Judah received, listed with the City of Salt and En Gedi ([[@6015061-6015062|Josh 15:61-62]]).

column5: One of the seven chosen by the Jerusalem church
column7: He was one of the seven men the church in Jerusalem chose to take charge of serving the needy ([[@44006003|Acts 6:3]]; [[@44006005|Acts 6:5]]).

column5: The Pharisee who came to Jesus by night
column7: He was a Pharisee and a ruler of the Jews who came to Jesus and heard his words about being born anew ([[@43003001-43003004|John 3:1-4]]). After Jesus died, he came bringing myrrh and aloes ([[@43019039|John 19:39]]).

column5: One of the seven, a man of Antioch
column7: He was a proselyte from Antioch and one of the seven men chosen by the church in Jerusalem ([[@44006005|Acts 6:5]]).

column5: Where Paul planned to spend the winter
column7: It is the place where Paul decided to spend the winter. Paul told Titus to hurry and come to him there ([[@56003012|Titus 3:12]]).

column5: Great river flowing through Egypt
column7: It is the great river that flows from south to north through the land of Egypt. In most passages it is simply called 'the river,' and the name 'Nile' itself appears only a few times, in books such as Isaiah and Jeremiah ([[@23019007|Isa 19:7]]). Pharaoh dreamed that he stood by the river ([[@1041001|Gen 41:1]]). Moses' mother put her baby in a papyrus basket and laid it in the reeds by the river's bank ([[@2002003|Exod 2:3]]). In the first plague, God turned all the water of the river into blood ([[@2007020|Exod 7:20]]).

column5: Waters in the land of Moab
column7: It was a source of water in the land of Moab. Speaking of judgment on Moab, Isaiah and Jeremiah said the waters of Nimrim would become desolate ([[@23015006|Isa 15:6]]; [[@24048034|Jer 48:34]]).

column5: The first mighty one on earth, a mighty hunter
column7: He was the son of Cush and began "to be a mighty one on the earth" ([[@1010008|Gen 10:8]]). He became a mighty hunter before the LORD, and his name became a saying ([[@1010009|Gen 10:9]]).

column5: Grandfather of King Jehu
column7: He was the grandfather of Jehu king of Israel ([[@12009002|2 Kgs 9:2]]). Jehu was often called 'the son of Nimshi' as well ([[@11019016|1 Kgs 19:16]]).

column5: Great city of Assyria
column7: It was the great city of Assyria, first named in Genesis ([[@1010011|Gen 10:11]]). God sent Jonah to rebuke its wickedness, and to show how large it was the Bible says, "Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, three days’ journey across." When they heard Jonah's warning, the people of Nineveh believed God, fasted, and put on sackcloth ([[@32003003-32003005|Jonah 3:3-5]]). Later the prophets Nahum and Zephaniah prophesied that Nineveh would be laid waste ([[@34003007|Nah 3:7]]; [[@36002013|Zeph 2:13]]).

column5: A Levite present when the temple vessels were weighed
column7: He was the son of Binnui, a Levite who was there in Ezra’s time when the silver, gold, and vessels were weighed and handed over to Meremoth ([[@15008033|Ezra 8:33]]).

column5: The prophetess who tried to frighten Nehemiah
column7: She was a prophetess who tried to make Nehemiah afraid. Nehemiah prayed that God would remember what she had done ([[@16006014|Neh 6:14]]).

column5: The righteous man saved from the flood
column7: Noah was the son of Lamech, and his father named him, saying, "This one will comfort us" ([[@1005029|Gen 5:29]]). Even when the whole earth was full of sin, he walked with God, as it says, "Noah found favor in the LORD’s eyes" ([[@1006008-1006009|Gen 6:8-9]]). He built the ark just as God commanded and was saved from the flood together with his family and the animals ([[@1006022|Gen 6:22]]). After the flood, God set the rainbow as the sign of his covenant and promised never again to destroy the world with water ([[@1009013|Gen 9:13]]).

column5: A daughter of Zelophehad
column7: She was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh ([[@4026033|Num 26:33]]). With her sisters she came to Moses to ask for her father's inheritance ([[@4027001|Num 27:1]]).

column5: Priests' town where Saul killed the priests
column7: It was the town where the priest Ahimelech and all the priests of his father's house lived in Saul's time ([[@9022011|1 Sam 22:11]]). David, fleeing from Saul, went to Nob and received from Ahimelech the showbread, that is, the holy bread, and Goliath's sword ([[@9021001-9021009|1 Sam 21:1-9]]). Doeg the Edomite, who saw this, reported it to Saul, and at Saul's command Doeg killed eighty-five priests who wore the linen ephod and struck the town of Nob, people and animals alike, with the sword ([[@9022009|1 Sam 22:9]], 18-19). Isaiah says the Assyrian army would halt at Nob and shake its fist toward Jerusalem, so it seems to have been near Jerusalem ([[@23010032|Isa 10:32]]).

column5: The land east of Eden where Cain lived
column7: It is the land where Cain lived after he left the LORD’s presence. It is said to have been east of Eden ([[@1004016|Gen 4:16]]).

column5: A son of David born in Jerusalem
column7: He was one of the sons born to David in Jerusalem, named alongside Nepheg and Japhia ([[@13003005-13003007|1 Chr 3:5-7]]; [[@13014006|1 Chr 14:6]]).

column5: The father of Joshua
column7: Nun was the father of Joshua. In the Bible he almost always appears only in the phrase "Joshua the son of Nun" ([[@4014006|Num 14:6]]). He was of the tribe of Ephraim ([[@4013008|Num 13:8]]), and Moses called Nun's son Hoshea, whom he sent as a spy, Joshua ([[@4013016|Num 13:16]]). In 1 Chronicles, at the end of the family line running from Ephraim to Joshua, it is written, "Nun his son, and Joshua his son" ([[@13007027|1 Chr 7:27]]). Nothing else about him is recorded in the Bible.

column5: A believer with a church in his house
column7: Paul sent greetings to Nymphas and to the assembly that met in his house. He was greeted along with the brothers in Laodicea ([[@51004015|Col 4:15]]).

column5: Ahab's palace official who hid the prophets
column7: He was in charge of Ahab's household and was a man who greatly feared the LORD ([[@11018003|1 Kgs 18:3]]). When Jezebel was killing the prophets, he hid a hundred of them in caves and fed them ([[@11018004|1 Kgs 18:4]]).

column5: A man in the genealogy of David’s royal house
column7: This name appears in the genealogy of David’s royal house after the exile, where his sons are recorded ([[@13003021|1 Chr 3:21]]).

column5: Son of Izrahiah of Issachar
column7: From the family of Tola of Issachar, he was a son of Izrahiah. Along with his brothers he was a chief man ([[@13007001-13007003|1 Chr 7:1-3]]).

column5: Son of Azel, a descendant of Saul
column7: He was one of the six sons of Azel, a descendant of Saul through Jonathan ([[@13008038|1 Chr 8:38]]; [[@13009044|1 Chr 9:44]]).

column5: A Levite descended from Jeduthun
column7: He was the son of Shemaiah and a great-grandson of Jeduthun, listed among the Levites who returned from exile ([[@13009002|1 Chr 9:2]]; [[@13009016|1 Chr 9:16]]). Some think he is the same as 'Abda' in Nehemiah ([[@16011017|Neh 11:17]]).

column5: A Gadite warrior who joined David
column7: He was the second of the Gadite warriors who joined David. The first, the chief, was Ezer ([[@13012008-13012009|1 Chr 12:8-9]]).

column5: Father of Ishmaiah, ruler of Zebulun
column7: He was the father of Ishmaiah, the ruler of Zebulun among those over the tribes of Israel in David’s time ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027019|1 Chr 27:19]]).

column5: A prince Jehoshaphat sent to teach
column7: He was one of the princes King Jehoshaphat sent to teach in the cities of Judah ([[@14017007|2 Chr 17:7]]).

column5: A Levite who oversaw temple repairs under Josiah
column7: He was a Levite of the sons of Merari who oversaw the work of repairing the LORD’s house in Josiah’s time ([[@14034012|2 Chr 34:12]]).

column5: A descendant of Joab who returned with Ezra
column7: He was the son of Jehiel, of the descendants of Joab. He came up from Babylon with Ezra along with two hundred eighteen men ([[@15008009|Ezra 8:9]]).

column5: A priest who sealed the covenant
column7: His name appears as a priest among those who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah’s time ([[@16010005|Neh 10:5]]; [[@16010008|Neh 10:8]]).

column5: The prophet who received the vision about Edom
column7: He is the prophet whose book bears his name. He delivered what the Lord GOD said about Edom ([[@31001001|Obad 1:1]]).

column5: Son of Joktan
column7: He was one of the sons of Joktan, a descendant of Shem ([[@1010028|Gen 10:28]]). In 1 Chronicles he is called 'Ebal' ([[@13001022|1 Chr 1:22]]).

column5: Son of Boaz and Ruth, David's grandfather
column7: He was the son born to Boaz and Ruth, the father of Jesse, who was David's father ([[@8004017|Ruth 4:17]]). His name also appears in the genealogy of Jesus ([[@40001005|Matt 1:5]]).

column5: Son of Ephlal, of Judah
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jerahmeel's descendants in Judah, as the son of Ephlal and the father of Jehu ([[@13002037-13002038|1 Chr 2:37-38]]).

column5: One of David’s mighty men
column7: He appears near the end of the list of David’s mighty men, together with Eliel and Jaasiel the Mezobaite ([[@13011047|1 Chr 11:47]]).

column5: Son of Shemaiah the gatekeeper
column7: He was a son of Shemaiah the son of Obed-Edom, from a family of gatekeepers. Among his relatives were valiant men ([[@13026006-13026007|1 Chr 26:6-7]]).

column5: Father of Azariah, a captain of hundreds
column7: He was the father of Azariah, one of the captains of hundreds who entered into a covenant with Jehoiada in the seventh year ([[@14023001|2 Chr 23:1]]).

column5: The man who kept the ark for three months
column7: He was the Gittite to whose house David carried the ark aside after Uzzah died while the ark was being moved ([[@10006007-10006010|2 Sam 6:7-10]]). The LORD's ark stayed in his house for three months, and the LORD blessed his whole household. When David heard this, he joyfully brought God's ark up from the house of Obed-Edom to David's city ([[@10006011-10006012|2 Sam 6:11-12]]). 1 Chronicles mentions a Levite named Obed-Edom who kept the doors before the ark and played the harp, but scholars differ on whether he is the same man ([[@13015021|1 Chr 15:21]]; [[@13015024|1 Chr 15:24]]).

column5: The Ishmaelite in charge of David’s camels
column7: He was an Ishmaelite who was in charge of King David’s camels. The same verse also names the men in charge of the donkeys and the flocks ([[@13027030|1 Chr 27:30]]).

column5: A place where Israel camped in the wilderness
column7: It was where the children of Israel camped after leaving Punon on their way through the wilderness ([[@4033043|Num 33:43]]). From there they set out and camped at Iye Abarim, facing Moab ([[@4021010-4021011|Num 21:10-11]]).

column5: Father of Pagiel, leader of the tribe of Asher
