column7: He was the father of Pagiel, the leader of the children of Asher in the wilderness ([[@4001013|Num 1:13]]). His son brought the offering on behalf of the children of Asher on the eleventh day ([[@4007072|Num 7:72]]).

column5: Father of the prophet Azariah
column7: He was the father of the prophet Azariah. The Spirit of God came on Azariah the son of Oded, and when King Asa heard the prophecy, he put away the detestable idols ([[@14015001|2 Chr 15:1]]; [[@14015008|2 Chr 15:8]]).

column5: The prophet who said to send the captives back
column7: He was a prophet of the LORD who went out to meet the army returning to Samaria. He told them to send back the captives they had taken from Judah ([[@14028009|2 Chr 28:9]]; [[@14028011|2 Chr 28:11]]).

column5: King of Bashan defeated by Israel
column7: He was the king of the land of Bashan east of the Jordan, one of the last of the Rephaim. His bedstead was made of iron and was nine cubits long and four cubits wide ([[@5003011|Deut 3:11]]). When Israel went up toward Bashan, he came out to fight at Edrei, but God delivered him and his people into Israel's hand ([[@4021033-4021035|Num 21:33-35]]). His land was given to the children of Gad and Reuben and to the half-tribe of Manasseh ([[@4032033|Num 32:33]]), and a psalm calls us to thank God, who struck down Og king of Bashan ([[@19136020|Ps 136:20]]).

column5: Son of Simeon
column7: He was one of the sons of Simeon, listed among Israel's family who went down to Egypt with Jacob ([[@1046010|Gen 46:10]]; [[@2006015|Exod 6:15]]).

column5: A man of Zerubbabel’s family
column7: He appears in the list of Zerubbabel’s descendants, one of five men named with Hashubah, Berechiah, and others ([[@13003019-13003020|1 Chr 3:19-20]]).

column5: A name for Samaria
column7: In the parable Ezekiel received, it says, "Samaria is Oholah" ([[@26023004|Ezek 23:4]]). Oholah is said to have played the prostitute, doting on her neighbors the Assyrians ([[@26023005|Ezek 23:5]]).

column5: A craftsman of Dan who built the tabernacle
column7: He was the son of Ahisamach of the tribe of Dan, appointed to work on the tabernacle with Bezalel ([[@2031006|Exod 31:6]]). God moved his heart and enabled him to teach ([[@2035034|Exod 35:34]]).

column5: Ezekiel's name for Jerusalem
column7: In Ezekiel's parable it is the name of the younger of two sisters, standing for Jerusalem ([[@26023004|Ezek 23:4]]). She was said to be even more corrupt than her older sister Oholah ([[@26023011|Ezek 23:11]]).

column5: Esau's wife, daughter of Anah the Hivite
column7: She was one of the wives Esau took in the land of Canaan, the granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite and the daughter of Anah ([[@1036002|Gen 36:2]], 14). She bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah to Esau, and these sons became chiefs of Edom ([[@1036005|Gen 36:5]], 18). Some think she is the same person as 'Judith,' who appears as Esau's wife in Genesis 26, but scholars differ ([[@1026034|Gen 26:34]]). The list of Edom's chiefs also includes 'chief Oholibamah' ([[@1036041|Gen 36:41]]).

column5: A tree whose fruit is pressed for oil
column7: The olive tree is a tree whose fruit is pressed for oil. After the flood, when the dove came back with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her mouth, Noah knew that the waters had gone down from the earth ([[@1008011|Gen 8:11]]). The lamps of the tabernacle were to burn continually with pure olive oil beaten from olives ([[@2027020|Exod 27:20]]). Paul compared Gentile believers to a wild olive grafted into the cultivated olive tree ([[@45011017|Rom 11:17]]). Jesus sat on the Mount of Olives and taught his disciples about the signs of the end of the age ([[@40024003|Matt 24:3]]).

column5: The mountain east of Jerusalem
column7: It is the mountain facing Jerusalem on the east ([[@38014004|Zech 14:4]]). David went up its path weeping as he fled from Absalom ([[@10015030|2 Sam 15:30]]). At Bethphage on this mountain Jesus prepared to enter Jerusalem, and sitting on the mountain he taught about the signs of the end of the age ([[@40024003|Matt 24:3]]). After the Last Supper, too, he sang a hymn with his disciples and went out to this mountain. Acts also calls it 'the mountain called Olivet' ([[@44001012|Acts 1:12]]).

column5: A believer in Rome whom Paul greeted
column7: He was one of those Paul greeted when he wrote to the church at Rome. He was greeted together with all the saints who were with them ([[@45016015|Rom 16:15]]).

column5: Grandson of Esau, a chief of Edom
column7: He was a son of Eliphaz, Esau’s firstborn ([[@1036011|Gen 36:11]]). He was one of the chiefs of Edom ([[@1036015|Gen 36:15]]).

column5: A unit for measuring manna, a tenth of an ephah
column7: The omer was a unit of measure, one tenth of an ephah ([[@2016036|Exod 16:36]]). In the wilderness, God had the people gather manna by the number of persons, an omer for each person ([[@2016016|Exod 16:16]]). When they measured it with an omer, the one who gathered much had nothing left over, and the one who gathered little had no lack ([[@2016018|Exod 16:18]]). Moses told Aaron to put an omer of manna in a pot and lay it up before the LORD to be kept throughout their generations ([[@2016033|Exod 16:33]]).

column5: King of Israel and father of Ahab
column7: He was the commander of Israel's army, and when Zimri killed King Elah, the people in the camp made him king over Israel ([[@11016016|1 Kgs 16:16]]). He besieged Tirzah and brought Zimri down, and when the people split in two and some followed Tibni, Omri's side won ([[@11016017-11016022|1 Kgs 16:17-22]]). He reigned twelve years; after reigning six years in Tirzah, he bought a hill from Shemer for two talents of silver and built the city of Samaria ([[@11016023-11016024|1 Kgs 16:23-24]]). But he did more evil in the LORD's sight than all who were before him, and when he died his son Ahab became king ([[@11016025-11016028|1 Kgs 16:25-28]]).

column5: Son of Becher of Benjamin
column7: He was one of the sons of Becher the son of Benjamin. These men were heads of their fathers’ houses and mighty men of valor ([[@13007006|1 Chr 7:6]]; [[@13007008-13007009|1 Chr 7:8-9]]).

column5: Grandfather of Uthai, who lived in Jerusalem
column7: He was a descendant of Perez the son of Judah. He was the grandfather of Uthai, who lived in Jerusalem after the exile ([[@13009003-13009004|1 Chr 9:3-4]]).

column5: Ruler of Issachar in David’s time
column7: He was the son of Michael and the ruler of the tribe of Issachar in David’s time. The same verse also names Elihu, the ruler of Judah ([[@13027018|1 Chr 27:18]]).

column5: Egyptian city where Potiphera was priest
column7: It was a city in Egypt, where Joseph's father-in-law Potiphera was priest. Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-Paneah and gave him "Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On" as his wife ([[@1041045|Gen 41:45]]). Before the famine came, Asenath bore Manasseh and Ephraim to Joseph ([[@1041050-1041052|Gen 41:50-52]]; [[@1046020|Gen 46:20]]). Some take 'Aven' in Ezekiel to be the same place, but scholars differ ([[@26030017|Ezek 30:17]]).

column5: A Reubenite in Korah’s rebellion
column7: He was the son of Peleth, of the tribe of Reuben. He joined Korah, Dathan, and Abiram in their rebellion ([[@4016001|Num 16:1]]).

column5: Son of Shobal the Horite
column7: He was one of the sons of Shobal, a descendant of Seir the Horite, the original inhabitants of the land ([[@1036020|Gen 36:20]]; [[@1036023|Gen 36:23]]).

column5: Son of Jerahmeel and Atarah
column7: He was the son of Jerahmeel by his other wife, Atarah. His sons were Shammai and Jada ([[@13002026|1 Chr 2:26]]; [[@13002028|1 Chr 2:28]]).

column5: Judah's second son
column7: He was Judah's second son ([[@1038004|Gen 38:4]]). Because he refused to do his duty of raising up offspring for his brother, the LORD put him to death too ([[@1038009-1038010|Gen 38:9-10]]).

column5: The man Paul sent back to Philemon
column7: He was a man from Colossae whom Paul called 'the faithful and beloved brother' ([[@51004009|Col 4:9]]). Paul appealed to Philemon for Onesimus, the son he had fathered while in chains ([[@57001010-57001012|Phlm 1:10-12]]).

column5: A man who often refreshed Paul
column7: He often refreshed Paul and was not ashamed of his chains ([[@55001016|2 Tim 1:16]]). Paul sent greetings to his household ([[@55004019|2 Tim 4:19]]).

column5: A Benjamite town near Lod
column7: It was a town that Shemed, a descendant of Benjamin, built along with Lod ([[@13008012|1 Chr 8:12]]). Sanballat and Geshem asked Nehemiah to meet them in 'the plain of Ono' so they could harm him ([[@16006002|Neh 6:2]]).

column5: A walled area of Jerusalem
column7: It was an area of Jerusalem, and Jotham built a great deal on the wall of Ophel ([[@14027003|2 Chr 27:3]]). Manasseh also encircled Ophel and raised it very high ([[@14033014|2 Chr 33:14]]).

column5: Son of Joktan
column7: He was one of the sons of Joktan, the son of Eber in Shem's line, and a brother of Havilah and Jobab ([[@1010025|Gen 10:25]]; [[@1010029|Gen 10:29]]).

column5: A distant land famous for fine gold
column7: It was a land famous for its fine gold, but scholars differ on exactly where it was. Solomon built ships at Ezion Geber, and Hiram's sailors went with Solomon's servants to Ophir and brought back four hundred twenty talents of gold ([[@11009026-11009028|1 Kgs 9:26-28]]). Hiram's ships also brought from Ophir great quantities of almug trees and precious stones ([[@11010011|1 Kgs 10:11]]). Jehoshaphat also sent ships to Ophir for gold, but the ships were wrecked at Ezion Geber ([[@11022048|1 Kgs 22:48]]). In Job, "the gold of Ophir" appears as something precious that still cannot compare with the value of wisdom ([[@18028016|Job 28:16]]).

column5: A town of Benjamin
column7: It was one of the towns the tribe of Benjamin received according to their families. It is listed with Chephar Ammoni and Geba ([[@6018021|Josh 18:21]]; [[@6018024|Josh 18:24]]).

column5: A town of the tribe of Benjamin
column7: It was one of the cities the tribe of Benjamin received ([[@6018021-6018023|Josh 18:21-23]]). In Saul’s day, one company of Philistine raiders went by 'the way that leads to Ophrah' to the land of Shual ([[@9013017|1 Sam 13:17]]).

column5: Gideon's hometown, a town of the Abiezrites
column7: It was a town that belonged to Joash the Abiezrite, and the hometown of his son Gideon. The angel of the LORD appeared there under the oak to Gideon while he was threshing wheat, and Gideon built an altar there and called it "The LORD is Peace" ([[@7006011-7006012|Judg 6:11-12]], 24). After the victory over Midian, Gideon made an ephod of gold and put it in Ophrah, and all Israel worshiped it like prostitutes, and it became a snare to Gideon and his house ([[@7008027|Judg 8:27]]). Gideon was buried in the tomb of his father Joash in Ophrah, and later Abimelech killed his seventy brothers at his father's house there ([[@7008032|Judg 8:32]]; [[@7009005|Judg 9:5]]).

column5: Son of Meonothai of Judah
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Judah as the son of Meonothai. The same verse also mentions Joab, the father of Ge Harashim, whose people were craftsmen ([[@13004014|1 Chr 4:14]]).

column5: A prince of Midian
column7: He was one of the two princes of Midian; he was captured and killed at Oreb’s rock ([[@7007025|Judg 7:25]]). Gideon said that God had delivered Oreb and Zeeb into the hands of the men of Ephraim ([[@7008003|Judg 8:3]]).

column5: Son of Jerahmeel
column7: He was a son of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron. He was a brother of Ram the firstborn, Bunah, Ozem, and Ahijah ([[@13002025|1 Chr 2:25]]).

column5: Jebusite who sold David his threshing floor
column7: A Jebusite who lived in Jerusalem; in 2 Samuel he is called 'Araunah' ([[@10024016|2 Sam 24:16]]). When a plague came because David had counted the people, the angel of the LORD stopped beside Ornan's threshing floor ([[@13021015|1 Chr 21:15]]). Ornan wanted to give the land and the offerings for free, but David paid for them, saying, "I will not take that which is yours for the LORD, nor offer a burnt offering that costs me nothing" ([[@13021024|1 Chr 21:24]]). Later Solomon built the temple on this very spot ([[@14003001|2 Chr 3:1]]).

column5: Naomi's Moabite daughter-in-law
column7: She was Naomi's Moabite daughter-in-law and Ruth's sister-in-law ([[@8001004|Ruth 1:4]]). She kissed her mother-in-law and went back to her own people ([[@8001014-8001015|Ruth 1:14-15]]).

column5: The man who settled peoples in Samaria
column7: Called "the great and noble Osnappar", he brought over various peoples and settled them in the city of Samaria and in the country beyond the River ([[@15004010|Ezra 4:10]]).

column5: Gatekeeper, son of Shemaiah
column7: Son of Shemaiah, the son of Obed-Edom, from a family of gatekeepers. Obed-Edom's descendants were able men, strong for their service ([[@13026007-13026008|1 Chr 26:7-8]]).

column5: First deliverer in Judges, son of Kenaz
column7: He was the son of Kenaz, and the Bible calls him "Caleb’s younger brother." When Caleb promised his daughter Achsah to whoever attacked and took Kiriath Sepher, Othniel took the town and won Achsah as his wife ([[@6015016-6015017|Josh 15:16-17]]). When Israel had served Cushan Rishathaim king of Mesopotamia for eight years and cried out to the LORD, the LORD raised up Othniel as a savior ([[@7003008-7003009|Judg 3:8-9]]). The Spirit of the LORD came on him, he became judge of Israel and defeated Cushan Rishathaim, and the land had rest for forty years ([[@7003010-7003011|Judg 3:10-11]]).

column5: Sixth son of Jesse
column7: The sixth son of Jesse and an older brother of David. David was the seventh ([[@13002013|1 Chr 2:13]]; [[@13002015|1 Chr 2:15]]).

column5: Son of Jerahmeel
column7: A son of Jerahmeel, the firstborn of Hezron. He was a brother of Ram, Bunah, Oren, and Ahijah ([[@13002025|1 Chr 2:25]]).

column5: One of David's mighty men, an Arbite
column7: Listed among David's mighty men alongside Hezro the Carmelite; he was an Arbite ([[@10023035|2 Sam 23:35]]).

column5: A place mentioned in some manuscripts of 1 Timothy
column7: Pacatiana is a place mentioned in some manuscripts of <ref="1Ti.6.21">1Ti.6.21</ref>, but its exact location and significance are unknown.

column5: Home of Rebekah and Laban in Mesopotamia
column7: It was a land in Mesopotamia where Abraham's relatives Bethuel and Laban lived. Isaac's wife Rebekah came from the Syrians of this place ([[@1025020|Gen 25:20]]). As his father Isaac told him, Jacob went to his uncle Laban in Paddan Aram and took a wife there ([[@1028002-1028005|Gen 28:2-5]]). Later he returned to Canaan with the livestock and possessions he had gained there ([[@1031018|Gen 31:18]]), and all of Jacob's sons except Benjamin were born in Paddan Aram ([[@1035023-1035026|Gen 35:23-26]]).

column5: A temple servant ancestor who returned from exile
column7: He was the ancestor of 'the children of Padon' among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon ([[@15002044|Ezra 2:44]]; [[@16007047|Neh 7:47]]).

column5: Leader of the tribe of Asher in the wilderness
column7: He was the son of Ochran and the leader of the children of Asher in the wilderness ([[@4001013|Num 1:13]]; [[@4002027|Num 2:27]]). On the eleventh day he brought the offering on behalf of the children of Asher ([[@4007072|Num 7:72]]).

column5: A family that returned from exile
column7: It was the name of a family that returned from exile, and the descendants of Pahathmoab numbered two thousand eight hundred twelve ([[@15002006|Ezra 2:6]]). Some of them also came up with Ezra ([[@15008004|Ezra 8:4]]).

column5: Ancestor of Hasshub, who repaired the wall
column7: In Nehemiah's time his son Hasshub repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall and the tower of the furnaces ([[@16003011|Neh 3:11]]).

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: One of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time; he is listed right after Parosh ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]).

column5: Son of Uzai who repaired the wall
column7: Son of Uzai, he repaired the section opposite the tower that stands out from the king's upper house in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003025|Neh 3:25]]).

column5: A son of Reuben
column7: He was a son of Reuben and one of the heads of Reuben's families ([[@1046009|Gen 46:9]]; [[@2006014|Exod 6:14]]). From him came the family of the Palluites, and his son was Eliab ([[@4026005|Num 26:5]]; [[@4026008|Num 26:8]]).

column5: Spy from the tribe of Benjamin
column7: Son of Raphu, the man from the tribe of Benjamin whom Moses sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013009|Num 13:9]]; [[@4013016|Num 13:16]]).

column5: The man given Michal as his wife
column7: The son of Laish from Gallim, he was given David's wife Michal by Saul ([[@9025044|1 Sam 25:44]]). In 2 Samuel he is called 'Paltiel' ([[@10003015|2 Sam 3:15]]).

column5: Issachar prince who helped divide the land
column7: Son of Azzan, he was the prince of the tribe of Issachar chosen to divide the land for inheritance ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034026|Num 34:26]]).

column5: A coastal region in southern Asia Minor
column7: It was one of the homelands of the people who came to Jerusalem at Pentecost ([[@44002010|Acts 2:10]]). Paul and his companions arrived at Perga in Pamphylia ([[@44013013|Acts 13:13]]).

column5: A city on the island of Cyprus
column7: A city on the island of Cyprus, it is where Paul and his companions met the false prophet Bar Jesus ([[@44013006|Acts 13:6]]). From there they sailed to Perga in Pamphylia ([[@44013013|Acts 13:13]]).

column5: A story that teaches a deeper meaning by comparison
column7: A parable is a saying that makes a deeper meaning known by comparing it to something familiar. An Old Testament poet also said, "I will open my mouth in a parable", promising to tell dark sayings of old ([[@19078002|Ps 78:2]]). Jesus taught with many parables, such as the story of the farmer who went out to sow, and he said nothing to the crowds without a parable ([[@40013003|Matt 13:3]], 34). When the disciples asked why he spoke in parables, Jesus answered that it had been given to them to know the mysteries of the Kingdom of Heaven ([[@40013010-40013011|Matt 13:10-11]]). And when he was alone with his disciples, he explained everything to them ([[@41004034|Mark 4:34]]).

column5: The blessed place of being with God
column7: Paradise originally means 'a beautiful garden', and in the Bible it refers to the blessed place of being with God. When one of the criminals crucified with Jesus asked him to remember him, Jesus promised, "today you will be with me in Paradise" ([[@42023042-42023043|Luke 23:42-43]]). Paul said he knew a man who was caught up into Paradise and heard words that no one may utter ([[@47012004|2 Cor 12:4]]). The Lord said that to the one who overcomes he will give fruit to eat from the tree of life in the Paradise of God ([[@66002007|Rev 2:7]]).

column5: City of the tribe of Benjamin
column7: One of the cities the tribe of Benjamin received according to their families. It is listed with Avvim and Ophrah ([[@6018021|Josh 18:21]]; [[@6018023|Josh 18:23]]).

column5: Wilderness north of the Sinai Peninsula
column7: It is a wide wilderness stretching across the north of the Sinai Peninsula. Ishmael, Hagar's son, lived in this wilderness of Paran ([[@1021020-1021021|Gen 21:20-21]]). When the Israelites left the wilderness of Sinai, the cloud settled in the wilderness of Paran, and from there Moses sent men to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4010012|Num 10:12]]; [[@4013003|Num 13:3]]). The spies came back to Kadesh in the wilderness of Paran and showed the fruit of the land ([[@4013026|Num 13:26]]). Later, after Samuel died, David also went down to the wilderness of Paran ([[@9025001|1 Sam 25:1]]).

column5: A mountain named with God's appearing
column7: Blessing the people of Israel before his death, Moses said of the LORD, "He shone from Mount Paran" ([[@5033001-5033002|Deut 33:1-2]]). Habakkuk also said the Holy One comes from Mount Paran ([[@35003003|Hab 3:3]]).

column5: Western court of the temple, where gatekeepers stood
column7: A place mentioned when the posts of the temple gatekeepers were assigned. Four men were stationed at the causeway to the west, and two at Parbar itself ([[@13026018|1 Chr 26:18]]).

column5: Son of Haman
column7: One of the ten sons of Haman, the son of Hammedatha and the enemy of the Jews; they were put to death ([[@17009009-17009010|Esth 9:9-10]]).

column5: One of the seven chosen by the Jerusalem church
column7: One of the seven men the Jerusalem church chose and put in charge of caring for the needy ([[@44006003|Acts 6:3]]; [[@44006005|Acts 6:5]]).

column5: Father of Elizaphan, a prince of Zebulun
column7: Father of Elizaphan, the prince of the tribe of Zebulun chosen when the land of Canaan was divided as an inheritance ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034025|Num 34:25]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family that returned from exile
column7: The descendants of Parosh who came back from exile in Babylon numbered 2,172 ([[@15002003|Ezra 2:3]]; [[@16007008|Neh 7:8]]). Some of his descendants had taken foreign wives ([[@15010025|Ezra 10:25]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family that returned with Ezra
column7: His descendant Zechariah came up from Babylon with Ezra, along with one hundred fifty men ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008003|Ezra 8:3]]).

column5: Father of Pedaiah, who repaired the wall
column7: Father of Pedaiah, who repaired the section of Jerusalem's wall next to Palal's in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003025|Neh 3:25]]).

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: In Nehemiah's time he is listed first among the chiefs of the people who made a covenant to keep God's law and sealed it ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010029|Neh 10:29]]).

column5: Son of Haman
column7: One of the ten sons of Haman, the son of Hammedatha and the enemy of the Jews; they were put to death ([[@17009007|Esth 9:7]]; [[@17009010|Esth 9:10]]).

column5: People in Jerusalem at Pentecost
column7: Named among the peoples in Jerusalem at Pentecost who heard the disciples speaking in their own native languages ([[@44002008-44002009|Acts 2:8-9]]).

column5: Father of Jehoshaphat, officer over Issachar
column7: Father of Jehoshaphat, the one of Solomon's twelve officers who was over Issachar ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004017|1 Kgs 4:17]]).

column5: Source of Solomon's gold
column7: The gold Solomon used to decorate the temple was gold from Parvaim ([[@14003006|2 Chr 3:6]]). Scholars disagree about where it was.

column5: Son of Japhlet, of the tribe of Asher
column7: Son of Japhlet, the son of Heber of the tribe of Asher. He was a brother of Bimhal and Ashvath ([[@13007032-13007033|1 Chr 7:32-33]]).

column5: Son of Eshton in Judah's genealogy
column7: Son of Eshton, the son of Mehir, in Judah's genealogy; he was one of the men of Recah ([[@13004011-13004012|1 Chr 4:11-12]]).

column5: A temple servant ancestor who returned from exile
column7: He was the ancestor of 'the children of Paseah' among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon ([[@15002049|Ezra 2:49]]; [[@16007051|Neh 7:51]]).

column5: Father of Joiada, who repaired the old gate
column7: Father of Joiada, who repaired Jerusalem's old gate together with Meshullam son of Besodeiah in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003006|Neh 3:6]]).

column5: Ancestor of a priestly family after the exile
column7: He was the ancestor of a priestly family that returned from exile. The descendants of Pashhur numbered one thousand two hundred forty-seven ([[@15002038|Ezra 2:38]]).

column5: Priest who sealed the covenant
column7: A name listed as a priest among those who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time. It appears along with Amariah and Malchijah ([[@16010003|Neh 10:3]]; [[@16010008|Neh 10:8]]).

column5: The priest who put Jeremiah in the stocks
column7: He was a priest, the son of Immer, and chief officer in the house of the LORD. He beat Jeremiah and put him in the stocks, and Jeremiah told him that the LORD had named him 'Magormissabib' ([[@24020001-24020003|Jer 20:1-3]]).

column5: Man Zedekiah sent to Jeremiah
column7: Son of Malchijah, sent by King Zedekiah to Jeremiah to ask him to pray to the LORD for them ([[@24021001|Jer 21:1]]).

column5: Feast remembering the rescue from Egypt
column7: Passover is the feast that remembers how God passed over the Israelite houses marked with blood when he struck the land of Egypt. God promised, "When I see the blood, I will pass over you" ([[@2012013|Exod 12:13]]). The people ate the lamb in haste with belts on their waists and staffs in their hands, and they were commanded to keep this day throughout their generations ([[@2012011|Exod 12:11]]; [[@2012014|Exod 12:14]]). Paul says, "Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed in our place" ([[@46005007|1 Cor 5:7]]).

column5: Place Paul reached after Rhodes
column7: Paul's company said farewell, set sail straight to Cos, came to Rhodes the next day, and went on from there to Patara ([[@44021001|Acts 21:1]]).

column5: A region in southern Egypt
column7: It was a region in the land of Egypt where Jews lived ([[@24044001|Jer 44:1]]). Isaiah said the Lord would bring back the remnant of his people even from Pathros ([[@23011011|Isa 11:11]]).

column5: Descendants of Mizraim
column7: They were one of the peoples descended from Mizraim, the son of Ham ([[@1010013-1010014|Gen 10:13-14]]; [[@13001012|1 Chr 1:12]]).

column5: Island where John was
column7: The island where John was because of God's Word and the testimony of Jesus. There, on the Lord's day, he heard a loud voice ([[@66001009-66001010|Rev 1:9-10]]).

column5: Believer in Rome greeted by Paul
column7: Someone Paul greeted in his letter to the church in Rome. He was greeted together with the brothers who were with him ([[@45016014|Rom 16:14]]).

column5: City of Hadar, king of Edom
column7: It was the city of Hadar, king of Edom ([[@1036039|Gen 36:39]]). In 1 Chronicles it is called 'Pai' ([[@13001050|1 Chr 1:50]]).

column5: The apostle who brought the gospel to the Gentiles
column7: He was a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia ([[@44021039|Acts 21:39]]). His original name was Saul, and he was there when Stephen was stoned to death ([[@44007058|Acts 7:58]]). While persecuting the church, he heard the voice of the risen Jesus near Damascus and turned around ([[@44009003-44009006|Acts 9:3-6]]). After that, under the name 'Paul', he traveled to many places, preaching the gospel to the Gentiles and founding churches ([[@44013009|Acts 13:9]]), and he wrote many letters, including Romans.

column5: Sacrifice for peace with God and thanksgiving
column7: Peace offerings were sacrifices for enjoying fellowship and peace with God and for giving thanks. An animal without defect was offered, and the fat covering the innards and the fat on the innards was given to the LORD as an offering made by fire ([[@3003001-3003003|Lev 3:1-3]]). When it was offered for thanksgiving, unleavened cakes mixed with oil and other cakes were offered with it, and the meat had to be eaten on the day it was offered ([[@3007012|Lev 7:12]]; [[@3007015|Lev 7:15]]). Those who brought peace offerings ate the meat together and rejoiced, just as the word says, "You shall rejoice before the LORD your God" ([[@5027007|Deut 27:7]]).

column5: Naphtali prince who helped divide the land
column7: Son of Ammihud, he was the prince of the tribe of Naphtali chosen to divide the land for inheritance ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034028|Num 34:28]]).

column5: Father of Gamaliel, leader of the tribe of Manasseh
column7: He was the father of Gamaliel, the leader of the children of Manasseh in the wilderness ([[@4001010|Num 1:10]]). His son brought the offering on behalf of the children of Manasseh on the eighth day ([[@4007054|Num 7:54]]).

column5: Maternal grandfather of King Jehoiakim
column7: A man of Rumah, the father of Zebidah, King Jehoiakim's mother. Jehoiakim became king at twenty-five ([[@12023036|2 Kgs 23:36]]).

column5: Son of Jeconiah, father of Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the sons of Jeconiah, king of Judah, and the father of Zerubbabel and Shimei ([[@13003017-13003019|1 Chr 3:17-19]]).

column5: Father of Joel, ruler of half of Manasseh
column7: Father of Joel, who in David's time was the ruler of the half-tribe of Manasseh among the leaders over Israel's tribes ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]; [[@13027020|1 Chr 27:20]]).

column5: Son of Parosh who repaired the wall
column7: Son of Parosh, he repaired the section of Jerusalem's wall next to that of Palal son of Uzai in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003025|Neh 3:25]]).

column5: Man who stood beside Ezra at the reading
column7: One of the men who stood on the left of Ezra the scribe when he stood on the wooden pulpit to read the book of the law ([[@16008003-16008004|Neh 8:3-4]]).

column5: Ancestor of Sallu, who lived in Jerusalem
column7: Great-grandfather of Sallu, a Benjaminite who lived in Jerusalem after the exile. He appears as the father of Joed, Sallu's grandfather ([[@16011007|Neh 11:7]]).

column5: Treasurer appointed by Nehemiah
column7: A Levite whom Nehemiah put in charge of the storehouses, with the task of distributing to his brothers ([[@16013013|Neh 13:13]]).

column5: Son of Remaliah, king of Israel
column7: The son of Remaliah, he was a captain under Pekahiah king of Israel, and with fifty men of Gilead he killed the king in the palace at Samaria and reigned in his place ([[@12015025|2 Kgs 15:25]]). He reigned twenty years in Samaria, did not turn from the sins of Jeroboam, and did evil in the LORD's sight ([[@12015027-12015028|2 Kgs 15:27-28]]). Together with Rezin king of Syria he came up to Jerusalem and besieged Ahaz king of Judah, but could not overcome him ([[@12016005|2 Kgs 16:5]]). In his days Tiglath Pileser king of Assyria took Galilee and all the land of Naphtali and carried the people captive, and in the end Hoshea the son of Elah conspired against him and killed him ([[@12015029-12015030|2 Kgs 15:29-30]]).

column5: Son of Menahem, king of Israel
column6: it is the Lord that opens
column7: He was the son of Menahem, and in the fiftieth year of Azariah king of Judah he became king of Israel in Samaria and reigned two years ([[@12015022-12015023|2 Kgs 15:22-23]]). His captain Pekah conspired against him, killed him, and became king in his place ([[@12015025|2 Kgs 15:25]]).

column5: Son of Elioenai, of David's royal line
column7: One of the seven sons of Elioenai, listed in the genealogy of David's royal line after the exile ([[@13003024|1 Chr 3:24]]).

column5: A Levite who helped the people understand the law
column7: He was one of the Levites who helped the people understand the law in Ezra's time ([[@16008007|Neh 8:7]]). He also appears among the Levites who sealed the covenant ([[@16010009-16010010|Neh 10:9-10]]).

column5: Grandfather of Adaiah, who lived in Jerusalem
column7: Grandfather of Adaiah, a priest who did the work of the temple in Jerusalem after the exile ([[@16011010|Neh 11:10]]; [[@16011012|Neh 11:12]]).

column5: Grandson of Zerubbabel, son of Hananiah
column7: Son of Hananiah, the son of Zerubbabel. He appears with his brother Jeshaiah in the genealogy of David's royal line ([[@13003019|1 Chr 3:19]]; [[@13003021|1 Chr 3:21]]).

column5: Simeonite captain who went to Mount Seir
column7: Son of Ishi, he became one of the captains of five hundred Simeonites who went to Mount Seir and struck the Amalekites ([[@13004042-13004043|1 Chr 4:42-43]]).

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: One of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah's time who made a covenant to keep God's law and sealed it ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010022|Neh 10:22]]).

column5: A leader of the people seen by Ezekiel
column7: The son of Benaiah, he was one of the leaders of the people whom Ezekiel saw at the east gate of the LORD's house. He died while Ezekiel was prophesying ([[@26011001|Ezek 11:1]]; [[@26011013|Ezek 11:13]]).

column5: Son of Eber, ancestor of Abraham
column7: He was the son of Eber, a descendant of Shem. He was named Peleg because in his days the earth was divided, and his brother's name was Joktan ([[@1010025|Gen 10:25]]). Peleg became the father of Reu at thirty, and after that he lived two hundred nine years and had other children ([[@1011018-1011019|Gen 11:18-19]]). Terah and Abram came from his descendants, and his name also appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus ([[@42003034-42003035|Luke 3:34-35]]). Scholars differ on what the dividing of the earth refers to.

column5: Son of Jahdai in Judah's genealogy
column7: Son of Jahdai in Judah's genealogy. He was a brother of Regem, Jothan, Geshan, Ephah, and Shaaph ([[@13002047|1 Chr 2:47]]).

column5: Warrior who came to David at Ziklag
column7: Son of Azmaveth, a Benjaminite warrior who came to David while he was at Ziklag ([[@13012001-13012003|1 Chr 12:1-3]]).

column5: Father of On, a Reubenite
column7: Father of On, a descendant of Reuben. On joined Korah, Dathan, and Abiram in their rebellion ([[@4016001|Num 16:1]]).

column5: Son of Jonathan, a descendant of Jerahmeel
column7: Son of Jonathan, a descendant of Jerahmeel. He was a brother of Zaza, and Jonathan was the son of Jada ([[@13002032-13002033|1 Chr 2:32-33]]).

column5: Soldiers who guarded David with the Cherethites
column7: They were soldiers in King David's time who always appear paired with the Cherethites. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was over the Cherethites and the Pelethites ([[@10008018|2 Sam 8:18]]). When David left Jerusalem because of Absalom's revolt, they went on before the king and stayed by his side ([[@10015018|2 Sam 15:18]]). When David made Solomon king, they went with Zadok, Nathan, and Benaiah, set Solomon on the king's mule, and brought him to Gihon ([[@11001038|1 Kgs 1:38]]). Scholars differ about the meaning of their name and where they came from.

column5: The home of Helez and Ahijah, David's mighty men
column7: Among David's mighty men were 'Helez the Pelonite' and 'Ahijah the Pelonite' ([[@13011027|1 Chr 11:27]]; [[@13011036|1 Chr 11:36]]).

column5: A stronghold of Egypt
column7: It was a stronghold of Egypt. Ezekiel prophesied that the LORD would pour out his wrath on Sin ([[@26030015-26030016|Ezek 30:15-16]]).

column5: Where Jacob saw God face to face
column7: It is the name Jacob gave the place, saying, "I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved" ([[@1032030|Gen 32:30]]). The sun rose on him as he passed Peniel ([[@1032031|Gen 32:31]]).

column5: Elkanah's wife, Hannah's rival
column7: One of Elkanah's two wives. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none ([[@9001002|1 Sam 1:2]]; [[@9001004|1 Sam 1:4]]).

column5: Feast of the fiftieth day, when the Spirit came
column7: Pentecost means 'fiftieth day'; it is the harvest feast the Old Testament calls the Feast of Weeks ([[@5016010|Deut 16:10]]). The law said to count "fifty days" from the day the sheaf of first grain was offered and then bring a new grain offering ([[@3023015-3023016|Lev 23:15-16]]). After Jesus went up to heaven, the Holy Spirit came on the disciples as they were gathered in one place on the day of Pentecost, and they began to speak in other languages ([[@44002001-44002004|Acts 2:1-4]]). Paul too hurried on his way so as to reach Jerusalem by Pentecost ([[@44020016|Acts 20:16]]).

column5: Descendant of Hur in Judah's genealogy
column7: A man in Judah's genealogy, descended from Hur, the firstborn of Ephrathah. Ezer the father of Hushah appears in the same verse ([[@13004004|1 Chr 4:4]]).

column5: Son of Shashak, a Benjaminite
column7: Son of Shashak in the Benjamite genealogy. He is listed with Iphdeiah among Shashak's sons ([[@13008014|1 Chr 8:14]]; [[@13008025|1 Chr 8:25]]).

column5: Jerusalem gate used by Judah's kings
column7: A gate of Jerusalem through which the kings of Judah came in and went out. The LORD told Jeremiah to stand in that gate ([[@24017019|Jer 17:19]]).

column5: The Moabite mountain where Balak took Balaam
column7: Balak took Balaam up to the top of Peor, which looks down on the desert ([[@4023028|Num 23:28]]). Later, when Israel sinned by following Balaam's advice and a plague broke out, it was called 'the matter of Peor' ([[@4031016|Num 31:16]]).

column5: Where the LORD rose up
column7: Isaiah said the LORD would rise up as on Mount Perazim to do his work ([[@23028021|Isa 28:21]]).

column5: Son of Machir and Maacah
column7: A son born to Maacah, the wife of Machir son of Manasseh. His brother's name was Sheresh ([[@13007014|1 Chr 7:14]]; [[@13007016|1 Chr 7:16]]).

column5: Son of Judah and Tamar, ancestor of David
column7: He was the son that Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law, bore to Judah ([[@13002004|1 Chr 2:4]]). When she gave birth to twins, his brother's hand came out first and then drew back, and he came out first, so the midwife said, "Why have you made a breach for yourself?" and he was named Perez ([[@1038027-1038029|Gen 38:27-29]]). The genealogy in Ruth begins, "this is the history of the generations of Perez", and runs down to David ([[@8004018-8004022|Ruth 4:18-22]]). His name also appears in Jesus' genealogy in Matthew ([[@40001003|Matt 1:3]]).

column5: Place where Uzza died
column7: The name David gave the place where Uzza died after he put out his hand to take hold of the ark ([[@13013010-13013011|1 Chr 13:10-11]]).

column5: A town of Pamphylia Paul visited
column7: It was a town of Pamphylia that Paul and his companions reached by ship from Paphos, and John left them there and returned to Jerusalem ([[@44013013|Acts 13:13]]). Later Paul and Barnabas came back and spoke the word in Perga ([[@44014025|Acts 14:25]]).

column5: One of the seven churches in Revelation
column7: It was home to one of the seven churches in Revelation ([[@66001011|Rev 1:11]]). The Lord wrote to this church as 'he who has the sharp two-edged sword' ([[@66002012|Rev 2:12]]).

column5: People who lived in the land of Canaan
column7: They were a people who lived in the land of Canaan from Abraham's time on. When the herdsmen of Abram and Lot quarreled, the Bible says, "The Canaanites and the Perizzites lived in the land at that time" ([[@1013007|Gen 13:7]]). When God promised to give a land flowing with milk and honey, he named the Perizzites among the peoples living there ([[@2003008|Exod 3:8]]). But Israel did not destroy them completely, and in Solomon's time their remaining descendants were made into forced laborers ([[@11009020-11009021|1 Kgs 9:20-21]]).

column5: Great empire that sent Judah's exiles home
column7: The people of Judah were carried off to Babylon and lived as servants "until the reign of the kingdom of Persia" ([[@14036020|2 Chr 36:20]]). Cyrus king of Persia commanded the people of Judah to go up to Jerusalem and build the house of the LORD ([[@15001002-15001003|Ezra 1:2-3]]). Later, under Persian kings such as Darius and Artaxerxes, the temple and the city wall were rebuilt. The story of Esther also took place in the Persian palace, and Persia often appears together with Media ([[@17001003|Esth 1:3]]).

column5: Believer who labored much in the Lord
column7: A believer in Rome whom Paul greeted as "the beloved, who labored much in the Lord" ([[@45016012|Rom 16:12]]).

column5: A descendant of Solomon's servants
column7: He was the ancestor of 'the children of Peruda' among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from exile in Babylon ([[@15002055|Ezra 2:55]]). In Nehemiah he is called 'Perida' ([[@16007057|Neh 7:57]]).

column5: Jesus' disciple, a leader of the early church
column7: He was a fisherman by the Sea of Galilee whose original name was Simon, and he was Andrew's brother ([[@40004018|Matt 4:18]]). Jesus gave him the name 'Cephas', which means Peter ([[@43001042|John 1:42]]). He confessed, "You are the Christ, the Son of the living God" ([[@40016016|Matt 16:16]]). On the night Jesus was arrested he denied him three times, but at Pentecost he stood up with the eleven apostles and boldly preached the gospel ([[@44002014|Acts 2:14]]).

column5: Nineteenth of the priestly divisions
column7: The nineteenth of the priestly divisions assigned by lot in David's time ([[@13024005|1 Chr 24:5]]; [[@13024016|1 Chr 24:16]]).

column5: Levite who married a foreign woman
column7: One of the Levites in Ezra's time who had married foreign women. He is listed with Jozabad, Shimei, and others ([[@15010023|Ezra 10:23]]).

column5: Levite who called the people to bless God
column7: One of the Levites in Nehemiah's time who called out to the people to stand up and bless the LORD their God ([[@16009005|Neh 9:5]]).

column5: Man at the king's hand for the people
column7: Son of Meshezabel, of the descendants of Zerah son of Judah, he served at the king's hand in all matters concerning the people ([[@16011024|Neh 11:24]]).

column5: The hometown of Balaam
column7: It was the place by the River where Balaam the son of Beor lived. Balak king of Moab sent messengers there ([[@4022005|Num 22:5]]). Deuteronomy calls it 'Pethor of Mesopotamia' ([[@5023004|Deut 23:4]]).

column5: Father of the prophet Joel
column7: Father of the prophet Joel. The LORD's word came to Joel the son of Pethuel ([[@29001001|Joel 1:1]]).

column5: Eighth son of Obed-Edom
column7: The eighth son of Obed-Edom. The text says that God blessed Obed-Edom ([[@13026005|1 Chr 26:5]]).

column5: Father of the prophetess Anna
column7: A man of the tribe of Asher, the father of the prophetess Anna, who never left the temple but served there ([[@42002036-42002037|Luke 2:36-37]]).

column5: The king of Egypt in Abram's time
column7: He was the king of Egypt who took Sarai into his palace when Abram went down to Egypt ([[@1012015|Gen 12:15]]). When the LORD struck Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, he called Abram, rebuked him, and sent him away ([[@1012017-1012020|Gen 12:17-20]]).

column5: The king of Egypt in Joseph's time
column7: Pharaoh is the title for the king of Egypt, and here it refers to the king in Joseph's time. He had dreams that no one could interpret, so he called Joseph out of prison to hear their meaning ([[@1041014-1041015|Gen 41:14-15]]). Seeing Joseph's wisdom, he set him over all the land of Egypt ([[@1041041|Gen 41:41]]). Later, when Jacob's family came to Egypt, he let them live in the land of Goshen ([[@1047006|Gen 47:6]]). The Bible does not give this king's name, so scholars differ on which king he was.

column5: King of Egypt around the time Moses was born
column7: He was the new king who did not know Joseph, and he laid heavy burdens on the children of Israel and made them build the storage cities Pithom and Raamses ([[@2001008-2001011|Exod 1:8-11]]). He commanded, "You shall cast every son who is born into the river" ([[@2001022|Exod 1:22]]). But Pharaoh's daughter drew the baby Moses out from among the reeds and made him her own son ([[@2002005-2002010|Exod 2:5-10]]). When Moses grew up and Pharaoh heard that he had killed an Egyptian, Pharaoh tried to kill him and Moses fled to Midian, and many years later this king died ([[@2002011-2002023|Exod 2:11-23]]).

column5: The king of Egypt who resisted the Exodus
column7: 'Pharaoh' is the title used for the king of Egypt. This entry refers to the king who would not let Israel go in Moses' time. God sent Moses to him ([[@2003010|Exod 3:10]]), but he refused, saying, "Who is the LORD, that I should listen to his voice to let Israel go?" ([[@2005002|Exod 5:2]]). Only after many plagues did he let the people go, and then he chased after them again, and his army sank in the sea ([[@2014028|Exod 14:28]]). Because Scripture does not give his name, scholars differ on which king he was.

column5: King of Egypt who became Solomon's father-in-law
column7: He was the king of Egypt who made an alliance with Solomon and gave him his daughter as a wife ([[@11003001|1 Kgs 3:1]]). He captured Gezer, burned it, and gave the city to his daughter as a wedding gift ([[@11009016|1 Kgs 9:16]]). Solomon built a separate house for Pharaoh's daughter, and she came up to it from David's city ([[@11007008|1 Kgs 7:8]]; [[@11009024|1 Kgs 9:24]]). Scholars differ on whether this Pharaoh is the same king who took in Hadad the Edomite in 1 Kings 11.

column5: The king of Egypt in Hezekiah's time
column7: The Rabshakeh, an official of the king of Assyria, warned Hezekiah not to rely on Egypt, comparing Pharaoh king of Egypt to a staff of bruised reed ([[@12018021|2 Kgs 18:21]]; [[@23036006|Isa 36:6]]).

column5: Father of Bithiah, whom Mered married
column7: In Judah's genealogy, the father of Bithiah, whom Mered took as his wife. The text calls him 'Pharaoh' ([[@13004018|1 Chr 4:18]]).

column5: King of Egypt in Jeremiah's day
column7: The king of Egypt named among those Jeremiah made drink the cup of the LORD's wrath ([[@24025017|Jer 25:17]]; [[@24025019|Jer 25:19]]).

column5: Jewish group strict about the law and tradition
column7: The Pharisees were a Jewish group in New Testament times who strictly kept the law and the tradition of the elders ([[@40015002|Matt 15:2]]). Their name is understood to mean 'separated ones'. Unlike the Sadducees, they believed in the resurrection, angels, and spirits ([[@44023008|Acts 23:8]]). Jesus rebuked their merely outward religion, comparing them to "whitened tombs" ([[@40023027|Matt 23:27]]). Yet some Pharisees, like Nicodemus, came to Jesus, and the apostle Paul himself was originally a Pharisee ([[@50003005|Phil 3:5]]).

column5: River of Damascus
column7: A river of Damascus. Naaman angrily asked whether Abanah and Pharpar were not better than all the waters of Israel ([[@12005012|2 Kgs 5:12]]).

column5: Commander of Abimelech's army
column7: He was the commander of the army of Abimelech king of Gerar, and together with Abimelech he made a covenant with Abraham at Beersheba ([[@1021022|Gen 21:22]], 32). Later, when Abimelech came to Isaac, Phicol the commander of his army came along too ([[@1026026|Gen 26:26]]).

column5: One of the seven churches in Revelation
column7: It was home to one of the seven churches in Revelation. The Lord wrote to this church as 'he who has the key of David' ([[@66003007|Rev 3:7]]).

column5: Paul's beloved fellow worker who received his letter
column7: He was the man Paul wrote to, and Paul and Timothy called him "Philemon, our beloved fellow worker" ([[@57001001|Phlm 1:1]]).

column5: Man who said the resurrection was past
column7: Along with Hymenaeus, he said the resurrection was already past and overthrew the faith of some ([[@55002017-55002018|2 Tim 2:17-18]]).

column5: One of Jesus' twelve disciples
column7: One of Jesus' twelve apostles, he was from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter ([[@43001044|John 1:44]]). When Jesus said, "Follow me", he followed, and he went to find Nathanael and brought him to Jesus ([[@43001043|John 1:43]], 45). When Jesus fed the crowd with five loaves and two fish, Philip answered that even two hundred denarii worth of bread would not be enough ([[@43006007|John 6:7]]). On the last night he asked Jesus to show them the Father and heard the words, "He who has seen me has seen the Father" ([[@43014009|John 14:9]]). He is a different person from Philip the evangelist, one of the seven deacons.

column5: Herod's brother, husband of Herodias
column7: He was the brother of Herod the tetrarch. When John the Baptizer rebuked Herod for marrying Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, Herod seized John and put him in prison ([[@40014003-40014004|Matt 14:3-4]]; [[@41006017-41006018|Mark 6:17-18]]).

column5: Tetrarch of Ituraea and Trachonitis
column7: Herod's brother, who was tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis in the fifteenth year of Tiberius Caesar ([[@42003001|Luke 3:1]]).

column5: One of the seven, an evangelist
column7: He was one of the seven men the Jerusalem church chose to take charge of the work ([[@44006005|Acts 6:5]]). When the believers were scattered by persecution after Stephen's death, he went down to the city of Samaria and proclaimed the Christ, and many believed ([[@44008005-44008012|Acts 8:5-12]]). Led by an angel of the Lord, he met an Ethiopian eunuch on a desert road, told him about Jesus starting from the Scripture passage, and baptized him ([[@44008035-44008038|Acts 8:35-38]]). Later he lived in Caesarea, and the Bible calls him "Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven" ([[@44021008|Acts 21:8]]).

column5: A city of Macedonia where Paul founded a church
column7: It was the foremost city of the district of Macedonia and a Roman colony ([[@44016012|Acts 16:12]]). Paul preached the gospel to Lydia, a seller of purple from the city of Thyatira, and the Lord opened her heart to listen to the word ([[@44016014|Acts 16:14]]). After Paul cast a spirit out of a slave girl, he and Silas were beaten and thrown into prison, but while they prayed and sang hymns at midnight, a great earthquake came and all the prison doors were opened ([[@44016018-44016026|Acts 16:18-26]]). Later Paul sent a letter "to all the saints in Christ Jesus who are at Philippi, with the overseers and servants", and this is the book of Philippians ([[@50001001|Phil 1:1]]).

column5: A neighboring people on Israel's western coast
column7: It was a people, and their land, on the southwestern coast of Canaan. The land of the Philistines appears even in Abraham's time ([[@1021032|Gen 21:32]]). There were lords over five cities: Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron ([[@6013003|Josh 13:3]]). They often troubled Israel in the days of the judges and of Saul, and Goliath of Gath was also a Philistine champion ([[@9017004|1 Sam 17:4]]). In David's time they were badly defeated and subdued ([[@10008001|2 Sam 8:1]]).

column5: A people descended from the Casluhim
column7: The genealogy records that the Philistines came from the Casluhim, among the descendants of Mizraim the son of Ham ([[@1010014|Gen 10:14]]; [[@13001012|1 Chr 1:12]]).

column5: Believer in Rome greeted by Paul
column7: Someone Paul greeted in his letter to the church in Rome. His name appears with Julia and Nereus ([[@45016015|Rom 16:15]]).

column5: Aaron's grandson, a priest jealous for the LORD
column7: He was a priest, the grandson of Aaron and the son of Eleazar ([[@2006025|Exod 6:25]]). When Israel at Shittim committed sexual immorality with Moabite women and worshiped idols, he rose up with a spear in his hand and punished the sin, and the plague was stopped ([[@4025007-4025008|Num 25:7-8]]). God said he had been jealous for his God and gave him the covenant of an everlasting priesthood ([[@4025013|Num 25:13]]). Later he led the delegation sent to settle a dispute with the tribes east of the Jordan, and a psalm also remembers what he did ([[@19106030|Ps 106:30]]).

column5: Son of Eli, brother of Hophni
column7: He was one of the two sons of Eli, the priest at Shiloh, and served as a priest of the LORD along with his brother Hophni ([[@9001003|1 Sam 1:3]]). But Eli's sons were wicked men who did not know the LORD and treated the LORD's offering with contempt ([[@9002012|1 Sam 2:12]], 17). God had said beforehand that both sons would die on the same day, and both were killed when the ark of the covenant was taken in battle with the Philistines ([[@9002034|1 Sam 2:34]]; [[@9004011|1 Sam 4:11]]). When Phinehas' wife heard the news, she gave birth and named the child Ichabod ([[@9004019-9004021|1 Sam 4:19-21]]). He is a different person from Phinehas the grandson of Aaron.

column5: Father of Eleazar
column7: Father of Eleazar, who was present in Ezra's time when the silver, gold, and vessels for the temple were weighed and handed over ([[@15008033|Ezra 8:33]]).

column5: Believer in Rome greeted by Paul
column7: Someone Paul greeted in his letter to the church in Rome. He was greeted together with the brothers who were with him ([[@45016014|Rom 16:14]]).

column5: A servant of the church at Cenchreae
column7: She was a servant of the church at Cenchreae. Paul commended her, 'our sister,' to the church in Rome ([[@45016001|Rom 16:1]]).

column5: A region on the Mediterranean coast
column7: The believers scattered after the persecution over Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, speaking the word to Jews ([[@44011019|Acts 11:19]]). On their way to Jerusalem, Paul and Barnabas passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, telling how the Gentiles had turned to the Lord ([[@44015003|Acts 15:3]]).

column5: Harbor of Crete
column7: A harbor of Crete where most of those on Paul's ship advised going to spend the winter ([[@44027012|Acts 27:12]]).

column5: A region of Asia Minor
column7: Among the people gathered in Jerusalem at Pentecost were some who lived in Phrygia ([[@44002010|Acts 2:10]]). Paul traveled through this region strengthening the disciples ([[@44016006|Acts 16:6]]; [[@44018023|Acts 18:23]]).

column5: Man of Asia who turned away from Paul
column7: One of all those in Asia who turned away from Paul; his name appears with Hermogenes ([[@55001015|2 Tim 1:15]]).

column5: Words of the law worn on the body
column7: Phylacteries were words of the law written down and bound on the wrist or the forehead. God told Israel to remember his words always: "You shall bind them for a sign on your hand, and they shall be for frontlets between your eyes" ([[@5006008|Deut 6:8]]). In the ordinance for remembering the exodus, too, he said it should be a sign on their hand and a memorial between their eyes ([[@2013009|Exod 13:9]]). In Jesus' time the scribes and Pharisees, wanting to be seen by people, would "make their phylacteries broad and enlarge the fringes of their garments", and Jesus rebuked this hypocrisy ([[@40023005|Matt 23:5]]).

column5: Egyptian city under Ezekiel's judgment
column7: An Egyptian city named when Ezekiel prophesied against Egypt; he said its young men would fall by the sword ([[@26030017|Ezek 30:17]]).

column5: The camp before crossing the Red Sea
column7: The LORD had the children of Israel camp before Pi Hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea ([[@2014002|Exod 14:2]]). The Egyptian army overtook them here ([[@2014009|Exod 14:9]]).

column5: The Roman governor who tried Jesus
column7: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor who ruled Judea in Jesus' time ([[@42003001|Luke 3:1]]). The chief priests and elders bound Jesus and handed him over to him ([[@40027002|Matt 27:2]]). He knew Jesus had done no wrong, but when a riot was about to break out, he took water, washed his hands, and said, "I am innocent of the blood of this righteous person" ([[@40027024|Matt 27:24]]). Then he released Barabbas, had Jesus flogged, and handed him over to be crucified ([[@40027026|Matt 27:26]]).

column5: Son of Nahor and Milcah
column7: A son that Milcah bore to Nahor, Abraham's brother. Bethuel was among his brothers ([[@1022020|Gen 22:20]]; [[@1022022|Gen 22:22]]).

column5: Chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: One of the chiefs of the people in Nehemiah's time who made a covenant to keep God's law and sealed it ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010024|Neh 10:24]]).

column5: Head of Moadiah's family in Joiakim's day
column7: A head of a priestly family in the days of Joiakim, leading the family of Miniamin, that is, Moadiah ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012017|Neh 12:17]]).

column5: An Edomite chief descended from Esau
column7: He was one of the chiefs of Edom descended from Esau, listed after chief Oholibamah and chief Elah ([[@1036040-1036041|Gen 36:40-41]]; [[@13001052|1 Chr 1:52]]).

column5: King of Jarmuth
column7: King of Jarmuth, summoned by Adoni-Zedek king of Jerusalem ([[@6010003|Josh 10:3]]). Joshua struck and killed those five kings ([[@6010026|Josh 10:26]]).

column5: A town in Ephraim, home of the judge Abdon
column7: The judge Abdon was a Pirathonite, and when he died he was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim ([[@7012013|Judg 12:13]]; [[@7012015|Judg 12:15]]).

column5: The mountain where Moses viewed the Promised Land
column7: It was a mountaintop in the land of Moab east of the Jordan, overlooking the desert ([[@4021020|Num 21:20]]). Balak king of Moab took Balaam up to its top, built seven altars, and tried to have him curse Israel ([[@4023013-4023014|Num 23:13-14]]). God told Moses, who would not cross the Jordan, to go up to the top of Pisgah and see the land with his own eyes ([[@5003027|Deut 3:27]]). Before he died, Moses went up Mount Nebo to the top of Pisgah opposite Jericho and saw all the land the LORD showed him ([[@5034001|Deut 34:1]]).

column5: First river that branched from Eden
column7: The first of the four rivers that branched off from Eden; it flowed around the whole land of Havilah, where there is gold ([[@1002011|Gen 2:11]]).

column5: A region of Asia Minor Paul passed through
column7: Paul and his companions went on from Perga to Antioch of Pisidia and went into the synagogue on the Sabbath day ([[@44013014|Acts 13:14]]). On their way back they passed through Pisidia again ([[@44014024|Acts 14:24]]).

column5: Son of Jether, of the tribe of Asher
column7: Son of Jether in Asher's genealogy. He was a brother of Jephunneh and Ara ([[@13007038|1 Chr 7:38]]; [[@13007040|1 Chr 7:40]]).

column5: Storage city built by Israel
column7: A storage city the Israelites built for Pharaoh in Egypt while bearing heavy burdens ([[@2001011|Exod 1:11]]).

column5: Son of Micah, a descendant of Saul
column7: He was one of the four sons of Micah, a descendant of Saul. Micah was the son of Jonathan's son Merib-baal ([[@13008034-13008035|1 Chr 8:34-35]]; [[@13009041|1 Chr 9:41]]).

column5: A descendant of Solomon's servants
column7: He was the ancestor of 'the children of Pochereth Hazzebaim' among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from exile in Babylon ([[@15002055|Ezra 2:55]]; [[@15002057|Ezra 2:57]]).

column5: A region in northern Asia Minor
column7: Among the people gathered in Jerusalem at Pentecost were some from Pontus ([[@44002009|Acts 2:9]]). Aquila was a Jew born in Pontus ([[@44018002|Acts 18:2]]), and 1 Peter was written also to the scattered foreigners in Pontus ([[@60001001|1 Pet 1:1]]).

column5: Son of Haman
column7: One of the ten sons of Haman, the son of Hammedatha and the enemy of the Jews; they were put to death ([[@17009008|Esth 9:8]]; [[@17009010|Esth 9:10]]).

column5: The Egyptian captain of the guard who bought Joseph
column7: An officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, he bought Joseph from the Midianites ([[@1037036|Gen 37:36]]; [[@1039001|Gen 39:1]]).

column5: Priest of On, Joseph's father-in-law
column7: He was a priest of On in Egypt, and Pharaoh gave his daughter Asenath to Joseph as a wife ([[@1041045|Gen 41:45]]). Asenath bore Manasseh and Ephraim to Joseph ([[@1046020|Gen 46:20]]).

column5: Gate at the entrance of the Hinnom Valley
column7: A gate at the entrance to the valley of the son of Hinnom, where Jeremiah went out with an earthen jar to proclaim the word ([[@24019001-24019002|Jer 19:1-2]]).

column5: The Roman governor's residence and court
column7: The Praetorium was the residence where the Roman governor stayed and held trials. Early in the morning the people led Jesus from Caiaphas to the Praetorium, but they themselves did not go in, so that they would not be defiled and could eat the Passover ([[@43018028|John 18:28]]). Pilate went into the Praetorium, called Jesus, and asked him, "Are you the King of the Jews?" ([[@43018033|John 18:33]]). The governor's soldiers took Jesus into the Praetorium and gathered the whole garrison, and the Gospel of Mark calls this place "the court, which is the Praetorium" ([[@40027027|Matt 27:27]]; [[@41015016|Mark 15:16]]).

column5: One who offered sacrifices to God
column7: A priest offered sacrifices to God for the people and taught God's statutes. The first person called a priest in the Bible is Melchizedek king of Salem, who was "priest of God Most High" ([[@1014018|Gen 14:18]]). Under the law, Aaron and his sons held the office of priest; they distinguished between the holy and the common and taught the people the statutes ([[@2028001|Exod 28:1]]; [[@3010010-3010011|Lev 10:10-11]]). The New Testament calls those who believe in Jesus "a royal priesthood" ([[@60002009|1 Pet 2:9]]).

column5: Wife of Aquila, Paul's co-worker
column7: She was Aquila's wife, and when Claudius ordered all Jews to leave Rome, she came from Italy with her husband and met Paul in Corinth ([[@44018001-44018002|Acts 18:1-2]]). Because the couple had the same trade as Paul, they worked together making tents, and later they sailed with Paul for Syria ([[@44018003|Acts 18:3]], 18). In Ephesus, when they saw that Apollos knew only the baptism of John, the couple took him aside and explained the way of God to him more accurately ([[@44018024-44018026|Acts 18:24-26]]). In his letter Paul calls her 'Prisca' and says she was a co-worker who risked her neck for his life ([[@45016003-45016004|Rom 16:3-4]]).

column5: One of the seven chosen by the Jerusalem church
column7: One of the seven men the Jerusalem church chose and put in charge of caring for the needy ([[@44006003|Acts 6:3]]; [[@44006005|Acts 6:5]]).

column5: One who receives and speaks God's word
column7: A prophet received God's word and passed it on to the people. In earlier times in Israel a prophet was also called a 'seer' ([[@9009009|1 Sam 9:9]]). God made himself known to prophets in visions or dreams, and as he said, "I will put my words in his mouth", he had them speak exactly what he told them ([[@4012006|Num 12:6]]; [[@5018018|Deut 18:18]]). Hebrews says that God, who spoke long ago through the prophets in many ways, has in these last days spoken through his Son ([[@58001001-58001002|Heb 1:1-2]]).

column5: A Gentile who converted to Judaism
column7: A proselyte is a Gentile who has converted to Judaism. Jesus rebuked the hypocritical scribes and Pharisees, who traveled around by sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he became one, made him twice as much a son of hell as themselves ([[@40023015|Matt 23:15]]). At Pentecost, "both Jews and proselytes" were in Jerusalem together ([[@44002010|Acts 2:10]]). Among the seven men chosen by the church in Jerusalem, Nicolaus was also "a proselyte of Antioch" ([[@44006005|Acts 6:5]]).

column5: Son of Issachar
column7: He was the second son of Issachar, called Puvah in Genesis ([[@1046013|Gen 46:13]]). The family of the Punites came from him ([[@4026023|Num 26:23]]), and 1 Chronicles calls him Puah ([[@13007001|1 Chr 7:1]]).

column5: Hebrew midwife who feared God
column7: A Hebrew midwife in Egypt. She feared God and disobeyed the king of Egypt's order to kill the baby boys ([[@2001015|Exod 1:15]]; [[@2001017|Exod 1:17]]).

column5: Father of the judge Tola
column7: Son of Dodo, a man of Issachar. His son Tola arose after Abimelech to save Israel ([[@7010001|Judg 10:1]]).

column5: The chief man of Malta who welcomed Paul
column7: The chief man of the island, he kindly gave Paul and his companions lodging for three days. Paul laid his hands on his father and healed him ([[@44028007-44028008|Acts 28:7-8]]).

column5: Man who sent greetings to Timothy
column7: One of those who sent greetings to Timothy. His name appears with Eubulus, Linus, and Claudia ([[@55004021|2 Tim 4:21]]).

column5: A camp in the wilderness
column7: In the wilderness the Israelites left Zalmonah and camped at Punon, then left Punon and camped at Oboth ([[@4033042-4033043|Num 33:42-43]]).

column5: A servant of Gideon
column7: Gideon's servant, he went down with Gideon to the edge of the Midianite camp and heard what they were saying ([[@7007010-7007011|Judg 7:10-11]]).

column5: Son of Ham
column7: He was one of the sons of Noah's son Ham, and a brother of Cush, Mizraim, and Canaan ([[@1010006|Gen 10:6]]; [[@13001008|1 Chr 1:8]]).

column5: Port Paul reached on the way to Rome
column7: The place Paul reached on his way to Rome: after Rhegium a south wind sprang up, and on the second day he came to Puteoli ([[@44028013|Acts 28:13]]).

column5: Family of Kiriath Jearim
column7: One of the families of Kiriath Jearim. They are listed with the Ithrites, the Shumathites, and the Mishraites ([[@13002053|1 Chr 2:53]]).

column5: Father-in-law of Eleazar
column7: Eleazar son of Aaron took one of his daughters as his wife, and she bore Phinehas ([[@2006025|Exod 6:25]]).

column5: Father of Sopater
column7: Father of Sopater of Beroea. Sopater went with Paul as far as Asia ([[@44020004|Acts 20:4]]).

column5: Brother who greeted the church in Rome
column7: A man Paul called a brother; he sent greetings to the church in Rome along with Erastus, the city treasurer ([[@45016023|Rom 16:23]]).

column5: The queen who came to see Solomon's wisdom
column7: She was the queen who heard of Solomon's fame concerning the LORD's name and came to Jerusalem to test him with hard questions ([[@11010001|1 Kgs 10:1]]). Seeing Solomon's wisdom, she declared, "Blessed is the LORD your God" ([[@11010006-11010009|1 Kgs 10:6-9]]). The queen gave him one hundred twenty talents of gold and a very great quantity of spices and precious stones, and Solomon also gave her all she asked for and sent her back to her own land ([[@11010010-11010013|1 Kgs 10:10-13]]). Jesus called her the "Queen of the South" and said that someone greater than Solomon is here ([[@40012042|Matt 12:42]]).

column5: Governor of Syria
column7: Governor of Syria at the time of the first enrollment, made by decree of Caesar Augustus ([[@42002001-42002002|Luke 2:1-2]]).

column5: Place that traded with Tyre
column7: A place that did business with Tyre. Together with Sheba, it traded with Tyre in all kinds of spices, precious stones, and gold ([[@26027022|Ezek 27:22]]).

column5: Storage city built by Israel
column7: A storage city the Israelites built for Pharaoh in Egypt, along with Pithom, while bearing heavy burdens ([[@2001011|Exod 1:11]]).

column5: A Babylonian official at the fall of Jerusalem
column7: It is the title of the Babylonian official 'Nergal Sharezer the Rabmag,' who sat in the middle gate when Jerusalem fell ([[@24039003|Jer 39:3]]; [[@24039013|Jer 39:13]]).

column5: Official sent by the king of Assyria
column7: An official the king of Assyria sent with Tartan and Rabshakeh, at the head of a great army, to Jerusalem against King Hezekiah ([[@12018017|2 Kgs 18:17]]).

column5: A Babylonian official at the fall of Jerusalem
column7: When Jerusalem fell, one of the Babylonian officials held the title 'Rabsaris,' meaning chief of the eunuchs ([[@24039003|Jer 39:3]]; [[@24039013|Jer 39:13]])

column5: City of the tribe of Issachar
column7: A city in the land the children of Issachar received by lot according to their families. It is listed with Kishion and Ebez ([[@6019017|Josh 19:17]]; [[@6019020|Josh 19:20]]).

column5: Assyrian official who threatened Hezekiah
column7: He was a high official the king of Assyria sent to Hezekiah. He came from Lachish to Jerusalem with a great army and stood by the conduit of the upper pool on the highway ([[@12018017|2 Kgs 18:17]]). The officials of Judah asked him to speak in the Syrian language, but he deliberately shouted in the Jews' language so that the people on the wall would hear ([[@12018026-12018028|2 Kgs 18:26-28]]). Telling them not to trust Hezekiah, he insulted God, scorning the idea "that the LORD should deliver Jerusalem out of my hand" ([[@12018035|2 Kgs 18:35]]). Isaiah brought the LORD's word not to be afraid of his words ([[@12019006|2 Kgs 19:6]]).

column5: A scornful word meaning 'worthless one'
column7: Raca means 'empty, worthless person', and it was a word Jews used to show contempt for someone. It appears once in the Bible, in Jesus' teaching in Matthew 5. Jesus said that everyone who is angry with his brother will be in danger of the judgment, "Whoever says to his brother, ‘Raca!’ will be in danger of the council", and whoever calls him a fool will be in danger of the fire of hell ([[@40005022|Matt 5:22]]). This teaching shows that the command not to murder covers not only killing with one's hands but also anger in the heart and words of contempt ([[@40005021-40005022|Matt 5:21-22]]).

column5: Jacob's wife, mother of Joseph and Benjamin
column7: Rachel was Laban's younger daughter and the wife Jacob loved. Jacob served seven years for her, and those years seemed to him only a few days ([[@1029020|Gen 29:20]]). For a long time she had no children, until God opened her womb and she gave birth to Joseph ([[@1030022-1030024|Gen 30:22-24]]). She died giving birth to her second son, Benjamin, and was buried on the way to Bethlehem ([[@1035018-1035019|Gen 35:18-19]]). The Gospel of Matthew describes Herod's killing of the children with the picture of Rachel weeping for her children ([[@40002018|Matt 2:18]]).

column5: Fifth son of Jesse
column7: The fifth son of Jesse and an older brother of David. He is listed after Nethanel, the fourth ([[@13002013-13002014|1 Chr 2:13-14]]).

column5: The woman of Jericho who hid the spies
column7: She was a prostitute in the city of Jericho who hid the two spies Joshua had sent in her house ([[@6002001-6002004|Josh 2:1-4]]). When Jericho fell, Joshua spared Rahab, her father's household, and all that she had ([[@6006025|Josh 6:25]]). As the mother of Boaz, Rahab is named in the genealogy of Jesus ([[@40001005|Matt 1:5]]), and Hebrews remembers her as one who by faith received the spies in peace ([[@58011031|Heb 11:31]]).

column5: Father of Jorkeam
column7: A man in the genealogy of Caleb's descendants. Shema became the father of Raham, and Raham was the father of Jorkeam ([[@13002042-13002044|1 Chr 2:42-44]]).

column5: Son of Sheresh, of Manasseh's line
column7: Son of Sheresh, the son of Machir, among Manasseh's descendants. He was a brother of Ulam ([[@13007014|1 Chr 7:14]]; [[@13007016|1 Chr 7:16]]).

column5: A fortified city of Naphtali
column7: It was one of the fortified cities in the land Naphtali's descendants received by lot, named between Hammath and Chinnereth ([[@6019032|Josh 19:32]]; [[@6019035|Josh 19:35]]).

column5: Place of the tribe of Dan
column7: A place in the land the tribe of Dan received by lot according to their families; it is listed with Me Jarkon ([[@6019040|Josh 19:40]]; [[@6019046|Josh 19:46]]).

column5: Son of Hezron, an ancestor of David
column7: He was the son of Hezron and the father of Amminadab ([[@13002009-13002010|1 Chr 2:9-10]]). He also appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Matthew ([[@40001003|Matt 1:3]]).

column5: Firstborn son of Jerahmeel
column7: The firstborn son of Jerahmeel, who was Hezron's firstborn, he was the father of Maaz, Jamin, and Eker ([[@13002025|1 Chr 2:25]]; [[@13002027|1 Chr 2:27]]).

column5: Family of Elihu
column7: The name of the family of Elihu son of Barachel the Buzite, who became angry with Job ([[@18032002|Job 32:2]]).

column5: Benjamite town near Gibeah
column7: It was a town in the land of the tribe of Benjamin, near Gibeon and Beeroth ([[@6018025|Josh 18:25]]). Baasha king of Israel built Ramah to block Judah, but when Asa king of Judah got Ben Hadad king of Syria to move against him, Baasha stopped building, and Asa used its stones and timber to build Geba and Mizpah ([[@11015017-11015022|1 Kgs 15:17-22]]). Jeremiah spoke of the voice of Rachel weeping for her children in Ramah, and Matthew wrote that these words were fulfilled in Herod's time ([[@24031015|Jer 31:15]]; [[@40002018|Matt 2:18]]). Scholars differ on whether it is the same place as Ramah, Samuel's hometown.

column5: City on Asher's border
column7: The border of the land Asher's descendants received turned to Ramah and reached the fortified city of Tyre ([[@6019024|Josh 19:24]]; [[@6019029|Josh 19:29]]).

column5: City of the tribe of Naphtali
column7: One of the fortified cities Naphtali's descendants received according to their families. It is listed with Adamah and Hazor ([[@6019035-6019036|Josh 19:35-36]]).

column5: Where Samson threw the jawbone
column7: The place Samson named after he killed a thousand men with a donkey's jawbone and threw it away ([[@7015015|Judg 15:15]]; [[@7015017|Judg 15:17]]).

column5: Home of Shimei, David's vineyard keeper
column7: Shimei, who was over David's vineyards, was called 'the Ramathite.' Zabdi was over the wine cellars ([[@13027027|1 Chr 27:27]]).

column5: Where Israel set out from Egypt
column7: It was one of the storage cities the children of Israel built for Pharaoh ([[@2001011|Exod 1:11]]). At the Exodus they set out from here and came to Succoth ([[@2012037|Exod 12:37]]).

column5: Son of Parosh who married a foreign woman
column7: One of those in Ezra's time who had married foreign women, listed among the sons of Parosh of Israel ([[@15010025|Ezra 10:25]]).

column5: Ramoth Gilead, the Gadite city of refuge
column7: Ramoth was a town in the land of Gilead east of the Jordan, and in the Bible it usually appears as "Ramoth Gilead". Moses set it apart as a city of refuge for the tribe of Gad ([[@5004043|Deut 4:43]]), and later it was given to the Levites ([[@6021038|Josh 21:38]]). Ahab king of Israel was struck by an arrow and died while fighting to take this city back from Syria ([[@11022034-11022035|1 Kgs 22:34-35]]). Elisha sent one of his disciples here to anoint Jehu ([[@12009001|2 Kgs 9:1]]). There is said to have been a Levite town of the same name in the land of Issachar as well.

column5: Ancestor of the Philistine giants
column7: It is a word for the ancestor of the Philistine giants in David's day. In the World English Bible he is simply called 'the giant.' One of his sons, Ishbibenob, carried a bronze spear weighing three hundred shekels and meant to kill David ([[@10021016|2 Sam 21:16]]). The tall man who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot was also descended from the giant ([[@10021020|2 Sam 21:20]]). These four, born to the giant in Gath, all fell by the hand of David and his servants ([[@10021022|2 Sam 21:22]]).

column5: Son of Binea, a descendant of Saul
column7: A descendant of Saul, he was the son of Binea and the father of Eleasah ([[@13008037|1 Chr 8:37]]). In 1 Chronicles 9 he is called 'Rephaiah' ([[@13009043|1 Chr 9:43]]).

column5: Father of the spy Palti
column7: Father of Palti, the Benjaminite spy whom Moses sent to explore the land of Canaan ([[@4013009|Num 13:9]]; [[@4013016|Num 13:16]]).

column5: Son of Micah, a Reubenite
column7: A descendant of Joel of the tribe of Reuben, and the son of Micah. His son was Baal ([[@13005004-13005005|1 Chr 5:4-5]]).

column5: A temple servant ancestor who returned from exile
column7: He was the ancestor of 'the children of Reaiah' among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon ([[@15002047|Ezra 2:47]]; [[@16007050|Neh 7:50]]).

column5: A Midianite king killed by Israel
column7: He was one of the five kings of Midian, whom Israel killed along with Balaam ([[@4031008|Num 31:8]]; [[@6013021|Josh 13:21]]).

column5: Isaac's wife, mother of Esau and Jacob
column7: She was Nahor's granddaughter and Bethuel's daughter ([[@1022023|Gen 22:23]]). As Abraham's servant prayed while looking for a wife for Isaac, she came out to the spring and gave water to the servant and his camels, and so she was known as the one God had prepared ([[@1024015-1024019|Gen 24:15-19]]). She left home and became Isaac's wife, and after a long time without children, God heard Isaac's prayer and she gave birth to the twins Esau and Jacob ([[@1025021-1025026|Gen 25:21-26]]). Later she came up with a plan so that Jacob would receive his father's blessing ([[@1027006-1027017|Gen 27:6-17]]).

column5: Place linked with Eshton's family
column7: In Judah's genealogy, Eshton's sons Beth Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah are all called 'the men of Recah' ([[@13004012|1 Chr 4:12]]).

column5: A captain who killed Ishbosheth
column7: He was a captain under Ishbosheth, Saul's son, and the son of Rimmon the Beerothite ([[@10004002|2 Sam 4:2]]). With his brother Baanah he killed Ishbosheth as he lay resting at noon ([[@10004005-10004007|2 Sam 4:5-7]]).

column5: Father of Jehonadab, ancestor of the Rechabites
column7: He was the father of Jehonadab, who helped Jehu and rode with him in his chariot. Jehonadab the son of Rechab came out to meet Jehu, took his hand, and got up into his chariot ([[@12010015|2 Kgs 10:15]]). First Chronicles speaks of "the Kenites who came from Hammath, the father of the house of Rechab" ([[@13002055|1 Chr 2:55]]). In Jeremiah's day the Rechabites drank no wine, as "Jonadab the son of Rechab, our father" had commanded ([[@24035006|Jer 35:6]]). Seeing their obedience, God promised that Jonadab would never lack a man to stand before him ([[@24035019|Jer 35:19]]).

column5: Father of Malchijah, who repaired the dung gate
column7: Father of Malchijah, who ruled the district of Beth Haccherem and repaired the dung gate and set up its doors in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003014|Neh 3:14]]).

column5: Sea Israel crossed in the Exodus
column7: It is the sea God parted for the people of Israel when they came out of Egypt. God led the people "by the way of the wilderness by the Red Sea" ([[@2013018|Exod 13:18]]). When Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, a strong east wind divided the waters and the people crossed on dry ground, while Pharaoh's army chasing them sank into the sea ([[@2014021-2014028|Exod 14:21-28]]). This event often appears in songs and stories of faith that remember God's salvation ([[@19136013|Ps 136:13]]; [[@58011029|Heb 11:29]]).

column5: Paying a price to buy back and set free
column7: Redemption means paying a price to win back what was lost or a person who was enslaved, and setting them free. God promised to bring Israel out of slavery in Egypt, saying, "I will redeem you with an outstretched arm, and with great judgments" ([[@2006006|Exod 6:6]]). Under the law, if a poor brother sold some of his property, his nearest kinsman could come and redeem it ([[@3025025|Lev 25:25]]). Jesus said he came to give his life as a ransom for many, and the New Testament says that in Christ we have "our redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses" ([[@41010045|Mark 10:45]]; [[@49001007|Eph 1:7]]).

column5: A leader who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the leaders who came back from exile in Babylon with Zerubbabel and Jeshua, named in the list in Ezra ([[@15002002|Ezra 2:2]]).

column5: Son of Jahdai in Judah's genealogy
column7: Son of Jahdai in Judah's genealogy. He was a brother of Jothan, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph ([[@13002047|1 Chr 2:47]]).

column5: Man sent by the people of Bethel
column7: A man the people of Bethel sent, along with Sharezer and their men, to entreat the LORD's favor ([[@38007002|Zech 7:2]]).

column5: Grandson of Moses, son of Eliezer
column7: Son of Eliezer, the son of Moses. Rehabiah's sons were very many ([[@13023015|1 Chr 23:15]]; [[@13023017|1 Chr 23:17]]).

column5: City on Asher's border
column7: A city on the border of the land Asher's descendants received according to their families. The border passed Rehob and reached as far as great Sidon ([[@6019024|Josh 19:24]]; [[@6019028|Josh 19:28]]).

column5: A Levite town of the tribe of Asher
column7: It was a town of the tribe of Asher that was given to the Levites ([[@6019030|Josh 19:30]]; [[@6021031|Josh 21:31]]). Asher did not drive out the inhabitants of Rehob ([[@7001031|Judg 1:31]]).

column5: Father of Hadadezer, king of Zobah
column7: He was the father of Hadadezer, king of Zobah. David struck and defeated Hadadezer ([[@10008003|2 Sam 8:3]]; [[@10008012|2 Sam 8:12]]).

column5: A Levite who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the Levites who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010009|Neh 10:9]]; [[@16010011|Neh 10:11]]).

column5: Solomon's son, king of Judah when the kingdom split
column7: He was Solomon's son and became king after his father ([[@11011043|1 Kgs 11:43]]).
