When the people gathered at Shechem and asked him to lighten their heavy yoke, he rejected the advice of the older men, followed the young men, and answered, 'I will make it even heavier' ([[@11012013-11012014|1 Kgs 12:13-14]]). Then the northern tribes left and made Jeroboam their king, and Rehoboam ruled only over the people living in the cities of Judah ([[@11012017|1 Kgs 12:17]]). He became king at forty-one and reigned seventeen years in Jerusalem ([[@11014021|1 Kgs 14:21]]).

column5: A well Isaac dug
column7: This was a well Isaac dug without any quarrel. Isaac said, "For now the LORD has made room for us" ([[@1026022|Gen 26:22]]).

column5: Hometown of Shaul, king of Edom
column7: It was a place by the River, and Shaul, a king of Edom, came from there ([[@1036037|Gen 36:37]]). It is also named in 1 Chronicles ([[@13001048|1 Chr 1:48]]).

column5: A leader who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the leaders of the people of Israel who returned from exile with Zerubbabel, Jeshua, Nehemiah, and others ([[@15002002|Ezra 2:2]]).

column5: The official who accused the people of Jerusalem
column7: He was an official who, with Shimshai the scribe, sent a letter to King Artaxerxes accusing the people of Jerusalem ([[@15004008|Ezra 4:8]]). The king sent them a reply ([[@15004017|Ezra 4:17]]).

column5: A Levite who repaired the wall
column7: The son of Bani the Levite, he repaired a section of Jerusalem's wall in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003017|Neh 3:17]]).

column5: A chief of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010025|Neh 10:25]]).

column5: One who did not side with Adonijah
column7: When Adonijah tried to make himself king, he was one of those, along with Zadok, Benaiah, Nathan, and Shimei, who did not side with Adonijah ([[@11001008|1 Kgs 1:8]]).

column5: A Midianite king killed by Israel
column7: He was one of the five kings of Midian, whom Israel killed along with Balaam ([[@4031008|Num 31:8]]; [[@6013021|Josh 13:21]]).

column5: A city of Benjamin
column7: It was one of the cities the tribe of Benjamin received by their families ([[@6018021|Josh 18:21]]; [[@6018027|Josh 18:27]]).

column5: Son of Hebron, of Judah
column7: He was one of the sons of Hebron among Caleb's descendants, a brother of Korah, Tappuah, and Shema, and the father of Shammai ([[@13002043-13002044|1 Chr 2:43-44]]).

column5: Father of Pekah king of Israel
column7: He was the father of Pekah king of Israel. His son Pekah was an officer who rebelled, killed King Pekahiah, and became king ([[@12015025|2 Kgs 15:25]], 27). Pekah attacked Judah together with Rezin king of Syria ([[@12015037|2 Kgs 15:37]]). In Isaiah, Pekah is called 'the son of Remaliah', and Isaiah compared the two kings to "these two tails of smoking torches", telling the king not to be afraid ([[@23007004|Isa 7:4]]).

column5: A town in the land of Issachar
column7: It was one of the towns in the land Issachar's descendants received by lot ([[@6019017|Josh 19:17]]; [[@6019021|Josh 19:21]]).

column5: Turning from sin and coming back to God
column7: Repentance means being sorry for sin and turning one's heart and life back to God. John the Baptist and Jesus both preached, "Repent, for the Kingdom of Heaven is at hand" ([[@40003002|Matt 3:2]]; [[@40004017|Matt 4:17]]). Jesus said that there is more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance ([[@42015007|Luke 15:7]]). Peter too urged the people gathered at the temple to "Repent therefore, and turn again", so that their sins might be blotted out ([[@44003019|Acts 3:19]]).

column5: Son of Shemaiah, of Obed-Edom's family
column7: The son of Shemaiah, the son of Obed-Edom, he was one of Obed-Edom's descendants, able men who served well in their duties ([[@13026007-13026008|1 Chr 26:7-8]]).

column5: Son of Beriah, of Ephraim
column7: He was a son of Beriah, whom Ephraim fathered, and a brother of Resheph. He appears in the family line of Ephraim ([[@13007023|1 Chr 7:23]]; [[@13007025|1 Chr 7:25]]).

column5: Father of Arnan in David's line
column7: He appears in the family line of David as the father of Arnan. His family is listed after Pelatiah and Jeshaiah, the sons of Hananiah ([[@13003021|1 Chr 3:21]]).

column5: Simeonite captain who struck the Amalekites
column7: The son of Ishi, he became a captain over five hundred Simeonites, went to Mount Seir, and struck the remaining Amalekites ([[@13004042-13004043|1 Chr 4:42-43]]).

column5: Son of Tola, of Issachar
column7: He was a son of Tola, the son of Issachar, and a head of his father Tola's house ([[@13007001-13007002|1 Chr 7:1-2]]).

column5: Son of Hur who repaired the wall
column7: The son of Hur, he ruled half the district of Jerusalem and repaired a section of the wall in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003009|Neh 3:9]]).

column5: A tall people of Canaan and east of the Jordan
column7: They were an ancient people who lived in Canaan and east of the Jordan before Israel came in. In Abraham's time Chedorlaomer struck "the Rephaim in Ashteroth Karnaim" ([[@1014005|Gen 14:5]]). Tall people like the Anakim were called Rephaim, and the Moabites called them Emim, while the Ammonites called them Zamzummim ([[@5002010-5002011|Deut 2:10-11]]; [[@5002020|Deut 2:20]]). Og king of Bashan "remained of the remnant of the Rephaim", and his iron bedstead was nine cubits long ([[@5003011|Deut 3:11]]).

column5: The valley where David defeated the Philistines
column7: It was a valley near Jerusalem, and the border of the tribe of Judah passed the northern end of the valley of Rephaim ([[@6015008|Josh 15:8]]). After David became king, the Philistines spread out in this valley twice, but each time David asked the LORD first and then struck them down ([[@10005018-10005025|2 Sam 5:18-25]]). When the Philistine army was camped here, three of the thirty chiefs came to David at the cave of Adullam ([[@10023013|2 Sam 23:13]]). They broke through the Philistine camp and drew water from the well of Bethlehem, but David would not drink it and poured it out to the LORD ([[@10023016|2 Sam 23:16]]).

column5: A wilderness camp where they quarreled over water
column7: It was the place where Israel camped but had no water to drink ([[@2017001|Exod 17:1]]). Amalek fought with Israel here ([[@2017008|Exod 17:8]]).

column5: A great city between Nineveh and Calah
column7: This was a great city that Nimrod built between Nineveh and Calah when he went out into Assyria ([[@1010011-1010012|Gen 10:11-12]]).

column5: Son of Beriah, father of Telah
column7: He appears in the family line of Ephraim as a son of Beriah, and his son was Telah ([[@13007023|1 Chr 7:23]]; [[@13007025|1 Chr 7:25]]).

column5: Son of Peleg, ancestor of Abraham
column7: He was a descendant of Shem, the son Peleg had at thirty ([[@1011018|Gen 11:18]]). Reu became the father of Serug at thirty-two, and after that he lived two hundred seven years and had other children ([[@1011020-1011021|Gen 11:20-21]]). From Serug came Nahor and Terah and then Abram, so Reu was an ancestor of Abraham ([[@1011022-1011026|Gen 11:22-26]]). His name also appears in the genealogy of Chronicles and in Luke's genealogy of Jesus ([[@13001025|1 Chr 1:25]]; [[@42003035|Luke 3:35]]).

column5: The firstborn son of Jacob and Leah
column7: He was Jacob's firstborn son, born to Leah ([[@1029032|Gen 29:32]]). When his brothers wanted to kill Joseph, he said, "Shed no blood" and suggested throwing him into a pit, hoping to save Joseph's life ([[@1037021-1037022|Gen 37:21-22]]). But because he lay with Bilhah, his father's concubine, he lost the honor that belonged to the firstborn ([[@1049003-1049004|Gen 49:3-4]]). His descendants, the tribe of Reuben, received land east of the Jordan ([[@4032033|Num 32:33]]).

column5: Son of Esau and Basemath
column7: He was the son born to Basemath, Esau's wife ([[@1036004|Gen 36:4]]). His sons were Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah ([[@1036013|Gen 36:13]]).

column5: Ancestor of a Benjamite in Jerusalem
column7: He appears in the family line of Meshullam, a Benjamite who lived in Jerusalem. Meshullam was "the son of Shephatiah, the son of Reuel" ([[@13009003|1 Chr 9:3]]; [[@13009008|1 Chr 9:8]]).

column5: Concubine of Nahor
column7: She was the concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother, and bore Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maacah ([[@1022020|Gen 22:20]]; [[@1022024|Gen 22:24]]).

column5: A place destroyed by Assyria
column7: It was one of the places the king of Assyria boasted that his fathers had destroyed ([[@12019012|2 Kgs 19:12]]; [[@23037012|Isa 37:12]]).

column5: King of Syria who attacked Judah in Ahaz's day
column7: He was the king of Syria in the days of Ahaz king of Judah. Together with Pekah king of Israel he came up to Jerusalem and besieged Ahaz, but could not overcome him ([[@12016005|2 Kgs 16:5]]). He recovered Elath for Syria and drove the people of Judah out of it ([[@12016006|2 Kgs 16:6]]). Isaiah told the frightened Ahaz not to be afraid, because Rezin and Pekah were only "these two tails of smoking torches" ([[@23007004|Isa 7:4]]). In the end, at Ahaz's request, the king of Assyria attacked and took Damascus and killed Rezin ([[@12016007-12016009|2 Kgs 16:7-9]]).

column5: A temple servant ancestor who returned from exile
column7: He was the ancestor of 'the children of Rezin' among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon ([[@15002048|Ezra 2:48]]; [[@16007050|Neh 7:50]]).

column5: Syrian king who opposed Solomon
column7: The son of Eliada, he fled from Hadadezer king of Zobah and became king in Damascus. God raised him up to be an adversary to Solomon ([[@11011023-11011024|1 Kgs 11:23-24]]).

column5: A stop on Paul's voyage to Rome
column7: This is where Paul's ship arrived on the way to Rome and stayed for one day. Then a south wind sprang up, and they went on to Puteoli ([[@44028013|Acts 28:13]]).

column5: A man in Jesus' genealogy
column7: This name appears in Jesus' genealogy in the Gospel of Luke, listed as the son of Zerubbabel and the father of Joanan ([[@42003027|Luke 3:27]]).

column5: Servant girl in Mary's house
column7: She was a servant girl in the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark. When she recognized Peter's voice, she was so glad that she ran in to tell the others without even opening the gate ([[@44012012-44012014|Acts 12:12-14]]).

column5: A stop on Paul's journey
column7: Paul and his companions sailed straight to Cos and arrived here the next day. From there they went on to Patara ([[@44021001|Acts 21:1]]).

column5: Father of Ittai, one of David's mighty men
column7: A man of Gibeah of the tribe of Benjamin, he was the father of Ittai, one of David's mighty men ([[@10023029|2 Sam 23:29]]; [[@13011031|1 Chr 11:31]]).

column5: A place on Canaan's eastern border
column7: The eastern border of the land of Canaan that the LORD set out was to go down from Shepham to Riblah ([[@4034010-4034011|Num 34:10-11]]).

column5: A town in Hamath where Babylon's king camped
column7: It was a town in the land of Hamath where the kings of Egypt and Babylon stayed around the time Judah fell. Pharaoh Necoh imprisoned Jehoahaz son of Josiah at Riblah in the land of Hamath so that he could not reign in Jerusalem ([[@12023031-12023033|2 Kgs 23:31-33]]). After Jerusalem fell, the Chaldean army captured King Zedekiah and brought him to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon at Riblah, and the king of Babylon killed his sons before his eyes ([[@24039005-24039006|Jer 39:5-6]]). The king of Babylon also put to death at Riblah all the people of Judah whom Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, had brought to him ([[@12025020-12025021|2 Kgs 25:20-21]]).

column5: Being right and upright before God
column7: Righteousness means what is right and upright before God. The Bible says that Abram believed the LORD, "who credited it to him for righteousness" ([[@1015006|Gen 15:6]]). God said he had chosen Abraham so that he would command his children and his household to keep the way of the LORD by doing righteousness and justice ([[@1018019|Gen 18:19]]). Jesus said, "But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness" ([[@40006033|Matt 6:33]]), and Paul, saying that God's righteousness is revealed in the gospel, passed on the word, "the righteous shall live by faith" ([[@45001017|Rom 1:17]]).

column5: Southern town given to Simeon
column7: It was one of the southern towns of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015032|Josh 15:32]]), and it later became part of the inheritance of the tribe of Simeon ([[@6019007|Josh 19:7]]).

column5: The rock where the Benjamites took refuge
column7: It was the rock to which the Benjamites fled toward the wilderness after losing the battle ([[@7020045|Judg 20:45]]). Later the congregation proclaimed peace to the Benjamites who were there ([[@7021013|Judg 21:13]]).

column5: Father of Rechab and Baanah
column7: A Beerothite from the tribe of Benjamin, he was the father of Baanah and Rechab, captains under Ishbosheth ([[@10004002|2 Sam 4:2]]). His two sons killed Ishbosheth while he was taking his midday rest ([[@10004005-10004006|2 Sam 4:5-6]]).

column5: A camp in the wilderness
column7: In the wilderness the Israelites left Rithmah and camped at Rimmon Perez, then left there and camped at Libnah ([[@4033019-4033020|Num 33:19-20]]).

column5: Son of Shimon, of Judah
column7: He appears in the family line of Judah as a son of Shimon, listed with Amnon, Ben Hanan, and Tilon ([[@13004001|1 Chr 4:1]]; [[@13004020|1 Chr 4:20]]).

column5: Son of Gomer
column7: He was a son of Gomer, the son of Japheth ([[@1010003|Gen 10:3]]). In 1 Chronicles he is called 'Diphath' ([[@13001006|1 Chr 1:6]]).

column5: A camp in the wilderness
column7: In the wilderness the Israelites left Libnah and camped at Rissah, then left Rissah and camped at Kehelathah ([[@4033021-4033022|Num 33:21-22]]).

column5: A camp in the wilderness
column7: In the wilderness the Israelites left Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah, then left Rithmah and camped at Rimmon Perez ([[@4033018-4033019|Num 33:18-19]]).

column5: Son of Ulla, of Asher
column7: He was a son of Ulla of the tribe of Asher, listed with Arah and Hanniel. The descendants of Asher were choice, mighty men of valor ([[@13007039-13007040|1 Chr 7:39-40]]).

column5: Saul's concubine, daughter of Aiah
column7: She was the daughter of Aiah and Saul's concubine ([[@10003007|2 Sam 3:7]]). When her sons were put to death, she spread out sackcloth and guarded their bodies from the birds and wild animals ([[@10021008|2 Sam 21:8]]; [[@10021010|2 Sam 21:10]]).

column5: Where Saul stopped chasing David
column7: Because Saul stopped pursuing David there and turned back to fight the Philistines, that place was called Sela Hammahlekoth ([[@9023028|1 Sam 23:28]]).

column5: Hometown of Barzillai the Gileadite
column7: It was where Barzillai the Gileadite lived. He brought food to David and his people when they came to Mahanaim, and he came down from Rogelim to escort the king to the Jordan ([[@10017027-10017029|2 Sam 17:27-29]]; [[@10019031|2 Sam 19:31]]).

column5: Son of Shemer, of Asher
column7: He was a son of Shemer of the tribe of Asher, listed with Ahi, Jehubbah, and Aram ([[@13007034|1 Chr 7:34]]; [[@13007040|1 Chr 7:40]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a singer
column7: He was one of the sons of Heman and was given the twenty-fourth turn in the service of praise ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]; [[@13025031|1 Chr 25:31]]).

column5: Capital of the Roman Empire
column7: Rome was the capital of the Roman Empire, which ruled the Mediterranean world in New Testament times. At Pentecost there were also "visitors from Rome" in Jerusalem ([[@44002010|Acts 2:10]]). Paul wrote a letter to the believers in Rome, where he had not yet been, and that letter is Romans ([[@45001007|Rom 1:7]]). Later Paul went to Rome as a prisoner, stayed two whole years in a rented house, and boldly preached God's Kingdom to all who came to him ([[@44028030-44028031|Acts 28:30-31]]).

column5: Son of Benjamin
column7: He was one of the sons of Benjamin, listed among Israel's family who went down to Egypt with Jacob ([[@1046008|Gen 46:8]]; [[@1046021|Gen 46:21]]).

column5: Son of Simon of Cyrene
column7: He was a son of Simon of Cyrene, who was compelled to carry Jesus' cross, and he is named with Alexander ([[@41015021|Mark 15:21]]).

column5: A believer in Rome greeted by Paul
column7: He was a believer whom Paul greeted, calling him "Rufus, the chosen in the Lord". Paul called Rufus's mother his own mother as well ([[@45016013|Rom 16:13]]).

column5: Moabite who followed Naomi, David's great-grandmother
column7: A Moabite woman, she was Naomi's daughter-in-law ([[@8001004|Ruth 1:4]]). After her husband died she would not leave Naomi, and saying, "Your people will be my people, and your God my God", she went with her to Bethlehem ([[@8001016|Ruth 1:16]]). While gleaning in the field of Boaz she became his wife and gave birth to Obed ([[@8004013|Ruth 4:13]]). Obed was David's grandfather, and Ruth's name is also listed in the genealogy of Jesus ([[@40001005|Matt 1:5]]).

column5: The seventh day, set apart for rest and holiness
column7: The Sabbath is the seventh day, when people rest from work and keep the day holy to God. Because God made heaven and earth in six days and rested on the seventh day, he blessed that day ([[@2020011|Exod 20:11]]). The word Sabbath first appears when the manna came down in the wilderness, and the Ten Commandments say, "Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy" ([[@2016023|Exod 16:23]]; [[@2020008|Exod 20:8]]). Jesus taught the true meaning of the Sabbath, saying, "The Sabbath was made for man" ([[@41002027|Mark 2:27]]).

column5: Son of Cush
column7: He was one of the sons of Cush, the son of Noah's son Ham, and a brother of Seba, Havilah, Raamah, and Sabteca ([[@1010007|Gen 10:7]]; [[@13001009|1 Chr 1:9]]).

column5: Son of Cush
column7: He was one of the sons of Cush, the son of Noah's son Ham, and a brother of Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, and Raamah ([[@1010007|Gen 10:7]]; [[@13001009|1 Chr 1:9]]).

column5: Obed-Edom's fourth son
column7: He was the fourth son of Obed-Edom, a member of Obed-Edom's family who served in the divisions of the gatekeepers ([[@13026001|1 Chr 26:1]]; [[@13026004|1 Chr 26:4]]).

column5: Son of Shaharaim
column7: He was a son born to Shaharaim, a Benjamite, by his wife Hodesh, and he was a head of a family ([[@13008009-13008010|1 Chr 8:9-10]]).

column5: Rough cloth worn in grief and repentance
column7: Sackcloth was a rough cloth woven from something like goat hair, worn on the body to show grief or repentance. Thinking Joseph was dead, Jacob tore his clothes, put sackcloth around his waist, and mourned ([[@1037034|Gen 37:34]]). When Mordecai learned that his people were to be destroyed, he put on sackcloth with ashes and wailed ([[@17004001|Esth 4:1]]). The people of Nineveh and their king also believed God, put on sackcloth, and repented ([[@32003005-32003006|Jonah 3:5-6]]). Jesus too said, "they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes" ([[@40011021|Matt 11:21]]).

column5: Jewish group that denied the resurrection
column7: The Sadducees were a Jewish group in New Testament times, and many of them were among those around the high priest ([[@44005017|Acts 5:17]]). They held a different view from the Pharisees, saying "there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit" ([[@44023008|Acts 23:8]]). So they tried to test Jesus with a question about the resurrection, and they were upset when the apostles proclaimed Jesus' resurrection ([[@40022023|Matt 22:23]]; [[@44004001-44004002|Acts 4:1-2]]). It is not clear when or how this group began, so scholars differ.

column5: Unknown location mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy
column7: Sahar is a place mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy, but its exact location is unknown (<ref="Ezk. 27:18">Ezk. 27:18</ref>).

column5: Where Paul and Barnabas preached
column7: This is where Barnabas and Saul arrived and proclaimed God's word in the Jewish synagogues ([[@44013005|Acts 13:5]]).

column5: A town of Bashan
column7: It was a town of Bashan, the kingdom of Og ([[@5003010|Deut 3:10]]). Its name comes up when the far edge of the land of Bashan is described ([[@6012005|Josh 12:5]]; [[@6013011|Josh 13:11]]).

column5: Near Enon, where John baptized
column7: Enon, where John was baptizing, was near this Salim. There was much water there, so people came and were baptized ([[@43003023|John 3:23]]).

column5: A Benjamite living in Jerusalem
column7: His name appears with Gabbai among the Benjamites who lived in Jerusalem ([[@16011007-16011008|Neh 11:7-8]]).

column5: A Benjamite living in Jerusalem
column7: He was a Benjamite living in Jerusalem, the son of Meshullam, the grandson of Hodaviah, and the great-grandson of Hassenuah ([[@13009003|1 Chr 9:3]]; [[@13009007|1 Chr 9:7]]).

column5: A Benjamite living in Jerusalem
column7: He was a Benjamite living in Jerusalem, the son of Meshullam and the grandson of Joed ([[@16011004|Neh 11:4]]; [[@16011007|Neh 11:7]]).

column5: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the priests who went up with Zerubbabel and Jeshua, and he was one of the chiefs of the priests in the days of Jeshua ([[@16012001|Neh 12:1]]; [[@16012007|Neh 12:7]]).

column5: Son of Hur, 'father of Bethlehem'
column7: A son of Hur among Caleb's descendants, he was called 'the father of Bethlehem' ([[@13002050-13002051|1 Chr 2:50-51]]). His descendants included Bethlehem and the Netophathites, among others ([[@13002054|1 Chr 2:54]]).

column5: Father of Boaz, an ancestor of David
column7: He was the son of Nahshon and the father of Boaz ([[@8004020-8004021|Ruth 4:20-21]]). Matthew records, "Salmon became the father of Boaz by Rahab" ([[@40001005|Matt 1:5]]).

column5: Near Crete, passed by Paul's ship
column7: Because of the wind, Paul's ship passed opposite this place and sailed under the lee of Crete ([[@44027007|Acts 27:7]]).

column5: The daughter who danced before Herod
column7: She danced on Herod's birthday and pleased him, and at her mother's prompting she asked for the head of John the Baptizer ([[@40014006|Matt 14:6]]; [[@40014008|Matt 14:8]]). The Bible does not give this daughter's name.

column5: Woman who watched Jesus' crucifixion
column7: When Jesus was crucified, she watched from afar along with Mary Magdalene and others ([[@41015040|Mark 15:40]]). When the Sabbath was past, she bought spices to anoint Jesus ([[@41016001|Mark 16:1]]).

column5: Used to season food and offerings
column7: Salt was used to season food, and it was also added to offerings made to God. The law said to season every meal offering with salt, and it called it "the salt of the covenant" ([[@3002013|Lev 2:13]]). Lot's wife, who looked back as they left Sodom, became a pillar of salt ([[@1019026|Gen 19:26]]). Jesus told his disciples, "You are the salt of the earth", and said that if salt loses its flavor, it is good for nothing but to be thrown out ([[@40005013|Matt 5:13]]). Paul urged that our speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt ([[@51004006|Col 4:6]]).

column5: The salty sea into which the Jordan flows
column7: It is the sea known today as the Dead Sea, which the Bible calls the Salt Sea. Genesis says the valley of Siddim is "also called the Salt Sea" ([[@1014003|Gen 14:3]]). This sea was also called the sea of the Arabah, and it marked the eastern border of the Promised Land ([[@5003017|Deut 3:17]]; [[@4034012|Num 34:12]]). In Joshua's time, when the waters of the Jordan stopped, "those that went down toward the sea of the Arabah, even the Salt Sea, were wholly cut off" ([[@6003016|Josh 3:16]]).

column5: The valley where the Edomites were struck down
column7: It was the place where David struck down eighteen thousand Edomites ([[@10008013|2 Sam 8:13]]). Amaziah king of Judah also killed ten thousand Edomites here ([[@12014007|2 Kgs 14:7]]).

column5: Father of Zimri, a Simeonite leader
column7: He was the father of Zimri, the Simeonite leader who was killed together with the Midianite woman ([[@4025014|Num 25:14]]).

column5: The capital of northern Israel
column7: This city became the capital of northern Israel. King Omri bought the hill from Shemer, built a city on it, and named it Samaria after the hill's owner ([[@11016024|1 Kgs 16:24]]). In Ahab's time a house of Baal was built here ([[@11016032|1 Kgs 16:32]]). After it fell to Assyria, people from other nations were brought in to live there ([[@12017024|2 Kgs 17:24]]). In New Testament times this region was called Samaria, and Jesus talked with a Samaritan woman at a well ([[@43004007|John 4:7]]).

column5: The people who lived in the land of Samaria
column7: Samaritans were the people the king of Assyria brought from many places to live in the land of Samaria after the northern kingdom of Israel fell, along with their descendants. At first they feared the LORD but also served their own gods ([[@12017024|2 Kgs 17:24]], 33). In New Testament times they were on bad terms with the Jews, and the Bible says, "For Jews have no dealings with Samaritans" ([[@43004009|John 4:9]]). Jesus told the parable of the Samaritan who helped a man attacked by robbers, and after he met the Samaritan woman many Samaritans believed in him ([[@42010033|Luke 10:33]]; [[@43004039|John 4:39]]).

column5: An official of the king of Babylon
column7: He was one of the officials of the king of Babylon who sat in the middle gate when Jerusalem fell ([[@24039002-24039003|Jer 39:2-3]]).

column5: A king of Edom from Masrekah
column7: He was from Masrekah and became king of Edom after Hadad ([[@1036036|Gen 36:36]]). He is also listed in 1 Chronicles as 'Samlah of Masrekah' ([[@13001047|1 Chr 1:47]]).

column5: A stop on Paul's journey
column7: Paul and his companions stopped here the day after passing opposite Chios, and the day after that they reached Miletus ([[@44020015|Acts 20:15]]).

column5: Where Paul sailed from Troas
column7: Paul and his companions set sail from Troas and went straight here, and the next day they went on to Neapolis ([[@44016011|Acts 16:11]]).

column5: A judge of Israel given great strength
column7: Samson was the son of Manoah and a Nazirite dedicated to God from birth ([[@7013005|Judg 13:5]]). When the Spirit of the LORD came mightily on him, he had such strength that he tore a lion apart with his bare hands ([[@7014006|Judg 14:6]]). He fought the Philistines many times, but after he told Delilah the secret of his strength, his head was shaved and his eyes were put out ([[@7016017-7016021|Judg 16:17-21]]). In the end he cried out to the LORD, pulled down the pillars that held up the house, and died together with many Philistines ([[@7016028-7016030|Judg 16:28-30]]). He judged Israel for twenty years.

column5: The last judge and a prophet
column7: He was the son of Elkanah and Hannah. Hannah, who had no children, prayed and bore him, and she named him, saying, "Because I have asked him of the LORD" ([[@9001020|1 Sam 1:20]]). He grew up at the tabernacle as a boy, and when he heard the LORD's call he answered, "Speak; for your servant hears" ([[@9003010|1 Sam 3:10]]). He judged Israel all the days of his life ([[@9007015|1 Sam 7:15]]), and he anointed Saul and David as kings ([[@9016013|1 Sam 16:13]]).

column5: The man who hindered Nehemiah's work on the wall
column7: He was a Horonite who was deeply grieved to hear that Nehemiah had come to help the children of Israel ([[@16002010|Neh 2:10]]). When he heard that the wall of Jerusalem was being built, he was very angry and mocked the Jews ([[@16004001|Neh 4:1]]). He tried to harm Nehemiah by asking to meet him in the plain of Ono, but Nehemiah did not go ([[@16006002-16006003|Neh 6:2-3]]). When one of the grandsons of Eliashib the high priest became Sanballat's son-in-law, Nehemiah chased him away ([[@16013028|Neh 13:28]]).

column5: Being set apart to God and made holy
column7: In the Bible, to sanctify means to set a person or thing apart for God. God told Israel to set apart every firstborn as holy to him, and before giving the covenant at Mount Sinai he had the people sanctified and had them wash their garments ([[@2013002|Exod 13:2]]; [[@2019010|Exod 19:10]]). God commanded them to sanctify themselves and be holy, "for I am holy" ([[@3011044|Lev 11:44]]). The New Testament also says, "this is the will of God: your sanctification", and it hopes that believers will live holy lives day by day ([[@52004003|1 Thess 4:3]]).

column5: Footwear worn on the feet
column7: Sandals were the footwear people wore on their feet. God told Moses, "Take off your sandals", saying that the place where he stood was holy ground, and Joshua heard the same words from the prince of the LORD's army ([[@2003005|Exod 3:5]]; [[@6005015|Josh 5:15]]). In ancient Israel, to confirm a redeeming or an exchange, it was the custom for a man to take off his sandal and give it to his neighbor ([[@8004007|Ruth 4:7]]). John the Baptist said that the one coming after him was mightier than he, and that he was not worthy even to carry his sandals ([[@40003011|Matt 3:11]]).

column5: The highest Jewish council
column7: The Sanhedrin was the highest Jewish council in New Testament times, where the chief priests, the elders of the people, and the scribes gathered to judge important matters ([[@42022066|Luke 22:66]]). The chief priests and the whole council looked for false testimony so they could put Jesus to death ([[@40026059|Matt 26:59]]). The apostles were also brought before the council, and the Pharisee Gamaliel stood up and said to leave these men alone ([[@44005034-44005039|Acts 5:34-39]]). Some say it began with the seventy elders of Moses' time, but this is not certain ([[@4011016|Num 11:16]]).

column5: A southern town of Judah
column7: It was one of the southern towns that the tribe of Judah received ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015031|Josh 15:31]]).

column5: A giant killed by Sibbecai the Hushathite
column7: He was a son of the giant, killed by Sibbecai the Hushathite when Israel fought the Philistines at Gob ([[@10021018|2 Sam 21:18]]). In 1 Chronicles he is called 'Sippai' ([[@13020004|1 Chr 20:4]]).

column5: Wife of Ananias
column7: She and her husband Ananias sold a property and kept back part of the price. She fell down at Peter's feet and died and was buried beside her husband ([[@44005001-44005002|Acts 5:1-2]]; [[@44005010|Acts 5:10]]).

column5: Abraham's wife, Isaac's mother
column7: Sarah was Abraham's wife, and at first her name was Sarai. She had no children for a long time, but God changed her name to Sarah and promised that she would be a mother of nations ([[@1017015-1017016|Gen 17:15-16]]). When she heard that she would bear a son in her old age, she laughed within herself ([[@1018012|Gen 18:12]]), but she gave birth to Isaac just as God had said ([[@1021002|Gen 21:2]]). She lived one hundred twenty-seven years, died in Hebron, and was buried in the cave of Machpelah ([[@1023001-1023002|Gen 23:1-2]], 19).

column5: Son of Shelah, descendant of Judah
column7: Saraph was a son of Shelah and a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogy of Judah.

column5: A place on Zebulun's border
column7: The border of the land Zebulun's descendants received by lot reached Sarid, and from Sarid it turned eastward to Chisloth Tabor ([[@6019010|Josh 19:10]]; [[@6019012|Josh 19:12]]).

column5: The evil one who opposes God and people
column7: Satan means 'adversary' or 'accuser'; he is the evil spirit who opposes God and his people. In Job, Satan accused Job, saying, "Does Job fear God for nothing?", and struck him with painful sores ([[@18001009|Job 1:9]]; [[@18002007|Job 2:7]]). When Jesus was tempted in the wilderness, he said, "Get behind me, Satan!" and overcame him with the word of God ([[@40004010|Matt 4:10]]). The Bible calls Satan the old serpent and the devil, and says that he will finally be bound ([[@66020002|Rev 20:2]]).

column5: Israel's first king
column7: He was the son of Kish, of the tribe of Benjamin ([[@9009001|1 Sam 9:1]]). Scripture calls him "an impressive young man" and says he was taller than all the people from his shoulders up ([[@9009002|1 Sam 9:2]]). Samuel anointed him, and he became Israel's first king ([[@9010001|1 Sam 10:1]]). But because he rejected the word of the LORD, he was rejected as king, and out of jealousy he pursued David for a long time. He died on the same day as his three sons while fighting the Philistines ([[@9031006|1 Sam 31:6]]).

column5: Jewish priest with seven sons
column7: He was a Jewish priest whose seven sons also tried to drive out evil spirits by invoking the Jesus whom Paul preached ([[@44019013-44019014|Acts 19:13-14]]).

column5: Those who copied and taught the law
column7: At first scribes were officials in charge of the royal records and documents ([[@10008017|2 Sam 8:17]]). After the exile, men like Ezra, "a skilled scribe in the law of Moses", copied the law and explained it, and the scribes of the New Testament were teachers of the law like this ([[@15007006|Ezra 7:6]]). Many of them, along with the Pharisees, were rebuked as hypocrites ([[@40023027|Matt 23:27]]). But to a scribe who asked about the first commandment and answered wisely, Jesus said, "You are not far from God’s Kingdom" ([[@41012034|Mark 12:34]]).

column5: An ancient book written and rolled up
column7: A scroll was an ancient book that was written on and then rolled up. God told Jeremiah to take a scroll and write in it all the words he had spoken to him up to that time ([[@24036002|Jer 36:2]]). When Jehoiakim king of Judah cut that scroll with a knife and threw it into the fire in the brazier to burn it, God had the words written again on another scroll ([[@24036023|Jer 36:23]], 28). Ezekiel ate the scroll God gave him, and it was as sweet as honey ([[@26003003|Ezek 3:3]]). In Ezra's time, a scroll found in the palace in Media recorded King Cyrus's decree to build the temple ([[@15006002-15006003|Ezra 6:2-3]]).

column5: A people Paul mentioned
column7: Paul said that in Christ there is no distinction between Greek and Jew, barbarian or Scythian ([[@51003011|Col 3:11]]).

column5: A stamp showing who owns a document or thing
column7: A seal was pressed onto a document or object to show whom it belonged to, and it is also called a signet. Judah gave Tamar his signet, cord, and staff as a pledge, and Pharaoh took off his signet ring and put it on Joseph's hand ([[@1038018|Gen 38:18]]; [[@1041042|Gen 41:42]]). Jezebel wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them with his seal, and plotted to have Naboth killed ([[@11021008-11021010|1 Kgs 21:8-10]]). The New Testament says that believers "were sealed with the promised Holy Spirit" ([[@49001013|Eph 1:13]]).

column5: Son of Cush
column7: He was one of the sons of Cush, the son of Noah's son Ham, and a brother of Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca ([[@1010007|Gen 10:7]]; [[@13001009|1 Chr 1:9]]).

column5: A nation named with Ethiopia
column7: It was a nation named together with Ethiopia. The LORD said he had given Egypt as Israel's ransom, and Ethiopia and Seba in Israel's place ([[@23043003|Isa 43:3]]). The psalm says the kings of Seba will offer gifts ([[@19072010|Ps 72:10]])

column5: Land requested by Reuben and Gad
column7: It was one of the places that the descendants of Gad and Reuben asked Moses for, because it was good land for livestock ([[@4032001-4032003|Num 32:1-3]]).

column5: A town in Judah's wilderness
column7: It was one of the wilderness towns that the tribe of Judah received ([[@6015020|Josh 15:20]]; [[@6015061|Josh 15:61]]).

column5: A district of Jerusalem
column7: This was the district of Jerusalem where the prophetess Huldah lived ([[@12022014|2 Kgs 22:14]]; [[@14034022|2 Chr 34:22]]). Zephaniah said that on the day of judgment a cry would go up from 'the second quarter' ([[@36001010|Zeph 1:10]]).

column5: Site of a great well near Ramah
column7: This is where the great well was that Saul came to as he went to Ramah looking for Samuel and David ([[@9019022|1 Sam 19:22]]).

column5: A Thessalonian who traveled with Paul
column7: A Thessalonian named alongside Aristarchus, he went with Paul as far as Asia ([[@44020004|Acts 20:4]]).

column5: Hiel's youngest son
column7: He was the youngest son, whom Hiel of Bethel lost when he set up the gates of Jericho. It happened just as the LORD had spoken through Joshua ([[@11016034|1 Kgs 16:34]]).

column5: Son of Hezron, father of Jair
column7: He was the son born to Hezron by the daughter of Machir the father of Gilead, and the father of Jair ([[@13002021-13002022|1 Chr 2:21-22]]).

column5: Hill country where Esau's descendants, Edom, lived
column7: It is a range of hill country stretching south of the Dead Sea, east of the Arabah. At first the Horites lived there ([[@1014006|Gen 14:6]]). When Jacob was returning home, he sent messengers to his brother Esau "to the land of Seir, the field of Edom" ([[@1032003|Gen 32:3]]). Later Esau settled there, and the Bible says, "Esau lived in the hill country of Seir. Esau is Edom" ([[@1036008|Gen 36:8]]). God told Israel not to quarrel with them, because he had given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession ([[@5002004-5002005|Deut 2:4-5]]).

column5: Ancestor of the Horites in Edom
column7: He was the ancestor of the Horites, the original inhabitants of the land, and Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, and others were his descendants ([[@1036020|Gen 36:20]]). His descendants became chiefs in the land of Edom ([[@1036021|Gen 36:21]]).

column5: The hill country where Esau's descendants, Edom, lived
column7: It was the hill country where Esau, that is, Edom, settled ([[@1036008|Gen 36:8]]). God told Israel not to fight with them, saying, "I have given Mount Seir to Esau for a possession" ([[@5002005|Deut 2:5]]). In Jehoshaphat's time, the people of Ammon, Moab, and Mount Seir who came to attack Judah struck one another down and were destroyed ([[@14020022-14020023|2 Chr 20:22-23]]). Ezekiel prophesied against Mount Seir that it would become a desolation ([[@26035002-26035003|Ezek 35:2-3]]).

column5: A mountain on Judah's border
column7: This is the mountain the border of the tribe of Judah reached when it turned westward from Baalah ([[@6015010|Josh 15:10]]).

column5: Where Ehud escaped
column7: This is where Ehud escaped after he drew the sword with his left hand and struck the king, passing beyond the stone idols ([[@7003021|Judg 3:21]]; [[@7003026|Judg 3:26]]).

column5: An Edomite stronghold taken by Amaziah
column7: It was the place Amaziah king of Judah captured when he struck Edom, and he named it 'Joktheel' ([[@12014007|2 Kgs 14:7]]).

column5: A word that often appears in the Psalms
column7: Selah is a word that often appears in the Psalms, usually at the end of a verse ([[@19003002|Ps 3:2]]). In Psalm 3 alone it appears three times ([[@19003002|Ps 3:2]], 4, 8). Outside the Psalms, it appears three times in the prayer of Habakkuk 3 ([[@35003003|Hab 3:3]], 9, 13). Its meaning is not certain, so scholars have different views. Many see it as a musical mark used in singing, but the Bible itself does not explain what it means.

column5: Where Paul set sail
column7: This is where Barnabas and Saul went down after being sent out by the Holy Spirit and boarded a ship for Cyprus ([[@44013004|Acts 13:4]]).

column5: Of Obed-Edom's family, brother of Elzabad
column7: He belonged to the family of Shemaiah, a descendant of Obed-Edom, and was a brother of Elzabad and an able man ([[@13026007-13026008|1 Chr 26:7-8]]).

column5: A man in Jesus' genealogy
column7: This name appears in Jesus' genealogy in the Gospel of Luke, between Mattathias and Joseph ([[@42003026|Luke 3:26]]).

column5: A family that returned from exile
column7: Among those who returned from exile, the descendants of Senaah numbered three thousand six hundred thirty ([[@15002035|Ezra 2:35]]). In Nehemiah the number is given as three thousand nine hundred thirty ([[@16007038|Neh 7:38]]).

column5: A rocky crag near Michmash
column7: This was the name of a rocky crag at the pass where Jonathan sought to cross over to the Philistine garrison ([[@9014004|1 Sam 14:4]]).

column5: Assyrian king who attacked Judah under Hezekiah
column6: the moon god has added brothers
column7: A king of Assyria, he came up in the fourteenth year of King Hezekiah and captured the fortified cities of Judah ([[@12018013|2 Kgs 18:13]]). He sent his officials to insult the living God, and Hezekiah went up to the temple and prayed to the LORD ([[@12019016|2 Kgs 19:16]]). That night the angel of the LORD struck down 185,000 soldiers in the Assyrian camp ([[@12019035|2 Kgs 19:35]]). Sennacherib went back to Nineveh, and later, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons killed him with the sword ([[@12019037|2 Kgs 19:37]]).

column5: The fourth priestly division
column7: He was the one chosen fourth when the priestly divisions were assigned by lot in David's time ([[@13024007-13024008|1 Chr 24:7-8]]).

column5: Boundary of the land of Joktan's sons
column7: The land where the sons of Joktan lived reached from Mesha toward Sephar, the mountain of the east ([[@1010029-1010030|Gen 10:29-30]]).

column5: Where captives from Jerusalem were living
column7: It is a place mentioned only in Obadiah, where the captives taken from Jerusalem were said to be ([[@31001020|Obad 1:20]]). Scholars differ on where it was.

column5: Town from which Assyria resettled people in Samaria
column7: It was one of the places from which the king of Assyria brought people to settle in the towns of Samaria in place of the Israelites ([[@12017024|2 Kgs 17:24]]). The people of Sepharvaim burned their children in the fire to their gods Adrammelech and Anammelech ([[@12017031|2 Kgs 17:31]]). The Assyrian Rabshakeh threatened Hezekiah, boasting, "Where are the gods of Sepharvaim, of Hena, and Ivvah?" ([[@12018034|2 Kgs 18:34]]). Scholars differ on its exact location.

column5: Daughter of Asher
column7: She was the sister of Asher's sons Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah ([[@1046017|Gen 46:17]]). When the people were counted in the wilderness, she was also listed by name as 'the daughter of Asher' ([[@4026046|Num 26:46]]).

column5: A secretary under David
column7: He was the secretary in King David's time. When Zadok and Ahimelech were priests and Jehoshaphat was recorder, Seraiah became secretary ([[@10008016-10008017|2 Sam 8:16-17]]).

column5: The chief priest when Judah fell
column7: He was the chief priest whom the captain of the guard took away when Jerusalem fell ([[@12025018|2 Kgs 25:18]]). The king of Babylon struck him down at Riblah in the land of Hamath ([[@12025021|2 Kgs 25:21]]).

column5: An army captain who came to Gedaliah
column7: The son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, he was one of the army captains who went to Gedaliah at Mizpah ([[@12025023|2 Kgs 25:23]]; [[@24040008|Jer 40:8]]).

column5: Son of Kenaz, father of Joab
column7: A son of Kenaz and brother of Othniel, he was the father of Joab, the ancestor of Ge Harashim ([[@13004013-13004014|1 Chr 4:13-14]]).

column5: Grandfather of Jehu, a Simeonite leader
column7: He appears in the list of Simeonite leaders as the grandfather of Jehu the son of Joshibiah ([[@13004035|1 Chr 4:35]]; [[@13004038|1 Chr 4:38]]).

column5: A priest who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: He was one of the priests who returned from exile with Zerubbabel and Jeshua ([[@16012001|Neh 12:1]]). In Joiakim's time the head of Seraiah's family was Meraiah ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]).

column5: Ordered to arrest Jeremiah
column7: The son of Azriel, he was ordered by the king to arrest Baruch and Jeremiah. But the LORD hid them ([[@24036026|Jer 36:26]]).

column5: Quartermaster who went to Babylon
column7: The son of Neriah, he was the chief quartermaster who went to Babylon with King Zedekiah. Jeremiah told him to read these words when he arrived in Babylon ([[@24051059|Jer 51:59]]; [[@24051061|Jer 51:61]]).

column5: Heavenly beings serving beside God's throne
column7: The seraphim are heavenly beings Isaiah saw in a vision, and in the Bible they appear only in Isaiah 6. In the year King Uzziah died, Isaiah saw the Lord sitting on a throne, high and lifted up, with the seraphim standing above him ([[@23006001-23006002|Isa 6:1-2]]). Each of the seraphim had six wings, covering their faces and feet and flying, and they called to one another, "Holy, holy, holy, is the LORD of Armies!" ([[@23006002-23006003|Isa 6:2-3]]). One of them touched Isaiah's mouth with a live coal taken from the altar and said that his sin was forgiven ([[@23006006-23006007|Isa 6:6-7]]).

column5: Son of Zebulun
column7: A son of Zebulun, he went down to Egypt with Jacob ([[@1046014|Gen 46:14]]). The family of the Seredites came from him ([[@4026026|Num 26:26]]).

column5: Proconsul who heard the word and believed
column7: He was a proconsul, a man of understanding, who called for Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear the word of God. When he saw what happened next, he believed ([[@44013007|Acts 13:7]]; [[@44013012|Acts 13:12]]).

column5: Son of Reu, great-grandfather of Abraham
column7: He was the son Reu had at thirty-two ([[@1011020|Gen 11:20]]). Serug became the father of Nahor at thirty, and after that he lived two hundred years and had other children ([[@1011022-1011023|Gen 11:22-23]]). Nahor became the father of Terah, and Terah the father of Abram, so Serug was Abraham's great-grandfather ([[@1011024-1011026|Gen 11:24-26]]). His name also appears in the genealogy of Chronicles and in Luke's genealogy of Jesus ([[@13001026|1 Chr 1:26]]; [[@42003035|Luke 3:35]]).

column5: The third son of Adam and Eve
column7: He was the son Adam and Eve had after Abel died, and he was named Seth because Eve said, "for God has given me another child instead of Abel, for Cain killed him" ([[@1004025|Gen 4:25]]). The Bible says that Adam, at one hundred thirty, became the father of a son in his own likeness ([[@1005003|Gen 5:3]]). When Seth's son Enosh was born, the Bible says, "At that time men began to call on the LORD’s name" ([[@1004026|Gen 4:26]]). Seth lived nine hundred twelve years and then died ([[@1005008|Gen 5:8]]).

column5: A spy from the tribe of Asher
column7: The son of Michael, he was the man from the tribe of Asher sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013002|Num 13:2]]; [[@4013013|Num 13:13]]).

column5: A Danite town where Amorites remained
column7: It was a town where the Amorites were determined to stay, but when the house of Joseph grew strong, they were put to forced labor ([[@7001035|Judg 1:35]]). In Solomon's time it was part of the land under Ben Deker ([[@11004009|1 Kgs 4:9]]).

column5: Where Saul searched for the donkeys
column7: This is a land Saul went through looking for the lost donkeys, but he did not find them ([[@9009003-9009004|1 Sam 9:3-4]]).

column5: Son of Jahdai
column7: He appears in the family line of Judah as a son of Jahdai, named with Regem, Jothan, Geshan, Pelet, and Ephah ([[@13002047|1 Chr 2:47]]).

column5: Father of Madmannah
column7: He was the son Caleb's concubine Maacah bore after Sheber and Tirhanah, and he was the father of Madmannah ([[@13002048-13002049|1 Chr 2:48-49]]).

column5: A town in the lowland of Judah
column7: It was one of the towns in the lowland of Judah ([[@6015036|Josh 15:36]]). After David defeated Goliath, the Philistines fell dead along the way to Shaaraim ([[@9017052|1 Sam 17:52]]).

column5: Eunuch in charge of the concubines
column7: He was the eunuch who kept the concubines in King Ahasuerus's second women's house ([[@17002012|Esth 2:12]]; [[@17002014|Esth 2:14]]).

column5: A Levite who backed the opponents
column7: He was a Levite who, with Meshullam, helped Jonathan and Jahzeiah when they opposed the plan to put away the foreign wives ([[@15010015|Ezra 10:15]]).

column5: Helped the people understand the law
column7: He was one of those in Ezra's time who, with the Levites, helped the people understand the law ([[@16008007|Neh 8:7]]).

column5: Levite over the outside work of God's house
column7: A chief of the Levites, he and Jozabad had oversight of the outward business of God's house ([[@16011016|Neh 11:16]]).

column5: Benjamite who had children in Moab
column7: A descendant of Benjamin, he had children in the country of Moab after sending away his two wives, Hushim and Baara ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]; [[@13008008|1 Chr 8:8]]).

column5: A place on Issachar's border
column7: This is a place the border of the land of Issachar's descendants reached, along with Tabor and Beth Shemesh ([[@6019017|Josh 19:17]]; [[@6019022|Josh 19:22]]).

column5: Where Saul searched for the donkeys
column7: This is a land Saul went through after the hill country of Ephraim, looking for the lost donkeys ([[@9009003-9009004|1 Sam 9:3-4]]).

column5: Gate at the ascending causeway
column7: This was a gate at the causeway that goes up, where Shuppim and Hosah, assigned to the west, kept watch beside it ([[@13026016|1 Chr 26:16]]).

column5: A king of Israel who reigned one month
column7: He was the son of Jabesh who killed King Zechariah and became king ([[@12015010|2 Kgs 15:10]]). He reigned one month in Samaria and was then killed by Menahem ([[@12015013-12015014|2 Kgs 15:13-14]]).

column5: Husband of Huldah the prophetess
column7: The husband of Huldah the prophetess, he was the keeper of the wardrobe ([[@12022014|2 Kgs 22:14]]; [[@14034022|2 Chr 34:22]]).

column5: Son of Sismai, of Judah
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jerahmeel's descendants in Judah, as the son of Sismai and the father of Jekamiah ([[@13002040-13002041|1 Chr 2:40-41]]).

column5: Josiah's fourth son
column7: He was the fourth son of King Josiah, listed in the genealogy with Johanan, Jehoiakim, and Zedekiah ([[@13003015|1 Chr 3:15]]).

column5: Son of Shaul, of Simeon
column7: He appears in the family line of Simeon as a son of Shaul, and his son was Mibsam ([[@13004024-13004025|1 Chr 4:24-25]]).

column5: Son of Zadok in the high priests' line
column7: In the line of the high priests he was the son of Zadok and the father of Hilkiah ([[@13006012-13006013|1 Chr 6:12-13]]). He was one of Ezra's ancestors ([[@15007002|Ezra 7:2]]).

column5: Chief of the Korahite gatekeepers
column7: He was the son of Kore, a descendant of Korah, and the chief of the gatekeepers ([[@13009017|1 Chr 9:17]]; [[@13009019|1 Chr 9:19]]). He and his relatives guarded the gates of the tabernacle ([[@13009019|1 Chr 9:19]]).

column5: Father of Jehizkiah, a leader of Ephraim
column7: He was the father of Jehizkiah, one of the leaders of Ephraim. Jehizkiah stood up against those who came back from the war ([[@14028012|2 Chr 28:12]]).

column5: A gatekeeper who married a foreign wife
column7: He was one of the gatekeepers in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010024|Ezra 10:24]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: An Israelite who married a foreign wife
column7: He was one of the Israelites in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010042|Ezra 10:42]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Repaired the wall with his daughters
column7: The son of Hallohesh, he ruled half the district of Jerusalem and repaired the wall together with his daughters ([[@16003012|Neh 3:12]]).

column5: Repaired the spring gate
column7: The son of Colhozeh, ruler of the district of Mizpah, he repaired the spring gate and the wall of the pool of Shelah ([[@16003015|Neh 3:15]]).

column5: Uncle of Jeremiah
column7: He was Jeremiah's uncle and the father of Hanamel, who asked Jeremiah to buy his field in Anathoth ([[@24032007|Jer 32:7]]).

column5: Father of Maaseiah
column7: He was the father of Maaseiah, who had a room in the LORD's house, and he appears as "Shallum, the keeper of the threshold" ([[@24035004|Jer 35:4]]).

column5: A temple servant ancestor who returned from exile
column7: He was the ancestor of 'the children of Shamlai' among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon ([[@15002046|Ezra 2:46]]). In Nehemiah he is called 'Salmai' ([[@16007048|Neh 7:48]]).

column5: Assyrian king who attacked Samaria
column7: A king of Assyria, he attacked Hoshea king of Israel and made him pay tribute ([[@12017003|2 Kgs 17:3]]). In the seventh year of Hoshea he came up against Samaria and besieged the city ([[@12018009|2 Kgs 18:9]]).

column5: One of David's warriors, son of Hotham
column7: The son of Hotham the Aroerite, he was one of David's mighty men ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011044|1 Chr 11:44]]).

column5: The judge who killed six hundred Philistines
column7: The son of Anath, he struck six hundred Philistines with an ox goad and saved Israel ([[@7003031|Judg 3:31]]). He is also mentioned in Deborah's song ([[@7005006|Judg 5:6]]).

column5: The fifth captain, for the fifth month
column7: An Izrahite, he was the fifth captain, in charge of the fifth month, and there were twenty-four thousand in his division ([[@13027008|1 Chr 27:8]]).

column5: A town in Judah's hill country
column7: It was one of the hill-country towns that the tribe of Judah received ([[@6015020|Josh 15:20]]; [[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]).

column5: Where the judge Tola lived
column7: It was a place in the hill country of Ephraim, where the judge Tola lived and where he was buried after he died ([[@7010001-7010002|Judg 10:1-2]]).

column5: Son of Micah, of Uzziel's line
column7: A descendant of Levi, he was one of the sons of Micah the son of Uzziel ([[@13024020|1 Chr 24:20]]; [[@13024024|1 Chr 24:24]]).

column5: Son of Zophah, of Asher
column7: He was a son of Zophah of the tribe of Asher, named with Suah, Bezer, Hod, and others ([[@13007036-13007037|1 Chr 7:36-37]]).

column5: Son of Reuel, a chief of Edom
column7: He was a son of Reuel, Esau's son ([[@1036013|Gen 36:13]]). He became one of the chiefs in the land of Edom who came from Reuel ([[@1036017|Gen 36:17]]).

column5: David's warrior who held the lentil field
column7: The son of Agee the Hararite, he stood in the middle of a field of lentils and struck down the Philistines when the people fled. The LORD worked a great victory ([[@10023011-10023012|2 Sam 23:11-12]]).

column5: A Harodite, one of David's mighty men
column7: A Harodite, he appears in the list of David's mighty men ([[@10023008|2 Sam 23:8]]; [[@10023025|2 Sam 23:25]]). In 1 Chronicles he is called 'Shammoth the Harorite' ([[@13011027|1 Chr 11:27]]).

column5: A Hararite, one of David's mighty men
column7: A Hararite, his name appears in the list of David's mighty men. He is listed with Ahiam the son of Sharar the Ararite ([[@10023033|2 Sam 23:33]]).

column5: Son of Onam
column7: He was a son of Onam, the son of Jerahmeel, and he became the father of Nadab and Abishur. His brother was Jada ([[@13002026|1 Chr 2:26]]; [[@13002028|1 Chr 2:28]]; [[@13002032|1 Chr 2:32]]).

column5: Son of Rekem, father of Maon
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Caleb's descendants, as the son of Rekem and the father of Maon, the father of Beth Zur ([[@13002044-13002045|1 Chr 2:44-45]]).

column5: Son of Mered and Bithiah
column7: He was a son of Mered, one of the sons of Bithiah, the daughter of Pharaoh, whom Mered had married ([[@13004017-13004018|1 Chr 4:17-18]]).

column5: A spy from the tribe of Reuben
column7: The son of Zaccur, he was the man from the tribe of Reuben sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013002|Num 13:2]]; [[@4013004|Num 13:4]]).

column5: Son of David born in Jerusalem
column7: He was a son born to David in Jerusalem, named along with Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon ([[@10005014|2 Sam 5:14]]). In 1 Chronicles 3 his name is written 'Shimea', and he is said to be a son of Bathshua ([[@13003005|1 Chr 3:5]]).

column5: Priestly family head of Bilgah
column7: He was one of the heads of the priestly families in Joiakim's day, the head of the family of Bilgah ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012018|Neh 12:18]]).

column5: Son of Jeroham
column7: He appears in the family line of Benjamin as a son of Jeroham, named with Shehariah and Athaliah ([[@13008026-13008027|1 Chr 8:26-27]]).

column5: Second leader among the Gadites
column7: Among the descendants of Gad living in the land of Bashan, he was second after Joel the chief ([[@13005011-13005012|1 Chr 5:11-12]]).

column5: King Josiah's scribe
column7: He was the son of Azaliah, a scribe in the time of King Josiah. While the temple was being repaired, he received the book of the law that Hilkiah the high priest had found, read it, and also read it to the king ([[@12022008-12022010|2 Kgs 22:8-10]]). At the king's command he went with Hilkiah, Ahikam, and others to the prophetess Huldah to ask what the LORD wanted ([[@12022014|2 Kgs 22:14]]). His son Ahikam protected Jeremiah ([[@24026024|Jer 26:24]]), and his grandson Gedaliah was put in charge of the remaining people after Jerusalem fell ([[@12025022|2 Kgs 25:22]]).

column5: Father of Jaazaniah
column7: He was the father of Jaazaniah, who in Ezekiel's vision stood among the elders holding censers before the idols ([[@26008010-26008011|Ezek 8:10-11]]).

column5: A spy from the tribe of Simeon
column7: The son of Hori, he was the man from the tribe of Simeon sent to spy out the land of Canaan ([[@4013002|Num 13:2]]; [[@4013005|Num 13:5]]).

column5: Father of Elisha
column7: He was the father of the prophet Elisha, from Abel Meholah ([[@11019016|1 Kgs 19:16]]). Elijah threw his cloak on Elisha the son of Shaphat while he was plowing ([[@11019019|1 Kgs 19:19]]).

column5: Son of Shemaiah, in David's line
column7: He appears in the family line of David as one of the sons of Shemaiah, the son of Shecaniah ([[@13003022|1 Chr 3:22]]).

column5: A Gadite living in Bashan
column7: Among the descendants of Gad living in the land of Bashan, he is named with Janai, after Joel the chief and Shapham the second ([[@13005011-13005012|1 Chr 5:11-12]]).

column5: In charge of David's herds
column7: The son of Adlai, he was in charge of the herds in the valleys, part of King David's property ([[@13027029|1 Chr 27:29]]; [[@13027031|1 Chr 27:31]]).

column5: A place Micah prophesied against
column7: This is the place about which Micah prophesied, "Pass on, inhabitant of Shaphir, in nakedness and shame." ([[@33001011|Mic 1:11]]).

column5: A man who married a foreign wife
column7: He was one of the men in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010040|Ezra 10:40]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Father of Ahiam, one of David's mighty men
column7: An Ararite, he was the father of Ahiam, one of David's mighty men ([[@10023033|2 Sam 23:33]]). In 1 Chronicles he is called 'Sacar' ([[@13011035|1 Chr 11:35]]).

column5: Son of Sennacherib who killed him
column7: A son of Sennacherib king of Assyria, he and Adrammelech struck their father with the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat ([[@12019037|2 Kgs 19:37]]; [[@23037038|Isa 37:38]]).

column5: Sent by the people of Bethel
column7: He was sent by the people of Bethel, together with Regem Melech, to entreat the LORD's favor ([[@38007002|Zech 7:2]]).

column5: Pasture lands where Gad lived
column7: These were the pasture lands where the descendants of Gad lived, along with Gilead in Bashan and its towns, as far as their borders ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005016|1 Chr 5:16]]).

column5: Beautiful and fertile plain
column7: It was a beautiful and fertile plain, a good place for grazing herds. In David's time Shitrai the Sharonite was in charge of the herds that grazed in Sharon ([[@13027029|1 Chr 27:29]]). The Song of Songs sings, "I am a rose of Sharon," and Isaiah said that on the day of restoration the wilderness would be given "the excellence of Carmel and Sharon" ([[@22002001|Song 2:1]]; [[@23035001-23035002|Isa 35:1-2]]). When Peter healed the paralyzed Aeneas at Lydda, all who lived in Lydda and Sharon turned to the Lord ([[@44009033-44009035|Acts 9:33-35]]).

column5: Town allotted to Simeon
column7: It was one of the thirteen towns that the tribe of Simeon received by lot from within the inheritance of the children of Judah ([[@6019001|Josh 19:1]], 6).

column5: A man who married a foreign wife
column7: He was one of the men in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010040|Ezra 10:40]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A Benjamite, father of several sons
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin's descendants, and Iphdeiah and Penuel were among his sons ([[@13008014|1 Chr 8:14]]; [[@13008025|1 Chr 8:25]]).

column5: A king of Edom from Rehoboth
column7: He was from Rehoboth by the River and became king of Edom after Samlah ([[@1036037|Gen 36:37]]). When he died, Baal Hanan the son of Achbor became king ([[@1036038|Gen 36:38]]).

column5: A son of Simeon
column7: He was the son Simeon had by a Canaanite woman ([[@1046010|Gen 46:10]]; [[@2006015|Exod 6:15]]). From him came the family of the Shaulites ([[@4026013|Num 26:13]]).

column5: A Kohathite Levite
column7: A descendant of Levi's son Kohath, he was the son of Uzziah. His name appears in the line of Korah, Assir, and Elkanah ([[@13006022-13006024|1 Chr 6:22-24]]).

column5: The valley also called the King's Valley
column7: The valley of Shaveh was also called 'the King's Valley.' The king of Sodom came out there to meet Abram as he returned from defeating Chedorlaomer ([[@1014017|Gen 14:17]]).

column5: A son of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: He was one of the descendants of Bani in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010029|Ezra 10:29]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Son of Jeconiah, father of Zerubbabel
column7: He was the son of Jeconiah, the king of Judah who was taken captive, and a descendant of the house of King David ([[@13003017|1 Chr 3:17]]). Zerubbabel, who returned from exile and rebuilt the temple, is called "Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel" in many places ([[@15003002|Ezra 3:2]]). But 1 Chronicles lists Zerubbabel as the son of Pedaiah, and scholars differ on why the two accounts differ ([[@13003019|1 Chr 3:19]]). Matthew's genealogy of Jesus also says that Jeconiah became the father of Shealtiel ([[@40001012|Matt 1:12]]).

column5: Zerubbabel's father in Jesus' genealogy
column7: This name appears in Jesus' genealogy in the Gospel of Luke, in the generation before Zerubbabel and after Neri ([[@42003027|Luke 3:27]]).

column5: Son of Isaiah
column7: He was Isaiah's son, who went out with his father at the LORD's word to meet Ahaz king of Judah ([[@23007001|Isa 7:1]]; [[@23007003|Isa 7:3]]).

column5: Son of Azel, a descendant of Saul
column7: He was one of the six sons of Azel, a descendant of Saul through Jonathan ([[@13008038|1 Chr 8:38]]; [[@13009044|1 Chr 9:44]]).

column5: Grandson of Cush, son of Raamah
column7: He was the grandson of Ham's son Cush and the son of Raamah, and the brother of Dedan ([[@1010006-1010007|Gen 10:6-7]]; [[@13001009|1 Chr 1:9]]). He should not be confused with Seba, a son of Cush, whose name is similar. Ezekiel says that "The traders of Sheba and Raamah" traded with Tyre in all kinds of spices, precious stones, and gold ([[@26027022|Ezek 27:22]]). Scholars differ on whether the 'Sabeans' in Job or the queen of Sheba who visited Solomon are connected with his descendants ([[@18001015|Job 1:15]]; [[@11010001|1 Kgs 10:1]]).

column5: Son of Joktan
column7: He was one of the sons of Joktan, the son of Eber in Shem's line, and a brother of Obal and Abimael ([[@1010025|Gen 10:25]]; [[@1010028|Gen 10:28]]).

column5: Son of Jokshan, grandson of Abraham
column7: He was a son of Jokshan, whom Abraham's later wife Keturah bore to him, and a brother of Dedan ([[@1025001-1025003|Gen 25:1-3]]; [[@13001032|1 Chr 1:32]]).

column5: A Benjamite who rebelled against David
column7: He was the son of Bichri, a Benjamite, who rebelled against David after Absalom's revolt had ended. When he blew the trumpet and cried, "We have no portion in David," the men of Israel left David and followed him ([[@10020001-10020002|2 Sam 20:1-2]]). David had Abishai take the king's servants and pursue him ([[@10020006-10020007|2 Sam 20:6-7]]). Sheba fled into the city of Abel of Beth Maacah, but the people, listening to a wise woman of the city, cut off his head and threw it out to Joab ([[@10020015-10020022|2 Sam 20:15-22]]).

column5: Kingdom of the queen who visited Solomon
column7: It was a kingdom in southern Arabia, famous for spices, precious stones, and gold ([[@26027022|Ezek 27:22]]). The queen of Sheba heard of Solomon's fame and came to Jerusalem to test him with hard questions ([[@11010001|1 Kgs 10:1]]). Seeing Solomon's wisdom, she exclaimed, "not even half was told me!" and gave him a great deal of gold and spices ([[@11010007-11010010|1 Kgs 10:7-10]]). Jesus called this queen "The Queen of the South" and said, "someone greater than Solomon is here" ([[@40012042|Matt 12:42]]).

column5: A Gadite living in Bashan
column7: He was one of seven kinsmen among the descendants of Gad who lived in the land of Bashan ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005013|1 Chr 5:13]]).

column5: Priest who blew a trumpet before the ark
column7: He was one of the seven priests who blew trumpets before God's ark, named with Joshaphat, Nethanel, and others ([[@13015024|1 Chr 15:24]]).

column5: Levite who led prayer in Nehemiah's time
column7: A Levite, he stood on the stairs with other Levites and cried with a loud voice to the LORD ([[@16009004|Neh 9:4]]). His name is also among those who called on the people to stand up and bless the LORD ([[@16009005|Neh 9:5]]).

column5: Priest who sealed the covenant under Nehemiah
column7: He was one of the priests who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010004|Neh 10:4]], 8). Later, the head of 'the family of Shebaniah' was Joseph ([[@16012014|Neh 12:14]]).

column5: A Levite who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the Levites who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010009|Neh 10:9]]; [[@16010012|Neh 10:12]]).

column5: Where the men of Ai chased Israel
column7: The men of Ai chased the Israelites from the city gate to Shebarim and struck them down on the slope ([[@6007005|Josh 7:5]]).

column5: Son of Caleb's concubine Maacah
column7: He was a son born to Maacah, Caleb's concubine, and his name appears in the genealogy with Tirhanah ([[@13002048|1 Chr 2:48]]).

column5: Scribe in Hezekiah's day
column7: He was an official in King Hezekiah's time, and when the Assyrian Rabshakeh came, he went out as "Shebnah the scribe" along with Eliakim and Joah ([[@12018018|2 Kgs 18:18]]). They asked Rabshakeh to speak in the Syrian language so that the people would not understand, and later they tore their clothes and reported his words to Hezekiah ([[@12018026-12018037|2 Kgs 18:26-37]]). Hezekiah sent them, covered with sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah ([[@12019002|2 Kgs 19:2]]). Isaiah contains a prophecy that the treasurer "Shebna, who is over the house" would be thrust from his office, and scholars differ on whether he is the same man as Shebna the scribe ([[@23022015-23022019|Isa 22:15-19]]).

column5: Descendant of Gershom, keeper of the treasuries
column7: A descendant of Moses' son Gershom, he became a chief and was in charge of the treasuries ([[@13023016|1 Chr 23:16]]; [[@13026024|1 Chr 26:24]]).

column5: Son of Heman, a singer
column7: He was one of the sons of Heman ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]). He seems to be the same person as 'Shubael,' who was given the thirteenth turn in the service of praise ([[@13025020|1 Chr 25:20]]).

column5: A descendant of David's royal line
column7: He appears in the genealogy of David's royal line as the father of Shemaiah. Shemaiah had six sons ([[@13003021-13003022|1 Chr 3:21-22]]).

column5: The tenth priestly division
column7: He was the one chosen tenth when the priestly divisions were assigned by lot in David's time ([[@13024007|1 Chr 24:7]]; [[@13024011|1 Chr 24:11]]).

column5: Distributed portions in the priests' cities
column7: He was one of the men under Kore in the cities of the priests who distributed portions to their brothers by their divisions ([[@14031014-14031015|2 Chr 31:14-15]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family that came with Ezra
column7: Among those who came up from Babylon with Ezra, this family is listed as "Of the sons of Shecaniah, of the sons of Parosh" ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008003|Ezra 8:3]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family that came with Ezra
column7: Among the descendants of Shecaniah who came up from Babylon with Ezra were the son of Jahaziel and three hundred men ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008005|Ezra 8:5]]).

column5: The man who confessed the sin of foreign marriages
column7: The son of Jehiel, of the descendants of Elam, he confessed to Ezra the sin of marrying foreign women and said, "there is hope for Israel" ([[@15010002|Ezra 10:2]]).

column5: Father-in-law of Tobiah
column7: The son of Arah, he became Tobiah's father-in-law. Because of this marriage, many in Judah were bound by oath to Tobiah ([[@16006018|Neh 6:18]]).

column5: An ancient town between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim
column7: Shechem was an ancient town in the valley between Mount Ebal and Mount Gerizim. When Abram came into Canaan, the first place he reached was the oak of Moreh at Shechem ([[@1012006|Gen 12:6]]). When Jacob returned from Paddan Aram, he camped in front of the city of Shechem ([[@1033018|Gen 33:18]]). At the end of his life Joshua gathered Israel at Shechem and made a covenant ([[@6024025|Josh 24:25]]). When the kingdom was about to split, Shechem was also where Rehoboam went to be made king ([[@11012001|1 Kgs 12:1]]).

column5: Son of Hamor the Hivite, who violated Dinah
column7: He was the son of Hamor the Hivite and a prince of that land ([[@1034002|Gen 34:2]]). Jacob bought the field where he had pitched his tent for one hundred pieces of money "at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father" ([[@1033019|Gen 33:19]]). Shechem violated Jacob's daughter Dinah and then asked his father to get her for him as a wife ([[@1034002-1034004|Gen 34:2-4]]). But Dinah's brothers Simeon and Levi attacked the city and killed Hamor and Shechem with the sword ([[@1034025-1034026|Gen 34:25-26]]).

column5: Son of Gilead, of Manasseh
column7: A son of Gilead among Manasseh's descendants, he was the ancestor of the family of the Shechemites ([[@4026030-4026031|Num 26:30-31]]; [[@6017002|Josh 17:2]]).

column5: Son of Shemida, of Manasseh
column7: He appears in the family line of Manasseh as a son of Shemida, and his brothers were Ahian, Likhi, and Aniam ([[@13007014|1 Chr 7:14]]; [[@13007019|1 Chr 7:19]]).

column5: Father of Elizur, leader of the tribe of Reuben
column7: He was the father of Elizur, the leader of the children of Reuben in the wilderness ([[@4001005|Num 1:5]]). His son brought the offering on behalf of the children of Reuben on the fourth day ([[@4007030|Num 7:30]]).

column5: The Sheep Gate in Jerusalem's wall
column7: It was a gate in the wall of Jerusalem, rebuilt in Nehemiah's time by Eliashib the high priest and the priests ([[@16003001|Neh 3:1]]). At the dedication of the wall, the procession passed by here ([[@16012039|Neh 12:39]]).

column5: Ephraim's daughter who built Beth Horon
column7: She was Ephraim's daughter, who built Lower and Upper Beth Horon and Uzzen Sheerah, which bears her name ([[@13007024|1 Chr 7:24]]).

column5: Son of Jeroham
column7: He was one of the sons of Jeroham, a Benjamite, named with Shamsherai and Athaliah ([[@13008026-13008027|1 Chr 8:26-27]]).

column5: The Hebrews' basic unit of weight and money
column7: The shekel was the basic unit of weight used by the Hebrews, used when weighing out silver or gold to pay a price. Abraham weighed out four hundred shekels of silver to Ephron the Hittite and bought land to bury his wife ([[@1023016|Gen 23:16]]). The standard was the shekel of the sanctuary, and one shekel was twenty gerahs ([[@2030013|Exod 30:13]]). When the men of Israel were counted, rich and poor alike gave half a shekel to the LORD ([[@2030015|Exod 30:15]]). Scholars differ on the exact weight of a shekel.

column5: Son of Arpachshad, father of Eber
column7: He was Shem's grandson and the son of Arpachshad, and an ancestor of Abraham. Arpachshad became the father of Shelah at thirty-five ([[@1011012|Gen 11:12]]). Shelah became the father of Eber at thirty, and after that he lived four hundred three years and had other children ([[@1011014-1011015|Gen 11:14-15]]). He also appears in Luke's genealogy of Jesus, where Cainan is placed between him and Arphaxad ([[@42003035-42003036|Luke 3:35-36]]). He is a different person from Shelah the son of Judah.

column5: The third son of Judah
column7: He was the third son born to Judah by the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite ([[@1038002-1038005|Gen 38:2-5]]). After his older brothers Er and Onan died, Judah told his daughter-in-law Tamar to wait until Shelah grew up, but fearing that Shelah too might die, he did not give him to Tamar even after he was grown ([[@1038011-1038014|Gen 38:11-14]]). After that Tamar bore Perez and Zerah to Judah ([[@1038029-1038030|Gen 38:29-30]]). From Shelah came the family of the Shelanites in the tribe of Judah ([[@4026020|Num 26:20]]).

column5: Pool near the City of David in Jerusalem
column7: It is a pool mentioned when the wall of Jerusalem was repaired in Nehemiah's time. Shallun repaired "the wall of the pool of Shelah by the king’s garden," as far as the stairs going down from the City of David ([[@16003015|Neh 3:15]]). Many scholars take this pool to be the same as 'the waters of Shiloah' in Isaiah or 'the pool of Siloam' in the Gospels ([[@23008006|Isa 8:6]]). Jesus put mud on a blind man's eyes and told him to go and wash in the pool of Siloam, and he washed and came back seeing ([[@43009006-43009007|John 9:6-7]]). Some also think 'the King's Pool' that Nehemiah reached while inspecting the wall at night refers to this pool ([[@16002014|Neh 2:14]]).

column5: A man who married a foreign wife
column7: He was one of the men in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010039|Ezra 10:39]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A man who married a foreign wife
column7: He was one of the men in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010041|Ezra 10:41]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Father of Hananiah, who repaired the wall
column7: He was the father of Hananiah, who repaired a section of the wall with Hanun, the sixth son of Zalaph, in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003030|Neh 3:30]]).

column5: A priest made a treasurer
column7: He was a priest whom Nehemiah made a treasurer along with Zadok the scribe and Pedaiah the Levite, because they were counted faithful ([[@16013013|Neh 13:13]]).

column5: Grandfather of Jehudi
column7: He was the father of Nethaniah and the grandfather of Jehudi. The officials sent Jehudi to Baruch to tell him to bring the scroll ([[@24036014|Jer 36:14]]).

column5: Ordered to arrest Jeremiah
column7: The son of Abdeel, he was ordered by the king, along with Seraiah and others, to arrest Baruch and Jeremiah ([[@24036026|Jer 36:26]]).

column5: Father of Jehucal
column7: He was the father of Jehucal, whom King Zedekiah sent to Jeremiah ([[@24037003|Jer 37:3]]). Elsewhere he appears in the phrase 'Jucal the son of Shelemiah' ([[@24038001|Jer 38:1]]).

column5: Father of Irijah
column7: The son of Hananiah, he was the father of Irijah, the captain of the guard who seized the prophet Jeremiah at Benjamin's gate ([[@24037013|Jer 37:13]]).

column5: Son of Joktan
column7: He was one of the sons of Joktan, the son of Eber in Shem's line, and a brother of Almodad and Hazarmaveth ([[@1010025-1010026|Gen 10:25-26]]; [[@13001020|1 Chr 1:20]]).

column5: Son of Helem, of Asher
column7: He was a son of Helem of the tribe of Asher, named with Zophah, Imna, and Amal ([[@13007035|1 Chr 7:35]]; [[@13007040|1 Chr 7:40]]).

column5: Father of Ahihud, leader of Asher
column7: He was the father of Ahihud, the leader of the tribe of Asher chosen to help divide the land ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034027|Num 34:27]]).

column5: Mother of the man who blasphemed the Name
column7: The daughter of Dibri of the tribe of Dan, she was the mother of the man who blasphemed the name of the LORD. Her son's father was an Egyptian ([[@3024010-3024011|Lev 24:10-11]]).

column5: A member of Zerubbabel's family
column7: In the genealogy of Zerubbabel's descendants she is listed after Meshullam and Hananiah: "Shelomith was their sister" ([[@13003019|1 Chr 3:19]]).

column5: Son of Izhar, a family head
column7: He was a son of Izhar, the son of Kohath the Levite, and he was a head of his family ([[@13023012|1 Chr 23:12]]; [[@13023018|1 Chr 23:18]]).

column5: Child of Rehoboam and Maacah
column7: This was one of the children Rehoboam had by Maacah, the daughter of Absalom ([[@14011020|2 Chr 11:20]]).

column5: A family that came up with Ezra
column7: Among those who came up from Babylon with Ezra is listed "Of the sons of Shelomith, the son of Josiphiah; and with him one hundred sixty males." ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008010|Ezra 8:10]]).

column5: Son of Shimei, of the Gershonites
column7: A son of Shimei of the Levite family of Gershon, he was one of the heads of the families of Ladan ([[@13023007|1 Chr 23:7]]; [[@13023009|1 Chr 23:9]]).

column5: Levite in charge of the dedicated treasuries
column7: A descendant of the Levite Eliezer, he was the son of Zichri ([[@13026025|1 Chr 26:25]]). He and his brothers were in charge of the treasuries of the holy things that David and the leaders had dedicated ([[@13026026|1 Chr 26:26]]).

column5: Leader of the tribe of Simeon in the wilderness
column7: He was the son of Zurishaddai and the leader of the children of Simeon in the wilderness ([[@4001006|Num 1:6]]; [[@4002012|Num 2:12]]). On the fifth day he brought the offering on behalf of the children of Simeon ([[@4007036|Num 7:36]]).

column5: Son of Noah, ancestor of the Semites
column7: He was one of Noah's three sons, and he went into the ship with Ham and Japheth and survived the flood ([[@1007013|Gen 7:13]]). When his father Noah lay drunk in his tent, he and Japheth went in backwards and covered their father's nakedness ([[@1009023|Gen 9:23]]). Noah blessed him, saying, "Blessed be the LORD, the God of Shem" ([[@1009026|Gen 9:26]]). Shem became the ancestor of all the children of Eber, and his family line leads down to Abram ([[@1011010-1011026|Gen 11:10-26]]).

column5: A southern town of Judah
column7: It was one of the southern towns that the tribe of Judah received ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015026|Josh 15:26]]).

column5: Son of Hebron, father of Raham
column7: He was one of the sons of Hebron among Caleb's descendants, and the father of Raham. Raham was the father of Jorkeam ([[@13002043-13002044|1 Chr 2:43-44]]).

column5: Grandfather of Bela, of Reuben
column7: He appears in the family line of Reuben as the grandfather of Bela. Bela lived in Aroer, and his land reached as far as Nebo and Baal Meon ([[@13005008|1 Chr 5:8]]).

column5: Head of the people of Aijalon
column7: A descendant of Benjamin, he and Beriah were heads of the families of Aijalon and drove out the people of Gath ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]; [[@13008013|1 Chr 8:13]]).

column5: Stood at Ezra's right hand
column7: He was one of the men who stood at Ezra's right hand as Ezra stood on a wooden pulpit and read the law ([[@16008003-16008004|Neh 8:3-4]]).

column5: Father of two sons who helped David
column7: A man of Gibeah, his two sons Ahiezer and Joash came to David at Ziklag and helped him in battle ([[@13012001|1 Chr 12:1]]; [[@13012003|1 Chr 12:3]]).

column5: A man of God in Rehoboam's time
column7: He was a man of God who received the word of God in Rehoboam's time ([[@11012022|1 Kgs 12:22]]). When Shishak invaded, he delivered the message, "You have forsaken me, therefore I have also left you" ([[@14012005|2 Chr 12:5]]).

column5: Ancestor of Ziza, a Simeonite leader
