column7: He appears as an ancestor in the family line of Ziza, a Simeonite leader; Ziza was a fifth-generation descendant of Shemaiah ([[@13004037-13004038|1 Chr 4:37-38]]).

column5: Son of Joel, of Reuben
column7: He appears in the family line of Reuben as a son of Joel, and his son was Gog ([[@13005003-13005004|1 Chr 5:3-4]]).

column5: A Merarite in Jerusalem after the exile
column7: A Levite of the descendants of Merari, he lived in Jerusalem after the exile and was the son of Hasshub ([[@13009014|1 Chr 9:14]]; [[@16011015|Neh 11:15]]).

column5: Descendant of Jeduthun, father of Obadiah
column7: The grandson of Jeduthun and son of Galal, he was the father of Obadiah, a Levite who returned after the exile ([[@13009016|1 Chr 9:16]]).

column5: Chief of the descendants of Elizaphan
column7: The chief of the descendants of Elizaphan, he led two hundred of his relatives and was one of the Levites David called when the ark was moved ([[@13015008|1 Chr 15:8]]; [[@13015011|1 Chr 15:11]]).

column5: Scribe who recorded the priestly divisions
column7: The son of Nethanel, he was a Levite scribe who wrote down the names of the priestly families in the presence of the king and the officials ([[@13024006|1 Chr 24:6]]).

column5: Firstborn of Obed-Edom, a gatekeeper
column7: He was the firstborn son of Obed-Edom ([[@13026004|1 Chr 26:4]]). His sons ruled over their father's house and were mighty men of valor ([[@13026006-13026007|1 Chr 26:6-7]]).

column5: A Levite sent out by Jehoshaphat
column7: He was one of the Levites Jehoshaphat sent to the towns of Judah to teach the people from the book of the LORD's law ([[@14017008-14017009|2 Chr 17:8-9]]).

column5: A Levite descended from Jeduthun
column7: He was a descendant of Jeduthun among the Levites who arose in Hezekiah's time ([[@14029012|2 Chr 29:12]]; [[@14029014|2 Chr 29:14]]).

column5: Distributed portions in the priests' cities
column7: He was one of the men under Kore in the cities of the priests who distributed portions to their brothers by their divisions ([[@14031014-14031015|2 Chr 31:14-15]]).

column5: Levite chief who gave Passover offerings
column7: A brother of Conaniah, a chief of the Levites, he gave the Levites sheep and cattle for the Passover offerings ([[@14035009|2 Chr 35:9]]).

column5: A son of Adonikam who came with Ezra
column7: He was one of the descendants of Adonikam who came up from Babylon with Ezra ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008013|Ezra 8:13]]).

column5: A leader Ezra sent for
column7: He was one of the leaders Ezra sent for when he found that there were no Levites among the people ([[@15008015-15008016|Ezra 8:15-16]]).

column5: A priest who married a foreign wife
column7: He was a descendant of Harim among the priests and had married a foreign woman ([[@15010018|Ezra 10:18]]; [[@15010021|Ezra 10:21]]).

column5: A son of Harim who married a foreign wife
column7: A descendant of Harim, he was one of those in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010031|Ezra 10:31]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Son of the east gatekeeper; repaired the wall
column7: The son of Shecaniah, the keeper of the east gate, he repaired a section of the wall in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003029|Neh 3:29]]).

column5: Tried to trap Nehemiah
column7: The son of Delaiah, he urged Nehemiah to hide inside the temple of God. He said this because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him ([[@16006010|Neh 6:10]]; [[@16006012|Neh 6:12]]).

column5: A priest who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the priests who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010008|Neh 10:8]]). The same name also appears in the list of priests who returned with Zerubbabel ([[@16012006|Neh 12:6]]).

column5: Ancestor of Zechariah the trumpeter
column7: He was the grandfather of Zechariah, a priest's son who held a trumpet at the dedication of Jerusalem's wall, and the father of Jonathan ([[@16012027|Neh 12:27]]; [[@16012035|Neh 12:35]]).

column5: Played David's instruments
column7: A brother of Zechariah, he was one of those who played the musical instruments of David the man of God ([[@16012035-16012036|Neh 12:35-36]]).

column5: Stood with the thanksgiving choirs
column7: He was one of those who stood in God's house with the thanksgiving choirs at the dedication of the wall ([[@16012040|Neh 12:40]]; [[@16012042|Neh 12:42]]).

column5: Father of Uriah
column7: A man of Kiriath Jearim, he was the father of Uriah, who prophesied just as Jeremiah did ([[@24026020|Jer 26:20]]).

column5: Shemaiah the Nehelamite, a false prophet
column7: A Nehelamite, he prophesied to the captives though the LORD had not sent him, and made them trust in a lie. The LORD said he would punish him and his offspring ([[@24029031-24029032|Jer 29:31-32]]).

column5: Father of the official Delaiah
column7: He was the father of Delaiah, an official who sat in the scribe's room with Elishama the scribe and others ([[@24036012|Jer 36:12]]).

column5: A Benjamite who helped David at Ziklag
column7: He was one of the Benjamite warriors who came to David at Ziklag and helped him in battle ([[@13012001-13012002|1 Chr 12:1-2]]; [[@13012005|1 Chr 12:5]]).

column5: Son of Rehoboam
column7: He was a son Rehoboam had by Mahalath, the daughter of David's son Jerimoth, and his brothers were Jeush and Zaham ([[@14011018-14011019|2 Chr 11:18-19]]).

column5: A son of Harim who married a foreign wife
column7: A descendant of Harim, he was one of those in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010031-15010032|Ezra 10:31-32]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A man who married a foreign wife
column7: He was one of the men in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010041|Ezra 10:41]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: King of Zeboiim
column7: He was king of Zeboiim, who fought with Bera king of Sodom and others against Chedorlaomer king of Elam and his allied kings ([[@1014001-1014002|Gen 14:1-2]]).

column5: Builder of Ono and Lod
column7: The son of Elpaal, he was a brother of Eber and Misham. He built Ono and Lod with their towns ([[@13008012|1 Chr 8:12]]).

column5: Father of Bani, of Merari's line
column7: He appears as the father of Bani in the family line of Ethan, a descendant of Merari who served on the left hand ([[@13006044|1 Chr 6:44]]; [[@13006046|1 Chr 6:46]]).

column5: Son of Gilead, ancestor of the Shemidaites
column7: A descendant of Gilead, Manasseh's grandson, he was the ancestor of the family of the Shemidaites ([[@4026029-4026032|Num 26:29-32]]). When the descendants of Manasseh received their inheritance by lot according to their families, the descendants of Shemida also received a share ([[@6017002|Josh 17:2]]).

column5: Levite who played strings in David's time
column7: He was a Levite whom David appointed in the rank next to the singers when the ark of the covenant was brought up ([[@13015018|1 Chr 15:18]]). He was given the task of playing stringed instruments set to Alamoth ([[@13015020|1 Chr 15:20]]).

column5: A Levite sent out by Jehoshaphat
column7: He was one of the Levites Jehoshaphat sent to the towns of Judah to teach the people from the book of the LORD's law ([[@14017008-14017009|2 Chr 17:8-9]]).

column5: Simeonite leader who helped divide the land
column7: The son of Ammihud, he was the leader of the tribe of Simeon chosen to help divide the land ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034020|Num 34:20]]).

column5: Son of Tola, of Issachar
column7: He was a son of Tola, the son of Issachar, and a head of his father Tola's house ([[@13007001-13007002|1 Chr 7:1-2]]).

column5: Where the Ebenezer stone was set up
column7: Samuel set up a stone between Mizpah and Shen and named it Ebenezer ([[@9007012|1 Sam 7:12]]).

column5: Son of Jeconiah
column7: He was one of the sons of Jeconiah the captive, named with Shealtiel, Malchiram, Pedaiah, and others ([[@13003017-13003018|1 Chr 3:17-18]]).

column5: The place where the dead were said to go
column7: In the Old Testament, this is the place where the dead are said to go down; its Hebrew name is 'Sheol'. Thinking Joseph was dead, Jacob mourned and said, "I will go down to Sheol to my son" ([[@1037035|Gen 37:35]]). Those who rebelled against Moses went down alive into Sheol when the earth opened its mouth ([[@4016033|Num 16:33]]). The psalmist confessed, "you will not leave my soul in Sheol", and Peter preached that this word came true in Jesus' resurrection ([[@19016010|Ps 16:10]]; [[@44002027|Acts 2:27]]).

column5: A place on the eastern border of the promised land
column7: It was a place on the eastern border of the promised land. The border ran from Hazar Enan to Shepham, and went down from Shepham to Riblah ([[@4034010-4034011|Num 34:10-11]]).

column5: Son of David and Abital
column7: He was the fifth son born to David in Hebron, and his mother was Abital ([[@10003004|2 Sam 3:4]]; [[@13003003|1 Chr 3:3]]).

column5: Father of Meshullam
column7: The son of Reuel and the father of Meshullam, he appears in the family line of the Benjamites who lived in Jerusalem ([[@13009003|1 Chr 9:3]]; [[@13009008|1 Chr 9:8]]).

column5: Haruphite who helped David at Ziklag
column7: A Haruphite, he was one of the Benjamite warriors who came to David at Ziklag and helped him in battle ([[@13012001-13012002|1 Chr 12:1-2]]; [[@13012005|1 Chr 12:5]]).

column5: Ruler of the Simeonites under David
column7: The son of Maacah, he was the ruler over the Simeonites among those in charge of the tribes of Israel in David's time ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]).

column5: Son of King Jehoshaphat of Judah
column7: He was one of the sons of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, named as a brother of Jehoram ([[@14021002|2 Chr 21:2]]).

column5: Ancestor of a family that returned from exile
column7: Among the people who returned from exile in Babylon, 'the children of Shephatiah' numbered three hundred seventy-two ([[@15002004|Ezra 2:4]]). In Ezra's time, too, one of his descendants, Zebadiah the son of Michael, came up with eighty males ([[@15008008|Ezra 8:8]]).

column5: A descendant of Solomon's servants
column7: He was the ancestor of 'the children of Shephatiah' among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from exile in Babylon ([[@15002055|Ezra 2:55]]; [[@15002057|Ezra 2:57]]).

column5: Ancestor of Athaiah, of Judah
column7: He appears in the family line of Athaiah, a descendant of Judah who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile. Athaiah was Shephatiah's great-great-grandson ([[@16011004|Neh 11:4]]).

column5: Official who sought Jeremiah's death
column7: The son of Mattan, he heard what Jeremiah was saying to the people and, with the other officials, told the king that Jeremiah should be put to death ([[@24038001|Jer 38:1]]; [[@24038004|Jer 38:4]]).

column5: Low hills between Judah's hill country and the coast
column7: It is the low hill country between the hill country of Judah and the coastal plain to the west, called 'the lowland' in the Bible. When the Bible describes the land of Canaan, it names this lowland separately, alongside the hill country, the South, and the Arabah ([[@5001007|Deut 1:7]]; [[@6010040|Josh 10:40]]). In the lowland that the tribe of Judah received were towns such as Eshtaol and Zorah ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]). Jeremiah prophesied that after the return from exile, people would again buy fields and sign deeds in the cities of the lowland too ([[@24032044|Jer 32:44]]).

column5: A camp in the wilderness
column7: In the wilderness the Israelites left Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher, then left there and camped at Haradah ([[@4033023-4033024|Num 33:23-24]]).

column5: One who feeds and guards a flock of sheep
column7: A shepherd is someone who feeds and guards a flock of sheep. Jacob's sons told Pharaoh that they had been shepherds since their fathers' time, and David also kept the sheep in the fields when he was young ([[@1047003|Gen 47:3]]; [[@9016011|1 Sam 16:11]]). The Bible pictures God as a shepherd who cares for his people, and David sang, "The LORD is my shepherd; I shall lack nothing" ([[@19023001|Ps 23:1]]). Jesus said, "I am the good shepherd", and he said that the good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep ([[@43010011|John 10:11]]).

column5: Son of Shobal the Horite
column7: He was a son of Shobal, a chief of the Horites descended from Seir ([[@1036020|Gen 36:20]]; [[@1036023|Gen 36:23]]; [[@1036029|Gen 36:29]]). In 1 Chronicles his name is written 'Shephi' ([[@13001040|1 Chr 1:40]]).

column5: A Levite who came with Ezra
column7: He was a Levite brought along with his sons and brothers, eighteen in all, when Ezra was looking for Levites ([[@15008018|Ezra 8:18]]). Together with the other Levites he helped the people understand the law ([[@16008007|Neh 8:7]]).

column5: Levite who sealed the covenant
column7: He was one of the Levites who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010012|Neh 10:12]]). As a chief of the Levites, he stood facing his brothers and praised God as David had commanded ([[@16012024|Neh 12:24]]).

column5: Son of Maacah, wife of Machir
column7: He was a son borne by Maacah, the wife of Machir, and the brother of Peresh. His sons were Ulam and Rakem ([[@13007016|1 Chr 7:16]]).

column5: Descendant of Anak living in Hebron
column7: He was one of the descendants of Anak that the spies saw in Hebron ([[@4013022|Num 13:22]]). Caleb drove him out of the land, and Judah attacked Hebron and struck him down ([[@6015014|Josh 15:14]]; [[@7001010|Judg 1:10]]).

column5: Gave his daughter to his Egyptian servant Jarha
column7: He had no sons, only daughters, so he gave his daughter as wife to Jarha, his Egyptian servant, and she bore Attai ([[@13002034-13002035|1 Chr 2:34-35]]).

column5: One of King Ahasuerus's seven princes
column7: He was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who were close to King Ahasuerus and sat first in the kingdom ([[@17001014|Esth 1:14]]).

column5: A Persian official who questioned the temple building
column7: He came with Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, and asked who had ordered them to build the temple ([[@15005003|Ezra 5:3]]). They reported this matter in a letter to King Darius ([[@15005006|Ezra 5:6]]).

column5: Son of Caleb's concubine Maacah
column7: He was a son borne by Maacah, Caleb's concubine, and is named as the father of Machbena and Gibea ([[@13002048-13002049|1 Chr 2:48-49]]).

column5: Western border of Asher's land
column7: This place appears on the border of the land the tribe of Asher received. The western border reached to Carmel and Shihorlibnath ([[@6019024|Josh 19:24]]; [[@6019026|Josh 19:26]]).

column5: A town on Judah's northern border
column7: This place appears on the border of the land of the tribe of Judah. The border went out to the north side of Ekron, reached Shikkeron, and passed along to Mount Baalah ([[@6015011|Josh 15:11]]).

column5: Maternal grandfather of King Jehoshaphat
column7: He was the father of Azubah, the mother of Jehoshaphat king of Judah ([[@11022042|1 Kgs 22:42]]; [[@14020031|2 Chr 20:31]]). His name appears only in these two verses, together with his daughter Azubah.

column5: Son of Naphtali
column7: He was the fourth son of Naphtali ([[@1046024|Gen 46:24]]). The family of the Shillemites came from him ([[@4026049|Num 26:49]]).

column5: A name in Jacob's blessing of Judah
column7: When Jacob blessed his son Judah, he said the scepter would not depart from Judah "until he comes to whom it belongs. The obedience of the peoples will be to him." ([[@1049010|Gen 49:10]]).

column5: The Ephraim town where the Tent of Meeting stood
column7: Shiloh was a town north of Bethel. After the land of Canaan was taken, the whole congregation of Israel gathered here and set up the Tent of Meeting, and Joshua cast lots here to divide the land among the remaining tribes ([[@6018001-6018010|Josh 18:1-10]]). Throughout the time of the judges it was the center of Israel's worship, and it was where young Samuel served the LORD under Eli and received his word ([[@9003021|1 Sam 3:21]]). Later God warned his people to remember what he had done to Shiloh because of their wickedness ([[@24007012|Jer 7:12]]).

column5: Ancestor of Maaseiah in Jerusalem
column7: This name appears at the very top of the family line of Maaseiah, a descendant of Judah who lived in Jerusalem after the exile. Maaseiah was a seventh-generation descendant of the Shilonite ([[@16011005|Neh 11:5]]).

column5: Son of Zophah, of Asher
column7: He was one of the sons of Zophah, the son of Helem, in the family line of Asher, named with Suah, Harnepher, and others ([[@13007035-13007037|1 Chr 7:35-37]]).

column5: Son of Uzzah, of Merari's line
column7: He appears in the family line of Merari as a son of Uzzah. His son was Haggiah, and Haggiah's son was Asaiah ([[@13006029-13006030|1 Chr 6:29-30]]).

column5: Grandfather of Asaph the singer
column7: He was an ancestor of Asaph, whom David put in charge of the singing; Asaph's father Berechiah was the son of Shimea. Shimea was the son of Michael ([[@13006031|1 Chr 6:31]]; [[@13006039-13006040|1 Chr 6:39-40]]).

column5: David's brother, Jesse's third son
column7: He was Jesse's third son and David's older brother ([[@13002013|1 Chr 2:13]]). In 1 Samuel he appears under the name Shammah: he passed before Samuel when Samuel was looking for the one to anoint but was not chosen, and later he went with his brothers to follow Saul into battle against the Philistines ([[@9016009|1 Sam 16:9]]; [[@9017013|1 Sam 17:13]]). His son Jonadab was Amnon's friend and "a very subtle man" ([[@10013003|2 Sam 13:3]]), and another son, Jonathan, killed the giant at Gath who had six fingers and six toes ([[@10021020-10021021|2 Sam 21:20-21]]).

column5: Son of Mikloth, a Benjamite
column7: He was the son of Mikloth in Benjamin's genealogy and lived in Jerusalem with his relatives ([[@13008032|1 Chr 8:32]]). In 1 Chronicles 9 his name is written 'Shimeam' ([[@13009038|1 Chr 9:38]]).

column5: Mother of the servant who killed King Joash
column7: She was the mother of Jozacar, the servant who struck down Joash king of Judah ([[@12012021|2 Kgs 12:21]]). 2 Chronicles calls her 'Shimeath the Ammonitess' and gives her son's name as 'Zabad' ([[@14024026|2 Chr 24:26]]).

column5: Son of Gershon, grandson of Levi
column7: He was the son of Gershon the son of Levi, and the brother of Libni ([[@2006016-2006017|Exod 6:16-17]]). From him came the family of the Shimeites, one of the Gershonite families ([[@4003021|Num 3:21]]). In the wilderness the Gershonite families camped behind the tabernacle on the west side and were in charge of things such as the tabernacle, the tent, its covering, and the screen for the door of the Tent of Meeting ([[@4003023-4003026|Num 3:23-26]]). Zechariah prophesied that when the land mourns, every family apart, there will also be "the family of the Shimeites apart" ([[@38012012-38012013|Zech 12:12-13]]).

column5: Benjamite of Saul's family who cursed David
column7: The son of Gera, he belonged to the family of Saul's house ([[@10016005|2 Sam 16:5]]). When David reached Bahurim fleeing from Absalom, Shimei cursed him, calling him "you man of blood, and wicked fellow", and threw stones, but David let him be ([[@10016007-10016011|2 Sam 16:7-11]]). When the revolt was over and David was crossing the Jordan to return, Shimei hurried down, fell before him, and begged forgiveness, and David swore not to put him to death ([[@10019018-10019023|2 Sam 19:18-23]]). Solomon ordered him not to leave Jerusalem, and when three years later he went to Gath to bring back his runaway servants, Solomon had Benaiah put him to death ([[@11002036-11002046|1 Kgs 2:36-46]]).

column5: A man who did not side with Adonijah
column7: He was one of those who did not side with Adonijah when Adonijah tried to make himself king near the end of David's life ([[@11001008|1 Kgs 1:8]]). Some identify him with Shimei the son of Ela, who was in charge of the district of Benjamin under Solomon ([[@11004018|1 Kgs 4:18]]).

column5: Son of Pedaiah, with Zerubbabel
column7: He was a son of Pedaiah, the son of Jeconiah the captive, and his name appears with Zerubbabel ([[@13003017-13003019|1 Chr 3:17-19]]).

column5: Son of Zaccur, of Simeon
column7: A descendant of Mishma of the tribe of Simeon, he was the son of Zaccur ([[@13004024-13004026|1 Chr 4:24-26]]). He had sixteen sons and six daughters ([[@13004027|1 Chr 4:27]]).

column5: Son of Gog, in Reuben's line
column7: He appears in the genealogy of the descendants of Reuben, Israel's firstborn, as the son of Gog, a descendant of Joel ([[@13005003-13005004|1 Chr 5:3-4]]).

column5: Son of Libni, of Merari's line
column7: He appears in the family line of Merari the son of Levi as a son of Libni. His son was Uzzah ([[@13006016|1 Chr 6:16]]; [[@13006029|1 Chr 6:29]]).

column5: A Levite of Ladan's family in David's time
column7: He appears in the genealogy of the family of Ladan, a Gershonite Levite, in David's time ([[@13023007-13023009|1 Chr 23:7-9]]). His three sons, Shelomoth, Haziel, and Haran, were the heads of Ladan's households ([[@13023009|1 Chr 23:9]]).

column5: Father of Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath
column7: He appears in the family line of Benjamin, and Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath were his sons ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]; [[@13008021|1 Chr 8:21]]).

column5: Ramathite over King David's vineyards
column7: A Ramathite, he was in charge of the vineyards among those who managed King David's property ([[@13027027|1 Chr 27:27]]; [[@13027031|1 Chr 27:31]]).

column5: Levite who cleansed the temple under Hezekiah
column7: A descendant of Heman, he was a Levite who rose up in King Hezekiah's time, sanctified himself with his brothers, and cleansed the LORD's house ([[@14029014-14029015|2 Chr 29:14-15]]).

column5: A Levite in charge of offerings under Hezekiah
column7: He was the brother of Conaniah the Levite in King Hezekiah's time. Together with his brother Conaniah he was in charge of the offerings and tithes brought into the temple ([[@14031012-14031013|2 Chr 31:12-13]]).

column5: A Levite who married a foreign wife
column7: His name appears as a Levite among those in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010023|Ezra 10:23]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A son of Hashum who married a foreign wife
column7: His name appears as a descendant of Hashum among those in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010033|Ezra 10:33]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A man who married a foreign wife
column7: His name appears with Bani and Binnui in the list of those in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010038|Ezra 10:38]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A Benjamite ancestor of Mordecai
column7: He was a Benjamite who appears in Mordecai's family line. Mordecai was "the son of Jair, the son of Shimei" ([[@17002005|Esth 2:5]]).

column5: A son of Harim who married a foreign wife
column7: His name appears as a descendant of Harim among those in Ezra's time who had married foreign women ([[@15010031|Ezra 10:31]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Shimon in the family line of Judah
column7: He appears in the family line of Judah, and Amnon, Rinnah, Ben Hanan, and Tilon were his sons ([[@13004020|1 Chr 4:20]]).

column5: Son of Shimei, of Benjamin
column7: He appears in the family line of Benjamin, named with Adaiah and Beraiah as a son of Shimei ([[@13008001|1 Chr 8:1]]; [[@13008021|1 Chr 8:21]]).

column5: Ancestor of Ziza, of Simeon
column7: He appears in the family line of Ziza, one of the leaders of the descendants of Simeon. Ziza was Shimri's great-great-grandson ([[@13004037-13004038|1 Chr 4:37-38]]).

column5: Father of Jediael, one of David's warriors
column7: His name appears as the father of Jediael, one of the mighty men of David's armies ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011045|1 Chr 11:45]]).

column5: Gatekeeper, son of Hosah of Merari
column7: He was a son of Hosah of the descendants of Merari. He was not the firstborn, but his father made him chief ([[@13026010|1 Chr 26:10]]).

column5: Levite who cleansed the temple under Hezekiah
column7: A descendant of Elizaphan, he was one of the Levites who cleansed the LORD's house in King Hezekiah's time ([[@14029013|2 Chr 29:13]]; [[@14029015|2 Chr 29:15]]).

column5: Son of Issachar
column7: He was the fourth son of Issachar ([[@1046013|Gen 46:13]]). The family of the Shimronites came from him ([[@4026024|Num 26:24]]).

column5: Canaanite town in the land of Zebulun
column7: The king of Shimron was among the Canaanite kings who came out with Jabin king of Hazor to fight Israel ([[@6011001|Josh 11:1]]). This town later became part of the inheritance of the tribe of Zebulun ([[@6019015|Josh 19:15]]).

column5: The scribe who accused the people of Jerusalem
column7: He was a scribe who, with Rehum the official, sent a letter to King Artaxerxes accusing the people of Jerusalem ([[@15004008|Ezra 4:8]]). The king sent them a reply ([[@15004017|Ezra 4:17]]).

column5: King of Admah in Abraham's day
column7: He was king of Admah in Abraham's time, one of the kings who fought against Chedorlaomer along with Bera king of Sodom and others ([[@1014001-1014002|Gen 14:1-2]]).

column5: A city allotted to Issachar
column7: It was one of the cities in the land the tribe of Issachar received by lot ([[@6019017|Josh 19:17]]; [[@6019019|Josh 19:19]]).

column5: Father of Ziza, of Simeon
column7: He was the father of Ziza, one of the leaders of the descendants of Simeon, and the son of Allon ([[@13004037-13004038|1 Chr 4:37-38]]).

column5: Zabdi, over David's wine cellars
column7: Among those who managed King David's property, Zabdi, who was in charge of the produce of the vineyards for the wine cellars, was a Shiphmite ([[@13027027|1 Chr 27:27]]).

column5: Hebrew midwife who feared God
column7: She was a Hebrew midwife whom the king of Egypt ordered to kill the baby boys. The midwives feared God, disobeyed the king's command, and saved the boys alive ([[@2001015-2001017|Exod 1:15-17]]).

column5: Father of Kemuel, leader of Ephraim
column7: He was the father of Kemuel, the leader of the tribe of Ephraim chosen when the land of Canaan was divided ([[@4034018|Num 34:18]]; [[@4034024|Num 34:24]]).

column5: The Egyptian king who attacked Judah under Rehoboam
column7: He was the king of Egypt to whom Jeroboam fled from Solomon ([[@11011040|1 Kgs 11:40]]). In the fifth year of King Rehoboam he attacked Jerusalem and took away the treasures of the temple and the king's palace ([[@11014025-11014026|1 Kgs 14:25-26]]).

column5: Sharonite over David's herds
column7: A Sharonite, he was in charge of the herds that grazed in Sharon, part of King David's property ([[@13027029|1 Chr 27:29]]; [[@13027031|1 Chr 27:31]]).

column5: The last camp before crossing the Jordan
column7: It was where Israel stayed and committed sexual immorality with the women of Moab ([[@4025001|Num 25:1]]). From here Joshua sent two spies to Jericho ([[@6002001|Josh 2:1]]).

column5: A valley in Joel's prophecy
column7: This is the valley that, in Joel's prophecy, a fountain flowing out of the LORD's house will water in that day ([[@29003018|Joel 3:18]]).

column5: Father of Adina, one of David's warriors
column7: A Reubenite, he was the father of Adina, a chief of the Reubenites and one of David's mighty men ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011042|1 Chr 11:42]]).

column5: A people in Ezekiel's prophecy
column7: This is a people named in Ezekiel's prophecy together with the Babylonians, the Chaldeans, Pekod, and Koa ([[@26023023|Ezek 23:23]]).

column5: Son of David born in Jerusalem
column7: He was a son born to David in Jerusalem ([[@10005014|2 Sam 5:14]]). The book of 1 Chronicles says his mother was Bathshua the daughter of Ammiel ([[@13003005|1 Chr 3:5]]).

column5: Son of Caleb the son of Hezron
column7: He was one of the sons Caleb the son of Hezron had by his wife Azubah and by Jerioth ([[@13002018|1 Chr 2:18]]).

column5: Commander of Hadadezer's army
column7: He was the commander of Hadadezer's army who came leading the Syrians from beyond the River ([[@10010016|2 Sam 10:16]]). David struck him, and he died there ([[@10010018|2 Sam 10:18]]).

column5: A gatekeeper family that returned from exile
column7: Among the gatekeepers who returned from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Shobai' ([[@15002042|Ezra 2:42]]; [[@16007045|Neh 7:45]]).

column5: A Horite chief among the sons of Seir
column7: He was a son of Seir the Horite, who lived in that land ([[@1036020|Gen 36:20]]). He was one of the chiefs of the Horites ([[@1036029|Gen 36:29]]).

column5: Son of Hur, father of Kiriath Jearim
column7: He was a son of Hur, a descendant of Judah, called 'the father of Kiriath Jearim' ([[@13002050|1 Chr 2:50]]). Among his descendants were Haroeh and half of the Menuhoth ([[@13002052|1 Chr 2:52]]).

column5: Sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's day
column7: His name appears among the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010024|Neh 10:24]]).

column5: Ammonite who helped David at Mahanaim
column7: He was the son of Nahash of Rabbah of the Ammonites. When David came to Mahanaim, he brought beds, grain, and other supplies along with Machir and Barzillai ([[@10017027-10017029|2 Sam 17:27-29]]).

column5: Son of Jaaziah, of Merari's line
column7: His name appears in the family line of Merari as one of those descended through Jaaziah ([[@13024027|1 Chr 24:27]]).

column5: Mother of Jehozabad, who killed King Joash
column7: Jehozabad, the servant who struck down Joash king of Judah, was the son of Shomer ([[@12012021|2 Kgs 12:21]]). In 2 Chronicles she appears as "Shimrith the Moabitess" ([[@14024026|2 Chr 24:26]]).

column5: Son of Heber, of Asher
column7: He was a son of Heber, of Asher's descendants ([[@13007031-13007032|1 Chr 7:31-32]]). His sons were Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram ([[@13007034|1 Chr 7:34]]).

column5: Bread always set out in the holy place
column7: The showbread was the bread always set out before God on the table in the holy place ([[@2025030|Exod 25:30]]). Twelve loaves were baked from fine flour and laid in two rows of six, and they were set out fresh every Sabbath. The bread that was taken away was eaten by Aaron and his sons in a holy place ([[@3024005-3024009|Lev 24:5-9]]). When David was fleeing from Saul, the priest gave him the showbread, and Jesus used this story to teach the Pharisees the true meaning of the Sabbath ([[@9021006|1 Sam 21:6]]; [[@40012003-40012004|Matt 12:3-4]]).

column5: Judah's Canaanite father-in-law
column7: He was a Canaanite whose daughter Judah took as his wife ([[@1038002|Gen 38:2]]). That daughter bore Judah three sons: Er, Onan, and Shelah ([[@13002003|1 Chr 2:3]]).

column5: Daughter of Heber, of Asher
column7: She was one of the children of Heber of the tribe of Asher, named as the sister of Japhlet, Shomer, and Hotham ([[@13007032|1 Chr 7:32]]).

column5: Son of Abraham and Keturah
column7: He is named last among the six sons Abraham had by Keturah ([[@1025001-1025002|Gen 25:1-2]]; [[@13001032|1 Chr 1:32]]).

column5: Land reached by Philistine raiders
column7: In Saul's time, one company of raiders from the Philistine camp took the road toward Ophrah and came to this land ([[@9013017|1 Sam 13:17]]).

column5: Son of Zophah, of Asher
column7: He appears in the genealogy of the tribe of Asher as the son of Zophah, the son of Helem ([[@13007035-13007036|1 Chr 7:35-36]]).

column5: Brother of Chelub, of Judah
column7: He appears in the family line of Judah, where Chelub, who became the father of Mehir, is introduced as "Chelub the brother of Shuhah" ([[@13004011|1 Chr 4:11]]).

column5: The people of Job's friend Bildad
column7: Of the three friends who came to sympathize with Job and comfort him, Bildad was a Shuhite ([[@18002011|Job 2:11]]). When he argues with Job, he is also called 'Bildad the Shuhite' ([[@18008001|Job 8:1]]).

column5: One of the families of Kiriath Jearim
column7: This was one of the families of Kiriath Jearim, named with the Ithrites, the Puthites, and the Mishraites ([[@13002053|1 Chr 2:53]]).

column5: Women from Shunem, such as Abishag
column7: The word refers to a woman from Shunem. When David was old, his servants brought the beautiful Abishag the Shunammite to care for the king ([[@11001003-11001004|1 Kgs 1:3-4]]). After David died, Adonijah asked for Abishag as his wife, and Solomon took this as asking for the throne ([[@11002021-11002022|1 Kgs 2:21-22]]). There was also a Shunammite woman who welcomed Elisha; she bore a son as Elisha had said ([[@12004017|2 Kgs 4:17]]), and when that son died, she received him back alive through Elisha ([[@12004035-12004036|2 Kgs 4:35-36]]).

column5: Town in the land of Issachar
column7: It was a town of the tribe of Issachar ([[@6019018|Josh 19:18]]). The Philistines camped here when they fought against Saul ([[@9028004|1 Sam 28:4]]), and the prominent woman who gave Elisha food lived here ([[@12004008|2 Kgs 4:8]]).

column5: Son of Gad, ancestor of the Shunites
column7: He was a son of Jacob's son Gad ([[@1046016|Gen 46:16]]). 'The family of the Shunites' came from him ([[@4026015|Num 26:15]]).

column5: Son of Ir in Benjamin's genealogy
column7: He was a son of Ir in Benjamin's genealogy ([[@13007012|1 Chr 7:12]]). His sister Maacah is said to have become Machir's wife ([[@13007015|1 Chr 7:15]]).

column5: Gatekeeper at the west gate
column7: He was a gatekeeper who, with Hosah, was assigned to the west and kept watch by the gate of Shallecheth at the causeway that goes up ([[@13026016|1 Chr 26:16]]).

column5: A wilderness east of Egypt
column7: It was a land before Egypt, where Hagar, fleeing from Sarai, met the angel of the LORD by a spring on the way to Shur ([[@1016006-1016007|Gen 16:6-7]]). Ishmael's descendants lived as far as "Shur that is before Egypt" ([[@1025018|Gen 25:18]]).

column5: Son of Ephraim
column7: He was a son of Ephraim, and the family of the Shuthelahites came from him ([[@4026035|Num 26:35]]). Among his descendants was the family of the Eranites ([[@4026036|Num 26:36]]).

column5: Son of Zabad, of Ephraim
column7: He appears in the family line of Ephraim as a son of Zabad, a descendant of Tahath. He is a different man from Shuthelah the son of Ephraim ([[@13007020-13007021|1 Chr 7:20-21]]).

column5: A temple servant family that returned from exile
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Siaha' ([[@15002043-15002044|Ezra 2:43-44]]). In Nehemiah the name is written 'Sia' ([[@16007047|Neh 7:47]]).

column5: One of David's mighty men who killed a giant
column7: He was a Hushathite who killed one of the sons of the giant in a battle with the Philistines ([[@10021018|2 Sam 21:18]]). In David's time he was the commander of the division for the eighth month ([[@13027011|1 Chr 27:11]]).

column5: A Moabite town famous for its vines
column7: It was a town built by the children of Reuben ([[@4032038|Num 32:38]]). Isaiah grieved over Moab, saying that the fields of Heshbon "languish with the vine of Sibmah" ([[@23016008|Isa 16:8]]).

column5: On the northern border in Ezekiel
column7: This is a place on the northern border of the land Ezekiel described, between the border of Damascus and the border of Hamath ([[@26047015-26047016|Ezek 47:15-16]]).

column5: Valley where the kings of Sodom fought
column7: This is where five kings, including the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah, gathered to fight the allied forces of Chedorlaomer, and it is said to be today's Salt Sea ([[@1014003|Gen 14:3]], 8). It was full of tar pits, and fleeing soldiers fell into them ([[@1014010|Gen 14:10]]).

column5: Firstborn son of Canaan
column7: He was a grandson of Noah's son Ham and the firstborn son of Canaan ([[@1010006|Gen 10:6]]; [[@1010015|Gen 10:15]]). In 1 Chronicles he also appears as Canaan's firstborn ([[@13001013|1 Chr 1:13]]).

column5: An ancient Phoenician city on the Mediterranean coast
column7: Sidon was an ancient Phoenician city on the Mediterranean coast. Canaan's firstborn son was also named Sidon ([[@1010015|Gen 10:15]]). The tribe of Asher did not drive out the people of Sidon ([[@7001031|Judg 1:31]]), and the idol worship of this region made its way into Israel. Jezebel, King Ahab's wife, was the daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians ([[@11016031|1 Kgs 16:31]]). Jesus went to the region of Tyre and Sidon, where he praised a Canaanite woman's faith and healed her daughter ([[@40015021-40015028|Matt 15:21-28]]).

column5: The Amorite king whose royal city was Heshbon
column7: Sihon was the king of the Amorites, with Heshbon as his royal city. He had fought the former king of Moab and taken his land as far as the Arnon ([[@4021026|Num 21:26]]). When Israel asked to pass through his land, he refused and gathered his people and came out to fight ([[@4021023|Num 21:23]]). Israel defeated him and took his land "from the Arnon to the Jabbok" ([[@4021024|Num 21:24]]). Along with the victory over Og king of Bashan, this victory was remembered in the Psalms in a song of thanksgiving ([[@19136019-19136020|Ps 136:19-20]]).

column5: Paul's partner on missionary journeys
column7: He was a man recognized as a leader among the brothers in the church in Jerusalem. To deliver the decision of the Jerusalem council, he went to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas along with Judas called Barsabbas, and as a prophet he encouraged the brothers ([[@44015022|Acts 15:22]], 32). After Paul parted from Barnabas, he chose Silas and set out with him on a missionary journey ([[@44015040|Acts 15:40]]). In Philippi he was beaten and thrown into prison with Paul, but "about midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God" and a great earthquake opened the prison doors ([[@44016025-44016026|Acts 16:25-26]]). In the letters he is called Silvanus ([[@52001001|1 Thess 1:1]]).

column5: Near where King Joash was killed
column7: Joash's servants conspired against him and killed him at the house of Millo, on the road that goes down to Silla ([[@12012020|2 Kgs 12:20]]).

column5: The second son of Jacob and Leah
column7: Simeon was the second son Jacob had by Leah. Leah named him because the LORD had heard that she was not loved ([[@1029033|Gen 29:33]]). Over the matter of his sister Dinah, he and Levi took their swords and killed the men of the city of Shechem ([[@1034025|Gen 34:25]]). When his brothers came to buy grain, Joseph took Simeon from among them, bound him, and kept him in Egypt ([[@1042024|Gen 42:24]]). The tribe of Simeon received land in Canaan within the inheritance of the children of Judah ([[@6019001|Josh 19:1]]).

column5: The man who held baby Jesus and praised God
column7: He was a righteous and devout man in Jerusalem who was looking for the consolation of Israel ([[@42002025|Luke 2:25]]). In the temple he took the baby Jesus in his arms and praised God, then blessed them and spoke to Mary ([[@42002028|Luke 2:28]]; [[@42002034|Luke 2:34]]).

column5: A man in Luke's genealogy
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Jesus recorded in the Gospel of Luke. The generation just before him is Judah ([[@42003030|Luke 3:30]]).

column5: Prophet in Antioch called Niger
column7: He was one of the prophets and teachers in the church at Antioch, known as "Simeon who was called Niger" ([[@44013001|Acts 13:1]]).

column5: Simon the Zealot, one of the twelve apostles
column7: He was one of the twelve apostles and was called "Simon the Zealot" ([[@40010004|Matt 10:4]]). Luke also calls him "Simon who was called the Zealot" ([[@42006015|Luke 6:15]]).

column5: Brother of Jesus
column7: He was a brother of Jesus, named along with James, Joses, and Judas ([[@40013055|Matt 13:55]]; [[@41006003|Mark 6:3]]).

column5: The leper of Bethany who hosted Jesus
column7: He was 'Simon the leper' who lived in Bethany, and while Jesus was in his house, a woman poured ointment on Jesus' head ([[@40026006-40026007|Matt 26:6-7]]; [[@41014003|Mark 14:3]]).

column5: Man of Cyrene who carried Jesus' cross
column7: A man of Cyrene, he was seized as he was coming in from the country and made to carry Jesus' cross ([[@40027032|Matt 27:32]]; [[@42023026|Luke 23:26]]). He was the father of Alexander and Rufus ([[@41015021|Mark 15:21]]).

column5: Father of Judas Iscariot
column7: He was the father of Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus. The Gospel of John calls Judas 'Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot' ([[@43006071|John 6:71]]; [[@43013026|John 13:26]]).

column5: The sorcerer of Samaria
column7: He was a man in Samaria who amazed the people with his sorcery, and he believed and was baptized ([[@44008009|Acts 8:9]]; [[@44008013|Acts 8:13]]). But he tried to buy with money the power to give the Holy Spirit and was rebuked by Peter ([[@44008018-44008020|Acts 8:18-20]]).

column5: Tanner in Joppa who hosted Peter
column7: He was a tanner in Joppa, and Peter stayed at his house for many days ([[@44009043|Acts 9:43]]). His house was by the seaside, and the men sent by Cornelius came there looking for Peter ([[@44010006|Acts 10:6]], 17).

column5: The wilderness between Elim and Sinai
column7: It was the wilderness the children of Israel reached after leaving Elim, lying between Elim and Sinai ([[@2016001|Exod 16:1]]). From there they set out and camped at Rephidim ([[@2017001|Exod 17:1]]).

column5: Sacrifice offered for the forgiveness of sin
column7: A sin offering was a sacrifice offered to be forgiven for sins a person had committed. If the anointed priest sinned, he offered a young bull without defect, and if one of the common people realized he had sinned unwittingly, he brought a female goat without defect and offered it ([[@3004003|Lev 4:3]]; [[@3004027-3004028|Lev 4:27-28]]). When the priest made atonement with that offering, they were forgiven ([[@3004020|Lev 4:20]]). Hebrews says that Christ offered "one sacrifice for sins forever" and sat down at the right hand of God ([[@58010012|Heb 10:12]]).

column5: The mountain where God gave the law
column7: Mount Sinai, also called Mount Horeb, is the mountain in the wilderness of Sinai that Israel reached in the third month after leaving Egypt ([[@2019001|Exod 19:1]]). The LORD came down on this mountain in fire, so that the whole mountain was covered with smoke and quaked greatly ([[@2019018|Exod 19:18]]). Here God gave Moses the law, along with the two tablets of the covenant written by God himself ([[@2031018|Exod 31:18]]). Israel stayed here and built the tabernacle. Scholars differ on its exact location.

column5: Wilderness before Mount Sinai where the law was given
column7: This is the wilderness where the children of Israel camped in front of Mount Sinai in the third month after they left Egypt ([[@2019001-2019002|Exod 19:1-2]]). The LORD came down on the top of Mount Sinai and called Moses ([[@2019020|Exod 19:20]]). In the Tent of Meeting in this wilderness, the LORD told Moses to count the children of Israel ([[@4001001-4001002|Num 1:1-2]]). On the twentieth day of the second month of the second year, the cloud lifted from the tabernacle of the covenant, and the children of Israel set out from the Wilderness of Sinai toward the Wilderness of Paran ([[@4010011-4010012|Num 10:11-12]]).

column5: A people descended from Canaan
column7: They were one of the peoples descended from Canaan, Noah's grandson ([[@1010015-1010017|Gen 10:15-17]]; [[@13001015|1 Chr 1:15]]).

column5: Where David sent plunder
column7: It was one of the places that received plunder when David sent it from Ziklag to the elders of Judah ([[@9030026|1 Sam 30:26]]; [[@9030028|1 Sam 30:28]]).

column5: The well where Abner was brought back from
column7: After leaving David, Joab sent messengers, and they brought Abner back from the well of Sirah ([[@10003026|2 Sam 3:26]]).

column5: Canaanite commander defeated by Deborah and Barak
column7: He was the commander of the army of Jabin, a Canaanite king who reigned in Hazor, and he lived in Harosheth of the Gentiles ([[@7004002|Judg 4:2]]). He oppressed Israel with nine hundred chariots of iron, but by the river Kishon the LORD routed his army before Barak ([[@7004013-7004015|Judg 4:13-15]]). Sisera fled on foot and hid in the tent of Jael, the wife of Heber, and while he slept Jael drove a tent peg into his temple and killed him ([[@7004021|Judg 4:21]]). The Song of Deborah also sings of this ([[@7005026|Judg 5:26]]).

column5: A temple servant family that returned from exile
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Sisera' ([[@15002053|Ezra 2:53]]; [[@16007055|Neh 7:55]]).

column5: Queen's sister given to Hadad by Pharaoh
column7: She was the sister of Tahpenes, queen of Egypt, and Pharaoh gave her as wife to Hadad the Edomite. She bore him a son, Genubath ([[@11011019-11011020|1 Kgs 11:19-20]]).

column5: Son of Uzziel, of Levi
column7: He was one of the sons of Uzziel, a descendant of Levi, named with Mishael and Elzaphan ([[@2006022|Exod 6:22]]).

column5: The second well Isaac dug
column7: When the herdsmen of Gerar argued again over a well Isaac had dug, Isaac named it Sitnah ([[@1026020-1026021|Gen 26:20-21]]).

column5: A weapon for hurling stones
column7: A sling was a weapon that held a stone and was swung around to hurl it far. Among the Benjamites were seven hundred chosen men who were all left-handed, and each of them "could sling a stone at a hair and not miss" ([[@7020016|Judg 20:16]]). David chose five smooth stones from the brook, put them in his bag, and went toward the Philistine with his sling in his hand ([[@9017040|1 Sam 17:40]]). And with no sword in his hand, he defeated the Philistine with a sling and a stone ([[@9017050|1 Sam 17:50]]).

column5: One of the seven churches of Asia
column7: It was one of the seven churches in Revelation ([[@66001011|Rev 1:11]]). The Lord told the church in Smyrna, "Be faithful to death, and I will give you the crown of life" ([[@66002008-66002010|Rev 2:8-10]]).

column5: King of Egypt to whom Hoshea sent envoys
column7: He was the king of Egypt to whom Hoshea king of Israel sent messengers. When Hoshea stopped paying tribute to Assyria, the king of Assyria put him in prison ([[@12017004|2 Kgs 17:4]]).

column5: A place whose founder was Heber of Judah
column7: In the family line of Judah, Heber, a son of Mered's Jewish wife, appears as "Heber the father of Soco". He is named with Jered the father of Gedor and Jekuthiel the father of Zanoah ([[@13004018|1 Chr 4:18]]).

column5: The town of Judah where the Philistines gathered against Israel
column7: It was a lowland town of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015033-6015035|Josh 15:33-35]]). In the battle when Goliath came out, the Philistines gathered at Socoh, which belonged to Judah ([[@9017001|1 Sam 17:1]]).

column5: A town in Judah's hill country
column7: It was one of the hill-country towns the descendants of Judah received, listed with Shamir and Jattir ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]).

column5: Father of Gaddiel the spy
column7: Among the men sent to spy out the land of Canaan, Gaddiel from the tribe of Zebulun was the son of Sodi ([[@4013010|Num 13:10]]).

column5: A Jordan-plain city destroyed for its sin
column7: Sodom was a city in the plain of the Jordan, where Lot moved his tent and stayed ([[@1013012|Gen 13:12]]). Scripture says, "the men of Sodom were exceedingly wicked and sinners against the LORD" ([[@1013013|Gen 13:13]]). Abraham pleaded with God not to destroy it even if only ten righteous people were found there ([[@1018032|Gen 18:32]]), but in the end the LORD rained down sulfur and fire from the sky and destroyed it along with Gomorrah ([[@1019024|Gen 19:24]]). After that, Sodom often appears as an example of God's judgment. Scholars differ on its exact location.

column5: David's son, the king famous for his wisdom
column7: He was the son born to David and Bathsheba ([[@10012024|2 Sam 12:24]]). After he became king, he asked for wisdom to judge the people rightly, and God gave him not only wisdom but also the riches and honor he had not asked for ([[@11003009-11003013|1 Kgs 3:9-13]]). He built the house of the LORD in Jerusalem ([[@11006001|1 Kgs 6:1]]). But in his old age his wives led him to follow other gods, and his heart was not wholly true to God ([[@11011004|1 Kgs 11:4]]).

column5: A colonnade in the temple
column7: It was a colonnade in the temple in Jerusalem. Jesus walked there ([[@43010023|John 10:23]]), and the apostles and believers gathered there with one accord ([[@44003011|Acts 3:11]]; [[@44005012|Acts 5:12]]).

column5: One of David's mighty men
column7: He appears in the list of David's mighty men as "the sons of Jashen, Jonathan" ([[@10023008|2 Sam 23:8]]; [[@10023032|2 Sam 23:32]]).

column5: High priest's grandson who married into Sanballat's family
column7: One of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, he became the son-in-law of Sanballat the Horonite, so Nehemiah drove him away ([[@16013028|Neh 13:28]]).

column5: A believer from Beroea who went with Paul
column7: From Beroea, he went with Paul as far as Asia ([[@44020004|Acts 20:4]]). Scholars differ on whether he is the same as the 'Sosipater' in Romans ([[@45016021|Rom 16:21]])

column5: A family of Solomon's servants' descendants
column7: Among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Sophereth' ([[@16007057|Neh 7:57]]). In Ezra the name is written 'Hassophereth' ([[@15002055|Ezra 2:55]]).

column5: The valley where Delilah lived
column7: This is the valley where Delilah, the woman Samson loved, lived. Samson came to love Delilah of this valley ([[@7016004|Judg 16:4]]).

column5: Ruler of the synagogue in Corinth
column7: He was the ruler of the synagogue in Corinth who was beaten before the judgment seat of the proconsul Gallio ([[@44018017|Acts 18:17]]). Scholars differ on whether he is the same as 'our brother Sosthenes,' who sent 1 Corinthians along with Paul ([[@46001001|1 Cor 1:1]]).

column5: A family of Solomon's servants' descendants
column7: Among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Sotai' ([[@15002055|Ezra 2:55]]; [[@16007057|Neh 7:57]]).

column5: The western land Paul hoped to reach
column7: For many years Paul had wanted to visit the church in Rome on his way to Spain ([[@45015023-45015024|Rom 15:23-24]]). He said that after delivering the collection to Jerusalem, he would go by way of Rome to Spain ([[@45015028|Rom 15:28]]).

column5: A believer in Rome whom Paul loved
column7: In his letter to the church in Rome, Paul greeted him as "Stachys, my beloved" ([[@45016009|Rom 16:9]]).

column5: A Corinthian believer whom Paul baptized
column7: He was a believer in Corinth whom Paul baptized ([[@46001016|1 Cor 1:16]]), and his household was the firstfruits of Achaia and devoted itself to serving the saints ([[@46016015|1 Cor 16:15]]).

column5: One of the seven, the first martyr
column7: He was one of the seven men the Jerusalem church chose to oversee the care of the needy, a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit ([[@44006003|Acts 6:3]], 5). Full of grace and power, he did great wonders and signs, and those who argued with him could not stand against his wisdom and the Spirit ([[@44006008-44006010|Acts 6:8-10]]). People threw him out of the city and stoned him, and the witnesses laid their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul ([[@44007058|Acts 7:58]]). Stephen knelt down and prayed, "Lord, don’t hold this sin against them!" and then he died ([[@44007060|Acts 7:60]]).

column5: The street in Damascus where Saul stayed
column7: This is the street in Damascus where the Lord told Ananias to go; Saul was praying in the house of Judah on that street ([[@44009010-44009011|Acts 9:10-11]]).

column5: Son of Zophah, of Asher
column7: He was one of the sons of Zophah, the son of Helem, in the family line of Asher, named with Harnepher, Shual, and others ([[@13007035-13007036|1 Chr 7:35-36]]).

column5: The first stop after leaving Egypt
column7: It was the first place the children of Israel reached after setting out from Rameses ([[@2012037|Exod 12:37]]). From there they set out and camped at Etham, at the edge of the wilderness ([[@2013020|Exod 13:20]]).

column5: Town east of the Jordan in Jacob and Gideon's stories
column7: It was a town in the valley east of the Jordan, and it became part of the land of the tribe of Gad ([[@6013024-6013027|Josh 13:24-27]]). After meeting Esau, Jacob built himself a house here and made shelters for his livestock, so the place was called Succoth ([[@1033017|Gen 33:17]]). When Gideon was pursuing the kings of Midian, the officials of Succoth refused to give bread to his exhausted men, and Gideon came back and punished its elders ([[@7008005-7008016|Judg 8:5-16]]). Solomon cast the bronze vessels for the temple in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarethan ([[@11007046|1 Kgs 7:46]]).

column5: A people who came with Shishak
column7: They were one of the peoples who came out of Egypt with Shishak king of Egypt when he attacked Judah, named with the Lubim and the Ethiopians ([[@14012002-14012003|2 Chr 12:2-3]]).

column5: Near where Moses proclaimed God's words
column7: In describing where Moses spoke to Israel beyond the Jordan, the Bible mentions "the Arabah opposite Suf" ([[@5001001|Deut 1:1]]).

column5: Named in the Book of the Wars
column7: This place appears in the words quoted from the Book of the Wars of the LORD: "Vaheb in Suphah, the valleys of the Arnon" ([[@4021014|Num 21:14]]).

column5: A gate guarded when Joash was crowned
column7: This was the gate where Jehoiada stationed a third of the captains when he had them guard the king's house ([[@12011004-12011006|2 Kgs 11:4-6]]).

column5: City of the Persian king's palace
column7: It was the city where the Persian kings had their palace, in the province of Elam ([[@27008002|Dan 8:2]]). While Nehemiah was "in Susa the palace" he heard news of Jerusalem, and he wept and prayed ([[@16001001-16001004|Neh 1:1-4]]). King Ahasuerus took the throne in the palace at Susa and gave a great feast, and the story of Esther and Mordecai also took place here ([[@17001002|Esth 1:2]]). The city of Susa, once troubled by Haman's decree, "shouted and was glad" when Mordecai was honored ([[@17008015|Esth 8:15]]).

column5: A woman who served Jesus
column7: She was a woman who, with Joanna and many others, served Jesus and his disciples from her own possessions ([[@42008003|Luke 8:3]]).

column5: Father of Gaddi the spy
column7: Among the men sent to spy out the land of Canaan, Gaddi from the tribe of Manasseh was the son of Susi ([[@4013011|Num 13:11]]).

column5: A Samaritan town near Jacob's well
column7: This is the town of Samaria Jesus came to, near the ground that Jacob gave to his son Joseph ([[@43004005-43004006|John 4:5-6]]).

column5: Town at the southern edge of Egypt
column7: This name, Seveneh in Ezekiel, was used to mark the southern edge of Egypt. Ezekiel prophesied that Egypt would be laid waste "from the tower of Seveneh even to the border of Ethiopia" ([[@26029010|Ezek 29:10]]; [[@26030006|Ezek 30:6]]).

column5: Where Jews gathered to read Scripture and pray
column7: A synagogue was where Jews gathered every Sabbath to read the Law and the Prophets and to pray ([[@44013014-44013015|Acts 13:14-15]]). Scholars differ on when synagogues first began. Jesus went throughout Galilee teaching in the synagogues, and in the synagogue at Nazareth he read from Isaiah and said, "Today, this Scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing" ([[@40004023|Matt 4:23]]; [[@42004016-42004021|Luke 4:16-21]]). Paul too, whenever he came to a city, went first into the synagogue and reasoned with the people from the Scriptures ([[@44017001-44017002|Acts 17:1-2]]).

column5: A woman of the church in Philippi
column7: She was a member of the church in Philippi whom Paul urged, along with Euodia, to think the same way in the Lord ([[@50004002|Phil 4:2]]).

column5: Where Paul stayed three days
column7: On the way to Rome, Paul's ship of Alexandria put in here, and they stayed three days ([[@44028011-44028012|Acts 28:11-12]]).

column5: The northern neighbor centered on Damascus
column7: It was the nation and people northeast of Israel, centered on Damascus. In the time of the judges, Israel also served "the gods of Syria" ([[@7010006|Judg 10:6]]). During the time of the kings, Syria often fought with Israel, and Ben Hadad king of Syria even besieged Samaria ([[@11020001|1 Kgs 20:1]]). The Syrian commander Naaman dipped himself in the Jordan River as Elisha told him and was healed ([[@12005014|2 Kgs 5:14]]). In the New Testament this region is called 'Syria' ([[@40004024|Matt 4:24]]).

column5: Sandbars feared by Paul's ship
column7: When Paul's ship was driven by the storm wind called Euroclydon, the sailors feared they would run aground here, so they lowered the sea anchor and let the ship be driven along ([[@44027014|Acts 27:14]]; [[@44027017|Acts 27:17]]).

column5: A Canaanite town near Megiddo
column7: It was a Canaanite town near Megiddo whose king Joshua defeated ([[@6012021|Josh 12:21]]). The town became Manasseh's share, but Manasseh did not drive out its inhabitants ([[@7001027|Judg 1:27]]). Later it was given from the half-tribe of Manasseh to the Levites of the family of Kohath ([[@6021025-6021026|Josh 21:25-26]]). Deborah's song says that the kings of Canaan fought "at Taanach by the waters of Megiddo" ([[@7005019|Judg 5:19]]).

column5: A place on Ephraim's border
column7: This place appears on the border of the land the descendants of Ephraim received by their families. The border turned eastward from Michmethath to Taanath Shiloh ([[@6016005-6016006|Josh 16:5-6]]).

column5: A temple servant family that returned from exile
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Tabbaoth' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]]; [[@16007046|Neh 7:46]]).

column5: Near where Midian fled from Gideon
column7: When Gideon's three hundred men blew their trumpets, the enemy army fled as far as the border of Abel Meholah, near Tabbath ([[@7007022|Judg 7:22]]).

column5: Father of the man Syria and Ephraim plotted to crown
column7: The kings of Syria and Ephraim plotted to attack Judah and set up "the son of Tabeel" as king; he was that son's father ([[@23007005-23007006|Isa 7:5-6]]).

column5: Wrote a letter to Artaxerxes
column7: In the days of Artaxerxes he wrote a letter to Artaxerxes king of Persia, together with Bishlam and Mithredath ([[@15004007|Ezra 4:7]]).

column5: Where the LORD's fire burned
column7: When the people complained in the wilderness, the LORD's fire burned the edge of the camp. So that place was called Taberah ([[@4011001-4011003|Num 11:1-3]]; [[@5009022|Deut 9:22]]).

column5: Portable tent for worshiping God in the wilderness
column7: The tabernacle was the holy, movable tent where the people of Israel worshiped God in the wilderness. God told them to make "a sanctuary, that I may dwell among them", following the pattern he showed Moses ([[@2025008-2025009|Exod 25:8-9]]). When the tabernacle was finished, the cloud covered the Tent of Meeting, and it is written that "the LORD’s glory filled the tabernacle" ([[@2040034|Exod 40:34]]). Hebrews says that the tabernacle was a copy and shadow of what is in heaven ([[@58008005|Heb 8:5]]). In the Bible it is also called the 'Tent of Meeting' or simply the 'tent'.

column5: Disciple in Joppa whom Peter raised
column7: She was a disciple in Joppa whose name translated means Dorcas, and she did many good works and acts of mercy ([[@44009036|Acts 9:36]]). When she died, Peter prayed and said, "Tabitha, get up!" and she opened her eyes ([[@44009040|Acts 9:40]]).

column5: Site of the oak Samuel spoke of
column7: Samuel told Saul that when he came to the oak of Tabor, he would meet three men going up to Bethel ([[@9010003|1 Sam 10:3]]).

column5: The mountain where Deborah and Barak gathered the army
column7: It is a mountain in northern Israel, and the border of the tribe of Issachar reached Tabor ([[@6019022|Josh 19:22]]). The judge Deborah told Barak to take ten thousand men of Naphtali and Zebulun and go to Mount Tabor ([[@7004006|Judg 4:6]]). On the day the LORD delivered Sisera into Barak's hand, Barak went down from Mount Tabor with ten thousand men to fight ([[@7004014|Judg 4:14]]). A psalm contains the praise, "Tabor and Hermon rejoice in your name" ([[@19089012|Ps 89:12]]).

column5: Father of Ben Hadad, king of Syria
column7: He was the father of Ben Hadad, king of Syria, who lived in Damascus, and the son of Hezion. King Asa of Judah sent silver and gold to his son Ben Hadad ([[@11015018|1 Kgs 15:18]]).

column5: A town Solomon built in the wilderness
column7: It was a town Solomon built along with Gezer, Beth Horon, and others, where 1 Kings names it 'Tamar in the wilderness' ([[@11009017-11009018|1 Kgs 9:17-18]]). 2 Chronicles says he built Tadmor in the wilderness ([[@14008004|2 Chr 8:4]])

column5: Ancestor of the Tahanite family of Ephraim
column7: He was one of the descendants of Ephraim, and the family of the Tahanites came from him. He is named with Shuthelah and Becher among the families of Ephraim ([[@4026035|Num 26:35]]).

column5: Son of Telah, of Ephraim
column7: He appears in the family line of Ephraim as the grandson of Resheph and the son of Telah. His son was Ladan ([[@13007025-13007026|1 Chr 7:25-26]]).

column5: Son of Nahor's concubine Reumah
column7: He was one of the children borne by Reumah, the concubine of Nahor, Abraham's brother ([[@1022020|Gen 22:20]]; [[@1022024|Gen 22:24]]).

column5: A camp on the wilderness journey
column7: It is where Israel camped after leaving Makheloth as they went through the wilderness. From there they went on to Terah ([[@4033026-4033027|Num 33:26-27]]).

column5: Son of Assir, a Kohathite
column7: A descendant of Levi's son Kohath, he was the son of Assir ([[@13006024|1 Chr 6:24]]; [[@13006037|1 Chr 6:37]]). He was one of the ancestors of Heman the singer ([[@13006033-13006037|1 Chr 6:33-37]]).

column5: Egyptian city where Judeans fled
column7: It was a city in Egypt that appears several times in Jeremiah. Johanan the son of Kareah and the army captains did not obey the LORD's voice, and they took the remnant of Judah, along with Jeremiah and Baruch, to Egypt and came to Tahpanhes ([[@24043005-24043007|Jer 43:5-7]]). In Tahpanhes the LORD had Jeremiah hide large stones in the brickwork at the entrance of Pharaoh's house ([[@24043008-24043009|Jer 43:8-9]]), and he said that Nebuchadnezzar would come and set his throne on those stones ([[@24043010|Jer 43:10]]). After that, Tahpanhes is also named as one of the places where the Jews living in Egypt stayed ([[@24044001|Jer 44:1]]).

column5: Egyptian queen whose sister married Hadad
column7: She was the queen of Pharaoh of Egypt, and her sister became Hadad's wife. Tahpenes weaned her sister's son Genubath in Pharaoh's house ([[@11011019-11011020|1 Kgs 11:19-20]]).

column5: A land reached in David's census
column7: When David ordered a census, those counting the people came to Gilead and to the land of Tahtim Hodshi ([[@10024002|2 Sam 24:2]]; [[@10024006|2 Sam 24:6]]).

column5: The Bible's largest unit of weight and money
column7: The talent was the largest unit of weight in the Bible, used for counting gold or silver. The lampstand of the tabernacle and all its utensils were made from one talent of pure gold ([[@2025039|Exod 25:39]]). The account of the silver the people gave for building the tabernacle shows that one talent was a great weight of about three thousand shekels ([[@2038025-2038026|Exod 38:25-26]]). In his parables Jesus told of a servant who owed ten thousand talents, and of servants who each received talents from their master according to their ability ([[@40018024|Matt 18:24]]; [[@40025015|Matt 25:15]]).

column5: Descendant of Anak living in Hebron
column7: He was one of the descendants of Anak that the spies saw in Hebron ([[@4013022|Num 13:22]]). Caleb drove him out, and Judah attacked Hebron and struck him down ([[@6015014|Josh 15:14]]; [[@7001010|Judg 1:10]]).

column5: King of Geshur, Absalom's grandfather
column7: The son of Ammihur, he was king of Geshur, and his daughter Maacah bore Absalom to David ([[@10003003|2 Sam 3:3]]). Later, Absalom fled and went to him ([[@10013037|2 Sam 13:37]]).

column5: A Levite gatekeeper after the exile
column7: He was a gatekeeper after the return from exile, named along with Akkub ([[@13009017|1 Chr 9:17]]; [[@16011019|Neh 11:19]]).

column5: Judah's daughter-in-law, mother of Perez and Zerah
column7: She was the daughter-in-law whom Judah took as a wife for his firstborn son Er ([[@1038006|Gen 38:6]]). The twins Perez and Zerah were born to her, and her name also appears in the genealogy of Jesus in Matthew ([[@1038027-1038030|Gen 38:27-30]]; [[@40001003|Matt 1:3]]).

column5: David's daughter, Absalom's sister
column7: She was the beautiful sister of Absalom, David's son ([[@10013001|2 Sam 13:1]]). Her brother Amnon pretended to be sick, called her in, and forced her, and afterward he hated her deeply and drove her out ([[@10013006-10013017|2 Sam 13:6-17]]). Tamar put ashes on her head, tore her robe of many colors, and went away crying aloud, and after that she lived desolate in her brother Absalom's house ([[@10013019-10013020|2 Sam 13:19-20]]). Two years later Absalom invited Amnon to a sheep-shearing feast and had his servants kill him ([[@10013023-10013029|2 Sam 13:23-29]]).

column5: Daughter of Absalom
column7: She was the only daughter among the three sons and one daughter born to Absalom, and the Bible says she was a woman with a beautiful face ([[@10014027|2 Sam 14:27]]).

column5: Southern border point in Ezekiel's vision
column7: This is where the southern border of the land of Israel begins in Ezekiel's vision. The border ran from Tamar to the waters of Meribath Kadesh ([[@26047019|Ezek 47:19]]; [[@26048028|Ezek 48:28]]).

column5: A Netophathite, father of Seraiah
column7: He was the father of Seraiah, one of the army captains who went to Gedaliah at Mizpah after Jerusalem fell ([[@12025023|2 Kgs 25:23]]; [[@24040008|Jer 40:8]]).

column5: Solomon's daughter, wife of Ben Abinadab
column7: She was Solomon's daughter. She became the wife of Ben Abinadab, one of Solomon's twelve officers, who was over all the height of Dor ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004011|1 Kgs 4:11]]).

column5: Town on the border of Ephraim and Manasseh
column7: The king of Tappuah was among the kings Joshua defeated ([[@6012017|Josh 12:17]]). The land of Tappuah belonged to Manasseh, but the town of Tappuah on the border belonged to the children of Ephraim ([[@6017008|Josh 17:8]]).

column5: A town in Judah's lowland
column7: It was one of the lowland towns the descendants of Judah received, named with Zanoah, En Gannim, and Enam ([[@6015033-6015034|Josh 15:33-34]]).

column5: A son of Hebron of the tribe of Judah
column7: In the genealogy of Judah, he is one of the sons of Hebron, a descendant of Caleb, listed together with Korah, Rekem, and Shema ([[@13002042-13002043|1 Chr 2:42-43]]).

column5: A town given to the tribe of Benjamin
column7: One of the towns the tribe of Benjamin received by their families, named along with Rekem and Irpeel ([[@6018021|Josh 18:21]]; [[@6018027|Josh 18:27]]).

column5: Son of Micah, of Saul's family
column7: He was a son of Micah, whose father was Saul's grandson Merib-baal, the son of Jonathan ([[@13008034-13008035|1 Chr 8:34-35]]). The same genealogy also appears in 1 Chronicles 9 ([[@13009041|1 Chr 9:41]]).

column5: Grandson of Japheth, son of Javan
column7: A grandson of Noah's son Japheth, he was a son of Javan ([[@13001007|1 Chr 1:7]]). He also appears in Genesis ([[@1010004|Gen 10:4]]).

column5: Trading place at the far end of the sea
column7: In the Bible it appears as a wealthy trading place far across the sea. Tarshish traded with Tyre in silver, iron, tin, and lead ([[@26027012|Ezek 27:12]]), and once every three years Solomon's ships of Tarshish brought back gold, silver, and ivory ([[@11010022|1 Kgs 10:22]]). Jonah boarded a ship at Joppa going to Tarshish to flee from the presence of the LORD ([[@32001003|Jonah 1:3]]). Isaiah said that God's glory would be made known even in faraway places like Tarshish ([[@23066019|Isa 66:19]]). Scholars differ on its exact location.

column5: A son of Bilhan of the tribe of Benjamin
column7: He was one of the sons of Bilhan, the son of Jediael of the tribe of Benjamin ([[@13007006|1 Chr 7:6]]; [[@13007010|1 Chr 7:10]]).

column5: One of King Ahasuerus' seven princes
column7: He was one of the seven princes of Persia and Media who were close to King Ahasuerus and sat first in the kingdom ([[@17001014|Esth 1:14]]).

column5: The hometown of Paul
column7: It was a city of Cilicia, and Paul said he was a Jew from Tarsus, "a citizen of no insignificant city" ([[@44021039|Acts 21:39]]). After his conversion the brothers sent Paul off to Tarsus ([[@44009030|Acts 9:30]]).

column5: A commander sent by the king of Assyria
column7: The king of Assyria sent him, along with Rabsaris and Rabshakeh and a great army, against Hezekiah in Jerusalem ([[@12018017|2 Kgs 18:17]]). Some take it as an official title rather than a personal name.

column5: The governor beyond the River who questioned the temple building
column7: He was the governor beyond the River who asked who had ordered the temple to be built and sent a letter to King Darius ([[@15005003|Ezra 5:3]]; [[@15005006|Ezra 5:6]]).

column5: One who collected taxes for Rome
column7: A tax collector gathered taxes for the Roman government. Because they often collected more than was set, the Jews hated them and treated them like sinners ([[@42003012-42003013|Luke 3:12-13]]). Jesus called Matthew the tax collector to be his disciple and ate with tax collectors and sinners, so people called him "a friend of tax collectors and sinners" ([[@40010003|Matt 10:3]]; [[@40011019|Matt 11:19]]). After meeting Jesus, the chief tax collector Zacchaeus said he would give half his goods to the poor and pay back four times whatever he had taken wrongfully ([[@42019008|Luke 19:8]]).

column5: A son of Nahor by his concubine Reumah
column7: He was one of the children borne by Reumah, the concubine of Abraham's brother Nahor ([[@1022020|Gen 22:20]]; [[@1022024|Gen 22:24]]).

column5: The third son of Hosah, a Merarite
column7: He was the third of the sons of Hosah, a descendant of Merari, and belonged to the divisions of the doorkeepers ([[@13026010-13026012|1 Chr 26:10-12]]).

column5: The father of Ir Nahash in Judah
column7: In the genealogy of Judah, he was a son of Eshton and the father of Ir Nahash, one of the men of Recah ([[@13004012|1 Chr 4:12]]).

column5: Town of Judah, hometown of the prophet Amos
column7: A town in the hill country of Judah, south of Bethlehem; Rehoboam fortified it ([[@14011006|2 Chr 11:6]]). Joab brought a wise woman from Tekoa and had her tell a made-up story so that David would call Absalom back ([[@10014002|2 Sam 14:2]]). Ira, one of David's mighty men, was also from Tekoa ([[@10023026|2 Sam 23:26]]). The prophet Amos was one "among the herdsmen of Tekoa" ([[@30001001|Amos 1:1]]).

column5: Where Ezekiel visited the exiles
column7: The place where Ezekiel came to the captives living by the river Chebar and sat among them for seven days ([[@26003015|Ezek 3:15]]).

column5: A place in Babylonia from which exiles came
column7: Among those who returned from exile in Babylon were some who came up from Tel Harsha. But they could not show that their families were of Israel ([[@15002059|Ezra 2:59]]; [[@16007061|Neh 7:61]]).

column5: A place in Babylonia from which exiles came
column7: Among those who returned from exile in Babylon were some who came up from Tel Melah. But they could not show that their families were of Israel ([[@15002059|Ezra 2:59]]; [[@16007061|Neh 7:61]]).

column5: A son of Resheph of the tribe of Ephraim
column7: In the genealogy of Ephraim, he appears as the son of Resheph, a son of Beriah. His son was Tahan ([[@13007025|1 Chr 7:25]]).

column5: Where Saul counted his army
column7: The place where Saul summoned and counted the people when he went to fight Amalek. There were two hundred thousand foot soldiers and ten thousand men of Judah ([[@9015004|1 Sam 15:4]]).

column5: Where the people of Eden lived
column7: When the Assyrian king's officials listed the nations Assyria had destroyed, they named the people of Eden who were in Telassar ([[@12019012|2 Kgs 19:12]]; [[@23037012|Isa 37:12]]).

column5: A town in the south of Judah
column7: One of the towns of the tribe of Judah in the south, near the border of Edom ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015024|Josh 15:24]]).

column5: A gatekeeper who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra's time, he is named as a gatekeeper among those who had taken foreign wives ([[@15010024|Ezra 10:24]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Son of Ishmael
column7: He was one of the sons of Ishmael, Abraham’s son ([[@1025013-1025015|Gen 25:13-15]]). The sons of Ishmael became twelve princes ([[@1025016|Gen 25:16]]).

column5: Land in the Arabian desert
column7: It appears in Job in the phrase 'the caravans of Tema' ([[@18006019|Job 6:19]]). Isaiah says the inhabitants of the land of Tema "met the fugitives with their bread" ([[@23021014|Isa 21:14]]).

column5: Temple-servant family back from exile
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Temah' ([[@15002053|Ezra 2:53]]; [[@16007055|Neh 7:55]]).

column5: Son of Eliphaz and grandson of Esau
column7: The son of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn, he was Esau's grandson ([[@1036011|Gen 36:11]]). He was one of the chiefs among Esau's descendants and was called 'chief Teman' ([[@1036015|Gen 36:15]]). A region and a clan in the land of Edom were also called Teman, which seems to be connected with his name. Job's friend Eliphaz was also "the Temanite" ([[@18002011|Job 2:11]]). Teman was also a place known for its wisdom ([[@24049007|Jer 49:7]]).

column5: A land of Edom famous for wisdom
column7: It was a place in Edom, and Jeremiah announced Edom's judgment, asking, "Is wisdom no more in Teman?" ([[@24049007|Jer 49:7]]). Amos also declared that God would send a fire on Teman ([[@30001012|Amos 1:12]]).

column5: A son of Ashhur and Naarah
column7: In the genealogy of Judah, he is named as one of the sons Naarah bore to Ashhur, the father of Tekoa ([[@13004005-13004006|1 Chr 4:5-6]]).

column5: Portable cloth dwelling for a moving life
column7: A tent is a cloth dwelling pitched so that people can live in it while moving from place to place. Jabal is said to have become "the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock" ([[@1004020|Gen 4:20]]). Abram pitched his tent on the mountain east of Bethel and built an altar to the LORD ([[@1012008|Gen 12:8]]), and Hebrews says that by faith he lived in tents in the promised land with Isaac and Jacob ([[@58011009|Heb 11:9]]). Paul compared our bodies to "the earthly house of our tent" and looked forward to the eternal house in the heavens ([[@47005001|2 Cor 5:1]]).

column5: Father of Abram
column7: He was the son of Nahor, and at seventy he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran ([[@1011024-1011026|Gen 11:24-26]]). His son Haran died before his father Terah, in the land of his birth, Ur of the Chaldees ([[@1011028|Gen 11:28]]). Terah took Abram, his grandson Lot, and his daughter-in-law Sarai and left Ur to go to the land of Canaan, but when they came to Haran they settled there, and he died in Haran at two hundred five ([[@1011031-1011032|Gen 11:31-32]]). Joshua said that when Terah lived beyond the River he served other gods ([[@6024002|Josh 24:2]]).

column5: Campsite on the wilderness journey
column7: This is a place where Israel camped after leaving Tahath on their journey through the wilderness. From there they went on to Mithkah ([[@4033027-4033028|Num 33:27-28]]).

column5: Eunuch who plotted against the king
column7: He was a eunuch who guarded King Ahasuerus’ gate, and together with Bigthan he plotted to kill the king. Mordecai learned of it and told Esther ([[@17002021-17002022|Esth 2:21-22]]; [[@17006002|Esth 6:2]]).

column5: The man who wrote down Romans
column7: He was the one who wrote down the letter to the Romans, and he said, "I, Tertius, who write the letter, greet you in the Lord" ([[@45016022|Rom 16:22]]).

column5: Orator who accused Paul
column7: He was the orator who came down with the high priest Ananias and accused Paul before Governor Felix ([[@44024001-44024002|Acts 24:1-2]]).

column5: A ruler in charge of a region
column7: Tetrarch originally meant someone who ruled a fourth part of a region, but in the New Testament it refers to a ruler in charge of a region. Luke records that when John the Baptist was at work, Herod was tetrarch of Galilee and his brother Philip was tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis ([[@42003001|Luke 3:1]]). Herod the tetrarch was rebuked by John over Herodias, his brother's wife, and later he sent and had John beheaded in the prison ([[@42003019|Luke 3:19]]; [[@40014010|Matt 14:10]]). When Herod heard the report about Jesus, he thought John the Baptist had risen from the dead ([[@40014001-40014002|Matt 14:1-2]]).

column5: A great city of Egypt
column7: It was a city of Egypt, and the LORD said he would punish "Amon of No" and Egypt ([[@24046025|Jer 46:25]]). Ezekiel also declared that God would cut off the multitude of No ([[@26030014-26030015|Ezek 30:14-15]]).

column5: The town where Abimelech died
column7: The place where Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth died after a woman threw an upper millstone on him from the wall ([[@10011021|2 Sam 11:21]]).

column5: Recipient of Luke and Acts
column7: He is the 'most excellent Theophilus' to whom Luke wrote and sent his Gospel ([[@42001003|Luke 1:3]]). The book of Acts also opens as a writing addressed to Theophilus ([[@44001001|Acts 1:1]]).

column5: A city of Macedonia where Paul founded a church
column7: It was a city in the region of Macedonia, where Paul reasoned from the Scriptures in the Jewish synagogue for three Sabbath days, proclaiming that this Jesus is the Christ ([[@44017001-44017003|Acts 17:1-3]]). A great multitude of devout Greeks and not a few of the chief women believed, but the Jews became jealous and set the city in an uproar, so the brothers sent Paul and Silas away by night to Beroea ([[@44017004-44017010|Acts 17:4-10]]). The church at Philippi sent help for Paul's needs even while he was in Thessalonica ([[@50004016|Phil 4:16]]). Paul, together with Silvanus and Timothy, wrote a letter to the church of the Thessalonians ([[@52001001|1 Thess 1:1]]).

column5: A rebel leader Gamaliel spoke of
column7: Gamaliel stood up in the council and spoke of him: he made himself out to be somebody and about four hundred men followed him, but when he was killed they were all scattered ([[@44005034-44005036|Acts 5:34-36]]).

column5: Disciple of Jesus called Didymus
column7: He was one of Jesus' twelve disciples ([[@40010003|Matt 10:3]]). He was also called 'Didymus', and when Jesus was about to go to Lazarus, he said to the other disciples, "Let’s also go, that we may die with him" ([[@43011016|John 11:16]]). Because he was not with them when the risen Jesus came to the disciples, he said he would not believe unless he saw the nail marks and put his finger into them ([[@43020024-43020025|John 20:24-25]]). Eight days later, when he saw Jesus, he confessed, "My Lord and my God!" ([[@43020026-43020028|John 20:26-28]]).

column5: Where believers from Rome met Paul
column7: The brothers from Rome came out as far as the Market of Appius and the Three Taverns to meet Paul. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and took courage ([[@44028014-44028015|Acts 28:14-15]]).
