column5: Beating out harvested grain to collect the kernels
column7: Threshing is beating harvested grain to collect the kernels, and the wide open place where this was done is called a threshing floor. The law commanded, "You shall not muzzle the ox when he treads out the grain" ([[@5025004|Deut 25:4]]). Boaz winnowed barley at night on the threshing floor, and Ruth went down there as her mother-in-law told her ([[@8003002|Ruth 3:2]], 6). Solomon began to build the temple on the threshing floor of Ornan the Jebusite, the place David had appointed ([[@14003001|2 Chr 3:1]]). John the Baptist said that the one who was coming would gather his wheat into the barn and burn up the chaff with unquenchable fire ([[@40003012|Matt 3:12]]).

column5: Lydia's hometown, one of the seven churches
column7: Lydia, the seller of purple, was from the city of Thyatira ([[@44016014|Acts 16:14]]). One of the seven churches in Revelation was here ([[@66001011|Rev 1:11]]; [[@66002018|Rev 2:18]]).

column5: Roman emperor in Jesus' day
column7: He was the Roman emperor during the time of Jesus' ministry. Luke records that "in the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar" the word of God came to John, the son of Zacharias, in the wilderness ([[@42003001-42003002|Luke 3:1-2]]). In the New Testament 'Caesar' is a title for the Roman emperor, and when people asked Jesus, "Is it lawful to pay taxes to Caesar, or not?" the Caesar at that time was Tiberius ([[@40022017|Matt 22:17]]). Jesus answered, "Give therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s" ([[@40022021|Matt 22:21]]).

column5: A city of Hadadezer where David took bronze
column7: A city of Hadadezer from which David took a great deal of bronze, and Solomon used it to make the bronze sea, the pillars, and the bronze vessels ([[@13018008|1 Chr 18:8]]).

column5: A rival of Omri for the throne
column7: He was the son of Ginath, and half the people of Israel wanted to make him king. Omri's side prevailed, Tibni died, and Omri became king ([[@11016021-11016022|1 Kgs 16:21-22]]).

column5: King of Goiim
column7: In Abraham’s time he was one of the four kings who fought alongside Chedorlaomer, and he was king of Goiim ([[@1014001|Gen 14:1]]; [[@1014009|Gen 14:9]]).

column5: Assyrian king who conquered northern Israel
column7: He was a king of Assyria who invaded in the days of Pekah king of Israel, took Gilead, Galilee, and all the land of Naphtali, and carried the people captive to Assyria ([[@12015029|2 Kgs 15:29]]). When Ahaz king of Judah was attacked by Syria and Israel, he sent him the silver and gold of the temple and the palace and asked for his help ([[@12016007-12016008|2 Kgs 16:7-8]]). Ahaz went to Damascus to meet him, saw the altar there, and sent back a drawing of it ([[@12016010|2 Kgs 16:10]]). Chronicles records that he carried away the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh ([[@13005026|1 Chr 5:26]]).

column5: Third river flowing out of Eden
column7: It was the third of the four rivers that flowed out of Eden, and it flowed in front of Assyria ([[@1002010|Gen 2:10]]; [[@1002014|Gen 2:14]]). Daniel saw a vision beside the river Hiddekel ([[@27010004|Dan 10:4]]).

column5: Father-in-law of the prophetess Huldah
column7: He was the father of Shallum, the husband of the prophetess Huldah ([[@12022014|2 Kgs 22:14]]). In 2 Chronicles his name is written 'Tokhath' ([[@14034022|2 Chr 34:22]]).

column5: The father of Jahzeiah in Ezra's time
column7: He was the father of Jahzeiah, who, together with Jonathan the son of Asahel, opposed the way the matter of the foreign wives was being handled in Ezra's time ([[@15010015|Ezra 10:15]]).

column5: A son of Shimon of the tribe of Judah
column7: In the genealogy of Judah, he is named as one of the sons of Shimon, along with Amnon, Rinnah, and Ben Hanan ([[@13004020|1 Chr 4:20]]).

column5: The father of blind Bartimaeus
column7: He was the father of Bartimaeus, the blind beggar sitting by the road when Jesus went out from Jericho. He is mentioned as "the son of Timaeus, Bartimaeus, a blind beggar" ([[@41010046|Mark 10:46]]).

column5: Eliphaz's concubine, mother of Amalek
column7: She was the concubine of Eliphaz, Esau's son, and she bore Amalek to Eliphaz. So Amalek is counted among the descendants of Adah, Esau's wife ([[@1036012|Gen 36:12]]).

column5: The town where Samson met a Philistine woman
column7: It was a town on the northern border of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015010|Josh 15:10]]), and its name also appears in the list of towns of the tribe of Dan ([[@6019043|Josh 19:43]]). Samson went down to Timnah, saw a woman among the daughters of the Philistines, and asked his parents to get her for him as his wife ([[@7014001-7014002|Judg 14:1-2]]). Genesis tells how Judah, going up to Timnah to shear his sheep, met his daughter-in-law Tamar sitting by the road ([[@1038012-1038014|Gen 38:12-14]]). Scholars differ on whether the Timnah in Genesis is the same place.

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: One of the towns in the hill country that the tribe of Judah received, listed with Kain and Gibeah ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015057|Josh 15:57]]).

column5: Town where Joshua lived and was buried
column7: It was the town in the hill country of Ephraim that Joshua asked for and received, and he rebuilt it and lived there ([[@6019050|Josh 19:50]]). When he died he was buried here, and Judges calls it 'Timnath Heres' ([[@6024030|Josh 24:30]]; [[@7002009|Judg 2:9]]).

column5: One of the seven chosen by the Jerusalem church
column7: One of the seven men chosen by the whole community of the Jerusalem church, picked along with Stephen and Philip ([[@44006003|Acts 6:3]]; [[@44006005|Acts 6:5]]).

column5: Paul's son in the faith and coworker
column7: He was a disciple from the area of Lystra; his mother was a Jewish believer and his father was a Greek ([[@44016001|Acts 16:1]]). He received a sincere faith from his grandmother Lois and his mother Eunice ([[@55001005|2 Tim 1:5]]). He traveled with Paul on his missionary journeys and served many churches, and his name appears with Paul's at the opening of letters such as Philippians ([[@50001001|Phil 1:1]]). Paul called him "my true child in faith" and wrote him the letters of 1 Timothy and 2 Timothy ([[@54001002|1 Tim 1:2]]).

column5: One end of Solomon's realm
column7: This place is mentioned when it says Solomon ruled over everything on this side of the River, from Tiphsah to Gaza ([[@11004024|1 Kgs 4:24]]).

column5: A town attacked by Menahem
column7: The place that Menahem king of Israel came from Tirzah and attacked because it did not open its gates to him ([[@12015016|2 Kgs 15:16]]).

column5: Son of Japheth
column7: He was one of the sons born to Noah’s son Japheth after the flood ([[@1010001-1010002|Gen 10:1-2]]). He also appears in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles ([[@13001005|1 Chr 1:5]]).

column5: King of Ethiopia
column7: He was king of Ethiopia in Hezekiah’s time. When the king of Assyria heard that he had come out to fight, he sent messengers to Hezekiah again ([[@12019009|2 Kgs 19:9]]; [[@23037009|Isa 37:9]]).

column5: A son of Caleb's concubine Maacah
column7: In the genealogy of Judah, he is named as a son whom Maacah, Caleb's concubine, bore along with Sheber ([[@13002048|1 Chr 2:48]]).

column5: A son of Jehallelel of the tribe of Judah
column7: In the genealogy of Judah, he is named as one of the sons of Jehallelel, along with Ziph, Ziphah, and Asarel ([[@13004016|1 Chr 4:16]]).

column5: A daughter of Zelophehad
column7: She was one of the five daughters of Zelophehad, the son of Hepher of the tribe of Manasseh ([[@4026033|Num 26:33]]). With her sisters she came to Moses to ask for her father's inheritance ([[@4027001|Num 27:1]]).

column5: An early capital of northern Israel
column7: Among the Canaanite kings whom Joshua and the children of Israel struck down was 'the king of Tirzah' ([[@6012007-6012024|Josh 12:7-24]]). After the kingdom was divided, it was where the kings of northern Israel lived, and Baasha became king in Tirzah and reigned twenty-four years ([[@11015033|1 Kgs 15:33]]). Zimri killed King Elah in Tirzah and was king for seven days, but when Omri besieged Tirzah, he set the palace on fire around himself and died in it ([[@11016009-11016018|1 Kgs 16:9-18]]). Omri also reigned six years in Tirzah and then bought the hill of Samaria and built a city there ([[@11016023-11016024|1 Kgs 16:23-24]]).

column5: The hometown of Elijah
column7: It was the hometown of the prophet Elijah, who was 'the Tishbite' living in Gilead ([[@11017001|1 Kgs 17:1]]; [[@11021017|1 Kgs 21:17]]).

column5: Giving a tenth of one's gain to God
column7: A tithe is a tenth of what one receives, given to God. Even before the law of Moses, Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of what he had gained ([[@1014020|Gen 14:20]]). The law says that a tenth of the grain of the land and of the fruit of the trees "is the LORD’s" ([[@3027030|Lev 27:30]]). God gave Israel's tithes to the descendants of Levi, who had no inheritance of land, in return for their work at the Tent of Meeting ([[@4018021|Num 18:21]]). The prophet Malachi urged the people to bring the whole tithe ([[@39003010|Mal 3:10]]).

column5: Paul's coworker who led the church in Crete
column7: A Greek who was Paul's son in the faith and his coworker. When he went up to Jerusalem with Paul, he was not forced to be circumcised ([[@48002003|Gal 2:3]]). He went to the church in Corinth to help with the collection, and he brought good news that comforted Paul ([[@47007006|2 Cor 7:6]]; [[@47008006|2 Cor 8:6]]). Paul left him in Crete to appoint elders in every town, and wrote him the letter to Titus ([[@56001004-56001005|Titus 1:4-5]]). In the end, we are told, he went to Dalmatia.

column5: The clan of Joha, one of David's mighty men
column7: Joha, one of the great mighty men of David's army, was a Tizite ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011045|1 Chr 11:45]]).

column5: The land where Jephthah fled
column7: It was the land where Jephthah lived after fleeing from his brothers ([[@7011003|Judg 11:3]]). The elders of Gilead went there to bring Jephthah back ([[@7011005|Judg 11:5]]).

column5: A Levite Jehoshaphat sent to teach the law
column7: One of the Levites whom King Jehoshaphat of Judah sent through the towns of Judah with the book of the law to teach the people ([[@14017008-14017009|2 Chr 17:8-9]]).

column5: Family unable to prove its ancestry
column7: 'The children of Tobiah,' who returned from exile in Babylon, could not show whether their family belonged to Israel ([[@15002059-15002060|Ezra 2:59-60]]; [[@16007062|Neh 7:62]]).

column5: The Ammonite who opposed Nehemiah's rebuilding of the wall
column7: He was an Ammonite servant who, along with Sanballat the Horonite, was deeply grieved to hear that Nehemiah had come to seek the welfare of the children of Israel ([[@16002010|Neh 2:10]]). Seeing the wall being built, he mocked, "What they are building, if a fox climbed up it, he would break down their stone wall" ([[@16004003|Neh 4:3]]). He was tied by marriage to the nobles of Judah, and he kept sending letters to make Nehemiah afraid ([[@16006017-16006019|Neh 6:17-19]]). While Nehemiah was away, the priest Eliashib prepared a room for him in the courts of God's house, but when Nehemiah returned, he threw all Tobiah's household stuff out of the room ([[@16013007-16013008|Neh 13:7-8]]).

column5: A Levite Jehoshaphat sent to teach the law
column7: One of the Levites whom King Jehoshaphat of Judah sent through the towns of Judah with the book of the law to teach the people ([[@14017008-14017009|2 Chr 17:8-9]]).

column5: Man who returned from Babylon
column7: He was one of those who had returned from Babylon. The LORD told Zechariah to take silver and gold from them, make crowns, and set them on the head of Joshua the high priest, and to keep the crowns in the temple as a memorial to Tobijah and the others ([[@38006010-38006011|Zech 6:10-11]]; [[@38006014|Zech 6:14]]).

column5: A town where the Simeonites lived
column7: One of the places where the descendants of Simeon lived, listed with Etam, Ain, Rimmon, and Ashan ([[@13004028|1 Chr 4:28]]; [[@13004032|1 Chr 4:32]]).

column5: Son of Gomer
column7: He was a grandson of Noah’s son Japheth and the son of Gomer ([[@1010002-1010003|Gen 10:2-3]]). The genealogy of 1 Chronicles also lists him as a son of Gomer ([[@13001006|1 Chr 1:6]]).

column5: Ancestor of Samuel
column7: He was the great-grandfather of Elkanah, Samuel's father. Elkanah was the son of Jeroham, the grandson of Elihu, and the great-grandson of Tohu ([[@9001001|1 Sam 1:1]]).

column5: King of Hamath who sent his son to David
column7: A king of Hamath, he heard that David had defeated the army of Hadadezer ([[@10008009|2 Sam 8:9]]). Since he had been at war with Hadadezer, he sent his son to greet David and present him with vessels ([[@10008010|2 Sam 8:10]]).

column5: Firstborn of Issachar
column7: He was the firstborn son of Issachar ([[@1046013|Gen 46:13]]). The family of the Tolaites came from him ([[@4026023|Num 26:23]]).

column5: A judge from Issachar who saved Israel
column7: A man of Issachar, the son of Puah and grandson of Dodo. After Abimelech he arose to save Israel and judged Israel for twenty-three years ([[@7010001-7010002|Judg 10:1-2]]).

column5: A town where the Simeonites lived
column7: One of the towns where the descendants of Simeon lived, and these towns belonged to them until the reign of King David ([[@13004028-13004029|1 Chr 4:28-29]]; [[@13004031|1 Chr 4:31]]).

column5: A place near where Moses spoke to Israel
column7: A place named along with Paran and Laban when describing where Moses spoke to Israel beyond the Jordan ([[@5001001|Deut 1:1]]).

column5: Place of child sacrifice in the Hinnom Valley
column7: A place in the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, south of Jerusalem, where people burned their own children in the fire as offerings to idols ([[@24007031|Jer 7:31]]). God called this something "which I didn’t command, nor did it come into my mind". King Josiah defiled Topheth so that no one could offer children to Molech there again ([[@12023010|2 Kgs 23:10]]). Jeremiah announced that it would one day be called 'the valley of Slaughter' ([[@24019006|Jer 19:6]]).

column5: Tower near Bethlehem
column7: After burying Rachel on the way to Bethlehem, Israel (Jacob) pitched his tent beyond the tower of Eder ([[@1035019-1035021|Gen 35:19-21]]).

column5: Tower on the wall of Jerusalem
column7: This was a tower on the wall of Jerusalem. In Nehemiah’s time, as the wall was rebuilt, it was sanctified as far as this tower ([[@16003001|Neh 3:1]]). Jeremiah said the city would be built again starting from the tower of Hananel ([[@24031038|Jer 31:38]]).

column5: Tower on the wall of Jerusalem
column7: This was a tower on the wall of Jerusalem that Malchijah and Hasshub repaired in Nehemiah’s time ([[@16003011|Neh 3:11]]). When the wall was dedicated, a company giving thanks passed along the wall above this tower ([[@16012038|Neh 12:38]]).

column5: A region Philip ruled as tetrarch
column7: A region that Herod's brother Philip ruled as tetrarch, together with Ituraea, in the time of Tiberius Caesar ([[@42003001|Luke 3:1]]).

column5: An offering made to repay a wrong
column7: The trespass offering was an offering made because of a wrong, especially when someone had caused loss involving the LORD's holy things or a neighbor's property. A person who unwittingly sinned regarding the LORD's holy things had to bring a ram without defect as a trespass offering, and repay what he had done wrong with a fifth part added ([[@3005015-3005016|Lev 5:15-16]]). Someone who had robbed a neighbor or dealt falsely with a deposit also had to return it in full with a fifth part added, and bring a trespass offering ([[@3006004-3006006|Lev 6:4-6]]). Isaiah foretold that the suffering Servant of the LORD would make his soul "an offering for sin" ([[@23053010|Isa 53:10]]).

column5: A coastal town of Mysia Paul visited
column7: Paul came down to it after passing by Mysia, saw a vision of a man of Macedonia in the night, and set sail from there ([[@44016008-44016011|Acts 16:8-11]]). Later he came again and stayed seven days ([[@44020006|Acts 20:6]]).

column5: A city near Ephesus, visited by Paul
column7: A town on the western coast of Asia Minor, where Paul “tarried” when on his way from Assos to Miletus, on his third missionary journey ([[@44020015|Acts 20:15]]).

column5: Ephesian companion of Paul
column7: An Ephesian, he was one of the group who went with Paul as far as Asia ([[@44020004|Acts 20:4]]; [[@44021029|Acts 21:29]]). The Jews supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple, and later he fell sick and was left at Miletus ([[@44021029|Acts 21:29]]; [[@55004020|2 Tim 4:20]]).

column5: An instrument for gathering people and giving signals
column7: The trumpet was an instrument used to gather people and give signals. When God came down on Mount Sinai, the sound of the trumpet was so loud that all the people in the camp trembled ([[@2019016|Exod 19:16]]). God had Moses make two trumpets of beaten silver to call the congregation together and to move the camps, and also had them blown when going out to war and at the feasts ([[@4010002|Num 10:2]], 9-10). At Jericho, when the priests blew the trumpets and the people gave a great shout, the wall fell down ([[@6006020|Josh 6:20]]). The New Testament says that when the Lord comes again, at the sound of God's trumpet the dead in Christ will rise first ([[@52004016|1 Thess 4:16]]).

column5: A woman in Rome whom Paul greeted
column7: A member of the church in Rome whom Paul greeted, together with Tryphosa, as one "who labor in the Lord" ([[@45016012|Rom 16:12]]).

column5: A woman in Rome whom Paul greeted
column7: A member of the church in Rome whom Paul greeted, together with Tryphaena, as one "who labor in the Lord" ([[@45016012|Rom 16:12]]).

column5: Son of Japheth
column7: He was one of the sons born to Noah’s son Japheth after the flood ([[@1010001-1010002|Gen 10:1-2]]). He also appears in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles ([[@13001005|1 Chr 1:5]]).

column5: A distant nation descended from Japheth
column7: It was a distant nation that also bore the name of one of Japheth's sons ([[@1010002|Gen 10:2]]). Along with Meshech, it traded with Tyre in people and bronze vessels ([[@26027013|Ezek 27:13]]).

column5: Faithful worker who brought Paul's news to churches
column7: He was a man from Asia who traveled with Paul as a co-worker. His name appears among those who went with Paul as far as Asia ([[@44020004|Acts 20:4]]). Paul called him "the beloved brother and faithful servant in the Lord" and sent him to tell the churches in Ephesus and Colossae how Paul was doing ([[@49006021|Eph 6:21]]; [[@51004007|Col 4:7]]). Later Paul says that he sent Tychicus to Ephesus ([[@55004012|2 Tim 4:12]]).

column5: The school where Paul taught daily
column7: In Ephesus, Paul separated the disciples and reasoned with them daily in "the school of Tyrannus", which is how this name appears ([[@44019001|Acts 19:1]]; [[@44019009|Acts 19:9]]).

column5: A Phoenician port city on the Mediterranean coast
column7: Tyre was a great Phoenician port city on the Mediterranean coast that grew very rich through sea trade. Hiram king of Tyre sent David cedar trees, carpenters, and masons to build his palace ([[@10005011|2 Sam 5:11]]), and when Solomon built the temple he also sent cedar and cypress timber ([[@11005008-11005010|1 Kgs 5:8-10]]). The prophet Ezekiel foretold that God would strike Tyre, which had rejoiced over the fall of Jerusalem ([[@26026002-26026003|Ezek 26:2-3]]). Jesus also once went to the region of Tyre and Sidon ([[@40015021|Matt 15:21]]).

column5: One to whom Agur spoke his sayings
column7: Agur the son of Jakeh spoke his proverbs to him, and he is named along with Ithiel. Proverbs 30 contains the sayings of Agur ([[@20030001|Prov 30:1]]).

column5: A son of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra's time, he is named among the sons of Bani who had taken foreign wives ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: River where Daniel saw a vision
column7: While Daniel was in the citadel of Susa in the province of Elam, he saw a vision by the river Ulai ([[@27008002|Dan 8:2]]). A voice calling to Gabriel was heard between the banks of the Ulai ([[@27008016|Dan 8:16]]).

column5: Manassite, son of Sheresh
column7: He was a descendant of Manasseh’s son Machir and the son of Sheresh ([[@13007016|1 Chr 7:16]]). His son was Bedan ([[@13007017|1 Chr 7:17]]).

column5: Firstborn of Eshek the Benjamite
column7: He was the firstborn son of Eshek, a Benjamite. His sons were mighty archers, and his sons and grandsons numbered one hundred fifty in all ([[@13008039-13008040|1 Chr 8:39-40]]).

column5: A town given to the tribe of Asher
column7: One of the towns the tribe of Asher received, named along with Aphek and Rehob ([[@6019024|Josh 19:24]]; [[@6019030|Josh 19:30]]).

column5: A descendant of Ithamar the son of Aaron.
column7: This unnamed descendant of Ithamar was an ancestor of Eli who acted as High Priest.

column5: Ancestor of Joseph, the husband of Mary.
column7: This is one of the ancestors of Joseph, the husband of Mary, the mother of Jesus.

column5: A descendant of Ithamar the son of Aaron.
column7: This unnamed descendant of Ithamar was an ancestor of Eli who acted as High Priest.

column5: Ancestor of Joseph, the husband of Mary.
column7: This is one of the ancestors of Joseph, the husband of Mary, the mother of Jesus.

column7: This unnamed descendant of Ithamar was an ancestor of Eli who acted as High Priest.
