column5: Levite harpist in David’s time
column7: He was one of the Levite singers appointed when David brought up the ark of the LORD ([[@13015018|1 Chr 15:18]]). He played a stringed instrument set to Alamoth ([[@13015020|1 Chr 15:20]]).

column5: A Levite who returned with Zerubbabel
column7: A Levite who returned with Zerubbabel; with Bakbukiah, he was close to his brothers according to their offices ([[@16012001|Neh 12:1]]; [[@16012008-16012009|Neh 12:8-9]])

column5: Place known for fine gold
column7: Jeremiah said idols are adorned with "gold from Uphaz" ([[@24010009|Jer 10:9]]). The man Daniel saw wore a belt of "pure gold of Uphaz" ([[@27010005|Dan 10:5]]).

column5: The Chaldean city Abram left
column7: It was 'Ur of the Chaldees', where Haran died, and Terah left it, taking Abram and Lot with him ([[@1011028|Gen 11:28]]; [[@1011031|Gen 11:31]]). The LORD said that he had brought Abram out of Ur of the Chaldees ([[@1015007|Gen 15:7]]).

column5: The father of Eliphal, one of David's mighty men
column7: He was the father of Eliphal, one of the great mighty men of David's army, mentioned as "Eliphal the son of Ur" ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011035|1 Chr 11:35]]).

column5: A believer in Rome Paul called a co-worker
column7: A member of the church in Rome whom Paul greeted, calling him "our fellow worker in Christ" ([[@45016009|Rom 16:9]]).

column5: Father of Bezalel, who made the tabernacle
column7: He was the son of Hur of the tribe of Judah and the father of Bezalel, who made the tabernacle ([[@2031002|Exod 31:2]]; [[@2038022|Exod 38:22]]).

column5: The father of Geber, Solomon's officer
column7: He was the father of Geber, one of Solomon's twelve officers, who was the only officer over the land of Gilead ([[@11004007|1 Kgs 4:7]]; [[@11004019|1 Kgs 4:19]]).

column5: A gatekeeper who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra's time, he is named as a gatekeeper among those who had taken foreign wives ([[@15010024|Ezra 10:24]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Bathsheba's husband, one of David's mighty men
column7: He was a Hittite and one of David's mighty men ([[@10023039|2 Sam 23:39]]). After David sinned with his wife Bathsheba, he called Uriah back from the battlefield and tried to send him home, but Uriah would not go, saying he could not go home while the ark and his fellow soldiers were out in the field ([[@10011011|2 Sam 11:11]]). Then David sent a letter to Joab by Uriah's own hand, ordering that Uriah be put at the front of the fiercest fighting so he would die, and Uriah died in that battle ([[@10011014-10011017|2 Sam 11:14-17]]). The prophet Nathan rebuked David for this ([[@10012009|2 Sam 12:9]]).

column5: A priest in King Ahaz's time
column7: He was the priest who built an altar exactly by the pattern King Ahaz sent of the altar he had seen in Damascus ([[@12016010-12016011|2 Kgs 16:10-11]]). Isaiah named him among his "faithful witnesses to testify: Uriah the priest" ([[@23008002|Isa 8:2]]).

column5: Father of the priest Meremoth
column7: He was the father of the priest Meremoth, who received the temple's silver and gold after the return from exile ([[@15008033|Ezra 8:33]]). In Nehemiah he is named as the father of Meremoth, who repaired the wall ([[@16003021|Neh 3:21]]).

column5: A man who stood at Ezra's right hand
column7: One of the men who stood at the right hand of Ezra the scribe as he stood on the wooden platform and read the book of the law ([[@16008003-16008004|Neh 8:3-4]]).

column5: Prophet put to death by Jehoiakim
column7: The son of Shemaiah of Kiriath Jearim, he prophesied against Jerusalem just as Jeremiah did ([[@24026020|Jer 26:20]]). He fled to Egypt to escape King Jehoiakim, but he was brought back and killed with the sword ([[@24026021|Jer 26:21]], 23).

column5: Kohathite, son of Tahath
column7: He was a descendant of Levi’s son Kohath and the son of Tahath. His son was Uzziah ([[@13006022-13006024|1 Chr 6:22-24]]).

column5: Kohathite chief who brought up the ark
column7: In David’s time he was chief of the sons of Kohath, leading one hundred twenty of his brothers ([[@13015005|1 Chr 15:5]]). David called him and told him to bring up the ark of the LORD ([[@13015011-13015012|1 Chr 15:11-12]]).

column5: The father of Micaiah, mother of King Abijah
column7: A man of Gibeah, the father of Micaiah, the mother of King Abijah of Judah. Abijah became king of Judah in the eighteenth year of King Jeroboam ([[@14013001-14013002|2 Chr 13:1-2]]).

column5: Means by which the high priest sought God's will
column7: The Urim and Thummim were put in the breastplate of judgment over the high priest's heart and used to ask God's will ([[@2028030|Exod 28:30]]; [[@3008008|Lev 8:8]]). Joshua was to go out and come in according to the decision that Eleazar the priest received by inquiring of the LORD by the Urim ([[@4027021|Num 27:21]]). When Saul inquired of God, no answer came, "by dreams, by Urim, or by prophets" ([[@9028006|1 Sam 28:6]]). The Bible does not say what they looked like or how they were used, so scholars differ.

column5: A descendant of Perez who lived in Jerusalem
column7: A descendant of Perez the son of Judah who lived in Jerusalem. He was the son of Ammihud ([[@13009003-13009004|1 Chr 9:3-4]]).

column5: A son of Bigvai who returned with Ezra
column7: He is named with Zabbud among the sons of Bigvai who returned with Ezra, and seventy men came with them ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008014|Ezra 8:14]]).

column5: Grandson of Shem, son of Aram
column7: He was a grandson of Noah’s son Shem and the son of Aram ([[@1010022-1010023|Gen 10:22-23]]). In 1 Chronicles he appears in the list of Shem’s sons ([[@13001017|1 Chr 1:17]]).

column5: The firstborn son of Nahor
column7: The firstborn son of Abraham's brother Nahor by his wife Milcah. His brothers included Buz and Kemuel ([[@1022020-1022021|Gen 22:20-21]]).

column5: Son of Dishan the Horite
column7: He was the son of Dishan, a chief of the Horites, the children of Seir ([[@1036021|Gen 36:21]]; [[@1036028|Gen 36:28]]). His brother was Aran ([[@13001042|1 Chr 1:42]]).

column5: Land where Job lived
column7: This is the land where Job lived ([[@18001001|Job 1:1]]). Lamentations speaks of the 'daughter of Edom, who dwells in the land of Uz' ([[@25004021|Lam 4:21]]).

column5: The father of Palal, who repaired the wall
column7: He was the father of Palal, who repaired part of the wall of Jerusalem in Nehemiah's time. Palal repaired the section opposite the turning of the wall and the tower that stands out from the upper house of the king ([[@16003025|Neh 3:25]]).

column5: Son of Joktan
column7: He was one of the sons of Joktan, the son of Shem’s descendant Eber ([[@1010025-1010027|Gen 10:25-27]]). He also appears in the genealogy of 1 Chronicles ([[@13001021|1 Chr 1:21]]).

column5: A place mentioned in Ezekiel's prophecy
column7: A wanderer, a descendant of Joktan ([[@1010027|Gen. 10:27]]; [[@13001021|1 Chr. 1:21]]), the founder apparently of one of the Arab tribes; the name also probably of the province they occupied and of their chief city.

column5: Garden where Manasseh and Amon were buried
column7: This was the palace garden where Manasseh king of Judah was buried ([[@12021018|2 Kgs 21:18]]). His son Amon is also said to have been buried "in his tomb in the garden of Uzza" ([[@12021026|2 Kgs 21:26]]).

column5: Uzza in the genealogy of Benjamin
column7: A man named with Ahihud in the family genealogy of Ehud of the tribe of Benjamin ([[@13008006-13008007|1 Chr 8:6-7]]).

column5: Temple-servant family back from exile
column7: Among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon were 'the children of Uzza' ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]]; [[@15002049|Ezra 2:49]]; [[@16007051|Neh 7:51]]).

column5: Son of Abinadab, struck down beside the ark
column7: He was the son of Abinadab, and when God's ark was carried on a new cart, he and his brother Ahio drove the cart ([[@10006003|2 Sam 6:3]]). At the threshing floor of Nacon, when the cattle stumbled, Uzzah reached out his hand and took hold of God's ark ([[@10006006|2 Sam 6:6]]). The LORD God was angry with Uzzah for his error and struck him, and he died there beside God's ark ([[@10006007|2 Sam 6:7]]). David called that place Perez Uzzah, and out of fear he did not bring the ark into David's city but had it carried aside to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite ([[@10006008-10006010|2 Sam 6:8-10]]).

column5: A son of Shimei, a Merarite
column7: In the genealogy of Merari the son of Levi, he appears as the son of Shimei. His son was Shimea ([[@13006029-13006030|1 Chr 6:29-30]]).

column5: A town built by Sheerah
column7: A town built by Sheerah, the daughter of Ephraim. Sheerah built it along with Lower and Upper Beth Horon ([[@13007024|1 Chr 7:24]]).

column5: A man in the priestly line of Aaron
column7: He was a descendant of Aaron, the son of Bukki and the father of Zerahiah ([[@13006005-13006006|1 Chr 6:5-6]]). He also appears in Ezra's genealogy ([[@15007004|Ezra 7:4]]).

column5: Issacharite, son of Tola
column7: He was a son of Tola, Issachar’s son, and a head of Tola’s family ([[@13007001-13007002|1 Chr 7:1-2]]). His son was Izrahiah ([[@13007003|1 Chr 7:3]]).

column5: A son of Bela of the tribe of Benjamin
column7: One of the five sons of Bela the son of Benjamin, a head of his father's house and a mighty man of valor ([[@13007006-13007007|1 Chr 7:6-7]]).

column5: The father of Elah, a Benjamite in Jerusalem
column7: Among the descendants of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem, he was the father of Elah and the son of Michri ([[@13009007-13009008|1 Chr 9:7-8]]).

column5: Overseer of the Levites in Jerusalem
column7: The son of Bani, he became overseer of the Levites living in Jerusalem, and he was one of the singers responsible for the service of God's house ([[@16011022|Neh 11:22]])

column5: Head of Jedaiah's family under Joiakim
column7: In the days of Joiakim, he was head of the family of Jedaiah among the heads of the priestly families ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012019|Neh 12:19]]).

column5: A man present at the wall's dedication
column7: One of the people who stood together with Maaseiah, Shemaiah, and others when the wall of Jerusalem was dedicated ([[@16012042|Neh 12:42]]).

column5: An Ashterathite among David's mighty men
column7: One of the great mighty men of David's army, an Ashterathite ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011044|1 Chr 11:44]]).

column5: Judah's king for fifty-two years, also called Azariah
column7: He was the son of Amaziah; he became king of Judah at sixteen and reigned fifty-two years in Jerusalem ([[@14026003|2 Chr 26:3]]). In 2 Kings he mostly appears under the name Azariah ([[@12015001|2 Kgs 15:1]]). He prospered as long as he sought God, but when he grew strong, his heart became proud, and he went into the LORD's temple to burn incense on the altar of incense himself. Then leprosy broke out on his forehead, and he lived alone in a separate house until the day he died ([[@14026016-14026021|2 Chr 26:16-21]]). "In the year that King Uzziah died," Isaiah saw the Lord on a throne, high and lifted up ([[@23006001|Isa 6:1]]).

column5: Kohathite, son of Uriel
column7: He was a descendant of Levi’s son Kohath and the son of Uriel. His son was Shaul ([[@13006022-13006024|1 Chr 6:22-24]]).

column5: The father of Jonathan, David's storehouse keeper
column7: He was the father of Jonathan, who, among those in charge of King David's property, was over the storehouses in the fields, cities, villages, and towers ([[@13027025|1 Chr 27:25]]; [[@13027031|1 Chr 27:31]]).

column5: A son of Harim who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra's time, he is named among the sons of Harim who had taken foreign wives ([[@15010021|Ezra 10:21]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: The father of Athaiah in Jerusalem
column7: After the exile, he was the father of Athaiah, a descendant of Perez among the people of Judah who lived in Jerusalem ([[@16011004|Neh 11:4]]).

column5: Son of Kohath, uncle of Moses and Aaron
column7: A grandson of Levi and the fourth son of Kohath, he was the younger brother of Amram, the father of Moses and Aaron ([[@2006018|Exod 6:18]]). His sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri ([[@2006022|Exod 6:22]]). When Nadab and Abihu died, Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan, "the sons of Uzziel the uncle of Aaron", and had them carry the bodies out of the camp ([[@3010004|Lev 10:4]]). His descendants formed one branch of the Kohathite clan ([[@4003027|Num 3:27]]).

column5: A captain of the Simeonites
column7: One of the four men whom five hundred Simeonites took as their captains; they went to Mount Seir and struck the remaining Amalekites ([[@13004042-13004043|1 Chr 4:42-43]]).

column5: A grandson of Benjamin, son of Bela
column7: One of the five sons of Bela the son of Benjamin, a head of his father's house and a mighty man of valor ([[@13007006-13007007|1 Chr 7:6-7]]).

column5: Son of Heman, temple musician
column7: He was one of the sons of Heman, who sang in the temple in David’s time ([[@13025004|1 Chr 25:4]]). Some take him to be the same person as 'Azarel' of the eleventh lot ([[@13025018|1 Chr 25:18]]).

column5: A Levite descended from Jeduthun
column7: He is named among the descendants of Jeduthun when the Levites arose in Hezekiah's time ([[@14029012|2 Chr 29:12]]; [[@14029014|2 Chr 29:14]]).

column5: A goldsmith who repaired the wall
column7: The son of Harhaiah, one of the goldsmiths, he repaired a section of the wall of Jerusalem with others in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003008|Neh 3:8]]).

column5: One of the ten sons of Haman
column7: One of the ten sons of Haman, the enemy of the Jews, he was killed by the Jews in the citadel of Susa ([[@17009006-17009010|Esth 9:6-10]]).

column5: A gate in the wall of Jerusalem
column7: Uzziah built towers at this gate and fortified them ([[@14026009|2 Chr 26:9]]). Nehemiah went out by this gate at night to inspect the broken walls, and Hanun and the inhabitants of Zanoah repaired it ([[@16002013|Neh 2:13]]; [[@16003013|Neh 3:13]]).

column5: A son of Bani who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra's time, he is named among the sons of Bani who had taken foreign wives ([[@15010034|Ezra 10:34]]; [[@15010036|Ezra 10:36]]).

column5: Persian queen removed for refusing the king's command
column7: She was the queen of King Ahasuerus of Persia, and she gave a feast for the women in the royal house of Ahasuerus ([[@17001009|Esth 1:9]]). The king ordered her to come wearing the royal crown to show off her beauty, but Vashti refused to come, and the king was very angry ([[@17001011-17001012|Esth 1:11-12]]). The official Memucan advised that Vashti never again come before the king, and the king did as he said ([[@17001019-17001021|Esth 1:19-21]]). Afterward the king made Esther queen in place of Vashti ([[@17002017|Esth 2:17]]).

column5: A place that traded with Tyre
column7: A place mentioned with Javan in Ezekiel's words about Tyre; it traded with Tyre in wrought iron, cassia, and calamus ([[@26027019|Ezek 27:19]]). Scholars differ on where it was.

column5: A plant that bears grapes
column7: The vine was an important fruit plant in the land of Canaan. In the Bible it first appears when Noah began farming and planted vines ([[@1009020|Gen 9:20]]). The spies Moses sent cut down a branch with one cluster of grapes in the valley of Eshcol and carried it on a staff between two of them ([[@4013023|Num 13:23]]). Isaiah compared Israel to a vineyard planted with the choicest vine that yielded wild grapes ([[@23005001-23005002|Isa 5:1-2]], 7). Jesus said, "I am the vine. You are the branches", and he said that whoever remains in him bears much fruit ([[@43015005|John 15:5]]).

column5: Father of Nahbi, the spy from Naphtali
column7: His son Nahbi of the tribe of Naphtali was one of the men Moses sent to spy out Canaan ([[@4013014|Num 13:14]]).

column5: A place named in the Book of the Wars of the LORD
column7: A quotation from 'the Book of the Wars of the LORD' mentions "Vaheb in Suphah, the valleys of the Arnon" ([[@4021014|Num 21:14]]). Its exact location is unknown.

column5: Field by the upper pool in Jerusalem
column7: It was a field by the conduit of the upper pool in Jerusalem, where Isaiah went to meet King Ahaz ([[@23007003|Isa 7:3]]). The commanders sent by the king of Assyria also came and stood on the highway here ([[@12018017|2 Kgs 18:17]]).

column5: The Jerusalem gate where Ezra read the law
column7: It was a gate on the east side of Jerusalem ([[@16003026|Neh 3:26]]). All the people gathered in the square before the Water Gate, and Ezra read the book of the law from early morning until midday ([[@16008001-16008003|Neh 8:1-3]]).

column5: The highway for those who walk in the Way
column7: The highway Isaiah foresaw: the unclean shall not pass over it, but it will be for those who walk in the Way ([[@23035008|Isa 35:8]])

column5: The unnamed grandmother of Jesus.
column7: The wife of Heli was sister of Elizather who mothered John the Baptist.

column5: Rocks in the wilderness of En Gedi
column7: When Saul heard that David was in the wilderness of En Gedi, he took three thousand chosen men and went here to look for David ([[@9024001-9024002|1 Sam 24:1-2]]).

column5: A drink made from grapes
column7: Wine is a drink made from grapes, and people commonly drank it in Bible times. The Psalms sing that God gives "wine that makes the heart of man glad" ([[@19104015|Ps 104:15]]). But the Bible warns against drunkenness, as in the time Noah got drunk on wine and lay uncovered inside his tent ([[@1009021|Gen 9:21]]; [[@20020001|Prov 20:1]]). Jesus did his first sign by turning water into wine at a wedding feast in Cana of Galilee ([[@43002009-43002011|John 2:9-11]]), and Paul urged, "Don’t be drunken with wine, in which is dissipation, but be filled with the Spirit" ([[@49005018|Eph 5:18]]).

column5: Tossing grain so the wind blows away the chaff
column7: Winnowing is putting threshed grain in a winnowing tray and tossing it so that the wind blows away the husks and chaff. In the Bible it often appears as the verb 'winnow'. Boaz winnowed barley at night on the threshing floor ([[@8003002|Ruth 3:2]]). Isaiah said that Israel would winnow its enemies and the wind would carry them away ([[@23041016|Isa 41:16]]). John the Baptist said that the one who was coming would have his winnowing fork in his hand and would cleanse his threshing floor, gathering the wheat into the barn and burning the chaff with unquenchable fire ([[@40003012|Matt 3:12]]).

column5: Men in royal courts who interpreted dreams and gave wisdom
column7: In the Bible, wise men were learned people in ancient royal courts who interpreted dreams and gave wise counsel. When Pharaoh was troubled by his dreams, he called all of Egypt's magicians and wise men, but no one could interpret the dreams ([[@1041008|Gen 41:8]]). The king of Babylon in his fury commanded that all the wise men be destroyed, and Daniel, who explained the dream, later became chief over all the wise men of Babylon ([[@27002012|Dan 2:12]], 48). When Jesus was born, wise men from the east saw his star and came to worship the child, offering him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh ([[@40002001-40002002|Matt 2:1-2]], 11).

column5: Gate in the wall of Jerusalem
column7: This was a gate in the wall of Jerusalem that Joiada and Meshullam repaired in Nehemiah’s time ([[@16003006|Neh 3:6]]). When the wall was dedicated, a company giving thanks passed by the old gate ([[@16012039|Neh 12:39]]).

column5: A town of the tribe of Naphtali
column7: One of the fortified cities the tribe of Naphtali received as their inheritance in Joshua's time ([[@6019032|Josh 19:32]]; [[@6019038|Josh 19:38]]).

column5: A place in Micah's prophecy
column7: When Micah lamented over the towns of Judah, he said, "The inhabitant of Zaanan won’t come out" ([[@33001011|Mic 1:11]]).

column5: Place with an oak on Naphtali’s border
column7: It was a place on the border of the land of the tribe of Naphtali ([[@6019033|Josh 19:33]]). Heber the Kenite pitched his tent by the oak in Zaanannim near Kedesh ([[@7004011|Judg 4:11]]).

column5: Son of Ezer the Horite
column7: He was a son of Ezer, a chief of the Horites, the children of Seir, and his brothers were Bilhan and Akan ([[@1036021|Gen 36:21]]; [[@1036027|Gen 36:27]]). In 1 Chronicles 'Akan' is written 'Jaakan' ([[@13001042|1 Chr 1:42]]).

column5: Son of Nathan, of Jerahmeel’s line in Judah
column7: He was a descendant of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah and the son of Nathan ([[@13002036|1 Chr 2:36]]). His son was Ephlal ([[@13002037|1 Chr 2:37]]).

column5: An Ephraimite, son of Tahath
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Ephraim as the son of Tahath, and his son was Shuthelah ([[@13007020-13007021|1 Chr 7:20-21]]). The Bible tells nothing more about him.

column5: One of David's mighty men, son of Ahlai
column7: The son of Ahlai, he is named in the list of David's great mighty men together with Uriah the Hittite ([[@13011026|1 Chr 11:26]]; [[@13011041|1 Chr 11:41]]).

column5: A son of Zattu who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra's time, he is named among the sons of Zattu who had taken foreign wives ([[@15010027|Ezra 10:27]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A son of Hashum who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra's time, he is named among the sons of Hashum who had taken foreign wives ([[@15010033|Ezra 10:33]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A son of Nebo who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra's time, he is named among the sons of Nebo who had taken foreign wives ([[@15010043-15010044|Ezra 10:43-44]]).

column5: A son of Bebai who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra's time, he is named among the sons of Bebai who had taken foreign wives ([[@15010028|Ezra 10:28]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: Father of Baruch, who repaired the wall
column7: His son Baruch earnestly repaired a section of the wall of Jerusalem, starting from the turning of the wall, in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003020|Neh 3:20]]).

column5: The grandfather of Achan
column7: He was of the family of the Zerahites in the tribe of Judah, and the grandfather of Achan ([[@6007001|Josh 7:1]]). When Joshua searched for the one who had sinned, Zabdi was taken from among the Zerahites, and from his household Achan was taken ([[@6007017-6007018|Josh 7:17-18]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Shimei
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin as one of the sons of Shimei ([[@13008019|1 Chr 8:19]]; [[@13008021|1 Chr 8:21]]). The Bible tells nothing more about him.

column5: Keeper of David's wine cellars
column7: A Shiphmite who was in charge of the produce of the vineyards for the wine cellars in David's time. Shimei the Ramathite was over the vineyards ([[@13027027|1 Chr 27:27]]).

column5: Father of Jashobeam
column7: His son Jashobeam was over the first division for the first month in David's time. There were twenty-four thousand in that division ([[@13027002|1 Chr 27:2]]).

column5: Overseer of the priests after the exile
column7: The son of Haggedolim, he became overseer of one hundred twenty-eight of the priests' brothers who lived in Jerusalem after returning from exile ([[@16011014|Neh 11:14]]).

column5: Solomon's chief minister, the king's friend
column7: The son of Nathan, he was chief minister and 'the king's friend' in Solomon's time. Nathan's other son Azariah was over the officers ([[@11004005|1 Kgs 4:5]]).

column5: Family that returned from exile
column7: Among those who returned from exile in Babylon, 'the children of Zaccai' numbered seven hundred sixty ([[@15002009|Ezra 2:9]]; [[@16007014|Neh 7:14]]).

column5: Chief tax collector who welcomed Jesus
column7: He was a chief tax collector and a rich man whom Jesus met while passing through Jericho ([[@42019001-42019002|Luke 19:1-2]]). When Jesus stayed at his house, he said he would give half of his goods to the poor and pay back four times anything he had taken wrongfully ([[@42019005|Luke 19:5]], 8).

column5: Father of Shammua, the spy from Reuben
column7: His son Shammua of the tribe of Reuben was one of the men Moses sent to spy out Canaan ([[@4013004|Num 13:4]]).

column5: A Simeonite, son of Hammuel
column7: In the genealogy of Mishma of the tribe of Simeon, he appears as the son of Hammuel and the father of Shimei ([[@13004025-13004026|1 Chr 4:25-26]]).

column5: A Levite descended from Merari
column7: One of the descendants of Merari through Jaaziah, listed with Beno, Shoham, and Ibri ([[@13024027|1 Chr 24:27]]).

column5: Son of Asaph, a singer
column7: A son of Asaph, he served in prophetic music under his father in King David's time ([[@13025002|1 Chr 25:2]]). Among the divisions of singers, the third lot fell to him ([[@13025010|1 Chr 25:10]]).

column5: A son of Bigvai who returned with Ezra
column7: Among those who came up from Babylon with Ezra, he was one of the sons of Bigvai, and together with Uthai he led seventy men ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008014|Ezra 8:14]]).

column5: Son of Imri, who built part of the wall
column7: The son of Imri, he built the section of the wall of Jerusalem next to the men of Jericho in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003002|Neh 3:2]]).

column5: A Levite who sealed the covenant
column7: He is named among the Levites who made a sure covenant and sealed it in Nehemiah's time ([[@16009038|Neh 9:38]]; [[@16010009-16010012|Neh 10:9-12]]).

column5: Father of Hanan, the treasurers' assistant
column7: His son Hanan, grandson of Mattaniah, was appointed to assist the treasurers in Nehemiah's time ([[@16013013|Neh 13:13]]).

column5: A priest in the days of David and Solomon
column7: Zadok was the son of Ahitub, and in David's time he became priest together with Ahimelech the son of Abiathar ([[@10008017|2 Sam 8:17]]). When Absalom rebelled, Zadok came out with David carrying the ark of the covenant, but at David's word he carried the ark back to Jerusalem ([[@10015024-10015029|2 Sam 15:24-29]]). When Adonijah tried to make himself king, Zadok also stood on David's side and anointed Solomon ([[@11001039|1 Kgs 1:39]]). Solomon made Zadok priest in place of Abiathar ([[@11002035|1 Kgs 2:35]]).

column5: Grandfather of King Jotham
column7: He was the father of Jerusha, the mother of Jotham king of Judah ([[@12015033|2 Kgs 15:33]]). Jotham did what was right, just as his father Uzziah had done ([[@14027001-14027002|2 Chr 27:1-2]]).

column5: Ancestor in a priestly family
column7: He appears in the genealogy of a priestly family as the son of Meraioth and the father of Meshullam ([[@13009011|1 Chr 9:11]]). His name also appears in the same place in the genealogy in Nehemiah ([[@16011011|Neh 11:11]]).

column5: Son of Baana, who repaired the wall
column7: The son of Baana, he repaired the section of the wall of Jerusalem next to Meremoth and Meshullam in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003004|Neh 3:4]]).

column5: Son of Immer, who repaired the wall
column7: The son of Immer, he repaired the section of the wall across from his own house in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003029|Neh 3:29]]).

column5: A leader of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: He is named among the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]; [[@16010021|Neh 10:21]]).

column5: A scribe Nehemiah made a treasurer
column7: A scribe whom Nehemiah appointed as a treasurer, together with Shelemiah the priest and Pedaiah the Levite ([[@16013013|Neh 13:13]]).

column5: A son of Rehoboam
column7: One of the sons that King Rehoboam of Judah had by his wife Mahalath ([[@14011018-14011019|2 Chr 11:18-19]]).

column5: Father of Hanun, who repaired the wall
column7: His sixth son Hanun repaired a section of the wall of Jerusalem in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003030|Neh 3:30]]).

column5: Ahohite among David’s mighty men
column7: He was an Ahohite, one of David’s mighty men ([[@10023028|2 Sam 23:28]]). In 1 Chronicles he appears as 'Ilai the Ahohite' ([[@13011029|1 Chr 11:29]]).

column5: Campsite on the wilderness journey
column7: This is a place where Israel camped after leaving Mount Hor on their journey through the wilderness. From there they went on to Punon ([[@4033041-4033042|Num 33:41-42]]).

column5: A Midianite king defeated by Gideon
column7: Along with Zebah, he was one of the two kings of Midian, and Gideon pursued them ([[@7008005|Judg 8:5]]). Gideon killed Zebah and Zalmunna and took the ornaments on their camels ([[@7008021|Judg 8:21]]).

column5: A town in the lowland of Judah
column7: It was one of the lowland towns of the tribe of Judah ([[@6015033-6015034|Josh 15:33-34]]). The inhabitants of Zanoah repaired the Valley Gate in Nehemiah's time ([[@16003013|Neh 3:13]]).

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: It is named as one of the towns in the hill country that the tribe of Judah received as an inheritance ([[@6015048|Josh 15:48]]; [[@6015056|Josh 15:56]]).

column5: A valley town given to the tribe of Gad
column7: It was a town in the valley that Moses gave to the tribe of Gad, land that had belonged to the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon ([[@6013027|Josh 13:27]]).

column5: The Sidonian town where Elijah stayed with a widow
column7: It was a town belonging to Sidon, where the LORD sent Elijah to a widow who would feed him ([[@11017009-11017010|1 Kgs 17:9-10]]). Jesus spoke of her as 'a widow in Zarephath' ([[@42004026|Luke 4:26]]).

column5: A place by the Jordan
column7: When Israel crossed the Jordan, the flowing water rose up in a heap far off "at Adam, the city that is beside Zarethan" ([[@6003016|Josh 3:16]]). Solomon cast the bronze vessels between Succoth and Zarethan ([[@11007046|1 Kgs 7:46]]).

column5: A family that returned from exile
column7: It was the name of a family that returned from exile, and the descendants of Zattu numbered nine hundred forty-five ([[@15002008|Ezra 2:8]]). Some of his descendants had married foreign women ([[@15010027|Ezra 10:27]]).

column5: A leader of the people who sealed the covenant
column7: He is named among the chiefs of the people who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time, along with Parosh, Pahathmoab, and Elam ([[@16010014|Neh 10:14]]).

column5: A son of Jonathan, of Jerahmeel's line
column7: In the genealogy of Jerahmeel of the tribe of Judah, he is named as a son of Jonathan, along with Peleth ([[@13002032-13002033|1 Chr 2:32-33]]).

column5: A name given to Simon of the Twelve
column7: The Zealots were a group of Jews who refused to pay taxes to Rome and resisted it, and the name was given to Simon, one of Jesus' twelve disciples. Luke called him "Simon who was called the Zealot", and Matthew wrote "Simon the Zealot" ([[@42006015|Luke 6:15]]; [[@40010004|Matt 10:4]]). After Jesus went up to heaven, he gathered with the other apostles in the upper room, and with one accord they devoted themselves to prayer ([[@44001013-44001014|Acts 1:13-14]]). The Bible does not say in detail what Simon's connection with this group was.

column5: A Benjamite, son of Beriah
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin as one of the sons of Beriah ([[@13008015-13008016|1 Chr 8:15-16]]). The Bible tells nothing more about him.

column5: A Benjamite, son of Elpaal
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin as one of the sons of Elpaal ([[@13008017-13008018|1 Chr 8:17-18]]). The Bible tells nothing more about him.

column5: A warrior who helped David at Ziklag
column7: The son of Jeroham of Gedor, he was one of the mighty men of the tribe of Benjamin who came to David at Ziklag and helped him in battle ([[@13012001-13012002|1 Chr 12:1-2]]; [[@13012007|1 Chr 12:7]]).

column5: Third son of Meshelemiah
column7: The third son of Meshelemiah, a Korahite doorkeeper, he is named in the divisions of the temple doorkeepers ([[@13026001-13026002|1 Chr 26:1-2]]).

column5: Son of Asahel, a commander under David
column7: The son of Asahel, Joab's brother, he is named as commander after his father over the division for the fourth month in David's time ([[@13027007|1 Chr 27:7]]).

column5: A Levite Jehoshaphat sent out
column7: One of the Levites whom King Jehoshaphat sent to the towns of Judah to teach ([[@14017007-14017008|2 Chr 17:7-8]]).

column5: A leader of Judah over the king's matters
column7: The son of Ishmael and ruler of the house of Judah, he was put in charge of all the king's matters in Jehoshaphat's time ([[@14019011|2 Chr 19:11]]).

column5: Son of Michael, who returned with Ezra
column7: The son of Michael, he came up from Babylon with Ezra, with eighty men ([[@15008008|Ezra 8:8]]).

column5: A son of Immer who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra's time, he is named among the sons of Immer who had taken foreign wives ([[@15010020|Ezra 10:20]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A Midianite king defeated by Gideon
column7: Along with Zalmunna, he was one of the two kings of Midian, and Gideon chased them ([[@7008005|Judg 8:5]]). In the end Gideon killed Zebah and Zalmunna ([[@7008021|Judg 8:21]]).

column5: Father of the apostles James and John
column7: He was the father of James and John, two of the twelve apostles ([[@40010002|Matt 10:2]]). When Jesus called his two sons, Zebedee was in the boat with them mending their nets, and the two sons immediately left the boat and their father and followed Jesus ([[@40004021-40004022|Matt 4:21-22]]). Mark says he was left in the boat with the hired servants ([[@41001020|Mark 1:20]]). Among the women who watched from afar when Jesus was crucified was the mother of the sons of Zebedee ([[@40027055-40027056|Matt 27:55-56]]).

column5: Mother of King Jehoiakim
column7: The mother of King Jehoiakim of Judah, the daughter of Pedaiah of Rumah. Jehoiakim became king at twenty-five ([[@12023036|2 Kgs 23:36]]).

column5: A son of Nebo who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra's time, he is named among the sons of Nebo who had taken foreign wives ([[@15010043-15010044|Ezra 10:43-44]]).

column5: A city destroyed along with Sodom
column7: It was a city near Sodom, Gomorrah, and Admah, and its king was Shemeber ([[@1014002|Gen 14:2]]). It was one of the cities the LORD overthrew in his anger ([[@5029023|Deut 29:23]]).

column5: A place where Benjamites lived
column7: One of the places where the people of Benjamin lived after returning from exile ([[@16011031|Neh 11:31]]; [[@16011034|Neh 11:34]]).

column5: A valley toward the wilderness
column7: In Saul's time, one company of Philistine raiders turned toward the border road that looks down on the valley of Zeboim ([[@9013017-9013018|1 Sam 13:17-18]]).

column5: Ruler of the city of Shechem under Abimelech
column7: He was the ruler of the city of Shechem, and he grew angry when he heard the words of Gaal the son of Ebed ([[@7009028|Judg 9:28]]; [[@7009030|Judg 9:30]]). He told Gaal to go out and fight Abimelech ([[@7009038|Judg 9:38]]).

column5: The sixth son of Jacob and Leah
column7: Zebulun was the sixth son Jacob had by Leah. Leah named him, saying, "Now my husband will live with me" ([[@1030020|Gen 30:20]]). When they went down to Egypt, he had three sons: Sered, Elon, and Jahleel ([[@1046014|Gen 46:14]]). Jacob blessed him, saying, "Zebulun will dwell at the haven of the sea" ([[@1049013|Gen 49:13]]). The tribe of Zebulun received land in Galilee, and this land appears in Isaiah's words that foretold Jesus' ministry ([[@40004015|Matt 4:15]]).

column5: Son of Jeroboam, king of Israel
column7: The son of Jeroboam, he succeeded his father as king of Israel ([[@12014029|2 Kgs 14:29]]). He reigned in Samaria for six months and was killed in Shallum's conspiracy ([[@12015008|2 Kgs 15:8]], 10).

column5: Grandfather of King Hezekiah
column7: He was the father of Abijah, the mother of Hezekiah king of Judah ([[@14029001|2 Chr 29:1]]). In 2 Kings she is called Abi, the daughter of Zechariah ([[@12018002|2 Kgs 18:2]]).

column5: A chief of the Reubenites
column7: Among the brothers of Beerah of the tribe of Reuben, he was a chief by family and genealogy, named along with Jeiel ([[@13005006-13005007|1 Chr 5:6-7]]).

column5: Firstborn of Meshelemiah, gatekeeper of the Tent
column7: He was the firstborn son of Meshelemiah, a Levite ([[@13026002|1 Chr 26:2]]). He became the gatekeeper of the Tent of Meeting ([[@13009021|1 Chr 9:21]]). When the gatekeepers cast lots for the gates they would guard, Zechariah was called "a wise counselor," and he was given the north gate ([[@13026014|1 Chr 26:14]]). There is also a Levite named Zechariah who played a stringed instrument before the ark in David's time ([[@13015020|1 Chr 15:20]]), and scholars differ on whether he is the same man.

column5: A Levite, son of Isshiah
column7: The son of Isshiah, Micah's brother, he appears in the genealogy of the Levites who cast lots for their divisions before King David ([[@13024025|1 Chr 24:25]]; [[@13024031|1 Chr 24:31]]).

column5: Fourth son of Hosah, a Merarite
column7: The fourth son of Hosah, a descendant of Merari, he is named among the divisions of the temple doorkeepers ([[@13026010-13026011|1 Chr 26:10-11]]).

column5: Father of Iddo, leader of Manasseh in Gilead
column7: His son Iddo was the leader of the half-tribe of Manasseh in Gilead in David's time ([[@13027021|1 Chr 27:21]]).

column5: An official Jehoshaphat sent out
column7: One of the princes whom King Jehoshaphat sent to the towns of Judah to teach in the third year of his reign ([[@14017007|2 Chr 17:7]]).

column5: Father of Jahaziel the Levite
column7: His son was Jahaziel, the Levite on whom the LORD's Spirit came in Jehoshaphat's time ([[@14020014|2 Chr 20:14]]).

column5: A son of King Jehoshaphat
column7: One of the sons of King Jehoshaphat of Judah, named along with Jehoram's brothers ([[@14021002|2 Chr 21:2]]).

column5: Priest killed in the temple court
column7: The son of the priest Jehoiada, he was moved by the Spirit of God to rebuke the people who had forsaken the LORD ([[@14024020|2 Chr 24:20]]). At King Joash's command he was stoned to death in the court of the LORD's house ([[@14024021|2 Chr 24:21]]).

column5: A man who understood visions in Uzziah's day
column7: He was a man "who had understanding in the vision of God", and King Uzziah sought God in his days ([[@14026005|2 Chr 26:5]]).

column5: A Levite descended from Asaph
column7: He is named among the descendants of Asaph when the Levites arose in Hezekiah's time ([[@14029012-14029013|2 Chr 29:12-13]]).

column5: A Kohathite who oversaw temple repairs
column7: A Levite of the Kohathites who oversaw the repair of the LORD's house in Josiah's time ([[@14034012|2 Chr 34:12]]).

column5: A ruler of God's house
column7: One of the rulers of God's house in Josiah's time, he gave Passover offerings to the priests ([[@14035008|2 Chr 35:8]]).

column5: The prophet who encouraged rebuilding the temple
column7: He was the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, a prophet who received the word of the LORD in the second year of King Darius ([[@38001001|Zech 1:1]]). He prophesied with Haggai, and through their encouragement the building of the temple prospered ([[@15005001|Ezra 5:1]]; [[@15006014|Ezra 6:14]]).

column5: A descendant of Parosh who returned with Ezra
column7: When he came up with Ezra, one hundred fifty men of the sons of Parosh listed by genealogy were with him ([[@15008003|Ezra 8:3]]).

column5: Son of Bebai, who returned with Ezra
column7: The son of Bebai, he came up from Babylon with Ezra, with twenty-eight men ([[@15008001|Ezra 8:1]]; [[@15008011|Ezra 8:11]]).

column5: A leader Ezra sent for
column7: One of the chief men Ezra sent for at the river when he found that there were no Levites ([[@15008015-15008016|Ezra 8:15-16]]).

column5: A son of Elam who married a foreign wife
column7: In Ezra's time, he is named among the sons of Elam who had taken foreign wives ([[@15010026|Ezra 10:26]]; [[@15010044|Ezra 10:44]]).

column5: A man who stood beside Ezra
column7: One of the men who stood at Ezra's left hand as he stood on the wooden platform and read the law ([[@16008004|Neh 8:4]]).

column5: An ancestor of Athaiah in Jerusalem
column7: He appears in the genealogy as the grandfather of Athaiah, a descendant of Perez of the tribe of Judah who lived in Jerusalem ([[@16011004|Neh 11:4]]).

column5: An ancestor of Maaseiah in Jerusalem
column7: An ancestor of Maaseiah, who lived in Jerusalem after the return from exile; the genealogy shows Maaseiah as his descendant six generations later ([[@16011005|Neh 11:5]]).

column5: An ancestor of Adaiah the priest
column7: He appears in the genealogy as an ancestor of Adaiah, a priest who worked in the house of God in Jerusalem ([[@16011010|Neh 11:10]]; [[@16011012|Neh 11:12]]).

column5: Head of the priestly family of Iddo
column7: In the days of Joiakim, he was a head of a priestly family, leading the family of Iddo. The head of the family of Ginnethon was Meshullam ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012016|Neh 12:16]]).

column5: A descendant of Asaph who played the trumpet
column7: One of the priests' sons who played trumpets at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem, a descendant of Asaph six generations later ([[@16012027|Neh 12:27]]; [[@16012035|Neh 12:35]]).

column5: A priest who blew a trumpet at the wall's dedication
column7: One of the priests who played trumpets at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem ([[@16012027|Neh 12:27]]; [[@16012041|Neh 12:41]]).

column5: Son of Jeberechiah, a faithful witness
column7: The son of Jeberechiah, he was called, along with Uriah the priest, to be one of the "faithful witnesses" when Isaiah wrote Maher Shalal Hash Baz on a tablet ([[@23008001-23008002|Isa 8:1-2]]).

column5: Priest, father of John the Baptist
column7: He was a priest of the division of Abijah in the days of Herod, king of Judea, and he and his wife Elizabeth were righteous before God but had no children ([[@42001005-42001007|Luke 1:5-7]]). While he was burning incense in the sanctuary, an angel appeared and told him, "Your wife, Elizabeth, will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John" ([[@42001013|Luke 1:13]]). Because Zacharias did not believe, saying he was old, he was made unable to speak until it came to pass ([[@42001018-42001020|Luke 1:18-20]]). After the child was born, he wrote on a tablet, "His name is John", and his mouth was opened and he praised God, and he was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied ([[@42001063-42001067|Luke 1:63-67]]).

column5: Son of Jeiel, father of Gibeon
column7: He was one of the sons of Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, and his wife Maacah ([[@13008029-13008031|1 Chr 8:29-31]]). In 1 Chronicles 9 he is called 'Zechariah' ([[@13009037|1 Chr 9:37]]).

column5: Place on the northern border of the promised land
column7: The northern border of the land God gave reached from the entrance of Hamath to Zedad ([[@4034008|Num 34:8]]). Ezekiel also named Zedad when describing the northern border ([[@26047015|Ezek 47:15]]).

column5: The false prophet who struck Micaiah
column7: He was the son of Chenaanah who made horns of iron and prophesied that Ahab would win ([[@11022011|1 Kgs 22:11]]). He struck the true prophet Micaiah on the cheek ([[@11022024|1 Kgs 22:24]]).

column5: The last king of Judah
column7: Zedekiah was a son of Josiah and the last king of Judah. His original name was Mattaniah, but the king of Babylon made him king in place of his nephew Jehoiachin and changed his name to Zedekiah ([[@12024017|2 Kgs 24:17]]). He became king at twenty-one and reigned eleven years in Jerusalem ([[@12024018|2 Kgs 24:18]]). He did not humble himself before the LORD's word spoken by the prophet Jeremiah, and he rebelled against the king of Babylon ([[@14036012-14036013|2 Chr 36:12-13]]). In the end Jerusalem fell, and after seeing his sons killed, he had his eyes put out and was taken to Babylon ([[@12025007|2 Kgs 25:7]]).

column5: A man in the line of Jehoiakim
column7: He is named after Jeconiah in the list of the sons of Jehoiakim ([[@13003016|1 Chr 3:16]]). The Bible tells nothing more about him.

column5: A man who sealed the covenant
column7: Among those who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah's time, he is named right after Nehemiah the governor, the son of Hacaliah ([[@16010001|Neh 10:1]]).

column5: False prophet in Babylon
column7: He was the son of Maaseiah and prophesied lies in the LORD’s name to the captives in Babylon ([[@24029021|Jer 29:21]]). Jeremiah said the king of Babylon would roast him in the fire ([[@24029022|Jer 29:22]]).

column5: An official in Jehoiakim's day
column7: The son of Hananiah, he was one of the princes sitting together in the scribe's room in the king's house in Jehoiakim's time ([[@24036009|Jer 36:9]]; [[@24036012|Jer 36:12]]).

column5: Midianite prince captured in Gideon’s day
column7: He was a prince of Midian whom the men of Ephraim captured in Gideon’s time and killed at Zeeb’s wine press ([[@7007025|Judg 7:25]]; [[@7008003|Judg 8:3]]). The Psalms hold him up as an example of the judgment that fell on God’s enemies ([[@19083011|Ps 83:11]]).

column5: Benjamite town where Saul was buried
column7: It was a town given to the tribe of Benjamin ([[@6018028|Josh 18:28]]). David buried the bones of Saul and Jonathan in the tomb of Kish in Zela ([[@10021014|2 Sam 21:14]]).

column5: Ammonite among David’s mighty men
column7: He was an Ammonite, one of David’s mighty men ([[@10023037|2 Sam 23:37]]). He also appears in the list of David’s mighty men in 1 Chronicles ([[@13011039|1 Chr 11:39]]).

column5: Man of Manasseh who left only daughters
column7: He was a man of the tribe of Manasseh, the grandson of Gilead and the son of Hepher ([[@4027001|Num 27:1]]). He died in the wilderness with no sons, leaving only five daughters ([[@4027003|Num 27:3]]). When his daughters asked that their father's name not be removed from his family, the LORD said, "The daughters of Zelophehad speak right", and had them given an inheritance ([[@4027007|Num 27:7]]). So that the inheritance would not pass to another tribe, the command was given that the daughters marry only within their father's tribe, and they did so ([[@4036006|Num 36:6]], 10).

column5: The place of Rachel's tomb
column7: Rachel's tomb was at Zelzah on the border of Benjamin, and Samuel told Saul he would meet two men there ([[@9010002|1 Sam 10:2]]).

column5: Benjamite town; mountain in Ephraim’s hill country
column7: It was a town given to the tribe of Benjamin ([[@6018022|Josh 18:22]]). Abijah king of Judah stood on Mount Zemaraim in the hill country of Ephraim and called out to Jeroboam and all Israel ([[@14013004|2 Chr 13:4]]).

column5: People descended from Canaan
column7: They were one of the peoples descended from Noah’s grandson Canaan ([[@1010015|Gen 10:15]]; [[@1010018|Gen 10:18]]; [[@13001016|1 Chr 1:16]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Becher
column7: The first named among the sons of Becher the son of Benjamin, listed with Joash, Eliezer, and others ([[@13007006|1 Chr 7:6]]; [[@13007008|1 Chr 7:8]]).

column5: A town in the lowland of Judah
column7: It is named as one of the towns in the lowland that the tribe of Judah received as an inheritance ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]; [[@6015037|Josh 15:37]]).

column5: A lawyer Paul asked Titus to help
column7: A lawyer; Paul told Titus to send him and Apollos on their journey quickly so that they would lack nothing ([[@56003013|Titus 3:13]]).

column5: The second priest in Zedekiah's time
column7: He was a priest, the son of Maaseiah, whom King Zedekiah sent to Jeremiah to ask him to pray ([[@24021001|Jer 21:1]]; [[@24037003|Jer 37:3]]). When Jerusalem fell, he was taken captive as the 'second priest' ([[@12025018|2 Kgs 25:18]]).

column5: A prophet in the days of Josiah
column7: A prophet who received the LORD's word in the days of King Josiah. He was the son of Cushi and the great-great-grandson of Hezekiah ([[@36001001|Zeph 1:1]]).

column5: Father of Josiah (Hen)
column7: He was the father of Josiah, whose house those returning from Babylon entered in the days of the prophet Zechariah ([[@38006010|Zech 6:10]]). In verse 14 he appears as 'Hen the son of Zephaniah' ([[@38006014|Zech 6:14]]).

column5: Where Asa fought the Ethiopian army
column7: The valley at Mareshah where King Asa of Judah drew up for battle against the army of Zerah the Ethiopian ([[@14014009-14014010|2 Chr 14:9-10]]).

column5: Son of Eliphaz, a chief of Edom
column7: He was a son of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn ([[@1036011|Gen 36:11]]). He became one of the chiefs of Edom, and in 1 Chronicles his name is written 'Zephi' ([[@1036015|Gen 36:15]]; [[@13001036|1 Chr 1:36]]).

column5: A fortified city of Naphtali
column7: One of the fortified cities the tribe of Naphtali received as an inheritance by their families, listed with Ziddim ([[@6019035|Josh 19:35]]; [[@6019039|Josh 19:39]]).

column5: Son of Reuel, a chief of Edom
column7: He was a son of Reuel, Esau's son ([[@1036013|Gen 36:13]]). He became one of the chiefs in the land of Edom who came from Reuel ([[@1036017|Gen 36:17]]).

column5: Father of Jobab, king of Edom
column7: He was the father of Jobab of Bozrah, who became king of Edom after Bela died ([[@1036033|Gen 36:33]]; [[@13001044|1 Chr 1:44]]).

column5: Son of Judah and twin brother of Perez
column7: He was one of the twin sons born to Judah and Tamar. During the birth he put out his hand first, and the midwife tied a scarlet thread on it, but he drew his hand back, Perez came out first, and Zerah came out after him ([[@1038028-1038030|Gen 38:28-30]]). His descendants became the family of the Zerahites ([[@4026020|Num 26:20]]), and Achan, who took some of the devoted things at Jericho, was also a descendant of Zerah ([[@6007001|Josh 7:1]]). His name also appears with Perez in Jesus' genealogy in Matthew ([[@40001003|Matt 1:3]]).

column5: A son of Simeon
column7: He was a son of Simeon, and from him came the family of the Zerahites ([[@4026013|Num 26:13]]; [[@13004024|1 Chr 4:24]]). In Genesis he appears as 'Zohar' ([[@1046010|Gen 46:10]]).

column5: Gershonite Levite
column7: He was a descendant of Levi’s son Gershom and the son of Iddo ([[@13006020-13006021|1 Chr 6:20-21]]). He was one of the ancestors of Asaph the singer ([[@13006039-13006041|1 Chr 6:39-41]]).

column5: The Ethiopian who attacked Judah under Asa
column7: An Ethiopian who came to Mareshah with an army of a million troops and three hundred chariots, but the LORD struck the Ethiopians ([[@14014009|2 Chr 14:9]]; [[@14014012|2 Chr 14:12]]).

column5: A man in the priestly line of Aaron
column7: He was a descendant of Aaron, the son of Uzzi and the father of Meraioth ([[@13006006|1 Chr 6:6]]). His name also appears in Ezra's genealogy ([[@15007004|Ezra 7:4]]).

column5: Father of Eliehoenai
column7: A descendant of Pahathmoab; his son Eliehoenai came up with Ezra, leading two hundred men ([[@15008004|Ezra 8:4]]).

column5: Brook that Israel crossed
column7: It was a valley where Israel camped in the wilderness ([[@4021012|Num 21:12]]). It took thirty-eight years from leaving Kadesh Barnea until they crossed the brook Zered ([[@5002014|Deut 2:14]]).

column5: Jeroboam's hometown
column7: Jeroboam the son of Nebat, who rebelled against Solomon, was an Ephraimite from Zeredah ([[@11011026|1 Kgs 11:26]]).

column5: Wife of Haman
column7: She was Haman’s wife ([[@17005010|Esth 5:10]]). Together with his friends she urged Haman to set up a tall gallows on which to hang Mordecai ([[@17005014|Esth 5:14]]).

column5: A son of Ashhur and Helah
column7: One of the sons that Helah bore to Ashhur, the father of Tekoa ([[@13004005|1 Chr 4:5]]; [[@13004007|1 Chr 4:7]]).

column5: A town of the tribe of Reuben
column7: A town 'in the mount of the valley' in the land Moses gave to the tribe of Reuben ([[@6013015|Josh 13:15]]; [[@6013019|Josh 13:19]]).

column5: Son of Jeduthun, temple musician
column7: He was one of the sons of Jeduthun, who in David’s time gave thanks and praised the LORD with the harp ([[@13025003|1 Chr 25:3]]). Some take him to be the same person as 'Izri' of the fourth lot ([[@13025011|1 Chr 25:11]]).

column5: An ancestor of Saul, grandfather of Kish
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Kish, Saul's father. Kish, a man of Benjamin, was "the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Becorath" ([[@9009001-9009002|1 Sam 9:1-2]]).

column5: Mother of Jeroboam
column7: The mother of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, Solomon's servant who rebelled against the king; she was a widow ([[@11011026|1 Kgs 11:26]]).

column5: Governor of Judah who led the returning exiles
column7: He was the son of Shealtiel and a descendant of David's royal line ([[@40001012|Matt 1:12]]). In the time of Cyrus king of Persia, he led the exiles back to Jerusalem ([[@15002002|Ezra 2:2]]). With Jeshua the high priest, he built God's altar and began the work of building the temple ([[@15003002|Ezra 3:2]], 8). The work stopped when it met opposition, but through Haggai God stirred the spirit of Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, and they went back to building the temple ([[@37001014|Hag 1:14]]). Scholars differ on whether he is the same person as Sheshbazzar in the book of Ezra.

column5: A man in the genealogy of Jesus
column7: In Luke's genealogy of Jesus, he appears as the son of Shealtiel and the father of Rhesa ([[@42003027|Luke 3:27]]). Many think he is the same person as "Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel", who led the people back from exile ([[@16012001|Neh 12:1]]).

column5: David's sister, mother of Joab and Abishai
column7: Zeruiah was David's sister and the mother of three brothers, Abishai, Joab, and Asahel ([[@13002016|1 Chr 2:16]]). All three sons became famous warriors in David's army, and the Bible often calls them 'the sons of Zeruiah' ([[@10002018|2 Sam 2:18]]). After Abner's death David lamented, "These men, the sons of Zeruiah are too hard for me" ([[@10003039|2 Sam 3:39]]). Very little of her own story is left in the Bible.

column5: Gershonite, son of Ladan
column7: He was a son of Ladan, of the Gershonite Levites, in David’s time ([[@13023007-13023008|1 Chr 23:7-8]]). A Zetham in charge of the treasuries of the LORD’s house is listed as a son of Jehieli of Ladan’s family ([[@13026022|1 Chr 26:22]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Bilhan
column7: One of the sons of Bilhan, the son of Jediael of the tribe of Benjamin; he was a head of his family and a mighty man of valor ([[@13007010-13007011|1 Chr 7:10-11]]).

column5: One of Ahasuerus' seven eunuchs
column7: One of the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus, sent to bring Queen Vashti ([[@17001010-17001011|Esth 1:10-11]]).

column5: A family member among the Gadites
column7: He is named as one of seven brothers of the families of the Gadites who lived in the land of Bashan ([[@13005011|1 Chr 5:11]]; [[@13005013|1 Chr 5:13]]).

column5: Servant of Saul's house who managed Mephibosheth's land
column7: He was a servant of Saul's house, and when David was looking for someone to show kindness to for Jonathan's sake, Ziba told him that Jonathan had a son who was lame ([[@10009002-10009003|2 Sam 9:2-3]]). David told Ziba to take his fifteen sons and twenty servants, farm Mephibosheth's land, and serve his master's son ([[@10009009-10009010|2 Sam 9:9-10]]). As David passed the top of the hill while fleeing, Ziba came with donkeys and food and claimed that Mephibosheth was trying to get the kingdom back ([[@10016001-10016004|2 Sam 16:1-4]]). Later Mephibosheth told the king that his servant had deceived him, and David told the two of them to divide the land ([[@10019026-10019029|2 Sam 19:26-29]]).

column5: Grandfather of Esau’s wife Oholibamah
column7: He was a Hivite, and Esau’s wife Oholibamah was the daughter of his daughter Anah ([[@1036002|Gen 36:2]]; [[@1036014|Gen 36:14]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Shaharaim
column7: One of the sons that Shaharaim had by his wife Hodesh in the land of Moab ([[@13008008-13008009|1 Chr 8:8-9]]).

column5: Mother of King Joash
column7: She was the mother of Joash king of Judah and came from Beersheba ([[@12012001|2 Kgs 12:1]]). Joash reigned forty years in Jerusalem ([[@14024001|2 Chr 24:1]]).

column5: A Levite, son of Izhar
column7: The son of Izhar, the son of Kohath, he appears in the genealogy of the Levites along with Korah and Nepheg ([[@2006018|Exod 6:18]]; [[@2006021|Exod 6:21]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Shimei
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin as one of the sons of Shimei ([[@13008019|1 Chr 8:19]]; [[@13008021|1 Chr 8:21]]). The Bible tells nothing more about him.

column5: A Benjamite, son of Shashak
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin as one of the sons of Shashak ([[@13008023|1 Chr 8:23]]; [[@13008025|1 Chr 8:25]]). The Bible tells nothing more about him.

column5: A Benjamite, son of Jeroham
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin as one of the sons of Jeroham ([[@13008027|1 Chr 8:27]]). The Bible tells nothing more about him.

column5: Son of Asaph, a Levite
column7: He was a son of Asaph the Levite, the father of Mica, and the grandfather of Mattaniah ([[@13009015|1 Chr 9:15]]). In Nehemiah his name is written 'Zabdi' ([[@16011017|Neh 11:17]]).

column5: A descendant of Eliezer, father of Shelomoth
column7: In the genealogy of Eliezer the son of Moses, he appears as the son of Joram and the father of Shelomoth ([[@13026024-13026025|1 Chr 26:24-25]]).

column5: Father of Eliezer, leader of Reuben
column7: His son Eliezer was the ruler of the Reubenites among those over the tribes of Israel in David's time ([[@13027016|1 Chr 27:16]]).

column5: Father of Amasiah
column7: His son was Amasiah, who willingly offered himself to the LORD and led two hundred thousand mighty men of valor in Jehoshaphat's time ([[@14017016|2 Chr 17:16]]).

column5: Father of Elishaphat the captain
column7: His son Elishaphat was one of the captains of hundreds who made a covenant with Jehoiada the priest in the seventh year ([[@14023001|2 Chr 23:1]]).

column5: A mighty man of Ephraim
column7: A mighty man of Ephraim who killed Maaseiah, the son of the king of Judah, as well as Azrikam the ruler of the house and Elkanah who was next to the king ([[@14028007|2 Chr 28:7]])

column5: Father of Joel the overseer
column7: His son Joel became overseer of the people of Benjamin who lived in Jerusalem in Nehemiah's time ([[@16011007|Neh 11:7]]; [[@16011009|Neh 11:9]]).

column5: Head of the priestly family of Abijah
column7: In the days of Joiakim, he was a head of a priestly family, leading the family of Abijah. The head of the family of Miniamin and Moadiah was Piltai ([[@16012012|Neh 12:12]]; [[@16012017|Neh 12:17]]).

column5: A fortified city of Naphtali
column7: One of the fortified cities the tribe of Naphtali received as an inheritance by their families, listed with Zer ([[@6019035|Josh 19:35]]; [[@6019039|Josh 19:39]]).

column5: Temple-servant family back from exile
column7: 'The children of Ziha' are the first named among the temple servants who returned from exile in Babylon ([[@15002043|Ezra 2:43]]; [[@16007046|Neh 7:46]]).

column5: Leader of the temple servants in Ophel
column7: After the return from exile, he was over the temple servants who lived in Ophel, named along with Gishpa ([[@16011021|Neh 11:21]]).

column5: The town David received from a Philistine king
column7: It appears in the list of towns in the south of Judah's land, and it is also among the towns the tribe of Simeon received within Judah's inheritance ([[@6015021-6015031|Josh 15:21-31]]; [[@6019001-6019005|Josh 19:1-5]]). When David fled from Saul to the land of the Philistines, Achish king of Gath gave him this town, and the Bible says, "Ziklag belongs to the kings of Judah to this day" ([[@9027001-9027006|1 Sam 27:1-6]]). While David was away, the Amalekites burned Ziklag and carried off the women and children, but David pursued them and recovered everything that had been taken ([[@9030001-9030018|1 Sam 30:1-18]]).

column5: Wife of Lamech, mother of Tubal Cain
column7: She was one of the two wives of Lamech, a descendant of Cain ([[@1004019|Gen 4:19]]). She gave birth to Tubal Cain, who forged tools of bronze and iron, and to his sister Naamah ([[@1004022|Gen 4:22]]).

column5: A Benjamite, son of Shimei
column7: He appears in the genealogy of Benjamin as one of the sons of Shimei ([[@13008020-13008021|1 Chr 8:20-21]]). The Bible tells nothing more about him.

column5: A captain from Manasseh who joined David
column7: One of the captains of thousands from the tribe of Manasseh who joined David as he went to Ziklag ([[@13012020|1 Chr 12:20]]).

column5: Leah's servant, mother of Gad and Asher
column7: She was the servant Laban gave to his daughter Leah as her maid ([[@1029024|Gen 29:24]]). When Leah saw that she had stopped having children, she gave Zilpah to Jacob as a wife ([[@1030009|Gen 30:9]]). Leah named Zilpah's first son Gad and her second son Asher ([[@1030010-1030013|Gen 30:10-13]]). Gad and Asher were counted among Jacob's twelve sons and became ancestors of tribes of Israel ([[@1035026|Gen 35:26]]).

column5: Gershonite Levite
column7: He was a descendant of Levi’s son Gershom and the son of Jahath ([[@13006020|1 Chr 6:20]]). A Zimmah also appears among the ancestors of Asaph the singer ([[@13006042|1 Chr 6:42]]).

column5: Father of Joah the Gershonite
column7: His son was Joah the Gershonite, one of the Levites who arose in Hezekiah's time ([[@14029012|2 Chr 29:12]]).

column5: Son of Abraham and Keturah
column7: He is named first among the six sons Abraham had by Keturah ([[@1025001-1025002|Gen 25:1-2]]; [[@13001032|1 Chr 1:32]]).

column5: A Simeonite leader killed with a Midianite woman
column7: The son of Salu and a leader of a family among the Simeonites, he was killed together with a Midianite woman ([[@4025014|Num 25:14]]).

column5: King of Israel who reigned seven days
column7: He was a servant of Elah king of Israel and commander of half his chariots. While Elah was drunk in Tirzah, Zimri struck him down, killed him, and reigned in his place ([[@11016009-11016010|1 Kgs 16:9-10]]). He destroyed the whole house of Baasha, just as the LORD had spoken through the prophet Jehu ([[@11016012|1 Kgs 16:12]]). Seven days after Zimri became king in Tirzah, the people in the camp made Omri king, came up, and besieged Tirzah ([[@11016015-11016017|1 Kgs 16:15-17]]). When Zimri saw that the city was taken, he set the palace on fire and died in it ([[@11016018|1 Kgs 16:18]]).

column5: A nation of kings Jeremiah named
column7: Among the nations that would drink the cup of the LORD's wrath, "all the kings of Zimri" appear along with Elam and the Medes ([[@24025015|Jer 25:15]]; [[@24025025|Jer 25:25]]). Its location is unknown.

column5: The wilderness south of Canaan where Kadesh lay
column7: It was a wilderness on the southern border of Canaan, alongside Edom ([[@4034003|Num 34:3]]). The twelve spies explored the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, at the entrance of Hamath ([[@4013021|Num 13:21]]). When the whole congregation of Israel came into the wilderness of Zin and stayed at Kadesh, Miriam died there ([[@4020001|Num 20:1]]). Because Moses and Aaron did not uphold God's holiness at the waters of Meribah of Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, they could not enter the Promised Land ([[@5032051|Deut 32:51]]). It is a different place from the wilderness of Sin, between Elim and Sinai, in Exodus.

column5: A town in the hill country of Judah
column7: It is named with Hebron as one of the towns in the hill country that the tribe of Judah received as an inheritance ([[@6015054|Josh 15:54]]).

column5: A town in the south of Judah
column7: One of the towns the tribe of Judah received in the south, toward the border of Edom ([[@6015021|Josh 15:21]]; [[@6015024|Josh 15:24]]).

column5: Place in Judah where David hid from Saul
column7: It appears with Maon and Carmel in the list of towns in the hill country of Judah ([[@6015055|Josh 15:55]]). David stayed "in the hill country in the wilderness of Ziph" while fleeing from Saul, and Jonathan came to him in the woods there and strengthened his hand in God ([[@9023014-9023016|1 Sam 23:14-16]]). But the Ziphites went to Saul at Gibeah and told him where David was hiding ([[@9023019|1 Sam 23:19]]). When the Ziphites reported again, Saul came down to the wilderness of Ziph with three thousand men, but David did not kill the sleeping Saul and left taking only his spear and water jug ([[@9026001-9026012|1 Sam 26:1-12]]).

column5: A son of Jehallelel
column7: In the genealogy of Judah, he is one of the sons of Jehallelel, listed with Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel ([[@13004016|1 Chr 4:16]]).

column5: A son of Jehallelel
column7: In the genealogy of Judah, he is one of the sons of Jehallelel, listed with Ziph, Tiria, and Asarel ([[@13004016|1 Chr 4:16]]).

column5: Son of Gad
column7: He is named first among the sons of Gad, Jacob’s son ([[@1046016|Gen 46:16]]). In Numbers he is called 'Zephon,' and from him came 'the family of the Zephonites' ([[@4026015|Num 26:15]]).

column5: A place on the Promised Land's northern border
column7: A place on the northern border of Israel that the LORD set out, with the border running on to Hazar Enan ([[@4034007-4034009|Num 34:7-9]]).

column5: Father of Balak king of Moab
column7: He was the father of Balak, king of Moab. The Bible often calls Balak "Balak the son of Zippor" ([[@4022002|Num 22:2]], 4). Balak was afraid of Israel and tried to call Balaam the son of Beor to curse them ([[@4022005-4022006|Num 22:5-6]]; [[@6024009|Josh 24:9]]). In his oracle Balaam said, "Listen to me, you son of Zippor", and instead spoke words that blessed Israel ([[@4023018|Num 23:18]]). The Bible tells us nothing about what Zippor himself did.

column5: Wife of Moses
column7: One of the seven daughters of the priest of Midian, she was given by her father to Moses as his wife ([[@2002016|Exod 2:16]], 21). On the way she circumcised her son with a flint, and later she came with her father Jethro to Moses in the wilderness ([[@2004025|Exod 4:25]]; [[@2018002|Exod 18:2]], 5).

column5: The ascent Moab and Ammon came up by
column7: When Moab and Ammon came to attack Judah in Jehoshaphat's time, the word came through Jahaziel the Levite that they would come up by this ascent and Judah should go down against them ([[@14020001|2 Chr 20:1]]; [[@14020014-14020016|2 Chr 20:14-16]]).

column5: A leader of the Simeonites
column7: The son of Shiphi, he appears in the genealogy of Simeon as a prince in his family, and their families increased greatly ([[@13004037-13004038|1 Chr 4:37-38]]).

column5: A son of Rehoboam and Maacah
column7: One of the sons Rehoboam had by Maacah, the granddaughter of Absalom, after he married her ([[@14011020|2 Chr 11:20]]).

column5: Gershonite, son of Shimei
column7: He was the second son of Shimei, of the Gershonite Levites, in David’s time ([[@13023011|1 Chr 23:11]]). In the verse before, his name is written 'Zina' ([[@13023010|1 Chr 23:10]]).

column5: Ancient city in northern Egypt
column7: It was an ancient city of Egypt. Numbers says that Hebron "was built seven years before Zoan in Egypt" ([[@4013022|Num 13:22]]). The Psalms sing that God did marvelous things in the sight of Israel's fathers in the field of Zoan ([[@19078012|Ps 78:12]], 43). Isaiah said the princes of Zoan were foolish, and Ezekiel prophesied that God would set a fire in Zoan ([[@23019011|Isa 19:11]]; [[@26030014|Ezek 30:14]]). Scholars generally identify it with Tanis in the lower Nile region.

column5: The small town near the Dead Sea where Lot fled
column7: It was a town near Sodom and Gomorrah, and its earlier name was Bela ([[@1014002|Gen 14:2]]). When Sodom was destroyed, Lot said he could not flee to the mountains and asked to escape to this nearby little town, and that town was spared ([[@1019019-1019021|Gen 19:19-21]]). So the town was called Zoar, and Lot arrived there as the sun rose ([[@1019022-1019023|Gen 19:22-23]]). Later Isaiah prophesied that the nobles of Moab would flee to Zoar weeping ([[@23015005|Isa 15:5]]).

column5: Syrian kingdom that fought against David
column7: It seems to have been a Syrian kingdom stretching from east of the Lebanon mountains toward the Euphrates River. Among the enemies Saul fought after he became king were the kings of Zobah ([[@9014047|1 Sam 14:47]]). David struck Hadadezer king of Zobah as he was going to the Euphrates River and won a great victory ([[@10008003-10008004|2 Sam 8:3-4]]). The Ammonites even hired foot soldiers from the Syrians of Zobah to fight David ([[@10010006|2 Sam 10:6]]). Rezon, who had fled from Hadadezer, later became an enemy of Solomon ([[@11011023|1 Kgs 11:23]]).

column5: A descendant of Hakkoz of Judah
column7: In the genealogy of Judah, he is one of the children of Hakkoz, named with Anub ([[@13004008|1 Chr 4:8]]).

column5: Father of Ephron the Hittite
column7: He was the father of Ephron the Hittite, from whom Abraham sought to buy the cave of Machpelah ([[@1023008-1023009|Gen 23:8-9]]). Abraham was buried in the cave in that field ([[@1025009|Gen 25:9]]).

column5: A son of Ishi
column7: In the genealogy of Judah, he appears as a son of Ishi, along with Ben Zoheth ([[@13004020|1 Chr 4:20]]). The Bible tells nothing more about him.

column5: Asherite, son of Helem
column7: He was a son of Helem, of the tribe of Asher ([[@13007035|1 Chr 7:35]]). His sons included Suah, Harnepher, and Shual ([[@13007036|1 Chr 7:36]]).

column5: One of Job's three friends
column7: He was a Naamathite, one of the three friends who came to comfort Job after hearing of the disaster that had come on him ([[@18002011|Job 2:11]]). He answered Job twice ([[@18011001|Job 11:1]]; [[@18020001|Job 20:1]]).

column5: The field where Balak took Balaam
column7: Balak led Balaam to the field of Zophim and built seven altars on the top of Pisgah ([[@4023013-4023014|Num 23:13-14]]).

column5: Samson's hometown, a town of the tribe of Dan
column7: It appears together with Eshtaol in the list of towns in the lowland of Judah ([[@6015033|Josh 15:33]]). Manoah, a man of the tribe of Dan, lived here in Zorah ([[@7013002|Judg 13:2]]). The place where the LORD's Spirit first began to move his son Samson was also "Mahaneh Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol" ([[@7013025|Judg 13:25]]). After Samson died, he was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol in the burial place of his father Manoah ([[@7016031|Judg 16:31]]).

column5: A family among Judah's descendants
column7: They were a family that came from the families of Kiriath Jearim ([[@13002053|1 Chr 2:53]]). Ahumai and Lahad, the sons of Jahath of the line of Shobal, became the families of the Zorathites ([[@13004002|1 Chr 4:2]]).

column5: Father of Nethanel, leader of the tribe of Issachar
column7: He was the father of Nethanel, the leader of the children of Issachar in the wilderness ([[@4002005|Num 2:5]]). His son brought the offering on behalf of the children of Issachar on the second day ([[@4007018|Num 7:18]]).

column5: Ancestor of Samuel
column7: He was the great-great-grandfather of Elkanah, Samuel's father ([[@9001001|1 Sam 1:1]]). In the Levite genealogy of 1 Chronicles, Zuph is listed as the son of Elkanah and the father of Toah ([[@13006035|1 Chr 6:35]]).

column5: Where Saul searched for the donkeys
column7: Saul traveled through several regions looking for his father's donkeys, and when he reached the land of Zuph, he suggested turning back so his father would not worry ([[@9009004-9009005|1 Sam 9:4-5]]).

column5: Father of Cozbi, a Midianite chief
column7: The head of a family of the Midianite people; Cozbi, the Midianite woman who was killed, was his daughter ([[@4025015|Num 25:15]]).

column5: Midianite king killed by Israel
column7: He was one of the five kings of Midian whom Israel killed when they attacked Midian ([[@4031008|Num 31:8]]). The book of Joshua also lists him among the chiefs of Midian ([[@6013021|Josh 13:21]]).

column5: Son of Jeiel, father of Gibeon
column7: He was the second son of Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, and his wife Maacah ([[@13008029-13008030|1 Chr 8:29-30]]; [[@13009035-13009036|1 Chr 9:35-36]]).

column5: Leader of the Merarite families
column7: The son of Abihail, he was the prince of the families and clans of Merari in the wilderness, and they camped on the north side of the tabernacle ([[@4003035|Num 3:35]]).

column5: Father of Shelumiel, leader of the tribe of Simeon
column7: He was the father of Shelumiel, the leader of the children of Simeon in the wilderness ([[@4001006|Num 1:6]]). His son brought the offering on behalf of the children of Simeon on the fifth day ([[@4007036|Num 7:36]]).

column5: A people defeated by Chedorlaomer
column7: A people struck in Ham by Chedorlaomer and the kings allied with him, who came out in the fourteenth year in Abram's time ([[@1014005|Gen 14:5]]).
